High-field-side (inboard) equatorial midplane - the inner-midplane counterpart of outboard_midplane. The inner-midplane reference is the inboard intersection of the horizontal plane through the magnetic axis (or the DD midplane_identifier) with the plasma boundary / first wall. DD: e.g. equilibrium/time_slice/profiles_1d/r_inboard (inboard major radius of the flux surface at the midplane).

The spatial location identified as the launching position in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.

Plasma-facing limiter. As a measurement locus, 'at_limiter' denotes the scrape-off-layer plasma immediately adjacent to the limiter surface; the DD provides only the limiter surface geometry (wall/description_2d/limiter) and the precise plasma evaluation point is not yet standardised (IMAS_3226). For the separatrix-limiter tangency CONTACT point use active_limiter_point; for a quantity distributed OVER the limiter surface (e.g. a peak power density) use the 'along' relation (along_limiter).
The limiter tile treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The directed observation path from a diagnostic aperture or detector through the observed domain.
The lower hybrid antenna treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged.
A diagnostic sensor used to measure a component of the local magnetic field.
The mass spectrometer treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The mass spectrometer channel treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The position in the cylindrical frame at which a diagnostic channel samples, used for the coordinates of that position where the coordinate serves many instrument families.
A reference plane through the tokamak on which the vertical coordinate is zero in the adopted coordinate system.
The surface where the absolute value of the safety factor is minimum.

Low-field-side (outboard) equatorial midplane. The outer-midplane reference follows the DD midplane_identifier (default option 'dr_dz_zero_sep': the outboard separatrix point where dr/dz = 0). For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix.

Intersection of the separatrix with the outboard (low-field-side) midplane - the outboard separatrix point where dr/dz = 0 (the local major-radius maximum of the separatrix). This is where a separatrix POINT value is evaluated. DD: equilibrium/time_slice/boundary_separatrix/dr_dz_zero_point; outer-midplane reference per the midplane_identifier.
The spatial location identified as the outer in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The spatial location identified as the outlet in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.

A discrete geometry element of a passive conducting loop.
The passive structure treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.

H-mode edge transport-barrier (pedestal) region. Ambiguous as a single point: for a profile VALUE use pedestal_top; for a maximum-gradient or fit POSITION use pedestal_maximum. Prefer the more specific token over this bare one. DD: summary/local/pedestal, summary/pedestal_fits/*.

Location of the maximum pedestal gradient (the steep mid-pedestal), i.e. the peak-gradient / fit position of the edge barrier. Distinct from the pedestal top. DD: summary/pedestal_fits/*/d_dpsi_norm_max_position, summary/local/pedestal/position/psi.
The edge transport-barrier region characterized by steep plasma-profile gradients.
Top of the H-mode edge pedestal (the barrier's inner shoulder), where 'the pedestal value' of a profile is conventionally reported. DD: summary/pedestal_fits/* pedestal-top fit outputs.
The spatial location identified as the pedestal top high field side in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The spatial location identified as the pedestal top low field side in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.

NAMES.name: absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short:
Absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic wave
power transferred from one coherent beam to the plasma along its trajectory.
NAMES.long:
Absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic wave
power transferred from a single coherent beam to plasma particles along the
beam trajectory. It is summed over the contributing plasma species and is
distinct from the residual wave power represented by
power_of_beam_tracing_beam.

Under the single-beam power balance, the absorbed power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs}} = P_0 - P_{\mathrm{res}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is this absorbed power, $P_0$ is the
[initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam),
and $P_{\mathrm{res}}$ is the residual power of the same beam at the
trajectory endpoint. The total includes contributions represented by
species-resolved quantities such as
[electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam)
and
[ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam).
It excludes power remaining in the wave and power assigned at launch but not
transferred along the traced trajectory.

NAMES.name: alpha_angle_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Signed inclination of the alpha-side lateral face of an oblique trapezoidal
ICRH antenna-strap cross-section relative to the directed strap base edge.
NAMES.long:
The alpha angle is the oriented inclination of the alpha-side lateral face
of an oblique trapezoidal ICRH antenna-strap cross-section, measured from
the directed strap base edge. It specifies the alpha-side geometry
complementary to the beta-side quantity represented by angle of antenna
strap.

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left(\hat{n}\cdot(\hat{b}\times\hat{a}),\,\hat{b}\cdot\hat{a}\right)
$$

where $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector along the directed strap base edge,
$\hat{a}$ is the unit vector along the alpha-side lateral face, and
$\hat{n}$ is the positive normal to the oriented cross-sectional plane. The
angle is restricted to the alpha-side face and is distinct from the
beta-side inclination.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when rotation from the directed strap base edge
toward the alpha-side lateral face follows the positive normal of the
oriented strap cross-section.

sources.leaf_definition: Inclination of first angle measured counter-clockwise from horizontal outwardly directed radial vector (grad R).
sources.parent_definition: Parallelogram description of the element

NAMES.name: back_surface_distance_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Geometric rear-surface clearance between an ion-cyclotron heating antenna
strap and the conducting wall or conductor behind it.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the geometric standoff between the rear surface of an
ion-cyclotron heating antenna strap and the conducting wall or other
conductor located behind that surface.

The clearance is the shortest separation between the two relevant surfaces:

$$
d_{back} = \min_{\mathbf{r}_b \in S_b,\,\mathbf{r}_c \in S_c} \left\|\mathbf{r}_c - \mathbf{r}_b\right\|
$$

where $d_{\rm back}$ is the rear-surface clearance, $S_b$ is the strap back
surface, $S_c$ is the facing conducting-wall or conductor surface, and
$\mathbf{r}_b$ and $\mathbf{r}_c$ are position vectors on those surfaces.

The quantity applies only to the rear-facing separation of the antenna strap
and does not denote the strap thickness, the distance to its inner or outer
cylindrical boundaries, or either oblique cross-sectional length. The
related [inner radius of the antenna
strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap), [outer radius of the antenna
strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap), [major length of the antenna
strap](name:major_length_of_antenna_strap), and [minor length of the antenna
strap](name:minor_length_of_antenna_strap) describe other strap dimensions
rather than this conductor clearance.

This geometric clearance is an antenna-design parameter that influences the
strap's loading resistance and radio-frequency coupling efficiency to the
plasma; it is not itself an electrical resistance, coupling coefficient, or
power quantity.

sources.leaf_definition: Distance to conducting wall or other conductor behind the antenna strap
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: binormal_wave_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Signed component of the oscillatory electromagnetic-wave magnetic
perturbation along the local binormal direction, distinct from the total
binormal magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the binormal component of the oscillatory magnetic
perturbation carried by a coherent electromagnetic wave. It excludes
equilibrium and other static magnetic-field contributions.

For a harmonic-wave phasor representation, the component amplitude is
defined by projection on the local binormal unit vector:

$$
\widetilde{B}_{\mathrm{wave,bi}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)=\widetilde{\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bi}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\omega$ is angular frequency,
$\widetilde{\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex amplitude of the
wave magnetic field, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bi}}$ is the local binormal
unit vector, and $\widetilde{B}_{\mathrm{wave,bi}}$ is the complex amplitude
of the binormal component. The corresponding physical time-dependent
component is obtained from the real part of the phasor convention; real- and
imaginary-part quantities are phase-resolved representations, not alternate
definitions of this field.

The binormal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface and
perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic-field direction, distinguishing
this quantity from the [parallel wave magnetic
field](name:parallel_wave_magnetic_field). It is the magnetic-field analog
of the [binormal wave electric field](name:binormal_wave_electric_field).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the wave magnetic-field projection is along
the declared positive binormal unit vector.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Magnitude of perpendicular (to the static magnetic field) wave magnetic field tangent to a flux surface, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: capacitance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Effective capacitance of an impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna, relating stored charge to the RF voltage used for circuit
tuning.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the non-negative lumped capacitance associated with an
impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron heating antenna module. It
represents the element's ability to store electric charge and participate in
tuning the radio-frequency transmission circuit.

For an ideal lumped capacitive element, the capacitance is defined by

$$
C = \frac{Q}{V}
$$

where $C$ is the capacitance, $Q$ is the charge stored on the element, and
$V$ is the electric potential difference across the element.

The quantity applies to the specified matching element of the antenna and
does not represent the capacitance of an unrelated circuit component or the
entire transmission system. It is a circuit parameter rather than a power,
current, or operating-frequency quantity.

Together with the [resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), it characterizes
the antenna's effective RF impedance; the [frequency of an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna](name:frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) identifies
the RF operating frequency at which the matching condition is evaluated.

sources.leaf_definition: Capacitance of the macthing element
sources.parent_definition: Set of matching elements

NAMES.name: current_density_due_to_distribution_function_driven
NAMES.short:
Net electric current-density vector obtained by summing signed charge fluxes
from all particle populations in the full kinetic distribution, including
fast-particle and thermal back-current contributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net electric current-density vector generated by the
charge-weighted particle motion represented in a full kinetic distribution.
It includes the fast-particle contribution together with the electron and
thermal-ion back-current contributions.

The current-density vector is defined by

$$
\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x})$ is the current-density vector at position
$\mathbf{x}$, $s$ indexes every included particle species or population,
$q_s$ is the signed electric charge per particle of species or population
$s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ is its
phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

The quantity is local in space and aggregated over all represented particle
species and kinetic populations. It is not restricted to fast particles and
is not restricted to any single coordinate projection; the electron and
thermal-ion back-current contributions remain part of the total.

The toroidal component is the more specific [toroidal current density due to
distribution-function-driven
processes](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_distribution_function_driven).
In contrast, [fast current density](name:fast_current_density) contains only
the selected fast-particle contribution and therefore does not represent
this full-distribution total.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the relevant component of $\mathbf{J}$ points
along the corresponding positive basis direction $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or
$\hat{Z}$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short:
Vector conventional electric current density attributable to non-inductive
wave–particle interactions, represented locally or after averaging over
magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
Wave-driven current density is the conventional electric-current-density
vector attributable to electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions that drive
plasma current non-inductively. It represents charge transport in the plasma
rather than the total current carried by an external circuit.

Its population-resolved definition is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{w}} = \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{w}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the wave-driven electric current-density
vector, $s$ indexes the contributing charged plasma populations, $q_s$ is
the signed charge of population $s$, and
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{w}}$ is that population's particle-flux
vector attributable to wave-driven current drive.

The species sum aggregates the charged plasma populations contributing to
the wave-driven current, while spatial, flux-surface, or mode aggregation
depends on the representation. The quantity excludes inductive current and
current driven by non-wave mechanisms; it is a current density, not a
volume-integrated net plasma current.

The [current density per toroidal mode due to wave-driven current
drive](name:current_density_per_toroidal_mode_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
is a representation that retains toroidal-mode resolution, whereas the
[flux-surface-averaged current density due to wave-driven current
drive](name:flux_surface_averaged_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
applies a magnetic flux-surface average. The related [current due to
wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
represents the corresponding net plasma-current quantity obtained from the
appropriate integration or projection of this density.

NAMES.name: current_density_per_toroidal_mode_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short:
Current density per toroidal mode due to wave-driven current drive is the
vector non-inductive current-density contribution from one toroidal Fourier
harmonic. It represents local charge transport produced by wave-particle
interactions before summing over toroidal modes or projecting onto
directions such as the magnetic-field-parallel direction.
NAMES.long:
Current density per toroidal mode due to wave-driven current drive is the
vector non-inductive current-density contribution associated with one
toroidal Fourier harmonic of the wave-driven current-drive source. It
represents the local conventional-current response produced by wave-particle
interactions for that harmonic, retaining the vector direction rather than
only a scalar projection.

The toroidal mode number labels Fourier harmonics in toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. The mode-summed wave-driven current
density is related to the per-mode contributions by

$$
\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_n \mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}$ is the [mode-summed wave-driven current
density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive),
$\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n$ is this per-toroidal-mode vector current
density for toroidal mode number $n$, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and
$t$ is time.

This quantity applies to the wave-driven non-inductive current-density
contribution at a local plasma position and is resolved for a single
toroidal mode. Its aggregation convention is mode-resolved:
per-toroidal-mode means attributed to one harmonic index, not divided by the
number of harmonics, and no sum over $n$ is included. It excludes inductive
or ohmic current density, total plasma current, particle flux, and wave
power.

The [parallel per-toroidal-mode wave-driven current
density](name:parallel_current_density_per_toroidal_mode_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
is the magnetic-field-aligned projection of $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n$
for the same toroidal mode. Summing $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n$ over mode
numbers gives the [mode-summed wave-driven current
density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive); it does not
give another per-toroidal-mode quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component represents conventional
current flowing in the positive direction of the component's explicitly
named basis vector or projection direction.

NAMES.name: current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive
NAMES.short:
Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by electron-cyclotron
wave absorption and resonant wave–particle interactions, summed over all
wave sources.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net toroidal plasma current attributable to
electron-cyclotron wave-driven current generation. It excludes inductive
current and current produced by other non-inductive mechanisms.

The total driven current is the toroidal projection of the driven current
density integrated over a poloidal cross-section:

$$
I_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_A j_{\phi,\mathrm{EC}}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{EC}}$ is the electron-cyclotron-driven
current-density component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$, $A$ is the plasma cross-sectional area in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $dA$ is its differential area. The
quantity is a current contribution, not the absorbed electron-cyclotron wave
power; its broader wave-driven-current counterpart is [current due to
wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the driven current flows in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by EC waves

NAMES.name: current_due_to_ion_cyclotron_current_drive
NAMES.short:
Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by ion-cyclotron wave
absorption and integrated over the plasma cross-section.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net plasma current driven by ion-cyclotron
wave–particle interactions, excluding inductive and non-wave current
contributions. It represents the toroidal component of the current generated
by the absorbed ion-cyclotron power.

The current is obtained by integrating the driven toroidal current density
over the plasma cross-section:

$$
I_{\mathrm{ICCD}} = \int_A j_{\phi,\mathrm{ICCD}}\,dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{ICCD}}$ is the driven current, $j_{\phi,\mathrm{ICCD}}$ is
the ion-cyclotron-driven toroidal current density in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $A$ is the plasma cross-sectional
area. The quantity is a net current, so oppositely directed local
contributions are algebraically summed. It is a source-specific component of
[current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
and is distinct from
[current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the driven current flows in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by IC waves

NAMES.name: current_due_to_lower_hybrid_current_drive
NAMES.short:
Net toroidal plasma current driven non-inductively by lower-hybrid slow
waves through wave–particle interactions, contributing to the total
non-inductive current.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net toroidal plasma current attributable to
lower-hybrid current drive. It represents the lower-hybrid contribution to
the plasma current and excludes inductive current and non-wave-driven
non-inductive contributions.

$$
I_{\mathrm{LH}} = \int_{A_p} j_{\phi,\mathrm{LH}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{LH}}$ is the lower-hybrid-driven current,
$j_{\phi,\mathrm{LH}}$ is the toroidal component of the lower-hybrid-driven
current density, and $A_p$ is a poloidal cross-sectional area of the plasma.
The quantity is a whole-plasma net current, so oppositely directed local
contributions may partially cancel. It is a wave-driven contribution within
[current due to wave-driven current
drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) and is distinct from
[current due to electron cyclotron current
drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the lower-hybrid-driven current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by LH waves

NAMES.name: current_due_to_neutral_beam_injection
NAMES.short:
Net toroidal plasma current driven by neutral-beam injection, combining the
fast-ion current and collisional electron return current after beam
ionization.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-beam-driven plasma current is the net toroidal current produced when
injected neutrals ionize and their fast ions transfer momentum to the
plasma. It includes both the directed fast-ion contribution and the
associated collisional electron return-current contribution.

The current is defined by integrating the net neutral-beam-driven toroidal
current density over the plasma cross-sectional area:

$$
I_{\mathrm{NBI}} = \int_{\mathcal{A}_{p}} j_{\phi,\mathrm{NBI}}(R,Z)\,d\mathcal{A}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{NBI}}$ is the neutral-beam-driven plasma current,
$j_{\phi,\mathrm{NBI}}$ is its toroidal current-density contribution, and
$\mathcal{A}_{p}$ is the plasma cross-sectional area in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This source contribution is distinct from absorbed power of a neutral beam
injector and is combined with other current sources, including plasma
current due to ohmic induction and [current due to electron-cyclotron
current drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net toroidal current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by this NBI unit

NAMES.name: current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short:
Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by wave–particle
interactions, including cumulative and toroidal-mode-resolved
representations.
NAMES.long:
Wave-driven current is the toroidal plasma current attributable to momentum
transfer from externally applied electromagnetic waves through wave–particle
interactions. It excludes inductive current and non-wave non-inductive
current sources.

For a selected poloidal cross-sectional area, the current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{wd}} = \int_A j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{wd}}$ is the wave-driven current, $A$ is the selected
poloidal area, $j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}$ is the toroidal component of the
wave-driven current density, and $(R,\phi,Z)$ is the right-handed
cylindrical frame. For a flux-surface-enclosed area, this gives the
cumulative quantity represented by [toroidal current due to wave-driven
current drive](name:toroidal_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive); the
same current may be decomposed into per-toroidal-mode current.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the wave-driven plasma current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: current_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Current of antenna strap is the oscillatory electric current carried along
an auxiliary-heating antenna strap during electromagnetic-wave coupling to a
plasma.
NAMES.long:
Current of antenna strap is the oscillatory electric current carried along
an auxiliary-heating antenna strap during electromagnetic-wave coupling to a
plasma. It is a scalar line-current quantity associated with the strap
itself.

The strap current is the current-density flux through an oriented
cross-section of the same strap:

$$
I_s(t) = \int_{S_s} \mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot d\mathbf{S}
$$

where $I_s(t)$ is the current of antenna strap at time $t$, $S_s$ is an
oriented cross-section of that strap, $\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t)$ is the
electric current density in the strap at position $\mathbf{x}$ and time $t$,
and $d\mathbf{S}$ is the vector area element whose orientation sets the
positive strap direction.

This quantity is scoped to an antenna strap, not to an arbitrary antenna
conductor, feed line, matching network, or complete antenna system. It
denotes current carried by the strap material and is not a voltage,
impedance, launched power, absorbed power, or a sum over multiple distinct
straps.

[Wave current of antenna strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap) is the
radio-frequency-wave specialization of this strap current and characterizes
the same strap-carried current with a specified wave-current representation,
such as peak amplitude or root mean square. The parent quantity identifies
the common antenna-strap current shared by such specialized names without
replacing their representation qualifiers.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional current has a net projection
along the assigned positive direction of the antenna strap.

NAMES.name: curvature_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Radius of curvature of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along a
selected first or second local tangential direction, characterizing
directional surface bending relevant to reflected-beam focusing or
defocusing.
NAMES.long:
Directional radius of curvature is the length scale of bending of the
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror surface in a selected mirror-local
tangential direction. It characterizes the direction-dependent geometric
contribution of the mirror surface to reflected-beam focusing or defocusing.

For direction $i$, the radius is the reciprocal of the magnitude of the
surface's normal curvature in that direction:

$$
R_i = \frac{1}{|\kappa_i|}
$$

where $R_i$ is the radius of curvature, $\kappa_i$ is the normal curvature
of the mirror surface in the normal section tangent to direction $i$, and
$i$ identifies the selected first or second local tangential direction. A
planar direction has zero normal curvature and an unbounded radius.

The selected direction is the [first local tangential
direction](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
or the [second local tangential
direction](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
The radius applies only when curvature is specified in that direction:
curvature types 2, 4, or 5 for the first direction, and types 3 or 5 for the
second. It is directional, not an average over the two directions.

The corresponding [first local tangential
width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [second local tangential
width](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
describe surface extent rather than bending. This mirror-surface radius is
distinct from the [wave curvature of an electron-cyclotron
beam](name:wave_curvature_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), which describes the
beam's phase-front curvature.

sources.leaf_definition: Radius of curvature in the X1 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 2, 4 or 5
sources.parent_definition: Description of the geometry of the mirror, in its reference position

sources.leaf_definition: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5
sources.parent_definition: Description of the geometry of the mirror, in its reference position

NAMES.name: fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Fast electron power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the fast
(non-thermal) electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Fast electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power
transferred to the fast, non-thermal electron population throughout the
plasma volume. It is the fast-electron component of [electron absorbed wave
power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power).

The volume-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-electron absorbed wave power,
$p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local coherent-wave power density
absorbed by fast electrons at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $V$ is the plasma
volume.

This quantity excludes wave power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons, ions,
and other populations, as well as wave power that is launched but not
absorbed. Unlike [fast electron power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it represents the
total plasma-volume integral rather than a cumulative value inside a
specified flux surface. The population scope is complementary to [thermal
electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave energy absorption by fast,
nonthermal electrons, including its flux-surface-averaged form.
NAMES.long:
Fast-electron absorbed wave power density is the rate at which coherent
radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to fast, nonthermal electrons
per unit physical volume. It describes local deposition and its average over
a magnetic flux surface.

The flux-surface-averaged form is defined by

$$
\overline{p}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{abs}} = \left\langle p_{e,f}^{\mathrm{abs}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle \frac{dP_{e,f}^{\mathrm{abs}}}{dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\overline{p}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged
absorbed wave power density, $p_{e,f}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is its local
counterpart, $P_{e,f}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the wave power absorbed by fast
electrons, $V$ is physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$
denotes a flux-surface average. The subscripts $e$ and $f$ identify
electrons and the fast population, respectively.

The recipient population is restricted to fast electrons; thermal-electron
and ion absorption are excluded. The averaging aggregates spatial deposition
on the flux surface, not different recipient populations. The corresponding
ion-recipient quantity is [fast-ion power
density](name:fast_ion_power_density).

This quantity excludes launched wave power and subsequent [collisional
electron energy transfer](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions).
Its volume integral gives the fast-electron contribution to [absorbed wave
power](name:absorbed_wave_power); integrating the flux-surface-averaged form
over the corresponding enclosed-volume intervals gives the same
contribution.

sources.leaf_definition: Flux surface averaged absorbed wave power density on the fast species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power density on the fast species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to fast
ions in one specified ion charge state, excluding collisional energy
exchange.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the direct electromagnetic-wave energy transfer rate to the
fast, non-thermal ions belonging to one specified charge state, integrated
over the full plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
P_{q,\mathrm{wave}} = \int_V p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{q,\mathrm{wave}}$ is the absorbed wave power for charge state $q$,
$p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})$ is its local wave-power deposition
density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $V$ is the full plasma volume.

This is a charge-state-resolved component of ion charge-state absorbed wave
power: it excludes power transferred subsequently through Coulomb collisions
and is not the cumulative value inside a selected flux surface, which is
represented by [fast ion charge-state power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
First local tangential coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror is its signed displacement from the
mirror-local origin along the first local tangential direction. That
direction is the more horizontally directed in-plane mirror tangent oriented
toward increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical
height.
NAMES.long:
First local tangential coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror is the signed scalar projection of the
point displacement from the mirror-local origin onto the mirror's first
local tangential axis. The mirror-local orthonormal triad $(\hat{\mathbf
t}_1, \hat{\mathbf t}_2, \hat{\mathbf n})$ has $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ and
$\hat{\mathbf t}_2$ tangent to the mirror outline plane and $\hat{\mathbf
n}$ as the plasma-facing normal. The first local tangential axis
$\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ is the more horizontally directed in-plane tangent,
oriented toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is defined by the Euclidean projection of the outline-point
position relative to the mirror-local origin onto the first local tangential
unit vector:

$$
\xi_1 = (\mathbf r - \mathbf r_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf t}_1
$$

where $\xi_1$ is the first local tangential coordinate of the mirror outline
point, $\mathbf r$ is the position vector of the outline point, $\mathbf
r_0$ is the mirror-local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ is the first local
tangential unit vector.

This coordinate is paired with the [second local tangential coordinate of
the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror),
which uses $\hat{\mathbf t}_2$ in the same mirror-local tangential plane.
The second local tangential direction is fixed by $\hat{\mathbf t}_2 =
\hat{\mathbf n} \times \hat{\mathbf t}_1$, so $\hat{\mathbf t}_1 \times
\hat{\mathbf t}_2 = \hat{\mathbf n}$. This local coordinate is distinct from
locating the mirror in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame
through quantities such as the radial centroid of the electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror and the [vertical coordinate of the electron-cyclotron
launcher
mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the displacement from the mirror-local origin
to the outline point has a component in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf
t}_1$.

sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x1 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the object in the (X1, X2) coordinate system, used only if geometry_type/index=1. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

NAMES.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Signed coordinate of a neutral beam injector source-outline vertex along the
injector’s first local tangential direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed first local tangential coordinate of a point on
a neutral beam injector source outline. It belongs to the injector’s
object-local frame and is paired with the [second local tangential
coordinate](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector)
to describe the outline in its tangent plane.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
x_1 = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_1
$$

where $x_1$ is the first local tangential coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the
position of the source-outline vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the origin of the
injector-local frame, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ is its positive first local
tangential unit vector.

The origin and orientation are determined by the neutral beam injector’s
local geometric convention; this quantity is not a coordinate in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and does not specify that
convention by itself.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the outline vertex lies in the direction of
the positive first local tangential basis vector from the local-frame
origin.

sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x1 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

NAMES.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Full physical extent of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its
first local tangential axis. This object-local axis is tangent to the mirror
surface and is the axis parameterized by the first local tangential
coordinate; the width applies to rectangular mirror geometry.
NAMES.long:
Full physical extent of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its
first local tangential axis is the edge-to-edge span of the mirror surface
in that object-local tangential direction. The first local tangential axis
is the axis parameterized by the [first local tangential
coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).

For a rectangular mirror surface, let $u_1$ denote the first local
tangential coordinate on the mirror surface $\mathcal{M}$. The width is the
range of that coordinate over the mirror surface:

$$
w_1 = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{M}} u_1(\mathbf{x}) - \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{M}} u_1(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $w_1$ is the first local tangential width and $\mathbf{x}$ is a point
on the mirror surface.

This quantity applies to rectangular mirror geometry and is distinct from
both a coordinate value at a point and the [second local tangential
width](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
As a full extent rather than a signed displacement, it is unchanged by
reversing the positive sense of the first local tangential coordinate.

sources.leaf_definition: Full width of the object in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type/index = 3
sources.parent_definition: Description of the geometry of the mirror, in its reference position

NAMES.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Full transverse extent of the rectangular neutral-beam injector ion-source
aperture along the first local tangential axis, defining one aperture
dimension for beam extraction.
NAMES.long:
Full transverse extent of the rectangular neutral-beam injector ion-source
aperture along the first local tangential axis is the distance between the
two opposite aperture edges in that object-local tangential direction. It
defines one aperture dimension for beam extraction.

The width is defined by the range of the first local tangential coordinate
over the aperture surface:

$$
w_1 = \max_{\mathbf{r}\in A} \xi_1(\mathbf{r}) - \min_{\mathbf{r}\in A} \xi_1(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $w_1$ is the first local tangential width, $A$ is the rectangular
ion-source aperture surface, $\mathbf{r}$ is a point on that aperture
surface, and $\xi_1$ is the object-local coordinate along the first local
tangential axis.

This quantity applies to rectangular ion-source aperture geometry. It is
distinct from the width along the second local tangential axis and from any
beam envelope, divergence, or focal width away from the ion-source aperture.
As a full width defined by a maximum minus a minimum, it is non-negative:
$w_1 \ge 0$.

sources.leaf_definition: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3
sources.parent_definition: Description of the surface of the ion source from which the beam is extracted

NAMES.name: forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the incident
radio-frequency power arriving at its back from the source through the feed
line.
NAMES.long:
Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna denotes the incident
radio-frequency traveling-wave power arriving at the back of the antenna
through its feed line. It is the source-to-antenna component at the antenna
reference plane, before reflected power is subtracted.

For a single antenna, the power components referred to the same reference
plane satisfy

$$
P_{\mathrm{fwd}} = P_{\mathrm{launched}} + P_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the forward incident power,
$P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the net [launched
power](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and
$P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the [reflected
power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) returning
toward the source.

This quantity applies to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna, not a sum over
an antenna set. It includes only the forward-traveling component, excluding
the backward-traveling reflected component. Subtracting reflected power
gives net launched power; forward power is neither this net quantity nor the
power subsequently absorbed by the plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: Forward power arriving to the back of the module
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

sources.leaf_definition: Forward power arriving to the back of the antenna
sources.parent_definition: Set of Ion Cyclotron antennas

NAMES.name: forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Forward power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the incident RF power traveling
from the transmission line toward the antenna input reference plane.
NAMES.long:
Forward power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative RF power
propagating toward the antenna input reference plane from the transmission
line. It is one per-antenna component of the wave-power budget represented
by power of a lower-hybrid antenna.

The per-antenna power components satisfy:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident power arriving at the reference
plane, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the power returning toward the transmission
line, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net power entering the vacuum vessel.
Thus, forward power includes the portion subsequently reflected and is
distinct from [reflected power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and [launched power
of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). The
quantity applies to one antenna and is not an aggregate over multiple
antennas.

sources.leaf_definition: Forward power arriving at the back of the antenna
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

NAMES.name: height_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Full vertical extent of an ICRH antenna strap conductor cross-section,
measured parallel to the Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The antenna-strap height is the full vertical extent of the rectangular
conductor cross-section, measured parallel to the $Z$ direction in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a geometric
cross-section dimension, not the antenna elevation or its distance from the
plasma.

$$
H = Z_{\max} - Z_{\min}
$$

where $H$ is the strap height and $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the vertical
coordinates of the upper and lower cross-section boundaries. The dimension
is non-negative and complements the toroidal width of the antenna strap and
[thickness of the antenna strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap), which
describe the other conductor extents. For an annular cross-section, the
radial boundaries are specified by the [inner radius of the antenna
strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) and [outer radius of the antenna
strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap).

sources.leaf_definition: Vertical full height
sources.parent_definition: Rectangular description of the element

NAMES.name: inner_radius_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Inner radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the inner cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Inner radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the inner cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section. It identifies the inner boundary of the conductor material
and is the smaller of the two annular boundary radii.

Use [radius of antenna strap](name:radius_of_antenna_strap) for the
boundary-radius concept without selecting a surface, and [outer radius of
antenna strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap) for the larger boundary
radius. If $r_\mathrm{in}$ and $r_\mathrm{out}$ denote the inner and outer
radii, respectively, then $0 \le r_\mathrm{in} \le r_\mathrm{out}$. This
quantity is distinct from the [height of antenna
strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), [toroidal width of antenna
strap](name:toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap), and [thickness of antenna
strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap).

sources.leaf_definition: Inner radius
sources.parent_definition: The element is an annulus of centre R, Z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

NAMES.name: ion_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the electromagnetic wave power
transferred from a single coherent beam to a selected ion species along its
trajectory.
NAMES.long:
The ion absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic
wave power transferred from a single coherent beam to one selected ion
species along the beam trajectory. It is a species-resolved contribution to
the [absorbed power of a beam-tracing
beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam), distinct from the electron
contribution represented by [electron absorbed power of a beam-tracing
beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam).

The species partition of the beam power balance is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs}} = P_e + \sum_s P_{\mathrm{ion},s}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total absorbed beam power, $P_e$ is the
electron contribution, $P_{\mathrm{ion},s}$ is the power absorbed by ion
species $s$, and the sum is over the contributing ion species. This quantity
denotes one term $P_{\mathrm{ion},s}$; its charge-state-resolved counterpart
is [ion charge-state absorbed power of a beam-tracing
beam](name:ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam). It
excludes residual wave power represented by power of a beam-tracing beam and
differs from volume-integrated [ion absorbed wave
power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.leaf_definition: Power absorbed along the beam by the species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Wave power absorbed by ions of a specified charge state from a single
coherent beam-tracing beam, giving the charge-state-resolved ion
contribution to total path-integrated wave energy deposition for that beam.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total wave
power transferred from a single traced coherent electromagnetic beam to the
ionic population in a specified charge state over its computed propagation
path. It is the charge-state-resolved ion contribution to the species-summed
[absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam),
complementing the electron channel provided by
[electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam).

For a ray arc length $s$ increasing along the direction of wave propagation,
the absorbed power for ion charge state $z$ is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},z} = \int_{s_0}^{s_{\mathrm{end}}} 2\kappa_{i,z}(s)\,P(s)\,ds
$$

where $\kappa_{i,z}(s)$ is the spatial amplitude-damping coefficient for the
specified ion charge state in m$^{-1}$, $P(s)$ is the remaining beam power
in W at arc-length position $s$ in m, and $s_0$ and $s_{\mathrm{end}}$ are
the start and end arc-length positions. The factor of 2 converts
amplitude-damping to power-damping because wave power is proportional to
squared wave-field amplitude, consistent with the parent formulation.

Summing over all charge states of all ion species and adding the electron
contribution recovers
[absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam)
for that beam. The residual power_of_beam_tracing_beam at the beam end
equals the entering power minus the sum of all species- and
charge-state-resolved absorbed powers.

sources.leaf_definition: Power absorbed along the beam by the species
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated power transferred from coherent electromagnetic waves to a
selected ion population, with specializations resolving thermal populations
and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated ion power is the electromagnetic-wave power transferred to
a selected ion population throughout the plasma. It denotes absorbed
transfer to the ions rather than the power incident on, launched by, or
remaining in the wave.

The volume-integrated quantity is defined from the corresponding local
transfer-power density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{ion}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the total power transferred to the selected ion
population, $p_{\mathrm{ion}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local power density
transferred to that population at position $\mathbf{r}$,
$V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential
volume element.

The recipient population is selected by the specialization and may be
resolved by thermal population and charge state; [thermal ion charge-state
power](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power) is the instance for bulk thermal
ions in one specified charge state. The defining aggregation is over plasma
volume, and a charge-state-resolved instance does not implicitly sum over
other charge states.

Power transferred to electrons, power not transferred from the wave, and
wave-system generator or launched power are outside this quantity. It is
distinct from the local power-density quantity, which describes the spatial
distribution before volume integration.

For a matching specialization, integrating [thermal ion charge-state power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density) over the plasma volume
gives the corresponding volume-integrated power. The broader [ion absorbed
wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) describes coherent-wave power
transferred directly to ion populations, while [total ion
power](name:total_ion_power) is a broader ion-power aggregation that can
include sources or sinks other than coherent electromagnetic-wave
absorption.

NAMES.name: launched_power_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
NAMES.short:
Power injected into the vacuum vessel by one electron-cyclotron beam after
transmission losses and before plasma absorption or reflection.
NAMES.long:
Launched power is the electromagnetic power carried by one specified
electron-cyclotron beam into the vacuum vessel toward the plasma. It
represents injected beam power rather than energy deposited in the plasma.

The power is defined as the rate of electromagnetic energy transport:

$$
P_{\mathrm{launched}} = \frac{dE}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the launched beam power, $E$ is the
electromagnetic energy transported by the beam, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to an individual electron-cyclotron beam and is not an
aggregate over multiple beams or a complete launcher system. Transmission
losses before launch are excluded from the launched value; plasma absorption
and power reflected after launch are also excluded.

The beam's carrier frequency, represented by the [electron-cyclotron beam
frequency](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), determines its
cyclotron-resonance condition, while launched power specifies the strength
of the injected electromagnetic beam.

sources.leaf_definition: Beam power launched into the vacuum vessel
sources.parent_definition: Set of Electron Cyclotron beam segments, including between mirrors

NAMES.name: launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Radio-frequency power launched toward the plasma by an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna, equal to forward incident power minus reflected return power.
NAMES.long:
The quantity denotes radio-frequency wave power launched toward the plasma
by an ion-cyclotron resonance heating antenna at the antenna reference
plane. It is the net launched component after accounting for the forward and
reflected traveling-wave components.

For a single antenna, the launched power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{launched}} = P_{\mathrm{fwd}} - P_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the launched radio-frequency power,
$P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the forward incident power traveling from the
generator toward the antenna, and $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reflected power
traveling from the antenna toward the generator.

This quantity applies to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna at its reference
plane and represents a net directional power, not a sum over an antenna set.
It excludes the reflected component and the power subsequently absorbed by
the plasma.

Within the broader power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna quantity, this
is the launched-power specialization. The [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and [reflected
power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) are the
components combined by the defining relation, whereas power due to
ion-cyclotron heating denotes power coupled from the waves into the plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: Power launched from this module into the vacuum vessel
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the net RF power coupled into
the vacuum vessel toward the plasma, equal to the forward power minus the
reflected power at the launching unit. The launching unit may be an antenna
module, a single antenna, or the complete antenna set, for which the value
is the sum over the constituent units.
NAMES.long:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative net RF power
coupled from the launching structure into the vacuum vessel toward the
plasma. It is the net-transfer component of the wave-power budget
represented by [power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The launched power is defined by the balance:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the [forward power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) arriving at the antenna
input reference plane from the transmission line, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is
the [reflected power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) returning toward the
transmission line, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net power entering the
vacuum vessel.

The launching unit may be an antenna module, a single antenna, or the
complete lower-hybrid antenna set. The quantity is extensive, so the
launched power of a composite unit is the sum of the launched powers of its
constituent units.

Launched power excludes the reflected contribution and is distinct from
forward power, which includes the portion subsequently reflected. It denotes
the net power delivered across the launching aperture into the vessel, not
the generator output on the transmission-line side of the reference plane,
and it does not by itself resolve where the power is subsequently deposited
within the plasma.

The [toroidal-mode-resolved launched
power](name:launched_power_per_toroidal_mode_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and
the [jointly toroidal- and poloidal-mode-resolved launched
power](name:launched_power_per_toroidal_and_poloidal_mode_number_of_lower_hybrid_antenna)
are distributions of this same quantity over refractive-index intervals;
integrating them over those intervals recovers the launched power of the
corresponding antenna row.

NAMES.name: maximum_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Maximum allowed value of the signed rotation angle of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror within its mechanical travel range.
NAMES.long:
The upper mechanical travel limit is the greatest permitted value of the
mirror’s signed rotation angle, bounding the accessible steering range of
the launcher. It is a limit of the mechanical actuator, not the mirror angle
during a particular operating condition.

Let $\theta$ denote the signed mirror angle defined by angle of
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. The upper limit $\theta_{\max}$ is
defined by

$$
\theta_{\max} = \sup\{\theta \mid \theta\text{ is mechanically accessible}\}
$$

The quantity excludes the lower travel limit and does not describe the
mirror’s position unless that position equals the upper boundary of the
allowed range.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the mirror rotates in the positive sense
defined for angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror.

sources.leaf_definition: Maximum angular displacement with respect to the reference position, counter-clockwise around the direction vector
sources.parent_definition: Set of degrees of freedom for this mirror, allowing the mirror to move around its reference position indicated in ../geometry. Can be cascaded for composite movements.

NAMES.name: net_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short:
Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the radio-frequency energy absorbed per
unit time by the plasma from a specific launcher, excluding losses outside
the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which radio-frequency waves
from a specific launcher transfer energy to the plasma. It includes
absorption by all plasma particle populations, not only ions.

The absorbed power is defined by

$$
P = \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} p_{\mathrm{abs}}\,dV
$$

where $P$ is the net absorbed power attributable to the launcher,
$V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the entire plasma volume, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the
local radio-frequency energy-transfer rate per volume summed over all
absorbing plasma populations and averaged over a radio-frequency cycle, and
$dV$ is a volume element.

This quantity applies to one launcher, not a sum over launchers. Unabsorbed
wave power and dissipation outside the plasma are excluded.

The [launched power of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is the
forward-minus-reflected power directed into the vessel before plasma
absorption; it need not equal the absorbed power defined here. The [total
power due to ion-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating) sums launched power
over all heating antennas and therefore differs in both absorption scope and
launcher aggregation.

NAMES.name: ordinary_mode_fraction_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
NAMES.short:
Fraction of the launched power of an electron-cyclotron beam carried by the
ordinary polarization mode, ranging from pure X-mode to pure O-mode.
NAMES.long:
The ordinary-mode power fraction quantifies the share of one launched
electron-cyclotron beam carried by the ordinary (O) polarization mode rather
than the extraordinary (X) mode.

It is defined by the ratio

$$
f_O = \frac{P_O}{P_{\mathrm{EC}}}
$$

where $f_O$ is the ordinary-mode power fraction, $P_O$ is the launched power
in the ordinary mode, and $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the total launched power of
the electron-cyclotron beam.

The quantity applies to a single electron-cyclotron beam and uses launched
beam power aggregated over the beam's ordinary-mode content. It excludes
power from other beams and does not represent the total launched power
itself. Values of $f_O=1$ and $f_O=0$ denote pure ordinary-mode and pure
extraordinary-mode launch, respectively.

This power partition is distinct from [polarization ellipticity of a
polarimeter beam](name:polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam), which
describes the shape and handedness of a polarization ellipse rather than the
O-mode fraction of an electron-cyclotron beam.

sources.leaf_definition: Fraction of EC beam power launched in ordinary (O) mode. If all power is launched in ordinary mode (O-mode), o_mode_fraction = 1.0. If all  power is launched in extraordinary mode (X-mode), o_mode_fraction = 0.0
sources.parent_definition: Wave polarization

NAMES.name: outer_radius_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Outer radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the outer cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Outer radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the outer cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section. It identifies the outer boundary of the conductor material
and is the larger of the two annular boundary radii.

Use [radius of antenna strap](name:radius_of_antenna_strap) for the
boundary-radius concept without selecting a surface, and [inner radius of
antenna strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) for the smaller boundary
radius. If $r_\mathrm{in}$ and $r_\mathrm{out}$ denote the [inner radius of
antenna strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) and the outer radius of
antenna strap, respectively, then $0 \le r_\mathrm{in} \le r_\mathrm{out}$.
This quantity is distinct from the [height of antenna
strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), [toroidal width of antenna
strap](name:toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap), and [thickness of antenna
strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap).

sources.leaf_definition: Outer radius
sources.parent_definition: The element is an annulus of centre R, Z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

NAMES.name: parallel_peak_launched_refractive_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave
spectrum launched by an antenna. It is the signed value at the dominant
spectral peak set by the measured phase difference between neighboring
waveguide rows, not an algebraic maximum over all launched components.
NAMES.long:
Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave
spectrum launched by an antenna is the signed parallel refractive-index
coordinate of the dominant launched spectral peak. The parallel direction is
taken along the local magnetic-field direction at the launcher aperture.

The defining value is the refractive index associated with the peak parallel
wave number of the launched spectrum:

$$
N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}} = \frac{c\,k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}}{\omega}
$$

where $N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the peak launched parallel refractive
index, $c$ is the speed of light, $k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the
parallel wave number at the dominant peak of the launched lower-hybrid
spectrum, and $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency.

For this quantity, the dominant peak is the main spectral peak inferred from
the measured phase difference between neighboring waveguide rows, through
the row-to-row phase advance per projected row separation in the parallel
phasing direction. This quantity is not the algebraic maximum of
$N_\parallel$ over all launched components; if the main spectral peak lies
at negative $N_\parallel$, the peak value is negative.

sources.leaf_definition: Peak parallel refractive index of the launched wave spectrum (simple estimate based on the measured phase difference)
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

NAMES.name: parallel_wave_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Signed component of the oscillatory electromagnetic-wave magnetic
perturbation along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, distinct
from the total parallel magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the field-aligned component of the oscillatory magnetic
perturbation carried by a coherent electromagnetic wave. It excludes
equilibrium and other static magnetic-field contributions.

The component is defined by

$$
B_{\rm parallel}^{\rm wave} = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\rm wave} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_{\rm wave}$ is the wave magnetic-field perturbation
and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq} = \mathbf{B}_{\rm eq}/|\mathbf{B}_{\rm eq}|$
is the local unit vector along the equilibrium magnetic field. It is a
component of the parent wave magnetic field, not its magnitude or a
complex-quadrature part. Unlike [parallel magnetic
field](name:parallel_magnetic_field), it does not include the equilibrium
field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the wave magnetic-field perturbation points
in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic-field unit vector.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Parallel (to the static magnetic field) component of the wave magnetic field, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy absorption by fast, suprathermal
electrons for each toroidal mode number, resolved across a poloidal
cross-section or represented as a flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Mode-resolved fast-electron absorbed wave power density is the rate at which
coherent-wave energy is absorbed by fast, suprathermal electrons per unit
physical volume for each toroidal mode number.

For a toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, the local mode-resolved power density
is defined as

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)} = \frac{dP_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the mode-resolved fast-electron
power density, $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the corresponding
[mode-resolved fast-electron absorbed wave
power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power), $V$ is
physical volume, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal mode number, and the subscripts
$e$ and $\mathrm{fast}$ identify the fast-electron recipient population.

The recipient population is fast, suprathermal electrons; thermal-electron
and ion absorption are distinct contributions. The quantity is specified
separately for each toroidal mode number and may be given locally across a
poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average over a magnetic flux
surface.

This is a volumetric absorption rate, not volume-integrated power or
launched wave power. The toroidal mode number identifies the wave harmonic
contributing to absorption, not a Fourier coefficient of the deposited-power
field.

Summing the mode contributions for the same spatial evaluation gives the
[fast-electron absorbed wave power
density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density). Integrating a
mode-resolved density over physical volume gives its corresponding
mode-resolved absorbed wave power. Fast-electron absorption is one recipient
contribution to the [mode-resolved total absorbed wave power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power_density), which
includes other plasma populations.

sources.leaf_definition: Flux surface averaged absorbed wave power density on the fast species, per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power density on the fast species, per toroidal mode number

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Absorbed coherent-wave power density deposited in thermal ions of a selected
species, resolved by toroidal mode number and represented locally across a
poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Absorbed coherent-wave power density per toroidal mode is the rate at which
energy from one toroidal Fourier component of a coherent wave is transferred
directly to the thermal ions of a selected species per unit physical volume.
It describes either the local spatial distribution across a poloidal
cross-section or the flux-surface average of that density.

For the local quantity, the mode-resolved deposition density is

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}}{dV}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the absorbed power density,
$P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the power transferred to the selected
species' thermal ions by the coherent-wave harmonic with toroidal mode
number $n_\phi$, $V$ is physical volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial
position. The index $i$ identifies the selected ion species, and
$\mathrm{th}$ identifies its thermal population.

The quantity applies to the thermal-ion population of one selected species
and one toroidal mode, and is summed over all charge states of that species,
not over distinct ion species or modes. It may retain local variation across
a poloidal cross-section or be averaged over a magnetic flux surface; the
flux-surface average is not a pointwise value.

It excludes absorption by electrons and nonthermal ions, as well as energy
transfer through non-wave processes; it is not the net thermal-ion energy
source from all processes. The [charge-state-resolved
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density)
resolves contributions by ion charge state, while [fast-ion power density
per toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density) describes
deposition into nonthermal ions.

Summing the modal contributions gives the mode-summed [thermal-ion absorbed
wave power density](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power_density) for the
same species and spatial averaging convention. Integrating the local density
over the plasma volume gives the [thermal-ion absorbed wave power per
toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power),
which is a power rather than a power density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when coherent-wave energy is transferred to the
thermal ions of the selected species.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_wave_vector_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Non-negative magnitude of the RF wave-vector component perpendicular to the
local equilibrium magnetic field launched by an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna.
NAMES.long:
This quantity measures the transverse spatial variation of the
radio-frequency wave launched by an ion-cyclotron heating antenna, relative
to the local equilibrium magnetic field.

The perpendicular wave-vector magnitude is defined by

$$
k_\perp = \left|\mathbf{k} - (\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}})\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right|
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the local RF wave vector,
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and vertical bars denote
vector magnitude.

Only the component transverse to the magnetic field is included; the
parallel component is excluded. The result is non-negative and has no
propagation-direction sign. It is the antenna-specific counterpart of the
general perpendicular wave-vector magnitude.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Main perpendicular wave number of IC waves

NAMES.name: poloidal_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short:
Poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam point is its angular position about
the magnetic axis in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured clockwise from the outward +R
direction.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam point is the angular coordinate of
that point about the magnetic axis in a poloidal cross-section of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is measured from
the outward $+R$ direction and uses the clockwise poloidal-angle sense in
the $(R,Z)$ plane.

The clockwise branch of the angle is defined by the displacement of the beam
point relative to the magnetic axis:

$$
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left[-(Z - Z_\mathrm{axis}),\, R - R_\mathrm{axis}\right]
$$

where $\theta$ is the poloidal angle of the beam-tracing beam point, $R$ and
$Z$ are the beam point major radius and vertical height, and
$R_\mathrm{axis}$ and $Z_\mathrm{axis}$ are the major radius and vertical
height of the magnetic axis. The function $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ is the
quadrant-resolving arctangent; the negative first argument makes increasing
$\theta$ clockwise when the cross-section is viewed with $R$ increasing to
the right and $Z$ increasing upward.

The scope is the position of beam-tracing beam trajectory points in the
wave-propagation geometry. The value is pointwise for each trajectory point;
no averaging over beam cross-section, path segment, or multiple beams is
implied.

This quantity is not the beam launch angle, propagation-direction angle,
wave-vector pitch, toroidal angle $\phi$, or a flux-surface label. It is the
beam-point locus counterpart of the [poloidal angle of a measurement
position](name:poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position) and uses the same
angular sense as the [poloidal angle of a flux
surface](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface); the distinction is the locus,
not the angular convention.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the displacement from the magnetic axis to
the beam point is clockwise from the outward $+R$ direction in a poloidal
cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame viewed
with $R$ increasing to the right and $Z$ increasing upward.

sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal angle (oriented clockwise when viewing the poloidal cross section on the right hand side of the tokamak axis of symmetry, with the origin placed on the plasma magnetic axis)
sources.parent_definition: Position of the ray/beam along its path

NAMES.name: poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Signed dimensionless poloidal component of the launched lower-hybrid wave
refractive-index vector, measured along increasing geometric poloidal angle
about the antenna reference point.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal launched-wave index is the projection of the lower-hybrid
launched wave refractive-index vector onto the direction of increasing
geometric poloidal angle about the antenna reference point. It describes the
poloidal part of the launch spectrum and is distinct from the corresponding
[toroidal launched-wave
index](name:toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The index is defined by

$$
N_\theta = \frac{\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta}{k_0} = \frac{k_\theta}{k_0}
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the launched wave vector,
$\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of
increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$, $k_\theta$ is the
corresponding wave-vector projection, and $k_0 = \omega/c$ is the free-space
wavenumber for angular frequency $\omega$ and speed of light $c$. The
projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity describes the launch condition only; it is not the local
poloidal wave index after propagation or interaction with the plasma.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the launched wave-vector projection points in
the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$.

sources.leaf_definition: Refraction index in the poloidal direction. The poloidal angle is defined from the reference point; the angle at a point (R,Z) is given by atan((Z-Zref)/(R-Rref)), where Rref=reference_point/r and Zref=reference_point/z
sources.parent_definition: Set of horizontal rows of waveguides (corresponding to different poloidal positions). A power spectrum is provided for each row.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_beam_tracing_point
NAMES.short:
Signed poloidal magnetic flux function evaluated at a beam-tracing point,
serving as the magnetic-surface label at that location.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a beam-tracing point is the value of the
equilibrium flux function at the point where the ray or beam path intersects
the plasma. In an axisymmetric equilibrium, it labels the nested magnetic
surface passing through that point and is distinct from the normalized
coordinate derived from axis and boundary values.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the flux function is
defined by

$$
\psi(R,Z) = \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, $R'$ is the integration
radius, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component. The beam-tracing
point supplies the coordinates at which $\psi$ is evaluated. Its value is
related to [poloidal magnetic flux at a flux
surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface), while [normalized
poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) uses the
magnetic-axis and plasma-boundary flux values for normalization.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $B_Z$ on the integration disk points in the
$+Z$ direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal flux
sources.parent_definition: Position of the ray/beam along its path

NAMES.name: power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.short:
Cumulative power associated with a specified plasma heating or
energy-transfer channel, integrated over the volume enclosed by a magnetic
flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative power associated with one physically defined
plasma heating or energy-transfer channel inside a specified magnetic flux
surface. The parent does not by itself select a species, population, source,
absorption mechanism, or whether the channel is absorbed power or net
transferred power.
