For a volumetric channel power density, the cumulative power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative channel power, $\psi$ is the
magnetic-flux-surface label, $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by that
surface, $p_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the corresponding volumetric power density,
$\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

Species- and population-specific instances include [electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), [ion power
at an inside flux surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), and [ion
charge-state power at an inside flux
surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface). Absorbed-power
channels count energy deposited in the recipient population, whereas
net-transfer channels follow the specified transfer direction and may be
signed.

NAMES.name: electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by all electron populations, thermal and
fast, from a specified wave source or source set within the plasma volume
enclosed by a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The electron power at inside flux surface is the cumulative rate at which
wave energy from a specified source or source set is deposited into the
electron population, spanning both thermal bulk electrons and fast
suprathermal electrons, within the plasma volume bounded by a closed
magnetic flux surface. It is an enclosed-volume channel quantity: each
bounding surface includes all electron wave absorption inside that surface.

For a local volumetric electron wave-power deposition density, the
cumulative power is

$$
P_e(\psi_s) = \int_{V(\psi_s)} p_e^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_e(\psi_s)$ is this cumulative electron wave power, $\psi_s$ is the
magnetic-flux-surface label of the bounding surface, $V(\psi_s)$ is the
plasma volume enclosed by that surface, $p_e^{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the local
volumetric rate of wave energy deposition into the electron population,
$\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

For the same wave channel and enclosed volume, this quantity satisfies the
population decomposition $P_e = P_{e,\mathrm{thermal}} +
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$, with components [thermal electron power at inside flux
surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and [fast
electron power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It is the
electron counterpart of [ion power at inside flux
surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and a species-specific
instance of [power at inside flux
surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface); it excludes ion absorption and
non-wave loss or exchange channels.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when wave energy is deposited into the electron
population.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) electron
population within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux
surface.
NAMES.long:
Fast electron power at an inside flux surface quantifies the total rate at
which coherent wave energy is absorbed by the non-thermal fast electron
population within the plasma volume bounded by a given magnetic flux
surface. It is the fast-electron contribution to [electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), distinct
from the bulk thermal-electron contribution [thermal electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

The quantity is obtained by integrating the flux-surface-averaged [fast
electron power density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density)
$p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}$ over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho) = \int_0^\rho p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho') \frac{dV}{d\rho'} \, d\rho'
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho)$ is the cumulative absorbed power, $\rho$
labels the limiting flux surface, $\rho'$ is the integration variable,
$p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}$ is the local fast-electron absorbed power density, and
$dV/d\rho'$ is the differential enclosed volume per unit flux-surface label.
Only absorption by fast electrons is included; thermal-electron and ion
absorption, launched power, and power absorbed outside the enclosed volume
are excluded. At the outermost closed flux surface, the quantity gives the
total wave power absorbed by fast electrons.

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified ion charge state, integrated
over the plasma volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative power associated with one physically defined
plasma heating or energy-transfer channel inside a specified magnetic flux
surface. Here, the channel is absorption of wave energy by one specified ion
charge state, and the ion population may be thermal or fast.

The cumulative absorbed power is

$$
P_{q,a}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p^{\mathrm{abs}}_{q,a}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{q,a}(\psi)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power, $q$ identifies
the ion charge state, $a$ identifies the thermal or fast ion population,
$\psi$ is the magnetic-flux-surface label, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed plasma
volume, $p^{\mathrm{abs}}_{q,a}$ is the corresponding volumetric wave-power
absorption density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the
volume element.

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved specialization of [power at
inside flux surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface). It excludes power
absorbed by other charge states and power that is launched but not absorbed;
corresponding thermal and fast instances are [thermal ion charge-state power
at inside flux
surface](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and
[fast ion charge-state power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

NAMES.name: ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by all ion populations — thermal and fast —
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The ion power at inside flux surface is the cumulative rate at which wave
energy is deposited into the ion population — spanning both thermal bulk
ions and fast (non-thermal) ions — within the plasma volume bounded by a
closed magnetic flux surface. It is the ion-channel component of the more
general [power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface),
separating ion energy absorption from the corresponding electron heating
contribution.

The quantity is the volume integral of the total ion wave-power density
$p_i(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\psi)$ enclosed by the flux
surface labeled $\psi$:

$$
P_i(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_i(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_i$ is the ion volumetric heating power density in W m$^{-3}$ and
$\psi$ is the chosen flux-surface label, such as the normalized toroidal
flux radius $\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$.

The population-resolved breakdown is given by
[thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface)
for the bulk ion channel and
[fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface)
for non-thermal beam or fusion-born ions. This cumulative radial profile
enables power-balance analysis and is inferred from combining absorbed-power
density profiles computed via wave ray-tracing or Monte Carlo
beam-deposition codes with equilibrium flux-surface geometry.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) ion population
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The fast-ion power at inside flux surface is the running volume integral of
wave power deposited into the fast (non-thermal) ion population, giving the
radial distribution of enclosed fast-ion wave absorption. It is the fast-ion
component of the more general
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
separating non-thermal ion energy absorption from the corresponding bulk
thermal-ion contribution.

The quantity is the volume integral of the fast-ion wave-power density
$p_f(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\psi)$ enclosed by the magnetic
flux surface labeled $\psi$:

$$
P_f(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_f(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $P_f(\psi)$ is the fast-ion power at inside flux surface, $p_f$ is the
fast-ion volumetric wave-power density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position in physical
space, $dV$ is the differential volume element, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed
plasma volume, and $\psi$ is the chosen magnetic flux-surface label.

The scope is the plasma volume inside the selected closed magnetic flux
surface and the fast, non-thermal ion population in that volume. Because
this is an extensive population quantity, it is summed over the represented
fast-ion species and over all their charge states; the charge-state-resolved
counterpart is
[fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).
It excludes wave energy deposited into the bulk thermal-ion population,
represented by
[thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
and excludes electron heating and wave power not absorbed by fast ions. For
the same flux-surface label,
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) is
the sum of this fast-ion contribution and the thermal-ion contribution.

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short:
Net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma through electron cyclotron
heating, with source aggregation determined by scope and excluding launched
or reflected power.
NAMES.long:
Electron-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which
electron-cyclotron-range electromagnetic waves transfer energy to the
plasma, principally through resonant electron absorption. It denotes
deposited plasma heating power rather than generator, launched, transmitted,
or reflected power.

The absorbed power is defined by the volume integral of the local
electron-cyclotron heating density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} Q_{\mathrm{EC}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the absorbed power, $Q_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the
local power-transfer density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and
$V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. Source aggregation is
scope-dependent; the [total electron-cyclotron heating
power](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating) sums the
contributions from all electron-cyclotron wave sources. The quantity is
non-negative for net absorption and is distinct from [electron absorbed wave
power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) when that quantity includes wave
absorption without restricting the mechanism to electron cyclotron heating.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron cyclotron heating power coupled to the plasma from this launcher

NAMES.name: radial_offset_of_beamlet_group
NAMES.short:
Signed major-radius displacement of a beamlet-group center from its nominal
position, measured along the radial direction in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed radial displacement of a beamlet-group center
from its nominal static position during a position variation. It describes
only the major-radius component of the group's displacement, not the
complete position vector or the injector's own reference position.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, the
offset is defined by:

$$
\Delta R_{\mathrm{bg}} = R_{\mathrm{bg}} - R_{\mathrm{bg},0}
$$

Here $R_{\mathrm{bg}}$ is the beamlet-group center's major-radius coordinate
and $R_{\mathrm{bg},0}$ is its nominal static reference coordinate; $R$ is
measured from the machine symmetry axis and increases outward.

For dynamic beam tilting, the offset describes the group's positional
variation and is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the neutral beam
injector](name:radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector), which refers to
the injector reference position. Related angular variation is described by
the perturbed beam tilt angle of the neutral beam injector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the beamlet-group center lies at larger major
radius than its nominal reference position.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Variation of the position of the beamlet group centre

NAMES.name: radius_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Radius of the circular ion-source surface from which neutral beams are
extracted, defining the radial extent of its extraction aperture.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the radius of the circular ion-source surface from which a
neutral-beam injector extracts its beam. It defines the radial extent of the
extraction aperture.

For a circular boundary, the radius is the distance from the surface center
to any point on its circumference:

$$
r_s = \left\lVert \mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}_c \right\rVert
$$

where $r_s$ is the ion-source-surface radius, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position
of a point on the circular boundary, $\mathbf{x}_c$ is the position of the
circle center, and the norm denotes Euclidean distance.

The quantity applies to one neutral-beam injector unit and only to its
circular ion-source geometry. It is not an aggregate over injector units and
does not represent the radius of a beamlet-group tangency surface or another
injector-associated aperture. For a rectangular ion-source aperture, the
corresponding transverse dimensions are given by the [first local tangential
width of the neutral-beam
injector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector) and
[second local tangential width of the neutral-beam
injector](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector),
rather than by this radius.

sources.leaf_definition: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2
sources.parent_definition: Description of the surface of the ion source from which the beam is extracted

NAMES.name: reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase angle of a reflected radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an
antenna element in an ion-cyclotron heating launcher, measured relative to
the forward power-wave phasor of that same element.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the relative phase of a complex reflected radio-frequency
power-wave phasor at a selected antenna strap or module with respect to the
complex forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor of the same strap or
module. It specifies the element-local reflection phase of an ion-cyclotron
heating launcher rather than an absolute phase or an inter-element phase.

For element $i$, the reflected phase is defined by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \arg\!\left(b_i^{\mathrm{ref}} (a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i}$ is this reflected phase, $b_i^{\mathrm{ref}}$
is the complex reflected power-wave phasor at element $i$,
$a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the complex forward power-wave phasor at the same
element, $(a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*$ is its complex conjugate, and $\arg$
extracts the phase angle. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$.

The scope is a single selected launcher strap or module and the pair of
forward and reflected traveling power waves at the same element reference
plane. The forward wave propagates toward the antenna element, and the
reflected wave propagates away from the antenna element toward the feeding
network. The first launcher element is not the phase reference for this
quantity, and the quantity is not averaged or summed over launcher elements.

This quantity is a reflected-wave member of the broader phase of the
ion-cyclotron heating antenna family. It is distinct from the [wave phase of
the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which describes
inter-element phasing, and together with the [reflected power of the
ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) it specifies
the phase-and-magnitude state of the reflected power wave without including
the magnitude itself.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the reflected-wave phasor at the selected
element leads the forward-wave phasor at the same element in phase under the
adopted temporal phasor convention.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the reflected power with respect to the forward power of this module
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna module is the RF power returning
toward the source through the transmission line because of impedance
mismatch at the plasma–antenna interface.
NAMES.long:
Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna module is the nonnegative RF power
propagating back toward the source because of impedance mismatch at the
plasma–antenna interface. It is the returning-power component of the
wave-power budget represented by [power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna), evaluated at the module input
reference plane.

The module power components satisfy:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) arriving at the module
input reference plane, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the reflected power
returning toward the source, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net [launched
power](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) entering the vacuum
vessel from that module. All three components refer to the same module and
reference plane.

Reflected power is the portion of forward power returned toward the source,
distinct from net launched power and power absorbed by the plasma. The
quantity applies to one antenna module and is not a sum over modules or
antennas.

sources.leaf_definition: Reflected power
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules

sources.leaf_definition: Reflected power
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

NAMES.name: resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the
effective radio-frequency loading impedance at the antenna feed reference
plane. It represents the resistive component associated with power coupled
to the plasma and dissipative antenna losses.
NAMES.long:
Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the
effective radio-frequency loading impedance presented by the antenna at its
feed reference plane. It characterizes the component of the antenna load
that absorbs radio-frequency power, including plasma loading and intrinsic
dissipative losses, distinct from the reactive energy storage represented by
antenna capacitance or inductance.

The antenna loading impedance is decomposed into resistive and reactive
parts as:

$$
Z_\mathrm{ant} = R_\mathrm{ant} + i X_\mathrm{ant}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{ant}$ is the complex antenna loading impedance,
$R_\mathrm{ant}$ is the antenna resistance in ohms, $X_\mathrm{ant}$ is the
antenna reactance in ohms, and $i^2=-1$.

For a sinusoidal strap current, the resistive power associated with this
load is $P_\mathrm{res}=R_\mathrm{ant} I_\mathrm{rms}^2$, where
$P_\mathrm{res}$ is in watts and $I_\mathrm{rms}$ is the root-mean-square
wave current of the antenna strap in amperes. This quantity is a feed-plane
impedance component and is not itself a forward, reflected, or net power;
those powers describe traveling-wave energy flow in the connected
radio-frequency circuit.

sources.leaf_definition: Coupling resistance
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_aperture
NAMES.short:
Signed coordinate of each aperture-outline vertex along the aperture’s
second local tangential axis, defining its location in the object-local
cross-sectional geometry.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed position of an aperture-outline vertex projected
onto the second local tangential axis of the aperture’s object-local $(X_1,
X_2)$ frame. Together with the first local tangential coordinate, it defines
the boundary geometry of the aperture.

The coordinate of vertex $v$ is defined by

$$
x_{2,v} = (\mathbf{r}_v - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{X}}_2
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the position of the outline vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$
is the origin of the local frame, and $\hat{\mathbf{X}}_2$ is its second
local tangential unit vector. This object-local axis is distinct from
machine radial, toroidal, and vertical directions. The same ordinal-axis
convention applies to the [second local tangential coordinate of diagnostic
aperture](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture).

sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x2 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

NAMES.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Signed coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror along its second local tangential axis in its object-local
planar frame, measured from the mirror-local origin.
NAMES.long:
Signed coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror along its second local tangential axis in its object-local
planar frame, measured from the mirror-local origin, is the scalar
projection of that point's displacement onto the mirror's second local
tangential direction. The mirror-local triad is
$(\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{n}})$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$ is the more-horizontal tangential direction directed
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height;
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the plasma-facing unit normal; and
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\times\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$ completes the
right-handed triad.

For an outline point with position vector $\mathbf{r}$ and mirror-local
origin $\mathbf{r}_0$, the coordinate is defined by

$$
x_2 = \left(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_0\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2
$$

where $x_2$ is the second local tangential coordinate of the outline point.

This coordinate specifies the second in-plane component of the mirror
outline and complements the [first local tangential
coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
It is not the cylindrical radial coordinate $R$, toroidal angle $\phi$, or
vertical coordinate $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the displacement from the mirror-local origin
to the outline point has a component in the direction
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\times\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$.

sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x2 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the object in the (X1, X2) coordinate system, used only if geometry_type/index=1. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

NAMES.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Signed second local-tangential coordinate of a neutral beam injector outline
vertex, measured in the injector-local frame and paired with the first
coordinate to locate that vertex.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed position of an outline vertex along the neutral
beam injector's second local tangential axis. It is paired with the [first
local-tangential
coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector)
to locate the same vertex in the injector-local frame.

The coordinate is defined by:

$$
x_2 = (\mathbf{r}_v-\mathbf{r}_0)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2
$$

where $x_2$ is this coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the vertex position,
$\mathbf{r}_0$ is the local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ is the second
local tangential unit vector. The local orthonormal basis
$(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3)$ is
right-handed; $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3$ is the plasma-facing normal, and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The coordinate applies to outline vertices associated with the neutral beam
injector and is distinct from the first local-tangential coordinate and from
global cylindrical coordinates.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the vertex displacement has a positive
projection along
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ from the
local origin.

sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x2 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

NAMES.name: second_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Full transverse extent of the rectangular ion-source aperture along the
neutral beam injector’s second local tangential axis, defining one aperture
dimension for beam extraction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the full geometric width of the rectangular ion-source
aperture measured along the neutral beam injector’s second local tangential
axis. It is one of the two orthogonal aperture dimensions used to define the
extraction opening.

The width is defined by the extrema of the aperture boundary coordinate:

$$
w_2 = x_{2,\rm max} - x_{2,\rm min}
$$

where $x_2$ is the [second local-tangential coordinate of the neutral beam
injector](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector),
and $x_{2,\rm max}$ and $x_{2,\rm min}$ are its maximum and minimum values
on the aperture boundary. This quantity applies to rectangular geometry and
denotes the full width, not a half-width or the orthogonal first local
tangential dimension represented by [first local tangential width of the
neutral beam
injector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector).

sources.leaf_definition: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3
sources.parent_definition: Description of the surface of the ion source from which the beam is extracted

NAMES.name: straight_field_line_angle
NAMES.short:
An angular coordinate that labels position along magnetic field lines after
a straight-field-line transformation, making field-line trajectories linear
on each magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
A straight-field-line angle is an angular coordinate for labeling position
along magnetic field lines in a magnetic-flux coordinate description. The
transformation is chosen so that field-line trajectories are straight, or
have constant angular slope, on each flux surface.

This quantity denotes the coordinate itself rather than a mechanical
steering angle, wave phase, or physical distance along a field line. Its
origin, angular orientation, and selected angular direction are defined by
the associated straight-field-line coordinate convention.

The [poloidal straight-field-line
angle](name:poloidal_straight_field_line_angle) is the poloidal
specialization of this general coordinate concept. Other specializations,
when defined, differ by the angular direction or coordinate convention
rather than by a different underlying physical quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when position advances in the defined positive
direction of the straight-field-line angular coordinate.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power
absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population, integrated over the plasma
volume.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the plasma-volume integral of the
local coherent-wave power deposition density into the bulk thermal electron
population. It is the thermal-electron component of [electron absorbed wave
power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), rather than the total absorbed
power across all plasma channels.

The defining volume integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal electron power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the
plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is differential
volume.

The integral includes only power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons and
excludes deposition into fast electrons, ions, and other channels. Unlike
[thermal electron power at inside flux
surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it covers the
complete plasma volume rather than a specified enclosed region.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron power at an inside flux surface quantifies the total rate
at which coherent wave energy is absorbed by the bulk thermal electron
population within the plasma volume bounded by a given magnetic flux
surface. It is the thermal-electron contribution to [electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), distinct
from the suprathermal contribution [fast electron power at an inside flux
surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

The quantity is obtained by integrating the flux-surface-averaged
thermal-electron power density $p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}$ over the enclosed
plasma volume:

$$
P_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho) = \int_0^\rho p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho') \frac{dV}{d\rho'} \, d\rho'
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho)$ is the cumulative absorbed power,
$\rho$ labels the limiting magnetic flux surface, $\rho'$ is the integration
variable, $p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}$ is the local thermal-electron absorbed
power density, and $dV/d\rho'$ is the differential enclosed volume per unit
flux-surface label. Only absorption by bulk thermal electrons is included;
fast-electron and ion absorption, launched power, and absorption outside the
enclosed volume are excluded. At the outermost closed flux surface, it gives
the total wave power absorbed by thermal electrons.

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into a selected thermal
ion species, summed over all charge states and evaluated locally or as a
flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Thermal-ion absorbed wave power density is the rate at which coherent
electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to the thermal population of
a selected ion species per unit physical volume. It encompasses the local
deposition density and its average over a magnetic flux surface.

The flux-surface-averaged quantity is defined by

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{th},i}
= \left\langle p_{\mathrm{th},i}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
= \left\langle \sum_z \frac{dP_{\mathrm{th},i,z}}{dV}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the local thermal-ion absorbed wave power
density, $\overline{p}_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is its flux-surface average, $i$
identifies the selected ion species, $z$ identifies an ionic charge state,
$P_{\mathrm{th},i,z}$ is the wave power deposited into that species' thermal
population in charge state $z$, $V$ is physical volume, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

The recipient population is the thermal, Maxwellian component of the
selected species, summed over all charge states; no sum over different ion
species is implied. It excludes [fast-ion wave
absorption](name:fast_ion_power_density), electron wave absorption, and
subsequent collisional redistribution of absorbed energy. It is therefore
distinct from a net ion-energy source that combines wave heating with other
source and loss processes.

Summing the flux-surface-averaged contributions from all recipient
populations gives the [flux-surface-averaged total absorbed wave power
density](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_absorbed_wave_power_density).
Integrating this species' local deposition density over the plasma volume
gives its thermal-ion contribution to [absorbed wave
power](name:absorbed_wave_power), rather than another volumetric quantity.

sources.leaf_definition: Flux surface averaged absorbed wave power density on the thermal species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power density on the thermal species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to the bulk thermal
ions of a specified charge state, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated power absorbed by the bulk thermal
ion population in a specified charge state from a coherent electromagnetic
wave. It is the thermal component of ion charge-state power and excludes
nonthermal ions and collisional energy exchange between plasma populations.

The total absorbed power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{th},q} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs},\mathrm{th},q}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th},q}$ is the thermal-ion power for charge state $q$,
$p_{\mathrm{abs},\mathrm{th},q}$ is the corresponding local coherent-wave
power-transfer density, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. The
total includes all toroidal Fourier modes; [per-toroidal-mode thermal ion
charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power)
resolves the same quantity by mode. It contributes to the broader [ion
absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) and is a
charge-state-resolved component of ion charge-state power.

sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface. It
is the portion of wave power transferred to thermal ions in that charge
state, accumulated over the volume inside the chosen surface.

The cumulative power is defined by integrating the local absorbed-wave-power
density for that thermal ion charge state over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda) = \int_{V(\lambda)} p_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power for
thermal ion charge state $q$ inside the magnetic flux surface labeled by
$\lambda$, $p_q^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local absorbed-wave-power density for
that thermal ion charge state, and $V(\lambda)$ is the plasma volume
enclosed by that magnetic flux surface.

This quantity is charge-state resolved and includes only absorption by the
thermal ion population; it excludes absorption by electrons, fast or
non-thermal ions, neutrals, and non-wave power exchange. Because power is
extensive, the sum over all thermal-ion charge states gives
[thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface).
It is the thermal-population contribution to
[ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface);
the corresponding fast-ion contribution is
[fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal ion population within the
plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The thermal-ion power at inside flux surface is the running volume integral
of wave power deposited into the bulk thermal ion population, giving the
radial distribution of enclosed thermal-ion wave absorption. It is the
bulk-ion component of
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
separated from both fast-ion and electron heating channels.

The quantity is the volume integral of the thermal-ion wave-power density
$p_{\mathrm{th},i}(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\chi)$ enclosed by
the flux surface labeled $\chi$:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th},i}(\chi) = \int_{V(\chi)} p_{\mathrm{th},i}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the thermal-ion volumetric wave-power density
in W m$^{-3}$, $dV$ is the volume element in m$^3$, $P_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is
the enclosed thermal-ion wave power in W, and $\chi$ is the chosen
flux-surface label, such as the normalized toroidal flux radius
$\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$.

This quantity includes only wave energy absorbed by bulk thermal ions inside
the selected closed magnetic flux surface. Wave energy absorbed by thermal
electrons is
[thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
wave energy absorbed by suprathermal ions is
[fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
and the sum over thermal and fast ion populations is
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: thickness_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Thickness of an ICRH antenna strap is the full, non-negative extent of the
strap conductor cross-section perpendicular to the central segment of the
strap rectangle in the thick-line geometric approximation. It is distinct
from strap width, height, and length.
NAMES.long:
Thickness of an ICRH antenna strap is the full, non-negative extent of the
strap conductor cross-section in the direction perpendicular to the central
segment of the strap rectangle in the thick-line geometric approximation. It
is a geometric length of the strap conductor, not an oriented displacement.

For a strap conductor cross-section $C$ and a unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$
along the modeled thickness direction, the thickness $t$ is the range of
projected positions:

$$
t = \max_{\mathbf{r}\in C}\left(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right) - \min_{\mathbf{r}\in C}\left(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right)
$$

where $t$ is the thickness of the antenna strap, $C$ is the conductor
cross-section, $\mathbf{r}$ is a position vector for a point of that
cross-section, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is a unit vector in the cross-section
perpendicular to the central segment of the strap rectangle.

The scope is a single ICRH antenna strap represented by the thick-line
strap-rectangle geometry. The aggregation convention is the complete
max-minus-min extent over the conductor cross-section along the modeled
thickness direction; it is not an average thickness, a local surface
separation, a half-thickness, or a signed offset.

Thickness is an independent strap-geometry extent that complements the width
of the antenna strap, [height of the antenna
strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), and length of the antenna strap. Those
quantities describe separate geometric extents of the same strap rather than
projections along the thickness direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Thickness
sources.parent_definition: The element is approximated by a rectangle defined by a central segment and a thickness in the direction perpendicular to the segment

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular coordinate of each antenna-strap outline point around the
machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal angle is the azimuthal coordinate assigned to each point on the
geometric outline of an antenna strap. It identifies the point’s
circumferential location in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to individual strap-outline points and is not a mean,
sum, nominal center coordinate, or mechanical orientation angle. No
aggregation over the outline is implied; each point retains its own $\phi$
value.

Together with the other coordinates of the outline, this angle locates the
strap geometry. It is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the antenna
strap](name:radial_coordinate_of_antenna_strap), which locates a strap
reference point, while [vertical outline of the antenna
strap](name:vertical_outline_of_antenna_strap) provides the corresponding
signed vertical coordinate for outline points. The same angular-coordinate
concept is used for a different object by [toroidal angle of a coil
conductor element](name:toroidal_angle_of_coil_conductor_element).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the angular displacement from the chosen
$\phi=0$ reference is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: Strap outline

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_aperture
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular coordinate locating the geometric center of a collimating
aperture around the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal angular coordinate $\phi_c$ of an aperture's
reference center, locating that center around the machine symmetry axis.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Using the right-handed
Cartesian basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$ as
horizontal unit vectors and $\hat{z}$ aligned with the vertical cylindrical
direction $\hat{Z}$, the coordinate is defined by:

$$
\phi_c = \operatorname{atan2}(Y_c, X_c)
$$

Here, $\phi_c$ is the toroidal angle of the aperture center, $X_c$ and $Y_c$
are its horizontal Cartesian coordinate values along $\hat{x}$ and
$\hat{y}$, and $\operatorname{atan2}$ is the two-argument azimuth function
referenced to the chosen $\phi=0$ direction.

The quantity applies to one aperture reference center. For a circular
aperture, this reference is the circle's geometric center; for an aperture
represented by a local plane, it is the origin of the local coordinate
system located within the aperture area. It is not the toroidal angle of an
arbitrary aperture point, the aperture orientation, the beam direction, or
an aggregate over multiple apertures.

This coordinate is the toroidal counterpart of the [vertical coordinate of
an aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_aperture), which gives the $Z$
location of the same center. The equivalent center-based convention is also
represented by [toroidal coordinate of an
aperture](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_aperture); neither coordinate
specifies the aperture's radial location, size, or orientation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the aperture center lies in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ from the chosen $\phi=0$ reference.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_beamlet_group
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular coordinate of a beamlet-group center around the machine
symmetry axis, using the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the toroidal angular coordinate of the representative center
position of a beamlet group about the machine symmetry axis. It locates the
group in the toroidal direction and is distinct from the position of any
individual beamlet.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the group-center
position is represented by

$$
\mathbf{r}_c = R_c\hat{\mathbf{R}}(\phi_c) + Z_c\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the beamlet-group center position, $R_c$ is its
major-radius coordinate, $Z_c$ is its vertical coordinate, $\phi_c$ is its
toroidal angle, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}(\phi_c)$ is the radial unit vector at that
angle, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The basis is
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

The scope is the defined center position of the beamlet group as a whole. No
aggregation over the toroidal angles of individual beamlets is implied; the
quantity does not represent an individual beamlet's location, direction,
trajectory, radial coordinate, or vertical coordinate. Together with the
center's radial and vertical coordinates, it specifies the group's
cylindrical position. Its angular convention is the same as that used for
the [toroidal angle of an antenna
strap](name:toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap), while the owning object is
different.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the center's angular displacement is in the
$+\hat{\phi}$ direction, toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: R, Z, Phi position of the beamlet group centre

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_launching_position
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angle of launching position is the azimuthal coordinate of the
physical point where a heating wave or particle beam is launched, measured
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame with R major radius, φ
toroidal angle, and Z vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal angle of launching position is the azimuthal coordinate of the
physical point where a heating wave or particle beam is launched. It is
defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a launch point whose horizontal Cartesian coordinates are expressed in a
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and $+\hat{x}$ defining $\phi=0$, the toroidal angle is

$$
\phi_\mathrm{launch} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_\mathrm{launch}, x_\mathrm{launch}) \bmod 2\pi
$$

where $x_\mathrm{launch}$ and $y_\mathrm{launch}$ are the horizontal
Cartesian coordinates of the launch point, in meters, and
$\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the quadrant-resolved azimuth.

This quantity specifies only the toroidal location of the launch point. The
vertical coordinate of the same point is
[vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position),
while steering or propagation orientation is represented by direction
quantities such as
[toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam](name:toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam);
this quantity is not a beam direction or wave-vector angle. Values differing
by integer multiples of $2\pi$ identify the same toroidal locus.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the angular displacement from the $\phi=0$
direction is counter-clockwise as viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side looking
toward decreasing $Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle
sources.parent_definition: Launching position of the beam

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Toroidal-angle coordinate of the geometric center of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity locates the geometric center used to define the
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror surface in the toroidal direction. For a
spherical mirror, the reference point is the sphere center.

The toroidal angle is defined from the center coordinates in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis:

$$
\phi_{\rm mir} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_{\rm mir}, x_{\rm mir})
$$

where $x_{\rm mir}$ and $y_{\rm mir}$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the
mirror center, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and the zero-angle direction fixed by
the facility convention. This is the device-centered counterpart of the
toroidal coordinate used for a
[reflector](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_reflector).

The coordinate describes the mirror geometry in its reference position and
does not represent the mirror steering angle or the toroidal location of the
launched beam.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the mirror center lies at increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: Coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the object. This origin is located within the object area and should be the middle point of the object surface. If geometry_type=2, it's the centre of the circular object. If geometry_type=3, it's the centre of the rectangular object.

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
NAMES.short:
Toroidal-angle coordinate of the middle reference position of a lower-hybrid
antenna row in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal coordinate $\phi$ locates the middle reference position of a
lower-hybrid antenna row around the machine symmetry axis. It is the angular
coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

This coordinate specifies the row's toroidal location and does not determine
its radial or vertical location. The corresponding radial location is given
by the radial coordinate of the lower-hybrid antenna row.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when
viewed from above along the $+Z$ direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle
sources.parent_definition: Position of the middle on the row

NAMES.name: toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal component of the refractive-index vector for a lower-hybrid
wave launched by a lower-hybrid antenna.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal launched-wave index is the signed projection of the
refractive-index vector of a wave launched by a lower-hybrid antenna onto
the toroidal direction. It characterizes toroidal phase variation and is
distinct from the dimensional [toroidal wave
vector](name:toroidal_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam).

The index is defined by

$$
n_\phi = \frac{\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{k_0} = \frac{k_\phi}{k_0}
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the launched-wave vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $k_\phi$ is the toroidal projection of
$\mathbf{k}$, and $k_0$ is the free-space wavenumber. The corresponding
poloidal quantity is the [poloidal launched-wave
index](name:poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the launched-wave vector has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Refraction index in the toroidal direction
sources.parent_definition: Set of horizontal rows of waveguides (corresponding to different poloidal positions). A power spectrum is provided for each row.

NAMES.name: toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Toroidal width of the antenna strap is its full edge-to-edge physical extent
in the direction around the toroidal symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
Width of antenna strap

The width $w_\phi$ follows the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance
from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical position. It is a non-negative
geometric length, not an angular span or a signed vector component.

The quantity applies to an individual strap and denotes its full width, not
a half-width or the combined span of multiple straps. It is distinct from
the [height of the antenna strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), which
describes its vertical extent, and the [thickness of the antenna
strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap), which describes a separate
conductor dimension.

sources.leaf_definition: Horizontal full width
sources.parent_definition: Rectangular description of the element

sources.leaf_definition: Width of strap in the toroidal direction
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: total_external_heating_power
NAMES.short:
Total non-inductive power coupled from external neutral-beam and
radio-frequency heating systems to the plasma, summed over auxiliary sources
and excluding Ohmic heating.
NAMES.long:
Total external heating power is the aggregate non-inductive power coupled to
the plasma by auxiliary heating systems. It includes neutral-beam injection
and electron-cyclotron, ion-cyclotron, and lower-hybrid systems, while
excluding power associated with Ohmic induction.

The defining aggregate relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ext}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}} P_s
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the total external heating power,
$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the set of included auxiliary heating
systems, and $P_s$ is the power coupled to the plasma by auxiliary source
$s$.

The quantity applies to the whole plasma and is summed over all included
auxiliary sources rather than resolved by source, species, or spatial
region. It represents external power input that may contribute to both
plasma heating and non-inductive current drive; it is distinct from Ohmic
heating and from generator power that is not coupled to the plasma.
Source-specific contributions include [total power due to electron-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating), [total power
due to ion-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating), and power absorbed
from a neutral-beam injector, whose aggregate forms contribute to the sum.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total additional external power (NBI+EC+IC+LH, without ohmic) coupled to the plasma

NAMES.name: total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short:
Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency
power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources
through resonant electron-cyclotron interactions. It excludes launched,
transmitted, reflected, and unabsorbed shine-through power.
NAMES.long:
Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency
power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources
through resonant interaction with electrons at the electron cyclotron
frequency or its harmonics. It is an absorbed heating power, not the
generated, launched, transmitted, reflected, or unabsorbed radiofrequency
power.

The total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power is the sum of the net
absorbed powers from the contributing electron-cyclotron sources:

$$
P_\mathrm{EC} = \sum_{s=1}^{N_\mathrm{EC}} P_{\mathrm{EC},s}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{EC}$ is the number of contributing electron-cyclotron
sources, $P_{\mathrm{EC},s}$ is the net electron-cyclotron power absorbed by
the plasma from source $s$ expressed in watts, and $P_\mathrm{EC}$ is the
total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power expressed in watts.

The per-source contribution is
[power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating](name:power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating).
This quantity is non-negative and is zero when no electron-cyclotron power
is absorbed by the plasma; it is a component of
[total_external_heating_power](name:total_external_heating_power) when total
external heating is formed over all auxiliary heating methods.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total EC power coupled to the plasma

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror is the $Z$ coordinate of that center in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is defined by projecting the mirror geometric-center position
onto the vertical coordinate axis:

$$
z_m = Z(\mathbf{r}_{m,c})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_{m,c}$ is the position of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror geometric center and $Z(\mathbf{r}_{m,c})$ is its vertical
coordinate.

Together with the radial centroid of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror
and the [toroidal coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror),
this quantity specifies the mirror geometric-center position in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is distinct from
coordinates defined for other mirror reference points, such as a sphere
center or a surface point.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the object. This origin is located within the object area and should be the middle point of the object surface. If geometry_type=2, it's the centre of the circular object. If geometry_type=3, it's the centre of the rectangular object.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position
NAMES.short:
Vertical Z coordinate of the physical point from which a heating beam or
wave is launched, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate $Z$ of the launching position locates the spatial
origin of a beam or electromagnetic wave's propagation trajectory within the
tokamak vessel, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where
$Z$ is the height along the machine symmetry axis.

For electron cyclotron heating systems, this coordinate specifies the height
at which the EC beam exits the launcher and enters the plasma. Together with
the major-radius and toroidal-angle components, it fully defines the
three-dimensional launch-point geometry needed for beam-tracing and
current-drive modeling. The angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
determines the beam injection direction from this spatial origin, while
[vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_line_of_sight)
gives $Z$ at discrete computed points along the propagating ray rather than
at its origin.

The launch height is set by the mechanical installation of the launcher on
the vacuum vessel and is determined by engineering survey. For
equatorial-port launchers, $Z$ is close to 0 m; upper-port or top-launch
geometries place the origin at $Z \approx 0.5$–$1.5$ m in medium-to-large
tokamaks.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Launching position of the beam

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Vertical Z-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate locates the reference point of a lower-hybrid
antenna along the vertical direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation is:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{ant}} = Z(P_{\mathrm{ant}})
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ant}}$ is the antenna reference point and
$Z(P_{\mathrm{ant}})$ is its vertical coordinate. This quantity refers to
the antenna reference point; the [vertical coordinate of a lower-hybrid
antenna row](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row) refers
instead to a row reference point.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the antenna reference point lies in the
direction of increasing $Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Reference point used to define the poloidal angle, e.g. the geometrical centre of the vacuum vessel. Used to define the poloidal refraction index under antenna/row

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
NAMES.short:
Vertical Z-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ
is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Vertical $Z$-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row
is the projection of that row reference point onto $\hat{Z}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a row reference point with position vector
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}}$, the coordinate is defined by:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{row}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This is a row-level coordinate and is distinct from the antenna-level
[vertical coordinate of the lower-hybrid
antenna](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). It is distinct
from the row vertical extent.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the row reference point lies in the
$+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame
from the $Z=0$ plane.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Position of the middle on the row

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Vertical coordinate Z of the declared reference position of a neutral beam
injector is the signed height of that point from the equatorial plane in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical coordinate $Z$ of the declared reference position of a neutral beam
injector is the signed height of that point relative to the equatorial plane
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It identifies only the
vertical component of the injector reference-point position.

The coordinate is the projection of the reference-point displacement onto
the vertical basis vector:

$$
Z_\mathrm{NBI} = \mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ is the displacement of the declared
reference position from an origin on the symmetry axis in the equatorial
plane, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

For an extended injector, this quantity locates only the declared reference
point; it does not define the injector aperture, beam-axis direction, beam
footprint, or full beam geometry. A complementary position coordinate is
[radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector)
when defined for the same reference point.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the declared reference position lies above
the equatorial plane in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Height

NAMES.name: vertical_displacement_of_beamlet_group
NAMES.short:
Signed vertical displacement of a neutral-beam-injection beamlet-group
center from its static geometry during dynamic beam tilting.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed change in the vertical position of a
beamlet-group center when the beamlet geometry is dynamically tilted away
from its static configuration. It represents the group center as a geometric
object, not the beamlet group's extent or focal length.

The displacement is defined by

$$
\Delta Z = Z_{\mathrm{dynamic}} - Z_{\mathrm{static}}
$$

where $\Delta Z$ is the vertical displacement, $Z_{\mathrm{dynamic}}$ is the
vertical coordinate of the beamlet-group center in the dynamically tilted
configuration, and $Z_{\mathrm{static}}$ is its corresponding coordinate in
the static geometry. These coordinates are expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The scope is one beamlet group treated as a single geometric object during
dynamic tilting; the quantity is a center displacement rather than a
per-beamlet value, an absolute position, or a displacement summed over
beamlet properties. It excludes the group's cross-sectional size, which is
described by its [vertical width](name:vertical_width_of_beamlet_group), and
its distance to a focal point, described by its [vertical focal
length](name:vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group).

The quantity is the vertical counterpart of a signed radial center
displacement such as [radial offset of a beamlet
group](name:radial_offset_of_beamlet_group). It differs from [perturbed
major radius](name:perturbed_major_radius), which describes dynamic
variation of a beam-line tangency radius rather than the vertical position
of the beamlet-group center.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the dynamically tilted beamlet-group center
is displaced toward increasing $Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Variation of the position of the beamlet group centre

NAMES.name: vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group
NAMES.short:
Vertical focal length of a beamlet group is the distance along the
neutral-beam line from the group’s ion source to the point where the group’s
vertical extent is minimized.
NAMES.long:
Vertical focal length of a beamlet group is the path length along the
neutral-beam line from the beamlet group's ion source to the group vertical
focus. The group vertical focus is the location at which the collective
beamlet envelope has its minimum vertical extent, with vertical measured
parallel to $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Using an along-beam coordinate $s$ that increases from the ion source along
the neutral-beam line, the focal length is defined by

$$
f_v = s_f - s_0, \qquad w_v(s_f) = \min_s w_v(s)
$$

where $f_v$ is the vertical focal length of the beamlet group, $s_0$ is the
ion-source position on the along-beam coordinate, $s_f$ is the
vertical-focus position, and $w_v(s)$ is the collective vertical envelope
extent of the beamlet group at position $s$.

The quantity applies to one beamlet group and aggregates all beamlets in
that group through their collective vertical envelope. It is not a
per-beamlet focal length and not a whole-unit focal length formed by
combining multiple groups; the distance is along the beam-line path rather
than a vertical separation.

It is distinct from the source-surface vertical width of a beamlet group and
from any vertical extent at locations other than the focus; those are
transverse extents, whereas this quantity is the along-beam separation to
the location of the minimum. It is the vertical counterpart of the
horizontal focal length of a beamlet group, which uses the minimum
horizontal extent instead of the minimum vertical extent.

sources.leaf_definition: Vertical focal length along the beam line, i.e. the point along the centre of the beamlet-group where the beamlet-group has its minimum vertical width
sources.parent_definition: Describes how the beamlet group is focused. Calculations of width_min_horizontal and width_min_vertical are on a plane defined by the average normal vector of the two constituent accelerator nbi target planes.

NAMES.name: vertical_width_of_beamlet_group
NAMES.short:
Full vertical cross-sectional extent of a neutral-beam-injection beamlet
group at the injection unit’s source surface.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the full vertical geometric width occupied collectively by
the beamlets in a neutral-beam-injection group at the injection unit’s
grounded-grid source surface.

The width is defined by the separation of the uppermost and lowermost
beamlet-group boundaries:

$$
w_v = Z_{\mathrm{top}} - Z_{\mathrm{bottom}}
$$

where $w_v$ is the vertical beamlet-group width, $Z_{\mathrm{top}}$ and
$Z_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ are the upper and lower vertical coordinates of the
group boundary, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal
angle.

This quantity applies to the aggregate cross-sectional envelope of the
beamlet group at the source surface, not to an individual beamlet. It
represents the full width rather than a half-width, local spread, or width
evaluated at another position along the beam line.

The width changes along the beam line as the beamlets converge. It is
therefore distinct from the [vertical focal length of the beamlet
group](name:vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group), which is the distance
to the point of minimum vertical width rather than the width itself.

sources.leaf_definition: Vertical width (dimensions of the smallest rectangle that surrounds the outer dimensions of the beamlets) of the beamlet group at the injection unit surface (or grounded grid)
sources.parent_definition: Group of beamlets with common vertical and horizontal focal point. If there are no common focal points, then select small groups of beamlets such that a focal point description of the beamlets group provides a fair description. Beamlet groups are assumed to be Gaussian.

NAMES.name: voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Electrical potential difference associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna, defined between the antenna conductor or feed and its reference
conductor. It is the general antenna-voltage quantity; specialized names
specify amplitude or another representation of the waveform.
NAMES.long:
Electrical potential difference associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna is the scalar electric potential of the specified antenna conductor
or feed relative to its associated reference conductor or node. It
represents the antenna voltage waveform before any child name specifies a
particular reduction or representation of that waveform.

The signed antenna voltage is defined by the potential difference between
the antenna node and its reference node:

$$
V_\mathrm{ant}(t) = \Phi_\mathrm{ant}(t) - \Phi_\mathrm{ref}(t)
$$

where $V_\mathrm{ant}(t)$ is the antenna voltage, $\Phi_\mathrm{ant}(t)$ is
the electric potential of the specified antenna conductor or feed,
$\Phi_\mathrm{ref}(t)$ is the electric potential of its associated reference
conductor or node, and $t$ is time.

The scope is voltages intrinsic to ion-cyclotron-heating antenna hardware,
including antenna conductors, straps, or feeds when they are the defined
electrical node. The unqualified parent does not by itself specify an
instantaneous value, phasor, peak amplitude, root-mean-square value, or any
aggregation over antenna elements; those distinctions belong to qualified
child names.

The [voltage amplitude of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is a
specialized reduction of this antenna voltage waveform to its peak
magnitude. This parent is distinct from antenna current, generator voltage
not defined at the antenna node, and launched or absorbed radio-frequency
power.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electric potential of the specified
antenna conductor or feed is greater than the electric potential of its
associated reference conductor or node.

NAMES.name: voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency voltage waveform on a single
transmission-line feed of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the peak magnitude of the radio-frequency electrical
potential difference on one transmission-line feed belonging to an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module.

For the feed voltage waveform $v(t)$, its amplitude is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{amp}} = \max_t |v(t)|
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the voltage amplitude, $v(t)$ is the
instantaneous feed voltage, and $t$ is time. The absolute value removes
instantaneous polarity, while the maximum selects the peak magnitude of the
waveform.

The quantity applies to one feed of one antenna module and is not a sum over
feeds, antenna modules, or the complete heating system. It excludes the
instantaneous signed voltage and its phase; it also does not represent
forward or launched radio-frequency power. It is the amplitude
transformation of the corresponding [ion-cyclotron-heating antenna
voltage](name:voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), retaining the feed
voltage's peak level while discarding its instantaneous sign and phase.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of voltage measurements

NAMES.name: wave_current_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Characterization of the radio-frequency current oscillating along an antenna
strap, encompassing peak-amplitude and root-mean-square representations of
the same wave current.
NAMES.long:
Wave current of an antenna strap is the radio-frequency electric current
oscillating along the strap conductor during electromagnetic-wave
excitation. The quantity is represented by a non-negative measure of the
oscillation rather than by the instantaneous signed waveform.

The underlying single-frequency current can be represented as

$$
I_{\mathrm{RF}}(t) = \operatorname{Re}\{\widetilde{I}_{\mathrm{RF}} e^{i\omega t}\}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ is the instantaneous radio-frequency current,
$\widetilde{I}_{\mathrm{RF}}$ is its complex phasor, $t$ is time, and
$\omega$ is the angular frequency of the oscillation.

This quantity applies to the radio-frequency current carried by an antenna
strap and includes representations evaluated at a strap position or formed
as an effective measure of the oscillation. It excludes the non-wave or
total current represented by [current of an antenna
strap](name:current_of_antenna_strap), as well as current density and plasma
current.

The accepted child quantities provide two representations of this common
quantity: [wave current amplitude of an antenna
strap](name:wave_current_amplitude_of_antenna_strap) gives the peak
magnitude of the oscillation, while [root-mean-square wave current of an
antenna strap](name:root_mean_square_wave_current_of_antenna_strap) gives
its effective magnitude. For a sinusoidal waveform, the root-mean-square
magnitude is the peak magnitude divided by $\sqrt{2}$.

NAMES.name: wave_current_amplitude_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency current at a specified position along
an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the peak magnitude of the radio-frequency current on an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap at a specified position. It
characterizes the local electromagnetic excitation of a strap fed through a
single transmission line.

The amplitude $I_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is defined from the local RF current
waveform $i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ by

$$
I_{\mathrm{amp}} = \max_t \left|i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)\right|
$$

where $i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ is the instantaneous radio-frequency current at
the specified strap position and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies locally along the antenna strap and represents the RF
wave-current amplitude, not a current summed over the antenna system or over
multiple straps. It is a non-negative magnitude and is distinct from the
signed instantaneous current and from an RMS current measure.

It is the amplitude transformation of the [wave current of an antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap): the parent denotes the
oscillating current, whereas this quantity retains its peak magnitude at the
specified position.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of current measurements

NAMES.name: wave_frequency
NAMES.short:
Temporal carrier frequency of a coherent electromagnetic wave used to
characterize its oscillation rate in plasma heating and current drive.
NAMES.long:
Wave frequency is the non-negative temporal carrier frequency of a coherent
electromagnetic wave interacting with a plasma. It describes the rate of
phase oscillation and applies to waves at launch or during propagation,
independent of the wave amplitude or absorbed power.

The frequency $f$ is related to the angular frequency by

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is frequency in hertz and $\omega$ is angular frequency in radians
per second. The launch-specific quantity launched wave frequency uses this
same definition as the absolute reference for a launched wave, while
[frequency of electron cyclotron heating
antenna](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam) is a device-specific
instance.

sources.leaf_definition: Wave frequency
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities for various time slices

NAMES.name: wave_mode_number
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless mode-number vector labeling the discrete Fourier periodicities
of a coherent wave perturbation.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the collection of discrete mode labels that identifies a
coherent wave perturbation through its periodic phase dependence. It is a
mode-index vector, not a spatial wavevector, physical displacement vector,
or full linear-MHD eigenmode label.

For a coherent perturbation represented by a single Fourier phase in
periodic coordinates, the wave mode-number vector is defined by

$$
\tilde{q}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}, t) = \hat{q}\,\exp\!\left[i\left(\mathbf{N}_w \cdot \boldsymbol{\alpha} - \omega t\right)\right]
$$

where $\tilde{q}$ is the coherent wave perturbation of a field quantity,
$\hat{q}$ is its complex amplitude, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ is the set of
periodic coordinates used to label the phase, $\mathbf{N}_w$ is the wave
mode-number vector, and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

This parent covers Fourier harmonic labels of coherent waves, such as the
[toroidal wave mode number](name:toroidal_wave_mode_number) associated with
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
It does not by itself assert a radial branch index or a poloidal harmonic;
those belong only to more specific quantities when explicitly defined, and
distinguish it from the broader linear-MHD mode number.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when increasing the associated periodic coordinate
at fixed time increases the Fourier phase in the representation above.

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
