Phase angle of the radio-frequency current phasor carried by one
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap, defined relative to a specified RF
phase reference.
NAMES.long:
Wave phase of an antenna strap is the phase angle of the oscillatory
radio-frequency current phasor carried by that strap. It describes the
strap-level excitation phase used in the antenna's toroidal phasing
configuration.

The complex strap-current phasor may be represented as

$$
I_s = |I_s|e^{i\phi_s}
$$

where $I_s$ is the complex radio-frequency current phasor, $|I_s|$ is its
current amplitude, and $\phi_s$ is the wave phase represented by this
quantity. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$ relative to a specified RF
reference phase.

This quantity applies to one antenna strap and is not summed or averaged
over multiple straps. It refers to the phase of the strap current, not the
phase of a forward power-wave phasor, which is represented by [forward wave
phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), or the
phase associated with a complete antenna element.

The associated [wave current of antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap) provides the phasor whose phase
is specified, while wave current of antenna strap amplitude determines its
magnitude rather than its phase. Relative phases between straps determine
the toroidal phasing of the antenna excitation and therefore influence the
launched wave excitation spectrum. The phase-reference plane and any
phase-unwrapping convention must be specified separately when comparing
values.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the strap current
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna specifies the relative
angular offset of coherent radio-frequency excitations at selected straps or
modules.
NAMES.long:
Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the relative phase of a
coherent radio-frequency excitation associated with a selected strap or
module. It describes excitation phasing rather than an absolute phase
independent of a reference.

For selected and reference excitations, the relative phase is defined by

$$
\varphi = \arg\!\left(A_{\mathrm{sel}} A_{\mathrm{ref}}^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\varphi$ is the wave phase, $A_{\mathrm{sel}}$ is the selected
complex excitation phasor, $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the coherent reference
excitation phasor, the superscript $*$ denotes complex conjugation, and
$\arg$ extracts the complex argument. Both phasors must be nonzero and refer
to the same radio-frequency component. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$.

The scope includes relative phasing between antenna straps or modules,
without summation or averaging over elements. The excitation quantity,
reference excitation, reference planes, and temporal phasor convention must
be specified. Feed-voltage phase and traveling power-wave phase are distinct
realizations and are not interchangeable without their electrical
relationship. Relative element phasing affects interference between
excitations and therefore the launched wave spectrum and current-drive
efficiency.

The [forward-wave
phase](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) specializes
this quantity to forward power-wave phasors referenced to the first module;
that reference is not imposed on the general quantity. The [wave phase of an
antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap) specifically identifies the
phase of its radio-frequency current phasor. Neither phase quantity includes
excitation magnitude.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected excitation phasor leads the
reference excitation phasor in phase under the declared temporal phasor
convention.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of voltage measurements

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Phase between straps

NAMES.name: forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase of the forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module, referenced to the first module for
inter-module toroidal phasing.
NAMES.long:
The forward-wave phase is the relative phase angle of the complex
radio-frequency power-wave phasor associated with one ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna module. It describes inter-module phasing rather than an absolute
phase.

For selected module $i$, the relative forward-wave phase is defined by

$$
\theta_i^{+} = \arg\left(\tilde{a}_i^{+}\right) - \arg\left(\tilde{a}_1^{+}\right)
$$

where $\theta_i^{+}$ is the relative forward-wave phase, $i$ identifies the
selected antenna module, module $1$ is the first reference module,
$\tilde{a}_i^{+}$ is the complex phasor of the forward radio-frequency power
wave associated with module $i$, and $\arg$ returns a phasor's phase angle.

The quantity applies only to the forward wave at an antenna module and is
defined relative to the first module; no absolute phase relative to a
generator or external reference is implied. It concerns the electromagnetic
power-wave phasor, not a plasma-particle quantity or a spatially distributed
plasma field.

This is the forward-wave specialization of the relative antenna phasor phase
defined by [wave phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna). It is distinct
from the relative phase of the reflected wave, [reflected phase of an
ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and from
the phase of the RF current carried by an antenna strap, [wave phase of an
antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected module's forward-wave phasor
leads the first reference module in phase.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the forward power with respect to the first module
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: wave_power
NAMES.short:
Rate at which electromagnetic-wave energy is transferred to a selected
plasma particle population or charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net electromagnetic-wave power absorbed by plasma
particles, representing energy transfer from the wave field to a selected
population or charge state.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power and $E_{\rm particles}$ is the
energy of the selected particle population; the subscript indicates that
only energy transfer caused by the electromagnetic wave is included.

The quantity excludes launched or generator power, unabsorbed wave power,
and energy merely transported by the wave. Spatially cumulative instances,
such as [ion charge-state power inside a flux
surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface), apply this
definition to a specified enclosed plasma volume.

NAMES.name: absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.short:
Net electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly from coherent waves to a
selected plasma particle population, integrated over the plasma volume and
resolved by species or charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves
transfer energy directly to selected plasma particles. The selected
population may be electrons, ions, or a specified ion charge state, with the
result integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the
energy of the selected particle population, and the subscript “waves”
restricts the energy-transfer rate to direct coupling from the
electromagnetic wave field. This is the absorbed component of [wave
power](name:wave_power), distinct from electromagnetic power that remains
carried by the wave.

The quantity includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes
subsequent collisional redistribution between particle populations.
Species-resolved and charge-state-resolved instances include [electron
absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) and ion charge-state
absorbed wave power.

NAMES.name: ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to ion
populations, integrated over the plasma volume and partitioned into thermal
and fast-ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
Ion absorbed wave power is the total rate of energy transfer from coherent
electromagnetic waves to ion populations. It includes direct absorption by
both bulk thermal ions and suprathermal fast ions.

The volume-integrated ion power is defined by

$$
P_i^{\mathrm{abs}} = \int_V p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{abs}} + P_{i,\mathrm{thermal}}^{\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_i^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total ion absorbed wave power,
$p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local wave power deposition density
to ions, $V$ is the plasma volume, and the two terms are the [fast-ion
absorbed wave power](name:fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [thermal-ion
absorbed wave power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power). This quantity is
the ion component of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power),
excluding power transferred directly to electron populations; [electron
absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) represents the
corresponding electron channel.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total coherent-wave power absorbed by the suprathermal ion population,
integrated over the plasma volume and excluding thermal-ion absorption.
NAMES.long:
The fast ion absorbed wave power is the volume-integrated power delivered by
coherent electromagnetic waves to the suprathermal, nonthermal ion
population through wave-particle interactions.

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\,ion}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast\,ion}}$ is the total absorbed power,
$p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local power-absorption
density for fast ions at position $\mathbf{r}$, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is
the plasma volume. This quantity is the fast-ion component of [ion absorbed
wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power), excluding power absorbed by
thermal ions and electrons. It is aggregated over the coherent-wave channels
and toroidal modes represented by the global quantity; [per-toroidal-mode
fast-ion absorbed wave
power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [fast-ion
power at an inside flux surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface)
provide more resolved scopes.

sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal (Maxwellian) ion
population, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The thermal ion absorbed wave power is the volume-integrated power delivered
by coherent electromagnetic waves to the bulk thermal (approximately
Maxwellian) ion population via wave-particle resonance interactions. It is
the thermal-ion component of
[ion_absorbed_wave_power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power), which spans all ion
populations.

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,i}} = \int_{V} p_{\mathrm{th,i}}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th,i}}$ is the local wave power density absorbed by
thermal ions and $V$ is the total plasma volume. The associated spatial
deposition profile is described by
[thermal_ion_power_density](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power_density).

This quantity excludes power deposited into suprathermal (fast) ions. No
ion-species qualifier is carried: it aggregates over all thermal ion species
present in the plasma. Charge-state-resolved contributions are provided by
[thermal_ion_charge_state_power](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power);
summing over all charge states and species recovers this global value.

sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Absorbed coherent-wave power transferred directly to thermal ions of one
species inside a magnetic flux surface, summed over charge states and
resolved by toroidal Fourier mode.
NAMES.long:
Thermal ion absorbed wave power per toroidal mode is the cumulative rate of
direct energy transfer from coherent electromagnetic waves to the bulk,
approximately Maxwellian ions of one selected species inside a closed
magnetic flux surface. Each contribution corresponds to one toroidal Fourier
harmonic.

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathcal S) = \int_{V(\mathcal S)} q_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}\,dV
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the cumulative absorbed power, $i$
identifies the selected ion species, $\mathrm{th}$ denotes its thermal
population, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, $\mathcal
S$ is the selected magnetic flux surface, $V(\mathcal S)$ is its enclosed
plasma volume, $q_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the local absorbed wave
power density summed over all charge states of that species for the same
harmonic, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The quantity is summed over all charge states of the selected species, but
not over ion species or toroidal modes. It is an enclosed-volume integral,
not a local power density or necessarily a whole-plasma total. It excludes
direct absorption by fast ions and electrons, energy remaining in the wave
field, and energy subsequently redistributed between particle populations by
collisions.

Its charge-state-resolved contributions are represented by
[per-toroidal-mode thermal ion charge-state
power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power); summing those
contributions over all charge states recovers this quantity. Summing over
all toroidal-mode contributions at a flux surface enclosing the entire
plasma recovers [thermal ion absorbed wave
power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power) for the same ion species and
coherent-wave field.

sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density), per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
X-axis component of the unit vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror’s translation or rotation axis at its home position.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the Cartesian x projection of the unit vector that defines
an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation direction or rotation
axis at its home position.

Let $\hat{d}$ denote this direction unit vector and $\hat{x}$ the x-axis
unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
basis. The component is defined by

$$
d_x = \hat{d} \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $d_x$ is the signed x-axis component and the unit-vector condition is
$|\hat{d}|=1$.

The component is dimensionless and is bounded by $-1 \leq d_x \leq 1$.
Together with the [y-axis direction
component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [z-axis direction
component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror),
it specifies the mirror-axis orientation.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along X axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector indicating the direction of the translation or the rotation axis at "home" position (i.e. ../../geometry/centre)

NAMES.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Signed component along the y axis of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed y projection of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position.

Let $d_y$ denote this component, $chat{\mathbf d}$ the defining unit
direction vector, and $chat{\mathbf y}$ the unit vector along the positive y
axis of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis:

$$
d_y = \hat{\mathbf d} \cdot \hat{\mathbf y}
$$

The corresponding [x-axis
component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [z-axis
component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
complete the Cartesian components of the same unit vector. This quantity
describes direction, not the mirror’s position or displacement.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector indicating the direction of the translation or the rotation axis at "home" position (i.e. ../../geometry/centre)

NAMES.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Signed component along the z axis of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Signed component along the z axis of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position is the scalar projection of that mirror direction
vector onto the z-axis basis direction in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The $\hat{z}$ basis direction is
vertical.

For mirror direction unit vector $\mathbf{u}$, the component is defined by:

$$
u_z = \mathbf{u}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}, \qquad \lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert = 1
$$

where $u_z$ is the z-axis component of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror direction unit vector, $\mathbf{u}$ is the unit vector defining that
mirror's translation direction or rotation axis at its home position,
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the positive z-axis basis vector in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, and $\lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert$
is the Euclidean norm of $\mathbf{u}$.

The quantity applies to an individual electron-cyclotron launcher mirror at
its home position. It is a single Cartesian component of the movement
direction or rotation axis, not an aggregate over launchers or mirrors and
not an average over a range of mirror motion.

It is not a mirror position, displacement, the vertical coordinate of a
point, or the angle of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. The
corresponding [x-axis
component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [y-axis
component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
complete the same home-position unit vector; with $u_x$ and $u_y$ denoting
those linked components, the components satisfy $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Z axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector indicating the direction of the translation or the rotation axis at "home" position (i.e. ../../geometry/centre)

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave energy absorption by fast
ions of a specified species and charge state or bundle, locally or averaged
over a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion charge-state power density is the rate at which coherent
radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to nonthermal fast ions of a
specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle per unit physical
volume. It encompasses local absorption and its flux-surface average, which
represents deposition averaged over a magnetic flux surface.

The local absorption density and its flux-surface-averaged form are defined
by

$$
p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}} = \sum_{z\in C}\frac{dP_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}}{dV},
\qquad
p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local fast-ion absorption
density, $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is its flux-surface average, $C$
is the selected set of ionic charge states, $z$ identifies an included
charge state, $P_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the wave power absorbed
by fast ions in that state, $V$ is physical volume, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

A single-state quantity includes only that charge state; a bundle is summed
over its included states, not over every charge state of the species. The
recipient population excludes thermal ions. The quantity describes direct
wave absorption, not subsequent collisional redistribution, stored fast-ion
energy, or volume-integrated absorbed power.

This is the fast-population, direct-wave-absorption contribution to [ion
charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), rather
than its full net energy-source term. Summing nonoverlapping contributions
over all ionic charge states gives [fast-ion power
density](name:fast_ion_power_density) for the same species, wave content,
and spatial averaging. The [toroidal-mode-resolved
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density)
additionally separates this absorption by toroidal Fourier mode.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of direct coherent-wave energy absorption by fast ions of a
specified species and charge state or bundle, resolved by toroidal mode. It
is expressed either locally or as an average over a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Mode-resolved fast-ion charge-state power density is the rate per physical
volume at which coherent-wave energy is absorbed directly by fast ions of a
specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle. The contribution
from each toroidal mode is resolved separately, and the spatial quantity may
be local or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.

The local absorbed power density for a toroidal mode is defined by

$$
p_{s,q}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{abs},s,q}^{(n_\phi)}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{s,q}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local power density absorbed
from mode $n_\phi$, $P_{\mathrm{abs},s,q}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the power absorbed
from that mode by the specified fast-ion population within volume $V$, $V$
is physical volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position. The index $s$
identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies its charge state or charge-state
bundle, and $n_\phi$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number. The
flux-surface-averaged form is the average of the local quantity over the
corresponding magnetic flux surface.

The recipient population is the fast-ion population of the specified species
and charge state or bundle; different species are not combined. A bundle
includes the sum over its constituent charge states, while separate toroidal
modes remain resolved. The quantity excludes absorption by thermal ions and
electrons, as well as subsequent collisional redistribution of absorbed
energy. It represents a mode's absorbed-power contribution, not a Fourier
coefficient of the spatial power-density field.

At fixed mode, summing over all charge states of the same species gives the
[per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density). Summing over
toroidal modes and integrating over the plasma volume gives the [fast-ion
charge-state absorbed wave
power](name:fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power) for the specified
species and charge state or bundle.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when coherent-wave energy is transferred to the
specified fast-ion population.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of energy transfer from coherent radio-frequency waves to
nonthermal fast ions of a selected species, summed over all ionic charge
states.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion power density is the rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves
transfer energy directly to the nonthermal fast-ion population of a selected
ion species per unit physical volume. It describes spatially resolved wave
absorption and also encompasses its flux-surface-averaged form.

The volumetric deposition rate is defined by

$$
Q_i^{\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{dP_i^{\mathrm{fast}}}{dV}
$$

where $Q_i^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion absorbed wave power density,
$P_i^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the wave power absorbed directly by the fast
population of ion species $i$, and $V$ is physical plasma volume.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of the selected species,
not over different ion species. The [fast-ion charge-state power
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) resolves the
corresponding contributions by charge state or charge-state bundle. Direct
absorption by thermal ions or electrons and subsequent collisional
redistribution of the absorbed fast-ion energy are excluded.

This quantity is the fast-ion direct-wave-absorption contribution to [ion
power density](name:ion_power_density), rather than the full ion energy
source from all processes. Flux-surface averaging preserves its recipient
population and energy-transfer scope but is not required by this general
definition. The [per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density) further resolves the
flux-surface-averaged deposition by toroidal Fourier harmonic.

sources.leaf_definition: Flux surface averaged absorbed wave power density on the fast species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power density on the fast species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy transfer to
fast, nonthermal ions of a selected species, summed over ionic charge states
and resolved by toroidal Fourier mode.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal-mode-resolved fast-ion power density is the flux-surface-averaged
rate at which an individual toroidal wave harmonic transfers energy to the
nonthermal fast-ion population of a selected species per unit physical
volume. It describes direct coherent-wave absorption, not subsequent
collisional redistribution of the absorbed energy.

For each toroidal harmonic, the averaged deposition density is defined by

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi) = \left\langle \frac{dE_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)}{dt\,dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)$ is the mode-resolved fast-ion power
density, $i$ labels the selected ion species, $\mathrm{f}$ identifies its
fast population, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, and
$E_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)$ is the energy transferred by that harmonic to
this population. Here $t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes averaging over the magnetic flux
surface.

The species contribution is summed over all ionic charge states, but not
over different ion species or toroidal harmonics. The [charge-state-resolved
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density)
separates the contributions whose sum gives this species-level quantity.
Thermal ions and electrons are excluded. The flux-surface average is
distinct from the unaveraged local deposition density and is not a
volume-integrated power.

Summing over a complete, consistently normalized set of toroidal harmonics
recovers the flux-surface-averaged [fast-ion power
density](name:fast_ion_power_density). Integrating the averaged density over
an enclosed physical volume gives the corresponding [mode-resolved fast-ion
absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power).
Each harmonic contribution is an absorbed power density, not a Fourier
amplitude of the deposited-power distribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when energy is transferred from the coherent wave
to the fast-ion population.

sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Signed imaginary quadrature of the left-hand circular E-plus wave
electric-field phasor along a beam or ray path, relative to a specified
phase reference.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the left-hand circularly
polarized E-plus component of a wave [electric field](name:electric_field)
phasor along its propagation path. It retains signed phase information and
is not the field amplitude or the instantaneous physical electric field.

The defining relation is:

$$
E_{+,I} = \operatorname{Im}(E_+)
$$

where $E_{+,I}$ is the signed imaginary quadrature, $E_+$ is the [left-hand
circularly polarized wave electric-field
phasor](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and
$\operatorname{Im}$ selects its imaginary part.

The parent polarization component is transverse to the local equilibrium
magnetic field. This quadrature is evaluated locally along the beam or ray
propagation path, including electron cyclotron emission paths; it is not
integrated along that path. It inherits the circular-polarization basis and
phase reference of the parent phasor.

Together with the [left-hand circularly polarized real
part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part), it
reconstructs the parent component through $E_+ = E_{+,R} + iE_{+,I}$, where
$E_{+,R}$ is the real, in-phase quadrature and $i$ is the imaginary unit.
Changing the phase reference mixes the two quadratures without changing the
physical polarization.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the E-plus phasor lies in the upper half of
the complex plane defined by the specified phase reference.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: Left hand polarised electric field component

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: Left hand polarised electric field component

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_particle_energy
NAMES.short:
Perpendicular fast-particle energy is the part of the suprathermal particle
kinetic energy associated with motion perpendicular to the local magnetic
field, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular fast-particle energy is the part of the kinetic energy of the
suprathermal particle population associated with motion perpendicular to the
local magnetic field. It complements [parallel fast-particle
energy](name:parallel_fast_particle_energy) within the total [fast-particle
energy](name:fast_particle_energy).

It is defined by

$$
W_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_{\mathcal{V}} \int \frac{1}{2} m v_\perp^2 f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\,d^3r
$$

where $\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume,
$f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})$ is the fast-particle phase-space
distribution, $m$ is particle mass, and $v_\perp$ is the speed component
perpendicular to the local magnetic field. For a gyrotropic distribution,
the corresponding energy density is the perpendicular pressure, so the
quantity equals the volume integral of [perpendicular fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), summed over the
included fast-particle species.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fast particles perpendicular energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the fast perpendicular pressure

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate locating the sphere center that defines an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the center of the sphere
that defines an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. It identifies the
mirror's geometric reference point rather than a point on the reflecting
surface.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the major-radius
coordinate relates to right-handed Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ through

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian
coordinate values in the $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's spherical
defining geometry and represents one geometric point. It is not a plasma
quantity, a surface coordinate, a mirror steering angle, or an average or
integral over the mirror.

The broader [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) concept is
specialized here to the sphere center of the mirror. Together with the
[vertical coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and
[toroidal coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), it
locates the same geometric center.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Position of the center of the sphere which defines the mirror, in the case of a spherical mirror (geometry_type = 2), derived from the above geometric data

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_launching_position
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of the beam launching position, measured from the
toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Major-radius coordinate of launching position

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the coordinate is
defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate at the launching position, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantities $x$ and $y$
are the horizontal coordinates of the same position in a right-handed
Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, whose vertical $z$ axis coincides with the
toroidal symmetry axis.

This is a locus-specific specialization of
[radial_coordinate](name:radial_coordinate): it applies pointwise to the
specified beam launching position, rather than representing an average over
beams or coordinates along a beam trajectory. It is distinct from the
[radial coordinate of an electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), which
locates the mirror's reference geometry rather than the beam launching
position.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Launching position of the beam

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of the neutral beam injector center, measured from
the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of a neutral beam injector is the major-radius
location of the injector unit center relative to the toroidal symmetry axis.
It is a nonnegative geometric coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the injector center, the radial coordinate is related to its Cartesian
coordinates by

$$
R = \\sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates of the same
injector center in the right-handed Cartesian $(\\hat{x},\\hat{y},\\hat{z})$
basis.

This quantity applies to one selected neutral beam injector unit and
represents the unit-center position only. It is not an aggregate over
multiple injectors and does not represent a beam trajectory, launch point,
deposition location, or plasma response.

It is the neutral-beam-injector specialization of the general [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), with the geometric point fixed to the
injector unit center.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Major radius

NAMES.name: radial_wave_electric_field
NAMES.short:
Complex phasor of the wave electric field projected onto the R direction of
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, preserving local amplitude,
phase, and radial polarization.
NAMES.long:
The radial wave electric field is the complex phasor obtained by projecting
the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the cylindrical
major-radius direction. It is a component of the [wave electric
field](name:wave_electric_field) and retains the local wave amplitude and
phase.

For a wave with angular frequency $\omega$, the radial phasor is defined by

$$
\widetilde{E}_r(\mathbf{r},\omega)=\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)\cdot\hat{R}
$$

where $\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex
wave-electric-field phasor, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\hat{R}$ is the
major-radius unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
Unlike the [normal wave electric field](name:normal_wave_electric_field),
this component follows the cylindrical $R$ direction and is not a projection
normal to a magnetic flux surface. It complements the [vertical wave
electric field](name:vertical_wave_electric_field) in describing cylindrical
polarization.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the corresponding electric-field component
points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Lower Hybrid electric field component in the major radius direction
sources.parent_definition: Physics quantities measured from polarized light spectroscopy

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into bulk thermal
electrons, including its average over a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Thermal-electron power density is the rate at which coherent electromagnetic
waves transfer energy directly to the bulk thermal electron population per
unit physical volume. Its flux-surface-averaged form describes the mean
deposition on a magnetic flux surface; the underlying local quantity
describes deposition within that surface.

The flux-surface-averaged deposition is defined by

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{e,th}} = \left\langle p_{\mathrm{e,th}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle \frac{dP_{\mathrm{abs,e,th}}}{dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\overline{p}_{\mathrm{e,th}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged
thermal-electron power density, $p_{\mathrm{e,th}}$ is the local
thermal-electron power density, $P_{\mathrm{abs,e,th}}$ is the coherent-wave
power absorbed by thermal electrons within physical volume $V$, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes an average over the magnetic
flux surface.

The recipient population is restricted to bulk thermal electrons. Absorption
by nonthermal electrons belongs to [fast-electron absorbed wave power
density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density). This quantity is
the direct wave-absorption contribution to [electron power
density](name:electron_power_density), not the net sum of all electron
heating and cooling channels; it excludes [collisional electron energy
exchange](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), including
subsequent collisional redistribution of deposited energy.

[Mode-resolved thermal-electron power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_power_density) specializes
this deposition by individual toroidal Fourier harmonic. Flux-surface
averaging retains the volumetric normalization rather than integrating over
the enclosed volume. Integrating that average with the enclosed-volume
measure gives the [cumulative thermal-electron absorbed power inside the
flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

sources.leaf_definition: Flux surface averaged absorbed wave power density on the thermal species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power density on the thermal species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Thermal-electron absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode is the
volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy absorption by bulk thermal electrons
attributed to an individual toroidal mode number. It is represented locally
across a poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Thermal-electron absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode is the rate
at which coherent-wave energy is absorbed by the bulk thermal-electron
population per unit physical volume, attributed to an individual toroidal
mode number.

For toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, the local absorbed power density is
defined as

$$
p_{e,n_\phi}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dE^{\mathrm{abs}}_{e,n_\phi}}{dt\,dV}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $p_{e,n_\phi}$ is the absorbed power density attributed to mode
$n_\phi$, $E^{\mathrm{abs}}_{e,n_\phi}$ is the energy absorbed by thermal
electrons from coherent waves attributed to that mode, $t$ is time, $V$ is
physical volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in a
poloidal cross-section, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal mode number, and $e$
identifies the electron population.

The recipient population is bulk thermal electrons, and the mode index
identifies an individual contribution to absorbed wave power. The quantity
may describe the local deposition across a poloidal cross-section or its
average over a magnetic flux surface. It excludes absorption by fast
electrons and ions, as well as electron energy transfer from non-wave
processes. The mode-resolved quantity is not a Fourier coefficient of the
spatially varying deposition field or a volume-integrated power.

For a complete modal decomposition, summing the contributions over mode
numbers gives the mode-summed coherent-wave absorbed power density for bulk
thermal electrons. This is one recipient-population component of the [total
absorbed wave power density per toroidal
mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power_density), and
contributes to the broader [thermal-electron power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), which can include non-wave
energy transfers. Integrating one mode's density over a physical volume
gives the corresponding [thermal-electron absorbed wave power per toroidal
mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.leaf_definition: Flux surface averaged absorbed wave power density on the thermal species, per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power density on the thermal species, per toroidal mode number

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave power absorbed by bulk thermal ions of a
selected species and charge state, or a selected bundle of charge states. It
is represented as a local value or as an average over a magnetic flux
surface.
NAMES.long:
Thermal ion charge-state power density is the volumetric rate of
coherent-wave power absorbed by bulk thermal ions associated with a selected
ion species and charge state, or a selected bundle of charge states. It can
be expressed as a local value or as an average over a magnetic flux surface.

The local absorbed-power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{th},a} = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{abs,th},a}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},a}$ is the thermal ion charge-state power density,
$P_{\mathrm{abs,th},a}$ is the coherent-wave power absorbed by the selected
thermal-ion population, $V$ is physical volume, the subscript $\mathrm{th}$
identifies the bulk thermal-ion population, and $a$ identifies the selected
species and charge state or charge-state bundle.

The recipient population is bulk thermal ions of the selected species. For a
charge-state bundle, the value is summed over its constituent charge states;
it is not summed over other charge states or species. The local value
resolves spatial deposition, while the flux-surface-averaged value averages
that deposition over a magnetic flux surface without changing the recipient
population or energy-transfer channel.

This quantity excludes absorption by nonthermal fast ions, described by
[fast-ion charge-state power
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density). It is the coherent-wave
absorption contribution to [ion charge-state power
density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), which is the net
energy-transfer rate across the included processes. Collisional energy
transfer to thermal ions is distinct from wave absorption and is described
by [thermal-ion charge-state power density due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The [toroidal-mode-resolved
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density)
resolves this deposition by toroidal Fourier harmonic. Integrating the
flux-surface-averaged density over the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux
surface gives the [thermal ion charge-state power at the enclosed flux
surface](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave
energy absorption by thermal ions of a specified species and charge state,
resolved by toroidal Fourier mode number.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal-mode-resolved thermal-ion charge-state power density is the
flux-surface-averaged rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves transfer
energy directly to thermal ions of a specified species and charge state per
unit physical volume. Each contribution corresponds to one toroidal Fourier
harmonic.

For a magnetic flux surface, the mode-resolved deposition is defined by

$$
p_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)} = \left\langle Q_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the flux-surface-averaged modal power density,
$Q_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the corresponding local volumetric rate of wave
energy transfer to thermal ions, $a$ identifies the ion species, $z$
identifies its charge state, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode
number, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes averaging over that
magnetic flux surface.

The recipient population is restricted to bulk thermal ions of the selected
species and charge state; neither charge states nor toroidal modes are
summed. This quantity describes direct wave absorption, not subsequent
collisional energy redistribution, a local deposition value before
flux-surface averaging, or volume-integrated absorbed power. The [fast-ion
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density)
instead describes absorption by nonthermal ions.

Summing over all included toroidal harmonics recovers the flux-surface
average of [thermal-ion charge-state power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density), not its unaveraged
local value.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_pellet_path
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Background-plasma electron temperature evaluated locally along the pellet’s
ablation trajectory, describing the thermal state encountered by the pellet
during transit.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local energy-equivalent temperature of background plasma
electrons at positions along the pellet trajectory. It describes the plasma
encountered by the pellet, not the thermal state of pellet material or an
average over the entire trajectory.

For an isotropic electron population, the energy-equivalent temperature is
defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_e\rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature expressed as an energy, and $\langle
E_e\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron.

The quantity applies only to background electrons and is evaluated locally
along the pellet path; it is not charge-state aggregated, path-averaged, or
a pellet ablation rate. The corresponding [electron density at the pellet
path](name:electron_density_at_pellet_path) describes the local
free-electron population at the same trajectory locations, while this
quantity specifies its thermal energy state.

sources.leaf_definition: Electron temperature along the pellet path
sources.parent_definition: 1-D profiles of plasma and pellet along the pellet path

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Helium-3 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed
over all helium-3 ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Helium-3 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local volumetric abundance of helium-3 ions, including all ionization
states. It applies to the helium-3 ion population at the core-side shoulder
of the H-mode edge transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{^3\mathrm{He}} = \sum_z n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the local helium-3 ion number density,
$n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of helium-3 ions in
charge state $z$, and $z$ is the positive integer ion charge state.

This quantity is evaluated locally at the pedestal top defined by the
[normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). The sum
includes all helium-3 ion charge states and excludes neutral helium-3; the
quantity is neither a flux-surface average nor a volume average. It is the
helium-3 species component of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), whereas [helium-3 density at the
limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter) refers to a different spatial
locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_tungsten_density
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Line-of-sight average of the number density of positively charged tungsten
ions, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the line-of-sight average of the charge-state-summed number
density of positively charged tungsten ions.

$$
\bar n_{\mathrm{W}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{L}} \left[\sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)\right] \, dl
$$

Here, $\bar n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the line-averaged tungsten-ion number
density, $\mathcal{L}$ is the specified averaging line, $L$ is its total
length, $l$ is distance along that line, $Z$ is the positive tungsten
charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)$ is the local number density
of tungsten ions in charge state $Z$. The sum includes all positive tungsten
ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

The quantity applies to the aggregate tungsten-ion population along the
specified line and is averaged over that line rather than evaluated locally
or averaged over volume. It therefore differs from the local or otherwise
spatially averaged [tungsten-ion density](name:tungsten_density) by its
line-of-sight aggregation, and from [volume-averaged tungsten
density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density) by using a line rather than
the enclosed plasma volume.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive
NAMES.short:
Vector electric-current-density contribution generated by neoclassical
bootstrap drive associated with plasma pressure and density gradients.
NAMES.long:
Current density due to bootstrap current drive is the vector contribution to
electric current density generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive
associated with plasma pressure and density gradients. It represents
conventional electric-current flow produced by this drive mechanism, before
selecting any particular component or projection.

The quantity is scoped to the bootstrap-driven contribution only. It
excludes current-density contributions from externally driven current,
inductive electric fields, neutral beams, radio-frequency waves, or any
total current density that aggregates multiple drive mechanisms.

This parent quantity denotes the full vector bootstrap-current-density
contribution. Component or projection quantities are more specific
descendants; for example,
[parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive)
is the field-aligned projection of this vector along the magnetic-field
direction, not a synonym for the full vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component represents conventional
current flowing in the positive direction of that component or projection.

NAMES.name: current_due_to_fusion_reactions
NAMES.short:
Net parallel plasma current generated by fusion reactions, associated with
fast alpha particles produced by deuterium–tritium reactions and distinct
from other non-inductive current-drive mechanisms.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net plasma current attributable to fusion reactions
within the plasma, associated with fast alpha particles produced by
deuterium–tritium reactions. It represents the parallel current contribution
rather than the total plasma current.

The defining relation is

$$
I_{\mathrm{fus}} = \int_S \mathbf{j}_{\alpha} \cdot \mathbf{b}\, dS
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{fus}}$ is the fusion-reaction-driven current,
$\mathbf{j}_{\alpha}$ is the current-density vector carried by the
fusion-born fast-alpha population, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector in the
local magnetic-field direction, and $S$ is the cross-sectional surface
through which the parallel current is evaluated; $dS$ is an element of that
surface.

The quantity is a net signed aggregation over the fusion-born alpha
population and the relevant plasma cross section. It includes only the
current attributable to fusion reactions and is not a local current density,
a current magnitude, or an all-population current.

It excludes current contributions driven by other mechanisms and must not be
interpreted as the total plasma current or the total non-inductive current.
It is an additive contribution to the non-inductive current balance.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the fusion-reaction-driven conventional
current is parallel to the local magnetic-field direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by this fusion reactions

NAMES.name: absorbed_radiated_power_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Net photon power deposited on one divertor target surface after subtracting
radiative power reflected from that surface.
NAMES.long:
Absorbed radiated power at a divertor target is the net photon-energy rate
deposited on one specified target surface. It includes incident radiative
energy absorbed by the target and excludes the reflected portion.

The net absorbed radiative power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}} = P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}} - P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}}$ is the absorbed radiated power,
$P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}}$ is the incident radiative power reaching the target,
and $P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}$ is the radiative power reflected from the target.

This quantity applies to one divertor target and excludes conductive,
convective, charged-particle, and other nonradiative deposition channels.
Summation over all divertor targets gives power of the divertor due to
radiation; the broader radiative deposition concept is described by power
due to radiation.

sources.leaf_definition: Net radiated power on this divertor target (incident - reflected)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: absorbed_radiated_power_of_divertor
NAMES.short:
Net radiative power retained by all divertor targets, obtained by
subtracting reflected radiation from incident radiation and summing over the
targets.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net radiative power absorbed by the complete set of
divertor target surfaces during plasma–wall interaction. It represents
incident radiation retained by the targets, rather than radiation that is
merely incident or reflected.

For target surfaces indexed by $k$, the net absorbed radiative power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}} = \sum_{k=1}^{N_t} \left(P_{\mathrm{inc,rad},k} - P_{\mathrm{refl,rad},k}\right)
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}}$ is the total absorbed radiative power, $N_t$ is
the number of divertor target surfaces, $P_{\mathrm{inc,rad},k}$ is the
radiative power incident on target $k$, and $P_{\mathrm{refl,rad},k}$ is the
radiative power reflected from target $k$.

The quantity is aggregated over all divertor targets and includes only the
radiative contribution. It excludes nonradiative particle and conductive
power included in [total incident power of the
divertor](name:total_incident_power_of_divertor), and it is distinct from
[thermal radiative power of the
divertor](name:thermal_radiative_power_of_divertor), which describes
radiation emitted by the target surfaces. The corresponding per-target
quantity is [absorbed radiated power at divertor
target](name:absorbed_radiated_power_at_divertor_target).

sources.leaf_definition: Net radiated power on the divertor targets (incident - reflected) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: current_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Net conventional electric current delivered by the plasma to one divertor
target surface is integrated over the wetted strike zone. Ion and electron
contributions are combined with their electric-charge signs, so this is not
an unsigned particle flux.
NAMES.long:
Net conventional electric current delivered by the plasma to one divertor
target surface is the signed charge-flow rate crossing the plasma-facing
target interface, integrated over the wetted strike zone. It represents the
net incident conventional current carried by charged plasma particles to
that target.

The target current is defined by the surface integral of incident
conventional-current density over the wetted target region:

$$
I_{\mathrm{target}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{wet}}} \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{target}} \, dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the current at the divertor target,
$S_{\mathrm{wet}}$ is the wetted strike-zone part of the target surface,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident conventional electric-current
density due to plasma particles at the target surface,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the unit normal directed from the
plasma into the target material, and $dA$ is the surface area element. For
multiple charged species, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the charge-weighted
sum of their incident particle flux densities, so ion and electron
contributions enter with opposite electric-charge signs.

The scope is one physical divertor target surface; the aggregation
convention is the surface integral over the wetted strike-zone region of
that target. It excludes neighboring targets, non-target plasma-facing
components, and return currents in external conducting structures. It is a
net conventional current, not an ion-only current, an electron-only current,
an unsigned collected-current magnitude, or a particle flux.

Summing this quantity over the target surfaces belonging to a divertor gives
the target-current contribution to [current of
divertor](name:current_of_divertor). If a target is partitioned into tiles,
summing [current of divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile) over the
tiles that cover the same wetted target region gives this per-target
quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net conventional current carried by
charged plasma particles is directed from the plasma into the divertor
target material.

sources.leaf_definition: Total current incident on this target
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: current_of_divertor
NAMES.short:
Net conventional electric current carried by charged particles into all
divertor target surfaces, including signed electron and ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
The total divertor current is the algebraic conventional current delivered
by charged particles crossing the plasma-facing surfaces of the complete
divertor assembly. It includes ion and electron contributions and excludes
neutral-particle flux and displacement current.

The current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the total current in A, $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is
the union of divertor target surfaces, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is
conventional charged-particle current density in A m$^{-2}$, $q_s$ is the
signed charge of species $s$ in C, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is its particle
flux density in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ points from the
plasma toward the material.

This assembly-integrated quantity differs from [current at a divertor
target](name:current_at_divertor_target), which applies to one target, and
[current of a divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile), which applies
to an individual tile.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional charged-particle current flows
from the plasma into the divertor material.

sources.leaf_definition: Total current incident on this divertor
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: current_of_divertor_tile
NAMES.short:
Conventional electric current of a divertor tile is the net signed charge
current crossing the electrostatic sheath from the plasma onto the
plasma-facing surface of one individual divertor tile.
NAMES.long:
Conventional electric current of a divertor tile is the net signed charge
current crossing the electrostatic sheath from the plasma onto the
plasma-facing surface of one individual divertor tile. It is a tile-level
incident sheath current, expressed using the direction of conventional
electric current rather than electron particle flow.

The current is the sheath-normal surface integral of the conventional
electric current density over the tile surface:

$$
I_\mathrm{tile} = \int_{S_\mathrm{tile}} \mathbf{j} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{tile}} \, dS
$$

where $I_\mathrm{tile}$ is the conventional electric current of the divertor
tile, $S_\mathrm{tile}$ is the plasma-facing surface of that tile,
$\mathbf{j}$ is the conventional electric current density,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{tile}}$ is the surface normal
directed from the plasma toward the tile, and $dS$ is the surface-area
element.

The scope is one individual divertor tile and the aggregation is the net
charge-weighted contribution of all charged species crossing the sheath onto
that tile surface. It is not the current of a complete divertor target, not
the current of an entire divertor, and not an electrical-conduction current
in supports or external circuitry after charge has entered the solid.

The [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target) is
obtained by summing this quantity over the divertor tiles that constitute
that target. The [current of a divertor](name:current_of_divertor) is
obtained by summing the corresponding tile or target contributions over the
divertor.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional electric current crosses the
electrostatic sheath from the plasma toward the plasma-facing surface of the
divertor tile.

sources.leaf_definition: Total current incident on this tile
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor tiles belonging to this target

NAMES.name: density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Local number density of a specified plasma species or species group
immediately upstream of a divertor-target sheath, with ion charge states
summed and neutral populations excluded unless explicitly named.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local particle count per volume for a selected plasma
species or species group at the plasma-facing side of a divertor target. It
is evaluated immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath, rather than
in the target material or as a quantity integrated over a target surface.

For a selected set of constituent populations, the number density is defined
by:

$$
n_S = \sum_{s \in S} n_s
$$

where $n_S$ is the number density of the selected species or species group,
$S$ is the set of included constituent populations, and $n_s$ is the number
density of constituent population $s$.

The selected population can be free electrons, one ion species, or a named
group of ion species such as deuterium and tritium. For an ion species, $S$
contains its positive atomic charge states and the sum is an unweighted
particle-count sum; for a compound fuel group, it contains the included
isotope ions. Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded unless explicitly
named as part of $S$. The quantity is local to the plasma immediately
upstream of one divertor-target sheath and is neither a target-surface
integral nor an aggregation over multiple targets.

Species-specific instances refine this common definition, including
[electron density at the divertor
target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), [boron density at the
divertor target](name:boron_density_at_divertor_target), and
[deuterium-tritium density at the divertor
target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target). In contrast,
[total ion number density at the plasma
boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) sums all charged ion
species at a plasma boundary, making it broader in species scope and
distinct in locus.

NAMES.name: argon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Number density of argon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over positive ionization
states and excluding neutral argon.
NAMES.long:
Number density of argon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the argon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed argon number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total argon-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the local number density of argon ions with
positive charge state $q$, and $q$ is the integer argon charge-state index.

This quantity applies to the argon-ion population immediately upstream of
the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target and is summed over all
positive argon charge states from singly ionized through fully stripped
argon. Neutral argon atoms and other neutral argon forms are excluded, as
are electrons and ions of other elements.

This is a local species density rather than a density integrated over the
target surface or summed over all plasma species. The corresponding argon
quantity at a limiter, [argon density at the
limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter), has the same charge-state
aggregation but a different evaluation locus; unlike [electron density at
the divertor target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), this
quantity describes argon ions rather than free electrons.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Number density of beryllium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over all positive ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of beryllium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the beryllium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local beryllium-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Be}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the number of beryllium ions in the volume, and $V$ is
a small plasma volume centered at the sheath entrance.

This quantity applies to the ionized beryllium population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target and is summed over all positive beryllium
ionization states, with each ion counted once regardless of charge state.
Neutral beryllium atoms are excluded; the quantity is a local number
density, not an areal particle flux, integrated inventory, or charge
density.

Compared with [beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density), this quantity
specifies the divertor-target sheath-entrance locus. It is distinct from
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target),
which counts free electrons rather than beryllium ions.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Boron density at the divertor target is the local number density of boron
ions immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath at the target-facing
plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Boron density at the divertor target is the local number density of boron
ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to the divertor target surface,
evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the
boron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed boron ion density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}} = \sum_{q=1}^{5} n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron ion number density and
$n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the number density of boron ions with positive
charge state $q$.

This quantity applies to the boron-ion population immediately upstream of
the sheath at a divertor target and aggregates all positive boron ionization
states, from singly ionized through fully stripped boron. Each boron ion is
counted once; neutral boron atoms are excluded.

Relative to the parent
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), this quantity
selects boron ions rather than an unspecified species or species group. It
is parallel to
[beryllium_density_at_divertor_target](name:beryllium_density_at_divertor_target),
differing in the selected ion species and its allowed charge states.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Number density of the carbon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for carbon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the carbon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the carbon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local carbon-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{C}^{+}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}$ is the carbon-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}$ is the number of carbon ions in all positive ionization
states, and $V$ is a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath
entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to carbon ions immediately upstream of the
electrostatic sheath at a divertor target and is summed over all positive
carbon ionization states, from singly ionized through fully stripped carbon.
Neutral carbon atoms, carbon-bearing neutral molecules, electrons, and ions
of other elements are excluded.

Unlike [carbon_density](name:carbon_density), which has the broader
elemental-carbon scope including neutral carbon, this quantity is restricted
to the charge-state-summed positive-ion population at the divertor target.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current
NAMES.short:
Deposited power at a divertor target due to halo current is the electrical
work rate delivered to one divertor target by halo current crossing its
plasma-facing surface.
NAMES.long:
Deposited power at a divertor target due to halo current is the electrical
work rate delivered to one divertor target by halo current crossing the
plasma-facing target surface. Halo current is current in the edge or
scrape-off-layer plasma that closes through conducting plasma-facing
structures; this quantity selects only its contribution to current-driven
target loading.

For a target surface with defined local current density and potential drop,
the target-surface definition is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{halo},t} = \int_{A_t} j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}(\mathbf{r})\,\Delta\Phi_t(\mathbf{r})\,dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{halo},t}$ is this deposited power, $A_t$ is the portion of
the plasma-facing target surface intercepted by halo current, $dA$ is a
target-surface area element, $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the
conventional halo-current density projected on the local unit normal
directed from the plasma into the target material, and $\Delta\Phi_t =
\Phi_{\mathrm{plasma}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the local
plasma-to-target potential drop.

The surface integral of $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ over $A_t$ is
the halo-current contribution to [current at divertor
target](name:current_at_divertor_target). This quantity excludes the
conductive, convective, radiative, and neutral-particle target-power
channels, and excludes current-driven target power not produced by halo
current; together with other current-driven components it is part of [power
at divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target), while sums over divertor
targets contribute to power of divertor. It is zero when no halo-current
electrical work is deposited on the target; positive values denote net
energy deposition on that target.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional halo current crosses from the
plasma into the target along the plasma-to-material surface normal across a
positive plasma-to-target potential drop.

sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on this divertor target due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Number density of deuterium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of deuterium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the deuterium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local deuterium number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_D = \frac{dN_D}{dV}
$$

where $N_D$ is the number of deuterium ions in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the deuterium-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and is summed over all positive atomic deuterium
ionization states, counting each ion once regardless of charge state.
Neutral deuterium atoms and molecules, electrons, and ions of other species
are excluded.

Unlike
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
which includes both fuel-ion species, this quantity contains deuterium ions
only. It is the divertor-target-localized counterpart of
[deuterium_density](name:deuterium_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species at
the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the
plasma-side sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species at the
divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath
entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is
the deuterium-tritium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local deuterium-tritium number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{DT} = \frac{dN_{DT}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{DT}$ is the number of particles represented by the effective
deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, and $V$ is a small plasma volume
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the ion population represented as one effective
deuterium-tritium fuel species, rather than to separately resolved deuterium
and tritium populations. It includes the positive ionic states represented
by that pseudo-species and excludes neutral deuterium-tritium atoms or
molecules, electrons, and other ion species.

The localized quantity is the divertor-target counterpart of
[deuterium_tritium_density](name:deuterium_tritium_density). Unlike
[deuterium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_density_at_divertor_target)
and
[tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
which describe the separately resolved isotope populations, this quantity
uses the prescribed effective deuterium-tritium pseudo-species.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: effective_charge_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Effective ionic charge of the plasma immediately upstream of a
divertor-target sheath, combining all positive ion species through charge
moments.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge at a divertor target is the local charge-squared-weighted
ionic content of the plasma adjacent to the target, evaluated at the sheath
entrance. It characterizes impurity content relative to the total positive
charge density.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{\sum_i n_i Z_i}
$$

where $n_i$ is the local number density of positive-ion species $i$ and
$Z_i$ is its positive integer charge state. The sums include all positive
ion species and charge states represented in the local plasma. The quantity
equals unity for a pure singly charged hydrogenic plasma and increases when
higher-charge ions contribute.

This effective-charge interpretation is the charge-moment form of charge at
the divertor target, with the same target-local plasma scope; it is not a
density or a charge-state-specific abundance.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Effective charge

NAMES.name: electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Rate at which incident electron energy is deposited on the high-field-side
inner divertor target, integrated over its wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Electron power at the inner divertor target is the rate at which energy
carried by incident electrons is deposited on the high-field-side divertor
target surface. It is the electron-channel contribution to the total target
load, rather than the combined contribution of all incident energy channels.

The deposited electron power is defined by the surface integral

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{inner}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}} q_{e,\mathrm{dep}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}$ is the wetted inner-target area,
$q_{e,\mathrm{dep}}$ is the electron energy-deposition flux density in W
m$^{-2}$, and $dA$ is an element of target surface area in m$^2$. The result
