is the electron contribution to power at the inner divertor target; ion
energy is represented separately by ion power at the inner divertor target,
while neutral and radiative contributions are excluded.

sources.leaf_definition: Electron power on the inner target
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to electrons

NAMES.name: electron_power_at_outer_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons,
integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons
integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface is the target-integrated
electron energy-transfer rate to the material surface of that target. The
outer divertor target is the target on the larger-major-radius side in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The deposited electron power is the surface integral of the local electron
energy-flux density directed into the wetted outer-target area:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{outer}} = \int_{A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}} q_{e,\perp}\,dA
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the electron power at the outer divertor
target, $A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the wetted strike-zone area, $dA$ is a
target-surface area element, and $q_{e,\perp}$ is the electron energy-flux
density directed from the plasma into the target material.

This is the electron-channel component of power at the outer divertor
target; ion, neutral, radiation, and other non-electron contributions are
excluded. It is the outer-target counterpart of [electron power at the inner
divertor target](name:electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target).

sources.leaf_definition: Electron power on the inner target
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to electrons

NAMES.name: flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Flux at a divertor target is the local scalar surface density of power
deposited on a divertor target surface, independent of how the incident
energy carriers are decomposed.
NAMES.long:
Flux at a divertor target is the local scalar surface density of power
deposited on a divertor target surface. It represents the target-surface
load itself, without assigning that load to a particular carrier species,
radiation component, or transport mechanism.

The target-surface flux is defined as the surface-area density of deposited
power:

$$
F_{\mathrm{t}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{dep}}}{dA_{\mathrm{t}}}
$$

where $F_{\mathrm{t}}$ is the flux at surface point $\mathbf{x}$,
$P_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the power deposited into the divertor target material,
and $A_{\mathrm{t}}$ is area on the divertor target surface.

This name is an umbrella for scalar divertor-target deposited-flux
quantities; the explicit energy-load specialization is [energy flux at
divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target). It excludes upstream
fluxes, volume power densities, and signed vector flux components.
Channel-resolved contributions are distinct quantities unless a more
specific standard name states that decomposition.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Local rate of energy deposition per unit divertor-target area, combining all
incident particle and radiative energy-carrying channels.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at a divertor target is the local surface density of power
deposited by incident plasma and radiative energy carriers on the
target-facing surface. It describes the energy load at each surface location
rather than power integrated over a target or divertor assembly.

The local energy flux is defined by

$$
q_E(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{\mathrm{d}P_E}{\mathrm{d}A}
$$

where $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ is the deposited energy flux at surface position
$\mathbf{x}$, $P_E$ is the cumulative deposited power from all included
incident energy carriers, and $A$ is target-surface area.

The quantity applies to one divertor target surface and combines the
contributions of incident particle and radiative energy channels. It does
not resolve separate electron, ion, conductive, convective,
neutral-particle, or radiative contributions, and it is not a
target-integrated power.

This quantity is the energy-deposition component represented by [flux at a
divertor target](name:flux_at_divertor_target); the latter provides the
carrier-independent target-surface load. The corresponding surface maximum,
[maximum of energy flux at a divertor
target](name:energy_flux_maximum_at_divertor_target), is obtained by
selecting the largest value of $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ over the target surface.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over positive ionization states and
excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the helium-3-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local helium-3 number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_3 = \frac{dN_3}{dV}
$$

where $n_3$ is the helium-3 ion number density, $N_3$ is the number of
helium-3 ions in a small plasma volume, and $V$ is that plasma volume. The
count $N_3$ includes singly ionized and fully stripped helium-3 ions.

This quantity applies to the helium-3 ion population immediately upstream of
the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target. It is summed over the
positive ionization states of helium-3, excludes neutral helium-3 atoms, and
excludes electrons and all other ion species.

Unlike
[helium_4_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_4_density_at_divertor_target),
this quantity describes the isotope with three nucleons. Unlike
[helium_3_density_at_limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter), it is
evaluated at a divertor target rather than at a limiter surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over singly and doubly
ionized states and excluding neutral helium-4.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the helium-4-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The helium-4 ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{He4}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the number of helium-4 ions, and $V$ is a small plasma
volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the ionized helium-4 population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target and is summed over the singly and doubly
ionized charge states, with each ion counted once. Neutral helium-4 atoms
are excluded, so this quantity is not the total helium-4 particle density
including neutrals or a charge density.

As a species-specific specialization, this quantity contributes to the
broader [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) family
without including other ion species. The isotope distinction from
[helium_3_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_3_density_at_divertor_target)
is maintained; the two quantities describe different helium isotopes.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons (4He)

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of the hydrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for hydrogen ions at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive charge states and excluding neutral hydrogen atoms and
molecules.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the hydrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the hydrogen-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local hydrogen-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{H}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the number of free hydrogen ions in a small plasma
volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side
at the divertor target, and $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the corresponding local
hydrogen-ion number density.

This quantity applies to the free hydrogen-ion population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target. It is summed over all positive hydrogen
ionization charge states, counting each ion once without charge weighting;
neutral hydrogen atoms and molecules, electrons, and other ion species are
excluded.

As a species-specific local component, it uses the same sheath-entrance
locus and charge-state-summed convention as [deuterium density at the
divertor target](name:deuterium_density_at_divertor_target), but represents
hydrogen ions rather than deuterium ions. Unlike the flux-surface-averaged
hydrogen density at the plasma boundary, it is evaluated locally at the
divertor target rather than averaged over a flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: ion_fluence_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Cumulative incident ion-particle dose delivered to a divertor target, with
each ion counted once across all species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Ion fluence at a divertor target is the cumulative number of incident ions
per unit target area over a specified time interval. It is the ion-only
component of fluence at the divertor target, including all ionic species and
charge states while counting each incident ion once.

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \left[\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}} \Gamma_{\perp,s}(t)\right] \, dt
$$

Here, $\Phi_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the ion fluence, $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the
interval endpoints in seconds, $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included ion
species and charge states, and $\Gamma_{\perp,s}$ is the incident normal
particle-flux density for state $s$, in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$. The flux is
directed from the plasma toward the target surface. Neutral atoms,
molecules, and nonparticle channels are excluded.

sources.leaf_definition: Positive charge fluence normal to an ideal axisymmetric surface of the divertor (assuming no shaping), estimated at the probe location.
sources.parent_definition: Set of embedded (in a plasma facing component) probes

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Number density of the iron species at the divertor target is the particle
count per volume for iron ions at the sheath entrance immediately upstream
of the target-facing plasma boundary. Positive charge states are summed;
neutral iron is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the iron species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the iron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local iron-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density, $\mathrm{Fe}$
denotes iron, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of free iron ions, and $V$ is
a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the
plasma side.

This quantity applies to the free iron-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and is summed over all positive iron charge states,
counting each iron ion once without charge-state weighting. Neutral iron
atoms, electrons, other ion species, and charge density are excluded.

It is a species-resolved component of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), whereas
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target)
describes the free-electron population and
[carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target)
applies the same target-locus and charge-state-summed convention to carbon
ions.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Number density of the krypton species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for krypton ions at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive ionization states and excluding neutral krypton atoms.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the krypton species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for krypton ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
krypton-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local krypton-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Kr}}$
is the number of krypton ions, and $V$ is the local plasma volume.

This quantity applies to the krypton-ion population immediately adjacent to
a divertor target, evaluated at the plasma-side entrance to the
electrostatic sheath. It is summed over all positive krypton ionization
states, counting each ion once; neutral krypton atoms, electrons, and ions
of other species are excluded.

As a species-specific target-locus quantity, it specializes the broader
[krypton_density](name:krypton_density) by restricting the evaluation point
to the divertor target. Its locus and charge-state aggregation follow the
corresponding
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
while the species is krypton rather than neon.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the lithium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for ionized lithium at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive ionization states and excluding neutral lithium.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the lithium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for ionized lithium at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
lithium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local lithium-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of ionized lithium ions in the local
plasma volume $V$, with the count summed over all positive lithium
ionization states.

This quantity applies to the ionized lithium population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and uses a charge-state-summed aggregation. Neutral
lithium atoms, electrons, and ions of other elements are excluded.

Unlike [lithium_density_at_limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which
is evaluated at a limiter, this quantity is evaluated at the divertor-target
sheath entrance. It therefore represents the divertor-target member of the
lithium-density family rather than a limiter or general plasma-boundary
value.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Number density of neon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over Ne1+ through Ne10+ and
excluding neutral neon.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the neon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local neon-ion number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{q=1}^{10} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the number of neon ions in charge state $q+$
within the local plasma volume $V$, $V$ is the local plasma volume, and $q$
is the positive integer neon charge-state number. The upper limit 10 denotes
fully stripped neon.

This quantity applies to the free neon-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target on the plasma side of the electrostatic sheath. It is
summed over all positive neon charge states from Ne1+ through Ne10+,
counting each ion once; neutral neon atoms are excluded. It is not the
density of all ion species or the free-electron population represented by
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target).

This member specializes
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) by selecting
neon ions while retaining the same target-sheath evaluation locus. It is the
species-specific counterpart of related quantities such as
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: neutral_power_of_divertor
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral power of divertor is the total rate of neutral-particle energy
deposited on wetted plasma-facing surfaces throughout the divertor assembly.
NAMES.long:
Neutral power of divertor is the total rate of neutral-particle energy
deposited on the wetted plasma-facing surfaces of the divertor assembly. It
sums neutral-particle deposition over all included divertor targets and
other divertor plasma-facing components.

The defining surface integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{neu,div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} q_{\mathrm{neu}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of the included wetted divertor
surfaces, $q_{\mathrm{neu}}$ is the neutral-particle deposited energy-flux
density on those surfaces, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is the surface-area element.
The neutral contribution includes charge-exchange neutrals and other
neutral-particle impact channels.

This quantity is the neutral-channel component of power_of_divertor. Unlike
[neutral_power_at_divertor_target](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target),
it aggregates deposition over the divertor assembly rather than one target.
Energy carried by neutral particles that does not reach an included divertor
surface, and deposition from charged-particle, radiative, or other
non-neutral channels, is excluded.

sources.leaf_definition: Net power from neutrals on the divertor targets (positive means power is deposited on the target) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
nitrogen-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local nitrogen-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_N = \frac{dN_N}{dV}
$$

where $N_N$ is the number of nitrogen ions in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the nitrogen-ion population immediately adjacent to
the divertor target and is summed over all positive nitrogen ionization
states. The aggregation counts each nitrogen ion once, regardless of its
charge state.

Neutral nitrogen atoms are excluded, as are nitrogen-bearing particles that
are not represented as nitrogen ions. This quantity is distinct from
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target),
which counts free electrons, and from
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
which applies the same target-local density definition to neon ions.

As a species-specific component, this quantity is one member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target); the parent
represents the same target-local number-density concept for a specified
species or species group.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor
NAMES.short:
Nuclear energy deposition rate integrated throughout the material volume of
one divertor structure, including neutron and other nuclear heating sources.
NAMES.long:
Nuclear heating power of a divertor is the rate at which nuclear
interactions deposit energy throughout the material volume of that divertor
structure.

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{div}}} q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the nuclear heating power,
$q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local volumetric nuclear
energy-deposition rate at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the
material volume of the divertor, and $dV$ is the differential volume
element.

The quantity applies to one indexed divertor structure and aggregates
neutron and all other included nuclear heating sources over its complete
material volume. It excludes energy deposited by nonnuclear convective
transport, such as [power of a divertor due to
convection](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection), and is distinct from
surface power deposited at an individual target, such as [neutral power at a
divertor target](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target).

sources.leaf_definition: Nuclear power heating the divertor
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for oxygen ions at the sheath entrance, summed
over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the oxygen-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local oxygen-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\rm O} = \frac{dN_{\rm O}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\rm O}$ is the total number of oxygen ions in a small plasma
volume $V$ centered at the sheath entrance on the plasma side of the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the oxygen-ion population at the specified divertor
target and sums the number densities of all positive oxygen ionization
states, counting each ion once. Neutral oxygen atoms are excluded;
therefore, it is distinct from [oxygen_density](name:oxygen_density), which
includes neutral oxygen as well as charged oxygen states.

The target-specific quantity has the same charge-state-summed convention as
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
while
[oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary)
represents the corresponding oxygen-ion density at the plasma boundary
without this divertor-target locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: power_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one
divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over
the target's wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one
divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over
the target's wetted strike-zone surface. The specified channel denotes a
particular physical contribution to deposition and does not by itself imply
an all-channel target total.

The deposited power for target $t$ and channel $c$ is defined from the
channel-resolved energy-flux-density vector over that surface:

$$
P_{t,c} = -\int_{A_t} \mathbf{S}_{E,c}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_t(\mathbf{x}) \, dA
$$

where $P_{t,c}$ is the deposited power on target $t$ due to channel $c$,
$A_t$ is the target's wetted strike-zone surface, $\mathbf{S}_{E,c}$ is the
energy-flux-density vector for channel $c$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_t$ is the
normalized surface normal directed from the target material toward the
plasma-facing side, $\mathbf{x}$ labels a point on the target surface, and
$dA$ is the surface element. The leading minus sign makes flux directed from
the plasma toward the target material contribute to the deposited target
power.

The channel label may distinguish conductive, convective, particle,
radiative, or other deposition mechanisms, but this name does not prescribe
a decomposition. For a complete mutually exclusive set of channel
contributions on the same target, the channel sum equals the surface
integral of the total [energy flux at a divertor
target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target); all-channel target powers at
the inner and outer divertor targets are represented by power at inner
divertor target and power at outer divertor target. Conductive and
convective channel contributions are represented by [power at divertor
target due to conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction)
and [power at divertor target due to
convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), respectively.

sources.leaf_definition: Total power incident on this target. This power is split in the various physical categories listed below
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: neutral_power_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Net rate of energy deposited on one divertor target by incident neutral
particles, including charge-exchange neutrals and neutral products of volume
recombination.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-particle target power is the rate at which neutral atoms or
molecules transfer energy to one specified divertor target through
bombardment from the plasma. It includes neutrals formed by charge exchange
and volume recombination, and is distinct from the charged-particle target
power [power at divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target).

$$
P_{\mathrm{n,t}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{t}}} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{net}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p\to t}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{n,t}}$ is the deposited neutral-particle power,
$A_{\mathrm{t}}$ is the surface area of the specified target,
$\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net neutral energy-flux
vector crossing that surface, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p\to t}}$
points from the plasma toward the target material.

The quantity excludes charged-particle sheath power, radiative absorption,
and conductive power. Summing the corresponding contributions over all
wetted divertor surfaces gives [neutral power of
divertor](name:neutral_power_of_divertor); recombination-only contributions
are covered by [power at divertor target due to
recombination](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination).

sources.leaf_definition: Net power from neutrals on this divertor target (positive means power is deposited on the target)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: power_due_to_conduction
NAMES.short:
Thermal power deposited on one or more plasma-facing surfaces by electron
and ion conduction along scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines, excluding
convective, radiative, and neutral-particle power.
NAMES.long:
Conductive deposited power is thermal power transferred from
scrape-off-layer plasma to one or more plasma-facing surfaces by electron
and ion heat conduction along magnetic field lines. The selected surface may
be an individual target, a divertor assembly, or a collection of wall and
divertor surfaces.

The defining surface integral is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{cond}} = \int_S \left(\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the deposited power, $S$ is the selected
plasma-facing surface, $\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ and
$\mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ are the electron and ion
conductive heat-flux vectors, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed
from the plasma toward the material, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a surface-area
element.

The quantity excludes convective enthalpy, radiative absorption, and
neutral-particle bombardment. A single-target instance is represented by
[power at divertor target due to
conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction), while the
corresponding all-channel energy flux density is distinguished by [energy
flux at divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: power_due_to_convection
NAMES.short:
Power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces by convective plasma particle
flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by
streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Convective power quantifies the energy transported to a plasma-facing
surface by the bulk flow of plasma particles — ions, electrons, and neutral
species — streaming along open magnetic field lines from the scrape-off
layer to bounding material surfaces. It represents the convective channel of
the total surface power balance, distinct from the conductive contribution
driven by parallel temperature gradients and from radiative deposition.

The local convective heat-flux density summed over particle species $s$ is

$$
q_{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_s n_s v_{\parallel,s} \left( \frac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_s - 1} k_B T_s + \frac{1}{2} m_s v_{\parallel,s}^2 \right)
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density, $v_{\parallel,s}$ the parallel flow
speed, $\gamma_s$ the adiabatic index (5/3 for monatomic species), $T_s$ the
temperature, and $m_s$ the particle mass. Integrating $q_{\mathrm{conv}}$
over the wetted surface area yields the total convective power in watts.

In experiments the convective power is inferred from Langmuir-probe
measurements of particle flux and sheath-entrance temperature, or decomposed
from total calorimetric measurements by subtracting the conductive fraction
estimated via two-point model analysis. More specific realizations include
[power at a single divertor target due to
convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), [convective
power summed over all divertor
targets](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection), and [convective power at
the first wall](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). The full surface load
integrating all channels is characterized by
heat_flux_of_plasma_facing_component.

NAMES.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection
NAMES.short:
Power deposited on a single divertor target by convective plasma particle
flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by
streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Convective power at a single divertor target quantifies the energy
transported to that target by plasma particles streaming from the scrape-off
layer. It includes thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried into
the material surface and is the target-local contribution to [power due to
convection](name:power_due_to_convection).

The target-integrated convective power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{conv,target}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{target}}} \sum_s n_s v_{n,s} \left[ \frac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_s-1} k_B T_s + \frac{1}{2}m_s v_{n,s}^{2} \right] \, dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the wetted target surface, $n_s$ is the
number density of species $s$, $v_{n,s}$ is its flow speed normal to and
into the target, $\gamma_s$ is its adiabatic index, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's
constant, $T_s$ is its temperature, and $m_s$ is its particle mass. The
species sum includes the particle channels assigned to convective transport
and excludes conductive and radiative deposition.

This quantity applies to one target; summing corresponding target
contributions gives [convective power of the
divertor](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection).

sources.leaf_definition: Power convected by the plasma on this divertor target
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: power_due_to_fusion
NAMES.short:
Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified
plasma region or material component. It counts fusion-product energy where
it is deposited, not merely where it is released.
NAMES.long:
Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified
plasma region or material component is the rate at which energy whose
ultimate source is fuel-ion fusion reactions is transferred to matter within
that region or component. It is an extensive deposited-power quantity, so
energy is assigned to the place where it is deposited, which may differ from
the place where the fusion reaction occurred.

For a specified region or component $\Omega$, the quantity is defined by the
local fusion-origin deposition rate density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\Omega) = \int_{\Omega} q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local rate density of
energy deposited at position $\mathbf{x}$ by fusion products, fusion-neutron
interactions, and secondary nuclear radiation, and $dV$ is the volume
element of $\Omega$.

Each reaction channel contributes according to the partition of its released
energy among products. For the deuterium-tritium channel, approximately one
fifth of the fusion energy is born in the alpha particle and four fifths in
the neutron; this birth partition does not imply local deposition.
Charged-product energy is included in a plasma region only for the fraction
actually deposited there during slowing down, while escaping charged
products or neutrons contribute where they subsequently deposit energy
through interactions and secondary radiation.

This name is distinct from [power density due to
fusion](name:power_density_due_to_fusion), which denotes local fusion energy
release rate before nonlocal transport, and from neutron power, which tracks
energy carried by neutrons rather than deposited energy in $\Omega$. Power
due to neutron interaction is the neutron-interaction contribution when the
interacting neutrons originate from fusion. The divertor specializations
[deposited power of divertor due to
fusion](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor) and [power of divertor due
to fusion](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor) restrict $\Omega$ to the
divertor; non-fusion heat loads such as conduction, plasma radiation,
charge-exchange neutrals, and externally supplied heating are excluded.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Power deposited on plasma-facing materials by recombination processes,
encompassing both plasma-ion recombination and surface recombination of
neutral atoms, without restriction to a particular surface location.
NAMES.long:
Recombination power is the heat load delivered to plasma-facing materials
when ions recover electrons and transition to neutral states, releasing
ionization potential energy and residual kinetic energy at or near material
surfaces. Two principal channels contribute: sheath-accelerated plasma-ion
recombination at target surfaces, and surface recombination of neutral atoms
into molecules, which deposits the molecular binding energy directly into
the wall or divertor plate material.

The integrated power from recombination events over a wetted area $A$ is:

$$P_\text{rec} = \sum_s \int_A \Gamma_s \, E_s \, dA$$

where $\Gamma_s$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ is the incident particle flux density for
species $s$ and $E_s$ [J] is the energy released per recombination event for
that species, including ionization potential and kinetic contributions.

This power channel is intrinsically non-negative and becomes particularly
significant in detached and partially detached divertor regimes, where
volumetric ion-electron recombination upstream of the strike point
redistributes energy deposition away from the target. Location-specific
realizations include [power deposited on a single divertor
target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), the [total over
the full divertor assembly](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination),
and power at first-wall surfaces. The neutral recombination particle flux
produced in these processes is characterized by
[neutral_energy_flux_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

NAMES.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Total power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes,
summing the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination channels at the
plasma-material interface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity captures the combined recombination power delivered to a
single divertor target, encompassing two physically distinct contributions:
energy released when plasma ions recombine at or near the target surface
(the plasma channel, quantified by
plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination) and energy deposited
when neutral particles undergo recombination into lower-energy bound states
at the material wall (the neutral channel, quantified by
[neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination)).

The total recombination power at the target decomposes additively:

$$
P_{\rm rec,target} = P_{\rm rec,plasma} + P_{\rm rec,neutral}
$$

where $P_{\rm rec,plasma}$ is the ion-recombination contribution and $P_{\rm
rec,neutral}$ is the neutral-particle recombination contribution, both in W.

This target-localized quantity is a spatial specialization of the
volume-integrated
[power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination), which
integrates recombination power over the full plasma domain. In attached
divertor operation, recombination power at the target is a minor fraction of
the total heat load; in detached or high-recycling regimes, surface and
volumetric recombination become significant energy sinks that reduce the
conducted and convected flux reaching the target. It is inferred from edge
plasma simulations or from particle flux measurements combined with surface
energy-release models, and is non-negative by definition.

NAMES.name: neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral-particle power deposited on a divertor target by recombination
processes at the plasma-material interface, excluding the plasma-ion
recombination channel.
NAMES.long:
This quantity captures the neutral-particle recombination power delivered to
a single divertor target, encompassing energy deposited when neutral
particles recombine into lower-energy bound states at the plasma-material
interface. Only the fraction of released binding, internal, and kinetic
energy accommodated by the target material contributes to this quantity.

The target-localized neutral recombination power is the inward surface
integral of the neutral-recombination energy-flux vector over the wetted
target area:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rec,n,target}} = \int_{\mathcal{A}_t} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{rec,n}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{mat}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{rec,n,target}}$ is the neutral-particle recombination
power at the target, $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{rec,n}}$ is the energy-flux vector
due only to neutral-particle recombination,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{mat}}$ is the unit normal to the target surface
directed into the material, and $\mathcal{A}_t$ is the target area receiving
that contribution.

This target-localized quantity is the neutral-particle channel of
[power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination),
distinct from
[plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination),
which describes recombination of plasma ions. It excludes conducted,
convected, radiative, charge-exchange, ionization, and plasma-ion
recombination heat loads. Summed over all divertor targets, it gives
[neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).

sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on this divertor target due to recombination of neutrals into a ground state (e.g. molecules)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Plasma-ion power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes
at the plasma-material interface, excluding the neutral-particle
recombination channel.
NAMES.long:
This quantity captures the plasma-ion recombination power delivered to a
single divertor target, representing energy deposited when plasma ions
recombine at or near the plasma-material interface. It excludes the
neutral-particle recombination channel quantified by [neutral-particle
recombination
power](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination).

The plasma-ion contribution is obtained from the total target recombination
power by subtracting the neutral-particle contribution:

$$
P_{\rm plasma,target} = P_{\rm rec,target} - P_{\rm neutral,target}
$$

where $P_{\rm plasma,target}$ is this plasma-ion recombination power,
$P_{\rm rec,target}$ is the [total recombination power at the divertor
target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), and $P_{\rm
neutral,target}$ is the neutral-particle contribution.

This is the single-target plasma-ion component of recombination power,
distinct from [total divertor recombination
power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which aggregates over
all divertor target surfaces and includes both plasma-ion and
neutral-particle channels.

sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on this divertor target due to recombination of plasma ions
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction
NAMES.short:
Thermal power deposited on all divertor targets by parallel electron and ion
heat conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines, excluding
convective, radiative, and neutral-particle channels.
NAMES.long:
The power of the divertor due to conduction is the total thermal energy
deposited on all divertor target surfaces by electron and ion heat
conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines. It excludes
convective particle enthalpy, absorbed radiation, recombination, and
neutral-particle contributions, and is the divertor-wide counterpart of
[power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction).

The total conductive power is defined by integrating the conductive
heat-flux vector over every wetted divertor target surface:

$$
P_{\mathrm{div,cond}} = \sum_k \int_{A_k} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_k\,dA
$$

where $A_k$ is the wetted surface of target $k$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_k$ points
from the plasma toward the target material, and $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}}$
is the sum of the electron and ion conductive heat-flux vectors. This
aggregate quantity covers the complete divertor assembly and is a
locus-specific component of
[power_due_to_conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), rather than the
global wall quantity
[power_at_wall_due_to_conduction](name:power_at_wall_due_to_conduction).

sources.leaf_definition: Power conducted by the plasma on the divertor targets (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_convection
NAMES.short:
Power deposited on all divertor targets by convective plasma particle flux,
comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming
ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Convective power at all divertor targets quantifies the energy transported
to those targets by plasma particles streaming from the scrape-off layer. It
comprises thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic-energy contributions carried
by convective plasma particle flux into the material surfaces, summed over
all divertor targets.

The all-target convective divertor power is the sum of the incident
convective energy flux over the wetted surfaces of the divertor targets:

$$
P_{\mathrm{conv,div}} =
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{A_k}
\sum_s \Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}}
\left(h_{s,k} + \frac{1}{2} m_s |\mathbf{u}_{s,k}|^2\right)
\, dA
$$

where $\mathcal{D}$ is the set of divertor target surfaces, $A_k$ is the
wetted surface of target $k$, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and $s$ labels
incident species in the convective channel, including streaming ion and
electron species. $\Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the particle-flux density
into the material, defined by the positive-into-target surface-normal
projection $n_{s,k}\max(\mathbf{u}_{s,k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf
n}_{\mathrm{in},k},0)$; $n_{s,k}$ is the particle density, $\hat{\mathbf
n}_{\mathrm{in},k}$ is the surface normal directed from the plasma into the
target, $h_{s,k}$ is the thermal enthalpy per particle, $m_s$ is the
particle mass, and $\mathbf{u}_{s,k}$ is the directed flow velocity of the
incident particles.

This quantity is the all-divertor-target realization of [convective
power](name:power_due_to_convection); the corresponding single-target
quantity is [convective power at a single divertor
target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), and the broader
plasma-facing-surface counterpart is [convective power at plasma-facing wall
and divertor surfaces](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). It excludes
[conductive divertor power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction),
radiative deposition, and [recombination-related divertor plasma
power](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which are
separate channels of the divertor power balance.

sources.leaf_definition: Power convected by the plasma on the divertor targets (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_ohmic_dissipation
NAMES.short:
Power deposited on all divertor targets by irreversible electrical-current
dissipation, summed over the complete divertor assembly.
NAMES.long:
Current-driven ohmic-deposition power is the irreversible conversion of
electrical work into heat in divertor targets, attributable to electric
currents and their associated electric fields. It represents net power
deposited in the target assembly.

For target conducting domains indexed by $i$, the current-dissipation power
is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{div,ohm}} = \sum_i \int_{V_i} \mathbf{j}_i \cdot \mathbf{E}_i\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{div,ohm}}$ is the total divertor ohmic-deposition power,
$i$ indexes the divertor targets, $V_i$ is the conducting domain of target
$i$, $\mathbf{j}_i$ is its electric-current density, $\mathbf{E}_i$ is its
electric field, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the differential volume element. The
integrand is the local rate of irreversible electrical-work conversion into
heat.

The scope is the sum over all divertor targets, with no inner-target,
outer-target, or individual-target selection and no target-level breakdown.
This is the divertor-localized component of
[total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation](name:total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation),
whose broader aggregation covers the complete applicable conducting domain.

This mechanism-specific quantity excludes power attributed to radiative,
conductive, convective, neutral-particle, or recombination deposition
channels. Unlike
[deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current](name:deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current),
which isolates a halo-current contribution at one target, it aggregates the
accepted ohmic or current-driven contribution over the complete divertor
target assembly. It is also distinct from
[power_at_divertor_target](name:power_at_divertor_target), which denotes
power at one target without this all-target ohmic aggregation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net electrical-current work deposits power
into the divertor targets.

sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Total power deposited on all divertor target surfaces by recombination
processes, comprising both the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination
channels summed over the full divertor assembly.
NAMES.long:
Total divertor recombination power is the combined rate at which
recombination processes at or near the target surfaces of the divertor
assembly release energy into the material, integrated over all targets. It
is the divertor-surface counterpart of the volumetric
[power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination) and unifies
two physically distinct deposition channels:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div} = P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma} + P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma}$ is
[plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination),
the energy deposited when plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the
material surface, and $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral}$ is
[neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination),
the energy carried by neutral particles undergoing recombination reactions
at the plasma-material interface.

This quantity is computed in edge-plasma codes that track ion and neutral
fluxes to the targets and apply sheath-energy coefficients along with
recombination cross-sections to determine surface deposition. It represents
one component of the total divertor heat load alongside conducted,
convected, and radiative contributions, and becomes a more prominent
fraction of that load in detached or partially detached divertor regimes
where volumetric recombination upstream suppresses the ion current reaching
the targets.

NAMES.name: neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Thermal power deposited on divertor targets by recombination reactions of
neutral particles at the plasma-material interface, summed over all targets.
It represents the neutral-particle surface recombination contribution to the
total divertor heat load.
NAMES.long:
Neutral recombination power of the divertor is the heat load delivered to
divertor target surfaces when neutral particles undergo recombination
reactions at the plasma-material interface. These reactions include surface
association or recombination of neutral atoms, molecules, or molecular
fragments into more tightly bound neutral species, such as molecule
formation on a material surface. It is the neutral-particle
surface-deposition channel of [total divertor recombination
power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).

The full-divertor value is the sum of the corresponding per-target neutral
recombination powers:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral} = \sum_t P_{\mathrm{rec},t}^\mathrm{neutral}
$$

where $t$ indexes divertor target surfaces and
$P_{\mathrm{rec},t}^\mathrm{neutral}$ is
[neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination)
for target $t$.

This quantity excludes heat delivered by plasma ions, electrons, photons,
conducted or convected plasma energy, and non-recombination neutral
interactions, except for energy deposited through the neutral recombination
process at the target. It is a surface-deposition quantity integrated over
the full divertor assembly, distinct from volumetric
[power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination).

sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to recombination of neutrals into a ground state (e.g. molecules) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Thermal power deposited on divertor targets by recombination or
neutralization of plasma ions at the plasma-material interface, summed over
all targets. It represents the plasma-ion surface recombination contribution
to the total divertor heat load.
NAMES.long:
Plasma recombination power of the divertor is the heat load delivered to
divertor target surfaces when plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the
plasma-material interface. It is the plasma-ion surface-deposition channel
of [total divertor recombination
power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), integrated over all
divertor targets.

It is defined as the surface integral of the local deposited-power density
over the divertor target assembly:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma} = \int_{A_\mathrm{div}} q_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{plasma} \, dA
$$

where $A_\mathrm{div}$ is the union of all divertor target surfaces, $dA$ is
a target-surface element, and $q_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{plasma}$ is the local
non-negative deposited-power density due only to recombination or
neutralization of plasma ions incident from the plasma side.

This quantity is the plasma-component counterpart of
[power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).
The complementary neutral-particle channel is
[neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination);
conducted, convected, radiated, and other non-recombination heat-load
contributions are excluded. It may be equivalently represented as the sum of
[plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination)
over the target surfaces included in $A_\mathrm{div}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to recombination of plasma ions (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: radial_length_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Non-negative span of a divertor target’s plasma-facing surface along the
major-radius direction, measured between its minimum and maximum R
coordinates.
NAMES.long:
The radial span of a divertor target is the extent of its plasma-facing
surface along the major-radius direction. It is a geometric extent, not the
distance along the target surface or a power-deposition width. The direction
is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$.

For the plasma-facing surface $S$, the span is defined by

$$
L_R = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S} R(\mathbf{x}) - \min_{\mathbf{x}\in S} R(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is a point on $S$ and $R(\mathbf{x})$ is its major-radius
coordinate. The quantity includes the full specified target surface and is
non-negative. It complements the [vertical length of the divertor
target](name:vertical_length_of_divertor_target), which uses the extrema of
$Z$, while the [x coordinate of the divertor
target](name:x_coordinate_of_divertor_target) identifies a Cartesian center
rather than a surface span.

sources.leaf_definition: Target length projected on the major radius axis
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: radial_outline_of_divertor_tile
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinates of points forming an individual divertor tile's
plasma-facing surface outline, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame. Each value is the non-negative perpendicular distance from the
toroidal symmetry axis, not a signed radial displacement.
NAMES.long:
Major-radius coordinates of points forming an individual divertor tile's
plasma-facing surface outline are the cylindrical $R$ coordinates of the
boundary points in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is the perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis and $Z$ is
vertical height. They specify only the radial placement of the outline
points.

The major-radius coordinate of each outline point is the cylindrical radius
associated with the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ frame whose $\hat{z}$
direction is vertical and whose toroidal symmetry axis is $x=y=0$:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the same outline point in
the plane perpendicular to the toroidal symmetry axis.

This quantity excludes the [vertical outline of the divertor
tile](name:vertical_outline_of_divertor_tile) and any toroidal angular
coordinate of the same surface outline. It is not a signed displacement
along $\hat{R}$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, a
surface arclength, or a normal distance from the tile surface; as a
cylindrical radius, $R$ is non-negative.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Outline of the tile surface facing the plasma

NAMES.name: surface_area_of_divertor_tile
NAMES.short:
Geometric area of the plasma-facing surface of an individual divertor tile,
defining the surface over which incident plasma loads are spatially
integrated.
NAMES.long:
The tile surface area is the geometric area of the plasma-facing wetted
surface of one individual divertor tile. It is a property of the tile
geometry, independent of the incident heat, particle, or current load.

The area is defined by

$$
A_{\rm tile} = \int_{S_{\rm tile}} dA
$$

where $S_{\rm tile}$ is the plasma-facing tile surface and $dA$ is an
elemental surface area. The result provides the geometric denominator for
converting an integrated load into a tile-averaged surface density, such as
the [energy flux at a divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

This quantity applies to one tile and must not be confused with the [wetted
area of a divertor target](name:wetted_area_of_divertor_target), which
characterizes a target-level deposited-flux region, or the total wetted area
of the divertor summed over multiple targets.

sources.leaf_definition: Area of the tile surface facing the plasma
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor tiles belonging to this target

NAMES.name: temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a
specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It refers to the sheath-entrance plasma population,
not to the solid target material or to an average over different
populations.
NAMES.long:
Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a
specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It characterizes the random kinetic part of the
particle distribution at the sheath entrance, the boundary at which
sheath-entry conditions such as the Bohm criterion are posed, and is not a
thermodynamic property of the solid target material.

For a population $s$, the scalar target temperature is the one-third trace
of the kinetic thermal-energy moment over the velocity-space domain of that
population at the sheath entrance:

$$
T_{s,t} = \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int_{\mathcal{V}_{s,t}} |\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t}|^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{s,t}$ is the temperature at the divertor target for population
$s$, subscript $t$ denotes the divertor-target sheath entrance, $m_s$ is the
particle mass of population $s$, $n_{s,t}$ is the number density of that
population at the sheath entrance, $\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ is the full
velocity-space domain of the specified sheath-entrance population,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow
velocity of the population at the sheath entrance, $f_{s,t}$ is its velocity
distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
distribution normalization is such that integrating $f_{s,t}$ over
$\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ gives $n_{s,t}$.

The specified population can be an electron population, an ion population, a
charge state, or another plasma population identified separately. If a
species is represented without charge-state resolution, this intensive value
is the density-weighted mean over all charge states. The unqualified
quantity does not imply an average over different plasma populations or over
positions on the divertor target.

For the electron population it corresponds to the [electron temperature at
divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), and for the
ion population it corresponds to the [ion temperature at divertor
target](name:ion_temperature_at_divertor_target). It is the divertor-target
specialization of the more general [plasma
temperature](name:plasma_temperature). The moment definition makes it two
thirds of the population-averaged random kinetic energy at the sheath
entrance, not the full mean random kinetic energy per particle.

NAMES.name: ion_temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of
the ion population averaged over ion species and evaluated at the plasma
side of a divertor-target sheath, distinct from the target material
temperature.
NAMES.long:
Ion temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of
the ion population averaged over ion species and evaluated at the plasma
side of a divertor-target sheath. It is a plasma boundary quantity for ions
at the downstream end of the scrape-off layer, not a thermodynamic property
of the solid target material.

For the ion population, the species-averaged target temperature is defined
from the ion kinetic thermal-energy moments by:

$$
T_{i,t} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int \lvert \mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t} \rvert^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_s
$$

where $T_{i,t}$ is the ion temperature at the divertor target, $i$
identifies the ion population, $t$ identifies the divertor-target
sheath-edge locus, $s$ indexes the included ion species, $m_s$ is the mass
of species $s$, $n_{s,t}$ is its number density at the target sheath edge,
$\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow velocity
of species $s$ there, $f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity distribution,
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and angle brackets denote
averaging over the included ion species.

This quantity applies exclusively to the ion population immediately upstream
of a specified divertor target and represents an intensive, per-particle
thermal-energy scale averaged over ion species. It is not an extensive sum
of ion energies or densities, and it excludes electron, neutral-particle,
and solid-target temperatures.

It is the ion-specific component of [temperature at the divertor
target](name:temperature_at_divertor_target). Unlike [electron temperature
at the divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), it
describes ion kinetic thermal energy at the same plasma-side target locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: total_incident_power_of_divertor
NAMES.short:
Total incident power of the divertor is the rate of plasma energy arrival at
all target surfaces through conduction, convection, radiation, and other
incident channels.
NAMES.long:
Total incident power of the divertor is the incoming plasma energy rate
summed over all divertor target surfaces. It aggregates all physical
contributions to the incident power rather than selecting a single target or
energy-transfer channel.

The defining aggregation is

$$
P = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} P_{i,c}
$$

where $P$ is the total incident power, $\mathcal{D}$ is the complete set of
divertor target surfaces, $i$ identifies a target, $\mathcal{C}$ is the
complete set of nonoverlapping incident-power categories, $c$ identifies a
category, and $P_{i,c}$ is the power incident on target $i$ through category
$c$.

The channel sum includes conducted, convected, radiated, and other incident
contributions without double counting. The quantity counts incoming energy
before subtracting reflected energy or outgoing thermal radiation; it is not
the net power retained by the target material. Thermal radiation emitted by
the targets is not an incoming contribution.

The [absorbed radiated power of the
divertor](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_divertor) accounts only for
radiation retained after reflection, rather than the full incident load. The
[power at a divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target) describes
deposition on one target, whereas this quantity aggregates incident power
over all targets.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total positive-ion number density at the divertor target, summed over all
ionic species and charge states at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local number density of all positive ions in the plasma
immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface. It is the all-ion
aggregate of ion density at the divertor target, rather than a
species-specific or charge-state-resolved density.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_{i,total} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{Z \in \mathcal{Z}_s} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the total ion number density, $s$ indexes
the included ionic species, $Z$ indexes their positive charge states, and
$n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of species $s$ in charge state $Z$. The sums
include all positive-ion populations evaluated at the entrance to the
electrostatic sheath.

Neutral atoms and molecules, as well as free electrons, are excluded. A
density resolved for one charge state is represented separately by [ion
charge state density](name:ion_charge_state_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: total_ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Rate of energy deposition by all incident ion species and charge states on
the inner, high-field-side divertor target, integrated over its wetted
surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the ion-carried contribution to power deposited on the
inner, high-field-side divertor target. It includes the thermal energy
entering the electrostatic sheath and the directed kinetic energy acquired
by ions across the sheath potential drop, while excluding electron,
neutral-particle, photon, and halo-current contributions. It is the
ion-resolved component of ion power at the inner divertor target and is
distinct from the all-channel power at the inner divertor target.

The deposited ion power is defined by

$$
P_{i,in} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wetted,in}}} \mathbf{q}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{t}\, dA
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{in}}$ is the integrated ion power,
$A_{\mathrm{wetted,in}}$ is the wetted inner-target surface, $\mathbf{q}_i$
is the total incident ion energy-flux density summed over ion species and
charge states, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{t}$ points from the plasma toward the
target material.
