NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the tritium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for tritium ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the tritium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the tritium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local tritium ion number density is defined by the positive-ion count:

$$
n_T = n_{T^+} = \frac{dN_T}{dV}
$$

where $n_T$ is the tritium ion number density, $n_{T^+}$ is the number
density of singly ionized tritium ions, $N_T$ is the number of tritium ions
in a small plasma volume, and $V$ is that plasma volume as its center
approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the tritium ion population immediately adjacent to
the divertor target and is summed over all positive atomic ionization
states; for tritium, the included atomic ion is $T^+$. Neutral tritium atoms
and molecules, electrons, deuterium ions, and other ion species are
excluded.

It specializes [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target)
by selecting only tritium ions. Unlike
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
it does not aggregate the deuterium and tritium fuel-ion populations.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over positive ionization states and
excluding neutral tungsten.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the tungsten-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed tungsten number density is defined by

$$
n_W = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{W^{Z+}}
$$

where $n_W$ is the total local number density of tungsten ions, $n_{W^{Z+}}$
is the local number density of tungsten ions with positive charge state $Z$,
and $Z$ is the integer tungsten ionization state from 1 through 74.

This quantity applies only to tungsten ions immediately upstream of the
electrostatic sheath at a divertor target. It includes every positive
tungsten ionization state once, without charge-state weighting, and excludes
neutral tungsten atoms and ions of all other elements.

The charge-state sum makes this the species-level tungsten component of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). Its
divertor-target locus distinguishes it from
[tungsten_density_at_limiter](name:tungsten_density_at_limiter), which
describes tungsten ion density at a limiter, and from
tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary, which applies at the plasma boundary.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: vertical_length_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Non-negative vertical span of a divertor target surface, defined by the
difference between its maximum and minimum Z coordinates in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical extent of a divertor target is the range of vertical positions
occupied by its surface, rather than the vertical position of its center.

$$
H_Z = Z_{\\max} - Z_{\\min}
$$

where $H_Z$ is the vertical span, and $Z_{\\max}$ and $Z_{\\min}$ are
respectively the maximum and minimum vertical coordinates over the target
surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame. Here, $R$ is
major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This
extent complements the [radial length of the divertor
target](name:radial_length_of_divertor_target) and is distinct from the [Z
coordinate of the divertor target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target),
which locates its surface center.

sources.leaf_definition: Target length projected on the height axis
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: vertical_outline_of_divertor_tile
NAMES.short:
Vertical outline of divertor tile is the signed vertical coordinate of each
contour point on the surface outline defining the geometric boundary of an
individual divertor tile in the poloidal cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Vertical outline of divertor tile is the signed $Z$ coordinate of each
contour point on the surface outline defining the geometric boundary of an
individual divertor tile. The coordinate is expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies pointwise to the contour points of the tile surface
boundary in the poloidal cross-section spanned by $R$ and $Z$ at fixed
$\phi$. It is not a tile-center position, a surface normal, a full surface
description, or an aggregate over the tile; no averaging, summing, or
extrema over contour points are implied.

Together with the [radial outline of divertor
tile](name:radial_outline_of_divertor_tile), it specifies the poloidal
contour of the divertor-tile surface boundary. The radial partner gives the
corresponding $R$ coordinate for the same contour points, while this
quantity gives only their $Z$ coordinate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the contour point is displaced in the
$+\hat{Z}$ direction from the origin of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Outline of the tile surface facing the plasma

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the xenon-specific
member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local xenon ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$
is the number of included xenon ions, and $V$ is a local plasma volume whose
center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the xenon-ion population immediately adjacent to
one divertor target and is summed over all positive xenon ionization states,
from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon. Neutral xenon atoms are
excluded; this is a local sheath-entrance density, not a volume-averaged
density or a density at a general plasma location.

Compared with [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which denotes xenon ion
density at a general plasma point, this quantity is specialized to the
divertor-target sheath entrance. Its charge-state-summed species convention
parallels
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target),
with xenon replacing oxygen.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: argon_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Charge-state-summed local number density of argon ions at the H-mode edge
pedestal top, excluding neutral argon.
NAMES.long:
The local argon-ion number density at the H-mode edge pedestal top is the
physical count of argon ions per plasma volume at that locus, aggregated
across ionization states. It excludes neutral argon and is neither
chord-averaged nor volume-averaged.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{z=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total local argon-ion number density, $z$ is
the positive integer argon charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{z+}}$ is the
local number density of argon ions in charge state $z$. The sum includes Ar+
through Ar18+.

The quantity is evaluated at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, whose
location is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is a
locus-specific form of [argon density](name:argon_density), whereas
[line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) represents
averaging along a plasma path rather than a local value.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Local number density of ionized beryllium at the top of the H-mode edge
pedestal, summed over all beryllium ion charge states and excluding neutral
beryllium.
NAMES.long:
Beryllium-ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal
represents the local concentration of ionized beryllium at the pedestal-top
location.

The total beryllium-ion density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \sum_{q=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the total beryllium-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions with charge
state $q+$, and $q$ is the positive integer charge state from one through
four.

The quantity is evaluated locally at the pedestal top, whose position is
defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It applies
to ionized beryllium only and is summed over all included beryllium ion
charge states; neutral beryllium is excluded, and individual charge-state
densities are not reported separately.

This is the pedestal-top specialization of [beryllium
density](name:beryllium_density). Its charge-state aggregation is the same
as for [beryllium density at the magnetic
axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis), while the evaluation locus
differs.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: boron_density
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Elemental boron number density, summed over neutral atoms and all ionic
charge states through fully stripped B5+.
NAMES.long:
Boron density is the elemental boron particle density, with neutral boron
and every ionic charge state included in one additive quantity.

$$
n_B = \sum_{Z=0}^{5} n_{B,Z}
$$

where $n_B$ is the elemental boron density, $Z$ is the boron ionic charge
state with $Z=0$ denoting neutral boron, and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density of
boron in state $Z$.

The quantity is the underlying boron density field; [line-averaged boron
density](name:line_averaged_boron_density) and [volume-averaged boron
density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density) are distinct averages of it. It
excludes no boron charge state but is not a charge-state-specific or
charge-weighted density.

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Boron ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over
all boron ionization states and excluding neutral boron.
NAMES.long:
Boron ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local
concentration of boron ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode transport
barrier, summed over all positive ionization states.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}} = \sum_{z=1}^{5} n_{\mathrm{B}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the total boron ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{B}^{z+}}$ is the number density of boron ions with charge state
$z+$, and $z$ is the positive integer ionization state from one through
five.

This quantity applies locally to boron ions at the pedestal top, whose
position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all boron ion charge states, excludes neutral boron, and is
neither line-averaged nor volume-averaged.

It is the boron-specific component of the broader [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [electron density at the pedestal
top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top), it counts boron ions rather
than electrons; unlike [boron density at the
limiter](name:boron_density_at_limiter), it is evaluated at the pedestal-top
locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: carbon_density
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Carbon density is the local number density of elemental carbon in the
plasma, summed over neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states through
fully stripped C6+.
NAMES.long:
Carbon density is the local number density of elemental carbon in the
plasma, summed over neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states through
fully stripped $C^{6+}$. It represents the elemental carbon population per
physical volume, independent of ionization balance.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by the number-density sum:

$$
n_C = \sum_{z=0}^{6} n_{C^{z+}}
$$

where $n_C$ is the carbon density, $z=0$ denotes neutral carbon,
$z=1,\ldots,6$ denote ionic charge states, and $n_{C^{z+}}$ is the number
density of carbon in charge state $z$.

This quantity is unweighted by charge, mass, or radiation emissivity and is
distinct from electron density, charge density, and individual charge-state
densities. Spatially averaged or locus-specific carbon-density quantities
include
[volume_averaged_carbon_density](name:volume_averaged_carbon_density),
flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary, and the ion-only
divertor-target quantity
[carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Carbon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of carbon ions, summed over all ionization states and
excluding neutral carbon.
NAMES.long:
Carbon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of carbon ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed carbon-ion density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{C}} = \sum_{z=1}^{6} n_{\mathrm{C}}^{z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the total carbon-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{C}}^{z+}$ is the number density of carbon ions with charge state
$z+$, and $z$ is the integer carbon-ion charge state.

This quantity applies locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined
by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all carbon ionization states from C$^{+}$ through C$^{6+}$,
excludes neutral carbon, and is not line-, volume-, or
flux-surface-averaged.

It is the carbon-species component of the total [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [carbon density at the
limiter](name:carbon_density_at_limiter), it is evaluated at the
pedestal-top locus rather than adjacent to a limiter surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short:
Characteristic outward distance over which a decaying plasma quantity
decreases by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for a plasma quantity that decreases
outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer.
The operand may be a particle density, temperature, or heat-flux magnitude.

$$
L_f = \left|\frac{d\ln f}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_f$ is the e-folding length, $f$ is the positive scalar quantity or
magnitude being characterized, and $x$ is outward distance from the confined
plasma in the direction normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The scale is
defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero.

The general quantity includes the electron number-density specialization
[electron decay length](name:electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer),
the ion number-density specialization ion decay length, and the heat-flux
specialization [heat decay
length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). It does not select a
species, transport channel, or particular decaying quantity.

NAMES.name: density_at_pedestal_maximum
NAMES.short:
Density at pedestal maximum is the selected plasma-particle number density
evaluated at the pedestal maximum, the steep mid-pedestal locus of maximum
pedestal-gradient magnitude. It is a density value at that locus, not a
density gradient.
NAMES.long:
Density at pedestal maximum is the selected plasma-particle number density
evaluated at the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the pedestal
maximum](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), the steep
mid-pedestal locus of maximum pedestal-gradient magnitude. The word maximum
identifies the peak-gradient pedestal locus, not a maximum of the density
value itself.

The defining relation is the evaluation of the selected density function at
that flux-coordinate locus:

$$
n_{\mathrm{ped,max}} = n(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{ped,max}}$ is the density at pedestal maximum, $n(\psi_N)$
is the selected plasma-particle number density as a function of the
normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\psi_N$, and $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}$ is
the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the pedestal
maximum](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

This parent quantity is species- or population-generic; concrete children,
such as [electron density at pedestal
maximum](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum), specialize the selected
particle population without changing the locus definition. When the selected
population is a species with charge states, the species-level density is
summed over all charge states unless a charge-state-resolved name explicitly
identifies one charge state.

It excludes pedestal-top density and any local slope or maximum-gradient
magnitude with respect to $\psi_N$; those quantities are distinct from the
density value evaluated at this locus.

NAMES.name: density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of a selected plasma population evaluated at the
plasma boundary, the last closed magnetic flux surface separating confined
plasma from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density at the plasma boundary is the amount of a selected
particle population per physical volume at the boundary of magnetically
confined plasma. The population is intentionally unspecified by this parent
quantity and is fixed by each specialized instance.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_P(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_P(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_P$ is the number density of population $P$, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_P$ is the velocity distribution function of population $P$, and
$d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. The selected population may be an electron population, an
ion or impurity population, a neutral population, an elemental population,
or an effective isotope mixture. The aggregation convention is additive over
exactly the particles included in population $P$; inclusion of neutral
particles and summation over charge states are specialization-dependent and
are not fixed by this subject-less parent quantity. This boundary quantity
is distinct from [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis)
and [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter), which use different loci.

Specialized instances fix the population and its aggregation convention:
[electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
selects electrons, while
[krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary)
selects krypton ions with charge-state aggregation. Elemental variants such
as [boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
may include both neutral atoms and ionic charge states. When population and
aggregation are held fixed, the corresponding boundary value is the
locus-specific counterpart of density evaluated at another defined plasma
location.

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally
on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization
states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the beryllium-ion
population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma
boundary is the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining density is the zeroth velocity-space moment, summed over all
beryllium ionization states:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}}\int f_{\mathrm{Be},z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$
is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ identifies a beryllium
ionization state, $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the set of included
beryllium ionization states, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$f_{\mathrm{Be},z}$ is the velocity distribution function for state $z$, and
$d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity applies locally at the plasma boundary and is additive over all
included ionic charge states. It includes beryllium ions and excludes
neutral beryllium atoms; it is not a flux-surface average.

This is the beryllium-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose
particle population is unspecified. It differs from
flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary because that
quantity averages the beryllium-ion density over the boundary surface, and
from [beryllium_density_at_limiter](name:beryllium_density_at_limiter),
which uses a limiter-adjacent locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Number density of boron at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic
flux surface, summed over neutral atoms and all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of boron at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive
particle count per physical volume for elemental boron evaluated on the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed
magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off-layer region.

The local elemental-boron number density at a boundary point is the zeroth
velocity moment summed over neutral boron and all ionic charge states:

$$
n_{\mathrm B}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{z=0}^{5} \int f_{\mathrm B,z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm B}$ is the elemental-boron number density, $\mathrm B$
denotes boron, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux
surface, $t$ is time, $z$ is the boron charge-state index with $z=0$
denoting neutral boron and $z=1$ through $5$ denoting the ionic states,
$f_{\mathrm B,z}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that state,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

This quantity applies specifically to elemental boron and includes neutral
atoms together with all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+. It
is a local value at the plasma boundary, with no averaging over the boundary
surface or over a volume, and excludes densities of other elements and
electrons. Unlike ion_density_at_plasma_boundary, it is not restricted to
charged ions.

It is the boron-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
[flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
applies the same neutral-plus-ionic boron aggregation but averages the
density over the last closed magnetic flux surface rather than giving the
local boundary value.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Number density of carbon impurity ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated
locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all
ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of carbon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the carbon-ion population evaluated on the
last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment, with explicit aggregation over
carbon ionization states, is

$$
n_C(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{q=1}^{6}\int f_{C^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_C$ is the carbon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the integer carbon charge-state
index, $f_{C^{q+}}$ is the velocity distribution function of carbon ions in
charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies locally to carbon ions in charge states C+ through C6+
and is summed over those ionization states. Neutral carbon is excluded, and
the value is not averaged over the boundary flux surface.

It specializes the population-unspecified
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to carbon
ions. It is distinct from
flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary, which applies the
same carbon-ion aggregation after averaging over the boundary surface, and
from [carbon_density](name:carbon_density), whose elemental scope includes
neutral carbon as well as ionic charge states.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Deuterium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of deuterium ions, summed over all charge states, at the
transport-barrier shoulder.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of deuterium ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_D = \sum_z n_{D,z}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium ion number density and $n_{D,z}$ is the number
density of deuterium ions in charge state $z$.

This quantity applies specifically to deuterium ions and is evaluated
locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized
poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all deuterium ion charge states and is not a density-weighted
average, line average, or volume average; neutral deuterium and electrons
are excluded.

It is the deuterium-specific component of the species-resolved [density at
the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). The corresponding [electron
density at the pedestal top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top)
describes the electron population at the same locus and is not included in
this ion density.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally
on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all ionic charge
states, and excluding neutral deuterium.
NAMES.long:
Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary is the local
particle count per physical volume for the deuterium-ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_D(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z>0}\int f_{D^{z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point
on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ is a positive ionic charge state,
$D^{z+}$ denotes deuterium in charge state $z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_{D^{z+}}$ is the velocity distribution function for that charge
state, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to deuterium ions, is evaluated locally
at the plasma boundary, and is additive over all included positive deuterium
charge states. Neutral deuterium atoms and molecules are excluded. It is
therefore distinct from the broader ion_density_at_plasma_boundary, which
does not select deuterium, and from
flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary, which applies a
flux-surface average rather than a local boundary evaluation.

This species-specific quantity is a specialization of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose
particle population and charge-state aggregation are unspecified. The local
deuterium value provides the pointwise boundary quantity from which the
corresponding flux-surface-averaged deuterium density is formed.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Deuterium-tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal
is the local concentration of the effective single fuel pseudo-species at
the transport-barrier shoulder.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal
is the local concentration of the effective single deuterium-tritium fuel
pseudo-species at the inner shoulder of the H-mode transport barrier.

The local density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{DT}} = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{N_{\mathrm{DT}}(\Delta V)}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the deuterium-tritium pseudo-species number
density, $N_{\mathrm{DT}}(\Delta V)$ is the number of pseudo-species ions
within the volume $\Delta V$, and $\Delta V$ is a shrinking spatial volume
around the evaluation point.

This quantity applies to the effective single deuterium-tritium fuel
pseudo-species, rather than to separately resolved deuterium and tritium
populations. It is a local value at the pedestal top, whose position is
defined by the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate at the pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), and is not a
flux-surface or line-of-sight average.

It is the deuterium-tritium species specialization of [density at the
pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [deuterium-tritium
density at the plasma
boundary](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which uses the
plasma boundary as its locus, this quantity is evaluated at the pedestal-top
location.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the
plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per
physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the
plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume
for that effective species evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux
surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local effective deuterium-tritium number density is the zeroth velocity
moment of its distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{DT}$ is the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-pseudo-species number
density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface,
$t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity of the effective pseudo-species,
$f_{DT}$ is its phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies to the deuterium-tritium fuel mixture represented as
one effective pseudo-species, rather than to separate deuterium and tritium
populations. It is a local boundary value with no averaging over the
boundary surface or over a volume, and no additional charge-state
aggregation is implied by the effective-species representation.

It is the deuterium-tritium-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). Unlike
flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary, it
denotes the local value at the plasma boundary rather than an average over
that last closed magnetic flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: edge_localized_mode_frequency
NAMES.subject: edge_localized_mode
NAMES.short:
Rate of recurrent edge-localized mode events during an ELMing H-mode phase,
expressing the cadence of pedestal-relaxation bursts rather than their
amplitude or exhaust.
NAMES.long:
The edge-localized mode frequency is the event rate of recurrent
pedestal-relaxation bursts during an ELMing H-mode phase. It characterizes
the cadence of ELM events, not their amplitude, duration, expelled particle
content, or transient energy.

$$
f_{\mathrm{ELM}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{ELM}}}{\Delta t}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is the ELM event frequency, $N_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is
the number of identified ELM events, and $\Delta t$ is the elapsed interval
over which those events are counted. The interval must represent the ELMing
phase being characterized; isolated events outside that phase are excluded.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: ELMs frequency

NAMES.name: effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Effective charge number of the ion mixture at the plasma boundary is the
charge-squared-weighted sum of ionic number densities divided by the
electron number density at that boundary. It equals one for a purely singly
charged hydrogenic ion mixture and increases with impurity charge content.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge number of the ion mixture at the plasma boundary is the
charge-squared-weighted sum of ionic number densities divided by the
electron number density, evaluated at the plasma boundary where the confined
plasma meets the last closed flux surface. Because each ion population is
weighted by the square of its charge number, higher charge states contribute
disproportionately to this quantity relative to their particle density.

The boundary value is defined from the charge-state-resolved ion densities
by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff},b} = \frac{\sum_i n_{i,b} Z_i^2}{n_{e,b}}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},b}$ is the effective charge at the plasma boundary,
$i$ indexes every ion species and charge state present at the boundary,
$n_{i,b}$ is the number density of ion population $i$ at the boundary in
$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $Z_i$ is its charge number, and $n_{e,b}$ is the electron
number density at the boundary in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$. Under quasineutrality,
$n_{e,b} = \sum_i n_{i,b} Z_i$, so the denominator equals the
charge-weighted (first-moment) sum of the same ion densities.

The sum includes all ion species and all charge states at the boundary; for
a quasineutral, purely singly charged hydrogenic ion mixture,
$Z_{\mathrm{eff},b} = 1$, and any admixture of multiply charged impurities
raises the value above unity. This local boundary value is distinct from
[flux-surface-averaged effective charge at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary),
which applies an explicit average over the boundary flux surface, and from
[effective charge at the limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter), which
is evaluated at the limiter contact location rather than at the plasma
boundary.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Effective charge

NAMES.name: electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Characteristic outward distance over which electron number density decreases
by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for electron number density that
decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. It is the electron-density member of the [decay-length
family](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), distinct from the ion
decay length.

$$
L_e = \left|\frac{d\ln n_e}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_e$ is the electron-density e-folding length, $n_e$ is electron
number density, and $x$ is outward distance normal to magnetic flux
surfaces. The quantity is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is
nonzero; the magnitude gives the positive distance associated with the
outward decrease. It does not denote the decay length of temperature or heat
flux, which are separate members of the family.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron density radial decay length inv(grad ne/ne)

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_launching_position
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron number density at the wave-launching position is the local
free-electron count per unit volume where an injected electromagnetic wave
first contacts the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local free-electron number density at the geometric
launching position, such as a wave launcher aperture or waveguide mouth
where an injected electromagnetic wave first contacts the edge plasma. It is
the electron-specific component of number density at the launching position.

The density is defined from the electron velocity-distribution function by

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}})=\int f_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_e$ is electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}}$ is
the launching position, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-distribution
function, and $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity.

This is a local value for free electrons at the launching position, not a
density summed over plasma species, a flux-surface average, or a wave-power
quantity. It is distinct from [electron number density at the plasma
boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which is evaluated at
the last closed flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Electron density profile in front of the antenna
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron density at pedestal maximum is the electron number density
evaluated at the pedestal maximum, the steep mid-pedestal location of
maximum pedestal-gradient magnitude. It is the density value at that locus,
not the slope with respect to normalized poloidal-flux coordinate.
NAMES.long:
Electron density at pedestal maximum is the electron number density
evaluated at the pedestal maximum, the steep mid-pedestal locus whose
position is given by the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is a
local density value of the electron population at that flux-coordinate
position.

The defining evaluation is

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{ped,max}} = n_e(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}})
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{ped,max}}$ is the electron density at pedestal maximum,
$n_e(\psi_N)$ is the [electron density](name:electron_density) as a function
of normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\psi_N$, and $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}$
is the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

The scope is the free-electron population in the pedestal region at this
single locus. The value is local rather than averaged over the pedestal or
integrated over a flux surface or volume, and no ion charge-state
aggregation is part of this electron quantity.

It is distinct from the pedestal-top electron density and from a maximum
value of $n_e$ over the pedestal; the word maximum denotes the
pedestal-gradient locus, not an extremum of electron density. It is also
distinct from the signed gradient or slope of electron density with respect
to $\psi_N$.

The associated derivative of electron density at pedestal maximum with
respect to normalized poloidal-flux coordinate is $\partial n_e/\partial
\psi_N$ evaluated at the same pedestal maximum locus; that derivative
characterizes the local gradient, whereas $n_{e,\mathrm{ped,max}}$ is the
value being differentiated.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of electrons at the H-mode pedestal top, giving the
electron-density pedestal height as a local particle concentration.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electron

The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the electron
distribution:

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}) = \int f_e(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}$ is the
position at the pedestal top, $f_e$ is the electron number distribution in
position and velocity space, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space volume element.

All free electrons contribute; ions and bound electrons are excluded. This
is a local density, neither flux-surface averaged nor line-of-sight
averaged. Pedestal height here denotes a density level, not a spatial width
or a density gradient.

It is the electron-specific member of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), not a sum over different plasma species.
[Electron density at the pedestal
maximum](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum) describes the same
electron population evaluated at a different locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron density

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Pedestal height

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Pedestal height

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary, counting all free
electrons and allowing pointwise values or an explicitly specified
flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electron

The local density is defined by

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the local electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is the
spatial position on the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity,
$f_e$ is the electron phase-space number distribution, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the full electron
velocity distribution.

The population includes thermal and nonthermal free electrons without an
orbit-class restriction; electrons bound in atoms or ions are excluded.
Unlike [ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), this quantity counts
electrons rather than ions.

This quantity encompasses pointwise values and explicitly specified
magnetic-flux-surface averages. The [flux-surface-averaged electron density
at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) is
its surface-averaged specialization, using inverse-magnitude
poloidal-flux-gradient weighting rather than pointwise evaluation. Neither a
chord average nor an average over the confined plasma volume is implied.

field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Radial e-folding decay length of the electron heat flux in the scrape-off
layer, defined by the inverse magnitude of its outward logarithmic gradient.
NAMES.long:
The electron heat decay length in the scrape-off layer (SOL) is the radial
distance over which the electron heat-flux profile falls to $1/e$ of its
separatrix value. It characterizes the spatial scale of electron heat
exhaust across the open-field-line region and specializes the
channel-unspecified [heat decay
length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

The decay length is defined as the inverse magnitude of the outward
logarithmic gradient of the electron heat flux:

$$
\lambda_{q,e} = \left| \frac{\partial \ln q_e}{\partial r} \right|^{-1}
$$

where $q_e$ is the electron heat flux and $r$ is radial distance measured
outward from the separatrix into the SOL.

This quantity includes only the electron heat channel and is distinct from
the corresponding [ion heat decay
length](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). As the magnitude
of a logarithmic gradient, the decay length is non-negative.

NAMES.name: electron_larmor_radius_normalized_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio of the electron Larmor radius to its macroscopic
normalization length at the high-field-side pressure-pedestal top, evaluated
with the local magnetic-field magnitude.
NAMES.long:
The normalized electron Larmor radius is the dimensionless gyroradius of the
electron population evaluated at the high-field-side pressure-pedestal top.
It characterizes electron orbit scale relative to the macroscopic length
prescribed by the normalization convention.

The defining relation is

$$
\rho_e^* = \frac{\rho_e}{L_{\mathrm{ref}}} = \frac{m_e v_{\perp,e}}{|q_e| B_{\mathrm{HFS}} L_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\rho_e^*$ is the normalized electron Larmor radius, $\rho_e$ is the
electron Larmor radius, $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the prescribed macroscopic
normalization length, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $v_{\perp,e}$ is the
characteristic electron speed perpendicular to the magnetic field, $q_e$ is
the electron charge, and $B_{\mathrm{HFS}}$ is the local magnetic-field
magnitude at the high-field-side pressure-pedestal top. The field magnitude
is the quantity represented by the [high-field-side pedestal-top
magnetic-field
magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side).

The quantity applies specifically to electrons and to the high-field-side
pressure-pedestal-top location. It is a local dimensionless scale ratio, not
an unnormalized Larmor radius, a magnetic-field component, or a quantity
aggregated over particle species. The normalization length and
characteristic-speed convention must be specified consistently; this
definition does not prescribe particular choices.

The [corresponding low-field-side
value](name:electron_larmor_radius_normalized_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side)
uses the same normalization concept with the low-field-side magnetic-field
evaluation. For equal characteristic electron speed and normalization
length, the two normalized radii vary inversely with their respective local
magnetic-field magnitudes.

NAMES.name: energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law coefficient relating the diffusive thermal energy flux of a
plasma constituent to its local temperature gradient, serving as the
species-agnostic parent abstraction over electron, ion, and neutral
population specializations.
NAMES.long:
The energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven thermal
energy transport for any plasma constituent — electrons, ions, or neutrals —
by specifying the proportionality between the diffusive heat flux and the
local temperature gradient in the Fick's-law sense. It is the thermal-energy
channel of the general diffusion_coefficient, which governs particle,
momentum, and energy transport alike, and it is distinct from convective or
$E \times B$ contributions to the total heat flux.

The defining relation for the diffusive energy flux
$\mathbf{Q}_\mathrm{diff}$ of a given constituent is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_\mathrm{diff} = -D_E \, \nabla T
$$

where $D_E$ is the energy diffusion coefficient and $\nabla T$ is the
temperature gradient of that constituent. In a magnetized plasma $D_E$ is
strongly anisotropic; radial cross-field values govern energy confinement
while values along field lines are orders of magnitude larger.

Species-resolved children include
[electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
for the electron population and
[ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
for the total ion population aggregated over all charge states;
neutral-particle transport is handled by analogous neutral specializations.
The effective diffusivity that combines diffusive and convective
contributions is tracked separately by energy_effective_diffusivity.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Number density of argon ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux
surface, summed over all argon ion charge states and excluding neutral
argon.
NAMES.long:
Number density of argon

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle$ is the averaged argon-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the local argon-ion number density, $S$ is the
plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux; $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of its spatial
gradient.

This quantity is summed over all charged argon ion states and excludes
neutral argon. It is a flux-surface average rather than a local point value,
line average, or volume average.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [argon ion
density](name:argon_density) and differs from the [volume-averaged argon
density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), which uses a plasma-volume
average instead of an inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface
average. Its species-specific structure parallels the [flux-surface-averaged
xenon density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

Number density of beryllium ions averaged over the plasma boundary, summed
over all ionization states and excluding neutral beryllium.

Number density of beryllium

$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}}\rangle$ is the averaged beryllium-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the local beryllium-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is summed over all beryllium ion charge states and excludes
neutral beryllium. It is a flux-surface average, not a local point value,
volume average, or chord average.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [beryllium ion
density at the plasma boundary](name:beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary).
It differs from the [volume-averaged beryllium
density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density), which uses a volume rather
than a flux-surface domain.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of boron, including neutral atoms and
all ionization states, evaluated on the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the boron particle number density averaged over the last
closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary. It includes neutral
boron and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+, rather than
selecting a single charge state. It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart
of [boron density at the plasma
boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary).

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm B}\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm B}\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

Here $n_{\mathrm B}$ is the local total boron particle number density,
$\psi$ is the poloidal-flux surface label, $\psi_b$ identifies the
plasma-boundary surface, and $dS$ is its surface element. The result is an
average over the complete surface, not the density at a selected point or
for a selected ionization state.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Number density of carbon ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux
surface at the plasma boundary, summed over all carbon ion charge states and
excluding neutral carbon.
NAMES.long:
Number density of carbon

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{C}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{C}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{C}}\rangle$ is the averaged carbon-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the local carbon-ion number density, $S$ is the
flux surface at the specified plasma-boundary locus, $dS$ is its surface
element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude
provides the weighting.

This quantity is summed over all carbon ion charge states and excludes
neutral carbon. It is a flux-surface average rather than a local point
value, a charge-state-resolved density, or a volume average. The
transformation from the local [carbon-ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary) replaces the pointwise
value with the inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface mean. It is
the carbon-specific counterpart of [flux-surface-averaged neon density at
the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =

the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is summed over all deuterium ion charge states. It is not a
local point value, a volume average, or a density that includes neutral

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [deuterium ion

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface average of the ion-mixture effective charge over the entire
plasma-boundary surface, distinct from the local boundary value.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the ion-mixture effective
charge over the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed flux
surface. It summarizes the charge composition across the complete boundary
surface rather than at a single location.

$$
\left\langle Z_{\mathrm{eff}} \right\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi_b} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}\,d\ell/B_p}{\oint_{\psi_b} d\ell/B_p}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{n_e}
$$

Here $\psi_b$ labels the plasma-boundary flux surface, $d\ell$ is poloidal
arc length, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, $n_i$ and $Z_i$
are the number density and charge number of ion population $i$, and $n_e$ is
the electron number density. The linked effective charge at the plasma
boundary denotes the corresponding local boundary quantity; this entry
denotes its flux-surface average.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged electron number density at the plasma boundary, using
inverse-magnitude poloidal-flux-gradient weighting rather than a pointwise
value.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electron

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle = \oint n_e\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_e\rangle$ is the averaged electron number density, $n_e$ is
the local electron number density, the subscript $e$ identifies electrons,
$S$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, $\psi$
is poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

This quantity applies only to the electron population at the plasma
boundary. Its aggregation is over the flux surface with inverse-gradient
weighting, not over particle species; it is neither an ion density, a
pointwise density, a volume average, nor an unweighted surface average.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [electron number density at the
plasma boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary): the parent
quantity supplies $n_e$ at each surface point, while this quantity applies
the normalized flux-surface integral. It differs from [flux-surface-averaged
total ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which represents charged ions rather than electrons.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of positively charged tungsten ions on
the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the number density of tungsten ions averaged over the last
closed magnetic flux surface, with all positive ionization states included
and neutral tungsten excluded. It is the surface-averaged counterpart of the
local tungsten density at the plasma boundary.

The flux-surface average at the plasma-boundary flux label is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm{W}}\,d\ell_p/B_p}{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} d\ell_p/B_p}
$$

where $\psi_b$ is the flux label of the plasma boundary, $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is
the local summed tungsten-ion density, $d\ell_p$ is poloidal contour length,
and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. The quantity is distinct
from [volume-averaged tungsten
density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), which averages over the
enclosed plasma volume.

NAMES.name: heat_convection_velocity
NAMES.short:
Heat convection velocity is the effective advective velocity whose product
with thermal-energy density gives the convective heat flux. It characterizes
heat transport only and does not imply equality to any bulk fluid velocity.
NAMES.long:
Heat convection velocity is the effective advective velocity associated with
convective transport of thermal energy. It relates a convective heat-flux
component to the corresponding thermal-energy density for the same heat
population, without requiring the effective velocity to equal a bulk fluid
velocity.

For a scalar component along an oriented transport direction, the defining
relation is

$$
q_h^{\mathrm{conv}} = w_h v_h^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $q_h^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective heat-flux component, $w_h$ is
the thermal-energy density of the transported heat population, and
$v_h^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the heat convection velocity.

This quantity is heat-specific: it is not a generic convection velocity for
arbitrary plasma scalars. For species-level specializations such as [ion
heat convection velocity](name:ion_heat_convection_velocity), the effective
velocity is an intensive quantity and is the density-weighted mean over all
charge states of the species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the associated convective heat-flux component
is directed along the positive orientation of the transport direction used
for that component.

NAMES.name: heat_flux
NAMES.short:
Vector of plasma energy transport per unit area, whose projection through an
oriented surface gives the power crossing it through convective, conductive,
and turbulent channels.
NAMES.long:
The heat-flux vector represents the net transport of plasma energy through
space, including convective, conductive, cross-field, field-aligned, and
fluctuation-driven contributions when included in the energy balance.

For an oriented surface $S$, the transported power is defined by

$$
P_S = \int_S \mathbf{q} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\,dA
$$

where $\mathbf{q}$ is the heat-flux vector, $P_S$ is the crossing power in
W, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit normal, and $dA$ is a surface
element in m$^2$. The [parallel heat flux](name:parallel_heat_flux) is its
projection along the local magnetic-field direction. Convective transport
may be parameterized by the ratio of heat flux to product of particle flux
and particle temperature due to convection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the local component of $\mathbf{q}$ points
along the chosen oriented surface normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux
surface and summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the helium-3 ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface, or separatrix, separating
confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local charge-state-summed helium-3 number density is the zeroth velocity
moment of the helium-3 ion distribution functions at a boundary point:

$$
n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{2} \int f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density,
$\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is
time, $q$ is the helium-3 ionic charge state, $f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}$ is
the phase-space distribution function for that charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is
ion velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to helium-3 ions, whose nuclei contain
three nucleons, and includes all ionized charge states from singly charged
through fully stripped helium-3. It excludes neutral helium-3, other helium
isotopes, and other plasma species. The value is local at the boundary and
is not averaged over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the helium-3-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary represents the
average of this local helium-3 ion density over the same last closed
magnetic flux surface rather than its value at a boundary point.

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Helium-4 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of helium-4 ions summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of helium-4 ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He4}}^{(q)}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{He4}}^{(q)}$ is the local number density of helium-4 ions in
charge state $q$, and $q$ is the positive ion charge-state index. The sum
includes singly and doubly ionized helium-4 and excludes neutral helium-4.

This quantity applies specifically to the helium-4 isotope and is evaluated
locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized
poloidal-flux coordinate at the pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is not a
flux-surface average, line-of-sight average, or total ion density.

It is the helium-4 species specialization of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). It differs from [helium-4 density at the
plasma boundary](name:helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary) because the
latter is evaluated at the plasma-boundary locus, and it is the mass-isotope
counterpart of [helium-3 density at the pedestal
top](name:helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top).

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the helium-4 ion population evaluated on the
last closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the charge-state-summed
helium-4 ion population at that locus.

The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_q\int f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density,
$\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the
ionic charge-state index, $f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}$ is the velocity
distribution function of helium-4 ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. This quantity applies only to helium-4 ions, is evaluated
locally at the boundary, includes all helium-4 ionic charge states, and
excludes neutral helium-4 atoms.

As a species-specific instance of [particle number density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), it fixes the otherwise
unspecified population to helium-4 ions. It differs from
flux-surface-averaged helium-4 density at the plasma boundary, which
averages the same charge-state-summed population over the boundary surface,
and from [helium-3 density at the plasma
boundary](name:helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary), which selects a
different helium isotope.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-4 ions averaged over the full plasma-boundary flux
surface, summed over all ionic charge states and excluding neutral helium-4.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium 4

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{He4}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{He4}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{He4}}\rangle$ is the averaged helium-4 ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the local helium-4 ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

The density is summed over all positive helium-4 ion charge states and is
not a local point value, a volume average, or a density that includes
neutral helium-4. It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local
[helium-4 ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary);
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting replaces that parent quantity's
pointwise value with a surface mean. The isotope-specific scope
distinguishes it from [flux-surface-averaged helium-3 density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

Related quantities:
[flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons (4He)

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Local number density of hydrogen ions at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge pedestal, summed over all hydrogen ion charge states and
excluding neutral hydrogen.
NAMES.long:
Hydrogen ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local count of hydrogen ions per unit volume at the pedestal's core-side
shoulder. It is specific to hydrogen ions rather than the total ion
population.

The charge-state-summed hydrogen ion density is defined by:

$$
n_{\mathrm H} = \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{\mathrm H}^{(Z+)}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm H}$ is the local hydrogen-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm
H}^{(Z+)}$ is the local number density of hydrogen ions with charge state
$Z+$, and $Z$ is the positive integer charge-state index.

This quantity applies locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined
by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). The
aggregation is a sum over all hydrogen ion charge states; neutral hydrogen
and ions of other elements are excluded.

It differs from [flux-surface-averaged hydrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which is averaged over a flux surface and evaluated at the plasma boundary,
and from [hydrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which has a different
spatial locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all hydrogen ion
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the hydrogen-ion population on the last closed
magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_H(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_H(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_H$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_H$
is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is evaluated locally at the plasma boundary and is summed over
the included hydrogen ion charge states. It excludes neutral hydrogen and is
distinct from electron density and from the total ion population represented
by ion_density_at_plasma_boundary.

The corresponding surface-averaged quantity,
flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary, applies the same
hydrogen-ion population to an average over the boundary surface rather than
a local evaluation. The subject-unspecified parent
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) defines the
common boundary-density concept, while this quantity fixes the population as
hydrogen ions.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of hydrogen ions averaged over the plasma-boundary flux
surface, with all hydrogen ion charge states summed and neutral hydrogen
excluded.
NAMES.long:
Number density of hydrogen

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{H}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{H}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{H}}\rangle$ is the averaged hydrogen-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the local hydrogen-ion number density, $S$ is
the averaging flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity applies to hydrogen ions on the plasma boundary, with all
hydrogen ion charge states summed and neutral hydrogen excluded. It is a
flux-surface average rather than a local point value, a volume average, or a
charge-state-resolved density.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [hydrogen ion density at the
plasma boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary): the local
density is replaced by an inverse-flux-gradient-weighted surface mean. The
same averaging operation applied to another species gives a distinct
quantity, such as [flux-surface-averaged helium-4 density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge states
evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pedestal.
NAMES.long:
Ion average temperature at the pedestal top is the density-weighted kinetic
temperature of the combined ion population at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode pedestal. It is the ion-specific component of average temperature at
the pedestal top.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{avg}}$ is the ion average temperature, $n_s$ is the
number density of ion species or charge state $s$, and $T_s$ is its kinetic
temperature. The sum includes all ion species and charge states in the
defined ion population; it is not an electron temperature or a temperature
for a single ion species. The weighting denominator is the total ion density
represented by total ion density at the pedestal top.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Number density of charged ions at the plasma boundary, with each
specialization defining whether the value is local or averaged over the last
closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ions at the plasma boundary is the particle count per
physical volume for a charged-ion population associated with the last closed
magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.

The defining charge-state-summed velocity-space moment is

$$
n_i(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{Z>0}\int f_{s,Z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the
plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of included ion
species, $Z$ is a positive ionic charge state, $f_{s,Z}$ is the velocity
distribution function of species $s$ in charge state $Z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The aggregation is additive over the included charged-ion species and all
their positive charge states; neutral atoms are excluded. A concrete
instance may provide the local boundary value, as in [total ion density at
the plasma boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), or its
average over the last closed magnetic flux surface, as in
[flux-surface-averaged ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary). This
ion-specific parent is narrower than [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose selected population and
neutral-particle inclusion are specialization-dependent.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Number density of ions of a specified species at the plasma boundary,
flux-surface averaged with inverse poloidal-flux-gradient weighting, summed
over all charge states, and excluding neutral atoms and molecules.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ion

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_i\rangle = \oint n_i\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_i\rangle$ is the averaged ion number density, $n_i$ is the
local [ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) of the represented ion
species, $i$ is the ion-species label, $S$ is the plasma-boundary flux
surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the [poloidal magnetic
flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) whose gradient magnitude is
$|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is evaluated on the confined-plasma side of the plasma
boundary. It is summed over all charge states of the represented ion species
and excludes neutral atoms and molecules; distinct ion species are not
implicitly combined. It is a flux-surface average, not a local point value,
volume average, or chord average.

The average is formed from the local [ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) by applying
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting over the surface. It differs from
the [flux-surface-averaged total ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which additionally aggregates charged-ion densities across ion species.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.
