NAMES.name: ion_heat_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion heat convection velocity is the effective vector velocity whose product
with ion thermal-energy density gives the convective flux of ion thermal
energy. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted
mean over all ion charge states and is not assumed to equal the bulk ion
flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
Ion heat convection velocity is the effective vector velocity that advects
aggregate ion thermal energy in an ion energy balance. It is a species-level
intensive velocity for the ion population, defined as the density-weighted
mean over all ion charge states.

The defining relation is the convective part of the ion thermal-energy flux:

$$
\mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{E}_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,\mathbf{v}_{Q_i}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of ion thermal
energy, $\mathcal{E}_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the ion thermal-energy density, and
$\mathbf{v}_{Q_i}$ is the ion heat convection velocity.

This quantity is not, by definition, the bulk ion flow velocity or an ion
particle convection velocity; it is defined by the ion thermal-energy flux
decomposition. Component-resolved specializations, such as [parallel ion
heat convection velocity](name:parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity), are
projections of this ion-heat transport velocity and do not change the
charge-state aggregation convention.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{v}_{Q_i}$
points along the positive basis vector for that component, such as
$+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Radial e-folding decay length of the ion heat flux in the scrape-off layer,
defined by its outward logarithmic decrease.
NAMES.long:
The ion heat decay length in the scrape-off layer (SOL) is the radial
distance over which the ion heat-flux profile falls to $1/e$ of its
separatrix value, characterizing the spatial scale of ion heat exhaust
across the open-field-line region.

The decay length is defined by the inverse magnitude of the outward
logarithmic radial gradient of the ion heat flux $q_i$:

$$
\lambda_{q,i} = \left| \frac{\partial \ln q_i}{\partial r} \right|^{-1}
$$

where $r$ is radial distance measured outward from the separatrix and $q_i$
is the ion contribution to the heat flux. This species-resolved quantity is
the ion-channel specialization of
[heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer);
the corresponding electron channel is
[electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer](name:electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).
It excludes the electron heat contribution and any unspecified total
heat-flux combination.

NAMES.name: ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Net rate of energy transfer to or from an ion population per unit physical
volume, summed over its ionic charge states and the included energy-transfer
processes.
NAMES.long:
Ion power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from
an ion population per unit physical volume. It is the source or sink term
for that recipient population in its energy balance.

The volumetric power density is defined by

$$
Q_i = \frac{dP_i}{dV}
$$

where $Q_i$ is the ion power density, $P_i$ is the net power transferred to
the selected ion population within physical volume $V$, and the subscript
$i$ identifies the ion recipient.

The recipient may be a specified ion species or an aggregate of species,
with contributions summed over all ionic charge states of each included
species. The net source combines the included energy-transfer processes; it
does not inherently require every heating or loss mechanism. Unlike [ion
charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), it does
not resolve individual charge states or charge-state bundles.

This quantity is neither stored ion energy nor volume-integrated power. It
is also distinct from the complete rate of change of ion energy, which
includes transport contributions. Energy transferred to electron or neutral
recipients is excluded.

[Fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density) specializes this
quantity to coherent-wave energy deposition into nonthermal ions of a
specified species. [Total ion power density](name:total_ion_power_density)
instead aggregates the net energy-transfer rate over all included ion
species and charge states.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when energy is transferred to the selected ion
population; negative when energy is removed from it.

NAMES.name: iron_density
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Total number density of iron impurity ions in the plasma, summed over all
ionization states from singly to fully ionized iron (atomic number Z = 26).
NAMES.long:
Iron density is the total number density of iron ions present in the plasma,
aggregated over all charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic
number $Z = 26$). It characterizes the iron impurity content without
resolving the per-charge-state distribution, and may refer to a local point
value or a spatially averaged quantity depending on the sampling convention.

The total iron ion number density $n_\mathrm{Fe}$ is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Fe} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron in charge state
$z$.

Iron enters confined plasmas primarily through physical sputtering of
high-$Z$ plasma-facing components. Spectroscopic measurements in the
vacuum-ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges resolve individual charge-state
emission lines; the total iron density is reconstructed by summing
ionization-state-resolved densities derived from ionization balance
calculations.

This general quantity is concretized by spatial-sampling variants:
flux_surface_averaged_iron_density averages the local density over a
magnetic flux surface,
[line_averaged_iron_density](name:line_averaged_iron_density) represents a
chord-integrated value divided by path length, and
[volume_averaged_iron_density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) integrates
over the full plasma volume. Position-specific forms are available at key
radial locations such as
[iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis),
iron_density_at_pedestal, and
[iron_density_at_limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter).

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Local number density of iron ions, summed over all ionization states,
evaluated at the core-side top of the H-mode edge pedestal.
NAMES.long:
Iron-ion number density is the local amount of ionized iron per unit plasma
volume at the H-mode edge-pedestal top.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{Fe}}} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the total iron-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the number density of iron ions in charge state
$q$, $q$ is the positive ionization-state index, and $Z_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is
the atomic number of iron and maximum positive charge state. The quantity is
evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal, whose
position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

The aggregation includes all positive iron ionization states and excludes
neutral iron and ions of every other element. It is therefore distinct from
a charge-state-resolved iron-ion density and from the total density of all
ion species.

This density is an additive species contribution to the total ion density at
the same location and provides one of the density weights entering the [ion
average temperature at the pedestal
top](name:ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top).

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Number density of iron impurity ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed
flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer, summed over all ion charge states from Fe+
through fully stripped Fe26+.
NAMES.long:
Iron density at the plasma boundary is the number of iron impurity ions per
unit volume — summed over all ion charge states from singly ionized Fe$^+$
through fully stripped Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$) — evaluated at
the separatrix, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically
confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It represents the
charge-state-summed iron impurity concentration on that boundary.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron ion number density at the plasma
boundary, $z$ is the positive ion charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$
is the partial number density of iron ions in charge state $z+$ at the same
boundary; these number-density variables have the unit specified for this
standard name.

The sum is over ion charge states only, so neutral iron Fe$^0$ is excluded.
As a scalar number density, the quantity is non-negative, with zero denoting
absence of iron ions at the plasma boundary. It is distinct from
flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary, which denotes a
flux-surface-averaged boundary value rather than the local boundary density.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Number density of iron ions averaged over the plasma-boundary flux surface,
summed over all iron ion charge states and excluding neutral iron.
NAMES.long:
Number density of iron

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\rangle$ is the averaged iron-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the local iron-ion number density, $S$ is the
plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude provides the averaging
weight.

This quantity applies to iron ions on the plasma-boundary flux surface and
is summed over all positive iron ion charge states, from singly ionized
through fully stripped iron. Neutral iron is excluded. The result is a
flux-surface average, not a local point value, volume average, or total iron
inventory.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [iron density at
the plasma boundary](name:iron_density_at_plasma_boundary): the same
charge-state-summed ion density is converted from a pointwise value to an
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface mean. It is distinct from
[iron density at the limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter), which refers to
a different evaluation locus.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Charge-state-summed number density of krypton ions at the top of the H-mode
pedestal, with neutral krypton excluded.
NAMES.long:
Krypton ion number density at the top of the H-mode pedestal counts ionized
krypton particles per unit plasma volume at that locus.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr,ion}} = \sum_{z=1}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr,ion}}$ is the total krypton ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}$ is the number density of krypton ions in charge state
$z+$, $z$ is the positive integer charge state, and 36 is krypton's atomic
number.

The quantity is evaluated at the top of the H-mode pedestal, whose position
is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all ionized krypton charge states and excludes neutral krypton.

This entry is the pedestal-top specialization of
[krypton_density](name:krypton_density); it is a local value rather than the
volume-averaged quantity
[volume_averaged_krypton_density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Local number density of charged lithium ions at the top of the H-mode edge
pedestal, summed over all lithium ionization states and excluding neutral
lithium.
NAMES.long:
Lithium-ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of charged lithium particles at the pedestal's inner
shoulder, where the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal) identifies
the evaluation location.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}} = \sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the total charged-lithium number density, $q$ is
the lithium ionization charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of lithium ions in charge state $q$. The aggregation includes
Li$^+$, Li$^{2+}$, and Li$^{3+}$ and excludes neutral lithium.

This quantity is a local value at the pedestal top, not a line average such
as [line-averaged lithium density](name:line_averaged_lithium_density) or a
flux-surface average such as [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the
plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary).
Its species scope is lithium only, and its charge-state aggregation is a sum
over all charged lithium ionization states.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the lithium-ion population evaluated on the
last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{3}\int f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is
a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the lithium
ionization-state index, $f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}$ is the velocity distribution
function for lithium ions in charge state $Z+$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is local at the plasma boundary and is not averaged over the
boundary flux surface. It includes lithium ions from Li+ through Li3+,
summed over these charge states, and excludes neutral lithium. It is the
lithium-specific specialization of [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

The corresponding flux-surface-averaged quantity, flux-surface-averaged
lithium density at the plasma boundary, applies a flux-surface average to
the same charge-state-summed lithium-ion density. The boundary locus also
distinguishes this quantity from [lithium density at the
limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which is evaluated at a limiter
rather than at the plasma boundary.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Number density of lithium ions averaged over the plasma-boundary flux
surface, summed over all lithium ion charge states and excluding neutral
lithium.
NAMES.long:
Number density of lithium

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Li}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}}\rangle$ is the averaged lithium-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, $\psi$ is
poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient operator,
so $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of that gradient.

This quantity applies to lithium ions on the plasma boundary and is summed
over all positive lithium ion charge states. It excludes neutral lithium and
is not a local point value, a volume average, or a line-of-sight average.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [lithium-ion number
density at the plasma boundary](name:lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary),
replacing the pointwise value with inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting
over the surface. It differs from the [volume-averaged lithium
density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density), which averages over plasma
volume, and the [line-averaged lithium
density](name:line_averaged_lithium_density), which averages along a
specified chord.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: mach_number
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vector ratio of plasma flow velocity to the local sound speed,
retaining directional components of the flow.
NAMES.long:
The Mach-number vector is the plasma flow velocity normalized by the local
sound speed. Its magnitude expresses flow speed relative to sound speed,
while its directional components retain the signed flow projection. The
family includes directional quantities such as the [parallel Mach
number](name:parallel_mach_number).

$$
\mathbf{M} = \frac{\mathbf{v}}{c_s}
$$

where $\mathbf{M}$ is the Mach-number vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
flow-velocity vector, and $c_s$ is the local sound speed. For a specified
direction $a$, the corresponding component is $M_a = v_a/c_s$, where $v_a$
is the flow-velocity projection along that direction.

The quantity is dimensionless and is distinct from the unnormalized flow
velocity; the sound-speed definition and the selected projection determine
the specific physical interpretation of each component.

NAMES.name: magnetic_shear_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Magnetic shear at the plasma boundary is the logarithmic derivative of the
safety factor with respect to the outward normalized toroidal flux radius.
NAMES.long:
Magnetic shear at plasma boundary

The defining relation is

$$
\hat{s} = \frac{\rho}{q}\frac{dq}{d\rho}
$$

where $\hat{s}$ is the magnetic shear, $q$ is the safety factor, and $\rho$
is the normalized toroidal flux radius, increasing outward. The expression
is evaluated at the plasma boundary, using the limit from the
confined-plasma side when required and where that limit exists.

The scope is a single boundary evaluation, with no additional flux-surface
averaging or averaging over neighboring flux surfaces. It is not an integral
across the edge or the magnetic shear evaluated at another named locus.

This quantity is the plasma-boundary specialization of [magnetic shear at a
flux surface](name:magnetic_shear_at_flux_surface): it uses the same
logarithmic safety-factor derivative, with the evaluation locus fixed to the
plasma boundary.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Neon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over
all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Neon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local
concentration of ionized neon particles there, aggregated over their
ionization states.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the total neon ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the number density of neon ions with charge state
$z+$, $z$ is the positive integer charge state, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the
atomic number of neon and the maximum ion charge state.

This quantity applies to ionized neon at the top of the H-mode edge
pedestal, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is local
and summed over all neon ion charge states; it excludes neutral neon,
individual charge-state densities, and line-, surface-, or volume-averaged
densities.

It is the neon-species component of the aggregate [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). In contrast, [neon density at the plasma
boundary](name:neon_density_at_plasma_boundary) describes the same
charge-state-summed neon population at a different spatial locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the
last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the neon-ion population evaluated on the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The population is summed over all ionization
stages from singly ionized neon, Ne$^+$, through fully stripped neon,
Ne$^{10+}$.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b)=\int f_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity,
$f_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the velocity distribution function aggregated over the
included neon ion charge states, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space
volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. This quantity is evaluated locally at that boundary and is
not averaged over the flux surface. It includes neon ions across all charge
states from Ne$^+$ through Ne$^{10+}$ and excludes neutral neon and other
particle species.

This quantity is the neon-specific specialization of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). It is
distinct from flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary, which
applies the same charge-state aggregation to a flux-surface average rather
than a local boundary value.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: neutral_species_density
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of a designated neutral species, counting its
neutral particles per physical volume.
NAMES.long:
The density of a specified neutral species is the local population of
neutral particles of that species per physical volume. It is resolved by
species rather than representing a combined density of different neutral
species.

$$
n_N = \frac{dN_N}{dV}
$$

where $n_N$ is the neutral-species number density, $N_N$ is the number of
neutral particles of the designated species, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity applies only to the neutral form of the designated species;
ions and other neutral species are excluded. Its aggregation is over neutral
particles of that one species, without implying a sum over species or a
particular population subdivision.

[volume_averaged_neutral_species_density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density)
is a volume-averaged specialization of this quantity over the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation.

NAMES.name: neutral_state_diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming bound on diamagnetic
momentum flux for a specified neutral species and internal state, limiting
flux magnitude without reversing its direction.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming bound on the
diamagnetic component of [momentum](name:momentum) flux carried by a
specified neutral species in a specified internal state. It controls the
admissible flux magnitude in a state-resolved fluid transport closure.

Its cap-setting role is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{\max} = \alpha\,\Pi_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\alpha$ is this coefficient, $\Pi_{\max}$ is the maximum admissible
diamagnetic momentum-flux magnitude, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the
nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude for the same
momentum component and neutral-state population.

The coefficient applies separately to the selected neutral species and
internal state; it is neither summed nor averaged over species or states.
Limiting reduces the flux magnitude without reversing its direction. This
coefficient is not a momentum diffusivity or a neutral-particle drift
velocity, and its definition does not prescribe a particular interpolation
between unrestricted and limited fluxes.

It is the neutral-state-resolved specialization of the [diamagnetic momentum
flux limiter
coefficient](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), within the
broader [momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) family. Unlike the
[neutral-state particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), it
bounds momentum transport rather than particle-number transport.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Local number density of nitrogen ions at the H-mode pedestal top, summed
over all ionization states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen ion number density at the H-mode pedestal top is the local number
of nitrogen ions per physical volume, with all ionic charge states
aggregated.

The charge-state sum is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{q=1}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the total nitrogen-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}$ is the number density of nitrogen ions in charge state
$q$, and $q$ is the positive integer ionic charge state from singly ionized
through fully stripped nitrogen.

This quantity applies locally at the inner shoulder of the H-mode edge
pedestal, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over nitrogen ion charge states and excludes neutral nitrogen; it is
not a charge-state-resolved density or a flux-surface average.

The locus distinguishes this quantity from [nitrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which represents the
same charge-state-summed nitrogen-ion density at the plasma boundary rather
than at the pedestal top.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the nitrogen ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from
the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local nitrogen ion number density at a boundary point is the zeroth
velocity moment summed over ionic charge states:

$$
n_N(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{7} \int f_{N^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_N$ is the nitrogen ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $q$ is the positive
integer ionic charge state, $N^{q+}$ is a nitrogen ion with charge state
$q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $f_{N^{q+}}$ is the phase-space
distribution function for that charge state, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to nitrogen ions and is summed over
charge states from singly ionized nitrogen through fully stripped nitrogen.
It excludes neutral nitrogen and electron density, and it is a local
boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the nitrogen-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary instead averages
the same charge-state-summed nitrogen ion density over the last closed
magnetic flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of nitrogen ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux
surface bounding the confined plasma, summed over all ion charge states and
excluding neutral nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Number density of nitrogen

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{N}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{N}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, /\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{N}}\rangle$ is the averaged nitrogen-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the local nitrogen-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
poloidal magnetic flux. The quantity $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of the
poloidal magnetic-flux gradient, and the closed-integral symbols denote
integration over the complete surface.

This quantity is summed over all nitrogen ion charge states and excludes
neutral nitrogen. It is a flux-surface average rather than the local value
given by [nitrogen ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), and it is not a volume
or line average. It follows the same species-specific family pattern as
[flux-surface-averaged neon density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary), with
nitrogen replacing neon.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Local number density of oxygen ions at the H-mode pedestal top, summed over
all positively charged ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The oxygen ion number density is the local population density of oxygen ions
at the H-mode pedestal top, the core-side shoulder of the edge transport
barrier. The location is identified by the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate at the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

The defining charge-state aggregation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{O}} = \sum_{q>0} n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the total oxygen ion number density, $q$ is the
positive integer charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is the number
density of oxygen ions in charge state $q$.

This quantity is specific to oxygen and is evaluated locally at the pedestal
top. It includes all positively charged oxygen states, from singly charged
through fully stripped oxygen, and excludes neutral oxygen and ions of other
species. It is distinct from the [oxygen ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which applies the same
charge-state aggregation at the plasma boundary rather than at the pedestal
top.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Signed projection of the local electric field along the local magnetic-field
direction, evaluated at the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The parallel electric field at the plasma boundary is the signed projection
of the local [electric field](name:electric_field) vector onto the local
magnetic-field direction at the last closed flux surface. It is a
point-local boundary value, distinct from the parallel flux-surface-averaged
electric field.

The defining projection is

$$
E_\parallel = \mathbf{E} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{E} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $E_\parallel$ and $\mathbf{E}$ are the parallel component and
electric-field vector in V m$^{-1}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit vector. All
quantities are evaluated at the same boundary location.

The plasma boundary is the separatrix or last closed flux surface; no
flux-surface or regional averaging is implied.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electric field has a component in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Average on the magnetic surface of (e_field.b_field) / B0, where B0 is global_quantities/b0/value

NAMES.name: parallel_electric_field_at_separatrix
NAMES.short:
Parallel electric field at the separatrix is the electric field projected
along the local magnetic field on the separatrix. It fixes the field-aligned
projection and separatrix locus, while more specific names may add an
aggregation over that locus.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electric field at the separatrix is the component of the
electric-field vector along the local magnetic-field direction evaluated on
the separatrix. The separatrix is the magnetic flux surface that separates
the closed-field-line region from the open-field-line edge region.

The field-aligned component at a separatrix point is defined by the
projection:

$$
E_\parallel(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{E}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x}), \qquad \mathbf{x}\in S
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is a spatial point on the separatrix $S$, $\mathbf{E}$ is
the electric-field vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$, and $E_\parallel$
is the resulting parallel electric field.

The scope is limited to the separatrix locus and to the component along
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$; it is not the electric-field magnitude, a component
perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction, or a flux-surface-normal
projection. This parent quantity does not by itself fix a spatial
aggregation over the separatrix; an aggregation qualifier belongs to a more
specific quantity.

The [flux-surface averaged parallel electric field at the
separatrix](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary)
is the flux-surface average of this same $E_\parallel$ over $S$; it differs
only by specifying the aggregation, while the parallel projection and
separatrix evaluation are already part of the present quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electric-field vector has a component in
the direction of the local magnetic-field vector at the separatrix.

NAMES.name: parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Temporal standard deviation of the total ion charge-current density after
projection onto the local magnetic-field direction at a plasma-facing probe.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the temporal standard deviation of the total ion-carried
charge-current density after projection onto the local magnetic-field
direction at the specified plasma-facing probe. Ion contributions from all
included species and charge states are summed with their signed charge
weighting before the fluctuation statistic is evaluated. It is the parallel
specialization of [fluctuating ion current
density](name:fluctuating_ion_current_density).

With $t$ denoting time in seconds, the defining relation is:

$$
\sigma_{j_i,\parallel}=\left\langle\left[j_{i,\parallel}(t)-\left\langle j_{i,\parallel}\right\rangle_t\right]^2\right\rangle_t^{1/2},\qquad j_{i,\parallel}(t)=\mathbf{j}_i(t)\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}(t),\qquad \hat{\mathbf b}(t)=\frac{\mathbf{B}(t)}{|\mathbf{B}(t)|}
$$

Here $\mathbf{j}_i$ is the aggregated ion current-density vector in A
m$^{-2}$, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic
field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field in tesla, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes the temporal average.

The aggregation and projection precede the standard-deviation operation;
this is not a sum of separately calculated species fluctuations. Unlike
[fluctuating saturated ion current
density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density), it represents the
total ion current rather than only the ion-saturation current component. The
result is nonnegative even when the underlying parallel current changes
sign.

sources.leaf_definition: Standard deviation of ion parallel current density at the probe position
sources.parent_definition: Set of embedded (in a plasma facing component) probes

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Kinematic diffusion coefficient governing down-gradient transport along the
magnetic field of flow momentum carried by ions of one species in a
specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the kinematic diffusion
coefficient for down-gradient transport of flow momentum carried by ions of
one species in a specified charge state. Parallel identifies the transport
direction along the local magnetic field, not necessarily the direction of
the transported momentum component.

For a local Fickian description, the parallel diffusive flux of the
represented momentum density is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,\parallel} = -D_{s,\parallel}\nabla_{\parallel} M_s
$$

Here, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,\parallel}$ is the diffusive flux of that
momentum density along the magnetic field, $D_{s,\parallel}$ is this
coefficient, and $M_s$ is the flow-momentum density carried by ion species
and charge state $s$. The index $s$ identifies that species and charge
state. The parallel gradient is $\nabla_{\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf
b}\cdot\nabla$, where $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. The minus sign
means the diffusive flux is directed down the field-parallel gradient.

The coefficient is resolved for one ion species and one specified charge
state; it is not summed or averaged over species or charge states. It
describes diffusive transport only, not convective transport or total
momentum flux. It is the parallel directional component of the
charge-state-resolved [ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), and is distinct
from the [radial ion charge-state momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient),
whose transport direction is cylindrical $\hat R$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(\hat R,\hat\phi,\hat Z)$ basis. Here, $\hat R$, $\hat\phi$,
and $\hat Z$ are the basis directions; $R$ is major radius from the machine
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when
viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed field-aligned effective velocity whose product with neutral energy
density gives the convective neutral-energy flux in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral-energy convection velocity is the effective coefficient of
the energy-density-proportional advective flux of neutral energy in the edge
plasma. It describes directed energy transport after gradient-driven
transport has been separated.

The parallel convective energy flux is defined by

$$
F_{n,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = U_n v_{n,\parallel}^{E}
$$

where $F_{n,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-parallel neutral-energy
flux due to convection, $U_n$ is the energy density of the selected neutral
population, and $v_{n,\parallel}^{E}$ is this effective convection velocity.

The quantity is the local magnetic-field-aligned projection,
$v_{n,\parallel}^{E}=\mathbf{v}_n^{E}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where
$\mathbf{v}_n^{E}$ is the neutral-energy convection velocity vector and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local nonzero magnetic
field. It applies to the selected neutral population, not to a sum of
particle-, heat-, and momentum-channel velocities.

It excludes conductive or diffusive energy flux and need not equal the
neutral bulk-flow velocity. The [radial neutral-energy convection
velocity](name:radial_neutral_energy_convection_velocity) describes the
corresponding major-radius projection rather than the field-parallel
projection. This neutral-energy coefficient is distinct from [ion heat
convection velocity](name:ion_heat_convection_velocity), which acts on ion
thermal energy.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral-energy convection is directed along
the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_mach_number
NAMES.short:
Signed ratio of the plasma flow component along the local magnetic-field
direction to the local plasma sound speed.
NAMES.long:
The parallel Mach number is the signed field-aligned flow speed normalized
by the local sound speed. It is the parallel component of the [Mach-number
vector](name:mach_number), rather than the magnitude of the full flow Mach
number.

$$
M_\parallel = \frac{v_\parallel}{c_s}, \qquad v_\parallel = \mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{b}
$$

where $M_\parallel$ is the parallel Mach number, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
flow velocity, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector in the local magnetic-field
direction, $v_\parallel$ is the field-aligned flow component, and $c_s$ is
the local plasma sound speed. The quantity excludes perpendicular flow
contributions and is distinct from the magnitude of the full Mach-number
vector.

sources.leaf_definition: Parallel Mach number
sources.parent_definition: Set of plunges of this probe during the pulse, each plunge being recorded as a time slice from the Access Layer point of view. The time child node corresponds to the time of maximum penetration of the probe during a given plunge. The dynamics of physical quantities within the plunge are described via the time_within_plunge vector.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Parallel flux-limiter coefficient that sets a nonnegative cap on the
field-aligned neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a specified
internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming bound,
without reversing the signed component.
NAMES.long:
Parallel flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles
occupying a specified internal state is the directional coefficient used to
bound the component of the corresponding neutral internal-state
momentum-flux density parallel to the magnetic field. The internal state may
be an electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation
state, and this scalar coefficient applies to the field-aligned projection
rather than to the poloidal or toroidal projection.

For the parallel component, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\parallel}| \le \lambda_{\parallel}\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\parallel}|,\qquad 0 \le \lambda_{\parallel} \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\parallel}$ is the limited component of the neutral
internal-state momentum-flux density parallel to the magnetic field,
$\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\parallel}$ is the corresponding collisionless
free-streaming component whose magnitude defines the bound, and
$\lambda_{\parallel}$ is this coefficient.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the
realized momentum-flux density. Because $\lambda_{\parallel}$ is
nonnegative, applying the limiter may reduce or bound a signed parallel
momentum-flux component but does not reverse its direction; a nonzero
limited component retains the sign of the underlying field-aligned component
to which the cap is applied. This scalar coefficient is the field-aligned
member of the [neutral internal-state momentum-flux limiter coefficient over
the edge
region](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region)
and is distinct from the
[poloidal](name:poloidal_momentum_neutral_internal_state_flux_limiter_coefficient)
and
[toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
directional members.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless parallel flux-limiter coefficient that scales the
free-streaming bound on the parallel momentum-flux-density magnitude,
projected along the local magnetic-field unit vector, for a specified
neutral particle state in edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter factor assigned to a specified neutral particle state in
edge-plasma transport closures. It scales the free-streaming bound on the
magnitude of the parallel component of neutral momentum-flux density, with
the projection taken along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b} =
\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

The cap set by the parallel coefficient is:

$$
\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm lim} = c_{\parallel}\,\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm FS}
$$

where $\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm lim}$ is the nonnegative limiter bound on the
magnitude of the modeled parallel neutral-state momentum-flux density,
$\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm FS}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming bound for the
same field-aligned projection, and $c_{\parallel}$ is this coefficient. The
signed projected flux satisfies $|\Pi_{\parallel}| \le \Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm
lim}$; when flux limiting is active, $c_{\parallel}$ is bounded in $[0, 1]$.

This quantity is the parallel projection component of the vector
[neutral-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region);
relative to that vector quantity, the specialization is the field-aligned
projection, not a different species or state aggregation. The coefficient
itself is a nonnegative cap and carries no directional sign, so it limits
the magnitude of the parallel momentum-flux-density component without
reversing the signed component. It differs from the
[radial](name:radial_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
and
[vertical](name:vertical_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
coefficients, which use $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ projections
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and from the
[poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
coefficient, which uses the poloidal projection.

sources.leaf_definition: Parallel component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Momentum flux limiter coefficient, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: parallel_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Parallel diffusion coefficient for total ion energy transport is the
effective scalar diffusivity in a Fickian flux-gradient closure along the
magnetic-field direction, with total ion energy summed over all ion species
and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel diffusion coefficient for total ion energy transport is the
effective scalar diffusivity that multiplies the parallel gradient of total
ion energy density in a Fickian closure. It is the parallel component of the
[total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient), where total ion
energy is summed over all ion species and charge states.

A local diffusive closure for the parallel total-ion-energy flux is

$$
q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{i,\parallel} = -D^{E_i}_{\parallel}\,\nabla_{\parallel} W^{\mathrm{tot}}_i
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{i,\parallel}$ is the diffusive flux of total ion
energy along the magnetic-field direction, $D^{E_i}_{\parallel}$ is this
coefficient, $\nabla_{\parallel} = \hat{b}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative
along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$, and $W^{\mathrm{tot}}_i$ is
the total ion energy density summed over all ion species and charge states.

This coefficient represents only the diffusive parallel contribution;
advective, convective, source, sink, and cross-field transport terms are
outside its definition. It is directionally distinct from the [poloidal
total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diffusive total-ion-energy flux is
directed down the parallel gradient of total ion energy density.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective diffusivity (in the parallel direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: particle_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating particle flux to
particle-number-density gradients, with directional or population-specific
components represented by more specific quantities.
NAMES.long:
Particle diffusivity is an effective Fickian coefficient describing the
diffusive part of particle transport driven by a particle-number-density
gradient. It may be resolved by transport direction or by the particle
population being transported.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{p,i}\,\frac{\partial n_p}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux,
$D_{p,i}$ is the corresponding diffusivity component, $n_p$ is the particle
number density, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the resolved transport
direction. The minus sign defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a
positive coefficient.

This parent quantity does not specify a particle population, charge-state
aggregation, transport direction, or microscopic mechanism. Population- and
direction-specific instances include [neutral particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_particle_diffusivity) and poloidal particle
diffusivity.

NAMES.name: neutral_species_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating neutral-species particle
flux to neutral-species number-density gradients, with directional
components represented by more specific quantities.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-species particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient
for particle spreading driven by a neutral-species number-density gradient.
It is the neutral-species specialization of [particle
diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional components
represented by more specific quantities.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux of neutral
species $s$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{n},s,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\mathrm{n},s,i}\,\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{n},s}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{n},s,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle
flux of neutral species $s$ along direction $i$, $D_{\mathrm{n},s,i}$ is the
corresponding neutral-species particle diffusivity component,
$n_{\mathrm{n},s}$ is the number density of neutral species $s$, and $x_i$
is the coordinate along the resolved transport direction. The minus sign
defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a positive coefficient.

This quantity selects the neutral-species population but does not select a
transport direction, neutral state, or microscopic mechanism.
Direction-specific instances include [parallel neutral-species particle
diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_species_particle_diffusivity). When a
neutral species is decomposed into neutral states, the species-level
diffusivity is the density-weighted mean over those states; the
state-resolved counterpart is [neutral-state particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_state_particle_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: neutral_state_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating neutral-state particle flux
to neutral-state number-density gradients, with directional components
represented by more specific quantities.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-state particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient
for particle spreading driven by a neutral-state number-density gradient. It
is the neutral-charge-state specialization of [particle
diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional components
represented by more specific quantities.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux of neutral
state $\alpha$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\alpha,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\alpha,i}\,\frac{\partial n_\alpha}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\alpha,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux of
neutral state $\alpha$ along resolved transport direction $i$,
$D_{\alpha,i}$ is the corresponding neutral-state particle diffusivity
component, $n_\alpha$ is the number density of that neutral state, and $x_i$
is the coordinate along the resolved transport direction. The minus sign
defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a positive coefficient.

This parent quantity selects a specified neutral state and does not
aggregate over different neutral states, but it does not specify a transport
direction or microscopic mechanism. Direction-specific instances include
[poloidal neutral-state particle
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_species_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Effective particle diffusivity for an ion species along the magnetic field,
relating its diffusive particle flux to its parallel number-density
gradient.
NAMES.long:
Effective parallel particle diffusivity for an ion species is the
directional transport coefficient that represents ion-particle spreading
driven by that species' number-density gradient. It is the field-parallel
specialization of [ion particle diffusivity](name:ion_particle_diffusivity),
with transport resolved along the magnetic field.

For the field-parallel direction, the diffusive ion-particle flux is defined
by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\parallel,i}\frac{\partial n_i}{\partial s_{\parallel}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the selected ion species,
$\Gamma_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is its parallel diffusive particle
flux, $D_{\parallel,i}$ is its parallel particle diffusivity, $n_i$ is its
ion number density, and $s_{\parallel}$ is physical arclength along the
magnetic-field direction. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport
for positive diffusivity.

The density and diffusive flux are summed over all ionic charge states of
the selected species, excluding neutral particles. This ion-species scope
differs from [neutral-species particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_species_particle_diffusivity) and its
field-parallel counterpart, [parallel neutral particle
diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity). The coefficient
describes particle diffusion only; it excludes convective particle flux and
is distinct from energy and momentum diffusion coefficients.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Poloidal electron beta at the high-field-side pedestal top is the ratio of
local electron thermal pressure to magnetic pressure based on the local
poloidal magnetic-field magnitude.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron beta at the high-field-side pedestal top compares local
electron thermal pressure with the magnetic-pressure scale associated with
the local poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. It is an electron-pressure
specialization of [plasma beta](name:beta) with a poloidal-field reference.

The defining local pressure ratio is

$$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$

where $\beta_{e,\mathrm{p,HFS}}$ denotes this poloidal electron beta,
$p_{e,\mathrm{ped,HFS}}$ is the local electron thermal pressure at the
high-field-side pedestal top, $B_{\mathrm{p,ped,HFS}}$ is the poloidal
magnetic-field magnitude at the same point, and $\mu_0$ is the vacuum
permeability.

Both inputs are point-local; neither flux-surface nor volume averaging is
applied. The numerator excludes ion pressure, and the magnetic-pressure
scale uses the poloidal field rather than the total magnetic-field
magnitude. The ratio is defined only for nonzero poloidal magnetic-field
magnitude.

It differs from [poloidal electron beta at the low-field-side pedestal
top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side) by its
evaluation locus. It also differs from [poloidal flux-surface-averaged
electron beta at the pedestal
top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_flux_surface_averaged_at_pedestal_top),
which uses flux-surface-averaged pressure and field rather than point-local
inputs, and from [poloidal beta](name:poloidal_beta), which uses a
whole-plasma total-pressure convention.

sources.parent_definition: Poloidal beta at pressure pedestal top for electrons using the high field side magnetic poloidal field

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Poloidal electron beta at the low-field-side pedestal top is the
dimensionless ratio of local electron thermal pressure to the local magnetic
pressure computed from the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude at the fitted
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. Both quantities are
evaluated at the outboard, low-field-side point.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron beta at the low-field-side pedestal top is the ratio of
local electron thermal pressure to the magnetic pressure computed from the
local poloidal magnetic-field magnitude at the fitted core-side shoulder of
the H-mode edge transport barrier. The low-field-side locus is the
outboard-midplane point, equivalently the largest-major-radius point on that
pedestal-top flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The quantity is defined by the local pressure-to-field-pressure ratio at
that point:

$$
\beta_{e,\mathrm{pol,LFS}} = \frac{p_{e,\mathrm{ped,LFS}}}{B_{\mathrm{pol,ped,LFS}}^2/(2\mu_0)} = \frac{2\mu_0 p_{e,\mathrm{ped,LFS}}}{B_{\mathrm{pol,ped,LFS}}^2}
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{ped,LFS}}$ is the local electron pressure at the
low-field-side point of the pedestal-top surface, $B_{\mathrm{pol,ped,LFS}}$
is the local poloidal magnetic-field magnitude at the same point, and
$\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability.

This is a point-local low-field-side beta: both the electron pressure and
the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude are evaluated at the same
low-field-side pedestal-top point. It differs from poloidal
flux-surface-averaged electron beta at the pedestal top, which uses
flux-surface averaging, from [poloidal electron beta at the high-field-side
pedestal top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side),
which uses the corresponding inboard point, and from [poloidal
beta](name:poloidal_beta), which uses a global plasma-pressure convention
rather than the local pedestal-top electron pressure.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Poloidal beta at pressure pedestal top for electrons using the low field side magnetic poloidal field

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Directional electron particle diffusion coefficient linking the poloidal
diffusive electron flux to the electron density gradient in a magnetized
plasma.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron diffusivity is an effective scalar transport coefficient
for diffusive electron-particle transport along the poloidal direction of
flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The constitutive relation is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,\theta}\,\nabla_\theta n_e
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal component of the
diffusive electron particle-flux vector, $D_{e,\theta}$ is the poloidal
electron diffusivity, $\nabla_\theta n_e$ is the metric-scaled
electron-density gradient along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, and
$n_e$ is electron number density. The associated flux component is positive
toward increasing $\theta$.

This is the poloidal projection of the anisotropic transport represented by
electron diffusivity. It describes diffusive transport only and excludes
convective fluxes, particle sources, and sinks; poloidal particle
diffusivity is the corresponding species-independent quantity.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the poloidal Fickian
diffusivity for thermal-energy transport of a specified ion charge state in
flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ), defined so the diffusive energy flux along
increasing poloidal angle θ at fixed radial flux label ρ and toroidal angle
φ is proportional to and opposite the corresponding gradient of that state's
thermal-energy density.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the effective transport
coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of the thermal-energy density of
one specified ion charge state along the poloidal direction in flux
coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It represents the Fickian part of that
charge state's thermal-energy transport along the poloidal coordinate
direction, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources,
and is the poloidal component of ion charge-state energy diffusivity.

The defining closure for the poloidal component is

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,z}\cdot\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}} = -\chi_{E,z}^{\mathrm{pol}}\,\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}\cdot\nabla w_z
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ion
charge state $z$, $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local unit tangent
generated by increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed radial flux label
$\rho$ and fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta,
\phi)$, $\chi_{E,z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal ion charge-state energy
diffusivity, $w_z$ is the thermal-energy density of that charge state, and
$\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}\cdot\nabla w_z$ is the corresponding poloidal
gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed
over ion species or charge states, unlike [poloidal ion energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity). The field-aligned
directional counterpart is [parallel ion charge-state energy
diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity). A
temperature-gradient form is equivalent only when the relevant density and
heat-capacity factors are explicitly included in the coefficient.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective kinematic coefficient governing diffusive redistribution of an ion
species’ poloidal bulk-flow momentum, with all ionic charge states included.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion momentum diffusivity is the effective kinematic transport
coefficient governing diffusive redistribution of the poloidal component of
ion bulk-flow [momentum](name:momentum). The poloidal direction is tangent
to a magnetic flux surface within a constant-toroidal-angle plane in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local, one-direction viscous closure, the diffusive flux of poloidal
momentum is:

$$
\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\varrho_i\chi_{i,\mathrm{p}}\frac{\partial u_{i,\mathrm{p}}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $i$ identifies the selected ion species, $\mathrm{p}$ denotes its
poloidal momentum component, $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
diffusive flux of that component along the transport direction, $\varrho_i$
is the species mass density summed over all ionic charge states,
$\chi_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is this diffusivity, $u_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is the
density-weighted mean poloidal velocity over all ionic charge states, and
$\ell$ is physical distance along the transport direction.

The poloidal qualifier selects the transported momentum component; it does
not require the transport direction to follow a poloidal arc. This kinematic
closure acts on the poloidal velocity gradient rather than the gradient of
total momentum density. It excludes convective momentum transport, residual
stress, and external momentum sources.

This quantity specializes [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity)
to the poloidal momentum of one ion species, without summing over different
ion species or including electrons or neutrals. It is a species-level
effective coefficient, not a sum of charge-state diffusivities; [poloidal
ion charge-state momentum diffusivity] instead applies to ions in one
specified ionization state.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Momentum effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

sources.parent_definition: Poloidal component

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_state_particle_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short:
Effective poloidal convection velocity for ion charge-state particle
transport, representing the signed pinch contribution rather than the ion
bulk flow.
NAMES.long:
Effective poloidal convection velocity for ion charge-state particle
transport is the coefficient of the convective, or pinch, contribution to
transport of the particle density of a specified ion charge state. It is
distinct from the poloidal component of the ion bulk velocity.

The associated poloidal convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol,conv}} = n\,v_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol,conv}}$ is the poloidal component of convective
particle flux, $n$ is the particle density of the specified ion charge
state, and $v_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component of
ion_state_particle_convection_velocity. The projection is taken in the local
poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with
the poloidal direction defined by increasing poloidal angle. The
corresponding radial coefficient is
[radial_ion_state_particle_convection_velocity](name:radial_ion_state_particle_convection_velocity),
while
[poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity)
applies the same transport concept to neutral particles.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective convection (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the signed value of the
poloidal magnetic flux function on the H-mode pedestal-top flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the signed value of the
poloidal magnetic flux function on the H-mode pedestal-top flux surface. The
pedestal top is the core-side top of the steep edge pedestal and may be
identified by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the value can
be represented as the flux through a horizontal disk bounded by a point on
that flux surface:

$$
\psi_\mathrm{ped} = \int_0^{R_\mathrm{ped}} B_Z(R', Z_\mathrm{ped})\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\psi_\mathrm{ped}$ denotes this quantity, $(R_\mathrm{ped},
Z_\mathrm{ped})$ is any point on the pedestal-top flux surface with
$R_\mathrm{ped}$ and $Z_\mathrm{ped}$ in meters, $R'$ is the
disk-integration radius in meters, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field
component in tesla. The integral fixes the additive reference to the
zero-radius disk on the toroidal symmetry axis; only differences in $\psi$
are invariant under an added constant.

This dimensional flux value is related to normalized poloidal magnetic flux
at the pedestal top through the normalization
$(\psi_\mathrm{ped}-\psi_0)/(\psi_b-\psi_0)$, where $\psi_0$ is the
[poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic
axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) and $\psi_b$ is the
[poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary). It is not a
radius-like coordinate such as [toroidal flux radius at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top), and it is distinct from
values at the pedestal center or maximum-gradient surface unless those loci
are defined to coincide with the pedestal top.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $B_Z$ on the horizontal integration disk
points in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal magnetic flux
sources.parent_definition: Radial position at which physics quantities are evaluated

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective poloidal diffusivity for neutral thermal-energy transport,
relating the diffusive energy flux tangent to constant-ρ surfaces to the
local poloidal gradient of neutral energy density.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusivity is the effective diagonal transport
coefficient for diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by neutral
atoms and molecules along the poloidal direction.

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, its defining constitutive relation
is

$$
q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}=-D_{n,\theta}\frac{\partial u_n}{\partial s_\theta}
$$

where $q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
neutral-energy flux density, $D_{n,\theta}$ is the poloidal diffusivity,
$u_n$ is neutral thermal-energy density, and $s_\theta$ is physical
arclength along the poloidal tangent at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$. The
diffusivity has units of m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, while $s_\theta$ is measured in m.

This quantity is the poloidal specialization of [neutral energy
diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It
aggregates the relevant neutral populations and is distinct from the
state-resolved [poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity).

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective diagonal diffusivity for down-gradient transport of energy carried
by neutral particles in a specified internal state along poloidal flux
surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity)
tensor expresses effective Fickian transport of energy carried by neutral
particles occupying a specified internal state. It acts along the poloidal
tangent to a flux surface, rather than along the magnetic-field direction.

$$
\Gamma_{E,\theta}=-D^{\mathrm{eff}}_{E,\theta}\left.\frac{\partial e_{n,s}}{\partial \ell_\theta}\right|_{\rho,\phi}
$$

Here $\Gamma_{E,\theta}$ is the poloidal energy flux,
$D^{\mathrm{eff}}_{E,\theta}$ is this diffusivity, $e_{n,s}$ is the energy
density of neutral particles in internal state $s$, and $\ell_\theta$ is
distance along the poloidal tangent. The coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$
are the flux-surface, poloidal-angle, and toroidal-angle coordinates; the
derivative is taken at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$.

This effective coefficient represents the net phenomenological response, not
a single microscopic mechanism. Its directional and state scope is shared by
the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
while the parallel counterpart resolves transport along magnetic field
lines.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient relating the poloidal diffusive flux of a neutral
species to its local number-density gradient in the same direction.
NAMES.long:
Effective poloidal particle diffusivity for neutral species is the
directional transport coefficient that represents neutral-particle spreading
driven by a neutral number-density gradient. It is the poloidal
specialization of [neutral particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_particle_diffusivity), with transport resolved
around the magnetic axis within a plane of constant toroidal angle.

For the poloidal direction, the diffusive neutral-particle flux is defined
by

$$
\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{0,\mathrm{p}}\frac{\partial n_0}{\partial s_{\mathrm{p}}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
neutral-particle flux density, $D_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal neutral
particle diffusivity, $n_0$ is the neutral-species number density, and
$s_{\mathrm{p}}$ is physical arclength along the poloidal direction. The
minus sign specifies transport down the neutral number-density gradient for
positive diffusivity.

The density and flux refer to the selected neutral species as a whole,
without resolving its internal states; no sum over different neutral species
is implied. This distinguishes the coefficient from the [poloidal neutral
internal-state diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient),
which applies to a specified internal state. This quantity describes
diffusive particle transport, not convective particle transport or energy
diffusion. Its directional counterpart, [parallel neutral particle
diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity), instead resolves
transport along the magnetic field.
