NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Signed effective poloidal velocity coefficient for density-proportional
convective particle transport of a specified neutral state in edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient of density-proportional
convective particle transport for a specified neutral state, projected onto
the poloidal direction. It represents directed drift or pinch transport
after density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has been separated.

The poloidal convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}} = n_s v_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}$ is the poloidal convective particle
flux, $n_s$ is the particle density of the specified neutral state, and
$v_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}$ is this effective velocity coefficient. The
quantity is the poloidal component of [neutral state particle convection
velocity](name:neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity), not the complete
particle flux and not the diffusive transport coefficient. Its species-state
and particle-channel meaning distinguishes it from the analogous [poloidal
ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity).

sources.leaf_definition: Particle effective convection (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets
sources.parent_definition: Transport quantities related to density equation of the state considered (thermal+non-thermal)

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_state_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle diffusivity is the effective
Fickian transport coefficient for diffusive particle transport of a
specified neutral internal-state population along the poloidal coordinate θ
in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle diffusivity is the effective
Fickian transport coefficient for diffusive particle transport of a
specified neutral internal-state population along the poloidal coordinate
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The neutral state is an
internal population of a neutral species, not an ion charge state or an
aggregate over neutral states.

The Fickian relation for neutral internal state $s$ is

$$
\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\theta,s}\,\frac{\partial n_s}{\partial \ell_\theta}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
particle-flux component of neutral internal state $s$, $D_{\theta,s}$ is
this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of neutral internal state $s$,
and $\ell_\theta$ is arc length in the direction of increasing $\theta$ at
fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$.

This coefficient is resolved for a single neutral internal state and
excludes summation or averaging over distinct neutral internal states. It
describes diffusive particle-number transport only and excludes advective
transport, sources and sinks, energy diffusivity, and momentum diffusivity;
related broader particle diffusivities include [neutral-state particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_state_particle_diffusivity), [poloidal neutral
particle diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity), and
poloidal particle diffusivity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the poloidal diffusive particle-flux
component is directed opposite to the poloidal number-density gradient.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: pressure_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short:
Kinetic plasma pressure evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier, including population-specific and total
pressure contributions.
NAMES.long:
Kinetic pressure at the pedestal top is the scalar stress associated with
random particle motion at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge
transport barrier. It may describe a selected plasma population or the
aggregate of the populations included in the plasma pressure.

The scalar pressure is defined from the kinetic pressure tensor by

$$
p = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{Tr}(\mathbf{P})
$$

where $p$ is the scalar kinetic pressure, $\mathbf{P}$ is the kinetic
pressure tensor, and $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the tensor trace. For a
specified population, $\mathbf{P}$ is that population's partial-pressure
tensor; the total plasma pressure is the sum of the partial pressures
included in the aggregation.

This quantity is restricted to the pedestal-top location, namely the fitted
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, rather than a
pressure value at an arbitrary point or across the entire edge region. A
population-specific instance such as [electron pressure at the pedestal
top](name:electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top) represents only the electron
partial-pressure contribution and is therefore distinct from the total
plasma pressure. The quantity is pressure itself, not the electron
temperature or a dimensionless beta formed by normalizing pressure to
magnetic-field energy.

NAMES.name: pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short:
Thermal pressure of a plasma constituent or neutral-gas population in the
open-field-line scrape-off layer, the region between the last closed flux
surface and the material plasma-facing components.
NAMES.long:
The scrape-off layer (SOL) is the open-field-line region extending from the
last closed flux surface to the material plasma-facing components, where
local pressure governs energy and particle exhaust, neutral recycling,
ionization balance, and the onset of divertor detachment. This parent name
generalizes over species-resolved SOL pressure quantities: [electron
pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) represents the electron
partial pressure and additionally anchors the pressure baseline offset in
H-mode pedestal profile fits, while [neutral pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) characterizes the
neutral gas inventory affecting recycling, pumping balance, and detachment
control.

For any thermally equilibrated species $s$, the scalar thermal pressure
satisfies:

$$
p_s = n_s k_B T_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the species number density and $T_s$ is its temperature in
energy units.

SOL pressure is inferred from a combination of diagnostics: Langmuir probes
provide local electron pressure at plasma-facing surfaces from saturation
current and electron temperature; neutral gas pressure gages directly
measure gas pressure in the divertor pumping region; Thomson scattering
resolves electron density and temperature profiles from which electron
pressure is derived. The characteristic radial scale over which pressure
falls from the separatrix outward is described by the [decay length over the
scrape-off layer](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

NAMES.name: electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged thermal pressure of electrons in the scrape-off layer, the
open-field-line region between the last closed flux surface and material
plasma-facing components.
NAMES.long:
Electron pressure over the scrape-off layer is the volume-averaged thermal
pressure of electrons in the open-field-line region between the last closed
flux surface and the material plasma-facing components. It represents the
electron partial-pressure contribution to [pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) over that volume.

The volume average is defined from the local electron thermal pressure over
the scrape-off-layer volume:

$$
\langle p_e \rangle_{\mathrm{SOL}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} n_e(\mathbf{x}) T_e(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $\langle p_e \rangle_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the volume-averaged electron
pressure over the scrape-off layer, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron
number density, $T_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron temperature
expressed as thermal energy per electron, $V_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the
scrape-off-layer volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\mathbf{x}$ is
position.

This quantity excludes ion partial pressures and the neutral-gas pressure
described by [neutral pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer). It is a SOL volume
average, not the electron pressure at the plasma boundary, and it is related
to electron density over the scrape-off layer through the same averaging
domain but is a density-temperature moment rather than a number-density
average.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Offset of the parent quantity in the SOL

NAMES.name: neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged thermal pressure of neutral atoms and molecules in the
scrape-off layer, the open-field-line region between the last closed flux
surface and material plasma-facing components.
NAMES.long:
Neutral pressure over the scrape-off layer is the volume-averaged thermal
pressure of neutral atoms and molecules in the open-field-line region
between the last closed flux surface and the material plasma-facing
components. It represents the neutral-gas contribution to the SOL pressure,
distinct from the electron partial pressure described by [electron pressure
over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer),
and is a component of [pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:pressure_over_scrape_off_layer).

The defining volume average is

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{n,SOL}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} \int_{\mathrm{SOL}} p_{\mathrm{n}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V, \qquad p_{\mathrm{n}}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_s n_s(\mathbf{r}) k_B T_s(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the scrape-off-layer volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is
position, $p_{\mathrm{n}}$ is local neutral pressure, $s$ indexes neutral
atomic and molecular species, $n_s$ is their number density, $T_s$ is their
thermodynamic temperature, and $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.

The quantity excludes charged-particle pressure and represents an average
over the entire scrape-off-layer domain rather than a pressure evaluated at
a particular location.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neutral pressure in the SOL

NAMES.name: radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian coefficient for radial diffusive transport of thermal
energy by ions in a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient is the effective
proportionality coefficient for down-gradient diffusive transport of thermal
energy carried by ions in a specified charge state. It characterizes the
radial transport component directed outward from the magnetic axis.

The diffusive radial ion-energy flux is defined by

$$
q_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{diff,rad}} = -n_{i,z} D_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{rad}} \nabla_{\mathrm{rad}} T_{i,z}
$$

where $q_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{diff,rad}}$ is the radial diffusive thermal-energy
flux, $n_{i,z}$ is the number density of ion charge state $z$,
$D_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{rad}}$ is this coefficient, $T_{i,z}$ is the
corresponding ion temperature, and $\nabla_{\mathrm{rad}}$ denotes the
outward radial gradient.

This quantity is the radial specialization of the [thermal ion charge-state
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It
applies to one specified charge state and excludes parallel, poloidal, and
toroidal transport contributions.

sources.leaf_definition: Energy effective diffusivity (in the radial direction), on various grid subsets
sources.parent_definition: Transport quantities related to the energy equation of the state considered

NAMES.name: temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short:
Temperature over the scrape-off layer is the thermal plasma temperature
associated with the open-field-line edge region outside the confined plasma.
It is a parent quantity whose specializations define any species, locality,
or averaging convention.
NAMES.long:
Temperature over the scrape-off layer is the scalar thermal plasma
temperature associated with particles in the scrape-off layer, the
open-field-line edge region outside the confined plasma. It denotes the
temperature concept for that region without fixing a particular plasma
species, spatial locus, or averaging measure.

This parent quantity applies only to plasma in the scrape-off layer and not
to temperatures in the closed-field-line confined plasma or to
material-surface temperatures. It also does not by itself specify whether
the represented SOL temperature is local, region-averaged,
field-line-associated, or otherwise aggregated; those semantics belong to
concrete specializations.

A specialization such as [average temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer) is a narrower
quantity that adds an averaging convention while retaining the same
scrape-off-layer temperature concept.

NAMES.name: average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short:
Averaged kinetic temperature of a specified plasma species over the
open-field-line scrape-off layer, with the averaging domain and measure
defined by its specialization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the temperature of a specified plasma species after
averaging over a defined domain or path within the scrape-off layer. The
scrape-off layer is the open-field-line region outside the last closed
magnetic flux surface.

The averaged temperature is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_s = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}} T_s\,d\mu}{\int_{\mathcal{D}} d\mu}
$$

where $\overline{T}_s$ is the averaged temperature, $T_s$ is the local
temperature of species $s$, $\mathcal{D}$ is the specified scrape-off-layer
domain or path, and $d\mu$ is the averaging measure. For [field-line-average
temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer),
$\mathcal{D}$ is an open magnetic field line between its defined upstream
and downstream locations and $d\mu$ is the corresponding path measure.

The quantity is species-specific and does not sum temperatures over multiple
species or represent a local pointwise temperature. It is an averaged
specialization of [temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), while the concrete averaging
domain and measure distinguish each child quantity.

NAMES.name: field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short:
Species-resolved temperature averaged by arc length along an open magnetic
field line between upstream and downstream locations in the scrape-off
layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the temperature of a specified plasma species averaged
along an open magnetic field line traversing the scrape-off layer. It
represents the common field-line-averaged quantity instantiated by the
electron and ion species-specific children.

The field-line average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{\sigma,\mathrm{FL}} = \frac{\int_{\ell_u}^{\ell_d} T_\sigma(\ell)\,d\ell}{\int_{\ell_u}^{\ell_d} d\ell}
$$

where $\overline{T}_{\sigma,\mathrm{FL}}$ is the field-line-averaged
temperature, $\sigma$ identifies the selected plasma species,
$T_\sigma(\ell)$ is its local temperature, and $\ell$ is arc length along
the open magnetic field line. The limits $\ell_u$ and $\ell_d$ identify the
upstream and downstream endpoints of the averaging interval.

The quantity applies to one species at a time and uses an arc-length average
along the open field line; it is neither a sum nor an average over multiple
species. It is restricted to the scrape-off layer and does not denote a
local temperature at one point or a volume average over that region.

This is the field-line-averaged, species-resolved specialization of [average
temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer). Its concrete
realizations include [electron field-line average temperature over the
scrape-off
layer](name:electron_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer)
and [ion field-line average temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:ion_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), which
differ only by the selected species.

NAMES.name: electron_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron temperature averaged along an open magnetic field line between
upstream and downstream locations in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the mean bulk-electron thermal temperature along an open
magnetic field line through the scrape-off layer, between specified upstream
and downstream locations. It represents the connected-field-line average
rather than the local electron temperature at a single position.

The field-line average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_e = \frac{1}{L_{\parallel}} \int_{s_u}^{s_d} T_e(s)\,ds
$$

where $T_e(s)$ is the local electron temperature, $s$ is arc length along
the magnetic field line, $s_u$ and $s_d$ are the upstream and downstream
endpoints, and $L_{\parallel}=s_d-s_u$ is the connection length.

The quantity applies to the bulk electron population in the scrape-off layer
and is aggregated by arc-length averaging along one open field line. It
excludes local single-point temperature values and does not represent a
flux-surface or volume average.

This is the electron-species specialization of the [field-line-averaged
temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer). It is
distinct from the corresponding [ion field-line-averaged
temperature](name:ion_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer),
which uses the ion temperature, and from [temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), which averages over the
region rather than along a connected field line.

NAMES.name: ion_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion temperature averaged along an open magnetic field line between upstream
and downstream locations in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the mean bulk-ion thermal temperature along an open
magnetic field line through the scrape-off layer, between specified upstream
and downstream locations. It represents the connected-field-line average
rather than the local temperature at a single position.

The field-line average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_i = \frac{1}{L_{\parallel}} \int_{s_u}^{s_d} T_i(s)\,ds
$$

where $T_i(s)$ is the local ion temperature, $s$ is arc length along the
magnetic field line, $s_u$ and $s_d$ are the upstream and downstream
endpoints, and $L_{\parallel}=s_d-s_u$ is the connection length. The result
is distinct from the local ion temperature at midplane and does not denote a
flux-surface average.

The time child node corresponds to the time of maximum penetration of the probe during a given plunge. The dynamics of physical quantities within the plunge are described via the time_within_plunge vector.

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the φ component, in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the density-weighted mean bulk
flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to the
confined core.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the $\phi$ component, in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of the density-weighted mean
bulk flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to
the confined core. As an intensive species-level quantity, it is the
density-weighted mean over all argon charge states, not a
charge-state-summed velocity.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by the density-weighted mean at the
pedestal top:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}^{\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes argon ionization state,
$n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the local number density of that
charge state, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is its toroidal
velocity component at the pedestal top.

It is inferred primarily from Doppler spectroscopy of argon emission, often
charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy when suitable neutral-beam
excitation is available. The observed line shift and viewing geometry
determine the velocity projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; estimating the
all-charge-state mean may require emissivity modeling, ionization-balance
information, or collisional equilibration assumptions.

Because pedestal argon rotation is sensitive to external torque, radial
electric-field shear, neoclassical friction, turbulence-driven momentum
transport, and charge-state distribution, no device-independent numerical
range is implied. This value is commonly interpreted with same-species
values at other loci, including [toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), [toroidal argon
velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
[toroidal argon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and toroidal
flux-surface-averaged argon velocity at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted mean argon flow points
in the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame of the
argon-ion bulk-flow velocity at the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of the argon-ion bulk-flow
velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed
flux surface. It is a pointwise boundary value rather than an average over
that flux surface.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{Ar},\phi} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z} v_{\mathrm{Ar},z,\phi}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{Ar},\phi}$ and $v_{\mathrm{Ar},z,\phi}$ are toroidal
velocity components in m s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$ is the argon-ion
number density in m$^{-3}$, and $z$ indexes argon ion charge states. The
toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The local value is distinct from the toroidal flux-surface-averaged argon
velocity at the plasma boundary, which averages the same component over the
boundary flux surface. Neutral argon is excluded from the ion bulk-flow
aggregation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the argon-ion bulk velocity projects onto the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of beryllium ions at the core-side shoulder of
the H-mode edge transport barrier, density-weighted over all ionization
states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the beryllium impurity-ion
bulk-flow velocity at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier, conventionally called the pedestal top.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{Be},\phi} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be},z} v_{\mathrm{Be},z,\phi}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be},z}}
$$

where $z$ indexes the included beryllium ion charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{Be},z}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and
$v_{\mathrm{Be},z,\phi}$ is the charge-state-resolved toroidal velocity in m
s$^{-1}$. The result is a density-weighted intensive mean, not a sum of
charge-state velocities; the corresponding elemental concentration is
represented by beryllium density at the pedestal top. It is evaluated at the
pedestal top rather than at the magnetic axis, as in [toroidal beryllium
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the beryllium bulk flow has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the
density-weighted bulk-flow velocity of all contributing carbon ion charge
states, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier. It is the toroidal component rather than the total
three-dimensional speed, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

$$
v_{\phi,C}=\frac{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}v_{\phi,C^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}}
$$

Here, $q$ indexes the contributing carbon ion charge states, $n_{C^{q+}}$ is
the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,C^{q+}}$ is its
toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. Neutral carbon is excluded because this
quantity is defined for impurity ions. The pedestal-top value is distinct
from the [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the carbon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the
last closed magnetic flux surface, resolved along increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The carbon impurity-ion toroidal velocity at the plasma boundary is the
local density-weighted mean of the bulk-flow velocities of all included
carbon ion charge states on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It is not
a flux-surface average; that distinct quantity is the toroidal
flux-surface-averaged carbon velocity, while the magnetic-axis counterpart
is [toroidal carbon velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

The defining local component is

$$
V_{\phi,C}(R,Z)=\frac{\sum_{q\in Q} n_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)\,\mathbf{V}_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_{q\in Q} n_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)}
$$

where $Q$ is the set of included carbon ion charge states, $n_{C^{q+}}$ is
the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{V}_{C^{q+}}$ is
its bulk velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The component is resolved in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the carbon-ion bulk flow has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity assigned to the effective
deuterium–tritium fuel species at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge
pedestal.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the bulk-flow velocity of deuterium and tritium treated as
one effective fuel species, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier. It is distinct from the velocity of deuterium
alone, such as [toroidal deuterium velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

The effective toroidal velocity is the mass-density-weighted mean of the
isotope flow components:

$$
v_{\mathrm{DT},\phi} = \frac{m_D n_D v_{D,\phi} + m_T n_T v_{T,\phi}}{m_D n_D + m_T n_T}
$$

where $m_D$ and $m_T$ are the deuterium and tritium masses in kg, $n_D$ and
$n_T$ are their number densities in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{D,\phi}$ and
$v_{T,\phi}$ are their toroidal velocity components in m.s$^{-1}$. The
effective species uses the deuterium–tritium fuel convention with mean
atomic mass 2.5; this local quantity is not a flux-surface average or a
value at the plasma boundary, such as [toroidal deuterium–tritium velocity
at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the velocity points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity of the fictitious
deuterium-tritium single-species (atomic mass 2.5 amu), evaluated at the
plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The toroidal deuterium-tritium velocity at the plasma boundary is the
$\hat{\phi}$-component of the bulk-flow velocity of a fictitious
single-species representing a deuterium-tritium fuel mixture with atomic
mass 2.5 amu, evaluated at the plasma boundary — the last closed flux
surface separating magnetically confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.

The toroidal projection is defined as:

$$
v_\phi^{DT} = \mathbf{v}_{DT} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{DT}$ is the bulk-flow velocity of the fictitious
deuterium-tritium species and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a local point evaluation at the plasma boundary, distinct
from
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary,
which gives the flux-surface mean at the same location, and from
[toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary),
which resolves the deuterium species independently rather than treating the
D-T mixture as a single effective species.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Toroidal deuterium-ion fluid velocity at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier, averaged over deuterium ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-ion toroidal fluid velocity at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier represents the bulk rotational flow of
deuterium ions. It is the density-weighted mean over all deuterium ion
charge states, rather than a thermal speed or velocity magnitude.

$$
v_{phi,D} = \frac{\sum_q n_{D,q} v_{phi,D,q}}{\sum_q n_{D,q}}
$$

where $q$ labels deuterium ion charge state, $n_{D,q}$ is its number density
in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,D,q}$ is its toroidal fluid-velocity component in
m.s$^{-1}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The locus
is the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, and the
quantity is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal hydrogen-ion
velocity](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of deuterium ions at the last
closed flux surface, resolved along increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The deuterium toroidal velocity is the local toroidal projection of the
density-weighted bulk-flow velocity of deuterium ions at the plasma
boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It excludes neutral
deuterium and is not a flux-surface average.

$$
v_{D,\phi}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\frac{\sum_{q\in Q_D}n_{D,q}\mathbf{v}_{D,q}}{\sum_{q\in Q_D}n_{D,q}}
$$

Here $Q_D$ is the set of included deuterium ion charge states, $n_{D,q}$ is
the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{D,q}$ is its bulk-flow
velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The local quantity is distinct from the
toroidal flux-surface-averaged deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary and
from the corresponding value at the [magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the deuterium bulk velocity points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top,
resolved along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame. It is the density-weighted mean over all helium-3 ion charge
states and is signed positive for flow toward increasing φ.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top is
the helium-3 ion bulk-flow component resolved along $\hat{\phi}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. For species-level helium-3,
this intensive quantity is the density-weighted mean over all helium-3 ion
charge states at the pedestal top.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\,^3\mathrm{He}}^{\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes helium-3 ion charge state,
$n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the number density of that charge
state at the pedestal top, $\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$
is its ion fluid velocity there, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity excludes radial and vertical components in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, vector speed, arithmetic averages over
charge states, and values at other loci such as the [magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis). It is defined where
the total helium-3 ion density in the averaging denominator is nonzero.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the helium-3 ion fluid velocity is directed
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal component of the helium-3 ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated
on the plasma boundary, along the direction of increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The helium-3 ion bulk-flow velocity at the plasma boundary is the
density-weighted mean flow of helium-3 ions over their ion charge states,
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface, or separatrix. It
describes toroidal motion rather than the full velocity vector.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{c6,{}^3\mathrm{He}} = \mathbf{u}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion bulk-flow velocity
and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Unlike the flux-surface-averaged helium-3 boundary velocity, this quantity
is the velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary and does not imply
flux-surface averaging.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the helium-4 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the
H-mode pressure pedestal top, resolved along the direction of increasing
toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the helium-4 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the
H-mode pressure pedestal top, resolved along the direction of increasing
toroidal angle, is the signed bulk-flow component of helium-4 ions along
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
pedestal top is the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pressure pedestal. As a
species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all
helium-4 ionization charge states in the ion population.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal component at the pedestal top is
defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{ped}}^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} =
\frac{\sum_q n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} \left(\mathbf{v}_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}
{\sum_q n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}}
$$

where $q$ labels helium-4 ionization charge states, $n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}$
is the local number density of charge state $q$,
$\mathbf{v}_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}$ is its fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is
the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$; all quantities are
evaluated at the pedestal-top location.

This quantity is local to the pedestal top and is not an average over the
full pedestal or scrape-off layer. It is a species-level helium-4 velocity,
so it differs from charge-state-resolved helium-4 velocities by the
density-weighted charge-state aggregation and from other isotope velocities
only by the selected ion species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the helium-4 ion flow is in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons (4He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal component of the bulk-flow velocity of helium-4 ions
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local bulk-flow velocity component of helium-4 ions at
the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed magnetic flux surface.
It is not a flux-surface average.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the component is
defined by

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}4}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}4}}$ is the bulk-flow velocity of the
helium-4 ion population and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The boundary-local value is
distinct from the [toroidal helium-4 velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and from a
flux-surface-averaged helium velocity.
