sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons (4He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Toroidal fluid velocity of hydrogen ions at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along increasing toroidal angle in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion fluid velocity component tangent to the
toroidal direction at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier. It describes the directed bulk motion of the hydrogen-ion
population, rather than its speed or a thermal velocity spread.

$$
v_{\phi,H} = \mathbf{v}_H \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_H$ is the hydrogen-ion fluid-velocity vector and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The pedestal-top locus denotes the inner shoulder of
the edge transport barrier and is distinct from the hydrogen-ion velocity
evaluated at an internal transport barrier, as in
[toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
The quantity is a directed component, not the magnitude of the hydrogen-ion
velocity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the hydrogen-ion fluid velocity points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Local toroidal component of the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity at the
plasma boundary, density-weighted over all hydrogen charge states.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity component tangent
to the toroidal direction at the plasma boundary, rather than a flux-surface
average. Hydrogen denotes the combined hydrogen-ion population.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{phi,H}(R,Z)=\mathbf{v}_H(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\phi},\qquad \mathbf{v}_H=\frac{\sum_q n_{H,q}\mathbf{v}_{H,q}}{\sum_q n_{H,q}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_H$ is the hydrogen bulk-flow velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the
toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
$n_{H,q}$ is the density of hydrogen charge state $q$, and
$\mathbf{v}_{H,q}$ is its bulk-flow velocity. The coordinates $R$ and $Z$
are major radius and vertical height, respectively. The local quantity is
distinct from the toroidal flux-surface-averaged hydrogen velocity at the
plasma boundary.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Toroidal ion velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component, in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the density-weighted
bulk-flow velocity of the total ion fluid at the plasma boundary. It is
distinct from random thermal motion and transport-model convection
velocities.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal ion velocity at the plasma boundary is the $\hat{\phi}$ component,
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, of the density-weighted
bulk-flow velocity of the total ion fluid evaluated on the plasma-boundary
surface. It represents directed collective ion motion, not random thermal
motion.

The total-ion population aggregation is the density-weighted mean over ion
species and charge states:

$$
v_{\phi i}\big|_{\partial p} =
\frac{\sum_{\alpha,c} n_{\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}\, v_{\phi,\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}}
{\sum_{\alpha,c} n_{\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}}
$$

where $v_{\phi i}\big|_{\partial p}$ is the toroidal ion velocity at the
plasma boundary, $\partial p$ denotes the plasma-boundary surface,
$n_{\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}$ is the ion number density for species
$\alpha$ in charge state $c$ at that surface, $v_{\phi,\alpha
c}\big|_{\partial p}$ is the corresponding toroidal bulk-flow velocity
component, and the sums run over all ion species and charge states.

The scope is the total ion fluid at the plasma-boundary surface: all ion
species and all charge states contribute, with intensive velocity values
averaged by density rather than summed. It excludes electrons and neutrals,
the radial component along $\hat{R}$ or any poloidal component in the
$R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and the
ion velocity magnitude. A transport-model convection velocity is outside
this definition unless it is explicitly the same density-weighted toroidal
bulk-flow component at the plasma boundary.

This parent fixes toroidal projection, total-ion population aggregation, and
plasma-boundary locus, but it does not by itself prescribe an additional
averaging operation over the boundary surface. The [flux-surface-averaged
toroidal ion velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary)
is a more specific child that adds flux-surface averaging to the same
quantity rather than adding the toroidal, ion-population, or boundary
qualifiers.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the total-ion bulk flow at the plasma
boundary is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron at the
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal iron velocity at the pedestal top is the density-weighted mean
bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron ions at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier. It includes all populated iron charge states
from Fe+ through fully stripped iron and excludes neutral iron.

For charge states $q=1,\ldots,26$, the velocity is defined by

$$
v_\phi^{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{26} n_q u_{\phi,q}}{\sum_{q=1}^{26} n_q}
$$

where $n_q$ is the number density of iron charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$,
$u_{\phi,q}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow component in m s$^{-1}$, and
$v_\phi^{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the resulting density-weighted velocity. This
charge-state aggregation is distinct from a charge-state-resolved velocity
and is analogous to [toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top); its locus differs from
[toroidal iron velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted iron-ion flow points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is
vertical height.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the bulk-flow velocity of iron impurity ions evaluated
at the last closed flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the bulk-flow velocity of
iron impurity ions at the last closed flux surface. The iron bulk-flow
velocity is the density-weighted mean over all included iron ionization
states.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the projection is
defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Fe}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the toroidal velocity component,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$; $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The value is local to the plasma boundary and is distinct from the
flux-surface-averaged toroidal iron velocity, which averages the same
projection over that surface. It is the iron-species counterpart of
[toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the iron bulk-flow velocity has a component
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top is the toroidal component of
the density-weighted mean krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the H-mode
pedestal top, taken over all krypton charge states. It is resolved along
increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame,
where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top is the toroidal component of
the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal-top
reference location. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the
density-weighted mean over all krypton ion charge states, not a sum of
charge-state velocities. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ basis
direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The charge-state aggregation and toroidal projection are defined by

$$
v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow velocity, and
$v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the resulting signed species-level toroidal
velocity.

This quantity is inferred from krypton line spectroscopy or other
impurity-flow diagnostics localized near the pedestal top, with
viewing-geometry corrections used to isolate the toroidal component. Because
line emission is often charge-state selective, interpretation must map
measured charge-state velocities onto the density-weighted species mean.
Momentum-balance or radial-force-balance analysis may combine this quantity
with poloidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top, pressure-gradient,
electric-field, and magnetic-field information.

No universal krypton-specific pedestal range applies across devices.
Representative signed impurity toroidal velocities at pedestal-top
conditions are commonly in the range $-5 \times 10^4$ to $5 \times 10^4$
m.s$^{-1}$, with higher-rotation cases approaching $\pm 10^5$ m.s$^{-1}$ in
either toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted krypton ion bulk flow at
the pedestal top is along $+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the local bulk flow velocity of krypton impurity ions
at the plasma boundary, projected along the φ direction of the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is a density-weighted mean over all krypton
ionization states represented in the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the local bulk flow velocity of krypton impurity ions
at the plasma boundary is the projection of the krypton ion bulk-flow
velocity onto the toroidal direction at the last closed flux surface. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. As an intensive species-level
quantity, the krypton bulk-flow velocity is the density-weighted mean over
all krypton ionization states represented in the plasma.

The boundary value is defined by projecting the charge-state-averaged
krypton bulk-flow velocity onto the toroidal unit vector at the last closed
flux surface:

$$
\left. v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}} \right|_{\mathrm{LCFS}}
=
\left.
\left(
\frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}}
\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}
\right|_{\mathrm{LCFS}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the toroidal krypton bulk-flow velocity, $z$
indexes krypton ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}$ is the number
density of krypton ions in ionization state $z$,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}$ is the bulk-flow velocity vector of that
ionization state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle.

This quantity is a local boundary value, not a flux-surface average; any
flux-surface-averaged krypton boundary velocity denotes an additional
average over the last closed flux surface. The unqualified krypton species
label denotes the density-weighted mean over charge states, not a sum of
velocity components.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the lithium impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the H-mode pedestal top. It represents the local azimuthal rotation of
lithium impurity ions at the steep-gradient edge transport barrier, not a
pedestal-region average.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal lithium ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top is the
$\hat{\phi}$-projection of the lithium impurity ion mean velocity vector at
the radial reference location where the H-mode edge transport barrier
steep-gradient region joins the flatter core profile. This is a
point-evaluated quantity, not a spatial average over the pedestal region.

The toroidal component is defined as:

$$
v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium ion fluid velocity vector
and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Lithium toroidal rotation at the pedestal is inferred from charge exchange
recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) using Doppler shifts of lithium spectral
lines following charge exchange with an injected neutral beam. The
pedestal-top reference location is identified from the steep-gradient region
of the relevant kinetic profile. Comparable pedestal-top rotation
measurements for other impurity species are provided by
[toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top)
and
[toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top);
the lithium ion rotation at other radial reference points is covered by
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis)
and
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}}$ points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the density-weighted neon-ion fluid velocity at the
core-side top of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neon-ion velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the
density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid velocities of all represented
neon ion charge states at the core-side shoulder of the edge transport
barrier. It is a signed projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
V_{\mathrm{Ne},\phi} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q} v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}}
$$

Here, $q$ labels neon ion charge state, $n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}$ is its number
density, and $v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}$ is its toroidal fluid-velocity
component. The quantity is distinguished from [toroidal neon velocity at the
internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) by its
pedestal-top location and is a species-specific counterpart of [toroidal
hydrogen velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of
the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon impurity ions at the last closed
flux surface, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the
density-weighted mean over all neon ion charge states and is local, not a
flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of
the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon impurity ions at the last closed
flux surface. The toroidal component is taken in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Because no neon ionization state
is specified, the elemental neon velocity is the density-weighted mean over
all neon ion charge states present at that locus.

The component and charge-state aggregation are defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \left(\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes neon ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is its
bulk velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity is a local boundary value and does not imply a flux-surface
average, poloidal average, toroidal average, or charge-state sum. The
flux-surface-averaged boundary counterpart is
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary; the same
toroidal component at other radial loci includes
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis)
and
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted neon ion flow is in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the area-normalized net momentum-transfer source for a
specified neutral internal state, resolved in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source term for a
neutral internal state is the signed projection of the state-resolved net
momentum-transfer source onto the local toroidal direction. It represents
the toroidal part of the area-normalized momentum exchange between that
neutral internal state and the plasma or other interacting populations.

The component is defined by projection onto the toroidal unit vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
S_{\phi,n,\alpha} = \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi
$$

where $S_{\phi,n,\alpha}$ is the toroidal momentum-source component,
$\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}$ is the area-normalized vector momentum source for
neutral species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi$
is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
coordinate.

This quantity is resolved for the specified neutral internal state:
contributions from other neutral internal states are excluded, and no sum
over neutral internal states is implied. It applies to the edge-plasma
momentum exchange and uses the net source rather than an individual transfer
process.

This component is derived from the vector [neutral state momentum
source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source). It is distinct from
the state-summed [toroidal neutral momentum
source](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_source), which combines the
corresponding toroidal contributions from all neutral internal states, and
from the field-aligned [parallel neutral state momentum
source](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_source), which uses a different
projection direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the area-normalized net momentum-transfer
source for the specified neutral internal state has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of ionized nitrogen across its
charge states, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge
transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal nitrogen velocity at the pedestal top is the density-weighted
mean flow of ionized nitrogen ions over all nitrogen charge states at the
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It describes flow
rather than abundance, which is represented by nitrogen density at the
pedestal top.

For nitrogen charge states $q=1,\ldots,7$, the species velocity is defined
by

$$
v_{\phi,N} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{7} n_q v_{\phi,q}}{\sum_{q=1}^{7} n_q}
$$

where $n_q$ is the number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$ and
$v_{\phi,q}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$, measured in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Neutral nitrogen is excluded.
The pedestal-top value is distinguished from the corresponding [toroidal
nitrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) by its edge-barrier
location.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted velocity points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of nitrogen ions, evaluated on
the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal nitrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity is the density-weighted mean
directed motion of all nitrogen ion charge states along the geometric
toroidal direction at the plasma boundary, which is the last closed magnetic
flux surface.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N}} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{N},z} v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},z}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{N},z}}
$$

where $z$ is the nitrogen ion charge-state index, $n_{\mathrm{N},z}$ is the
number density of that charge state, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},z}$ is its
toroidal bulk-flow velocity. Neutral nitrogen is excluded. The corresponding
[toroidal oxygen velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) has the same
definition with oxygen replacing nitrogen, while [toroidal nitrogen velocity
at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) uses
a different evaluation locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the H-mode pedestal reference location, projected along the direction of
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal oxygen velocity at the pedestal top characterizes the impurity
ion fluid flow projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction at the H-mode edge
transport barrier's outer shoulder, where the steep-gradient pedestal region
transitions to the flatter core profile. Oxygen (atomic number $Z = 8$) is a
common intrinsic or deliberately seeded impurity in tokamaks, present in
charge states spanning O$^{5+}$ through O$^{8+}$ in the pedestal; this
quantity represents the oxygen fluid velocity aggregated over the
predominant charge states unless a specific ionization state is separately
resolved.

The toroidal component is defined by the projection:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
and $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen ion fluid velocity vector
evaluated at the pedestal-top locus.

This quantity is measured via charge exchange recombination spectroscopy,
which resolves the Doppler shift of oxygen emission lines following charge
exchange with an injected neutral beam. Toroidal rotation velocities at the
pedestal top in H-mode span roughly $10^3$–$10^5$ m s$^{-1}$, reflecting
neutral beam torque input, intrinsic rotation, and impurity-specific flow
corrections. Comparison with
[toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top)
and
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top)
enables cross-species benchmarking of pedestal rotation profiles.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion bulk flow velocity evaluated
at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The toroidal velocity of oxygen impurity ions at the plasma boundary
quantifies the toroidal momentum carried by the oxygen ion population at the
last closed flux surface, which separates the magnetically confined plasma
from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This local point value is
distinct from the flux-surface-averaged quantity
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary, which
integrates the velocity weighted by the boundary flux-surface geometry.

The toroidal component $v_\phi$ is the projection of the oxygen bulk flow
velocity onto the toroidal direction:

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O}$ is the oxygen ion bulk flow velocity and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Oxygen toroidal velocity at the boundary is primarily measured by charge
exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), exploiting the Doppler shift of
oxygen emission lines to extract the ion flow velocity component along
$\hat{\phi}$. Analogous boundary velocities for other impurity species
include
[toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary)
and
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed
from above in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short:
Toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top is the volume-integrated
toroidal linear momentum of the confined plasma inside the pedestal-top flux
surface, summed over electrons and all ion species. It is the pedestal-top
endpoint of total toroidal plasma momentum, not a local momentum density or
toroidal angular momentum.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top is the cumulative toroidal
component of plasma linear momentum contained inside the flux surface
located at the top of the H-mode pedestal, summed over electrons and all ion
species. The toroidal component is taken in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

Let $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ denote the radial flux-surface label of the
pedestal-top flux surface and let $V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})$ be the plasma
volume enclosed by that surface. The quantity is the radial cumulative
[toroidal_total_plasma_momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum)
evaluated at the pedestal-top endpoint:

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{ped}} = P_\phi(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}) = \int_{V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})} \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x}) v_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_\phi(\rho)$ is the cumulative toroidal plasma momentum inside the
flux surface labeled by $\rho$, $s$ indexes electrons and all ion species,
$m_s$ is the species particle mass, $n_s$ is the species number density,
$v_{\phi,s}$ is the signed toroidal velocity component, $\mathbf{x}$ is
position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

This quantity is an endpoint value of a volume-integrated radial function:
it is not the local toroidal momentum density $\sum_s m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ on
the pedestal-top surface, and it is not a flux-surface average. It is also
not toroidal angular momentum; the angular-momentum integral would include
the moment arm $R$ multiplying the toroidal linear-momentum density. The
same cumulative quantity has related endpoint values at the [magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis) and at the plasma
boundary.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net toroidal plasma momentum points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total plasma toroidal momentum, summed over ion species and electrons

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted mean toroidal velocity of tungsten impurity ions at the
H-mode pedestal top, averaged over all tungsten ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal tungsten velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the
density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid velocities of tungsten impurity
ions over their ionization states. It is evaluated at the core-side shoulder
of the edge transport barrier in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The defining charge-state average is

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{W}} = \frac{\sum_q n_q v_{\phi,q}}{\sum_q n_q}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{W}}$ is the tungsten toroidal velocity, $n_q$ is the
number density of tungsten ions in charge state $q$, and $v_{\phi,q}$ is
their toroidal velocity component.

The average is density-weighted over tungsten ion charge states, not a sum
of velocities and not a flux-surface average. It therefore differs from the
toroidal flux-surface-averaged tungsten velocity at the plasma boundary;
[toroidal carbon velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) is the analogous
species-specific quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the tungsten velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of tungsten
impurity ions at the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma
from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the tungsten impurity-ion
bulk velocity at the plasma boundary, defined on the last closed flux
surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer. It is a
density-weighted mean over the included tungsten ion charge states.

$$
v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{W}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)=\\frac{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)\\left[\\mathbf{v}_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)\\cdot\\hat{\\boldsymbol{\\phi}}\\right]}{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)}
$$

Here, $q$ is the tungsten ion charge state, $n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its
number density, $\\mathbf{v}_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its bulk velocity,
$\\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the boundary, and $\\hat{\\boldsymbol{\\phi}}$
is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$
frame. Unlike
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary, this
quantity is local rather than flux-surface averaged.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the tungsten-ion velocity component points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of xenon ions, averaged over
all ionization states at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity
at the H-mode pedestal top. It is the density-weighted mean over all xenon
ionization states, rather than a sum of their velocities.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe},q} V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe},q}}
$$

Here $q$ labels xenon ionization state, $n_{\mathrm{Xe},q}$ is the number
density of that state, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe},q}$ is its toroidal
bulk-flow component. The denominator is the total xenon ion density
corresponding to xenon density at the pedestal top. The value is evaluated
at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier and is
distinct from [toroidal xenon velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
[toroidal xenon velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$ is
positive in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated on the
plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the
geometric toroidal direction at the plasma boundary. The xenon-ion bulk
velocity is the density-weighted mean over all xenon ion charge states and
excludes thermal random motion.

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity in m
s$^{-1}$ and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ frame. The plasma
boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface. This local value is
distinct from the flux-surface average
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $v_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: total_ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Positive e-folding distance for the outward decrease of total ion number
density across magnetic flux surfaces in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the positive cross-field decay length of the total ion
number density in the scrape-off layer. It is the species- and
charge-state-summed specialization of ion decay length over the scrape-off
layer.

$$
\lambda_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \left|\frac{1}{n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}\frac{\partial n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial \ell_\perp}\right|^{-1}
$$

Here $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density, summed over the
included ion species and charge states, and $\ell_\perp$ is outward distance
normal to magnetic flux surfaces, measured in m. The quantity excludes
electron and neutral-particle densities and is non-negative by definition.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion density radial decay length inv(grad ni/ni)

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total ion number density at the plasma boundary is the local particle count
per volume, summing all charged ion species and charge states while
excluding neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Total ion density at the plasma boundary is the local number density of all
positively charged ion populations at the separatrix, the last closed flux
surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off
layer. It is the charge-state-summed specialization of ion density at the
plasma boundary.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state
$Z$, and the sums include every charged ion species and charge state present
at the boundary.

Neutral particles are excluded, and each ion contributes one particle
regardless of its charge. The corresponding surface average is
flux-surface-averaged total ion density at the plasma boundary, which
averages this local quantity over the separatrix.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of all charged ion species at the
plasma boundary, summed over charge states and excluding neutral particles.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ion

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_i\rangle = \oint n_i\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_i\rangle$ is the averaged total ion number density, $n_i$
is the local total ion number density, $S$ is the plasma-boundary flux
surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic
flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity includes all charged ion species and is summed over their
positive charge states; neutral particles are excluded. It is a flux-surface
average rather than a local point value, a volume average, or a
neutral-inclusive density.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [total ion number density at the
plasma boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), replacing that
pointwise value with inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting. It differs
from the [line-averaged total ion
density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density), which averages the same
charge-state-summed ion population along a specified plasma chord rather
than over the plasma-boundary flux surface.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

Related quantities:
[flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary),
[flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: total_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of
total plasma momentum, distinct from the plasma bulk flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective,
non-diffusive transport of total plasma momentum for a selected momentum
component and transport direction. It is a transport closure quantity, not
an actual plasma bulk flow velocity.

For each selected total-momentum component and transport direction, the
convective total-momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}} P_\mathrm{tot}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding
convective flux of total plasma momentum, $V_{\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}}$
is the total momentum convection velocity, and $P_\mathrm{tot}$ is the
corresponding total plasma momentum density. The definition applies
componentwise when the momentum component or transport direction is
resolved.

The scope is total plasma momentum only; it does not denote
species-resolved, charge-state-resolved, neutral-only, or
attributed-contribution momentum convection velocities. A resolved
projection of this quantity is the [parallel total momentum convection
velocity](name:parallel_total_momentum_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the associated convective total-momentum flux
is in the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported
total-momentum density.

NAMES.name: total_power_at_separatrix
NAMES.short:
Net energy power leaving the confined plasma through the last closed
magnetic flux surface and entering the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Separatrix power is the net global energy loss from the confined plasma into
the scrape-off layer across the last closed magnetic flux surface. It
represents the aggregate power crossing the entire separatrix rather than a
local surface value.

The defining boundary integral is

$$
P_{\rm sep} = \oint_{S_{\rm sep}} \mathbf{S}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix power, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the last
closed magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{S}_E$ is the net plasma-energy flux
density, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the confined
plasma toward the scrape-off layer, and $dA$ is an element of separatrix
area.

This is a total, net quantity integrated over the complete separatrix. It
applies to the confined plasma as a whole, with no selection of species,
reaction channel, or individual transport mechanism; outward energy transfer
is the plasma loss represented by the quantity. It is not a pointwise
energy-flux density or a power associated with a single surface location.

The boundary total is distinct from [radiated power over the core
region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region), which describes
electromagnetic power emitted within the core and is not necessarily equal
to power crossing the separatrix. It is also distinct from [power due to
conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), which describes
conduction-mediated power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces downstream of
the separatrix.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Power through separatrix

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed
over all tritium charge states.
NAMES.long:
Tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of tritium ions at the core-side shoulder of the edge
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{T}} = \sum_z n_{\mathrm{T}}^{z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the tritium ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{T}}^{z+}$ is the number density of tritium ions with charge
state $z$, and $z$ is the positive integer charge state. For tritium, the
physically ionized population has one positive charge state, so the sum
reduces to the density of singly ionized tritium.

The quantity applies only to tritium ions and is evaluated locally at the
pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is not a
chord-, volume-, or species-averaged density, and it excludes neutral
tritium and all non-tritium species.

This is the tritium-specific component of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), rather than the corresponding total or
non-species-resolved density. The same tritium ion density concept evaluated
at a different transport-barrier location is [tritium density at the
internal transport
barrier](name:tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the tritium-ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from
the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local tritium-ion number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the
tritium-ion distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is
tritium-ion velocity, $f_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion phase-space
distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to ionized tritium and excludes neutral
tritium, deuterium, protium, electrons, impurity ions, and total ion
density. It is a local boundary value, with no averaging over the boundary
surface or over a volume; for tritium, the relevant positive ion population
is singly ionized tritium, so no aggregation over multiple positive
ionization stages is applied.

It is the tritium-specific instance of [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
flux-surface-averaged tritium density at the plasma boundary instead
represents the average of tritium-ion density over the same last closed
magnetic flux surface, while [hydrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [deuterium density
at the plasma boundary](name:deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) refer to
different hydrogen-isotope ion populations.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of tritium ions averaged over the plasma boundary, summed
over all tritium ion charge states and excluding neutral tritium.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tritium

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{T}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{T}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{T}}\rangle$ is the averaged tritium-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the local tritium-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is summed over all tritium ion charge states and excludes
neutral tritium. It is a flux-surface average, not a local point value,
volume average, or chord average.

The average is formed from the local [tritium density at the plasma
boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary) by applying
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting over the surface. It differs from
the [volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density),
which uses a volume rather than a flux-surface domain.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Tungsten ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of ionized tungsten, summed over all tungsten charge
states.
NAMES.long:
Tungsten ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of ionized tungsten at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{W}}} n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the total tungsten-ion number density, $q$ is the
positive tungsten charge state, $Z_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the atomic number of
tungsten, and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is the number density of tungsten ions
in charge state $q$. Neutral tungsten is excluded.

This quantity applies to the local tungsten-ion population at the pedestal
top, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate
at the pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).
It is summed over all positive tungsten charge states and is neither
flux-surface averaged nor line-of-sight averaged.

It is the tungsten-specific component of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [tungsten density at the internal
transport barrier](name:tungsten_density_at_internal_transport_barrier),
which is evaluated on an internal-transport-barrier flux surface, this
quantity is evaluated at the pedestal-top location.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_separatrix
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Tungsten-ion number density on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed
over all positive ionization states and distinguished from its flux-surface
average.
NAMES.long:
Tungsten-ion number density at the plasma boundary represents the local
population of positively charged tungsten ions on the separatrix, the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The same physical quantity may also be
evaluated as a flux-surface average over that boundary surface; the local
and averaged forms are distinct.

The charge-state-summed local density is defined from the velocity
distributions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{Z=1}^{Z_{\max}} \int f_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the tungsten-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is a
position on the separatrix, $Z$ is the positive tungsten ion charge state,
$Z_{\max}$ is the highest included charge state, $f_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z}$ is the
velocity distribution of that charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies to tungsten ions evaluated at the plasma boundary and
sums over all positive ionization states. It excludes neutral tungsten and
does not select an individual charge state. The local form is evaluated at a
boundary position, whereas the flux-surface-averaged tungsten density at the
plasma boundary averages the same charge-state-summed density over the
boundary flux surface.

The flux-surface-averaged quantity is therefore an aggregation of this local
density over the same separatrix, not a different species or charge-state
convention. It is distinct from [volume-averaged tungsten
density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), which averages tungsten-ion
density over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Magnetic vector-potential quantity covering the full potential, its
directional components, and fluctuations about an equilibrium potential.
NAMES.long:
The magnetic vector potential is a vector field whose spatial curl
determines the associated magnetic field. A perturbation denotes the
departure from an equilibrium vector potential and may be represented by a
reference-scaled amplitude.

$$
\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}
$$

where $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic vector-potential field, $\mathbf{B}$ is
its associated magnetic-field vector, and $\nabla \times$ is the spatial
curl operator. The potential is gage-dependent: replacing $\mathbf{A}$ by
$\mathbf{A} + \nabla\chi$, where $\chi$ is a scalar gage function, leaves
$\mathbf{B}$ unchanged. The family includes directional components such as
the [radial vector potential](name:radial_vector_potential) and [poloidal
vector potential](name:poloidal_vector_potential), as well as the perturbed
vector potential.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a specified gage-fixed component points along
its corresponding positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ increases away from the symmetry axis, $\phi$
increases toroidally, and $Z$ increases vertically.

NAMES.name: poloidal_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Magnetic vector-potential quantity given by the signed projection of the
electromagnetic vector potential onto the local poloidal direction tangent
to increasing poloidal angle in the poloidal cross-section of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is
toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the magnetic vector potential is the signed
projection of the electromagnetic vector potential onto the local poloidal
direction in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The local poloidal unit vector is tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$; $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The component is defined by the scalar projection of the vector potential
onto the poloidal unit direction:

$$
A_\theta = \mathbf{A}\cdot\hat{e}_\theta
$$

where $A_\theta$ is the poloidal vector potential, $\mathbf{A}$ is the
magnetic vector-potential field, and $\hat{e}_\theta$ is the local unit
vector tangent to increasing $\theta$ in the $R$-$Z$ plane.

This quantity is a component of the gage-dependent vector potential, not a
component of the magnetic field. The associated magnetic-field vector
satisfies $\mathbf{B}=\nabla\times\mathbf{A}$ after a gage is fixed, and
replacing $\mathbf{A}$ by $\mathbf{A}+\nabla\chi$ leaves $\mathbf{B}$
unchanged. Related directional variants include the [radial vector
potential](name:radial_vector_potential), [poloidal magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_magnetic_vector_potential), [radial magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_magnetic_vector_potential), and [vertical magnetic
vector potential](name:vertical_magnetic_vector_potential).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the gage-fixed vector potential has a
component along $\hat{e}_\theta$, the local direction tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Magnetic vector potential, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_neutral_species_density
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Mean number density of a specified neutral species over the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the spatial mean of the local number density of one
specified neutral species within the plasma volume enclosed by the last
closed flux surface during plasma initiation. The local quantity is
distinguished from [neutral_density](name:neutral_density), which is
evaluated at a point.

$$
\overline{n}_0 = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_0(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_0(\mathbf{r})$ is the local number density of the specified neutral
species at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the volume enclosed
by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average is species-specific and excludes neutral particles outside the
enclosed volume. It is not the charge-state or population aggregate
represented by [total_neutral_density](name:total_neutral_number_density),
nor the volume average of ion density represented by
[volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Volume averaged density of this neutral species (averaged over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different neutral species

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Xenon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over
all xenon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Xenon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local
concentration of xenon ions with all positive charge states combined.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the total xenon ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of xenon ions with charge state
$z$, and $z$ is the positive integer xenon charge state.

The quantity applies locally at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, the
inner shoulder of the edge transport barrier, whose position is defined by
the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over xenon ions from the singly ionized through fully ionized states
and excludes neutral xenon; it is not a chord, flux-surface, or volume
average.

This is the xenon-specific component of the total [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), whereas [xenon
density](name:xenon_density) denotes the corresponding local xenon ion
density without fixing the pedestal-top locus. The same charge-state
aggregation evaluated at another boundary location is given by [xenon
density at the plasma boundary](name:xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary is the amount of the
xenon ion population per physical volume at the last closed magnetic flux
surface. It is the local boundary value, not a flux-surface average.

The local charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{54}\int f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the xenon ion charge-state
number, $f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}$ is the velocity distribution function for charge
state $Z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. The aggregation is additive over all xenon ion charge
states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral
xenon atoms. The value is local at the boundary rather than averaged over
that surface.

This entry specializes the population-unspecified
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to xenon ions.
The corresponding flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
applies the same xenon charge-state aggregation after averaging over the
plasma-boundary flux surface, so it is distinct from this local quantity.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of xenon ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux
surface, summed over all xenon ion charge states and excluding neutral
xenon.
NAMES.long:
Number density of xenon

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\rangle$ is the averaged xenon-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the local xenon-ion number density, $S$ is the
plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is charge-state-summed over xenon ions and is not a local
point value, a volume average, or a density that includes neutral xenon. It
is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [xenon ion density at
the plasma boundary](name:xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary), with
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting replacing the pointwise value by
its surface mean. It differs from the [volume-averaged xenon
density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which averages over the plasma
volume rather than over the plasma-boundary surface.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

Related quantities:
[flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary),
[flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

NAMES.name: coulomb_logarithm_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short:
Natural logarithm of the effective upper-to-lower impact-parameter ratio
governing cumulative small-angle Coulomb scattering between charged
particles at the pressure pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
The Coulomb logarithm at the [pressure pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal) expresses the
effective logarithmic range of impact parameters contributing to cumulative
small-angle Coulomb scattering between charged particles at that location.

Its defining relation is

$$
\ln\Lambda = \ln\left(\frac{b_{\max}}{b_{\min}}\right)
$$

where $\ln\Lambda$ is the local Coulomb logarithm, $\ln$ denotes the natural
logarithm, $\Lambda$ is the effective impact-parameter ratio, $b_{\max}$ is
the upper impact-parameter cutoff associated with plasma screening, and
$b_{\min}$ is the lower cutoff associated with strong deflections or quantum
diffraction, as applicable. Both cutoffs refer to local plasma conditions at
the pressure pedestal top.

This quantity is the local evaluation of the [Coulomb
logarithm](name:coulomb_logarithm), not an average or integral across the
pedestal. No particular colliding species pair is specified.

NAMES.name: diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Signed projection of the heat-viscosity electric-current contribution onto
the local diamagnetic direction in a collisional magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Diamagnetic current density due to heat viscosity is the local diamagnetic
component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity
stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection is

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic current density due to heat
viscosity, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the unit vector along the designated
local diamagnetic direction, perpendicular to the magnetic field. The
positive orientation of this direction must be specified by the local
component convention; the heat-viscosity attribution alone does not
determine it.

This is a local, unaveraged contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density), not a surface-integrated current or the
total current density from all mechanisms. Only the heat-viscosity
contribution is included; the definition imposes no restriction to a
particular plasma region.

Unlike [parallel current density due to heat
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), which
projects the same parent vector along the local magnetic field, this
quantity projects onto the local diamagnetic direction. The diamagnetic
qualifier identifies the projection, not a replacement of the heat-viscosity
mechanism by pressure-gradient-driven current.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the heat-viscosity current has a component
along the designated positive local diamagnetic direction
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}$.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Number density of oxygen ions flux-surface-averaged at the plasma boundary,
summed over all charged oxygen ionization states and excluding neutral
oxygen.
NAMES.long:
Number density of oxygen

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{O}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{O}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, /\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{O}}\rangle$ is the averaged oxygen-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the local oxygen-ion number density, $S$ is the
plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux. The factor $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of the
spatial gradient of poloidal magnetic flux, and both closed integrals extend
over $S$.

This quantity is not a local point value, a volume average, an individual
charge-state density, or a density that includes neutral oxygen. It is the
flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [oxygen density at the plasma
boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary), using
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting to replace the pointwise value with
a surface mean.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge
flux carried by ions, obtained by charge-weighting their directed particle
motion across unit area.
NAMES.long:
Ion current density $\mathbf{J}_i$ is the vector density of conventional
electric charge flux carried by ions. It represents signed charge transport
from all included ion species and charge states.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the
ion distribution functions:

$$
\mathbf{J}_i(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s \int \mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s n_s \mathbf{u}_s
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes ion species and
charge states, $q_s$ is the charge of population $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_s$ is its velocity-space distribution function, $n_s$
is its number density, and $\mathbf{u}_s$ is its mean velocity.

This quantity includes ion-carried charge flux and excludes electron-carried
and displacement-current density. Its qualified instances may select a
magnetic-field-aligned projection such as [parallel ion current
density](name:parallel_ion_current_density), a temporal fluctuation measure
such as [fluctuating ion current
density](name:fluctuating_ion_current_density), or an ion-saturation
collection condition.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when an ion-carried charge-flux component is
aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or oriented
surface normal.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Parallel ion current density is the signed conventional electric-charge flux
carried by ions along the local magnetic field at a plasma-facing surface.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion current density at a plasma-facing surface is the signed
projection of the [ion current-density vector](name:ion_current_density)
onto the local magnetic-field direction.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\parallel,i} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\mathbf{J}_i
$$

where $j_{\parallel,i}$ is the parallel ion current density, $\mathbf{J}_i$
is the ion current-density vector, and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity applies locally at a plasma-facing surface, including a
divertor surface; it is not surface- or flux-surface-averaged. Contributions
from all included ion species and charge states are summed algebraically.
Each charge-state contribution equals its [parallel ion charge-state
particle flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) multiplied by
its electric charge. Electron current is excluded.

It is the ion contribution to [current density](name:current_density)
projected along the magnetic field, whereas [parallel current
density](name:parallel_current_density) has no ion-only restriction. It is
neither the magnitude of the ion current-density vector nor its projection
onto the surface normal.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net conventional ion charge transport is in
the direction of the local magnetic-field vector.

NAMES.name: saturated_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Conventional ion charge flux per collecting area at a Langmuir-probe
collector in the negative-bias saturation regime, where electron collection
is suppressed.
NAMES.long:
The saturated ion current density is the limiting conventional ion
charge-flux density reaching a Langmuir-probe collector biased sufficiently
negative relative to the plasma to suppress electron collection. It is the
ion-saturation specialization of [ion current
density](name:ion_current_density), rather than the unrestricted [current
density](name:current_density) carried by all charged particles.

The charge-weighted ion flux defines the current-density vector:

$$
\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}} = \sum_a \sum_{z\geq 1} z e\,\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,z}^{\mathrm{sat}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the saturated ion current-density
vector, $i$ denotes the ion population, $a$ labels ion species, $z$ is the
positive ionic charge number, $e$ is the elementary charge, and
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,z}^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is the particle-flux vector of
that species and charge state at the collector in ion saturation.

The sum includes all collected ion species and charge states, weighted by
their electric charge. Electron and neutral-particle contributions are
excluded. This is a charge flux per collecting area, not an area-integrated
current or an unweighted ion particle flux.

The [saturated ion current](name:saturated_ion_current) is the surface
integral of the collector-directed component:
$I_{i,\mathrm{sat}}=\int_S\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{col}}\,dA$,
where $I_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the collected saturated ion current, $S$ is
the collecting surface, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{col}}$ is the unit normal directed from the
plasma into the collector. The [fluctuating saturated ion current
density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density) is the temporal
standard deviation of the collected current-density component; no temporal
statistical operation is implied here.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive ion charge flows from the plasma
into the collector, as defined by the collector-directed normal.

NAMES.name: fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Temporal standard deviation of the ion charge flux per collecting area at a
Langmuir-probe collector biased into ion saturation, with electron
collection suppressed.
NAMES.long:
The fluctuating saturated ion current density is the temporal standard
deviation of [saturated ion current
density](name:saturated_ion_current_density). It describes the amplitude of
boundary-plasma ion-collection fluctuations, not the mean saturation level.

The fluctuation amplitude is defined by:

$$
\sigma_{j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}} = \sqrt{\left\langle\left(j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}(t)-\left\langle j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}\right\rangle_t\right)^2\right\rangle_t}
$$

where $\sigma_{j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}}$ is the temporal standard deviation,
$j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}(t)$ is the collected ion saturation current density at
time $t$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes temporal averaging over the
same specified interval at one collector. The subscript $i$ denotes ions and
$\mathrm{sat}$ denotes the ion-saturation regime.

The collector is sufficiently negatively biased relative to the local plasma
to suppress electron collection. The underlying ion signal includes the
charge-weighted contributions of all collected ion species and charge
states; the standard deviation is taken after those contributions are
combined, rather than summed from their separate standard deviations.
Electron-current fluctuations are excluded, and the averaging is temporal
rather than spatial.

This is a fluctuation statistic of collector-defined [current
density](name:current_density), not an instantaneous signed perturbation or
an uncertainty in the temporal mean. Unlike [parallel fluctuating ion
current density](name:parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density), it refers
to ion-saturation collection rather than projection onto the local
magnetic-field direction.
