NAMES.name: momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper
bound on momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport
closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction
unchanged.
NAMES.long:
In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive
closures can produce momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically
realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions such
as the scrape-off layer and divertor. A flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_m$
is introduced to bound the effective flux: the limited momentum-flux density
magnitude cannot exceed $\alpha_m$ times a free-streaming reference scale,
while the sign follows the underlying diffusive flux direction.

The limited momentum-flux density $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is formed by the
harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux
estimate, $\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} = m n v_{\mathrm{th}}^2$ is the free-streaming
scale with $m$ the particle mass, $n$ the number density, and
$v_{\mathrm{th}}$ the thermal speed. When $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg
\alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm \alpha_m
\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$; when $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \ll \alpha_m
\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

Specializations target individual projection directions, such as
parallel_momentum_coefficient for field-aligned transport, and individual
particle populations, such as ion_state_momentum_coefficient for specific
ion charge states or parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient for
neutral-particle parallel transport. The coefficient is intrinsically
non-negative; values in the range 0.1–1 are common in edge-plasma
simulations, selected by calibration against experimental separatrix and
divertor data.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient that scales the
collisionless free-streaming bound component-by-component, capping flux
magnitude while preserving its sign.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for
gradient-driven momentum transport, providing one limiter factor for each
selected spatial transport component. It is the ion specialization of
[momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
scaling the collisionless free-streaming bound while preserving the
direction supplied by the underlying diffusive closure.

For each selected component, the limited momentum-flux density is defined by
the harmonic-mean closure:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\alpha_m$ is the momentum-flux limiter coefficient,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming reference
momentum-flux density, $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive
momentum-flux estimate, and $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the resulting limited
flux density.

The shared quantity spans parallel, poloidal, and radial ion components;
[parallel ion momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and
[poloidal ion momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) are
concrete instances. It applies to momentum flux rather than particle, heat,
or energy flux, and the coefficient is non-negative.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming
upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density component-by-component
in edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum coefficient is the neutral-particle specialization of
the general momentum_coefficient vector, providing one dimensionless limiter
factor per spatial direction for neutral momentum transport in multi-fluid
edge plasma models. Each directional component independently bounds the
corresponding neutral momentum flux density, preventing unphysical
exceedance of the free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is
large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The component $\alpha_\alpha$ in direction $\hat{e}_\alpha$ is defined as
the ratio of the modeled flux to its free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_\alpha = \frac{\Pi_\alpha}{\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free}}
$$

where $\Pi_\alpha$ is the modeled neutral momentum flux density in direction
$\hat{e}_\alpha$ and $\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free} = m_n n_n u_\alpha^{\rm free}$
is the free-streaming estimate, with $m_n$ the neutral particle mass, $n_n$
the neutral number density, and $u_\alpha^{\rm free}$ the direction-$\alpha$
free-streaming reference speed. The constraint $\alpha_\alpha \in [0, 1]$
ensures the closure preserves the sign of the momentum flux while bounding
its magnitude. The field-aligned component is analogous to
parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient, which resolves the same
quantity by internal neutral state.

Components are computed within edge-plasma transport closures as a function
of local collisionality; values near 1 characterize the collision-dominated
limit, while values near 0 indicate strongly free-streaming conditions where
the limiter actively constrains the flux.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless factor setting the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on
field-aligned ion momentum flux without reversing the flux direction.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum flux limiter coefficient sets the collisionless
free-streaming cap for gradient-driven transport of ion
[momentum](name:momentum) along the local magnetic field. Limiting restricts
the flux magnitude without reversing its direction.

The coefficient defines the cap through:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cap}} = \alpha_{i,\parallel}\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\alpha_{i,\parallel}$ is this coefficient,
$\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cap}}$ is the nonnegative upper bound on the
field-aligned ion momentum-flux magnitude, and
$\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless
free-streaming reference magnitude. The subscript $i$ identifies the
selected ion population, and $\parallel$ denotes the local magnetic-field
direction. The limited flux magnitude cannot exceed this cap; the
coefficient does not prescribe a particular interpolation between the
unlimited flux and the cap.

This is the field-aligned component of the [ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), whereas the
[poloidal ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) selects
the poloidal component. It applies to ion rather than neutral momentum
transport and is a limiter parameter, not a momentum flux or diffusivity. No
sum or average over ion species or charge states is implied.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless factor scaling the collisionless free-streaming cap on the
magnetic-field-parallel component of neutral momentum flux in edge-fluid
transport closures.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient sets the free-streaming upper bound on the parallel
component of neutral-particle [momentum](name:momentum) flux in edge-fluid
transport closures. Parallel denotes the local magnetic-field direction,
used as a geometric reference without implying that neutral particles follow
magnetic field lines.

The limiting flux magnitude is defined by

$$
\Pi^{0,\max}_{\parallel} = \alpha^0_{\parallel}\Pi^{0,\mathrm{fs}}_{\parallel}
$$

where $\alpha^0_{\parallel}$ is this nonnegative limiter coefficient,
$\Pi^{0,\mathrm{fs}}_{\parallel}$ is the nonnegative collisionless
free-streaming reference magnitude, and $\Pi^{0,\max}_{\parallel}$ is the
resulting upper bound. The superscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and
$\parallel$ denotes the magnetic-field-parallel component. The limited
neutral momentum flux $\Pi^0_{\parallel}$ satisfies
$|\Pi^0_{\parallel}|\leq\Pi^{0,\max}_{\parallel}$; limiting its magnitude
does not reverse its direction. The free-streaming normalization and
limiting function are specified by the transport closure, not by this
coefficient alone.

This quantity is the parallel directional component of the [neutral momentum
flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
not the momentum flux itself or a momentum diffusivity. It applies to the
selected neutral population without explicit internal-state resolution,
unlike the [parallel neutral-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
No summation or averaging rule for state-resolved coefficients is implied.

NAMES.name: toroidal_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper
bound on toroidal momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport
closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction
unchanged.
NAMES.long:
In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive
closures can produce toroidal momentum-flux densities that exceed the
physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient
regions. A toroidal momentum-flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_{m,\phi}$ is
introduced to bound the effective $\hat{\phi}$-projected momentum-flux
density, where $m$ denotes momentum and $\phi$ denotes the toroidal
projection. The toroidal projection is along $\hat{\phi}$, the tangent to
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ and $\hat{R} \times
\hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

The bounded toroidal momentum-flux density satisfies the limiter constraint:

$$
|\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{lim}}| \le \alpha_{m,\phi}\,\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited toroidal momentum-flux
density, $\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the toroidal free-streaming
momentum-flux reference scale, and $\alpha_{m,\phi}$ is the toroidal
momentum-flux-limiter coefficient.

This coefficient is the toroidal directional specialization of
[momentum-flux-limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
not a particle-, heat-, or energy-flux limiter and not the momentum-flux
density itself. It is intrinsically non-negative: it caps the magnitude of
the modeled toroidal momentum-flux density and does not carry the positive
or negative sign of that flux. Directional siblings include the poloidal,
radial, [parallel](name:parallel_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), and
[diamagnetic](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
momentum-flux-limiter coefficients.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vertical momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the
free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density in
edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The vertical neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient is the vertical
component of the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum
flux-limiter coefficient vector, providing the dimensionless limiter factor
for neutral momentum transport along the vertical $Z$ direction of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame in multi-fluid edge-plasma
models. It bounds the vertical neutral momentum-flux density by the
free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is large relative to
macroscopic gradient scales.

The vertical component $\alpha_Z$ is defined as the ratio of the magnitude
of the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density to its positive
free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_Z = \frac{|\Pi_Z|}{\Pi_Z^{\rm free}}, \qquad \Pi_Z^{\rm free} = m_n n_n \left(u_Z^{\rm free}\right)^2
$$

where $\Pi_Z$ is the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density
component along $\hat{Z}$, $\Pi_Z^{\rm free}$ is the corresponding
free-streaming upper bound, $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the
neutral number density, and $u_Z^{\rm free}$ is the nonnegative
free-streaming reference speed for neutral motion along $\hat{Z}$. The
constraint $\alpha_Z \in [0, 1]$ makes the coefficient a magnitude limiter;
any sign of the vertical momentum flux is carried by $\Pi_Z$, not by
$\alpha_Z$.

This quantity is the vertical member of the [neutral momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) vector and is
distinct from the [parallel neutral momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which
is taken along the magnetic-field direction, and the toroidal neutral
momentum flux-limiter coefficient, which is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a limiter coefficient,
not the neutral momentum-flux density itself.

NAMES.name: neutral_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux
density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and
attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
NAMES.long:
Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux
density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and
associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The quantity
denotes the diamagnetic contribution without selecting a particular flux
direction or transported momentum component.

The contribution is defined componentwise by:

$$
\Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \rho_{\mathrm{ns}} v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} u_{b,\mathrm{ns}}
$$

where $\Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the momentum flux, $a$ is its
flux-direction index, $b$ is its transported-momentum index,
$\rho_{\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state mass density,
$v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic drift velocity, and
$u_{b,\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state linear flow velocity.

This is the neutral-state specialization of
[momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
It excludes contributions attributed to other transport mechanisms and is
closely related to
[neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux](name:neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the transported neutral-state momentum
crosses the oriented reference surface along its positive flux direction.

NAMES.name: neutral_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective convection velocity for the pressure-gradient diamagnetic
contribution to neutral-species momentum transport, retaining transport
direction rather than only speed.
NAMES.long:
The neutral diamagnetic momentum-convection velocity is the effective vector
coefficient assigned to the pressure-gradient-associated diamagnetic
contribution to neutral momentum transport. It is distinct from the total
mean velocity of neutral particles.

For a selected component of neutral momentum density, its constitutive role
is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{\pi,\ast} = \pi^{0}\mathbf{v}^{0}_{\ast}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}^{0}_{\ast}$ is the effective diamagnetic convection
velocity, $\pi^{0}$ is the selected component of neutral momentum density,
and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{\pi,\ast}$ is its associated convective
momentum-flux vector. The superscript $0$ denotes the neutral population,
and the subscript $\ast$ identifies the diamagnetic contribution.

The quantity applies to a selected neutral species without selecting an
individual internal state; no aggregation over different neutral species is
implied. An internal-state-resolved counterpart, [neutral-state velocity due
to diamagnetic drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift),
instead applies to one specified neutral state.

The diamagnetic attribution identifies an effective momentum-transport
contribution, not a Lorentz-force drift of electrically neutral particles.
Consequently, a charged-particle diamagnetic-drift formula does not define
this coefficient, and perpendicularity to the magnetic field is not implied.
Diffusive momentum transport and other convection contributions are
excluded.

This is the neutral momentum-transport member of the [velocity due to
diamagnetic drift](name:velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) family. Its
[neutral velocity magnitude due to diamagnetic drift] is the norm
$|\mathbf{v}^{0}_{\ast}|$, which discards the transport direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a velocity component advects positive neutral
momentum density along the specified positive direction of that component.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal
NAMES.short:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate locating the pedestal as a linear flux
fraction, referenced to zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed
flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = \frac{\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux on the surface containing the
pedestal location, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [magnetic-axis flux
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), and
$\psi_{\mathrm{b}}$ is the [boundary flux
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary) at the last closed
flux surface. The denominator must be nonzero.

The normalization gives zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed
flux surface. This quantity uses the linear fraction, not its square root;
it specifies a location rather than a geometric radius, a [pedestal
width](name:pedestal_width), or a spatial average. The [coordinate of the
selected plasma
boundary](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary)
evaluates the same linear fraction at a different locus.

$$\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = (\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})/(\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})$$

NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the signed charge flux
along the local magnetic field generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a
collisional magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the magnetic-field-aligned
component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity
stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection is

$$
j_\parallel = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is the parallel current density due to heat viscosity,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$
is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. Specifically,
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude; the projection
requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This is a local, unaveraged contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density), not a surface-integrated current or the
total current density from all mechanisms. It represents net plasma charge
transport attributable to heat viscosity, rather than an individual species
contribution; the definition imposes no restriction to a particular plasma
region.

Unlike [toroidal current density due to heat
viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), which
projects the same parent vector onto the geometric toroidal direction, this
quantity projects along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the heat-viscosity conventional electric
current flows along the local magnetic-field vector.

NAMES.name: parallel_diamagnetic_current_density
NAMES.short:
Parallel component of the diamagnetic current density, obtained by
projecting the magnetic-field–pressure-gradient drift current onto the local
magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
The parallel diamagnetic current density is the projection of the total
[diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) onto the
local magnetic-field direction. It arises from the
magnetic-field–pressure-gradient drift current and represents the signed
field-aligned component of [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},\parallel}$ is the parallel diamagnetic current
density, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector in the local
magnetic-field direction, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector,
$B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude, and
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

This quantity applies to the total included edge-plasma current density
carried by all included charge carriers; it is not species- or
charge-state-resolved unless those qualifiers are part of the standard name.
It is a signed component, not the scalar magnitude [diamagnetic current
density](name:diamagnetic_current_density), and not a perpendicular
component with respect to the magnetic-field direction.

It is distinct from signed cylindrical projections such as [radial
diamagnetic current density](name:radial_diamagnetic_current_density),
[vertical diamagnetic current
density](name:vertical_diamagnetic_current_density), and toroidal
diamagnetic current density. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height, radial, toroidal, and vertical projections are along
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ respectively; the parallel projection is
along $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, not along any fixed cylindrical basis vector.

The same resolved contribution is denoted by [parallel current density due
to diamagnetic
drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) when
expressed as a contribution to [current density](name:current_density). For
the ideal isotropic scalar-pressure relation
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}=\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p/B^2$, where $p$ is total
scalar plasma pressure and $\nabla p$ is its spatial gradient,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$ and therefore
$j_{\mathrm{dia},\parallel}=0$; this is distinct from return-current
contributions such as [Pfirsch-Schlüter current
density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic current-density vector has a
component in the local magnetic-field direction $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

sources.parent_definition: Current density due to the diamgnetic drift, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Parallel component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Parallel component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma. It is the
field-aligned component of the vector defined by [ion charge-state
convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) for that
charge-state population.

The parallel component is defined by projection onto the local
magnetic-field direction:

$$
v_{s,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_{s,\parallel}$ is this parallel ion charge-state convection
velocity, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the [ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) vector for ion charge
state $s$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

The scope is charge-state resolved: $s$ denotes one specified ion charge
state in the edge plasma, with no summation over charge states and no
density-weighted mean over all charge states. The quantity is an effective
particle-transport coefficient for that charge state, including the
applicable thermal and nonthermal populations represented by the
charge-state particle population.

It is distinct from the parallel ion fluid velocity or kinetic bulk
velocity: it is the coefficient multiplying charge-state number density in
convective particle transport and need not equal a moment of the particle
velocity distribution. The total particle flux may also contain diffusive
transport, which is excluded from this convective velocity.

The field-aligned convective particle-flux component
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ satisfies
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}} = n_s v_{s,\parallel}$, where
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-aligned convective
particle-flux component and $n_s$ is the number density of ion charge state
$s$. Together with directional components such as the [poloidal ion
charge-state convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and [radial
ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), it is a
projection of the same parent vector; the parallel direction is
field-aligned and is not the poloidal tangent direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective convection velocity is directed
along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective convection (in the parallel direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
parallel diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to
its local temperature gradient.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E,\parallel}$
quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by
ions in one specified charge state $z$ along the magnetic field. It is the
parallel component of the direction-agnostic [ion charge-state energy
diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

The defining relation for the density-normalized parallel diffusive energy
flux is:

$$
\frac{Q_{i,z,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E,\parallel}\,\nabla_{\parallel} T_{i,z}
$$

where $Q_{i,z,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel diffusive
thermal-energy flux of charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is its number density,
$T_{i,z}$ is its temperature, and $\nabla_{\parallel}$ is the derivative
along the magnetic-field direction.

This coefficient applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed
over charge states. It excludes convective, advective, and $E \times B$
contributions; the broader [parallel ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) represents the
corresponding transport aggregated over ion species.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the
area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It
represents momentum transfer along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the
area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It
represents directional momentum transfer to or from that charge state
resolved along the local magnetic-field direction, rather than summed over
charge states.

The parallel projection is defined by projecting the momentum-source vector
for that charge state onto the local magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
S_{\parallel,i,Z} = \mathbf{S}_{i,Z} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,Z}$ is the area-normalized momentum-source vector
acting on ion species $i$ in charge state $Z$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} =
\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

This quantity is distinct from the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum
source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source) and the [toroidal
ion charge-state momentum
source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which use poloidal
and toroidal projections of the same charge-state-resolved momentum source.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the momentum-source vector acting on the
charge state has a component in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the
local magnetic-field unit vector.

sources.leaf_definition: Parallel component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
diffusive thermal-energy flux of the ion population to the local
ion-temperature gradient along magnetic field lines.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion energy diffusion coefficient quantifies gradient-driven
diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the ion population,
providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the density-normalized
diffusive parallel ion heat flux and the ion-temperature gradient along
magnetic field lines. It is the field-aligned component of the
direction-agnostic [ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient), excluding convective
and other non-Fickian heat-flux contributions.

The defining Fickian relation for the parallel diffusive ion thermal-energy
flux is:

$$
Q_{i,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}} = -n_i D_{i,E,\parallel} \nabla_\parallel T_i
$$

where $Q_{i,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel diffusive ion
thermal-energy flux, $n_i$ is the ion number density associated with the
modeled ion population, $D_{i,E,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion energy
diffusion coefficient, $T_i$ is the corresponding ion temperature, and
$\nabla_\parallel T_i$ is its derivative along the magnetic-field direction.
The coefficient does not select a particular charge state or impose the
total-ion aggregation represented by [parallel total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient);
[parallel ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is
the charge-state-resolved counterpart.

NAMES.name: pedestal_thermal_electron_energy
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated random kinetic energy of bulk thermal electrons within the
plasma pedestal, excluding suprathermal electrons and non-electron
populations.
NAMES.long:
Pedestal thermal electron energy is the random kinetic energy stored by the
bulk thermal electron population within the plasma pedestal. It is an
extensive energy content, not a local energy density or an energy-transfer
rate.

For nonrelativistic thermal electrons, the defining pressure integral is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{ped},e} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\mathrm{ped}}} p_{e,\mathrm{th}}\,dV
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{ped},e}$ is the pedestal thermal electron energy,
$V_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the volume occupied by the pedestal region,
$p_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the scalar thermal-electron pressure, and $dV$ is the
physical volume element. The scalar pressure is one-third of the trace of
the pressure tensor associated with random thermal-electron motion.

The integral covers only the pedestal region, rather than the entire
confined plasma, and excludes suprathermal electrons, directed bulk-flow
energy, and non-electron populations. Restricting the volume integral
defining [thermal electron energy](name:thermal_electron_energy) to the
pedestal gives this quantity. The corresponding energy stored by pedestal
ions is [pedestal thermal ion energy](name:pedestal_thermal_ion_energy).

NAMES.name: pedestal_thermal_ion_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated random kinetic energy of thermal ions within the H-mode
edge pedestal, excluding electron energy, bulk-flow energy, and nonthermal
ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
Pedestal thermal ion energy is the internal energy stored by thermal-ion
populations within the H-mode edge pedestal. It is the pedestal-region
contribution to [thermal ion energy](name:thermal_ion_energy), rather than
the energy of the entire confined ion population.

For isotropic, nonrelativistic thermal ions, the defining relation is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{ped},i} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\mathrm{ped}}} p_{\mathrm{th},i}\,dV
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{ped},i}$ is the pedestal thermal ion energy,
$V_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the pedestal integration region, $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$
is the thermal-ion pressure summed over all included ion species and
positive charge states, and $dV$ is a differential physical volume element.

The quantity is a volume-integrated energy content, not the local [ion
average temperature at the pedestal
top](name:ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top). It excludes directed
bulk-flow energy, fast-ion and other suprathermal contributions, and
electron energy. The separate [pedestal thermal electron
energy](name:pedestal_thermal_electron_energy) supplies the electron
contribution; their sum gives the combined ion–electron thermal energy for
the same pedestal region.

NAMES.name: plasma_momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface, summed over charged plasma populations and excluding neutral
transport.
NAMES.long:
The plasma momentum flux describes the rate at which charged plasma
populations transport linear momentum through a unit area of an oriented
surface. It includes convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or
turbulent-stress contributions.

$$
\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pl}} = \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}, \qquad \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}} = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{charged}}\left(\rho_s\mathbf{v}_s\mathbf{v}_s + p_s\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_s\right)
$$

Here, $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the momentum-flux vector,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the charged-plasma momentum-flux tensor,
and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the oriented unit surface normal. The sum covers
charged species $s$; $\rho_s$ is mass density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ bulk velocity,
$p_s$ scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ the identity tensor, and
$\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ the viscous or turbulent stress tensor.

This charged-plasma specialization belongs to the broader [momentum
flux](name:momentum_flux) family and excludes the neutral contribution
represented by [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux). Its
field-aligned projection is [parallel plasma momentum
flux](name:parallel_plasma_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when momentum transport across the surface is
directed along the chosen surface normal.

NAMES.name: parallel_plasma_momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Parallel plasma momentum flux is the transfer rate per unit area of
field-aligned linear momentum across an oriented surface, summed over
charged plasma populations.
NAMES.long:
Parallel plasma momentum flux is the signed rate per unit area at which the
field-aligned component of [linear momentum](name:momentum) crosses an
oriented surface. The parallel qualifier selects the transported momentum
component, not the direction normal to the surface.

It is the field-aligned projection of the [plasma momentum
flux](name:plasma_momentum_flux):

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{pl}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf F_{\mathrm{pl}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\left(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{pl}}$ is this parallel momentum flux,
$\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the nonzero local magnetic field,
$\mathbf F_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the vector of plasma momentum transported per
unit area and time across the oriented surface,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma momentum-flux tensor, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen positive unit normal to that surface.

The quantity applies to aggregate charged-population momentum transport in
the edge plasma, summed over electrons and all ion species and ionic charge
states. It includes convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or
turbulent-stress contributions; it is not restricted to diffusive transport
and excludes neutral momentum transport. The [parallel ion charge-state
momentum flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) instead
restricts the transported momentum to one ion charge state.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net momentum transferred across the
surface in its chosen positive-normal direction is co-directed with the
local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Poloidal current density due to heat viscosity is the signed local charge
flux in the poloidal direction generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a
collisional magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to heat viscosity is the local poloidal
component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity
stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection is

$$
j_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal current density due to heat
viscosity, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit vector along the designated
local poloidal direction. This direction lies in a plane of constant
toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Its
positive orientation must be specified by the local poloidal-component
convention; the heat-viscosity attribution alone does not determine it.

This is a local, unaveraged contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density), not a surface-integrated current or the
total current density from all mechanisms. Only the heat-viscosity
contribution is included; the definition imposes no restriction to a
particular species or plasma region. The quantity is a signed directional
projection, not the magnitude of the current in the poloidal plane.

Unlike [parallel current density due to heat
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), which
projects the same parent vector along the local magnetic field, this
quantity projects onto the designated local poloidal direction. Poloidal
therefore identifies the projection, not the orientation of the viscous
stress responsible for the current.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the heat-viscosity current has a component
along the designated positive local poloidal direction
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short:
Poloidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the signed
electric-charge flux contribution along the local poloidal tangent arising
from momentum exchange between ions and neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the poloidal
projection of the [current density due to ion–neutral
friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). It represents
the electric-current contribution attributable to frictional momentum
exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles.

The component is defined by

$$
j_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{p}}$ is this poloidal current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion–neutral-friction current-density
vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local unit poloidal
tangent directed toward increasing poloidal angle. The tangent lies in a
plane of constant toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The positive poloidal-angle
orientation must be specified independently; the cylindrical basis alone
does not fix it.

This is a local contribution in a partially ionized plasma, without spatial
averaging or integration. It excludes contributions assigned to other
mechanisms and does not represent the total plasma [current
density](name:current_density). The [toroidal current density due to
ion–neutral
friction](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) is a
different projection of the same mechanism-resolved vector, rather than an
additional mechanism. The poloidal projection is not the
magnetic-field-parallel projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion–neutral-friction contribution carries
conventional electric current along the local poloidal tangent toward
increasing poloidal angle.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient relating the poloidal diffusive flux of electron
thermal energy to the poloidal gradient of electron thermal-energy density
in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal electron energy diffusivity describes local, gradient-driven
smoothing of electron thermal-energy density in the edge plasma. It is the
poloidal specialization of the [electron energy
diffusivity](name:electron_energy_diffusivity).

The defining local closure is:

$$
Q_{e,W,\mathrm{p},\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,W,\mathrm{p}}\,\frac{\partial u_e}{\partial l_{\mathrm{p}}}
$$

where $Q_{e,W,\mathrm{p},\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal component of
diffusive electron thermal-energy flux density, $D_{e,W,\mathrm{p}}$ is this
diffusivity, $u_e$ is electron thermal-energy density, and $l_{\mathrm{p}}$
is physical distance along the local poloidal transport direction. The minus
sign expresses down-gradient transport for a nonnegative diffusivity.

The poloidal direction runs around the magnetic axis within a plane of
constant toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. This differs from the field-aligned direction associated with
[parallel electron energy
diffusivity](name:parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity).

This coefficient applies locally to electron thermal energy, without spatial
averaging or aggregation with ion or neutral energy transport. It excludes
advective and convective contributions, including the contribution
parameterized by [electron energy convection
velocity](name:electron_energy_convection_velocity). It is an
energy-density-gradient coefficient, not directly a temperature-gradient
heat-transport coefficient; conversion requires the electron density,
heat-capacity factors, and their spatial dependence to be specified.

NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Radial current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed major-radius
projection of the electric current contribution associated with
magnetic-field-aligned viscous stress.
NAMES.long:
Radial current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
projection of the current contribution associated with the divergence of
parallel viscous stress onto the major-radius direction. Parallel identifies
the viscous-stress mechanism, not the direction of the current.

The defining projection is:

$$
j_R^{(\mathrm{pv})} = \mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}\cdot\hat{R}
$$

where $j_R^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the radial current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the full [current-density vector due to
parallel viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), and
$\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is distance from the
toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. The superscript $\mathrm{pv}$ identifies the parallel-viscosity
contribution.

In the magnetized edge plasma, this is a local, mechanism-resolved
contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the total
radial current density or a flux-surface average. It excludes the
perpendicular-viscosity contribution. The major-radius direction is not
generally the flux-surface-normal direction or a direction perpendicular to
the magnetic field.

Parallel viscosity does not require its full current-density contribution to
be field aligned. The [parallel current density due to parallel
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) is the
magnetic-field-aligned projection of the same parent vector, rather than its
major-radius projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the parallel-viscosity current-density
contribution points toward increasing major radius, away from the toroidal
symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed major-radius component of the effective velocity multiplying electron
number density in the advective part of electron-particle transport.
NAMES.long:
Radial electron convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the
density-proportional advective electron particle flux. It represents
directed convection after density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has
been separated.

The radial convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_e v_{e,R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the major-radius component of
electron particle flux due to convection, $n_e$ is electron number density,
and $v_{e,R}$ is this radial convection velocity.

The quantity applies to the electron particle channel, not to ion or neutral
transport, and is not a sum over species. It is the radial component in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius
measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height. This major-radius direction is not generally normal to a
magnetic flux surface.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven transport, whose radial
coefficient is the [radial effective electron
diffusivity](name:radial_effective_electron_diffusivity), and need not equal
the radial bulk electron flow velocity. It specializes [electron convection
velocity] by specifying the major-radius projection; [electron particle
convection velocity](name:electron_particle_convection_velocity) is the
corresponding unprojected vector coefficient.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electron convective velocity points
toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Radial ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle
diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the radial
direction.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle
diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the radial
direction. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the radial
diffusive particle flux density of that charge state to the negative radial
gradient of its number density.

For the radial projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R} = -D_{s,R}\,\nabla_R n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R}$ is the radial diffusive particle flux
density of charge state $s$, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the
number density of charge state $s$, and $\nabla_R n_s =
\hat{\mathbf{R}}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is its derivative along increasing $R$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and applies to one ionization state,
unlike the charge-state-averaged ion diffusivity. It is the radial
counterpart of [ion charge-state
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and is equivalent to [radial
ion charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when the
same Fickian closure is used. Radial denotes the cylindrical
$\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ projection and is not synonymous with a
flux-surface-normal projection; convective transport and particle sources or
sinks are excluded.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective diffusivity (in the radial direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: radial_ion_particle_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Radial component of the effective convective velocity used for ion particle
transport in the edge plasma, taken along increasing major radius R in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It represents collective
particle-transport advection and is distinct from the ion fluid velocity.
NAMES.long:
Radial component of the effective convective velocity used for ion particle
transport is the scalar transport velocity whose multiplication by ion
particle density gives the advective part of the ion particle flux in the
radial direction. For this quantity, the radial direction is the
major-radius direction $\hat R$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The defining relation for the radial convective contribution to the ion
particle flux is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_i v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective ion particle
flux, $n_i$ is the ion particle density, and $v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is
the radial ion particle convection velocity.

The quantity applies to collective ion particle transport in the edge plasma
and to the ion species as a whole. Because velocity is an intensive
per-particle field, the species-level ion value is the density-weighted mean
over all ion charge states; if $q$ indexes ion charge state,
$v_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convection velocity of charge
state $q$, and $n_{i,q}$ is its particle density, then
$v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = (\sum_q n_{i,q}
v_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{conv}})/(\sum_q n_{i,q})$.

This is an effective transport coefficient, not the ion fluid velocity, not
an individual charge-state flow velocity, and not the diffusive contribution
to the radial particle flux. A flux-surface-normal convection velocity is a
different projection; it coincides with this radial component only where the
flux-surface normal is parallel to $\hat R$.

The direction-complement and population-resolved sibling [parallel ion
charge-state convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) describes the
magnetic-field-parallel convective velocity for one ion charge state. This
quantity instead describes the radial component for the
charge-state-aggregated ion population.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the velocity is directed toward increasing
major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective convection (in the radial direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius
NAMES.short:
Vertical plasma vorticity divided by the local major radius, retaining the
signed rotation rate about the vertical axis with inverse-length scaling.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the major-radius-scaled form of [vertical
vorticity](name:vertical_vorticity), measuring local bulk-plasma rotation
about the vertical direction per unit major radius. It is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\omega_Z^*(R,\phi,Z)=\frac{\omega_Z(R,\phi,Z)}{R},\qquad \omega_Z=(\nabla\times\mathbf{v})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
bulk-velocity vector, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, and
$\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The scaling applies to the
vertical-vorticity component itself and does not represent the full
[vorticity](name:vorticity) vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the bulk-flow rotation is in the $+Z$ sense,
namely counterclockwise in the $(R,\phi)$ plane when viewed from $+Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along the height axis, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Vorticity divided by the local major radius, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating density-normalized diffusive
thermal-energy flux of the ion population to its local ion-temperature
gradient, without selecting a transport direction.
NAMES.long:
The ion energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven
diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the ion population. It is
the direction-agnostic ion-population coefficient underlying
component-specific quantities such as the [total thermal ion energy
diffusion coefficient](name:total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
and the radial form [radial total thermal ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
and is distinct from convective or drift contributions to the ion heat flux.

The defining Fickian relation for the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}} = -n_i D_{i,E}\nabla T_i
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion thermal-energy
flux, $n_i$ is the total ion number density, $D_{i,E}$ is the ion energy
diffusion coefficient, $T_i$ is the total-ion temperature expressed as
thermal energy per ion, and $\nabla T_i$ is its spatial gradient.

For a total-ion quantity, the coefficient is the density-weighted mean over
all ion species and charge states. Direction-specific projections, including
the radial component, retain this physical definition while selecting a
transport direction. The leading minus sign specifies down-gradient Fickian
diffusion for a positive coefficient.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient relating diffusive transport of total thermal energy
carried by thermal ions to the spatial gradient of their energy density,
without fixing a direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity characterizes diffusive transport of the total thermal energy
carried by the thermal-ion population. It is the direction-independent
parent of directional components such as the [radial total thermal-ion
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

For a selected transport direction $a$, the effective coefficient is defined
through the diffusive energy flux:

$$
q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(a)} = -D_{i,E}^{(a)}\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial x_a}
$$

where $q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(a)}$ is the thermal-ion diffusive energy-flux
component, $D_{i,E}^{(a)}$ is the corresponding energy-diffusion
coefficient, $w_i$ is the total thermal-ion energy density, and $x_a$ is the
coordinate along the selected direction. The coefficient excludes
convective, conductive, and explicit source or sink contributions. It is the
total-energy specialization of the broader [thermal-ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: radial_total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective radial coefficient for diffusive transport of total thermal energy
carried by the ion population in edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective diffusivity for radial transport of total ion
thermal energy. “Total” denotes the sum over the included ion species, while
the thermal scope distinguishes energy transport from particle and momentum
transport.

The diffusive radial energy flux is related to the radial gradient of total
ion energy density by:

$$
q_{i,E,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,E,R}\frac{\partial w_{i,E}}{\partial R}
$$

where $q_{i,E,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive flux of ion
energy, $D_{i,E,R}$ is this radial energy diffusion coefficient, $w_{i,E}$
is total ion energy density, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The coefficient describes the diffusive contribution only; it excludes
advective transport represented by the [radial ion-state energy convection
velocity](name:radial_ion_state_energy_convection_velocity). Its directional
role parallels that of the [radial momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), while its
transported quantity is ion energy.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed toroidal
projection of the electric current contribution associated with
magnetic-field-aligned viscous stress.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
projection of the current contribution associated with the divergence of
parallel viscous stress onto the geometric toroidal direction. Parallel
identifies the viscous-stress mechanism, not the current projection.

The defining projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame
is:

$$
j_\phi^{(\mathrm{pv})} = \mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_\phi^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the toroidal current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the full [current-density vector due to
parallel viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
Here $R$ is the major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $Z$ is
vertical height, and the superscript $\mathrm{pv}$ identifies the
parallel-viscosity contribution.

In the magnetized edge plasma, this is a local, mechanism-resolved
contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the total
toroidal current density or a flux-surface average. It excludes the
perpendicular-viscosity contribution, whose toroidal projection is [toroidal
current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).

Parallel viscosity does not require its full current-density contribution to
be field aligned. The [parallel current density due to parallel
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) is the
magnetic-field-aligned projection of the same parent vector and is not
generally equal to this toroidal projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the parallel-viscosity current-density
contribution points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short:
Non-negative radius-like toroidal-flux label identifying the magnetic flux
surface at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the non-negative, radius-like toroidal-flux label of the
magnetic flux surface at the H-mode [pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), the core-side
shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It locates that surface on the
physical toroidal-flux scale rather than specifying a geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from enclosed toroidal magnetic flux by:

$$
\rho_{\rm tor} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\rm tor}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\rm tor}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\rm tor}$ is
the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux, $B_0$ is the positive reference vacuum
toroidal-field magnitude that sets the coordinate scale, and $\pi$ is the
circular constant.

The value applies to the single nested magnetic flux surface passing through
the pedestal top. It is a local flux-surface label, not a flux-surface or
volume average, and it has no particle-population or charge-state
aggregation.

This is the pedestal-top specialization of the parent [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate), obtained by evaluating that
coordinate on the pedestal-top surface. Unlike the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate at the pedestal
top](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top), it retains
the radius-like physical scale of the toroidal flux coordinate.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal flux coordinate. rho_tor = sqrt(b_flux_tor/(pi*b0)) ~ sqrt(pi*r^2*b0/(pi*b0)) ~ r [m]. The toroidal field used in its definition is indicated under global_quantities/b0
sources.parent_definition: Radial position at which physics quantities are evaluated

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a
specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an
edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a
specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an
edge plasma. It is resolved for one ion species and charge state rather than
summed over charge states.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
S_{\phi,i,q} = \mathbf{S}_{i,q} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,q}$ is the area-normalized momentum source for ion
species $i$ in charge state $q$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit
vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is the toroidal specialization of the charge-state-resolved
vector [ion charge state momentum
source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). It represents net momentum
transfer associated with ionization, recombination, charge exchange, and
related collisional processes; unlike [toroidal ion momentum
source](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_source), it is not summed over ion charge
states. Its corresponding poloidal projection is [poloidal ion charge state
momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the sourced momentum points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Kinematic coefficient for down-gradient diffusion of neutral momentum along
the toroidal direction, resolved for one electronic, vibrational, or
rotational internal state.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient governs diffusive transport of [momentum](name:momentum)
along the toroidal direction for a selected neutral species in one specified
internal state. The toroidal direction follows increasing toroidal angle in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a local, componentwise Fick-law closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{0a,\phi} = -D_{0a,\phi}\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial g_{0a}}{\partial\phi}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{0a,\phi}$ is the toroidally directed diffusive
flux of a selected momentum component, $D_{0a,\phi}$ is this diffusion
coefficient, and $g_{0a}$ is the corresponding momentum density. The
subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and $a$ identifies their internal
state. The derivative is taken at fixed major radius and vertical height;
the geometric factor converts the angular derivative to a derivative along
physical toroidal arc length.

The coefficient applies to the specified internal state, without summation
or averaging over other internal states. The toroidal qualifier selects the
flux and gradient direction, not the transported momentum component. This
momentum-density-gradient closure excludes convective transport,
nondiffusive momentum flux, and momentum sources; it is not defined by a
flow-velocity gradient.

This quantity is the toroidal directional member of the [neutral
internal-state momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).
The corresponding [poloidal
member](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
instead selects the poloidal transport direction.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Toroidal neutral momentum flux measures signed toroidal linear-momentum
transfer per unit area and time across an oriented surface in the edge
plasma, summed over neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral momentum flux describes the transfer of the toroidal
component of [linear momentum](name:momentum) across an oriented surface by
neutral atoms and molecules in the edge plasma. It is the toroidal
projection of the [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux).

For a surface with a chosen orientation, this component is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_\phi^0 = \hat{\phi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^0(\hat{\mathbf n})
$$

where $\Gamma_\phi^0$ is the toroidal neutral momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^0(\hat{\mathbf n})$ is the vector of neutral linear
momentum transferred per unit area and time across the surface, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface unit normal. The superscript $0$
denotes the neutral population. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points along
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The flux includes convective transport and isotropic neutral-pressure
contributions, summed over all neutral species and internal states; ion and
electron contributions are excluded. The [internal-state-resolved
counterpart](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) instead
restricts the neutral population to one specified internal state.

The toroidal qualifier selects the transported momentum component, not the
surface-normal direction: the surface normal need not be toroidal. This
quantity is a flux of linear momentum, not angular momentum.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net neutral momentum transferred across
the surface, counted in the chosen normal orientation, has a positive
projection along increasing toroidal angle.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral
population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states. Its sign
distinguishes neutral momentum transfer along increasing versus decreasing
toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the
neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states, is
the net neutral momentum transfer per unit area resolved along the toroidal
direction. It is one component of the aggregate [neutral momentum
source](name:neutral_momentum_source) acting in the neutral momentum
balance.

The toroidal component is defined by projecting the parent source vector
onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
S_{\phi,n} = \boldsymbol{S}_n \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $S_{\phi,n}$ is the toroidal neutral momentum source,
$\boldsymbol{S}_n$ is the area-normalized [neutral momentum
source](name:neutral_momentum_source) vector, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the
toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The quantity is summed over all neutral states and excludes ion momentum
sources. Unlike the [radial neutral momentum
source](name:radial_neutral_momentum_source), [poloidal neutral momentum
source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), and [parallel neutral
momentum source](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_source), it resolves
momentum transfer along the toroidal direction rather than along major
radius, the local poloidal direction, or the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neutral momentum source points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Particle-flow velocity component assigned to a neutral species state and
projected in the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame, attributed to effective diamagnetic pressure-gradient transport.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift is the signed
toroidal component of particle-flow velocity assigned to a specified neutral
atomic or molecular state and attributed to the diamagnetic,
pressure-gradient part of transport. For an uncharged neutral state, it
denotes an effective contribution in a modeled velocity decomposition rather
than a direct single-particle Lorentz-force drift. The toroidal direction is
$hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when
viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The toroidal scalar component is the projection of the effective
neutral-state diamagnetic velocity vector onto $\hat{\phi}$:

$$
v_{a,\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{a}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $a$ labels the neutral state, $\mathbf{v}_{a}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the
effective diamagnetic velocity contribution for that state, and $\hat{\phi}$
is the unit vector tangent to increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity is a component of an effective neutral-state velocity
decomposition, not the total neutral-state velocity and not a mechanical
drift of an isolated neutral particle. It is distinct from the radial,
vertical, poloidal, and field-parallel component refinements and retains
only the toroidal contribution assigned to the diamagnetic part of the
decomposition.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Velocity due to the diamagnetic drift, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: total_momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic pressure, and viscous
stress contributions from any species or population.
NAMES.long:
The [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) describes the rate at which linear
momentum crosses a unit area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It
encompasses convective ram pressure, isotropic thermal pressure, and viscous
or turbulent stress contributions from the selected plasma populations.

The momentum-flux tensor for a fluid or aggregated population is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi} = \rho\,\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v} + p\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}
$$

where $\rho$ is the mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ is the bulk flow velocity,
$p$ is the scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and
$\boldsymbol{\pi}$ is the viscous or turbulent stress tensor. The momentum
current through a surface with outward unit normal $\hat{n}$ is
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}$.

This structural quantity is independent of species, population, and
directional projection. Contributions may be aggregated over charged or
neutral populations; [toroidal total momentum
flux](name:toroidal_total_momentum_flux) is a representative directional
projection that combines the total edge-plasma contributions.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Toroidal total momentum flux is the stress-like rate per unit area at which
the toroidal component of plasma linear momentum is transported across an
oriented surface. Contributions from included plasma species and charge
states are combined; for flux-surface transport, it is the outward
flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal total momentum flux is the stress-like flux density of the toroidal
component of plasma [momentum](name:momentum) across an oriented surface. It
combines contributions from included plasma species, with charge-state
contributions summed over all charge states. It describes transported linear
momentum, not stored momentum or a momentum source or torque.

The toroidal momentum flux through an oriented surface is the projection of
the total momentum-flux tensor onto the toroidal direction and the surface
normal:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi n}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \cdot \left(\sum_s \boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{tot}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

Here, $\Gamma_{\phi n}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is this flux, $s$ indexes the
included plasma species and charge states, and
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total momentum-flux tensor
contributed by $s$, including convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or
turbulent-stress contributions as applicable. The vector
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the oriented surface normal. The toroidal
direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The quantity is defined locally across an oriented surface. For transport
across magnetic flux surfaces, the crossing direction is the outward
flux-surface normal and the flux is the flux-surface average; this
surface-normal direction is distinct from the toroidal momentum direction.
The quantity is the toroidal component of [total momentum
flux](name:total_momentum_flux), rather than a flux in the toroidal
direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive toroidal linear momentum, directed
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, is transported outward across the
flux surface.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short:
Vertical current density due to ion–neutral friction is the signed
electric-charge flux contribution along the symmetry axis arising from
momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Vertical current density due to ion–neutral friction is the vertical
projection of the [current density due to ion–neutral
friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). It represents
the electric-current contribution attributable to frictional momentum
exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles.

The component is defined by

$$
j_Z = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $j_Z$ is this vertical current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion–neutral-friction current-density
vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the toroidal
symmetry axis toward increasing height. The direction is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the distance
from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the
vertical height.

This is a local contribution in a partially ionized plasma, without spatial
averaging or integration. It excludes contributions assigned to other
mechanisms and does not represent the total plasma [current
density](name:current_density). The [radial current density due to
ion–neutral
friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) is a
different projection of the same mechanism-resolved vector, rather than an
additional mechanism.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion–neutral-friction contribution carries
conventional electric current toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vertical ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient
that scales the free-streaming bound on vertical momentum transport for a
specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The vertical ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge
state in the vertical $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. It is the vertical component of the vector quantity [ion
charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

The coefficient $\alpha_{s,Z}$ bounds the vertical momentum-flux density
through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_{s,Z} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \, \Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_{s,Z} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited vertical momentum-flux
density for ion charge state $s$, $\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
collisional diffusive estimate of that vertical momentum-flux density, and
$\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming
reference scale with $m_s$ the ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number
density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the thermal speed. When
$|\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_{s,Z}\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$, the
vertical flux saturates at $\pm\alpha_{s,Z}\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise
the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

The coefficient is specific to the vertical component and is distinct from
the
[parallel](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
and
[toroidal](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficients. The neutral-particle
analog is
[neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
The coefficient is intrinsically non-negative.
