NAMES.long:
The imaginary part of the complex radial vacuum magnetic-field perturbation,
$\delta B_R^{\rm im}$, is the quadrature component of the first-order
linearized magnetic-field perturbation projected along $+\hat{R}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, in the current-free vacuum
region surrounding the plasma. In linear MHD stability analysis, perturbed
fields are cast as complex Fourier harmonics in the toroidal angle $\phi$;
the imaginary part encodes the phase of the eigenmode relative to the
normalization reference, together with the [real
part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).

In the vacuum region, $\delta\mathbf{B}$ satisfies $\nabla \times
\delta\mathbf{B} = 0$ and $\nabla \cdot \delta\mathbf{B} = 0$. The complex
radial component decomposes as:

$$
\delta\tilde{B}_R^{\rm vac} = \delta B_R^{\rm re} + i\,\delta B_R^{\rm im}
$$

where $\delta B_R^{\rm re}$ is the [real
part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part) and $\delta
B_R^{\rm im}$ is this imaginary part. The perturbation amplitude is
$|\delta\tilde{B}_R^{\rm vac}| = \sqrt{(\delta B_R^{\rm re})^2 + (\delta
B_R^{\rm im})^2}$ and the phase is $\theta = \mathrm{atan2}(\delta B_R^{\rm
im},\,\delta B_R^{\rm re})$.

This quantity is computed by linear MHD stability codes for a specified
toroidal mode number $n$. Matching conditions at the plasma-vacuum interface
link it to its plasma-region counterpart, the radial plasma imaginary part.
Alongside [the toroidal vacuum imaginary
component](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), it
characterizes the helical spatial structure of the perturbed vacuum field.
As with all linear eigenfunctions, the partition between real and imaginary
parts depends on the phase normalization convention applied to the
eigenmode.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: First coordinate (radial)

NAMES.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part
NAMES.short:
Real part of the radial perturbed vacuum magnetic field is the in-phase
coefficient of the R component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame for a complex vacuum magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction of one
toroidal Fourier harmonic.
NAMES.long:
Real part of the radial perturbed vacuum magnetic field is the in-phase
coefficient of the radial component of a complex magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region outside the plasma for one
toroidal Fourier harmonic. Radial means projection onto $\hat R$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; it is not projection
onto the equilibrium flux-surface-normal direction.

For a complex harmonic amplitude $\delta\tilde{\mathbf
B}^{\mathrm{vac}}_n(\mathbf{x})$, with physical perturbation represented by
$\operatorname{Re}\{\delta\tilde{\mathbf B}^{\mathrm{vac}}_n(\mathbf{x})
e^{i(n\phi-\omega t)}\}$, this quantity is defined by:

$$
\delta B^{\mathrm{vac,Re}}_{R,n}(\mathbf{x}) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta\tilde{\mathbf B}^{\mathrm{vac}}_n(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat R\right]
$$

where $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes real part, $n$ is the toroidal mode
number, $\omega$ is the angular frequency associated with the chosen complex
representation, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\hat R$ is the radial basis
vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The [imaginary
counterpart](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) is
the quadrature coefficient of the same complex radial component, and the two
together specify the [complex radial vacuum perturbation
amplitude](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) for the chosen
eigenfunction phase. This vacuum-region quantity is distinct from the
corresponding plasma-region perturbation; a linear eigenfunction amplitude
is defined only up to an overall complex normalization unless a separate
normalization condition is imposed.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when, at Fourier phase $n\phi-\omega t=0$ for the
representation above, the vacuum magnetic-field perturbation has a component
in the $+\hat R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Real part
sources.parent_definition: First coordinate (radial)

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the complex first-order magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region outside the plasma, resolved
for a single toroidal Fourier mode number in linear MHD stability analysis.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal projection $\delta B_\phi = \delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}$
of the linearized magnetic-field perturbation in the current-free vacuum
surrounding the plasma constitutes one scalar component of the full
perturbed vacuum magnetic-field vector. In the vacuum exterior, $\nabla
\times \delta\mathbf{B} = 0$, so $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is derivable from a
scalar magnetic potential satisfying Laplace's equation; the toroidal
component is determined by matching conditions at the plasma-vacuum
interface and at any conducting wall boundaries. The eigenfunction is
complex-valued, and this parent quantity abstracts over its two real-valued
projections:
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part),
which carry the in-phase and quadrature contributions of the mode structure
relative to the toroidal reference angle $\phi$. This projection is one
component of the full
[perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field)
vector, alongside the poloidal and radial components captured by
[poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).
Computed by solving the vacuum Maxwell equations exterior to the plasma
boundary in linear MHD stability analysis; the absolute amplitude is
normalization-dependent, while the relative phase between vacuum and plasma
regions carries reconnection information relevant to resistive and
resistive-wall modes.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\delta B_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Imaginary part of the complex toroidal component of the first-order
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region,
for a specified toroidal mode number in linear MHD stability analysis.
NAMES.long:
In linear MHD stability analysis for a specified toroidal mode number $n$,
the first-order magnetic-field perturbation $\delta\mathbf{B}$ in the
current-free vacuum region surrounding the plasma is a complex eigenfunction
satisfying $\nabla \times \delta\mathbf{B} = 0$ and $\nabla \cdot
\delta\mathbf{B} = 0$. This name gives the imaginary part of the toroidal
projection of that eigenfunction:

$$
\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac} = \delta\mathbf{B}^\mathrm{vac} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
so that $\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac} = \mathrm{Re}(\delta
B_\phi^\mathrm{vac}) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac})$.

The real part is given by
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part),
and together they constitute the parent complex eigenfunction
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field).
Boundary conditions at the plasma–vacuum interface link this vacuum
eigenfunction to the corresponding plasma-region toroidal component
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part);
the radial vacuum counterpart is
[radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part).
Absolute eigenfunction amplitudes are normalization-convention-dependent in
linear stability calculations.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac})$ is
directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: Third coordinate (toroidal)

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part
NAMES.short:
In-phase real coefficient of the toroidal magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum surrounding the plasma, resolved
for one toroidal Fourier mode.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the real part of the toroidal component of the first-order
complex magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum
surrounding the plasma. It is one component of the full [toroidal perturbed
vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) and
excludes the equilibrium field and perturbations within the plasma.

The real coefficient is defined from the complex toroidal perturbation by

$$
\delta B_{\phi,\mathrm{R}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta B_\phi\right], \qquad \delta B_\phi = \delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the complex first-order perturbed magnetic-field
vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\delta
B_{\phi,\mathrm{R}}$ is its real part. The projection is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and the quantity belongs to the
specified toroidal Fourier mode; its quadrature counterpart is the
[imaginary part of the toroidal perturbed vacuum magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part). In the
vacuum region, the perturbation is current-free and satisfies $\nabla \times
\delta\mathbf{B}=0$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the toroidal perturbation component points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Real part
sources.parent_definition: Third coordinate (toroidal)

NAMES.name: plasma_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Plasma magnetic-field strength of the local magnetic induction associated
with the confined plasma, including equilibrium and plasma-interior
perturbed contributions while excluding the separate vacuum-field
definition.
NAMES.long:
The plasma magnetic field $B_{\rm plasma}$ is the scalar magnitude of the
local [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) associated with the confined
plasma. It represents field strength at a plasma location, including
equilibrium and plasma-interior perturbed contributions when present, rather
than retaining vector direction or selecting a signed component.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, its value may be written
from the components of the associated plasma magnetic-induction vector as

$$
B_{\rm plasma}=\left|\mathbf{B}_{\rm plasma}\right|=\sqrt{B_{R,{\rm plasma}}^2+B_{\phi,{\rm plasma}}^2+B_{Z,{\rm plasma}}^2}
$$

where $B_{\rm plasma}$ is the plasma magnetic-field strength,
$\mathbf{B}_{\rm plasma}$ is the local plasma magnetic-induction vector,
$B_{R,{\rm plasma}}$ is its signed component along increasing major radius
$R$, $B_{\phi,{\rm plasma}}$ is its signed component along increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$, and $B_{Z,{\rm plasma}}$ is its signed component
along increasing vertical height $Z$.

This quantity applies locally within the confined plasma region and has no
species population. Its aggregation convention is a point value of
magnetic-field strength, not a spatial average, flux-surface average, volume
integral, or finite-volume reduction.

This scalar magnitude is distinct from the vector [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field) and from component-resolved fields such as
the [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), [radial
magnetic field](name:radial_magnetic_field), and [vertical magnetic
field](name:vertical_magnetic_field), which retain directional sign. It is
also distinct from the [vacuum magnetic field](name:vacuum_magnetic_field),
which excludes plasma-current and plasma-interior contributions, and from
the [perturbed plasma magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field),
which denotes the perturbation contribution rather than the total local
plasma-associated field strength.

NAMES.name: perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Perturbed plasma magnetic field is the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or
corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by
the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium field. It excludes
externally imposed vacuum perturbations when those are represented
separately.
NAMES.long:
Perturbed plasma magnetic field is the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or
corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by
the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium magnetic field. It
represents magnetic-field bending and current perturbations inside the
confined plasma and excludes any externally imposed vacuum perturbation that
is retained as a separate field.

The plasma-response perturbation is defined by subtracting the equilibrium
field and any separately represented vacuum perturbation from the total
field in the confined plasma region:

$$
\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathbf{x},t) = \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x},t) - \mathbf{B}_0(\mathbf{x}) - \delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{x}$ is
position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic field,
$\mathbf{B}_0$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, and
$\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the externally imposed vacuum magnetic
perturbation that would exist without plasma response. If no separate vacuum
perturbation is present or retained, set $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}=0$;
the field satisfies $\nabla\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}=0$.

Externally imposed vacuum-field quantities, including
[perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field),
[radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field](name:radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field),
and non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field_at_control_surface, can drive the plasma
response but are not included in $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ when
represented separately. Fourier harmonic amplitudes, eigenfunction
components, and spatial projections must carry their stated phase, harmonic,
and direction definitions; they are not interchangeable with the
unrestricted vector. The related component quantities
[radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field),
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field),
and
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field)
describe resolved quantities: radial is the $\hat{R}$ projection in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, poloidal requires an explicitly
defined poloidal projection direction such as the tangent to increasing
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, and the toroidal entry
denotes the single-harmonic $\hat{\phi}$-resolved quantity specified by that
standard name.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a real resolved component of
$\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$, or the real part of a complex resolved
component after applying its stated phase convention, is directed along the
positive basis direction; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame
with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, $+\hat{R}$ is toward increasing
major radius $R$, $+\hat{\phi}$ is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $+\hat{Z}$ is
toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the poloidal component of the
complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the
magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about
equilibrium.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the poloidal component of the
complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the
magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an
equilibrium magnetic field. It is the poloidal projection of the [perturbed
plasma magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), rather than
the unrestricted magnetic-field vector.

$$
\delta B_{\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf{x})\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

Here, $\delta B_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component, $\hat{\mathbf
e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the chosen poloidal unit vector in the poloidal plane
of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response perturbation after
subtracting the equilibrium field and any separately represented externally
imposed vacuum perturbation. The complex quantity includes the [poloidal
real part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and
[poloidal imaginary
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part); the
[toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) is its complementary
toroidal projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the perturbed magnetic field points in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle within the poloidal plane of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
The imaginary part of the complex poloidal component of the first-order
perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier
mode in linear MHD stability analysis.
NAMES.long:
The imaginary part of the complex poloidal component of the first-order
perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier
mode in linear MHD stability analysis is the coefficient of $+i$ in the
poloidal projection of that eigenfunction. The projection is onto $\hat
e_\theta$, the local unit direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in
the flux-coordinate system $(s,\theta,\phi)$, where $s$ is a radial
flux-surface label and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with $R$ major radius, $Z$ vertical height,
and $\phi$ increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat Z$.

For the normal-mode representation with toroidal Fourier factor
$\exp[i(n\phi-\omega t)]$, the defining relation is:

$$
B_{\theta,\mathrm{Im}}(s,\theta) = \operatorname{Im}\!\left\{\tilde{\mathbf{B}}(s,\theta)\cdot\hat e_\theta\right\}
$$

where $B_{\theta,\mathrm{Im}}$ is this quantity, $\tilde{\mathbf{B}}$ is the
complex first-order perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction,
$\operatorname{Im}$ extracts the coefficient multiplying $+i$, and $i$ is
the imaginary unit. The projection $\tilde{\mathbf{B}}\cdot\hat e_\theta$
and $B_{\theta,\mathrm{Im}}$ have unit T; $n$, $\omega$, and $t$ are the
integer toroidal mode number, complex angular eigenfrequency, and time,
respectively.

This quantity applies to the perturbed magnetic field in the plasma region
and excludes the corresponding [poloidal perturbed vacuum magnetic field
imaginary
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part). It is
the imaginary counterpart of [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field real
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and, together
with that real part, specifies the complex [poloidal perturbed plasma
magnetic field](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) for the
chosen eigenfunction normalization and overall complex phase; changing that
phase rotates the real and imaginary parts without changing the physical
mode.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the coefficient multiplying $+i$ in the
projection of the complex eigenfunction onto the local $+\hat e_\theta$
direction is positive for the Fourier factor $\exp[i(n\phi-\omega t)]$.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: Second coordinate (poloidal)

NAMES.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part
NAMES.short:
Real part of the complex poloidal component of the first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier
mode in linear MHD stability analysis.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field real part gives the in-phase
component of the complex eigenfunction projection $\delta B_\theta =
\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the poloidal unit vector in flux coordinates
$(\psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $\psi$ the poloidal magnetic flux, $\theta$ the
poloidal angle, and $\phi$ the toroidal angle.

The defining relation is:

$$
\mathrm{Re}(\delta B_\theta) = \mathrm{Re}\!\left[\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta\right]
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ is the first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for a single toroidal mode number
$n$ and $\delta B_\theta$ has unit T.

Together with
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part),
this quantity fully specifies the complex poloidal eigenfunction component.
The counterpart quantities
[radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part)
complete the vector decomposition of $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$.
Absolute eigenfunction amplitudes depend on normalization convention;
physically meaningful results are obtained from spatial ratios between
components and from plasma-to-vacuum matching against
[poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the real part of
$\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is directed in
the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

sources.leaf_definition: Real part
sources.parent_definition: Second coordinate (poloidal)

NAMES.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the R component of the complex
linear-MHD plasma-response perturbation in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the major-radius-directed
component of the complex linear-MHD magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction, or of its corresponding real perturbation, carried by the
confined plasma. It is the radial projection of the [perturbed plasma
magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field). The right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame has $R$ as major radius, $\phi$ as toroidal
angle, and $Z$ as vertical height.

The plasma-response component is defined by

$$
\delta B_{R,\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\delta B_{R,\mathrm{pl}}$ is the radial component,
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response magnetic
perturbation, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$
is the cylindrical major-radius unit vector. For a Fourier-resolved
eigenfunction, the projection applies to the specified complex harmonic
coefficient.

Here radial means the cylindrical $R$ direction, not the normal to an
equilibrium magnetic flux surface. The component excludes the equilibrium
field and any separately represented externally imposed vacuum perturbation.
Together with the [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), it describes
directional components of the plasma response; its in-phase component is
represented by the [radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real
part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the magnetic perturbation points toward
increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Imaginary part of the radial flux-coordinate component of the complex
first-order perturbed magnetic-field eigenfunction in the confined plasma,
for a single toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis. It is
not the cylindrical major-radius component.
NAMES.long:
Imaginary part of the radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the
imaginary component of the complex first-order magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the confined plasma. It applies to one toroidal Fourier
mode in linear MHD stability analysis and to the radial coordinate component
in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

The complex radial component is decomposed into real and imaginary parts as:

$$
\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) = \delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) + i\,\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta)
$$

where $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$ is the radial flux-coordinate component of the
complex perturbed magnetic-field eigenfunction for toroidal mode number $n$,
$\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}$ is the corresponding [real
part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), $\delta
B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ is this quantity, $i$ is the imaginary unit,
$\rho$ is the radial flux coordinate, and $\theta$ is the poloidal flux
coordinate.

The scope is the confined-plasma region for the specified toroidal mode; it
excludes the perturbed magnetic field in the vacuum region, any sum over
toroidal mode numbers, and any real-valued instantaneous perturbation
obtained after applying a toroidal and temporal phase factor. The radial
direction here is the coordinate direction associated with increasing $\rho$
in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$; it is distinct from the
major-radius $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.
The quantity is a local eigenfunction component, not a flux-surface average,
volume integral, or magnitude.

Together with the [real
part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), this quantity
forms the complex radial component $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$. Together with
the [poloidal](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part)
and [toroidal](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part)
imaginary components, it forms the imaginary vector part of the perturbed
plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction. The overall complex phase of a linear
eigenfunction is arbitrary, so a phase rotation mixes the real and imaginary
parts while leaving the represented complex eigenfunction unchanged.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the imaginary radial component points toward
increasing radial flux coordinate $\rho$ in the flux-coordinate system
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ for the adopted complex eigenfunction phase.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: First coordinate (radial)

NAMES.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part
NAMES.short:
Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real part is the in-phase radial
component of the complex first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation for
one toroidal Fourier harmonic. The radial direction is the R component in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real part is the real part of the
cylindrical radial component of a complex first-order plasma magnetic-field
perturbation for a selected toroidal Fourier harmonic. The radial direction
is the $+\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The defining component is

$$
\delta B_{R,n}^{\mathrm{re}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\widetilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_n \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\right)
$$

where $\delta B_{R,n}^{\mathrm{re}}$ is this real component,
$\widetilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_n$ is the complex first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation for toroidal Fourier mode number $n$,
$\operatorname{Re}$ takes the real part, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the
radial basis vector.

Together with [radial perturbed plasma magnetic field imaginary
part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), it
determines the complex [radial perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field); changing the chosen
complex phase of the harmonic rotates the real and imaginary parts without
changing the represented perturbation. It is the radial component
counterpart of [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) and is distinct from a
flux-surface-normal projection, which would use a unit normal to a specified
flux coordinate rather than $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the in-phase radial perturbation component
points in the $+\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ direction of increasing major radius $R$.

sources.leaf_definition: Real part
sources.parent_definition: First coordinate (radial)

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the toroidal component of the
complex linear-MHD magnetic-field perturbation carried by the
confined-plasma response about equilibrium.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the toroidal component of the
complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the
magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an
equilibrium field. It is the toroidal projection of the [perturbed plasma
magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) and excludes
separately represented externally imposed vacuum perturbations.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\delta B_{\mathrm{pl},\phi}(\mathbf{x},t) = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\delta B_{\mathrm{pl},\phi}$ is the toroidal component,
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response perturbation,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the
toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with
oriented basis
$(\hat{\mathbf{R}},\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}},\hat{\mathbf{Z}})$. Here $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The response field is
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}=\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{B}_0-\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$,
where $\mathbf{B}$ is total field, $\mathbf{B}_0$ is equilibrium field, and
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is a separately represented vacuum
perturbation. For a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic, the [real
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and
[imaginary
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) are
phase components of this same toroidal quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the corresponding real-valued perturbation
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Imaginary part of the complex toroidal component of the first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier mode
in linear MHD stability analysis.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the complex plasma magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the projection $\delta B_\phi =
\delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}$ along the toroidal unit vector
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This
imaginary part, $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)$, together with the [real
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), fully
specifies the complex toroidal component of the [perturbed plasma
magnetic-field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) eigenfunction
associated with a single toroidal mode number $n$ within the confined plasma
region.

The full complex toroidal amplitude is decomposed as:

$$
\delta B_\phi = \mathrm{Re}(\delta B_\phi) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)
$$

where the ratio of imaginary to real parts encodes the spatial phase of the
perturbation relative to the chosen eigenmode gage convention. The absolute
magnitude of the eigenfunction is normalization-dependent and is set by the
stability solver's normalization choice.

This quantity is defined within the confined plasma region and is computed
alongside
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part)
and radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part to fully
characterize the phase-resolved perturbed magnetic-field vector inside the
plasma. The vacuum-region counterpart for the same toroidal component is
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)$ is directed
along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: Third coordinate (toroidal)

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part
NAMES.short:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic-field real part is the in-phase φ
component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the complex
first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for one
specified toroidal Fourier harmonic. In this frame, R is major radius, φ is
toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic-field real part is the real component of
the toroidal projection of the complex first-order plasma magnetic-field
perturbation eigenfunction in the plasma region for one specified toroidal
Fourier harmonic. The toroidal projection is the component along
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when
viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The physical toroidal perturbation associated with the complex eigenfunction
is represented by

$$
\delta B_\phi(R,\phi,Z,t) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta\tilde{B}_\phi(R,Z)\exp\!\left(i(n\phi-\omega t)\right)\right]
$$

where $\delta B_\phi$ is the physical first-order toroidal magnetic-field
perturbation, $\delta\tilde{B}_\phi$ is the complex toroidal eigenfunction
amplitude, $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real-part operator, $n$ is the
toroidal mode number, $\omega$ is the mode angular frequency, and $t$ is
time. This quantity is $\operatorname{Re}[\delta\tilde{B}_\phi(R,Z)]$.

Together with
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part),
this quantity specifies the complex toroidal perturbation component
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field)
for the selected harmonic. It is distinct from the radial and poloidal
real-part components
[radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part),
from the equilibrium toroidal magnetic field, and from the vacuum-region
counterpart
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).
A global complex phase rotation of the eigenfunction changes the split
between real and imaginary parts while leaving the reconstructed physical
perturbation unchanged when the same Fourier convention is used.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\operatorname{Re}[\delta\tilde{B}_\phi]$ is
directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Real part
sources.parent_definition: Third coordinate (toroidal)

NAMES.name: plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Plasma-associated magnetic vector potential whose curl gives the
corresponding magnetic induction, including perturbations relative to a
reference state in a gage-dependent vector representation.
NAMES.long:
The plasma magnetic vector potential is the gage-dependent vector field
associated with the magnetic field in the plasma. It retains the complete
vector quantity rather than selecting a radial, poloidal, toroidal,
vertical, or field-parallel component.

The defining relation connecting the vector potential to its associated
magnetic induction is:

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm pl} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}_{\rm pl}
$$

where $\mathbf{A}_{\rm pl}$ is the plasma-associated magnetic vector
potential, $\mathbf{B}_{\rm pl}$ is the corresponding plasma-associated
magnetic induction, and $\nabla \times$ is the spatial curl operator. Only
the curl is directly field-defining; $\mathbf{A}_{\rm pl}$ itself depends on
the chosen gage.

This parent denotes the full unprojected plasma-associated vector potential
across equilibrium and perturbed states. It retains its radial, poloidal,
toroidal, vertical, and field-parallel components as a vector, without
component averaging, Fourier selection, or magnitude formation. The concrete
[perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential) represents the
change in this quantity relative to a reference state.

The plasma-associated quantity is distinct from the external-source-only
[vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential).
Together with the broader [magnetic vector
potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential), it provides the
plasma-associated contribution to the magnetic-field description; the vacuum
quantity instead excludes plasma-current contributions.

NAMES.name: perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Vector-potential perturbation associated with a change in the plasma
magnetic field relative to a reference state, retaining radial, poloidal,
and toroidal components.
NAMES.long:
The perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential is the vector-valued
departure of the plasma magnetic vector potential from its reference state.
Its curl determines the associated perturbed magnetic field, subject to the
chosen vector-potential gage.

The perturbation is defined by

$$
\delta \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{A} - \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\delta \mathbf{A}$ is the perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential,
$\mathbf{A}$ is the plasma magnetic vector potential, and
$\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is its reference-state value. The associated
magnetic-field perturbation satisfies $\delta \mathbf{B} = \nabla \times
\delta \mathbf{A}$, where $\delta \mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed magnetic
field and $\nabla$ is the spatial differential operator.

This quantity denotes the complete perturbation vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It includes the radial,
poloidal, and toroidal components without summing their signed projections.
The [radial perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential),
[poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential), and
[toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential) are
component-specific instances of this vector quantity.

The perturbation excludes the reference-state contribution and is distinct
from the full [plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:plasma_magnetic_vector_potential), which includes both
reference and perturbed parts. Because a vector potential is gage-dependent,
only its curl determines the corresponding magnetic-field perturbation
uniquely.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of $\delta \mathbf{A}$
points along its defined positive radial, poloidal, or toroidal direction in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Poloidal component of the first-order perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential, represented as a linear MHD eigenfunction and distinct from its
radial and toroidal components.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential is the poloidal
component of the first-order departure of the plasma magnetic vector
potential from its reference state. In linear magnetohydrodynamic
eigenfunction descriptions, it carries the poloidal part of the
magnetic-vector-potential perturbation without selecting a real or imaginary
phase component.

The perturbed magnetic field associated with the full vector potential
perturbation satisfies

$$
\delta \mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \delta \mathbf{A}
$$

where $\delta \mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed plasma magnetic field, $\nabla$
is the spatial gradient operator, and $\delta \mathbf{A}$ is the full
perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential. The poloidal component is
defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the
major-radius coordinate, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical
coordinate.

This quantity is restricted to the poloidal component and is not the
complete vector potential, its radial component, its toroidal component, or
the perturbed magnetic field itself. It is also distinct from the
real-valued specialization [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential real
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part),
which selects one phase component of the corresponding eigenfunction.

The component is a specialization of the full [perturbed plasma magnetic
vector potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential); its curl
contributes to the associated perturbed magnetic field. A gage
transformation can change the vector-potential representation without
changing this curl, so the vector-potential component is not uniquely
identical to a magnetic-field component. The radial component provides an
adjacent component specialization of the same perturbed-vector-potential
family.

NAMES.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part
NAMES.short:
Real-valued poloidal component of the perturbed plasma
magnetic-vector-potential eigenfunction for a specified toroidal mode in
linear MHD stability analysis.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the real-valued poloidal component of the perturbed plasma
magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction associated with one toroidal mode of
a linear MHD perturbation.

$$
A_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{real}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}\right)
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{real}}$ is the real poloidal component,
$\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the complex poloidal component of the
perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, and $\operatorname{Re}$ is the
real-part operator.

The quantity applies to the confined plasma contribution for a specified
toroidal mode and retains only the poloidal component and real part of the
complex eigenfunction. It is not the full perturbed vector potential, its
imaginary component, a magnitude, or a component of the perturbed magnetic
field.

The parent [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential)
contains the corresponding complex poloidal component before real-part
extraction. The real and imaginary components together represent the complex
eigenfunction amplitude; the perturbed magnetic field is obtained from the
curl of the full perturbed vector potential rather than from this component
alone.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the real component points along the positive
poloidal basis direction used to define $\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Real part
sources.parent_definition: Second coordinate (poloidal)

NAMES.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Radial component of the first-order perturbed plasma magnetic
vector-potential eigenfunction for a linear MHD mode, retaining its signed
projection toward increasing major radius.
NAMES.long:
Radial component of the first-order perturbed plasma magnetic
vector-potential eigenfunction associated with a linear MHD mode.

The radial component is defined by

$$
\delta A_R = \delta\mathbf{A} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\delta A_R$ is the radial component, $\delta\mathbf{A}$ is the
perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the
unit vector toward increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity represents one signed component of the plasma perturbation
about a reference state; it is not the complete vector, a magnitude, a sum,
or an average. The complete vector quantity is the [perturbed plasma
magnetic vector potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential),
while the [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential)
provides an adjacent directional component. It includes the full radial
eigenfunction rather than selecting only its real or imaginary quadrature;
the latter is represented by the [radial perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential imaginary
part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part).

The associated perturbed magnetic field $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is obtained from
the curl relation $\delta\mathbf{B}=\nabla\times\delta\mathbf{A}$, where
$\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed magnetic field and $\nabla\times$ is the
spatial curl operator. The vector potential is gage-dependent, whereas its
curl determines the corresponding magnetic-field perturbation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\delta A_R$ points toward increasing major
radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Imaginary part of the radial component of the first-order perturbed
magnetic-vector-potential eigenfunction describing a confined-plasma MHD
mode.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the radial component of a
first-order perturbed magnetic vector potential eigenfunction in the
confined plasma.

The complex radial component is decomposed as

$$
\widetilde{A}_r = A_{r,\mathrm{R}} + i A_{r,\mathrm{I}}
$$

where $\widetilde{A}_r$ is the complex radial component of the perturbed
magnetic vector potential, $A_{r,\mathrm{R}}$ is its real part,
$A_{r,\mathrm{I}}$ is its imaginary part, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.
This quantity is $A_{r,\mathrm{I}}$.

The definition is restricted to the radial component in the confined plasma
and to the selected linear MHD eigenfunction; it is not a sum over vector
components or modes. It excludes the real quadrature and the poloidal and
toroidal components. Together with the real part, it fully specifies the
complex component and is the imaginary-part specialization of the [radial
perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential).

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: First coordinate (radial)

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential,
retaining the signed projection along increasing toroidal angle for
linear-MHD mode representations.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential is
the signed projection of the vector-potential perturbation onto the
geometric toroidal direction within the plasma. It represents the toroidal
member of the component family derived from the [perturbed plasma magnetic
vector potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the component
is defined by

$$
\delta A_\phi = \delta\mathbf{A} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\delta A_\phi$ is the toroidal component, $\delta\mathbf{A}$ is the
perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The associated
perturbed magnetic field is determined by $\delta\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times
\delta\mathbf{A}$, where $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed magnetic field
and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

This quantity applies to the plasma magnetic-vector-potential perturbation
itself and is a local toroidal component, not a species sum, charge-state
sum, surface average, or volume average. The vector potential depends on the
selected gage, whereas its curl gives the gage-invariant magnetic-field
perturbation. It is distinct from the [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), which is the toroidal
component of $\delta\mathbf{B}$ rather than of $\delta\mathbf{A}$. The
corresponding component construction in another direction is represented by
the [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential). For
complex linear-MHD eigenfunctions, an imaginary-quadrature specialization
retains only the imaginary part of this toroidal component.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\delta A_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Imaginary quadrature of the complex toroidal magnetic-vector-potential
perturbation eigenfunction for a linear MHD mode in the plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the first-order perturbed
magnetic vector potential eigenfunction for a specified linear MHD mode in
the plasma. It is projected onto the toroidal direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The defining relation is

$$
\delta A_{\phi}^{\mathrm{im}}(\mathbf{x}) = \operatorname{Im}\!\left[\delta A_{\phi}(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $\delta A_{\phi}^{\mathrm{im}}$ is the imaginary component,
$\operatorname{Im}$ extracts the imaginary part, $\delta A_{\phi}$ is the
complex toroidal component of the perturbed magnetic vector potential, and
$\mathbf{x}$ is the position in the plasma. Here, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies only to the perturbed plasma eigenfunction and excludes
equilibrium or unperturbed magnetic-vector-potential contributions. It is
the imaginary quadrature, not the full complex component and not the
toroidal component of the perturbed magnetic field. Its sign and magnitude
depend on the phase convention selected for the complex eigenfunction.

This quantity is the imaginary-part transformation of the [toroidal
perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential);
together with the corresponding real quadrature, it reconstructs the complex
toroidal component. It is distinct from the [toroidal perturbed plasma
magnetic field imaginary
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), which
represents a magnetic-field component rather than a vector-potential
component.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: Third coordinate (toroidal)

NAMES.name: plasma_pressure_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Plasma pressure imaginary part is the scalar coefficient multiplying the
imaginary unit in a complex representation of isotropic plasma pressure. It
is a phase-quadrature part of the pressure representation, not the complete
complex pressure quantity.
NAMES.long:
Plasma pressure imaginary part is the scalar coefficient multiplying the
imaginary unit in a complex representation of isotropic plasma pressure. It
represents the imaginary phase quadrature of that pressure representation
and is not the complete complex pressure quantity.

A complex plasma-pressure quantity is decomposed into real and imaginary
quadratures as:

$$
p = p_\mathrm{R} + i\,p_\mathrm{I}
$$

where $p$ is the complex plasma-pressure quantity, $i$ is the imaginary
unit, $p_\mathrm{R}$ is its real-part quadrature, and $p_\mathrm{I}$ is the
plasma pressure imaginary part defined here.

This parent quantity applies to any complex scalar representation of
isotropic plasma pressure. It does not by itself specify perturbation order,
Fourier mode number, reference phase, eigenfunction normalization, or
spatial dependence.

The perturbation-specific [perturbed plasma pressure imaginary
part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part) is a specialization of
this parent in which $p$ is restricted to the complex first-order
plasma-pressure perturbation eigenfunction. The quantity is distinct from
plasma pressure, which denotes the pressure scalar itself rather than the
imaginary quadrature of a complex representation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the pressure phasor projects onto the $+i$
direction of the complex plane.

NAMES.name: perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part
NAMES.short:
Imaginary part of the complex first-order plasma pressure perturbation
eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability
analysis.
NAMES.long:
The perturbed plasma pressure $\tilde{p}$ is the complex scalar
eigenfunction representing the linearized first-order pressure perturbation
for a single toroidal mode number $n$ in a linear MHD stability calculation.
The total pressure decomposes as $p = p_0 +
\mathrm{Re}[\tilde{p}\,e^{i(n\phi - \omega t)}]$, where $p_0$ is the
equilibrium pressure profile, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\omega$ is the complex
eigenfrequency.

This quantity is the imaginary component of $\tilde{p}$ under the standard
complex decomposition:

$$
\tilde{p} = \mathrm{Re}(\tilde{p}) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p})
$$

where both $\mathrm{Re}(\tilde{p})$ and $\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p})$ are
real-valued scalar fields resolved on the two-dimensional poloidal
cross-section. Combined with
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part),
this quantity fully specifies the complex pressure perturbation amplitude at
each grid point for the given mode.

The imaginary part encodes the local spatial phase of the pressure
perturbation relative to the phase reference convention of the linear MHD
eigenvalue solver. Eigenfunction normalization is solver-dependent, so
absolute amplitudes are physically meaningful only when a normalization
convention is explicitly fixed. This quantity is structurally analogous to
[perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part),
which follow the same Fourier decomposition for their respective physical
scalars.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p}) > 0$ under the
decomposition $\tilde{p} = \mathrm{Re}(\tilde{p}) +
i\,\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p})$ with toroidal Fourier factor $e^{in\phi}$, where
$\phi$ increases counter-clockwise viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Imaginary part
sources.parent_definition: Perturbed pressure for given toroidal mode number

NAMES.name: plasma_pressure_real_part
NAMES.short:
Plasma pressure real part is the real quadrature of a complex scalar
representation of isotropic plasma pressure. For perturbation
eigenfunctions, it is the signed real component of the pressure
perturbation, not the full complex eigenfunction.
NAMES.long:
Plasma pressure real part is the scalar real quadrature of a complex
representation of isotropic plasma pressure. It represents the component
obtained after the phase convention for the complex pressure quantity has
been fixed, and it is distinct from the complete complex quantity.

The real part is defined by applying the real-part operator to the
corresponding complex plasma-pressure quantity:

$$
p_R = \operatorname{Re}(\tilde{p})
$$

where $p_R$ is the plasma pressure real part, $\tilde{p}$ is the
corresponding complex scalar plasma-pressure quantity, and
$\operatorname{Re}$ denotes extraction of the real component.

This parent quantity is restricted to real-part quantities of isotropic
plasma pressure and does not by itself specify perturbation order,
Fourier-mode labeling, phase normalization, or spatial locus. It applies to
the plasma scalar pressure field; it is not a species-resolved pressure, a
pressure-tensor component, or an anisotropic-pressure component.

It excludes the imaginary quadrature, modulus, phase, and complete complex
pressure quantity. More specific children add the physics qualifier while
preserving the same real-part operation; for example, [perturbed plasma
pressure real part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part) is the real
component of a complex first-order plasma-pressure perturbation
eigenfunction. If the corresponding complex quantity is written as
$\tilde{p}=p_R+i p_I$, then $p_I$ is its imaginary quadrature and $i$ is the
imaginary unit, while this name denotes only $p_R$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected real quadrature denotes an
increase of isotropic plasma pressure relative to the reference pressure
state.

NAMES.name: perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part
NAMES.short:
Real part of the complex first-order plasma pressure perturbation
eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability
analysis.
NAMES.long:
The real part of the complex pressure perturbation eigenfunction $\tilde{p}$
gives the in-phase component of the linearized first-order pressure
variation associated with a given toroidal MHD mode, distributed over the
poloidal cross-section.

The full pressure field decomposes as:

$$
p = p_0 + \text{Re}\!\left[\tilde{p}(R,Z)\, e^{i(n_\phi \phi - \omega t)}\right]
$$

where $p_0$ is the equilibrium pressure profile, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal
mode number, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\omega$ is the complex MHD eigenfrequency. The
quantity $\text{Re}(\tilde{p})$ is the real component of the parent
eigenfunction perturbed_plasma_pressure evaluated on the poloidal plane.

Together with the
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part),
it fully specifies the complex amplitude and phase of $\tilde{p}$; the
amplitude is $|\tilde{p}| = \sqrt{\text{Re}(\tilde{p})^2 +
\text{Im}(\tilde{p})^2}$. Analogous real-part eigenfunctions for other
linearized MHD perturbation quantities include
[perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part).

This quantity is produced by linear MHD stability solvers as part of the
eigenvalue problem on the poloidal grid. Because the eigenfunction phase is
fixed by the solver normalization convention, the absolute sign of
$\text{Re}(\tilde{p})$ is convention-dependent; only relative magnitudes and
phase angles among the perturbed quantities in the same eigenfunction carry
physical content.

sources.leaf_definition: Real part
sources.parent_definition: Perturbed pressure for given toroidal mode number

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_active_wall_point
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of the active wall point where the plasma boundary
contacts the wall, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the major-radius location of the active wall point, defined
as the point where the plasma boundary is in contact with the wall. It
identifies one specific plasma–wall contact location rather than a general
wall or boundary position.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the coordinate is
defined from the horizontal Cartesian position of the contact point by

$$
R_{\mathrm{active}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{active}}^2+y_{\mathrm{active}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{active}}$ is the major-radius coordinate, and
$x_{\mathrm{active}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{active}}$ are the horizontal Cartesian
coordinates of the active wall point in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

This is a pointwise coordinate for the active wall contact and is neither an
average nor a coordinate sequence describing a contour. It is a
locus-specific specialization of
[radial_coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), retaining the same major-radius
meaning while fixing the active wall point as its locus. It differs from
[radial_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point](name:radial_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point),
which refers specifically to the wall point nearest the plasma boundary, and
from
[radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary](name:radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary),
which describes coordinates along the boundary outline.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: R,Z position of the point of the plasma boundary in contact with the wall

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode_center
NAMES.short:
Toroidal flux coordinate at the neoclassical tearing mode center, a
non-negative, radius-like magnetic-surface label derived from enclosed
toroidal magnetic flux.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux coordinate

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\Phi/(\pi B_0)}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate at the mode
center, $\Phi$ is the magnitude of the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by
the associated surface, and $B_0$ is the positive vacuum toroidal
magnetic-field strength at the reference major radius.

This quantity is the [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate) evaluated at the stated locus,
not a geometric major radius or a distance from the magnetic axis. It is
dimensional rather than normalized; its normalized counterpart is obtained
by dividing it by the [toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.parent_definition: Detailed NTM evolution on a finer timebase than the time_slice array of structure
