energy band is recorded as an accepted count by the neutron detector.
NAMES.long:
Neutron spectral efficiency is the conditional probability that an incident
neutron in the detector's assigned energy interval produces an accepted
detector count.

For incident neutron energy $E$, the efficiency is defined by

$$
\epsilon(E) = \frac{N_{\mathrm{recorded}}(E)}{N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)}
$$

where $\epsilon(E)$ is the detection probability, $N_{\mathrm{recorded}}(E)$
is the number of accepted counts produced by neutrons in a narrow interval
around energy $E$, and $N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)$ is the number of neutrons
impacting the detector in that interval.

This quantity applies only to the neutron detector and its specified
incident-energy band. It is a conditional probability for individual
incident neutrons, not a sum over neutron populations or energy bands, and
it excludes the incident neutron flux itself and detector signals rejected
by the counting criterion.

The energy domain is bounded by the detector-band limits, including the
[maximum neutron energy of the neutron
detector](name:neutron_maximum_energy_of_neutron_detector). It is the
neutron counterpart of [spectral efficiency of a hard X-ray
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector), which describes
the analogous counting probability for photons rather than neutrons.

sources.leaf_definition: Probability of detection of a photon impacting the detector as a function of its energy
sources.parent_definition: Set of energy bands in which neutrons are counted by the detector

NAMES.name: surface_area_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short:
Geometric area of the neutron-sensitive detector surface, excluding passive
housing, shielding, supports, electronics, projection effects, and
solid-angle weighting.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the geometric area of the neutron-sensitive active surface
of the detector. It includes the physical sensitive face, including
contributions from segmented or curved surfaces, and excludes passive
detector structures.

The area is defined by integration over the neutron-sensitive surface:

$$
A = \int_{S_{\rm active}} dS
$$

where $S_{\rm active}$ is the neutron-sensitive surface and $dS$ is an
element of geometric surface area. This is the active-surface component
represented by area of neutron detector; it is not an effective area
weighted by detection efficiency, neutron incidence angle, projection, or
solid angle.

sources.leaf_definition: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data
sources.parent_definition: Detector geometry

NAMES.name: temperature_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short:
Absolute thermodynamic temperature of a neutron detector assembly or
converter material, describing its thermal state independently of
neutron-counting response.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the thermodynamic temperature of the neutron detector
assembly or neutron-conversion material, characterizing its thermal state
rather than the detector's electrical response or neutron-counting behavior.

The temperature is defined thermodynamically by

$$
\frac{1}{T}=\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial U}\right)_{V,N}
$$

where $T$ is thermodynamic temperature, $S$ is entropy, $U$ is internal
energy, $V$ is volume, and $N$ is the amount of material or particle number
held fixed in the derivative. The quantity applies to the specified detector
or converter material and is distinct from the local material temperature at
a sensor attachment point. It is not the neutron-energy threshold
represented by energy of a neutron detector.

sources.leaf_definition: Temperature of the detector
sources.parent_definition: Set of neutron detection systems

NAMES.name: thomson_scattering_laser_pulse_energy_at_outlet
NAMES.short:
Energy carried by a Thomson-scattering probing laser pulse after it has
traversed the plasma, representing the transmitted post-plasma pulse.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total energy carried by a Thomson-scattering laser
pulse at the beam exit after crossing the plasma. It represents the
transmitted pulse available for comparison with the pre-plasma pulse.

The pulse energy is defined by the time integral of the outgoing laser
power:

$$
E_{\mathrm{out}} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} P_{\mathrm{out}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the post-plasma laser-pulse energy,
$P_{\mathrm{out}}(t)$ is the laser power exiting the plasma at time $t$, and
$t_1$ and $t_2$ delimit the pulse.

The scope is restricted to the probing laser pulse after plasma crossing and
includes the complete pulse over its temporal extent. It excludes the
incident pre-plasma pulse energy, energy deposited in the plasma, and
Thomson-scattered radiation. The ratio of this quantity to the corresponding
incident pulse energy defines the pulse transmission factor and quantifies
attenuation through the plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: Energy of the laser pulse measured after crossing the plasma
sources.parent_definition: Set of probing lasers

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short:
Toroidal coordinate of a neutron detector is the angular location of the
detector's geometric center about the machine symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal coordinate of a neutron detector is the angular coordinate of the
detector's geometric center about the machine symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},
\hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$. Here $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, $\phi$ is
the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical-height coordinate.

For a detector center whose projection onto the plane perpendicular to
$\hat{Z}$ has Cartesian coordinates $x_c$ and $y_c$ in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and
$\phi=0$ along $+\hat{x}$, the toroidal coordinate is

$$
\phi_\mathrm{n} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_c, x_c)
$$

where $\phi_\mathrm{n}$ is the toroidal coordinate of the neutron detector,
and $x_c$ and $y_c$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the detector geometric
center projected onto the plane perpendicular to $\hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies specifically to a neutron detector and to the point
representing its geometric center. The aggregation convention is none: it
denotes one detector center, not an average, sum, or representative angle
over several detectors; it is geometrically undefined for a center on the
symmetry axis, where no toroidal direction is selected.

It is not a detector orientation, angular extent, line-of-sight direction,
or the toroidal coordinate of an aperture or other component. It specializes
the generic [toroidal coordinate of a
detector](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_detector) to neutron detectors and is
distinct from [toroidal coordinate of an
aperture](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_aperture), which refers to an
aperture's own geometric center.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the detector geometric center is displaced in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when
viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angle locating the endpoint of a Thomson-scattering laser in the
right-handed cylindrical frame (R, φ, Z).
NAMES.long:
The toroidal coordinate φ identifies the azimuthal location of the
Thomson-scattering laser endpoint about the machine symmetry axis. Together
with the corresponding radial coordinate, it locates the endpoint in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.

The endpoint position is represented as

$$
\mathbf r_{\rm end}=R_{\rm end}\,\hat{\mathbf R}(\phi_{\rm end})+Z_{\rm end}\,\hat{\mathbf Z}
$$

where $\mathbf r_{\rm end}$ is the endpoint position, $R_{\rm end}$ is its
major-radius coordinate, $\phi_{\rm end}$ is this toroidal coordinate,
$Z_{\rm end}$ is its vertical coordinate, and $\hat{\mathbf R}$ and
$\hat{\mathbf Z}$ are the cylindrical radial and vertical unit vectors. The
radial counterpart is the [radial coordinate of the Thomson-scattering
laser](name:radial_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the angular displacement is counter-clockwise
viewed from above along the positive $Z$ direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: Position of the laser end point

NAMES.name: voltage_of_mass_spectrometer
NAMES.short:
Mass-spectrometer detector bias voltage is the signed detector-bias
potential difference between the detector electrode or electron-multiplying
stage and its bias reference. It is a device-level setting;
voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel denotes a channel-specific detector
bias.
NAMES.long:
Mass-spectrometer detector bias voltage is the signed detector-bias
potential difference applied between the detector electrode or
electron-multiplying stage and its bias reference. It is a device-level
electrical setting that affects ion collection efficiency or
electron-multiplier gain.

The detector-bias potential difference is defined by the detector and
reference electric potentials:

$$
V_\mathrm{bias} = \Phi_\mathrm{det} - \Phi_\mathrm{ref}
$$

where $V_\mathrm{bias}$ is the detector bias voltage of the mass
spectrometer, $\Phi_\mathrm{det}$ is the electric potential of the detector
electrode or electron-multiplying stage, and $\Phi_\mathrm{ref}$ is the
electric potential of its bias reference.

This quantity applies to the mass spectrometer as a device-level detector
bias common to the instrument or defined independently of channel selection.
It excludes channel-specific detector biases, which are represented by
[mass-spectrometer channel detector bias
voltage](name:voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel).

This quantity is distinct from [mass-spectrometer channel ion
current](name:ion_current_of_mass_spectrometer_channel): the ion current is
the electrical current associated with collected ions in a channel, whereas
the detector bias voltage is the applied potential difference that can
affect collection efficiency or gain.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the detector electrode or
electron-multiplying stage is at higher electric potential than its bias
reference.

sources.leaf_definition: Voltage applied on the microchannel plate detector
sources.parent_definition: Mass spectrometer diagnostic

NAMES.name: voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel
NAMES.short:
Signed bias potential applied between the photomultiplier detector electrode
and its electronics reference for one mass-resolved channel, setting
ion-signal gain.
NAMES.long:
The mass-spectrometer channel voltage is the detector-bias potential
difference associated with one channel assigned to a selected atomic mass.
It is an instrumental operating parameter of the photomultiplier detector
that controls the gain applied to the collected ion signal, rather than a
plasma thermodynamic or field quantity.

The defining potential difference is

$$
V_{\mathrm{ch}} = \phi_{\mathrm{det}} - \phi_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the channel detector-bias voltage,
$\phi_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the electric potential of the photomultiplier
detector electrode, and $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the electronics reference
potential.

This quantity applies to one mass-resolved channel and its associated
detector circuit. It is not summed or averaged across channels, mass
assignments, detector electrodes, or ion populations, and it does not
represent a local plasma voltage.

The channel-level quantity specializes the device-level [mass-spectrometer
detector bias voltage](name:voltage_of_mass_spectrometer) to one channel. It
is distinct from the [ion current of a mass-spectrometer
channel](name:ion_current_of_mass_spectrometer_channel), which is the
collected electrical signal, and from the [voltage of a spectrometer
channel](name:voltage_of_spectrometer_channel), which denotes an electrical
output signal rather than the detector-bias potential.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the detector electrode potential exceeds the
electronics reference potential.

sources.leaf_definition: Voltage applied to the photomultiplier
sources.parent_definition: Set of mass channels, each corresponding to a given atomic mass measured continuously by the spectrometer

NAMES.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short:
X component of the neutron-detector direction unit vector is the direction
cosine along the x axis of the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame, from
a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center. It is a component
of a normalized pointing direction, not a position coordinate.
NAMES.long:
X component of the neutron-detector direction unit vector is the projection
of the normalized direction from a field-of-view voxel center to the
neutron-detector center onto the positive $\hat{x}$ axis. The component is
resolved in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis
and is a direction cosine, not a Cartesian position coordinate.

The normalized pointing component is defined by

$$
d_x = \left(\frac{\mathbf r_{\rm det}-\mathbf r_{\rm vox}}{\left\lVert \mathbf r_{\rm det}-\mathbf r_{\rm vox}\right\rVert}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf x}
$$

where $d_x$ is the x component of the neutron-detector direction unit
vector, $\mathbf r_{\rm det}$ is the detector-center position, $\mathbf
r_{\rm vox}$ is the voxel-center position, and $\hat{\mathbf x}$ is the
positive x basis vector.

Together with the [y
component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector) and [z
component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector), $d_x$
specifies the full normalized direction from the voxel center toward the
detector center; for nonzero separation the components satisfy
$d_x^2+d_y^2+d_z^2=1$.

sources.leaf_definition: Components along X axis for each voxel
sources.parent_definition: Vector that points from the centre of the voxel to the centre of the detector, described in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis.

NAMES.name: xenon_density
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of xenon ions at a given point in the plasma, summed over all
ionization states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon,
excluding neutral xenon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Xenon is a high-$Z$ noble-gas impurity (atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Xe} = 54$)
introduced into fusion plasmas for radiative-mantle experiments,
impurity-transport studies, and disruption mitigation. The xenon ion number
density $n_\mathrm{Xe}$ quantifies the local concentration of all charged
xenon species and enters the plasma effective charge through $Z_\mathrm{eff}
= \sum_i Z_i^2 n_i / n_e$, where $n_i$ is the partial density of ion species
$i$ and $n_e$ is the electron density.

The total xenon ion density is the sum over all ionic charge states:

$$
n_\mathrm{Xe} = \sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of xenon ions
carrying charge $ze$. The charge-state distribution is determined by coronal
equilibrium or collisional-radiative modeling at the local electron
temperature and density.

The xenon density profile is inferred from vacuum-ultraviolet or soft-X-ray
line emission via spectroscopy and tomographic inversion, or from
charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy using neutral-beam injection.
Spatially resolved forms include
[xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis) at the
innermost flux surface and xenon_density_at_pedestal in the edge transport
barrier, while
[volume_averaged_xenon_density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density) provides
the global impurity content figure of merit. The dimensionless impurity
fraction relative to electron density is given by xenon_fraction.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_xenon_density
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of xenon ions averaged along a chord through the plasma,
summed over all ionization states from singly ionized through fully stripped
xenon and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged xenon ion number density is the chord-length mean of the
local [xenon density](name:xenon_density), which sums xenon ions from singly
ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral xenon atoms. It
represents the xenon ion content sampled by a specified chord, not the local
value at any single point unless the local density is uniform along that
chord.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe},L} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{C}} n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)\, d\ell
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe},L}$ is the line-averaged xenon ion number
density, $\mathcal{C}$ is the chord segment over which the average is
defined, $L = \int_{\mathcal{C}} d\ell$ is its path length, $\ell$ is
distance along the chord, and $n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)$ is the local [xenon
density](name:xenon_density) evaluated on the chord.

The species aggregation is performed over charge states before the line
average: $n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)=\sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}(\ell)$,
where $z$ is the xenon ionic charge-state index, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is
the partial density of xenon ions carrying charge $ze$, and $e$ is the
elementary charge. The physical population is charged xenon ions located on
the chord segment through the plasma; neutral xenon atoms and
charge-state-resolved xenon densities are excluded.

This quantity differs from [volume-averaged xenon
density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which averages the same local
xenon density over the plasma volume, and from [xenon density at magnetic
axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which evaluates it at the
magnetic-axis locus. It is the xenon counterpart of [line-averaged argon
density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) under the same chord-mean
convention.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short:
Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the y direction
cosine, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) basis, of the unit vector
from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center.
NAMES.long:
Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the signed
projection, in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
basis, of the unit vector directed from a field-of-view voxel center toward
the detector center. It is the y direction cosine of that line-of-sight
direction.

The component is defined by projecting the detector-directed unit vector
onto the $\hat{y}$ basis vector:

$$
u_y = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}} \cdot \hat{y} = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}) \cdot \hat{y}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}} \rVert}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the unit vector from the
field-of-view voxel center to the detector center,
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the detector-center position,
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}$ is the field-of-view voxel-center position, and
$\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},
\hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity is a signed direction-cosine component, not a position
coordinate, distance, or unnormalized displacement component. Together with
the corresponding x and z components it satisfies $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 =
1$ when the field-of-view voxel center and detector center are distinct.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis  for each voxel
sources.parent_definition: Vector that points from the centre of the voxel to the centre of the detector, described in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis.

NAMES.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short:
Z component in the right-handed Cartesian (x̂, ŷ, ẑ) basis of the unit
direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the neutron detector
center, with ẑ vertical. It is the vertical direction cosine, not a
position coordinate.
NAMES.long:
Z component in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
basis of the unit direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the
neutron detector center is the projection of that voxel-to-detector
direction onto the vertical basis vector $\hat{z}$. It represents the
vertical direction cosine of the ray from the voxel toward the detector
center.

The component is defined by the normalized displacement from the voxel
position to the detector-center position:

$$
u_z = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v) \cdot \hat{z}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v \rVert}
$$

where $u_z$ is the z component of the direction unit vector, $\mathbf{r}_v$
is the field-of-view voxel position, $\mathbf{r}_d$ is the neutron
detector-center position, and $\hat{z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

Together with
[x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector)
and
[y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector),
it forms the direction-cosine triplet of the same voxel-to-detector ray, so
$u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$ and $-1 \le u_z \le 1$. This quantity is a
direction cosine, not a vertical position coordinate or displacement
magnitude; it is the neutron-detector analog of
[z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera).

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Z axis  for each voxel
sources.parent_definition: Vector that points from the centre of the voxel to the centre of the detector, described in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis.

NAMES.name: floating_electrostatic_potential
NAMES.short:
Electrostatic potential of an electrically floating Langmuir-probe collector
relative to a chosen electrical reference, at which the net electric current
to the collector vanishes.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the electrostatic potential of an electrically floating
Langmuir-probe collector, relative to a chosen electrical reference. It is a
current-balance-constrained value of [electrostatic
potential](name:electrostatic_potential), specifying electrostatic
interaction energy per positive test charge at the collector.

The defining floating condition is

$$
I_{\mathrm{net}}(V_{\mathrm{f}})=0
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{f}}$ is the collector's floating electrostatic potential
relative to the chosen reference and $I_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the total
electric current entering the collector, including particle collection and
any emission contributions. Zero net current does not require the individual
electron, ion, or emitted-particle currents to vanish.

This quantity applies to an individual plasma-exposed collector, whether
fixed or moving. It is not a wall-surface or magnetic-flux-surface average,
and it does not denote an externally imposed collector bias.

It is distinct from the [plasma electrostatic potential at a Langmuir-probe
position](name:electrostatic_potential_at_langmuir_probe_position): a sheath
can sustain a potential difference between the plasma and the floating
collector. That difference is governed by current balance and depends on the
electron temperature, particle distributions, and any emission
contributions; no universal fixed offset is implied.

The [fluctuating floating electrostatic
potential](name:fluctuating_floating_electrostatic_potential) is the
standard deviation of fluctuations of this quantity, rather than its signed
value.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a positive test charge has greater
electrostatic potential energy at the floating collector than at the chosen
reference.

sources.leaf_definition: Floating potential
sources.parent_definition: Set of embedded (in a plasma facing component) probes

sources.leaf_definition: Floating potential
sources.parent_definition: Set of probe collectors including measurements specific to each collector. The number of collectors (size of this array of structure) is assumed to remain constant for all plunges

NAMES.name: line_averaged_argon_density
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Chord-averaged number density of argon ions along a specified plasma path,
with contributions from all ionization stages summed together.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged argon ion number density is the argon ion concentration
averaged along a specified chord through the plasma, including all
ionization stages.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{Ar} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl
$$

where $L$ is the chord length, $l$ is distance along the chord,
$\mathbf{r}(l)$ is the position on the chord, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}$ is the
local number density of argon ions in charge state $q$.

This path average is distinct from the local [argon ion
density](name:argon_density) and from the plasma-volume average
[volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_boron_density
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density
averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all
boron ionization states, giving a chord-averaged measure of elemental boron
impurity content.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density
averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all
ionization states of boron, so it represents the chord-averaged elemental
boron impurity content rather than a local point value.

The line average over a chord of path length $L$ is defined by the path
integral of the local charge-state-summed boron density along arc length
$l$:

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{z=0}^{5} n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)\, dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell}$ is the line-averaged boron density,
$n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)$ is the local boron number density in ionization
state $z$ at position $l$ along the chord, $z=0$ denotes neutral boron,
$z=5$ denotes fully stripped B$^{5+}$, and $L$ is the total path length used
for the average.

This quantity is a chord average of the charge-state-summed elemental [boron
density](name:boron_density); it is not a charge-state-resolved boron
density and does not exclude neutral boron. It differs from [volume-averaged
boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density), which averages the same
elemental density over the confined plasma volume.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_carbon_density
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Line-averaged total number density of elemental carbon along a specified
plasma chord, summed over neutral carbon and all ionic charge states through
C6+.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged carbon density is the chord average of the total number
density of elemental carbon, encompassing neutral carbon atoms and all ionic
charge states from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+.

It is defined from the local [carbon density](name:carbon_density) along the
chord:

$$
\bar n_C = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_C(\ell)\,d\ell = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{z=0}^{6} n_{C^{z+}}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\bar n_C$ is the line-averaged carbon density, $n_C(\ell)$ is the
local carbon density in m$^{-3}$, $n_{C^{z+}}(\ell)$ is the local density of
carbon charge state $z+$ in m$^{-3}$, $\ell$ is distance along the chord in
m, and $L$ is the chord length in m. This chord average is distinct from
[volume-averaged carbon density](name:volume_averaged_carbon_density), which
averages over the confined plasma volume.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_deuterium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number
density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is
charge-state-summed over ionized deuterium and excludes neutral or molecular
deuterium and non-deuterium species.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number
density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It represents the
path-length mean of the local deuterium density along the specified chord,
with deuterium treated as a species-level ion density.

The line average is defined by the path-length average of the local
[deuterium density](name:deuterium_density):

$$
\langle n_D \rangle_\ell = \frac{1}{L} \int_{\ell_0}^{\ell_1} n_D(\ell) \, d\ell
$$

where $\langle n_D \rangle_\ell$ is the line-averaged deuterium density,
$\ell$ is arclength along the chord, $\ell_0$ and $\ell_1$ are the endpoints
of the averaging interval, $L = \ell_1 - \ell_0$ is the chord path length,
and $n_D(\ell)$ is the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) at
position $\ell$.

The local deuterium density entering the integral is charge-state-summed
over ionized atomic charge states; for deuterium this reduces to the singly
ionized deuteron population. Neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium,
and non-deuterium species are excluded. This quantity is a path average;
local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) and [deuterium ion density
averaged over the total plasma
volume](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) are distinct quantities.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_effective_charge
NAMES.short:
Effective charge of a plasma ion mixture averaged uniformly along a
specified line of sight, expressing its chord-mean composition factor for
electron–ion Coulomb scattering.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge averaged along a specified plasma line of sight describes
the chord-mean charge-state composition of the ion mixture relevant to
electron–ion Coulomb scattering.

The line average is defined by:

$$
\bar{Z}_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L Z_{\mathrm{eff}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{Z}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the line-averaged effective charge,
$Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge),
$L$ is the length of the specified plasma chord, and $l$ is distance along
that chord.

The local composition factor is $Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_a n_a Z_a^2/n_e$,
where $a$ indexes all ion species and their ionized charge states, $n_a$ is
the number density of each ionic population, $Z_a$ is its charge number, and
$n_e$ is the free-electron number density. The mixture includes both fuel
and impurity ions; it is not the mean charge number of a selected species.

The averaging uses uniform length weighting of the local effective charge.
It is distinct from an unnormalized chord integral, an emissivity-weighted
average, or a ratio formed from separately chord-integrated charge moments.

sources.leaf_definition: Average effective charge along the line of sight
sources.parent_definition: Set of channels (detector or pixel of a camera)

sources.leaf_definition: Ionic effective charge, line average along the channel line-of-sight
sources.parent_definition: Set of channels (lines-of-sight). The line-of-sight is defined by the centre of the collimating aperture and the position of the measurements.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Effective charge

NAMES.name: line_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Thermal energy of the bulk electron population expressed as an
energy-equivalent temperature, averaged along a plasma chord.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged electron temperature is the energy-equivalent measure of the
mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged along a
plasma chord.

The defining path-length average is:

$$
T_{e,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L T_e(l)\,dl
$$

where $T_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-averaged electron temperature,
$T_e(l)$ is the local [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature) at
path coordinate $l$, and $L$ is the total chord length. The coordinate $l$
measures distance along the specified plasma chord, and the averaging is
uniform with respect to path length.

This is an intensive quantity for the bulk electron population, aggregated
along the chord rather than summed over electron energies or particle
populations. It excludes ion temperatures and differs from the local
electron temperature because it combines values along the entire chord.

The line average is a chord-integrated representation of the parent
[electron_temperature](name:electron_temperature), whereas
[volume_averaged_electron_temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature)
applies a volume average over the confined plasma and is therefore a
distinct spatial aggregation.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron temperature

NAMES.name: line_averaged_hydrogen_density
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Line-averaged number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma,
giving the path-length-normalized H+ concentration along a specified chord.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the mean concentration of
protium ions along a specified chord through the plasma. It represents the
path-integrated hydrogen ion content normalized by the chord length.

The line average is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{C}} n_H(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl
$$

where $\overline{n}_H$ is the line-averaged hydrogen density,
$n_H(\mathbf{r}(l))$ is the local protium-ion number density at position
$\mathbf{r}(l)$ along the chord, $l$ is the path-length coordinate,
$\mathcal{C}$ is the specified chord, and $L$ is its total length.

The quantity applies to charged protium ions, with any included protium ion
charge states summed before the line average; neutral atomic hydrogen and
heavier hydrogenic isotopes are excluded. It is a chord average rather than
the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density) at a point or the volume
average represented by
[volume_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density).

Unlike
[line_averaged_total_ion_density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density), it
does not include other ion species or hydrogen isotopes. The path-length
normalization preserves the same density meaning as the parent local
quantity while replacing its pointwise value with an average along the
chord.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_iron_density
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Line-averaged iron density is the path-length mean of total iron
impurity-ion number density, summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged iron density is the chord-length mean of the total iron ion
number density along a specified line of sight. It includes all ionization
states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and does not resolve their
individual contributions.

The line average is defined as

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}}$ is the line-averaged density,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)$ is the local iron ion number density at path coordinate
$l$, and $L$ is the total chord length.

The local quantity being averaged is the charge-state-summed [iron
density](name:iron_density). This chord average is distinct from
[line_averaged_argon_density](name:line_averaged_argon_density), which
applies the same path averaging to argon ions, and from a volume-averaged
iron density, which averages over a plasma volume rather than a line of
sight.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Chord-averaged number density of tritium ions, obtained by averaging local
tritium ion density along a specified chord.
NAMES.long:
Chord-averaged tritium ion density is the path-length mean of the local
tritium ion number density along a specified chord. It is derived from the
local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density) and represents the
chord-integrated fuel content normalized by chord length.

$$
\overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_T(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\overline{n}_T$ is the chord-averaged density, $n_T(\ell)$ is the
local tritium ion density at path coordinate $\ell$, and $L$ is the chord
length. The average includes the specified chord segment and is distinct
from the confined-volume mean
[volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density) and
from the corresponding helium-4 quantity
[line_averaged_helium_4_density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser
NAMES.short:
Major-radius location of the Thomson-scattering laser endpoint, measured as
perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of a Thomson-scattering laser is the major-radius
position of its laser-beam endpoint, measured from the toroidal symmetry
axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
R_{\mathrm{end}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{end}}^2+y_{\mathrm{end}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{end}}$ is the endpoint major-radius coordinate, and
$x_{\mathrm{end}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{end}}$ are the endpoint coordinates along
the two horizontal axes of the right-handed Cartesian basis
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{z}$ aligned with the vertical
direction $\hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies to one laser endpoint and is a geometric point
coordinate, not a path average, scattering-volume coordinate, beam
attribute, or plasma-population quantity. It is neither summed nor averaged
over lasers, endpoints, or plasma regions.

It is the Thomson-scattering-laser-specific realization of [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), providing the $R$ coordinate of the
endpoint. It is distinct from the [toroidal coordinate of the
Thomson-scattering
laser](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser), which
specifies the endpoint's toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Position of the laser end point

NAMES.name: ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Local ion concentration relative to the electron population, defined as the
number-density ratio for a specified impurity or fuel ion species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local abundance of a specified impurity or fuel ion
species relative to the free-electron population. It compares particle
populations rather than electric charge density or mass density.

The local ion-to-electron concentration ratio is defined by

$$
\mathcal{R}_{i/e} = \frac{n_i}{n_e}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{i/e}$ is the ion-to-electron concentration ratio, $n_i$
is the local number density of the specified ion species, $n_e$ is the local
free-electron number density, $i$ identifies the selected ion species, and
$e$ identifies the electron population.

Both densities are evaluated at the same local plasma point. For a
species-level numerator without an explicitly selected charge state, $n_i$
is summed over all ionization states of that species; a
charge-state-resolved numerator applies only to the selected state. No
spatial average or line integration is implied.

The numerator is supplied by the corresponding [ion
density](name:ion_density), while [ion charge state
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) represents the density when one
charge state is isolated. A named-species example of the same construction
is the [ratio of iron density to electron
density](name:ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density). This quantity is
distinct from an ion charge-state fraction, electric charge-density ratio,
or mass-density ratio.

sources.leaf_definition: Ion concentration (ratio of the ion density over the electron density) at the channel measurement point
sources.parent_definition: Physical quantities related to ion species and charge stage (H+, D+, T+, He+2, Li+3, Be+4, C+6, N+7, O+8, Ne+10, Si+14, Ar+16 or Ar+18) derived from the measured charge exchange emission of each species, at the position of the measurement

NAMES.name: total_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population, with all species and charge states contributing according to
their number densities.
NAMES.long:
The total ion temperature is the density-weighted effective temperature of
the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion
species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes
directed bulk-flow energy.

The local effective temperature is defined by

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_s T_s}{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_s}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density and $T_s$ is the ion temperature of
species or charge state $s$, and $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of included
thermal ion populations. Thus, “total” denotes a density-weighted
combination, not an arithmetic sum of temperatures. Spatially transformed
instances apply line or volume averaging to this combined quantity, as in
[line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature)
and
[volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature);
the underlying species-resolved quantity is
[ion_temperature](name:ion_temperature).

NAMES.name: line_averaged_total_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population, with all species and charge states contributing by number
density and averaged along a specified plasma chord.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged total ion temperature is the line average of the local
density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It
represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The chord average is defined by

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{C}} T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)\,d\ell}{\int_{\mathcal{C}}d\ell}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-averaged quantity,
$T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)$ is the local [total ion
temperature](name:total_ion_temperature), $\ell$ is path length along the
chord, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the specified chord. Species and charge states
are combined by number density before the line average is taken. Unlike the
[volume-averaged total ion
temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity
weights positions by chord length rather than plasma volume.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: accumulated_ammonia_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of ammonia molecules introduced into the
plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count
units assigned to each neutral NH3 molecule.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated ammonia count is the cumulative post-breakdown amount of NH3
introduced into the plasma vessel, represented using an equivalent-electron
accounting convention. It is the post-breakdown component of the total
ammonia count, not a direct count of free plasma electrons.

$$
C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = (Z_\mathrm{N}+3Z_\mathrm{H})N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}
$$

Here, $C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the accumulated
equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the
cumulative number of ammonia molecules introduced after plasma breakdown,
and $Z_\mathrm{N}=7$ and $Z_\mathrm{H}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen
and hydrogen. The quantity excludes ammonia introduced during prefill, which
is represented by [ammonia prefill count](name:ammonia_prefill_count), and
does not represent instantaneous injection rate, retained neutral inventory,
ionization state, or actual free-electron content.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ammonia (NH3)

NAMES.name: accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3),
expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units per molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative number of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3)
molecules introduced after plasma breakdown, converted to an
equivalent-electron count. It is the post-breakdown contribution to
ammonia_deuterated_count, distinct from the prefill contribution
[ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count](name:ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count).

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = 10N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the dimensionless
equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the
cumulative neutral-molecule count after breakdown, and $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$
and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen and deuterium.
This is a bookkeeping quantity, not the number of free electrons in the
plasma and not an instantaneous injection rate.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterated ammonia (ND3)

NAMES.name: accumulated_argon_count
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of
argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each argon
atom contributes 18 equivalent electrons, equal to its atomic number; this
is delivered inventory, not plasma electron content or ionization state.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of
argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each
delivered argon atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ equivalent electrons,
equal to the atomic number of argon.

The accumulated count is defined by integrating the delivered argon atom
injection rate from the plasma-breakdown time:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t')\,dt', \qquad Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron argon
count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate in atoms per
second, $t$ is time in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time in seconds.

This quantity includes only argon delivered after breakdown. Argon
introduced before breakdown belongs to the pre-breakdown inventory
represented by argon_count; the accumulated value is not a measure of free
electrons, plasma argon content, retained argon, or argon ionization state,
and is not reduced by subsequent pumping, exhaust, wall retention,
ionization, radiation, or redistribution.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon

NAMES.name: accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown carbon inventory from gas injection, expressed as
six equivalent-electron counts for every injected neutral carbon atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of carbon atoms
delivered by gas injection, represented as an equivalent-electron count. It
excludes carbon introduced during the plasma prefill phase and does not
represent an instantaneous source rate or a charge-state-resolved ion
inventory.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}(t)=6N_{\mathrm{C}}(t)=6\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$
is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}$ is the carbon injection rate,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation
time. The factor 6 is carbon's atomic number. This is the post-breakdown
component of carbon count due to gas injection and is distinct from [carbon
prefill count due to gas
injection](name:carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon

NAMES.name: accumulated_deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of deuterium delivered by gas
injection after plasma breakdown.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of deuterium atoms
delivered through gas injection, expressed using an equivalent-electron
weighting. It represents delivered fuel inventory rather than an
instantaneous injection rate or the number of electrons currently present in
the plasma.

The equivalent-electron convention is defined by

$$
N_D^{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_D N_D
$$

where $N_D^{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron inventory, $Z_D$ is the
atomic number of deuterium and equals one, and $N_D$ is the cumulative
number of deuterium atoms delivered after plasma breakdown.

The scope is restricted to deuterium introduced after plasma breakdown by
gas injection. Contributions are accumulated over the injection history and
weighted per deuterium atom; prefill delivery and other injected species are
excluded. Ionization after delivery does not change the assigned
equivalent-electron weighting.

The weighting convention is shared by
[accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection)
and
[accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection),
while this quantity remains specific to deuterium.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium

NAMES.name: accumulated_ethane_count
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of ethane molecules injected after
plasma breakdown, assigning 18 equivalent-electron counts to each neutral
C2H6 molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the post-breakdown cumulative ethane-gas inventory
expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral C2H6 molecule
contributes 18 counts: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six
hydrogen atoms.

The accumulated count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 18\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the ethane molecule injection rate,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation
time.

This quantity is the accumulated post-breakdown form of the ethane count
convention. It excludes ethane introduced during prefill, represented by
[ethane prefill count](name:ethane_prefill_count), and differs from the
instantaneous [ethane source rate](name:ethane_source_rate).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ethane (C2H6)

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas
injection after plasma breakdown, assigning two count units to each atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of helium-3 atoms
delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It
represents delivered atomic inventory, not the number of free plasma
electrons or the ionization state of the helium-3.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t')\,dt'
$$

Here, $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count,
$Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the helium-3 atom delivery rate in atoms
per second, $t$ and $t'$ are times in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time.

The quantity includes only helium-3 delivered after breakdown and is
cumulative rather than instantaneous. The corresponding instantaneous
delivery rate is [helium-3 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), while
[accumulated helium-3 prefill count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection)
covers delivery before breakdown.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms introduced by gas
injection during plasma prefill before plasma breakdown, with two count
units assigned per atom.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the cumulative inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas
injection during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. It covers injection before plasma breakdown and
excludes helium-3 introduced after breakdown.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} = 2\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count,
$Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number,
$N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injected helium-3 atom count,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injection rate in s$^{-1}$, and
$t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in s.

This is the pre-breakdown counterpart of [accumulated helium-3 count due to
gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection);
[helium-3 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) represents the
instantaneous rate rather than the accumulated inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons

NAMES.name: accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown equivalent-electron inventory of neutral hydrogen
delivered by gas injection, with one count unit assigned to each hydrogen
atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral hydrogen atoms
delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Hydrogen contributes one equivalent electron per
atom because its atomic number is one.

$$
N_{H,mathrm{gas}}(t)=Z_H\,\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_H(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{H,\mathrm{gas}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count,
$Z_H=1$ is hydrogen's atomic number, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time, and $\dot{N}_H$ is the neutral-hydrogen injection
rate. The corresponding instantaneous rate is [hydrogen source rate due to
gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The accumulation begins at breakdown and excludes hydrogen introduced during
prefill; it represents delivered hydrogen inventory rather than the number
of free plasma electrons or the ionization-state distribution. It is the
post-breakdown component of hydrogen count due to gas injection, distinct
from [accumulated hydrogen prefill
count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen

NAMES.name: accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of hydrogen atoms introduced by gas
injection during prefill before plasma breakdown; hydrogen contributes one
count per atom.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the cumulative hydrogen atom inventory delivered by gas
injection during the prefill interval ending at plasma breakdown, expressed
using the equivalent-electron convention. It is the hydrogen-specific
contribution to the hydrogen prefill count.

$$
N_{\mathrm{H,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}N_{\mathrm{H}} = N_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{H}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}(t)\,dt
$$

Here $N_{\mathrm{H,eq}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ are dimensionless
equivalent-electron and atom counts, $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ is hydrogen's atomic
number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen injection rate in s$^{-1}$,
and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in
s. Only pre-breakdown gas injection is included; post-breakdown delivery is
represented by [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen

NAMES.name: accumulated_krypton_count
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma
breakdown, expressed as 36 equivalent electrons for each krypton atom.
NAMES.long:
Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma
breakdown, expressed as 36 equivalent electrons for each krypton atom, is
the post-breakdown time integral of the krypton atom influx into the machine
with a fixed species multiplier. The multiplier is the krypton atomic number
used as an equivalent-electron counting convention.

The accumulated count at time $t$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Kr,acc}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Kr,acc}}$ is the accumulated krypton count,
$Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the krypton atomic-number multiplier,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton atom injection rate into the machine,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ is the evaluation time,
and $t'$ is the integration time.

The scope is krypton introduced after plasma breakdown; it excludes krypton
present before breakdown, non-krypton species, instantaneous injection rate,
and any plasma number density. The species population is not charge-state
resolved; if charge-state labels are used, krypton contributions are summed
over all charge states before applying the fixed multiplier.

The equivalent-electron convention means this quantity equals 36 times the
unweighted accumulated krypton atom count. It follows the same
post-breakdown accumulated-species convention as [accumulated neon
count](name:accumulated_neon_count), [accumulated ammonia
count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count), and [accumulated helium-3 count due
to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
factor 36 is a counting convention and does not specify the ionization state
of the injected krypton.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton

NAMES.name: accumulated_lithium_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown lithium inventory delivered by gas injection,
expressed as three equivalent-electron counts per injected lithium atom.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the cumulative inventory of lithium atoms introduced by gas
injection after plasma breakdown, re-expressed as an equivalent-electron
count. It represents delivered lithium inventory, not the number of
electrons currently present in the plasma or a lithium ion charge-state
population.

The cumulative value at time $t$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Li,eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{Li}}\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li,eq}}(t)$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron lithium
inventory, $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is lithium's atomic number and equals three,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}(t')$ is the lithium-atom injection rate at
integration time $t'$, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

The accumulation begins at plasma breakdown and includes only lithium
delivered by gas injection, with three equivalent-electron counts assigned
to each lithium atom. It excludes lithium introduced during prefill,
represented by [accumulated lithium prefill count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection), and
excludes inventories of other species. The equivalent-electron weighting is
an inventory convention, not a measurement of lithium ionization or the
instantaneous plasma electron population.

The corresponding instantaneous source is the [lithium source rate due to
gas injection](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection); integrating
that source from breakdown gives the accumulated post-breakdown inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium

NAMES.name: accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of lithium introduced by gas
injection during plasma prefill, assigning three count units to each lithium
atom.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated lithium prefill count is the equivalent-electron inventory
of lithium introduced by gas injection before plasma breakdown. Each lithium
atom contributes three equivalent-electron counts, corresponding to its
atomic number.

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,Li}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}} N_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3\int_{t_{\mathrm{start}}}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,Li}}$ is the equivalent-electron inventory,
$Z_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is lithium's atomic number, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the
introduced lithium-atom inventory, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium
injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ is the prefill start time, and
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity describes delivered lithium inventory during prefill, not the
instantaneous [lithium source
rate](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), post-breakdown
[accumulated lithium
count](name:accumulated_lithium_count_due_to_gas_injection), or the
inventory of all injected species represented by [accumulated total prefill
gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium

NAMES.name: accumulated_neon_count
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma
breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons; each injected neon atom
contributes ten equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma
breakdown is the time integral of the neon atom injection rate due to gas
injection, weighted by the neon atomic number. It is a species-specific
accumulated count expressed in equivalent electrons, so each injected neon
atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ equivalent electrons.

The accumulated neon count $N_{\mathrm{Ne,acc}}$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ne,acc}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne,inj}}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ is the evaluation
time, $t'$ is the integration time, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne,inj}}$ is the
neutral-neon atom injection rate due to gas injection, and
$Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the number of electrons in a neutral neon atom.

The scope is neon supplied by gas injection during the interval from plasma
breakdown to the evaluation time; the aggregation is cumulative over
injected neon atoms, with equivalent-electron weighting applied per atom. It
excludes neon present before breakdown, neon supplied by non-gas-injection
sources, retained inventory, pumped-out amount, and charge-state-resolved
plasma neon populations.

This quantity is the accumulated gas-injection counterpart of the species
neon count convention, with the additional accumulation interval and
equivalent-electron weighting. It follows the same accumulated
equivalent-electron convention as [accumulated krypton
count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) and [accumulated ammonia
count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count); a neutral-neon atom count without
equivalent-electron weighting is obtained by dividing by $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon

NAMES.name: accumulated_nitrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown nitrogen inventory delivered by gas injection,
expressed as seven equivalent-electron counts for each injected nitrogen
atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of nitrogen
delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. It represents the
nitrogen contribution to the injected fueling and impurity inventory.

The equivalent-electron inventory is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{N}} N_{\mathrm{N}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory,
$Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ is the atomic number of nitrogen, and $N_{\mathrm{N}}$ is
the cumulative number of nitrogen atoms delivered by gas injection after
breakdown.

The quantity applies only to nitrogen delivered after plasma breakdown and
aggregates all such delivered nitrogen over the accumulation interval. It is
a cumulative inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate, and it is the
nitrogen-specific contribution rather than an all-species inventory.

The equivalent-electron convention counts seven contributions per nitrogen
atom; it does not represent the number of free electrons currently present
in the plasma and is independent of the nitrogen ionization state. This
convention is shared by accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection, which
applies the corresponding atomic-number weighting to accumulated carbon.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen

NAMES.name: accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Cumulative oxygen gas introduced during the prefill phase by gas injection,
expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each oxygen atom contributes
8 count units equal to its atomic number.
NAMES.long:
The prefill phase precedes plasma breakdown, during which controlled gas
injection establishes an initial neutral gas background in the vessel. This
quantity accumulates the total oxygen inventory delivered during that phase,
representing each oxygen atom as 8 equivalent electrons equal to the atomic
number $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$.

The equivalent-electron inventory is defined as:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{O} \cdot N_\mathrm{O}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{O}$ is the total number of oxygen atoms injected during the
prefill interval and $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$ is the atomic number of oxygen.

The count is inferred from calibrated gas injection valve records integrated
over the prefill interval, from the start of the prefill phase through
plasma breakdown. It is the accumulated component of
oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection and follows the same
equivalent-electron convention applied to helium-3 in
[accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection)
and to lithium in
[accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).
Post-breakdown oxygen injection is tracked separately by
[oxygen_count](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen

NAMES.name: accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
NAMES.short:
Cumulative number of particles released by ablation from an injected pellet
up to a specified position along its trajectory.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative particle release from pellet ablation as the
pellet travels through the plasma. It counts particles removed from the
pellet up to the specified trajectory position, rather than particles
remaining in the pellet.

The accumulated release at path distance $\ell$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{abl}}(\ell)=\int_{\ell_0}^{\ell}\frac{dN_{\mathrm{abl}}}{d\ell'}\,d\ell'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{abl}}$ is the dimensionless released-particle count,
$\ell$ and $\ell'$ are distances along the pellet trajectory in m, $\ell_0$
is the trajectory entry position, and $dN_{\mathrm{abl}}/d\ell'$ is the
local ablation release per unit path distance.

The count is nondecreasing along the trajectory when the ablation release
rate is nonnegative. It represents deposited pellet material and is distinct
from the initial pellet inventory given by count of pellet.

sources.leaf_definition: Number of ablated particles (electrons) along the pellet path
sources.parent_definition: 1-D profiles of plasma and pellet along the pellet path

NAMES.name: accumulated_propane_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown propane inventory delivered by gas injection,
expressed as 26 equivalent electrons for each neutral molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral propane
($\mathrm{C_3H_8}$) molecules delivered by gas injection after plasma
breakdown. It represents delivered propane inventory, not the number of free
electrons in the plasma or the ionization state of the propane.

For evaluation time $t$ after breakdown, the equivalent-electron count is
defined by:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 26N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t) = \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} 26\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count,
$N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of propane molecules
delivered by time $t$, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t')$ is the instantaneous
propane molecular delivery rate at integration time $t'$, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$
is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t'$ is the integration variable. The
factor 26 is the total number of electrons in one neutral propane molecule:
three carbon atoms contribute six each and eight hydrogen atoms contribute
one each.

The scope is restricted to propane introduced by gas injection after
breakdown and includes all such molecules delivered up to the evaluation
time. It excludes prefill propane and does not represent inventory from
other gas species, free plasma-electron content, or an
ionization-state-resolved amount.

Unlike the [propane prefill count](name:propane_prefill_count), which covers
propane introduced before breakdown, this quantity covers the post-breakdown
interval. Unlike the [propane source rate](name:propane_source_rate), it is
cumulative rather than instantaneous.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Propane (C3H8)

NAMES.name: accumulated_silane_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: silane
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of silane molecules delivered by gas
injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 equivalent
electrons per neutral SiH4 molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral silane (SiH4) molecules
delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, represented on an
equivalent-electron basis.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = 18N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count and
$N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}$ is the cumulative number of neutral silane molecules
delivered after breakdown. The factor 18 is the sum of silicon's 14
atomic-number electrons and four hydrogen atoms' one atomic-number electron
each.

The scope is silane delivered after plasma breakdown specifically by gas
injection. The count is cumulative over all such delivery and is not an
instantaneous rate, a count of free electrons in the plasma, or a
charge-state-resolved inventory; subsequent ionization, transport,
retention, and removal do not change the delivered-inventory convention. The
corresponding instantaneous quantity is the [silane source
rate](name:silane_source_rate).

Like the [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), this
quantity uses an equivalent-electron aggregation, but silane contributes 18
equivalent electrons per molecule rather than one per hydrogen atom.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Silane (SiH4)

NAMES.name: accumulated_total_gas_count
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of all gas species delivered by
injection after plasma breakdown, summed across species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of gas
introduced into the plasma by injection after plasma breakdown. It combines
all injected gas species into one total inventory.

The total is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = \sum_s z_s N_s(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $s$
identifies an injected gas species, $N_s(t)$ is the cumulative number of
particles of species $s$ delivered since plasma breakdown, and $z_s$ is the
equivalent-electron contribution per particle; for an atomic species, $z_s$
is its atomic number, while for a molecule it is the sum of the atomic
numbers of its constituent atoms.

The quantity applies to all gas species and uses a cumulative sum over the
post-breakdown injection history. It excludes gas introduced during prefill
before plasma breakdown, instantaneous injection rates, and any
single-species inventory such as [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

It is the post-breakdown counterpart of the prefill inventory [accumulated
total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count); the two
quantities differ by the injection phase they accumulate.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total accumulated injected gas (sum over species)

NAMES.name: accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Cumulative number of tritium atoms delivered by gas injection since plasma
breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each tritium atom
corresponds to one equivalent electron.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated tritium count due to gas injection is the running total of
tritium ($^3\mathrm{H}$) atoms introduced to the plasma vessel through gas
injection valves, accumulated continuously from plasma breakdown onward. The
quantity is dimensionless, representing each injected atom as an
equivalent-electron contribution scaled by its atomic number.

For tritium, whose atomic number is $Z = 1$, the equivalent-electron
inventory equals the raw atom count directly:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z \cdot N_\mathrm{atoms} = N_\mathrm{atoms}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{atoms}$ is the total number of tritium atoms injected after
breakdown. The equivalent-electron convention provides a species-independent
basis for comparing injected particle inventories — for higher-$Z$ species
such as argon ($Z = 18$), the multiplier is correspondingly larger.

This is the time-integrated form of tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection,
accumulating monotonically as gas is puffed after breakdown. Tritium
introduced before breakdown is tracked separately as tritium_prefill_count.
The deuterium analog in the same equivalent-electron framework is
[deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium

NAMES.name: accumulated_xenon_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Cumulative post-breakdown xenon inventory delivered by gas injection,
expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 54 count units assigned to
each xenon atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of xenon atoms introduced by gas
injection after plasma breakdown, represented using an equivalent-electron
counting convention. It denotes delivered xenon inventory rather than
instantaneous xenon content in the plasma.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} N_{\mathrm{Xe}} = 54 N_{\mathrm{Xe}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron xenon
inventory, $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon atomic number, and
$N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the cumulative number of xenon atoms delivered by
post-breakdown gas injection.

The scope is limited to xenon atoms delivered after plasma breakdown, with
contributions from all post-breakdown gas-injection events cumulatively
summed. No other injected species are included, and the quantity is not an
instantaneous injection rate.

The equivalent-electron convention uses the xenon atomic number and does not
represent the actual number of free plasma electrons supplied by xenon; it
is independent of the xenon ionization state. Gas introduced before
breakdown is excluded and belongs to the distinct [accumulated xenon prefill
inventory](name:accumulated_xenon_prefill_count), which provides the
corresponding prefill contribution.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon

NAMES.name: accumulated_xenon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon introduced during
plasma prefill, ending at plasma breakdown, with 54 count units per atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon gas
introduced between the start of prefill and plasma breakdown. It represents
the accumulated prefill contribution, not an instantaneous injection rate.

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}^{\mathrm{prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)$ is the neutral xenon atom injection rate,
$t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times, and
$Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}=54$ is xenon's atomic number. The resulting count assigns
54 equivalent-electron units to each xenon atom.

This quantity is the prefill component of xenon_prefill_count and excludes
xenon introduced after breakdown, which is represented by
accumulated_xenon_count.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon

NAMES.name: ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
NAMES.short:
Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ND3
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count with 10 count units per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterated
ammonia (ND3) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown,
expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ND3 molecule
contributes ten equivalent electrons: seven from nitrogen and one from each
of its three deuterium atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = 10\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are atomic numbers,
$N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated molecule count,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}$ is the molecule injection rate, and $t_0$ and
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times.

This quantity includes only ND3 introduced before breakdown and excludes
wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and
retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterated-ammonia component of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count), distinct from
[ammonia_prefill_count](name:ammonia_prefill_count) and post-breakdown
[accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterated ammonia (ND3)

NAMES.name: ammonia_deuterated_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
