NAMES.short:
Instantaneous molecular injection rate of deuterated ammonia (ND3) supplied
to the plasma vessel by gas injection.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the rate at which deuterated ammonia (ND3) molecules are
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection. It counts ND3 molecules
directly rather than converting them to an equivalent-electron inventory.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of injected ND3
molecules and $t$ is time. The rate is distinct from the [ammonia source
rate](name:ammonia_source_rate), which refers to NH3 molecules, and its time
integral gives the injected molecular inventory represented by the
[accumulated deuterated ammonia
count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterated ammonia (ND3)

NAMES.name: ammonia_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short:
Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of NH3 introduced before plasma
breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count of 10 per neutral
molecule.
NAMES.long:
Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ammonia, NH3,
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count. Each neutral NH3 molecule contributes ten count units: seven from
nitrogen and one from each of its three hydrogen atoms.

The count is defined by the accumulated molecular amount over the prefill
interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} 10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated number of ammonia
molecules, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the ammonia injection rate in
molecules per second, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the start of
prefill and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This species-specific contribution is included in the common prebreakdown
bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count). Ammonia introduced after
breakdown is excluded and is represented by
[accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ammonia (NH3)

NAMES.name: ammonia_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous ammonia source rate expressed as equivalent-electron count per
time, assigning ten count units to each neutral NH3 molecule introduced into
the plasma vessel.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate of ammonia delivery to the plasma
vessel, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention for neutral
ammonia molecules. It represents injected NH3 inventory, not the plasma
electron source or the ionization state of ammonia.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = 10\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the molecular ammonia injection rate, and the
factor 10 is the total atomic-electron count of one neutral NH3 molecule.
Time integration gives the corresponding
[accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count). The
isotopologue-specific counterpart is
[ammonia_deuterated_source_rate](name:ammonia_deuterated_source_rate).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ammonia (NH3)

NAMES.name: argon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18
per atom.
NAMES.long:
Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced
during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral argon atom contributes 18 equivalent
electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected argon
atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the argon atomic
number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt = 18\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-argon atom
count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ is the argon atomic number,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the
prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only argon introduced before breakdown and excludes
wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and
retained or ionized inventory. It is the argon-specific component of
[prefill count](name:prefill_count) and follows the isotope-resolved
convention used for tritium prefill count.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon

NAMES.name: carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory introduced as carbon gas during
plasma prefill, with six count units assigned to each injected carbon atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of carbon
introduced by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, before plasma
breakdown. It represents injected carbon atoms rather than an instantaneous
injection rate.

The defining relation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{C}}N_{\mathrm{C}} = 6N_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$
is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms, and $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ is
the carbon atomic number. Both counts are dimensionless.

The prefill interval ends at plasma breakdown, so post-breakdown carbon
delivery is represented separately by [accumulated carbon count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
aggregation convention parallels [accumulated hydrogen prefill
count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count), with the atomic number
providing the equivalent-electron weighting.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon

NAMES.name: coolant_pressure
NAMES.short:
Absolute static pressure of the coolant or working fluid at a plant-system
component port, referenced to perfect vacuum rather than atmospheric or
another gage reference.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local thermodynamic pressure of the coolant or working
fluid at a component-port interface, with perfect vacuum as the
zero-pressure reference. Static pressure is the isotropic mechanical stress
of the fluid and excludes kinetic-energy contributions associated with bulk
flow.

$$
\boldsymbol{\sigma}=-p_{\mathrm{abs}}\mathbf{I}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the isotropic fluid Cauchy stress,
$p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the absolute static pressure, and $\mathbf{I}$ is the
identity tensor.

The value represents local pressure at the port, not stagnation pressure,
pressure drop, or pressure difference. At a cooling-circuit inlet, it is
related to cooling-circuit inlet pressure, while coolant flow through a
plant component port describes mass transport rather than mechanical
pressure.

sources.leaf_definition: Fluid pressure
sources.parent_definition: Set of ports (input or output) of the component

NAMES.name: coolant_temperature_of_plant_component_port
NAMES.short:
Thermodynamic temperature of the working coolant at a generic inlet or
outlet port of a power-conversion component.
NAMES.long:
Coolant temperature is the thermodynamic temperature describing the thermal
state of the working fluid at a connection port of a power-conversion
component.

The quantity applies to coolant at a generic plant-component port, which may
be an inlet or an outlet. It denotes the local fluid state at that port; no
summation, spatial averaging, or integration is implied. It excludes the
temperature of the component structure or any other material.

Unlike [coolant temperature at outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet),
this quantity does not restrict the port to an outlet. It is a thermal-state
quantity, whereas [coolant transit time of plant component
port](name:coolant_transit_time_of_plant_component_port) describes the
elapsed transport time between component ports rather than the coolant
temperature.

sources.leaf_definition: Fluid temperature
sources.parent_definition: Set of ports (input or output) of the component

NAMES.name: core_atomic_count_of_pellet
NAMES.short:
Core atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of individual atoms
contained in its core material, independent of bonding, phase, or species.
NAMES.long:
Core atomic count is the inventory of individual atoms contained in the core
material of one pellet. Molecules, compounds, and mixtures are resolved into
their constituent atoms before summation, independently of bonding, phase,
and species. It is the core-restricted component of atomic count of pellet
and is distinct from the outer atomic count of pellet.

For constituent entity types indexed by $i$, the core atomic inventory is
defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{core,atom}} = \sum_i a_i N_{i,\mathrm{core}}
$$

where $N_{i,\mathrm{core}}$ is the number of core entities of type $i$ and
$a_i$ is the number of atoms in each entity. The quantity includes atoms in
the pellet core and excludes atoms in other pellet layers and separately
counted propellant gas molecules; the whole-pellet inventory is atomic count
of pellet.

sources.leaf_definition: Total number of atoms of desublimated gas
sources.parent_definition: Core of the unshattered pellet

NAMES.name: deuterium_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with one
count unit per atom.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium (D)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral deuterium atom contributes one
equivalent electron.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected deuterium
atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the deuterium atomic
number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-deuterium atom
count, $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the deuterium atomic number,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the deuterium atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the
prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only deuterium introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterium-specific
component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count) and uses the same
isotope-resolved convention as tritium_prefill_count.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium

NAMES.name: deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous rate of deuterium particles supplied by active injection,
expressed on a common equivalent-electron basis.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection
systems for deuterium, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. Because
each deuterium atom has nuclear charge number one, the equivalent-electron
rate equals the deuterium particle rate.

The defining relation is

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{D}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)=\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the injected deuterium particle rate, and
$Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the dimensionless deuterium nuclear charge number.
This is a component of the multi-species [source rate due to
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection) and is distinct from the
charge-weighted [electron source rate due to
injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection). It represents
injected inventory supply, not a local volumetric particle source or a net
plasma production-minus-loss rate.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium

NAMES.name: diameter_of_pellet
NAMES.short:
Transverse extent of the intact cylindrical pellet before injection and
shattering, defined as the full width of its circular cross-section
perpendicular to the pellet axis.
NAMES.long:
Transverse extent of the intact cylindrical pellet before injection and
shattering is the full width of its circular cross-section measured
perpendicular to the pellet axis. It defines the pellet cross-sectional
geometry before fragmentation, ablation, or interaction with the plasma.

For an ideal right circular cylindrical pellet, the diameter and axial
length determine the pellet volume by

$$
V_\mathrm{pellet} = \frac{\pi}{4} d_\mathrm{pellet}^2 L_\mathrm{pellet}
$$

where $V_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the pellet volume, $d_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the
pellet diameter, and $L_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the [length of
pellet](name:length_of_pellet).

This quantity excludes the axial extent of the pellet, which is the [length
of pellet](name:length_of_pellet), and excludes characteristic sizes of
shattered fragments, ablated material, or the post-shattering material
cloud.

sources.leaf_definition: Pellet diameter
sources.parent_definition: Information related to the pellet

NAMES.name: efficiency_of_plant_system
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system converts
input power or energy into a specified useful output, abstracting over
thermal and net efficiency definitions.
NAMES.long:
The efficiency of a plant system is a dimensionless performance metric
expressing the fraction of input power or energy that the plant converts
into a specified useful output. The exact physical scope depends on the
efficiency type applied: [thermal
efficiency](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system) characterizes
heat-to-work conversion across all thermodynamic conversion stages, while
[net efficiency](name:net_efficiency_of_plant_system) accounts for the
signed ratio of exported electrical power to total plant electrical
consumption including recirculating power.

The general defining relation takes the form:

$$
\eta = \frac{W_\text{out}}{W_\text{in}}
$$

where $W_\text{out}$ is the useful output (work, exported electrical power,
or heat converted to work) and $W_\text{in}$ is the total input power or
energy over the same operating interval.

Efficiency is evaluated from calorimetric heat-flow surveys, electrical
generation meters, and auxiliary power consumption measurements across all
plant subsystems. For fusion facilities, thermal conversion efficiencies in
steam-cycle plants lie in the range 30–45%, and net electrical efficiencies
are further reduced by recirculating power fractions for heating, current
drive, and cooling systems.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_pellet_path
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Local free-electron number density of the background plasma at points along
a pellet's ablation trajectory.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local number density of free electrons in the background
plasma at each point traversed by an injected pellet. It describes the
plasma encountered by the pellet, not electron content in pellet material or
electron production by ablation.

At a path point, the electron number density is defined by the local
number-to-volume ratio:

$$
n_e = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{\Delta N_e}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\Delta N_e$ is the number of
free electrons in the volume element $\Delta V$, and $\Delta V$ is the
volume element centered at the path point.

The quantity is evaluated locally along the pellet trajectory and is
distinct from the [electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet
injection](name:electron_source_rate_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection),
which describes electron production rather than background density. It has
the same physical meaning as [electron density at the launching
position](name:electron_density_at_launching_position), but at a different
locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Electron density along the pellet path
sources.parent_definition: 1-D profiles of plasma and pellet along the pellet path

NAMES.name: electron_source_rate_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the
charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and
ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected
pellet trajectory.
NAMES.long:
Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the
charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and
ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected
pellet trajectory. It counts the free-electron source associated with
material reaching that path position, not the electron concentration of the
surrounding plasma.

For trajectory coordinate $\ell$ and time $t$, the local rate is defined by
the charge-weighted sum over ablated pellet constituents contributing at
that same path position:

$$
S_e(\ell,t) = \sum_a Z_a^\mathrm{eff}(\ell,t)\,\dot{N}_a(\ell,t)
$$

where $S_e$ is the electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet
injection, $a$ indexes the pellet constituents or represented charge-state
groups, $\dot{N}_a$ is the local production rate of constituent $a$ by
ablation and ionization, and $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective number of
free electrons contributed by one produced constituent. For a fully ionized
atomic constituent, $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ reduces to its nuclear charge.

This is a path-position rate, not a source density per distance along the
pellet trajectory or a volume-integrated source. The [electron source rate
due to injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection) is obtained
only after aggregating the appropriate local electron-equivalent
contributions, while electron density of pellet path describes electron
concentration along the same trajectory. The [accumulated particle count at
pellet path due to pellet
injection](name:accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection)
is an unweighted cumulative particle count; it is not an electron-equivalent
accumulated source unless the same charge weighting and time integration are
applied.

The value is non-negative and is zero where injected pellet material at the
considered path position does not produce free electrons.

sources.leaf_definition: Ablation rate (electrons) along the pellet path
sources.parent_definition: 1-D profiles of plasma and pellet along the pellet path

NAMES.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_injection
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous rate of electron-equivalent particles supplied by active
injection, obtained by nuclear-charge weighting each injected atomic
species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection
systems, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis when multiple injected
species are combined. It represents the electron inventory that the supplied
material can contribute after ionization.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=\sum_s Z_s\dot{N}_s(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $\dot{N}_s$ are source rates, $s$ indexes
the injected atomic species, and $Z_s$ is the dimensionless nuclear charge
number. For molecular feeds, each constituent atom is included with its
nuclear-charge weighting. This is the charge-weighted instance of the
[source rate due to injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection); for
unit-charge deuterium, it equals the [deuterium source rate due to
injection](name:deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection).

This is an injected inventory rate, not a local volumetric particle source
or a net plasma production-minus-loss rate such as the [total electron
source rate](name:total_electron_source_rate).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when active injection increases the supplied
equivalent-electron inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Number of electrons injected per second
sources.parent_definition: Set of valves connecting a gas bottle to pipes

NAMES.name: ethane_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short:
Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18
equivalent electrons per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced
during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethane molecule contributes 18
equivalent electrons: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six
hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = 18N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}18\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ and
$N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ are pure counts, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$
is the neutral-ethane introduction rate in molecules s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$, and $t$ are the prefill start, plasma-breakdown, and time
variables in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral ethane introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethane component of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count);
[accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) represents
distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while
[ethylene_prefill_count](name:ethylene_prefill_count) applies the same
convention to a different hydrocarbon.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ethane (C2H6)

NAMES.name: ethane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous ethane-gas injection rate into the plasma vessel, expressed as
equivalent electrons per second, with 18 equivalent electrons assigned to
each neutral C2H6 molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which neutral ethane molecules
are delivered to the plasma vessel, converted to an equivalent-electron
rate. It counts the electrons associated with neutral molecular composition,
not free electrons produced by ionization.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron injection rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the neutral ethane molecular injection rate
in molecules per second, and $t$ is time in seconds. The factor
$18=2\times6+6\times1$ is the total atomic-number electron count of one C2H6
molecule.

This is an instantaneous rate rather than a cumulative inventory; its time
integral gives the accumulated equivalent-electron count represented by
[accumulated ethane count](name:accumulated_ethane_count). It excludes other
molecular species, including the distinct [ethylene source
rate](name:ethylene_source_rate).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ethane (C2H6)

NAMES.name: ethylene_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ethylene
NAMES.short:
Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4)
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count with 16 equivalent electrons per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethylene molecule contributes
sixteen equivalent electrons: twelve from two carbon atoms and four from
four hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = (2Z_{\mathrm{C}}+4Z_{\mathrm{H}})N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = 16N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}16\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of
carbon and hydrogen, $N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}}$ is the accumulated
ethylene-molecule count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}$ is the ethylene
introduction rate, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and
plasma-breakdown times.

This quantity includes only neutral ethylene introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethylene component
of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count);
[accumulated_ethylene_count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count) represents the
distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while
[ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) applies the same
convention to a different molecule.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ethylene (C2H4)

NAMES.name: ethylene_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ethylene
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous injection rate of ethylene (C2H4) gas into the plasma vessel,
expressed as equivalent electrons per second with each molecule counted as
16 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
Ethylene (C2H4) is a two-carbon, four-hydrogen molecule used as a gaseous
source of both carbon and hydrogen in plasma fueling and wall-conditioning
experiments. The source rate is the instantaneous equivalent-electron
delivery rate to the plasma vessel, where each molecule is assigned 16
equivalent electrons based on the total atomic electron inventory of the
molecular formula.

The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq}$ relates to the molecular
injection rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ by

$$
\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq} = 16\,\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}
$$

where the factor $16 = 2Z_\mathrm{C} + 4Z_\mathrm{H}$, with $Z_\mathrm{C} =
6$ the carbon atomic number and $Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$ the hydrogen atomic
number.

The injection rate is inferred from valve conductance calibrations and
upstream pressure measurements. Its time-integral gives the [accumulated
ethylene count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count), which tracks the total
equivalent-electron inventory delivered since plasma breakdown. Related
molecular and atomic injection rates include
[silane_source_rate](name:silane_source_rate) for SiH4 and
[hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection)
for atomic hydrogen delivery.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when ethylene gas flows from the injection system
into the plasma vessel.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ethylene (C2H4)

NAMES.name: first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Unit direction vector defining the first measurement direction associated
with an elliptic shatter cone in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the unit direction vector assigned to the first measurement
direction of an elliptic shatter cone. It describes orientation, not
position, length, or cone-axis magnitude. Its components are resolved in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ representing the vertical direction.

$$
\hat{\mathbf{d}}_1 = d_{1x}\hat{x} + d_{1y}\hat{y} + d_{1z}\hat{z}, \qquad d_{1x}^2+d_{1y}^2+d_{1z}^2=1
$$

Here, $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_1$ is the first measurement-direction unit vector,
$d_{1x}$, $d_{1y}$, and $d_{1z}$ are its Cartesian projections, and
$\hat{x}$, $\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$ are the Cartesian basis vectors. The
designation “first” follows the shatter-cone measurement-direction
convention and does not imply alignment with the Cartesian $x$ axis. It is
distinct from the [X component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit
vector](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes cone
geometry rather than measurement-direction ordering.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along X axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector of the cone direction

NAMES.name: incident_thermal_power_at_wall
NAMES.short:
Thermal power carried from the plasma and incident on the first wall,
defining the wall-directed heat load before downstream coolant extraction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the thermal power transported from the plasma toward and
incident on the first wall. It represents an integrated wall load rather
than a local heat-flux density.

The incident thermal power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{wall}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{th,inc}}}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the thermal power incident on the first wall
and $E_{\mathrm{th,inc}}$ is the thermal energy delivered from the plasma to
the wall.

The quantity applies to the thermal plasma contribution and aggregates the
incident power over the first-wall surface. It excludes power extracted by
coolant after deposition and is distinct from [total thermal
coolant-absorbed power at the
wall](name:total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall), which describes
the downstream removal of deposited energy. It is also not limited to the
radiative component represented by [absorbed radiated power at the
wall](name:absorbed_radiated_power_at_wall).

The total incident load can contain conductive and convective contributions,
represented by [power due to conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction) and
[power due to convection](name:power_due_to_convection) when those
components are resolved.

sources.leaf_definition: Heat flow towards the wall
sources.parent_definition: Energy conversion

NAMES.name: krypton_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 36
count units per atom.
NAMES.long:
Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton (Kr) introduced
during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral krypton atom contributes 36
equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected
krypton atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the krypton
atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt = 36 \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless
equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless
accumulated neutral-krypton atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the
dimensionless atomic number of krypton, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the
neutral-krypton atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and
$t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only krypton introduced before breakdown and excludes
later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It
uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with xenon_prefill_count providing the
analogous noble-gas convention for xenon.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton

NAMES.name: length_of_pellet
NAMES.short:
End-to-end extent of an intact cylindrical pellet measured along its
symmetry axis before injection or shattering.
NAMES.long:
The pellet axial length is the distance between the two end faces measured
parallel to the symmetry axis of the intact cylindrical pellet.

$$
L_p = z_2 - z_1
$$

where $L_p$ is the axial length and $z_1$ and $z_2$ are the axial
coordinates of the two end faces, ordered so that $z_2 > z_1$ along the
chosen axial direction.

This quantity describes the unshattered pellet before injection or
fragmentation and excludes its transverse size, which is described by the
[diameter of the pellet](name:diameter_of_pellet).

sources.leaf_definition: Pellet length (cylindrical pellet)
sources.parent_definition: Information related to the pellet

NAMES.name: maximum_gas_flow
NAMES.short:
Maximum gas flow is the largest pressure-volume throughput that a gas
injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the upper bound of its
controllable range.
NAMES.long:
Maximum gas flow is the upper reliable operating limit of the
pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It represents
the aggregate gas stream rather than a particular molecular species, charge
state, mass flow, or particle-number rate.

The defining pressure-volume throughput at the upper delivery limit is

$$
Q_g^{\max} = p_g \frac{dV_g}{dt}
$$

where $Q_g^{\max}$ is the maximum gas pressure-volume throughput, $p_g$ is
the gas pressure at the flow boundary, $V_g$ is the volume of gas crossing
that boundary, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to gas delivered through a gas injection valve for
fueling, impurity seeding, or disruption mitigation. The maximum qualifier
denotes a reliable upper delivery limit for the aggregate gas stream, not a
species-resolved flow, mass-flow rate, or particle-number rate.

The quantity is the upper-bound member of the gas flow family: gas flow
denotes the same pressure-volume throughput without an upper-limit
restriction, while [minimum gas flow](name:minimum_gas_flow) denotes its
lower reliable operating limit.

sources.leaf_definition: Maximum flow rate of the valve
sources.parent_definition: Set of valves connecting a gas bottle to pipes

NAMES.name: methane_carbon_13_source_rate
NAMES.subject: methane_carbon_13
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous injection rate of carbon-13-labeled methane into the plasma
vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate with 10 equivalent
electrons assigned to each neutral molecule.
NAMES.long:
Instantaneous injection rate of carbon-13-labeled methane into the plasma
vessel is the rate at which neutral $^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ enters the plasma
vessel, counted using the equivalent-electron convention. Each neutral
carbon-13-labeled methane molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons.

The constitutive relation between the equivalent-electron source rate and
the molecular injection rate is:

$$
\dot{S}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4} = 10\,\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the carbon-13-labeled methane source
rate, $\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the molecule-counted injection rate
of neutral carbon-13-labeled methane, and $^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ denotes
methane with carbon-13 as the carbon isotope.

This quantity applies only to neutral carbon-13-labeled methane crossing
into the plasma vessel by gas injection, aggregated over the relevant
injection locations as an instantaneous total. It excludes unlabeled
methane, other hydrocarbons, gas remaining upstream of the vessel, and
accumulated injected amount.

It is distinguished from a molecule-counted [methane source
rate](name:methane_source_rate) by the equivalent-electron counting
convention: the present quantity is 10 times the corresponding
molecule-counted rate for the same carbon-13-labeled methane population.
When the corresponding accumulated count is used, this source rate is the
time derivative of the [accumulated methane carbon-13 count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection)
under the same equivalent-electron convention.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when carbon-13-labeled methane enters the plasma
vessel.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Methane (CH4 with carbon 13)

NAMES.name: methane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: methane
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous rate of neutral methane-molecule delivery into the plasma
vessel by gas injection, counted per molecule rather than as an
equivalent-electron or elemental source.
NAMES.long:
Methane source rate is the instantaneous rate at which neutral methane
molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection. It counts
methane molecules directly, rather than converting them to equivalent
electrons or to elemental carbon or hydrogen.

The source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t) = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of methane molecules
delivered by gas injection and $t$ is time. The quantity is distinct from
the [methane carbon-13 source rate](name:methane_carbon_13_source_rate),
which applies specifically to carbon-13-labeled methane.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Methane (CH4)

NAMES.name: minimum_gas_flow
NAMES.short:
Minimum gas flow is the smallest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas
injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the lower bound of its
controllable range.
NAMES.long:
Minimum gas flow is the lower reliable operating limit of the
pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It identifies
the smallest controllable value of the aggregate gas stream throughput,
rather than a molecular-species flow or particle-number rate.

The pressure-volume throughput represented by this quantity is defined as

$$
Q_g = p_g \frac{dV_g}{dt}
$$

where $Q_g$ is gas pressure-volume throughput, $p_g$ is gas pressure at the
flow boundary, $V_g$ is the volume of gas crossing that boundary, and $t$ is
time.

This quantity applies to the aggregate gas stream delivered through an
injection system across a defined flow boundary. The stream is not
restricted to a particular molecular species or charge state, and this
quantity is distinct from mass flow and particle-number rate. Its defining
distinction is the lower reliable operating bound, rather than an
unrestricted instantaneous throughput.

The gas flow quantity defines the same pressure-volume throughput without
imposing a lower-limit condition; minimum gas flow is its lower reliable
operating bound. Conversely, [maximum gas flow](name:maximum_gas_flow) is
the upper reliable operating bound, so the two quantities delimit the
controllable range rather than represent different throughput definitions.

sources.leaf_definition: Minimum flow rate of the valve
sources.parent_definition: Set of valves connecting a gas bottle to pipes

NAMES.name: minor_angle_of_pellet_injector
NAMES.short:
Minor directional half-opening angle of the elliptic fragment-dispersion
cone formed by a shattered pellet injector.
NAMES.long:
Minor half-opening angle of the elliptic shatter cone formed by a shattered
pellet injector is the angular separation between the cone axis and its
boundary along the minor transverse semi-axis. It is the minor directional
component of the angle of the pellet injector.

$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{minor}} = \arccos\left(\hat{u}_{\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}\right)
$$

where $\alpha_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the minor half-opening angle,
$\hat{u}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the shatter-cone axis unit vector, and
$\hat{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the unit vector along the cone's minor
semi-axis. The quantity describes a half-angle, not the full angular
opening; the corresponding major-direction value is the major angle of the
pellet injector.

sources.leaf_definition: Angle between the cone direction and unit_vector_minor
sources.parent_definition: Description of the elliptic shatter cone

NAMES.name: molecular_neutral_species_flow_at_outlet
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume
throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet.
It is defined by the outlet partial pressure of that species and the
corresponding effective pumping speed, not by total neutral pressure.
NAMES.long:
Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume
throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet.
It is species-specific and uses the outlet partial pressure of that
molecular neutral species rather than the [total neutral
pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure).

The outlet throughput is defined by the product of the outlet species
partial pressure and the effective pumping speed for that species:

$$
Q_{s,\mathrm{out}} = p_{s,\mathrm{out}} S_{s,\mathrm{out}}
$$

where $Q_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is this molecular neutral species flow at the
outlet, $p_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the outlet partial pressure of molecular
neutral species $s$, and $S_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the effective pumping speed
for species $s$ at the outlet.

This quantity is an outlet removal throughput, distinct from a gas source
into the vessel such as [gas
injection](name:total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection).
It is the molecular, species-resolved outlet form of neutral species flow
and a species-specific specialization of gas flow.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the molecular neutral species is removed
through the outlet in the pumping direction away from the vessel.

sources.leaf_definition: Pumping flow rate of that species
sources.parent_definition: Molecular species pumped via this duct

NAMES.name: neon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 10
equivalent electrons per atom.
NAMES.long:
Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced
during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral neon atom contributes 10 equivalent
electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the neon
equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the accumulated
neutral-neon atom count, both pure counts; $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the
atomic number of neon; $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neutral-neon atom
introduction rate in atoms s$^{-1}$; and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the
prefill start and plasma-breakdown times, with $t$ in s.

This quantity includes only neutral neon introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. The equivalent-electron
convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic
composition, not a statement that the gas is fully ionized during prefill.
It is the neon component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count);
[accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) represents distinct
post-breakdown accumulation, while
[argon_prefill_count](name:argon_prefill_count) applies the same convention
to a different noble gas.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon

NAMES.name: neon_source_rate
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel, expressed
as an equivalent-electron count rate with ten counts assigned to each
injected neon atom.
NAMES.long:
Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel is the time
rate of increase of the equivalent-electron count associated with injected
neon. The equivalent-electron convention assigns ten counts to each injected
neon atom, reflecting neon's atomic number.

The defining relation to injected atom count is:

$$
S_\mathrm{Ne} = \frac{dN_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^\mathrm{Ne}}{dt} = 10\,\frac{dN_\mathrm{Ne}}{dt}
$$

where $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the neon source rate,
$N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^\mathrm{Ne}$ is the equivalent-electron count assigned to
injected neon, $N_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the count of injected neon atoms, $t$ is
time, and the label $\mathrm{Ne}$ denotes neon.

This quantity is species-specific to neon gas entering the plasma vessel and
is aggregated over the injected neon population by summing the
equivalent-electron contributions from all injected neon atoms. It excludes
injection of other gasses, total gas throughput, pumping or exhaust flow,
retained neutral inventory, and source terms from wall recycling,
sputtering, or ionization inside the plasma.

The corresponding [accumulated neon count](name:accumulated_neon_count) is
the time integral of $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ over the accumulation interval using
the same factor of ten. Conversely, where differentiable, $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ is
the time derivative of that accumulated count.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neon is added to the plasma vessel.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon

NAMES.name: net_efficiency_of_plant_system
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system delivers
signed net electrical power to an external load relative to the total
internal electrical consumption needed to operate it.
NAMES.long:
The net efficiency of a plant system is the dimensionless ratio of signed
net electrical power exported outside the plant boundary to total internal
electrical power consumed by plant systems over the same accounting
interval. It is the net-electrical-gain specialization of [efficiency of a
plant system](name:efficiency_of_plant_system), with recirculating
electrical loads included in the net exported power balance.

The defining relation, including the corresponding net-power balance, is:

$$
\eta_{\mathrm{net,plant}} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{net}}}{P_{\mathrm{cons}}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{net}} = P_{\mathrm{gen}} - P_{\mathrm{int}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{cons}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}} P_{\mathrm{load},i}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net electrical power of the plant system in
W, $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is the positive total electrical consumption
represented by [power of the plant system](name:power_of_plant_system) in W,
$P_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is gross generated electrical power in W,
$P_{\mathrm{int}}$ is the internal operational electrical consumption
subtracted in the net-power balance in W, $P_{\mathrm{load},i}$ is the
electrical consumption of included load $i$ in W, and
$\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}$ is the set of electrically powered plant
loads included in the accounting boundary.

The denominator $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is a gross positive consumption
quantity, not the signed net exchange $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ and not the gross
generated power $P_{\mathrm{gen}}$. It equals the internal-consumption term
$P_{\mathrm{int}}$ only when the same loads, plant boundary, and interval
define both the net-power balance and the denominator. Unlike [thermal
efficiency of the plant system](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system),
this quantity relates net electrical export to internal electrical
consumption rather than gross electrical output to thermal input.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when signed net electrical power is exported from
the plant system to an external electrical network or load.

sources.leaf_definition: Electricity gain of the plant (ratio of net electric / plant electricity during operation)
sources.parent_definition: Electrical and thermal power balance of the plant

NAMES.name: nitrogen_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂)
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count with 7 per atom or 14 per N₂ molecule.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral nitrogen atom contributes 7
equivalent electrons, so each N₂ molecule contributes 14.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}} = 7N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}} + 14N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \left[7\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}(t) + 14\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}(t)\right]dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}}$ are
accumulated neutral atom and molecule counts, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}$ and
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ are their introduction rates. The counts are pure
counts, the rates are in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the
prefill start and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral nitrogen introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the nitrogen component
of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), whereas accumulated_nitrogen_count
represents post-breakdown nitrogen accumulation.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen

NAMES.name: nitrogen_source_rate
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous rate of neutral molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma
vessel, expressed as equivalent-electron particles with fourteen counts
assigned to each molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron source rate carried by neutral
molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma vessel. It represents delivered
molecular inventory, not free-electron production, ionization rate, or
nitrogen ions retained in the plasma.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = 14\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ is the injection rate of nitrogen molecules. The
factor 14 assigns seven equivalent-electron counts to each of the two
nitrogen atoms in a molecule.

This species-resolved rate is consistent with the aggregate [source rate due
to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Integrating it
over a time interval gives the corresponding accumulated nitrogen inventory
represented by accumulated nitrogen count.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pellet_path
NAMES.short:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a pellet-path point is the value of the
equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function evaluated at the position of a
pellet along its injection trajectory. For an axisymmetric equilibrium it
depends only on the major-radius and vertical coordinates of that trajectory
point.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a pellet-path point is the value of the
equilibrium [poloidal_magnetic_flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function
sampled at the location of a pellet along its injection trajectory. It
labels the magnetic flux surface threading that trajectory point and shares
the sign and normalization of the underlying equilibrium flux function.

The quantity is the equilibrium poloidal flux function evaluated at the
pellet position:

$$
\psi_p = \psi\!\left(R_p, Z_p\right)
$$

where $\psi(R, Z)$ is the axisymmetric equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux
function in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the
major radius and $Z$ the vertical height, and $(R_p, Z_p)$ are the
major-radius and vertical coordinates of the pellet-path point. Because the
equilibrium is axisymmetric, $\psi$ is independent of the toroidal angle
$\phi$, so the toroidal location of the trajectory point does not enter this
value.

This is one scalar flux value associated with a single point on the pellet
trajectory; sampled at successive points or instants along the path it
traces the sequence of flux-surface labels crossed by the pellet. It differs
from
[poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface),
which is the flux value attached to a specified magnetic flux surface
independent of any trajectory. It is not the toroidal magnetic flux, the
pellet trajectory geometry, or a derivative of the flux label with respect
to a flux coordinate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the vertical magnetic field on the horizontal
disk that defines the equilibrium poloidal flux points in the $+Z$ direction
of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal flux along the pellet path
sources.parent_definition: 1-D profiles of plasma and pellet along the pellet path

NAMES.name: power_of_plant_subsystem
NAMES.short:
Real electrical power consumed by an individual plant subsystem at its
electrical boundary, contributing to auxiliary-load accounting without
including plant-wide aggregation.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the real electrical power consumed by one plant subsystem
at its electrical boundary. It represents the subsystem's contribution to
auxiliary electrical load, distinct from plant-wide aggregation and net
electrical balance quantities.

$$
P_{\rm sub} = \left\langle v(t)i(t) \right\rangle_t
$$

where $P_{\rm sub}$ is the boundary real power, $v(t)$ is the instantaneous
terminal voltage, $i(t)$ is the instantaneous current directed into the
subsystem, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes averaging over the relevant
operating interval. For multiple terminals, the boundary power is the
algebraic sum of the terminal power contributions. Positive power denotes
consumption by the subsystem; exported or generated power is not included as
consumed load. The quantity is distinct from absorbed power of a plant
system, total power of a plant system, and net power of a plant system.

sources.leaf_definition: Electrical power used to operate the subsystem
sources.parent_definition: Set of subsystems

NAMES.name: power_of_plant_system
NAMES.short:
Real electrical power assigned at a plant-system boundary, representing
absorbed load, net generation balance, or an aggregate of included system
loads.
NAMES.long:
Real electrical power is the rate of electrical-energy transfer or
accounting associated with a plant system at its electrical boundary. It
excludes reactive power and other non-electrical energy flows.

The instantaneous power is defined by

$$
P = \frac{\mathrm{d}E}{\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $E$ is the electrical energy associated with the accounting boundary
and $t$ is time.

The accounting convention is fixed by the specialized quantity. Absorbed
power of a plant system represents one-way incoming electrical load, net
power of a plant system represents generation minus internal consumption and
is positive for net export, and total power of a plant system is the sum of
the loads of all included systems. These forms are distinct applications of
the same plant-boundary electrical-power concept.

sources.leaf_definition: Electrical power used to operate the system
sources.parent_definition: Set of systems involved in the electric plant operation

NAMES.name: prefill_gas_pressure
NAMES.short:
Pressure of the neutral gas introduced before plasma breakdown, governing
the pressure-dependent ionization conditions for early electron-avalanche
breakdown.
NAMES.long:
Prefill gas pressure is the thermodynamic pressure of the neutral gas
present before plasma breakdown. It establishes the gas conditions used in
the Townsend electron-avalanche criterion during plasma initiation.

For an ideal neutral gas, pressure is related to particle density and
temperature by:

$$
p_g = n_g k_B T_g
$$

where $p_g$ is the prefill gas pressure, $n_g$ is the neutral particle
number density, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, and $T_g$ is the neutral-gas
temperature. This ideal-gas relation applies when the ideal-gas
approximation is valid.

This quantity describes the prebreakdown gas state; it is not the
accumulated injected inventory represented by
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count) or the pressure of the plasma formed
after breakdown.

sources.leaf_definition: Prefill gas pressure used in Townsend E field calculation
sources.parent_definition: Magnetic field line tracing results, given at various time slices

NAMES.name: propane_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short:
Propane prefill count is the total amount of C3H8 introduced before plasma
breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 26 count units per
neutral propane molecule.
NAMES.long:
Propane prefill count is the total amount of neutral propane (C3H8)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each propane molecule contributes 26 equivalent
electrons: 18 from three carbon atoms and 8 from eight hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected
propane molecules over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = (3Z_C + 8Z_H)N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = 26N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the
equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the accumulated
propane molecule count, $Z_C=6$ and $Z_H=1$ are the atomic numbers of carbon
and hydrogen, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}$ is the propane molecule injection
rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only propane introduced before breakdown and excludes
later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It
uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with
[ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) providing the analogous
molecular-species convention.

sources.parent_definition: Propane (C3H8)

NAMES.name: propane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous propane (C3H8) injection rate into the plasma vessel,
converted from molecules to equivalent electrons using 26 electrons per
neutral molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous source rate of propane gas entering the
plasma vessel, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention. Each
neutral C3H8 molecule contributes the total electron count of its
constituent atoms.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)=26\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the propane molecular injection rate in
molecules per second, $t$ is time, and 26 is the dimensionless electron
count per neutral molecule: three carbon atoms contribute 18 electrons and
eight hydrogen atoms contribute 8 electrons. This is an instantaneous rate,
distinct from the accumulated propane count, which is the time-integrated
equivalent-electron inventory.

NAMES.name: radial_velocity_of_pellet
NAMES.short:
Signed major-radius component of the pellet center-of-mass velocity,
describing motion toward or away from the toroidal symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed major-radius component of the translational
velocity of the pellet center of mass. It resolves motion in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The radial velocity is defined by:

$$
v_R = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}} \cdot \hat{R} = \frac{dR_{\mathrm{cm}}}{dt}
$$

where $v_R$ is the radial velocity component, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is
the center-of-mass translational velocity vector, $\hat{R}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing major radius, $R_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the
center-of-mass major-radius coordinate, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to the pellet center of mass. For fragment-resolved
motion, it applies to the individual fragment center of mass; for collective
fragment-cloud motion, it applies to the cloud center of mass at the shatter
cone origin. The cloud center of mass is mass-weighted, rather than an
equal-weight average of fragment positions, and its motion is distinct from
the spread of individual fragment velocities.

This component is not the total speed, a flux-surface-normal velocity, or
rotational motion about the represented center of mass. Together with the
[toroidal velocity](name:toroidal_velocity_of_pellet) and [vertical
velocity](name:vertical_velocity_of_pellet), it specifies the translational
velocity vector when all components refer to the same entity and instant.
For the pellet at vacuum-chamber entry, it is the radial component of the
[initial velocity](name:initial_velocity_of_pellet); the radial quantity
itself is not restricted to that instant.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the represented center of mass moves toward
increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: shattered_pellet_species_number_density_of_pellet_fragment
NAMES.subject: shattered_pellet_species
NAMES.short:
Number density of a specified atomic species within the solid material of an
individual shattered-pellet fragment.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local volumetric abundance of one selected atomic
species in the material composing an individual shattered-pellet fragment.

It is defined by

$$
n_s = \frac{N_s}{V_f}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of the selected atomic species, $N_s$ is
its number of constituent atoms in the fragment, and $V_f$ is the physical
volume occupied by the fragment.

The scope is restricted to one fragment and one specified atomic species in
the fragment material. The quantity is species-selective rather than summed
over different species, and it describes pellet composition rather than the
number density of particles in the surrounding plasma. No plasma
ionization-state aggregation or charge-state resolution is implied.

Multiplying this density by the fragment volume gives the corresponding
constituent-atom count. It therefore provides a fragment-local density
counterpart to the whole-pellet inventory represented by atomic count of
pellet, while [fast neutral internal state number
density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density) describes a
plasma-particle population distinguished by internal state.

NAMES.name: silane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: silane
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous injection rate of silane (SiH4) gas into the plasma vessel,
expressed as an electron-equivalent particle rate with 18 equivalent
electrons for each SiH4 molecule.
NAMES.long:
Instantaneous injection rate of silane ($\mathrm{SiH}_4$) gas into the
plasma vessel is the silane gas source rate expressed on an
electron-equivalent particle-counting basis. Each $\mathrm{SiH}_4$ molecule
contributes 18 equivalent electrons, equal to the total electron count of a
neutral molecule.

The conversion from a molecular silane injection rate to this
electron-equivalent source rate is

$$
S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ is the silane source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ is the molecular injection rate of neutral silane
into the plasma vessel, and 18 is the electron-equivalent count of one
neutral $\mathrm{SiH}_4$ molecule.

This quantity applies only to silane gas introduced into the plasma vessel
and is aggregated over all silane introduced into that vessel on the same
electron-equivalent basis. It excludes source rates for other gasses, total
gas-source rates, silicon-only or hydrogen-only atomic source rates, mass
flow, neutral-gas inventory, and pressure.

The silane source count is the time integral of $S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ using
the same factor of 18 between molecular count and electron-equivalent count.
This quantity is the silane analog of the [ethylene source
rate](name:ethylene_source_rate) and [ethane source
rate](name:ethane_source_rate); the molecular identity fixes the conversion
factor in each case.
NAMES.sign: Positive when silane is added to the plasma vessel.

sources.parent_definition: Silane (SiH4)

NAMES.name: source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate delivered to the plasma vessel
by gas injection systems, where each injected atom contributes Z equivalent
electrons per second according to its atomic number.
NAMES.long:
The source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at
which neutral gas is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection
hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Every injected
atom of atomic number $Z$ contributes $Z$ equivalent electrons per second to
the total inventory rate, providing a unified accounting framework across
species of differing nuclear charge.

The defining relation for a single injected species is:

$$
\dot{S} = Z \cdot \dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}$ is the raw atomic delivery rate in atoms
per second and $Z$ is the atomic number of the injected species. For
simultaneous multi-species injection, contributions are summed over all
active species.

This rate is inferred from calibrated mass-flow controllers or upstream
pressure-rise measurements on the gas supply plumbing. It is the
instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated
equivalent-electron inventories, such as
[accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count) or
accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection. The nearest-peer quantity
gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection provides the
vessel-integrated analog expressed in raw gas-phase particles rather than
equivalent electrons.

NAMES.name: argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron argon source rate delivered to the plasma
vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected argon atom with Z = 18
contributes 18 equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The argon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral argon with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count rate. The equivalent-electron convention counts
each injected neutral argon atom as 18 equivalent electrons because neutral
argon has 18 electrons; this is an inventory-accounting convention, not a
statement about subsequent ionization or confinement.

The defining relation for injected argon is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the raw argon-atom delivery rate in atoms per
second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is the dimensionless atomic number of
argon.

This quantity is the argon-species member of
[source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
It is the instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated
equivalent-electron inventory
[accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count), and differs from
raw gas-particle source rates by the factor $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when argon is delivered into the plasma vessel,
increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

NAMES.name: beryllium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of beryllium atoms introduced
by gas injection, with four equivalent electrons assigned to each atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate of beryllium supplied by gas
injection, represented using an equivalent-electron counting convention. It
describes injected beryllium input rather than the creation rate of free
plasma electrons or a time-integrated beryllium inventory.

The equivalent-electron rate is defined from the beryllium atom injection
rate by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,Be}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Be}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Be}}(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,Be}}$ is the equivalent-electron count assigned to
injected beryllium, $N_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the number of injected beryllium
atoms, $Z_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the atomic number of beryllium, $t$ is time, and
the dot denotes differentiation with respect to time. For beryllium,
$Z_{\mathrm{Be}}=4$.

The scope is beryllium delivered by gas injection alone, aggregated over all
injected beryllium atoms. It excludes source contributions from other
species and other injection mechanisms, and it is not a
charge-state-resolved plasma source; the equivalent-electron convention
assigns four counts per injected beryllium atom.

This is the beryllium-specific member of the gas-injection source-rate
family, using the same equivalent-electron basis as the [hydrogen
gas-injection source rate](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection),
[helium-4 gas-injection source
rate](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), and [lithium
gas-injection source rate](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
Unlike the broader [electron source rate due to
injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection), it isolates the
nuclear-charge-weighted beryllium contribution. Integrating this
instantaneous rate over a time interval gives the corresponding accumulated
equivalent-electron inventory.
