sources.parent_definition: Beryllium

NAMES.name: carbon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron carbon source rate delivered to the plasma
vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected carbon atom contributing
six equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The carbon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral carbon with atomic number six is admitted to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. It is the carbon-specific component of [source rate due to gas
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

For carbon injection, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}} = 6\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the raw carbon-atom delivery rate; both rates have
units of inverse seconds.

This quantity counts injected carbon atoms, not electrons currently present
in the plasma, carbon ionization states, or the net carbon balance after
transport and removal. Its time integral gives [accumulated carbon count due
to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
same equivalent-electron convention applies to [tritium source rate due to
gas injection](name:tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), with a
different atomic-number factor.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when carbon gas is delivered into the vessel,
increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon

NAMES.name: helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron helium-3 source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected helium-3 atom
contributes two equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The helium-3 source rate due to gas injection characterizes the
instantaneous rate at which neutral helium-3 is admitted to the plasma
vessel by gas-injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. Each helium-3 atom contributes two equivalent-electron counts because
helium has atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{He}} = 2$.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}} = Z_{\mathrm{He}}\,\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}} = 2\,\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}$ is the helium-3
equivalent-electron source rate due to gas injection,
$\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}$ is the raw neutral helium-3 atomic
delivery rate due to gas injection, and $Z_{\mathrm{He}}$ is the atomic
number of helium.

This quantity is isotope-specific: it applies only to neutral helium-3 gas
admitted through gas injection and is aggregated over all gas-injection
paths feeding the plasma vessel. It excludes helium-4 and other injected
species, particle sources not due to gas injection, and raw gas-particle
accounting represented by the gas particle source rate over vessel due to
gas injection.

It is the time derivative of the [accumulated helium-3 count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection) under the
same equivalent-electron weighting. Summing species-specific
equivalent-electron source rates over active injected species gives the
[source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
The [helium-4 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) uses the same
helium atomic-number weighting but applies to a different isotope, whereas
the [hydrogen source rate due to gas
injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) differs through
the hydrogen atomic number.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when helium-3 gas is delivered into the plasma
vessel, increasing the helium-3 equivalent-electron inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons

NAMES.name: helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of helium-4 delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, with each helium-4 atom contributing two
equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The helium-4 source rate due to gas injection characterizes the
instantaneous rate at which neutral helium-4 is admitted to the plasma
vessel by gas-injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. Each helium-4 atom contributes two counts because helium has atomic
number 2.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}} = Z_{\mathrm{He}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}} = 2\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 atom delivery rate in atoms per
second, and $Z_{\mathrm{He}}=2$ is helium's atomic number. This is the
helium-4 component of the [source rate due to gas
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection); integrating it over time
gives the [accumulated helium-4 count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
[helium-3 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) uses the same
atomic-number weighting but represents a separate isotope inventory.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when helium-4 gas is delivered into the vessel,
increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons

NAMES.name: hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron hydrogen source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems; each hydrogen atom contributes one
equivalent-electron count.
NAMES.long:
The hydrogen source rate due to gas injection characterizes the
instantaneous rate at which neutral hydrogen atoms are admitted to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. Because hydrogen has atomic number one, each atom contributes one
equivalent-electron count.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{H}} = 1
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the neutral hydrogen-atom delivery rate in atoms
per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen atomic number. This is the
hydrogen component of the total [source rate due to gas
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Its time integral gives
the accumulated hydrogen inventory [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when hydrogen gas is being delivered into the
vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen

NAMES.name: krypton_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron krypton source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected krypton atom
with Z = 36 contributes 36 equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The krypton source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral krypton with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count rate. Each neutral krypton atom contributes
$Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ equivalent electrons to the equivalent particle inventory;
this accounting uses nuclear charge and does not imply ionization at the
injection location.

The defining relation for krypton injection is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton equivalent-electron source rate
in equivalent-electron counts per second, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the
neutral krypton atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}
= 36$ is the atomic number of krypton.

This is the krypton-species contribution to
[source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection)
and is the instantaneous time derivative of
[accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) when the same
equivalent-electron accounting is used. It excludes krypton supplied by
mechanisms other than gas injection and differs from
gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection, which is counted
as raw gas-phase particles rather than equivalent electrons. It is directly
parallel to same-family species quantities such as
[argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection),
differing by the injected species and its atomic number.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton

NAMES.name: lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron lithium source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected lithium atom
contributing three equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The lithium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral lithium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count rate. It is the lithium-specific component of the
[source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection),
rather than the raw lithium-atom delivery rate.

For lithium, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium equivalent-electron source
rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the raw lithium atom delivery rate in atoms
per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is lithium's dimensionless atomic
number.

The equivalent-electron convention assigns three source counts to each
injected lithium atom and excludes other gas species. This rate is the time
derivative of the corresponding accumulated lithium count; its atomic-number
weighting distinguishes it from the [helium-3 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when lithium is delivered into the vessel,
increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium

NAMES.name: oxygen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous oxygen injection rate from gas fueling, expressed on an
equivalent-electron basis with eight equivalent electrons assigned to each
oxygen atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous source rate of oxygen atoms supplied by
gas injection, expressed using an equivalent-electron weighting. It
describes injected oxygen input, not the subsequent oxygen population or its
ionization state.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined from the oxygen-atom
injection rate by:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,O}}(t) = 8\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t)
$$

where $t$ is physical time, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,O}}(t)$ is the oxygen
source rate on the equivalent-electron basis, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t)$ is
the injected oxygen-atom rate, and the factor $8$ is the atomic number of
oxygen.

The scope is oxygen introduced by gas injection; contributions from other
species and from non-gas-injection sources are excluded. The rate is
instantaneous and aggregates the injected oxygen amount over the
gas-injection input, weighting each oxygen atom by eight equivalent
electrons. This bookkeeping weighting does not represent physical
free-electron production and does not resolve oxygen charge states.

Time integration of this rate over the post-breakdown interval gives the
corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventory represented by
[accumulated oxygen count due to gas
injection](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection); unlike that
quantity, this standard name denotes the instantaneous source rate.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen

NAMES.name: thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket
NAMES.short:
Thermal power of the breeder blanket is the integrated non-nuclear heat load
entering the blanket through its plasma-facing surface, excluding volumetric
neutron and photon heating. It is a blanket-level surface-deposition power,
distinct from module-level coolant heat removal.
NAMES.long:
Thermal power of the breeder blanket is the total rate at which non-nuclear
thermal energy enters the breeder blanket through its plasma-facing surface.
It represents an integrated surface heat load on the blanket, not a local
heat-flux density.

For a surface heat-load representation, the integrated power is defined by
the area integral of the local non-nuclear heat flux entering the blanket:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,bb}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf,bb}}} q_{\mathrm{th}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th,bb}}$ is the thermal power of the breeder blanket,
$A_{\mathrm{pf,bb}}$ is the plasma-facing surface area of the breeder
blanket included in the blanket-level total, $q_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local
non-nuclear heat-flux density directed into the blanket, and $dA$ is the
surface element.

This quantity excludes volumetric neutron and photon energy deposition in
blanket material, which is represented by
[nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket).
It also differs from thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module, which denotes
module-level thermal power associated with an individual breeder-blanket
module rather than the blanket-level plasma-facing surface load.

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_at_pellet_path_point
NAMES.short:
Azimuthal location of a sampled point along the pellet path in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame about the machine symmetry axis.
Phi increases counterclockwise when viewed from above +Z.
NAMES.long:
Azimuthal location of a sampled point along the pellet path is the toroidal
coordinate $\phi$ of that point about the machine symmetry axis. It is the
angular component of the point position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is the [toroidal angle](name:toroidal_angle), and $Z$
is vertical height.

For the same point projected onto the plane perpendicular to the symmetry
axis, using the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis
with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and $\hat{x}$ defining $\phi=0$, the coordinate is
defined by the oriented azimuth:

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y, x)
$$

where $x$ is the coordinate along $\hat{x}$, $y$ is the coordinate along
$\hat{y}$, and $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ is the quadrant-resolving azimuth
to the transverse projection of the pellet path point.

The scope is a single geometrical point on the pellet path; the quantity is
point-local and is not averaged or accumulated over any segment of the path.
It is an absolute coordinate, not a toroidal offset from another locus, and
it is not the radial coordinate $R$, the vertical coordinate $Z$, path
length, velocity, or injection direction.

This quantity is the pellet-path-point specialization of [toroidal
angle](name:toroidal_angle). Together with the corresponding $R$ and $Z$
coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it
identifies the point up to the angular periodicity of $\phi$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when rotation from the $\phi=0$ reference
direction toward the point projection is counterclockwise about the symmetry
axis when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: Position of the first point

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_at_shattering_position
NAMES.short:
Toroidal azimuthal coordinate of the point where the pellet center-of-mass
trajectory intersects the shattering element.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal coordinate of the shattering position is the azimuthal
coordinate of the intersection between the pellet center-of-mass trajectory
and the shattering element.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, its coordinate is
defined by

$$
\mathbf{r}_s = R_s(\cos\phi_s\,\hat{x} + \sin\phi_s\,\hat{y}) + Z_s\hat{z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_s$ is the shattering-position vector, $R_s$ is its
major-radius coordinate, $Z_s$ is its vertical coordinate, $\phi_s$ is this
toroidal coordinate, and $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ is the right-handed
Cartesian basis with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

This event-location coordinate is distinct from the [toroidal coordinate at
a pellet path point](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_pellet_path_point) and from
the [toroidal coordinate of a pellet
fragment](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment), which refer to
different physical locations.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the angular displacement from the $\phi=0$
reference is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: Position where the pellet is shattered. It is defined as the intersection of the trayectory of the pellet center of mass with the shattering element

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet
NAMES.short:
Toroidal azimuthal coordinate of a pellet’s center of mass, locating the
pellet around the machine symmetry axis in cylindrical geometry.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the azimuthal position of the pellet center of mass around
the toroidal symmetry axis, expressed as the angle coordinate in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The toroidal coordinate is defined from the horizontal Cartesian coordinates
of the pellet center of mass by

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y,x)
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. The coordinate is periodic over one complete toroidal
circuit and identifies the pellet’s azimuthal location, distinct from the
post-shattering [toroidal coordinate of a pellet
fragment](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment).

The angle uses the same geometric convention as the general [toroidal
angle](name:toroidal_angle), but is evaluated at the pellet center of mass.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when increasing $phi$ follows the direction of
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle
sources.parent_definition: Position of the centre of mass of the pellet

NAMES.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment
NAMES.short:
Azimuthal location of a shattered-pellet fragment’s center of mass around
the machine symmetry axis, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the toroidal angle $\phi_f$ of a shattered-pellet fragment’s
center of mass. It specifies that position around the machine symmetry axis
in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, whose
coordinate values are $(R,\phi,Z)$; $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical
height.

Using Cartesian coordinates $(x_f,y_f,z_f)$ of the same center of mass in
the right-handed $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, the toroidal angle is

$$
\phi_f = \operatorname{atan2}(y_f,x_f)
$$

where $\operatorname{atan2}$ gives the oriented azimuth relative to the
defined $\phi=0$ direction. The angle is periodic modulo $2\pi$ and is
distinct from the [toroidal coordinate at the shattering
position](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_shattering_position) and the [toroidal
coordinate of the intact pellet](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the fragment center of mass lies in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle
sources.parent_definition: Position of the centre of mass of the pellet

NAMES.name: total_gas_source_rate_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short:
Gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection is the non-negative total
unweighted rate at which neutral gas particles are injected by gas valves
assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane. It is not an electron-equivalent
or charge-weighted rate.
NAMES.long:
Gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection is the instantaneous total
unweighted source rate of neutral gas particles injected by gas-injection
valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane. It counts injected
neutral gas particles themselves, not electron-equivalent particles,
charge-weighted particles, or particles produced by later plasma or wall
interactions.

For the set of midplane injection valves, the total rate is the sum of the
individual unweighted valve particle throughputs:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}} \dot{N}_k
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}}$ is the gas source rate at
midplane due to gas injection, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is the set of
gas-injection valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane, and
$\dot{N}_k$ is the unweighted neutral-particle throughput of valve $k$.

The total includes all gas-injection valves in the midplane group and
excludes upper, lower, wall, recycling, pumping, ionization, and transport
contributions. It is not additive with regional gas-source quantities that
use an electron-equivalent or charge-weighted convention. Its time integral
is the corresponding [accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_total_gas_count_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Gas injection rate from all valves located near the equatorial midplane

NAMES.name: total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower
vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves, summed over lower-region
valves and expressed using the equivalent-electron convention across
injected species.
NAMES.long:
Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower
vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves is the lower-region aggregate
equivalent-electron source rate due to gas injection. It counts each
injected neutral atom or molecule by the number of electrons associated with
its neutral composition and sums over all injected species and all
lower-region gas-injection valves.

The multi-species aggregate is defined by:

$$
\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}} = \sum_{v \in \mathrm{lower}} \sum_m E_m\,\dot{N}_{v,m}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}}$ is this total lower gas
source rate, $\dot{N}_{v,m}$ is the neutral gas injection rate of atomic or
molecular species $m$ from lower-region valve $v$, and $E_m = \sum_a
\nu_{a,m} Z_a$ is the equivalent-electron count for one neutral injected
particle of species $m$, with $\nu_{a,m}$ the stoichiometric count of atom
$a$ in species $m$ and $Z_a$ its atomic number.

This quantity is an injected source into the vacuum vessel and excludes
pumping, wall recycling, ionization losses after entry, and gas introduced
outside the lower region. Species-level quantities such as [neon source
rate](name:neon_source_rate) and [propane source
rate](name:propane_source_rate) are individual species contributions under
the same equivalent-electron convention; gas source rate of the vacuum
vessel due to gas injection is the vessel-level source quantity without the
lower-region restriction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral gas is introduced into the vacuum
vessel through lower-region injection valves.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Gas injection rate from all valves located near near the bottom of the vaccuum chamber

NAMES.name: total_neutral_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of neutral gas introduced into
the vessel by gas injection, summed over all injected species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous neutral-gas throughput supplied to the
vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate. It
combines all injected neutral species rather than representing one gas
species.

For the set of injected species, the equivalent-electron rate is defined by:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} Z_s\,\dot{N}_s
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the total equivalent-electron source rate,
$\mathcal{S}$ is the set of injected neutral gas species, $\dot{N}_s$ is the
particle injection rate of species $s$, and $Z_s$ is the equivalent-electron
weighting per injected particle. For an atomic species, $Z_s$ is its atomic
number; for a molecule, it is the sum of the atomic numbers of its
constituent atoms.

The quantity applies to the vessel-level gas input and is aggregated by
summing over all injected neutral species. It is an instantaneous rate, not
a time-integrated inventory, and excludes ionization and subsequent plasma
particle sources. Species-resolved rates such as the [hydrogen source rate
due to gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection)
provide individual contributions to this total. Unlike the [total lower gas
source rate of the vacuum vessel due to gas
injection](name:total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection),
it is not restricted to the lower vessel region.

The corresponding accumulated quantity, such as the [accumulated hydrogen
count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), is
obtained by time integration and represents delivered inventory rather than
instantaneous throughput.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total gas injection rate (sum over species)

NAMES.name: total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall
NAMES.short:
Thermal power extracted by active coolant circuits from cooled plasma-facing
wall surfaces, representing energy removal from the wall rather than
incident plasma power.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total heat-transfer rate from cooled plasma-facing wall
structures into their active coolant circuits. It represents energy removed
from the wall and is distinct from [total incident power at the
wall](name:total_incident_power_at_wall), which measures plasma power
arriving at wall surfaces.

$$
P_{\mathrm{cool}} = \sum_i \dot{Q}_{i}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cool}}$ is the total coolant-absorbed thermal power and
$\dot{Q}_{i}$ is the heat-transfer rate from the wall into coolant circuit
$i$. The sum includes all active cooling circuits serving the cooled
plasma-facing surfaces and excludes heat deposited on uncooled structures or
power merely incident on the wall.

sources.leaf_definition: Power to cooling systems
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: total_thermal_power_at_outlet
NAMES.short:
Total thermal power at the outlet is the aggregate rate at which thermal
energy leaves a power-conversion cycle through all heat-rejection outlet
streams. It includes all rejected heat contributions and excludes useful
electrical output.
NAMES.long:
Total thermal power at the outlet is the aggregate rate at which thermal
energy leaves a power-conversion cycle through all heat-rejection outlet
streams. It represents the total rejected heat load delivered from the
conversion cycle to its heat sink, excluding useful electrical output.

The total outlet thermal power is the sum of the thermal-power contributions
from the individual heat-rejection outlet streams:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,out}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{O}} P_{\mathrm{th,out},i} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{waste,out}}}{dt}
$$

where $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of heat-rejection outlet streams,
$P_{\mathrm{th,out},i}$ is the thermal power carried by outlet stream $i$,
$E_{\mathrm{waste,out}}$ is the cumulative rejected thermal energy in J, and
$t$ is time in s.

This quantity is the aggregate over outlet streams; an individual
outlet-stream contribution is thermal_power_at_outlet. For a steady
conversion cycle with no net energy accumulation inside the conversion
boundary, it is related to total_thermal_power_at_inlet by the first-law
balance $P_{\mathrm{th,out}}^{\mathrm{tot}} =
P_{\mathrm{th,in}}^{\mathrm{tot}} - P_{\mathrm{net}}$, where
$P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net useful electrical power delivered by the
conversion system.

sources.leaf_definition: Total heat flow being rejected from the thermal plant
sources.parent_definition: Energy conversion

NAMES.name: tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron tritium source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, with each injected tritium atom contributing
one equivalent-electron count.
NAMES.long:
The tritium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral tritium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{T}} = 1$ is
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count rate. It is the tritium-specific component of the
[source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}} = Z_{\mathrm{T}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the raw tritium atom delivery rate in atoms per
second, and $Z_{\mathrm{T}}$ is tritium's atomic number. The rate is the
instantaneous derivative of the accumulated inventory [accumulated tritium
count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection), and it
counts delivered atoms rather than plasma electron content or ionization
state.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when tritium gas is being delivered into the
vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium

NAMES.name: vertical_velocity_of_pellet
NAMES.short:
Signed vertical component of the pellet center-of-mass velocity, parallel to
the symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed vertical component of the translational velocity
of the pellet center of mass. It resolves motion in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The vertical velocity is defined by:

$$
v_Z = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{dZ_{\mathrm{cm}}}{dt}
$$

where $v_Z$ is the vertical velocity component, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}$
is the pellet center-of-mass velocity vector, $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit
vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$, $Z_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is
the vertical coordinate of the pellet center of mass, and $t$ is time.

For a shattered pellet, this quantity describes the mass-weighted bulk
motion of the fragment cloud, not an individual fragment's velocity. It
excludes rotational motion about the center of mass and is not restricted to
the initial value at vacuum-chamber entry.

Together with the [radial velocity of the
pellet](name:radial_velocity_of_pellet) and [toroidal velocity of the
pellet](name:toroidal_velocity_of_pellet), it specifies the translational
velocity vector when all components refer to the same pellet and instant.
This signed component is distinct from the speed, which is the magnitude of
that vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the pellet center of mass moves toward
increasing $Z$.

sources.parent_definition: Set of shattered pellet fragments

NAMES.name: volume_of_pellet_fragment
NAMES.short:
Geometric volume occupied by the material of an individual shattered pellet
fragment, distinguishing fragment size from the intact pellet and
surrounding propellant.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the geometric volume enclosed by the material boundary of
one shattered pellet fragment. It describes the fragment’s physical size
rather than the volume of the complete pellet, injector, or surrounding
propellant.

The volume is defined from the fragment’s material domain:

$$
V_f = \int_{\mathcal{D}_f} d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $V_f$ is the volume of the individual fragment, $\mathcal{D}_f$ is the
three-dimensional region occupied by its material, and $d^3\mathbf{r}$ is
the volume element integrated over that region.

The scope is one individual fragment within the shattered-pellet population.
This is an extensive geometric quantity for that fragment and is not an
aggregate over multiple fragments; it excludes surrounding gas and does not
represent the volume of the intact pellet, injector, or complete fragment
cloud.

The associated [toroidal coordinate of the pellet
fragment](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment) locates the same
fragment around the machine symmetry axis, while this quantity characterizes
its geometric size.

sources.leaf_definition: Volume of the fragment
sources.parent_definition: Set of shattered pellet fragments

NAMES.name: x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Cartesian x-component of the unit vector directed along the major geometric
axis of the elliptic shatter cone.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the projection of the shatter cone’s major-axis unit vector
onto the Cartesian x direction. The major-axis unit vector specifies the
orientation of the elliptic shatter cone.

In the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, the
component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{major},x} = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}} \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}}$ is the unit vector along the
cone’s major axis, $\hat{x}$ is the Cartesian x-direction unit vector, and
$u_{\mathrm{major},x}$ is their scalar projection. The component
participates in the unit-vector constraint with the corresponding y and z
components. The [y major-axis unit-vector
component](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) resolves the same
axis in the y direction, whereas the [x minor-axis unit-vector
component](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) describes the
orthogonal minor axis.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along X axis
sources.parent_definition: Major unit vector describing the geometry of the elliptic shatter cone

NAMES.name: x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Signed x projection of the unit vector along an elliptic shatter cone’s
minor geometric axis in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed projection of the unit vector directed along the
minor geometric axis of an elliptic shatter cone onto the Cartesian x
direction. It specifies one orientation coordinate of that hardware axis.

Let $u_x$ denote this x component, $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ the
unit vector along the shatter cone’s minor axis, and $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ the
unit vector toward increasing x in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$
frame. The defining projection is

$$
u_x = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{minor}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{x}}
$$

The component is bounded between −1 and 1 because
$\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is normalized.

This quantity applies only to the minor axis of the shatter cone and
represents one Cartesian component; it is neither the complete direction
vector, its magnitude, nor an aggregation over axes or hardware objects. It
is distinct from the corresponding [x component of the major-axis unit
vector](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

Together with the other Cartesian components of the same minor-axis unit
vector, including the [z component of the minor-axis unit
vector](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this component
specifies the minor-axis orientation.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along X axis
sources.parent_definition: Minor unit vector describing the geometry of the elliptic shatter cone

NAMES.name: x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
NAMES.short:
Cartesian x component of the unit vector along the unshattered pellet
velocity immediately before shattering, resolved in the right-handed
Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the x-directed Cartesian component of the unit vector
aligned with the unshattered pellet velocity immediately before shattering.
It describes the injection direction associated with the pellet injector,
not a hardware-axis orientation or a post-shattering fragment direction.

The injection-direction vector is decomposed in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis as

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}=u_x\hat{x}+u_y\hat{y}+u_z\hat{z},\qquad u_x=\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}\cdot\hat{x},\qquad |\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}|=1
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}$ is the unshattered pellet
velocity-direction unit vector, $u_x$ is its x component, and $\hat{x}$,
$\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$ are the Cartesian basis unit vectors. The
corresponding components are given by the [y unit vector of the pellet
injector](name:y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector) and [z direction unit
vector of the pellet
injector](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector).

sources.leaf_definition: Component along X axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector of the unshattered pellet velocity direction right before shattering

NAMES.name: xenon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate for xenon atoms supplied by
gas injection, assigning 54 equivalent electrons to each xenon atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which xenon is supplied by gas
injection, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. It represents injected
xenon inventory rather than electron production or the xenon content already
present in the plasma.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t) = 54\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t)$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the atomic number of xenon, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)$
is the xenon-atom injection rate due to gas injection, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies only to xenon supplied by gas injection and aggregates
the injected xenon-atom rate by weighting each atom with xenon's atomic
number. It is species-resolved and instantaneous, not a total rate over all
injected gasses.

The factor 54 is an equivalent-electron bookkeeping convention based on
nuclear charge, not a count of free electrons produced by ionization. This
rate is distinct from an accumulated xenon inventory; integrating it over
time gives the equivalent-electron inventory delivered by gas injection. The
same species-resolved convention is used for the [helium-4 gas-injection
source rate](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) and [hydrogen
gas-injection source rate](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon

NAMES.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Signed Y-axis projection of the unit vector defining the orientation of an
elliptic shatter cone in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed projection of an elliptic shatter cone's
direction unit vector onto the Cartesian Y axis.

The component is defined by

$$
d_y = \hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\rm cone} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $d_y$ is the Y component, $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\rm cone}$ is the
shatter-cone direction unit vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the unit
vector along increasing $y$ in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},
\hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

This quantity applies only to the shatter-cone direction and represents one
Cartesian component; no population, regional, charge-state, averaging, or
summation convention applies. It is not the direction-vector magnitude and
must not be confused with the [Y component of the shatter-cone major-axis
unit vector](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes
a geometric axis rather than the cone direction. The complete direction
requires all three Cartesian components.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector of the cone direction

NAMES.name: y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
The signed y component of the unit vector along the major axis of an
elliptic shatter cone is its projection in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y,
z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The signed y component of the unit vector along the major axis of an
elliptic shatter cone is the projection of that major-axis direction onto
the $y$ basis direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y},
\hat{z})$ frame. The major-axis direction is the orientation of the
principal semiaxis of the cone's elliptic cross-section.

The component is defined by

$$
e_{\mathrm{maj},y} = \hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}} \cdot \hat{y}
$$

where $e_{\mathrm{maj},y}$ is the y component of the shatter-cone major-axis
unit vector, $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$ is the unit vector along the major
axis of the elliptic shatter cone, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of
the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity applies to the geometry of an elliptic shatter cone and to the
major semiaxis orientation of its elliptic cross-section; its aggregation
convention is none, because it is a single vector component rather than a
sum or mean. It is distinct from the unsigned major-axis length, from the [y
component of the shatter-cone direction unit
vector](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes the
cone direction rather than the major-axis orientation, and from the [y
component of the minor-axis unit
vector](name:y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which refers to the
orthogonal minor semiaxis.

Together with the [x
component](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z
component](name:z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this quantity
forms the Cartesian representation of $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$; the linked x
and z components and $e_{\mathrm{maj},y}$ satisfy $(e_{\mathrm{maj},x})^2 +
(e_{\mathrm{maj},y})^2 + (e_{\mathrm{maj},z})^2 = 1$, where
$e_{\mathrm{maj},x}$ and $e_{\mathrm{maj},z}$ are the linked x and z
components. The major-axis and minor-axis unit vectors jointly orient the
elliptic cone and satisfy $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}} \cdot
\hat{e}_{\mathrm{min}} = 0$, where $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{min}}$ is the
minor-axis unit vector with
[x](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone),
[y](name:y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), and
[z](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) components.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$ has a component in
the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y},
\hat{z})$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis
sources.parent_definition: Major unit vector describing the geometry of the elliptic shatter cone

NAMES.name: y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Y component of the unit vector along the minor axis of an elliptic shatter
cone, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The minor-axis unit vector specifies one orientation of the elliptic shatter
cone. This quantity is its signed projection onto the Cartesian y direction,
complementing the [x minor-axis
component](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z minor-axis
component](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

The component is defined by

$$
u_y = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the unit vector along the
shatter-cone minor axis and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y-directed unit vector
in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The
complete minor-axis vector has unit norm, so its components satisfy $u_x^2 +
u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis
sources.parent_definition: Minor unit vector describing the geometry of the elliptic shatter cone

NAMES.name: y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
NAMES.short:
Cartesian y component of the unit vector aligned with the unshattered pellet
velocity direction immediately before shattering.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the projection onto the Cartesian y axis of the
unit-normalized direction of the unshattered pellet velocity immediately
before shattering.

The component is defined by

$$
u_y = \hat{\mathbf{u}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{u}} = \frac{\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|}
$$

where $u_y$ is the y component, $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$ is the pellet
injection-direction unit vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is the unshattered pellet
velocity, $|\mathbf{v}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y
unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
frame.

This quantity describes direction only, not pellet speed or position. Its
value is bounded between $-1$ and $1$; together with the [x component of the
pellet-injector unit vector](name:x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector) and [z
component of the pellet-injector direction unit
vector](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector), it specifies the
injection direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector of the unshattered pellet velocity direction right before shattering

NAMES.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
NAMES.short:
Z component of the unit vector aligned with the unshattered pellet velocity
immediately before shattering, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y,
z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed projection of the unshattered pellet-injection
direction onto the Cartesian z axis immediately before shattering. It
describes orientation only, not the pellet speed or the velocity of
shattered fragments.

The component is defined by:

$$
d_z = \hat{\mathbf{d}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{d}}$ is the unit vector aligned with the unshattered
pellet velocity and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing z
in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. Together
with the corresponding [x component](name:x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector)
and [y component](name:y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector), it specifies the
injection direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Z axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector of the unshattered pellet velocity direction right before shattering

NAMES.name: z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Signed z-component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit vector, specifying
its orientation along z in the right-handed Cartesian frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed projection of the shatter-cone major-axis unit
vector onto the Cartesian z direction. It specifies the major-axis
orientation along z, not an axis length or a position coordinate.

The component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{major},z} = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}} \cdot \hat{z}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}}$ is the unit vector along the
shatter-cone major axis and $\hat{z}$ is the z basis vector in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ frame. Together with the
[x major-axis unit-vector
component](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [y major-axis
unit-vector component](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), it
defines the Cartesian orientation of that axis. It is distinct from the [z
minor-axis unit-vector
component](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Z axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector of the cone direction

NAMES.name: z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Signed Z component of the minor-axis unit vector defining the orientation of
an elliptic shatter cone in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the projection of the unit vector along an elliptic shatter
cone's minor geometric axis onto the Cartesian z direction.

The component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{minor},z} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the unit vector directed along the
shatter cone's minor axis, $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit basis vector for
increasing $z$ in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
frame, and $u_{\mathrm{minor},z}$ is their scalar projection.

This quantity applies only to the minor geometric axis of the shatter cone
and represents one Cartesian component, not the complete orientation vector,
its magnitude, or a component of the major axis. It is a signed component
and is not an aggregate over multiple axes or objects.

Together with the remaining Cartesian components, including the [x component
of the shatter-cone minor-axis unit
vector](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), it defines the
minor-axis orientation. It is distinct from the [z component of the
shatter-cone major-axis unit
vector](name:z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes the
other principal axis.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Z axis
sources.parent_definition: Minor unit vector describing the geometry of the elliptic shatter cone

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pellet_path
NAMES.short:
Normalized toroidal magnetic-flux surface label assigned to each pellet
location, identifying the nested magnetic surface reached along the pellet’s
in-plasma ablation trajectory.
NAMES.long:
This quantity identifies the nested magnetic surface containing the pellet
at a specified location along its in-plasma ablation trajectory. It is a
magnetic-surface coordinate, not a cylindrical distance or a local vector
component.

At pellet position $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}$, the normalized toroidal flux
coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}) = \left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right]^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate,
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}$ is the pellet position,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p})$ is the toroidal magnetic flux
labeling the magnetic surface through that position,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its value at the equilibrium boundary. The
position is interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The scope is the pellet’s in-plasma ablation trajectory, with the coordinate
evaluated pointwise at each pellet location. It does not represent distance
traveled along the path, a path integral, an average over the trajectory, or
an aggregate over multiple pellets.

This is the locus-specific realization of the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). The axis and boundary
references set the coordinate endpoints, so the value increases outward
across nested magnetic surfaces while remaining distinct from a cylindrical
radial coordinate.

sources.leaf_definition: Normalized toroidal coordinate along the pellet path
sources.parent_definition: 1-D profiles of plasma and pellet along the pellet path

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of the shatter-cone origin, locating its reference
point by perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of a shatter-cone origin is the major-radius location
of that geometric reference point relative to the toroidal symmetry axis. It
is the $R$ coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
with basis vectors $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ satisfying $\hat{R}
\times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies specifically to the origin of the elliptic shatter
cone. It denotes one geometric coordinate of that reference point, with no
averaging, integration, or aggregation over the cone surface, its axis, or
injected fragments; it is distinct from radial coordinates assigned to other
injector features or positions.

It is a locus-specific specialization of [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate): the parent defines the major-radius
coordinate generally, while this quantity evaluates it at the shatter-cone
origin.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Coordinates of the origin of the shatter cone

NAMES.name: total_heating_power_due_to_fusion_reactions
NAMES.short:
Gross thermal power delivered to a fusion power plant’s thermal-to-electric
conversion cycle from fusion reactions, including blanket energy
multiplication.
NAMES.long:
Total fusion-attributed heating power is the gross thermal input delivered
to a fusion power plant’s thermal-to-electric conversion cycle. It combines
heat released by fusion reactions with additional thermal power produced by
nuclear energy multiplication in the blanket.

$$
P_{\mathrm{cycle}}^{\mathrm{fusion}} = P_{\mathrm{fusion}} + P_{\mathrm{blanket}}^{\mathrm{mult}}
$$

Here, $P_{\mathrm{cycle}}^{\mathrm{fusion}}$ is the total fusion-attributed
thermal power supplied to the conversion cycle, $P_{\mathrm{fusion}}$ is the
thermal power released by fusion reactions and entering the plant heat
stream, and $P_{\mathrm{blanket}}^{\mathrm{mult}}$ is the additional thermal
power generated by energy multiplication in the blanket.

The quantity is aggregated over all included fusion-reaction and
blanket-multiplication contributions at the plant conversion-cycle boundary.
It is a gross thermal input, not local plasma heating or a power density.
The cumulative plasma heating or energy-transfer quantity [power at an
inside flux surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface) describes energy
associated with a plasma region and is therefore distinct from this
plant-level cycle input.

sources.leaf_definition: Total heat flow being supplied to the thermal plant (fusion thermal power)
sources.parent_definition: Energy conversion

NAMES.name: field_line_length
NAMES.short:
Arclength of an individually traced magnetic field line during plasma
initiation, resolving the field-line length distribution rather than
reporting an average connection length.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the geometric arclength of one magnetic field line traced
during plasma initiation. It characterizes the distribution of individual
field-line lengths associated with the evolving magnetic topology.

For a field-line trajectory parameterized by $(s)$, its length is

$$
L = \int_{s_0}^{s_1} \left\lVert \frac{d\mathbf{r}}{ds} \right\rVert ds
$$

where $L$ is the field-line length, $(s)$ is the position vector along the
traced magnetic field line, $s$ is a tracing parameter, and $s_0$ and $s_1$
delimit the traced segment.

The quantity applies separately to each traced magnetic field line during
the plasma-initiation phase; it is not an average, sum, or charge-state
aggregation. It does not impose the open-field-line averaging and
closed-line replacement convention of [connection
length](name:connection_length), and it is distinct from field-line
fraction, which describes the fraction of lines that are open.

The set of individual lengths provides a geometric characterization of
magnetic topology, while the open-line fraction identifies the prevalence of
open field lines within the same traced population.

sources.leaf_definition: Length of each field line
sources.parent_definition: Magnetic field line tracing results, given at various time slices

NAMES.name: absorbed_radiated_power_at_wall
NAMES.short:
Net radiative power deposited on plasma-facing wall surfaces, equal to
incident plasma radiation minus the portion reflected back toward the
plasma.
NAMES.long:
Net absorbed radiative power is the total photon power retained by
plasma-facing wall surfaces after reflection losses. It represents the
wall's radiative power load and excludes nonradiative particle, conductive,
and other thermal-power contributions.

The net retained power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,wall}} = P_{\mathrm{inc,wall}} - P_{\mathrm{ref,wall}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,wall}}$ is the absorbed radiative power at the wall,
$P_{\mathrm{inc,wall}}$ is the total plasma-radiation power incident on the
wall, and $P_{\mathrm{ref,wall}}$ is the portion of that incident radiation
reflected away from the wall. The quantity is integrated over the wall
rather than expressed as a local power per unit area.

This wall-wide quantity includes the aggregate radiative load over all
applicable plasma-facing wall surfaces. It is broader than [absorbed
radiated power of divertor](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_divertor) and
[absorbed radiated power of breeder blanket
module](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which apply
the same incident-minus-reflected principle to specified wall components,
and it is distinct from [total incident neutral energy flux at
wall](name:total_incident_neutral_energy_flux_at_wall), which describes
neutral-particle energy transport rather than absorbed photon power.

sources.leaf_definition: Net radiated power from plasma onto the wall (incident-reflected)
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: density_at_limiter
NAMES.short:
Local number density of a selected charged plasma population evaluated
immediately on the plasma-facing side of a limiter surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local number density of a selected charged plasma
population at the plasma-facing side of a limiter. The selection may be
electrons, an ion species summed over its ionization states, or a defined
fuel pseudo-species formed by combining constituent ion populations.

$$
n_s(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_s}{dV}
$$

where $n_s$ is the selected population number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_s$ is
the number of counted particles, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$
is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. The position is immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing
limiter, on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

Population aggregation is part of the specialization: ion species quantities
may be summed over positive ionization states while excluding neutrals,
electrons count the electron population, and the deuterium–tritium
pseudo-species combines the corresponding ion densities. Concrete members
include [electron density at a limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter),
ion density at a limiter, and [deuterium-tritium density at a
limiter](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter). The bare quantity does
not imply a sum over all charged populations.

NAMES.name: argon_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Argon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states
and excluding neutral argon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Argon density at a limiter is the local number density of argon ions in the
boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The
evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance, and neutral argon atoms are excluded.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\sum_{q>0} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L)
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ are number densities in
m$^{-3}$, $q$ is the positive argon ionization state, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is
the limiter-side position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

This is the argon-specific member of [density at a
limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It counts argon ions rather than the
electrons represented by [electron density at a
limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter), and is local rather than the
flux-surface average represented by flux-surface-averaged argon density at
the plasma boundary.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Beryllium ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to
a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all beryllium ionization states
from Be1+ through Be4+.
NAMES.long:
Beryllium density at a limiter is the local number density of beryllium ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath
or sheath entrance, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the
material surface. Unless a specific ionization stage is resolved, this
quantity is summed over all charged beryllium states; neutral beryllium
atoms are excluded.

The charge-state-summed density is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Be} = \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in
ionization state $z$, spanning all four stages accessible under edge-plasma
conditions.

Beryllium is used as a plasma-facing material in several tokamak devices;
sputtering of beryllium limiter surfaces introduces impurity ions into the
scrape-off layer, where they contribute to fuel dilution and raise the
effective charge $Z_\mathrm{eff}$. This limiter-edge density sets the
impurity source boundary condition in edge transport models and is inferred
from spectroscopic line-emission measurements of beryllium charge states
combined with sheath or presheath models, or computed self-consistently in
coupled plasma-fluid and impurity-continuity solvers.

This quantity is the limiter-surface analog of
[beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary)
at the last-closed flux surface and of
[beryllium_density_at_divertor_target](name:beryllium_density_at_divertor_target)
at the divertor target. The parent
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) defines the evaluation locus
shared by all species-resolved limiter density quantities, including the
fuel-ion member
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter). The
volumetric profile away from the limiter is given by
[beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Boron ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states
and excluding neutral boron atoms.
NAMES.long:
Boron density at a limiter is the local number density of boron ions in the
boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The
evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance.

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}=\sum_{q=1}^{5}n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L)
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron-ion number density in m$^{-3}$,
$N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of counted boron ions, $V$ is volume in
m$^3$, $n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the density of boron charge state $q$, and
$\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The sum includes boron ions from B$^{+}$ through fully stripped B$^{5+}$ and
excludes neutral boron atoms. This is the boron-specific specialization of
[density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter); unlike [boron density at
the plasma boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary), it is evaluated
specifically at the limiter-side location.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Carbon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all carbon ionization states and
excluding neutral carbon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Carbon density at a limiter is the local number density of carbon ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance, consistent with the parent
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) framework. Carbon supports six
ionization states ($\text{C}^{1+}$ through $\text{C}^{6+}$), and this
quantity sums over all of them; neutral carbon atoms are excluded from this
count.

The total charge-state-summed carbon density at the limiter is:

$$
n_\text{C} = \sum_{z=1}^{6} n_{\text{C}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\text{C}^{z+}}$ is the number density of carbon ions in charge
state $z$ at the limiter evaluation point.

Carbon enters the edge plasma primarily through physical sputtering,
chemical erosion, and recycling from carbon-based plasma-facing components.
The density is inferred from spectroscopic line emission (C II through C VI)
analyzed with collisional-radiative models that convert observed photon
emissivities to charge-state-resolved densities.

In carbon-wall configurations, $n_\text{C}$ at the limiter spans
approximately $10^{15}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on the carbon source
rate, local electron temperature, and scrape-off-layer plasma density.
Carbon impurities contribute to
[effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) and radiate
strongly at edge electron temperatures of 10–100 eV. Analogous carbon
densities at other boundary locations are tracked by
[carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary)
and
[carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Deuterium ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to
a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the
magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium density at a limiter is the local number density of deuterium ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance, where open scrape-off-layer field lines
terminate on the limiter material. Because deuterium carries only a single
ionization state ($\mathrm{D}^+$, charge number $Z = 1$), no charge-state
summation is required, in contrast to impurity-species counterparts such as
[carbon_density_at_limiter](name:carbon_density_at_limiter) or
[argon_density_at_limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter).

This density, together with
[electron_temperature_at_limiter](name:electron_temperature_at_limiter),
determines the ion saturation current flux to the limiter and governs local
deuterium recycling and redeposition. In two-point model analyzes of the
scrape-off layer, the limiter-side density is linked to the upstream
separatrix density through parallel momentum and energy balance along
magnetic field lines, with the Bohm sheath criterion $v_s = c_s = \sqrt{(T_e
+ T_i)/m_i}$ setting the flow speed at the sheath entrance, where $T_e$ and
$T_i$ are the electron and ion temperatures and $m_i$ is the deuterium ion
mass.

Measurement methods include flush-mounted Langmuir probes that yield the ion
saturation current density from which the density is extracted,
spectroscopic observation of deuterium Balmer emission combined with
collisional-radiative modeling, and edge transport simulations constrained
by upstream density profiles. Representative scrape-off-layer values at the
limiter span $10^{17}$–$10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on global plasma
density, fueling, and limiter geometry.

As a member of the [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) parent
family, this quantity complements the tritium fuel-ion counterpart
[tritium_density_at_limiter](name:tritium_density_at_limiter) and
[hydrogen_density_at_limiter](name:hydrogen_density_at_limiter). The
corresponding quantity at the magnetic separatrix is
[deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species in the boundary
plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, equal to the
sum of the local deuterium and tritium ion densities.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-tritium density at the limiter is the local number density of the
combined DT fuel ion pseudo-species in the boundary plasma immediately
adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of
the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The DT pseudo-species represents
deuterium and tritium ions as a single fictitious fuel constituent with an
effective per-ion mass of $\bar{m} \approx 2.5\,m_u$ (where $m_u$ is the
unified atomic mass unit) for an equimolar D-T mixture.

The quantity equals the sum of the separate deuterium and tritium ion
densities at the limiter contact point:

$$
n_{DT} = n_D + n_T
$$

where $n_D$ is the local deuterium ion number density and $n_T$ is the local
tritium ion number density at the same evaluation point.

This quantity is the limiter-contact analog of
[deuterium_tritium_density](name:deuterium_tritium_density) and the DT-fuel
counterpart of
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter) at the
same locus. It differs from
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary)
in evaluation geometry: the limiter contact lies in the scrape-off layer on
open field lines, not at the last-closed flux surface. As a member of the
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) parent family, the presheath
evaluation convention and locus definition follow those of
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter) and other
sibling fuel-species densities.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: effective_charge_at_limiter
NAMES.short:
Effective charge number of the local ion mixture in boundary plasma
immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
NAMES.long:
The effective charge at a limiter quantifies the charge-squared-weighted
composition of the local positive-ion mixture immediately adjacent to the
plasma-facing limiter surface. It is the limiter-local specialization of
charge_at_limiter.

$$
Z_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{\sum_i n_i Z_i}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective charge number, $n_i$ is the number
density of ion population $i$ in m$^{-3}$, and $Z_i$ is its positive integer
charge number. The sum includes positive ion species and charge states,
while neutral atoms are excluded. A pure hydrogenic ion mixture gives
$Z_\mathrm{eff}=1$; admixture of multiply charged impurity ions raises the
value. The limiter location distinguishes this quantity from
[effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary](name:effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary),
which is evaluated at the plasma boundary.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Effective charge

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Electron density at a limiter is the local number density of electrons in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or
sheath entrance.

$$
n_e(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_e}{dV}
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_e$ is the number
of electrons, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side
evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Unlike ion density at a limiter, this quantity counts electrons only and
includes neither ions nor neutral atoms. It is the electron-specific member
of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and is distinct from
[electron density at the plasma
boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which uses a different
evaluation locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron density

NAMES.name: electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Rate at which particles represented as equivalent electrons are removed from
the plasma region by wall pumping, giving global electron-equivalent exhaust
throughput.
NAMES.long:
The rate at which particles of the electron-equivalent population are
removed from the plasma region by wall pumping is the global scalar
representation of the wall particle-removal flux. It describes pumped
particle exhaust using equivalent-electron counting rather than a local wall
flux density.

The global removal rate is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{pump}} = \frac{dN_{e,\mathrm{removed}}}{dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{pump}}$ is the pumped particle-removal rate
expressed in equivalent electrons, $N_{e,\mathrm{removed}}$ is the
cumulative number of electron equivalents removed by wall pumping, and $t$
is time.

This quantity is aggregated over the wall and represents the total pumping
throughput for the electron-equivalent population. The electron-equivalent
basis does not assert that all removed particles are physical electrons, and
the quantity is not an areal flux density, an electrical current, or a rate
for one specified neutral species.

It is the electron-specific specialization of the general [particle-removal
flux at the wall due to pumping](name:particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping).
In contrast, [neutral particle flux at the wall due to
pumping](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping) uses a specified
neutral species as its counting population rather than equivalent-electron
counting.

sources.leaf_definition: Pumped particle flux (in equivalent electrons)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to electrons

NAMES.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission
of material from plasma-facing surfaces, weighted by the electron
contribution of each emitted species after ionization.
NAMES.long:
Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission
is the rate at which ionization of material released from plasma-facing
surfaces adds electrons to the plasma particle balance. It aggregates all
emitted fuel, molecular, and impurity species over all plasma-facing
surfaces, with each emitted particle weighted by the number of bound
electrons it can contribute after full ionization.

The global rate is defined by integrating the emitted particle flux density
over the plasma-facing surface area:

$$
S_e^{\mathrm{surf}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf}}} \sum_s \nu_{e,s}\,\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $S_e^{\mathrm{surf}}$ is the electron-equivalent surface-emission
source rate, $A_{\mathrm{pf}}$ is the total plasma-facing surface area, $s$
indexes emitted species, $\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the
emitted particle flux density of species $s$ at surface position
$\mathbf{x}$ directed toward the plasma, $dA$ is a surface element, and
$\nu_{e,s}$ is the electron yield of one emitted particle on full
ionization. For an emitted atom, $\nu_{e,s}=Z_s$ with $Z_s$ the nuclear
charge number; for an emitted molecule or compound particle, $\nu_{e,s}$ is
the sum of the nuclear charge numbers of its constituent atoms.

Surface emission includes recycling, delayed outgassing, and physical or
chemical sputtering only insofar as the released material returns toward the
plasma and is ionized. This quantity is the electron-specific counterpart of
source_rate_due_to_surface_emission, is distinct from externally supplied
material represented by
[electron_source_rate_due_to_injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection),
excludes electron loss by incidence on surfaces, and contributes to
[total_electron_source_rate](name:total_electron_source_rate).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when ionization of material emitted from
plasma-facing surfaces supplies electron-equivalent particles to the plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: Particle flux from the wall corresponding to the conversion into various neutral types (first dimension: 1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast), in equivalent electrons
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to electrons

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Kinetic temperature of the electron population evaluated at the
plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open scrape-off-layer field lines
terminate.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local kinetic temperature of the electron population at
the plasma-wall interface on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open
scrape-off-layer field lines terminate. It is the electron-specific member
of temperature at limiter.

For an isotropic electron population, its temperature expressed in energy
units is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_{\mathrm{kin},e} \rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron kinetic temperature and $\langle
E_{\mathrm{kin},e} \rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron.

The quantity refers to electrons on the plasma-facing side of the limiter
interface and does not denote the temperature of the limiter material. It is
distinct from the density-weighted population average average temperature at
limiter, which combines the relevant plasma populations.
