NAMES.name: flux_at_limiter
NAMES.short:
Flux at a limiter is the local surface rate density at which an
energy-dimensioned plasma-borne quantity is deposited on the plasma-facing
surface of a limiter. It fixes the limiter locus and the local surface-flux
character; more specific quantities state the energy channel being carried,
as in energy flux at limiter.
NAMES.long:
Flux at a limiter is the local surface rate density at which an
energy-dimensioned plasma-borne quantity is deposited on the plasma-facing
surface of a limiter. As a structural parent, it fixes the limiter locus and
the local per-area rate character shared by its members, while each more
specific name states the particular energy channel being deposited.

For a local limiter surface element, the flux is the rate of the deposited
quantity per surface area:

$$
q_{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\partial^2 Q_{\mathrm{plasma}\to\mathrm{lim}}}{\partial A_{\mathrm{lim}}\,\partial t}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the flux at limiter,
$Q_{\mathrm{plasma}\to\mathrm{lim}}$ is the energy-dimensioned quantity
delivered by the plasma to the limiter surface element, $A_{\mathrm{lim}}$
is the area of that limiter plasma-facing surface element, and $t$ is time.

The scope is restricted to plasma-facing limiter surfaces, and the quantity
is local to the surface element: it carries no built-in integration,
maximum, average, or other aggregation over the limiter unless a more
specific standard name states such an aggregation. The carried quantity
always has the dimension of energy, so every member of this family shares
the same surface power-density character; the family does not extend to
particle-count or momentum surface fluxes, which are dimensionally distinct
quantities.

This quantity excludes fluxes to non-limiter wall components, the total
power deposited on a limiter, and signed vector heat-flux components normal
to a surface. The more specific [energy flux at
limiter](name:energy_flux_at_limiter) is the attested member that fixes the
carried quantity as plasma energy deposition, inheriting the local
limiter-surface rate-density semantics defined here.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_limiter
NAMES.short:
Plasma energy deposition rate per unit area on the plasma-facing surface of
a limiter, without implying a maximum or other surface aggregation.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at a limiter is the plasma energy deposition rate per unit area
on the plasma-facing surface of a limiter. It is a surface power-density
quantity for plasma-wall interaction with the limiter material.

For a surface element on the limiter, the local limiter energy flux $q_E$ is
defined by the deposited plasma power per surface area:

$$
q_E = \frac{dP_\mathrm{dep}}{dA}
$$

where $q_E$ is the energy flux at the limiter, $P_\mathrm{dep}$ is the
plasma power deposited on the limiter surface element, and $A$ is the area
of that surface element.

This parent quantity applies to limiter plasma-facing surfaces and does not
by itself specify a spatial maximum, average, integral, component, or
normalization. It excludes total power deposited on the limiter, which is
obtained by integrating the energy flux over surface area, and it excludes
energy deposition on non-limiter plasma-facing components unless those
components are acting as the limiter surface.

The [maximum energy flux at limiter](name:energy_flux_maximum_at_limiter) is
the surface maximum of this limiter energy-flux quantity over the limiter
plasma-facing surface.

NAMES.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Flux at a plasma-facing wall due to recombination is the wall-area density
of a recombination-caused transfer rate at the wall. It fixes the wall locus
and recombination cause; a more specific quantity specifies what is
transported, such as energy, and how incident populations, charge states,
channels, and products are aggregated.
NAMES.long:
Flux at a plasma-facing wall due to recombination is the wall-area density
of a transfer rate attributable to charged plasma particles recombining into
lower-charge or neutral states at a plasma-facing material surface. It is
the common at-wall recombination-flux concept: the wall locus and
recombination cause are fixed, while the transported quantity is specified
by a more specific member.

For a member transporting an extensive quantity $X$, the local wall-area
density is defined by

$$
F_X^{\mathrm{rec,wall}} = \frac{d\dot{X}^{\mathrm{rec,wall}}}{dA}
$$

where $F_X^{\mathrm{rec,wall}}$ is the at-wall flux density of the
transported quantity $X$ due to recombination, $\dot{X}^{\mathrm{rec,wall}}$
is the corresponding recombination-at-wall transfer rate, $A$ is
plasma-facing wall surface area, and the superscript $\mathrm{rec,wall}$
identifies the recombination contribution at the wall.

The quantity applies only to plasma-facing wall surfaces and to
recombination events occurring at or mediated by those surfaces. For the
unqualified at-wall recombination contribution, the scope is inclusive over
contributing incident plasma populations and charge states, recombination
channels, and product species or internal states unless a more specific
member explicitly narrows one of those categories.

It is not a flux through an arbitrary surface, not a volume recombination
rate, and not the total wall flux from all plasma-wall interaction
mechanisms. It excludes contributions from non-recombination processes such
as direct impact energy transfer, ionization, sputtering, radiation, or
reflection unless those processes are part of the recombination channel
being specified.

The [energy flux at wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) is the member
obtained by taking $X$ to be energy; it inherits the same at-wall
recombination locus and cause while adding the energy-specific
interpretation and its stated aggregation over incident-ion species, charge
states, recombination channels, and emitted products. The parent relation
itself does not impose energy weighting on every possible member; it defines
the shared wall-area-density form for the recombination contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the recombination contribution transports the
specified quantity from the material wall toward the plasma-facing side.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Outgoing energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident
plasma ions recombine at the surface, summed over incident-ion species,
incident-ion charge states, recombination channels, and emitted product
species and states.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which
recombination-associated energy is emitted from a plasma-facing surface per
unit area as a result of incident plasma ions recombining or neutralizing at
the material boundary. It is the total outgoing energy flux carried by
emitted recombination products or quanta, not the incident plasma energy
flux or heat deposited in the wall material.

The total recombination energy flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ is
defined as the product-energy moment of the outgoing recombination source:

$$
Q_\mathrm{rec}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{i,\,\zeta,\,c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{out}\,\frac{d\Gamma_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{out})\,dE_\mathrm{out}
$$

where $i$ identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion
charge state, $c$ the surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$
the emitted product species, $k$ the product internal state or emission
class, $E_\mathrm{out}$ the energy carried into the plasma-facing half-space
by an emitted product or quantum, and
$d\Gamma_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{out}$ the corresponding outgoing
recombination-product flux distribution with respect to product energy. For
discrete product energies, the integral is replaced by the corresponding
sum.

This quantity is the energy-weighted counterpart of particle flux at the
wall due to recombination, which counts the same surface recombination
source without energy weighting, and is the energy-flux realization of [flux
at the wall due to recombination](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).
The incident-ion decomposition is charge-state-summed in this total: [ion
charge-state energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination)
resolves a specified incident-ion species and charge state, while [ion
energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) is the
corresponding ion contribution after summing over charge states.
Neutral-product particle specializations such as [neutral particle flux at
the wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination)
partition emitted-product counts and do not by themselves include energy
weighting.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when recombination-associated energy is emitted
away from the plasma-facing wall surface into the plasma-facing half-space.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_eddy_current
NAMES.short:
Eddy-current-attributed energy flux is the areal rate at which energy
generated by Joule dissipation of induced eddy currents is transferred
across a surface. It denotes the eddy-current contribution only, not a
generic process-labeled wall flux or total heat flux.
NAMES.long:
Eddy-current-attributed energy flux is the areal rate at which energy
generated by Joule dissipation of induced eddy currents is transferred
across a surface. It is a process-attributed scalar energy flux: the process
is fixed to eddy currents, while more specific names may add a locus such as
a wall surface.

The scalar flux is defined as the surface density of eddy-current-attributed
power:

$$
F_{\mathrm{eddy}} = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{eddy}}}{dA}
$$

where $F_{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the eddy-current-attributed energy flux,
$P_{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the power associated with Joule dissipation of
induced eddy currents, and $A$ is the area over which that power is
distributed.

The scope is the eddy-current contribution in conducting plasma-facing
structures; if several induced-current paths contribute to the same surface
element, their eddy-current-attributed power contributions are summed before
division by area. This quantity excludes total wall heat flux and
energy-flux contributions attributed to radiation, particle impact,
externally applied heating, or non-eddy-current mechanisms, and it does not
by itself specify that the evaluation locus is the wall.

Energy flux due to eddy current is the explicitly energy-qualified form of
this same process-attributed flux. [Flux at wall due to eddy
current](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current) is a locus-specialized form
evaluated at a plasma-facing wall; the present quantity retains only the
shared eddy-current mechanism attribution, not that child locus.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a material surface through
emission processes such as particle recycling, sputtering, or secondary
electron and photon emission.
NAMES.long:
Surface emission encompasses the range of physical processes by which
plasma-facing material surfaces re-emit particles, energy, or radiation into
the plasma or surrounding environment. These include neutral recycling
(incident ions reflected or thermally desorbed as neutrals), physical and
chemical sputtering (wall atoms ejected by energetic ion bombardment),
secondary electron emission (electrons liberated by ion or electron impact),
and thermal or fluorescence photon emission from heated or excited surface
atoms.

The emitted flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{emit}$ at a surface element is related to
the incident driving flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ through a
process-specific emission yield $Y$:

$$
\Gamma_\mathrm{emit} = Y \cdot \Gamma_\mathrm{incident}
$$

where $Y$ is the emission yield (dimensionless for particle emission, or
carrying the appropriate units ratio for energy or photon emission), and
$\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ is the incident flux of the driving species.

The specific instantiation of this flux at the first wall is described by
[flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
For the total radiated thermal power emitted by wall material, see
thermal_power_of_wall_material_due_to_radiation_emission. General energy
transport through a surface is captured by energy_flux.

NAMES.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, photon emission,
and secondary-electron emission. The transported quantity may be particle
number, energy, momentum, or radiative power in a more specific member.
NAMES.long:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, thermal
evaporation, photon emission, secondary-electron emission, or surface
de-excitation. It is the surface-normal flux density generated by the
material response at the wall and carried from the material side toward the
plasma side.

The emission flux is related to incident driving fluxes through
surface-emission yield or response coefficients:

$$
F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}} = \sum_k Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}} F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}
$$

where $F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted flux density of physical quantity
$Q$, $F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is incident channel $k$ that drives surface
emission, and $Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the surface-emission coefficient
for producing the emitted $Q$ flux.

This quantity is the wall-specific member of
[flux_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_due_to_surface_emission) and is an
abstraction over component channels. The energy channel is
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
while energy_flux_at_wall denotes energy flux at the wall without specifying
surface emission as the cause. It excludes flux incident on the wall from
the plasma or radiation field except as a driver of emission;
flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation denotes radiative flux at the wall rather than
material emission generated by the wall.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net emitted flux is directed from the
wall material into the plasma.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short:
Energy flux at the wall due to surface emission is the energy carried away
per unit area and time, summed over emitted species and energy
contributions.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at the wall due to surface emission is the outward energy
transport rate per unit area associated with surface-emission processes. It
includes the kinetic energy of emitted particles and other emitted energy
contributions, rather than being restricted to radiation alone.

The local emitted energy flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_W^{\mathrm{em}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}W_{\mathrm{em}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\Gamma_W^{\mathrm{em}}$ is the emitted energy flux density,
$W_{\mathrm{em}}$ is the energy carried away through surface emission, $A$
is wall surface area, and $t$ is time.

Contributions are summed over emitted species, their charge states, and
emitted energy channels. The quantity is local to the wall, not a
surface-integrated power or spatial maximum. It excludes incident energy and
is not the net energy deposited at the wall.

This is the energy-transport specialization of [flux at the wall due to
surface emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). Its
[kinetic-energy
contribution](name:kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission)
accounts for energy carried by emitted particle motion. The net energy flux
received by the wall equals the [incident energy
flux](name:incident_energy_flux_at_wall) minus this emitted energy flux.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when energy is carried away from the wall into the
plasma.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Helium-3 ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states
and excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
NAMES.long:
Helium-3 density at a limiter is the local number density of helium-3 ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_{^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{^3\mathrm{He}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density,
$N_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the counted number of helium-3 ions, $V$ is volume,
and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The density is summed over all positive helium-3 ionization states and
excludes neutral helium-3 atoms. It is the helium-3-specific member of
[density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and differs from ion density
at a limiter, which is not restricted to helium-3; [helium-4 density at a
limiter](name:helium_4_density_at_limiter) describes the corresponding
isotope.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Local particle number density of helium-4 ions evaluated in the boundary
plasma immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing limiter surface, on the
plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The value is
summed over He+ and He2+ ionization states and excludes neutral helium-4
atoms.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 density at a limiter is the local number density of helium-4 ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance, not inside the limiter material or in neutral
gas retained at the surface. It is summed over the helium-4 ion charge
states He$^+$ and He$^{2+}$, and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms.

The charge-state-summed helium-4 ion density is related to the
charge-state-resolved velocity distribution functions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} \int f_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $q$ is the positive ion charge state, $f_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}$ is the
velocity distribution function of helium-4 ions with charge state $q+$, and
the integral is taken over all particle velocities at the limiter-side
evaluation point.

This quantity is the helium-4 isotope contribution to
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and to the unweighted ion
population represented by
[total_ion_density_at_limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter). In a
quasineutral boundary plasma,
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter) is coupled
to the charge-weighted ion sum, so helium-4 contributes $\sum_{q=1}^{2}
q\,n_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}$ to that balance. The corresponding helium-3
isotope quantity is
[helium_3_density_at_limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons (4He)

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Local particle number density of hydrogen ions in the boundary plasma
immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the
plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Hydrogen density at a limiter is the local number density of hydrogen ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance; neutral hydrogen is excluded. For hydrogen,
the charge-state sum reduces to the density of positively charged hydrogen
ions, H+.

The local hydrogen-ion density is defined from the velocity distribution
function:

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}^+} = \int f_{\mathrm{H}^+}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}^+}$ is the hydrogen-ion number density,
$f_{\mathrm{H}^+}$ is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity at the evaluation point.

This quantity is the hydrogen-specific component of
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It counts hydrogen ions
separately from
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter), and does
not include neutral hydrogen or other ion species.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: incident_angle_at_wall
NAMES.short:
Incident angle at wall is the angle between the incoming neutral-particle
velocity and the wall-surface normal directed into the material. It is the
species-specific angular coordinate for physical sputtering by neutral
projectiles; zero is normal incidence and grazing incidence approaches a
right angle.
NAMES.long:
Incident angle at wall is the geometrical angle between the velocity
direction of an incident neutral particle at impact and the local
wall-surface normal directed from the plasma-facing side into the wall
material. It characterizes the incidence direction of a selected
neutral-particle species on the wall.

The incidence angle $\alpha$ is defined by

$$
\alpha = \arccos\left(\hat{\mathbf{v}}_\mathrm{inc}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{in}\right)
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{v}}_\mathrm{inc}$ is the unit direction of the incoming
neutral-particle velocity at the impact point and
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{in}$ is the local wall-surface unit normal
directed into the wall material.

The scope is a specified neutral incident species interacting with the wall.
The allowed interval is $0 \le \alpha \le \pi/2$: $\alpha=0$ corresponds to
normal incidence into the wall, and $\alpha=\pi/2$ corresponds to tangential
grazing incidence. Directions for which the particle is leaving the
wall-facing half-space are not incident angles.

This quantity is the angular argument for the physical sputtering dependence
of that neutral species at the wall. It is not the physical sputtering
coefficient, not an angle for emitted or sputtered particles, and not an
average over neutral species or wall locations.

sources.leaf_definition: Array of incident angles of this incident species, on which the physical sputtering coefficient is tabulated
sources.parent_definition: Sputtering coefficients due to a set of incident species

NAMES.name: incident_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current
NAMES.short:
Incident energy flux at the wall is the incoming energy-transfer rate per
unit area attributable to eddy-current processes, before subtraction of
emitted energy.
NAMES.long:
Incident energy flux at the wall due to eddy-current processes is the
incoming contribution to the corresponding surface energy balance. It
describes energy arriving at a wall component before accounting for energy
emitted from that component.

The local incident energy flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{W,\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}}}{\partial A\,\partial t}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the incident energy flux
attributed to eddy-current processes, $W_{\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is
the cumulative incident energy attributed to those processes, $A$ is wall
surface area, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to the wall component under consideration and is an
energy-transfer rate per unit area, not a component-integrated power or a
sum over wall components. It includes only the eddy-current-attributed
contribution, not the sum of all incident energy-transfer channels.

Within this mechanism's energy balance, the net flux received by the wall
equals this incident contribution minus the [emitted eddy-current energy
flux]. Incident and emitted contributions are separate nonnegative
directional quantities, unlike their net difference.

sources.parent_definition: Current energy fluxes

NAMES.name: incident_ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Kinetic-energy power delivered per unit wall area by ions in one specified
charge state as they cross the sheath and strike the wall.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the incident kinetic-energy power flux delivered to a wall
surface by ions belonging to one specified ion charge state. It represents
the kinetic energy carried by those ions after traversing the sheath and
arriving at the wall.

At a wall point, the incident kinetic-energy flux is defined by

$$
q^{\mathrm{kin}}_{s,\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s\lvert\mathbf{v}\rvert^2(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{kin}}_{s,\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident kinetic-energy
flux, $s$ identifies the specified ion charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of
that ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is the ion velocity at the wall,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the plasma toward the
wall, $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of that charge state,
and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integration condition
selects ions moving toward the wall.

The quantity applies locally to the wall surface and is specific to one ion
charge state; it is not summed over ionization states or ion species. It
includes kinetic energy only and excludes neutral-particle energy, radiative
energy, recombination energy, and other non-kinetic contributions.

Summing the charge-state-resolved contributions gives the corresponding
all-ion quantity [ion kinetic energy flux at
wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall), while [ion charge state
particle flux at wall](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall) counts
arriving ions rather than weighting them by kinetic energy. It is distinct
from [total incident neutral energy flux at
wall](name:total_incident_neutral_energy_flux_at_wall), which concerns
neutral particles.

NAMES.name: incident_ion_particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Areal arrival rate of particles from a selected ion species at a wall
surface, summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Incident ion particle flux at a wall is the local rate at which particles
from a selected ion species arrive at a wall surface per unit area. It
counts arriving particles rather than their charge or deposited energy.

The flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{inc}}(A,t)=\frac{\partial^2 N_i^{\mathrm{inc}}}{\partial A\,\partial t},\qquad N_i^{\mathrm{inc}}=\sum_z N_{i,z}^{\mathrm{inc}}
$$

where $\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident particle flux of ion species
$i$, $A$ is wall surface area, $t$ is time, $N_i^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the
cumulative number of incident particles of species $i$, $z$ is the
ionization-state index, and $N_{i,z}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the cumulative
number arriving in state $z$.

The quantity applies locally to the selected wall surface and to the
selected ion species, with contributions summed over all of that species'
ionization states. It includes particles moving toward and reaching the
wall, but excludes emitted particles, neutral particles, other ion species,
and charge-state-resolved values.

It is the charge-state sum represented by the [ion charge-state particle
flux at the wall](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall). Unlike the
[incident ion energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:incident_ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
it counts arriving particles without weighting them by deposited or carried
energy.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Incident fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Incident neutral particle flux at the wall is the wall-integrated arrival
rate of neutral particles of one specified species moving from the plasma
side toward plasma-facing material. It excludes neutral particles emitted by
the wall.
NAMES.long:
Incident neutral particle flux at the wall is the wall-integrated rate at
which neutral particles of one specified species arrive at plasma-facing
material from the plasma side. It counts incoming neutral particles crossing
the material boundary toward the wall, not particles emitted by the wall.

The wall-integrated arrival rate is the surface integral of the
corresponding local incident flux:

$$
\dot{N}_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{A_\mathrm{wall}} \Gamma_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x})\, dA
$$

where $\dot{N}_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ denotes this incident
neutral particle flux at the wall, $A_\mathrm{wall}$ is the plasma-facing
wall surface included in the total,
$\Gamma_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the incident
component of the local neutral particle flux at the wall for the same
neutral species at wall position $\mathbf{x}$, and $dA$ is the surface-area
element.

The quantity is species-resolved for one neutral species and aggregated over
wall position by surface integration. It is not the local per-area neutral
particle flux at the wall at a given wall position, and it is not a signed
net balance between incoming and outgoing neutrals.

Wall-emitted neutral particles belong to the opposite direction of exchange
and are represented separately by quantities such as [neutral particle flux
at the wall due to surface
emission](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
Contributions from disjoint wall regions add to form the global incident
rate.

sources.leaf_definition: Particle flux from the plasma for that species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the various neutral species

NAMES.name: ion_average_temperature_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge
states on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, providing the ion component
of the local average plasma temperature.
NAMES.long:
The ion component of the local plasma temperature at a limiter is the
density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all positive ion species and
charge states on the plasma-facing side of the limiter. It is the
ion-specific component of average temperature at the limiter.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q} T_{s,q}}{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q}}
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes their positive charge states,
$n_{s,q}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and $T_{s,q}$ is its
kinetic temperature. The denominator is the [total ion density at the
limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter).

This quantity includes all ion species and charge states in the local plasma
population and excludes electrons, neutral particles, and the solid limiter
material. It is distinct from temperature at the limiter, which may denote a
specified population or a different population aggregation.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Outgoing recombination energy flux at the wall is the emitted energy per
unit area and time attributable to a specified incident-ion species and
charge state.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination is the
outgoing energy transfer associated with surface recombination of a
specified incident-ion species and charge state. The charge-state label
identifies the incident ion responsible for recombination, not the charge
state of an emitted product.

The local emitted energy flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{W,s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}}{\partial A\,\partial t}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}$ is the outgoing recombination
energy flux attributable to incident-ion species $s$ and charge state $Z$,
$W_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{em,rec}}$ is the corresponding cumulative emitted
recombination-associated energy, $A$ is wall area, and $t$ is time. The
superscripts $\mathrm{em}$ and $\mathrm{rec}$ denote emission and
recombination, respectively.

The quantity applies locally at the wall, with incident-ion species and
charge state held fixed. Recombination channels and emitted product species
and states are summed; incident-ion species and charge states are not. It is
an energy flux per unit area, not a wall-integrated power, and excludes
energy transferred through non-recombination channels.

Summing over incident-ion species and charge states gives the [ion energy
flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), the
ion-associated contribution to the broader [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). Unlike the
[incident-ion recombination energy
flux](name:incident_ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), this
quantity describes energy emitted from the wall rather than energy delivered
to it. It is neither incoming kinetic-energy flux nor an
incident-minus-emitted net balance.

NAMES.name: ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Outgoing energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident
plasma ions recombine at the surface, restricted to the ion-associated
channel and summed over incident-ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at
which recombination-associated energy from incident plasma ions leaves a
plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the ion-associated component
summed over incident-ion species and charge states, not the incident plasma
energy flux or energy deposited in the wall material.

The aggregate is defined from charge-state-resolved components by:

$$
Q_{\mathrm{rec,ion}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{s,q} Q_{\mathrm{rec},s,q}(\mathbf{x}_w)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_w$ is the wall location, $s$ identifies an incident-ion
species, $q$ identifies its charge state, and $Q_{\mathrm{rec},s,q}$ is the
corresponding [ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).
The sum includes all represented incident-ion species and charge states.

As a component of [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), this quantity
retains only the ion-associated energy channel. Unlike particle flux at the
wall due to recombination, it weights the outgoing recombination
contribution by carried energy; it is distinct from incident [ion kinetic
energy flux at the wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall).

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: incident_ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Incident ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination is the energy
delivered per unit wall area by ions that strike the wall and recombine
there. It is summed over ion species and charge states and excludes
kinetic-energy flux and emitted-particle contributions.
NAMES.long:
Incident ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination is the
wall-directed energy transfer associated with ions that arrive at a material
wall and recombine there. It represents the recombination-energy channel
only, not the ions' translational kinetic-energy flux or other wall
energy-transfer mechanisms.

The quantity is defined as the species- and charge-state-summed
recombination-energy flux of incident ions:

$$
q_{\mathrm{rec},i}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \sum_s \sum_Z \Gamma_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{inc}} \, \epsilon_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{rec}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{rec},i}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident ion energy flux at
the wall due to recombination, $s$ indexes ion species, $Z$ indexes charge
states, $\Gamma_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the particle flux of incident ions
of species $s$ and charge state $Z$ to the wall, and
$\epsilon_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{rec}}$ is the recombination energy delivered to the
wall per such incident ion.

The scope is local material wall surfaces and incident ions only. The
aggregation convention is summation over all ion species and all charge
states represented in the ion population. The quantity excludes neutral and
electron recombination-energy contributions, particles emitted from the
wall, kinetic-energy flux, radiation, and other non-recombination energy
channels.

Within the recombination energy-flux decomposition, this quantity is the
incident-ion component related to the [ion energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). The
corresponding [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) is the broader
recombination-channel quantity over the particle classes included in that
decomposition. These relationships are aggregations over species, charge
states, or particle classes; they do not define an incident-minus-emitted
net balance.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Incident fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Incident kinetic-energy power flux delivered by all plasma ions striking a
plasma-facing wall, summed over ion species and charge states and excluding
electrons and neutrals.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the ion-resolved component of the incident kinetic-energy
flux at a plasma-facing wall. It contributes to the parent kinetic energy
flux at wall and includes all incident ion species and charge states, but
excludes electron, neutral-particle, radiative, and electromagnetic
contributions.

For an outward wall normal $\hat{n}$ directed from the material into the
plasma, the flux is defined by

$$
q_{i}^{\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}<0} \frac{1}{2}m_s |\mathbf{v}|^2 (-\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species and charge states, $m_s$ is the ion mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_s$ is the incident velocity
distribution. The minus sign converts the inward particle velocity into a
positive arrival flux; the resulting quantity is non-negative.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Incident fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Iron ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all ionization stages and
excluding neutral iron atoms.
NAMES.long:
Iron density at a limiter is the local number density of iron ions in the
boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The
evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance, consistent with the parent
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). Unless a single ionization
stage is specified in context, this quantity is summed over all iron charge
states from Fe$^{1+}$ to Fe$^{26+}$, excluding neutral iron atoms.

The total iron ion number density at the limiter is defined as:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of iron in charge
state $z$.

Iron enters the edge plasma primarily through physical sputtering of
metallic plasma-facing components by energetic ions and charge-exchange
neutrals impacting the limiter surface. At the limiter, where open
scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the material boundary, sputtered
iron atoms are ionized within a thin ionization front and become subject to
parallel and cross-field impurity transport. The local iron ion density at
the limiter characterizes the impurity source strength at this plasma-wall
interface and serves as a boundary condition for edge impurity transport
modeling. It connects to
[iron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:iron_density_at_plasma_boundary) and
[iron_density_at_divertor_target](name:iron_density_at_divertor_target),
which describe the same impurity density evaluated at different
plasma-facing surfaces.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short:
Kinetic-energy power flux density carried away from a plasma-facing surface
by emitted particles, including ions and electrons and aggregated over
species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by
particles emitted from a plasma-facing surface through sputtering,
reflection, secondary emission, or related surface-emission processes. It
includes all emitted particle species and charge states, rather than
selecting a particular ion or charge state.

The kinetic-energy flux density is defined by

$$
q_{\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ indexes emitted particle species and charge states, $m_s$ is
particle mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity in m/s,
$v=|\mathbf{v}|$, $\mathbf{n}$ is the outward surface-normal unit vector,
and $f_s$ is the emitted-particle velocity distribution. The outward
condition excludes particles incident on the surface. This is the kinetic
component of [energy flux at wall due to surface
emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), excluding
particle potential-energy contributions and photon or other radiative
energy; [ion charge-state kinetic energy flux at wall due to surface
emission](name:ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission)
is a charge-state-resolved instance.

NAMES.name: electron_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Kinetic-energy power carried away per unit wall area by electrons emitted
from a plasma-facing surface after passage through the sheath.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by
electrons released from a plasma-facing wall through surface-emission
processes. It represents energy transported by the emitted electron
population after sheath transmission.

The emitted electron kinetic-energy flux density is related to the emitted
particle flux and the mean kinetic energy per emitted electron by

$$
q_{\mathrm{e,kin}}^{\mathrm{em}} = \Gamma_{\mathrm e}^{\mathrm{em}}\,\overline{E}_{\mathrm{kin,e}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{e,kin}}^{\mathrm{em}}$ is this kinetic-energy flux
density, $\Gamma_{\mathrm e}^{\mathrm{em}}$ is the [electron particle flux
due to surface
emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), and
$\overline{E}_{\mathrm{kin,e}}$ is the mean kinetic energy carried by each
emitted electron.

The quantity applies specifically to emitted electrons at the wall surface
and is aggregated over the emitted electron population, rather than
representing an individual electron energy or a spatial maximum. It excludes
energy carried by incident electrons, emitted ions, emitted photons, and
non-kinetic energy of emitted electrons.

It is the electron kinetic contribution to the broader [energy flux at the
wall due to surface
emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), which also
includes other emitted energy channels. It is distinct from the incident
wall energy represented by energy flux at the wall and from the
corresponding emitted-ion quantity [ion kinetic energy flux at the wall due
to surface
emission](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when kinetic energy is carried away from the wall
into the plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Kinetic-energy power flux density carried by ions in a specified charge
state leaving a plasma-facing surface through sputtering, reflection, or
related surface-emission processes.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by ions in
a specified species and charge state emitted from a plasma-facing surface
through sputtering, reflection, or related surface-emission processes.

The charge-state-resolved kinetic-energy flux density is defined by

$$
q_{\mathrm{kin},s} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the selected ion species and charge state, $m_s$ is its
particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$,
$\mathbf{n}$ is the outward surface-normal unit vector, and $f_s$ is its
emitted-particle velocity distribution. The outward condition excludes
particles incident on the surface.

This is one charge-state contribution to [kinetic-energy flux at wall due to
surface emission](name:kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
excluding other ion charge states, electrons, particle potential energy,
photons, and other radiative energy. The ion-aggregated quantity [ion
kinetic-energy flux at wall due to surface
emission](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) sums
this contribution over ion species and charge states.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Kinetic energy flux density carried by ions leaving the plasma-facing wall
through surface emission processes such as physical sputtering and ion
backscattering.
NAMES.long:
The kinetic energy flux density at the plasma-facing wall surface carried by
ions emitted outward via surface emission — the family of plasma–wall
interaction processes, including physical sputtering, chemical sputtering,
and ion backscattering, that return ionic species from the wall to the
plasma. The `kinetic` qualifier restricts this to translational kinetic
energy of the emitted ion velocity distribution, excluding potential energy
stored in electronic excitation or residual ionization charge, which is
captured separately by
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

The emitted kinetic energy flux $\Phi_{\mathrm{kin,emit}}$ sums over all
emitted ion species $s$:

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{kin,emit}} = \sum_s \int_{v_n > 0} \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2 \, v_n \, f_{s,\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion mass of species $s$, $v = |\mathbf{v}|$ is the ion
speed, $v_n > 0$ is the outward surface-normal velocity component at the
wall, and $f_{s,\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution
function of emitted ions.

In plasma–surface interaction modeling, this flux is evaluated by convolving
incident plasma conditions with energy-resolved surface emission yields and
backscattering coefficients from binary-collision approximation databases.
It is the mechanism-attributed form of ion_energy_flux_at_wall and the
emitted counterpart to
[ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall),
which captures the incident kinetic flux. Charge-state-resolved
contributions are tracked by ion_state_energy_flux_at_wall, and the electron
analog is
[electron_energy_flux_at_wall](name:electron_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Krypton ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all krypton ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Krypton density at a limiter is the local number density of krypton ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance at the plasma–limiter contact, where open scrape-off-layer field
lines terminate on the material boundary.

Unless a single charge state is explicitly specified, the quantity
represents the charge-state-summed total:

$$
n_\mathrm{Kr} = \sum_{q=1}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the number density of krypton ions in
ionization state $q$, ranging from $q = 1$ (singly ionized) to $q = 36$
(fully stripped). Neutral krypton atoms are excluded from this quantity.

Krypton is a high-$Z$ noble gas ($Z = 36$) injected as a seeding impurity to
enhance radiative dissipation in the scrape-off layer, redistributing heat
load away from plasma-facing components. Its local density at the limiter
characterizes krypton availability for charge exchange, ionization, and
plasma–material interactions at the wall. Even modest krypton concentrations
significantly elevate
[effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) due to its
high nuclear charge.

Within the [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) family, krypton
density serves as a heavier-impurity counterpart to lighter noble-gas seeds
such as [argon_density_at_limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter), and
contrasts with fuel-ion species such as
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter). Under
quasi-neutrality, the charge-weighted sum of all ion densities at the
limiter equals
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Local number density of lithium ions in the boundary plasma immediately
adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive
ionization states and excluding neutral lithium atoms.
NAMES.long:
Lithium density at a limiter is the local number density of lithium ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or
sheath entrance.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density in m$^{-3}$,
$N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the counted number of lithium ions, $V$ is volume in
m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the evaluation position in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius in m, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle in radians, and $Z$ is vertical height in m.

The quantity is summed over all positive lithium ionization states and
excludes neutral lithium atoms. It is the lithium-specific specialization of
[density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and differs from the broader
ion density at a limiter, which does not select lithium.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Neon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all neon ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Neon density at a limiter is the local number density of neon ions in the
boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The
evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance at the limiter contact, not the magnetic separatrix, consistent
with the parent [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter).

Unless a charge-state-resolved quantity specifies a particular ionization
stage, this density is summed over all positive neon charge states
($\mathrm{Ne}^{1+}$ through $\mathrm{Ne}^{10+}$):

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z=1}^{10} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of neon ions in
charge state $z$.

Neon is introduced as a controlled radiative impurity for power exhaust and
divertor detachment. At the limiter, the local neon density governs
recycling fluxes, charge-exchange with neutral neon, and impurity-driven
edge plasma cooling near the wall. Edge Langmuir probes and vacuum
ultraviolet or extreme ultraviolet spectroscopy provide experimental access
to this quantity.

The neon density in the scrape-off layer at neon-seeded discharges spans
roughly $10^{16}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$, falling toward the lower end at low
seeding rates and rising with neon puff level. The corresponding quantity
evaluated at the separatrix is
[neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:neon_density_at_plasma_boundary);
[xenon_density_at_limiter](name:xenon_density_at_limiter) is the analogous
quantity for xenon impurity injection.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: neutral_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Incident neutral energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area carried by
neutral particles associated with recombination at the surface, summed over
incident-ion species, incident-ion charge states, recombination channels,
neutral species, and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at
which recombination-associated energy carried by neutral particles is
incident on a plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the
neutral-particle carrier of energy associated with recombination or
neutralization processes at the boundary, not the outgoing neutral emission
from the surface.

The incident neutral recombination energy flux at wall location
$\mathbf{x}_w$ is defined as the energy moment of the incident neutral
particle-flux distribution:

$$
Q_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{i,\,\zeta,\,c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{in}\,\frac{d\Gamma^{\mathrm{inc}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{in}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{in})\,dE_\mathrm{in}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident neutral energy
flux at the wall due to recombination, $\mathbf{x}_w$ is a wall-surface
location, the subscript $n$ denotes the neutral-particle channel, the
superscript $\mathrm{inc}$ denotes the incident wall-crossing direction, $i$
identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion charge state,
$c$ the surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$ the neutral
species, $k$ the neutral internal state, $E_\mathrm{in}$ the energy carried
by a neutral particle crossing the surface in the incident direction, and
$d\Gamma^{\mathrm{inc}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{in}$ the corresponding
incident neutral particle-flux distribution with respect to $E_\mathrm{in}$.
For discrete incident-neutral energies, the integral is replaced by the
corresponding sum.

This quantity applies to neutral particles crossing the plasma-facing
surface toward the material. It is aggregated over incident-ion species,
incident-ion charge states, recombination or neutralization channels,
neutral species, and neutral internal states; no neutral species, state,
incident-ion species, or charge-state resolution remains. It excludes
ion-carried energy flux, photon or radiation energy flux, outgoing neutral
recombination products, and the subsequent partition of incident energy into
wall heating, reflection, or re-emission.

This quantity is the energy-weighted counterpart of [incident neutral
particle flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which counts the same incident neutral population without weighting by
$E_\mathrm{in}$. It is directionally distinct from [neutral particle flux at
the wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which refers to outgoing neutral recombination products, and it is not the
total [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). [Ion energy
flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) describes
the ion-associated channel rather than neutral-carried incident energy.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral particles carrying
recombination-associated energy cross the plasma-facing surface from the
plasma-facing volume toward the material surface.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Incident fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral particles in a
specified internal quantum state as they arrive at a plasma-facing wall.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral
atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state as they cross onto
a plasma-facing wall. It includes only translational kinetic energy and only
particles moving from the plasma toward the wall.

$$
q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w<0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\left(-\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w\right) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

Here $q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident kinetic-energy flux
density, $s$ identifies the internal quantum state, $m_s$ is the particle
mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity relative to the wall, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w$ is
the unit normal directed from the wall toward the plasma, and
$f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of that state. Unlike
[neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall),
this quantity weights arrivals by translational kinetic energy;
neutral_energy_flux_at_wall aggregates the corresponding kinetic-energy flux
over internal states. Internal excitation, potential, and rest-mass energies
are excluded.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Incident fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Outgoing neutral internal-state particle number flux density at a
plasma-facing wall due to recombination, resolved by neutral product species
and internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
Outgoing neutral internal-state particle number flux density at a
plasma-facing wall due to recombination is the surface flux density of
neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state that are
produced by recombination at the wall and cross the wall surface away from
the wall. It is resolved by neutral product species and by the internal
quantum state of that product.

For neutral product species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, with
$\hat{\mathbf n}_w$ the unit normal directed from the wall material into the
adjacent plasma, the outgoing recombination contribution is defined by

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{rec,out}}_{n,\alpha} = \int_{\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w > 0} (\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w)\, f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}(\mathbf v)\, d^3\mathbf v
$$

where $\mathbf v$ is neutral-particle velocity and
$f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}$ is the velocity-space distribution function at
the wall for neutral recombination products of species $n$ in internal state
$\alpha$, normalized so that its velocity integral gives the corresponding
local neutral-product number density.

This quantity includes only the emitted, outward wall-normal component of
neutral recombination products in the specified internal state. Aggregating
over internal states for the same neutral product species gives the [neutral
particle flux at wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); the
broader internal-state-resolved recombination-flux family is internal state
particle flux at wall due to recombination. The distinct inward wall-normal
counterpart is [incident neutral internal-state particle flux at wall due to
recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination)
and is not included here.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral recombination products cross the wall
surface in the direction of the wall normal from the wall material into the
adjacent plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Number flux density of neutral recombination products in a specified
internal quantum state arriving at a plasma-facing wall surface.
NAMES.long:
Incident internal-state neutral particle flux due to recombination is the
density of neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state
that arrive at a plasma-facing wall surface from the plasma-facing side. It
is a particle-count flux, not an energy flux.

The incident flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}^{(s)} = \frac{\mathrm{d}N_{\mathrm{inc}}^{(s)}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{inc}}^{(s)}$ is the number of incident neutral
recombination products in internal state $s$, $A$ is wall surface area, and
$t$ is time.

This quantity selects the incident direction and the specified internal
state from the state-resolved wall particle flux represented by [neutral
internal-state particle flux at wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).
It excludes particles in other internal states and differs from the
state-summed [incident neutral particle flux at wall due to
recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Incident fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Rate at which particles of a specified neutral species are removed from the
plasma region by wall pumping, giving global neutral-particle exhaust
throughput.
NAMES.long:
The rate at which particles of a specified neutral species are removed from
the plasma region by wall pumping is the global scalar representation of the
wall particle-removal flux. It describes pumped neutral-particle exhaust at
material surfaces due only to pumping.

The pumped neutral-particle flux is defined as the removal term in the
neutral-particle inventory balance:

$$
\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}} = -\left.\frac{dN_n}{dt}\right|_{\mathrm{pump}}
$$

where $\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ is the neutral particle flux at the wall due
to pumping, $N_n$ is the total particle inventory of the specified neutral
species in the plasma region, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to one specified neutral species and is aggregated
globally over the wall pumping interface. It is not summed over different
neutral species and does not include ionized-particle exhaust, recycling or
sputtering sources, neutralization sources, or particle losses not
attributed to wall pumping.

This flux is the neutral-species member of the broader [particle flux at
wall due to pumping](name:particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping) family and
is distinct from the [electron-equivalent particle flux at wall due to
pumping](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping). It is the
removal rate itself, not a pumping-speed or first-order loss coefficient; if
a model represents pumping by a coefficient $S_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ acting on
$N_n$, then $\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ is related to that model by
$\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}} = S_{n,\mathrm{pump}} N_n$, where
$S_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ is the neutral-species pumping coefficient.

sources.leaf_definition: Pumped particle flux for that species
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the various neutral species

NAMES.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Outgoing neutral-particle number flux density from recombination at a
plasma-facing wall, summed over emitted neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Recombination-associated neutral particle flux at a plasma-facing wall is
the rate per unit wall area at which neutral products leave the surface and
enter the adjacent plasma. It counts particles rather than the energy or
momentum they carry.

The flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outgoing
recombination-associated neutral particle-number flux density,
$N_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the corresponding number of emitted
neutral particles, $A$ is plasma-facing wall area, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to neutral products generated when incident plasma ions
recombine or neutralize at the wall. It is summed over contributing
incident-ion species and charge states, recombination channels, emitted
neutral species, and emitted internal states. It excludes energy weighting
and therefore differs from
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

This neutral emitted-particle quantity is the neutral-product specialization
of particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination. It is distinct from
[incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which counts recombination-associated neutral particles arriving at the
wall, and from
[neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which resolves the emitted flux by internal state.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral particles travel from the
plasma-facing wall into the adjacent plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Incident number flux density of neutral recombination products arriving at a
plasma-facing wall, summed over neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the incoming neutral-particle count flux at a wall
attributable to recombination, with neutral product species and internal
states aggregated. It selects particles arriving at the surface, rather than
neutral particles emitted from it.

The incident flux density is defined from the recombination-attributed
neutral distribution by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{rec}}(\mathbf{x}_w)=\int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}<0} \left|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right| f_{\mathrm{n,rec}}(\mathbf{x}_w,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_w$ is the wall position, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the outward
wall normal, $\mathbf{v}$ is neutral-particle velocity, and
$f_{\mathrm{n,rec}}$ is the recombination-attributed neutral distribution
summed over species and internal states.

This incident quantity is distinct from the outgoing emission described by
[neutral particle flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). A
state-resolved counterpart, [incident neutral internal-state particle flux
at the wall due to
recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
retains the internal-state distinction.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Nitrogen ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all ionization states and
excluding neutral nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen density at a limiter is the local number density of nitrogen ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance, where the limiter terminates open field lines
in the scrape-off layer.

The charge-state-summed density is defined from the velocity distribution
functions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} \int f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $q$ is the positive nitrogen ion charge state, $q_{\max}$ is the
highest included ionization state, and $f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is
the velocity distribution function of that ion state at the evaluation
point.

This is the nitrogen-specific component of
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It excludes neutral nitrogen
and is distinct from
[neon_density_at_limiter](name:neon_density_at_limiter), which applies the
same boundary definition to neon ions.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Oxygen density at a limiter is the local number density of oxygen ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface,
summed over all oxygen ionization states from O+ through O8+ and excluding
neutral oxygen atoms.
NAMES.long:
Oxygen density at a limiter is the local number density of oxygen ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or
sheath entrance at the limiter. It is summed over all oxygen ionization
states from O$^+$ through O$^{8+}$, and excludes neutral oxygen atoms.

For oxygen ion charge states from singly ionized to fully stripped, the
charge-state-summed limiter density is defined as:

$$
n_{\mathrm{O},\mathrm{lim}} = \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+},\mathrm{lim}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O},\mathrm{lim}}$ is the oxygen ion density at the
limiter, $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+},\mathrm{lim}}$ is the local density of oxygen
ions with charge state $q$, and the upper limit is the nuclear charge of
oxygen.

This quantity is species-specific and charge-state-summed; it is not the
neutral oxygen density,
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter), or
[total_ion_density_at_limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter). At the
sheath entrance, oxygen charge-state densities contribute to quasineutrality
through their charge-weighted sum and to the local effective charge. The
analogous oxygen density at divertor target surfaces is
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short:
Particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through
surface-emission processes and directed from the wall material into the
plasma.
NAMES.long:
Particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through
surface-emission processes is the surface-normal rate density of particles
generated by the wall material and carried into the plasma.

The emitted particle flux density is defined by:

$$
F_N^{\mathrm{emit}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}N_{\mathrm{emit}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $F_N^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted particle-number flux density,
$N_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the number of particles emitted, $A$ is emitting wall
area, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to emitted electrons, selected ion species, and
neutral particles. For an ion-species quantity, the particle number is
summed over all ionization states; the parent does not require summation
across distinct particle species. It is a local flux density per wall area,
not a total emission rate integrated over the wall, and excludes particles
incident on the wall and the resulting net wall flux.

This is the particle-number specialization of
[flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission)
and is the common abstraction for
[electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
[ion_species_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:ion_species_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
and
[neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
Unlike
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
it counts emitted particles rather than the energy they carry.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the emitted particle flux is directed from
the wall material into the plasma.

NAMES.name: ion_species_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: ion_species
NAMES.short:
Number flux density of ions from a selected species emitted by a
plasma-facing wall through surface-emission processes, summed over all
ionization states and directed into the plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local rate at which ions of one selected species leave
a plasma-facing wall through surface-emission processes, expressed per unit
wall area. It represents the emitted component of particle exchange rather
than the total or net ion exchange at the wall.

The local emitted particle flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{em}} = \frac{dN_{i,\mathrm{em}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{em}}$ is the emitted ion particle flux density,
$N_{i,\mathrm{em}}$ is the number of emitted ions of the selected species,
$A$ is wall surface area, $t$ is time, the subscript $i$ identifies the
selected ion species, and the subscript $\mathrm{em}$ identifies the
surface-emission contribution.

The quantity applies locally at a plasma-facing wall and is summed over all
positive ionization states of the selected species. It excludes neutral
particles and has no spatial maximum, surface integral, or spatial average
over the wall.

Unlike the [ion charge-state particle flux at the
wall](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall), which describes ions
incident on the wall in a specified charge state, this quantity describes
ions leaving the wall and is not the net difference between incident and
emitted flux. The corresponding emitted-electron quantity, [electron
particle flux at the wall due to surface
emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
applies the same wall-local process distinction to electrons.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through surface-emission processes and directed from the wall material into
the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Neutral particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through surface-emission processes is the surface-normal rate density of
neutral particles generated by the wall material and carried into the
plasma.

The emitted neutral particle flux density is defined by:

$$
F_N^{\mathrm{emit}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}N_{\mathrm{emit}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $F_N^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted neutral particle-number flux
density, $N_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the number of emitted neutral particles, $A$
is the emitting wall area, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to the emitted neutral-particle population at the wall
and is aggregated over the neutral particles represented by that population,
without combining them with emitted electrons or ions. It is a local flux
density per wall area, not a total emission rate integrated over the wall,
and excludes neutral particles incident on the wall and the resulting net
wall flux.

This is the neutral-particle specialization of
[particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
It counts emitted particles rather than their carried energy, unlike
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
and complements the emitted electron quantity
[electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
It is distinct from
[incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall),
which describes neutral particles arriving at the wall.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the emitted neutral particle flux is directed
from the wall material into the plasma.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Emitted fluxes for various wall components (grid subsets)

NAMES.name: plasma_power_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short:
Power deposited on plasma-facing wall surfaces when incident plasma ions
recombine at the material boundary, representing the ion-channel
contribution to total wall recombination power.
NAMES.long:
Plasma-ion recombination power at the wall is the rate at which
recombination energy from incident plasma ions is deposited in plasma-facing
wall material. It is the ion-channel contribution to the total wall heat
load from recombination.

The contribution is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{rec,wall}}^{\mathrm{plasma}} = \sum_s \int_A \Gamma_s^{\mathrm{ion}} E_{\mathrm{rec},s}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $s$ indexes the contributing plasma-ion species and charge states,
$\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the incident particle flux,
$E_{\mathrm{rec},s}$ is the recombination energy deposited per event, and
$A$ is the total plasma-facing wall area.

This quantity excludes surface recombination of incident neutral particles
into molecules, represented by neutral recombination power at the wall.
Together, the two channels form total recombination power at the wall, which
is distinct from volumetric [power due to
recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination).

sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the wall due to recombination of plasma ions
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: power_at_wall_due_to_ohmic_dissipation
NAMES.short:
Resistive Joule-heating power deposited in conducting wall structures by
induced or halo currents flowing through them.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the rate of irreversible electrical-energy conversion into
heat within conducting wall and vessel structures, caused by currents
flowing through those structures.

For the conducting wall domain, the ohmic power is defined by

$$
P_{\rm wall}^{\rm ohm} = \int_{V_{\rm wall}} \eta\,\lvert\mathbf{J}\rvert^2\,dV
$$

where $P_{\rm wall}^{\rm ohm}$ is the wall ohmic power, $V_{\rm wall}$ is
the conducting wall volume, $\eta$ is the electrical resistivity of the wall
material, and $\mathbf{J}$ is the current-density vector.

The quantity aggregates resistive heating over the conducting wall and
vessel structures as a single deposited power. It includes Joule heating
from induced currents and halo currents, but excludes ohmic dissipation in
the plasma or other conducting domains and excludes wall power deposited
through thermal conduction, radiation, or particle transport without
resistive current dissipation.

This is the wall-locus specialization of [total ohmic-dissipation
power](name:total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation), which aggregates
irreversible electrical-energy conversion over the complete applicable
conducting domain rather than only the wall structures. The resistivity
governing the integrand is the [electrical resistivity of wall
material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material).
