NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity
for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial
projection.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity
for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial
projection. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the
diffusive particle flux component of that charge state to the negative
directional gradient of its number density.

For a chosen projection direction $\hat{\mathbf{e}}$, the defining Fickian
relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e} = -D_s\,\nabla_e n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e}$ is the projected diffusive particle
flux density of charge state $s$, $D_s$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the
number density of charge state $s$, and $\nabla_e n_s =
\hat{\mathbf{e}}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is the directional derivative of that
number density. A positive flux component is directed along
$+\hat{\mathbf{e}}$; the minus sign makes a positive diffusivity drive
diffusive flux opposite to the projected density gradient.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved: it applies to a single ionization
state rather than to the density-weighted mean over all charge states
represented by ion diffusivity. It is the same physical coefficient as [ion
charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when that name is
used for the same Fickian closure. Directionally specified counterparts
include [radial ion charge-state
diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and [parallel ion
charge-state diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_diffusivity);
convective or pinch transport, particle sources and sinks, and energy or
momentum transport coefficients are separate quantities.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Ion charge-state energy flux is the net conductive and convective energy
transport per unit area and time in a specified direction for one ion
species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state energy flux is the signed net energy transported through an
oriented surface per unit area and time by ions of one species in one
specified charge state. It includes conductive and convective contributions
to that population's energy transport.

The local directional flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,z}^{(\hat{\mathbf n})} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{i,z}^{\mathrm{cross}}}{\partial A\,\partial t} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,z}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $z$ identifies its charge state,
$\Gamma_{i,z}^{(\hat{\mathbf n})}$ is the directional energy flux,
$W_{i,z}^{\mathrm{cross}}$ is the cumulative net energy carried across the
surface patch by those ions, $A$ is the patch area, $t$ is time,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,z}$ is their energy-flux-density vector, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the selected positive unit normal.

This quantity is not summed over ion species or charge states and excludes
energy carried by electrons or neutrals. It is a signed projection, not a
vector magnitude or surface-integrated power. Unlike the [ion charge-state
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), it
represents transported energy rather than a coefficient relating the
diffusive contribution to a temperature gradient.

No particular surface orientation is fixed by this parent definition. The
[radial component](name:radial_ion_charge_state_energy_flux) selects the
major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height. The [parallel
component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux) instead selects the
local magnetic-field direction. Summing the charge-state-resolved fluxes
over all ion species and charge states, using the same projection direction,
gives the corresponding component of [total ion energy
flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net energy transport by the specified ions
crosses the surface in the selected direction $\hat{\mathbf n}$.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Lower-bound charge number is the smallest ionic charge number included in a
specified charge-state bundle of a single ion species.
NAMES.long:
Lower-bound charge specifies the inclusive lower endpoint of the ionization
charge-number range represented by a charge-state bundle of one ion species.
It identifies the bundle's extent independently of the relative populations
of its constituent charge states.

The lower bound is defined by:

$$
Z_{\min} = \min_{Z \in \mathcal{B}} Z
$$

where $Z_{\min}$ is the lower-bound charge number and $\mathcal{B}$ is the
set of ionic charge numbers represented by the bundle. Each $Z$ is an ionic
charge number defined by $Z=q/e$, where $q$ is the net electric charge per
particle and $e$ is the positive elementary charge. This is [normalized
particle charge](name:normalized_particle_charge) with the reference charge
chosen as $e$.

Together with the [maximum charge
number](name:ion_state_maximum_charge_number), denoted $Z_{\max}$, the lower
bound delimits the included range through $Z_{\min}\leq Z\leq Z_{\max}$. A
single resolved charge state has $Z_{\min}=Z_{\max}$; for a neutral state,
both bounds are zero.

The lower bound is not a population-weighted [charge-number moment of the
bundle](name:ion_charge_state_charge_number), a sum over charge states, or
the [nuclear charge number](name:ion_atomic_number), which counts protons
rather than net ionic charge.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of
momentum carried by a specified ion species and charge state, distinct from
its bulk flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective,
non-diffusive transport of momentum for a specified ion species and charge
state. It is a transport closure quantity, not the actual bulk flow velocity
of that ion charge state.

For each selected momentum component and transport direction, the convective
momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv}} P
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum
flux, $V_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the momentum convection velocity, and $P$ is
the corresponding momentum density. The generic momentum convection velocity
uses the same closure relation across momentum populations.

This charge-state-resolved quantity applies to one ion charge state and
excludes summation over other charge states. Its vector may be resolved into
radial, poloidal, toroidal, vertical, or field-aligned components; unlike
energy convection velocity, it transports momentum rather than energy. It is
distinct from the ion charge state's material flow velocity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the associated convective momentum flux is in
the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported momentum
density.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity multiplying the density of a specified ion charge state
in its convective cross-field particle transport.
NAMES.long:
The ion-charge-state particle convection velocity is the effective
coefficient of the density-proportional, convective contribution to
transport of a specified ion charge state across magnetic flux surfaces. It
is the ion-charge-state specialization of particle convection velocity, not
a velocity magnitude.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_s v_s^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective particle flux of the
specified ion charge state, $n_s$ is its particle number density, and
$v_s^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection velocity.

This quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and is
not summed over other ion charge states. The magnitude-only counterpart
[ion-state particle convection velocity
magnitude](name:ion_state_particle_convection_velocity_magnitude) removes
the directional sign.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the convective particle flux of the specified
ion charge state follows the positive orientation assigned to the underlying
transport coordinate.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net flow of thermal and
nonthermal ions of one species and charge state through an oriented surface
per unit area and time.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state particle flux is the net number flow of ions of one
specified species and ionization charge state through an oriented surface
per unit area and time. It includes thermal and nonthermal ions without
selecting a fixed geometric or magnetic-field direction.

For a local oriented surface, the defining particle-number moment is:

$$
\Gamma_{s,q} = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})\,f_{s,q}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_{s,q}$ is the particle flux for ion species $s$ and ionic
charge number $q$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen surface-normal unit
vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,q}$ is the
particle-number distribution in position and velocity for that species and
charge state. The symbols $\mathbf{x}$ and $t$ denote position and time, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element; the integral includes all
velocities.

Thermal and nonthermal contributions are added within the specified charge
state, but different charge states are not summed. The quantity counts
particles rather than their charge or energy. It is a net flux density, not
a surface-integrated crossing rate or a one-way incident flux. No spatial
averaging is intrinsic to the general definition; the flux-surface-normal
specialization additionally uses a surface average.

Summing over all ionic charge states of the same species, with the same
orientation and averaging convention, gives the [ion particle
flux](name:ion_particle_flux). The [parallel
component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) selects the local
magnetic-field direction as the surface normal, whereas the [poloidal
component](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) selects the local
poloidal direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net ion transport follows the chosen
surface-normal direction.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Pressure of ions in a specified charge state combines thermal and nonthermal
random kinetic stresses without requiring an isotropic velocity
distribution.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of ions in a specified charge state is the isotropic part of their
kinetic pressure tensor, including both thermal and nonthermal populations.
It represents random kinetic stress rather than bulk-flow ram stress; for an
anisotropic population, the scalar pressure is one-third of the
pressure-tensor trace.

The total pressure of the specified ion charge state combines its thermal
and fast-ion contributions additively:

$$
p_{s,c} = p_{s,c}^{\mathrm{thermal}} + p_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $s$ labels the ion species, $c$ labels its ionic charge state,
$p_{s,c}$ is the combined charge-state pressure,
$p_{s,c}^{\mathrm{thermal}}$ is the [thermal ion charge-state
pressure](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure), and
$p_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the isotropic trace contribution of the
[fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure).

This quantity applies to one specified species and ionic charge state.
Thermal and nonthermal pressure contributions are added directly, not
density-weighted; there is no summation over other charge states or ion
species. Electron pressure is excluded, and the quantity is not restricted
to the thermal population alone.

The thermal contribution is isotropic. For a gyrotropic fast-ion population,
the scalar fast-ion contribution is one-third of the sum of its parallel
pressure and twice its perpendicular pressure. Thus, the combined scalar
pressure does not select either magnetic-field-relative component and does
not imply that those components are equal.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of
suprathermal ions in a specified ionization state, formed from velocity
fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is represented by the
parallel and perpendicular pressure components relative to the local
magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of
suprathermal ions for a specified ion species and ionization state, formed
from velocity fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is
represented by the pair of pressure components parallel and perpendicular to
the local magnetic-field direction; this pair parameterizes a gyrotropic
pressure tensor and is not a spatial vector.

The component pair is defined from the fast-ion distribution function by the
velocity-fluctuation moments:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}} \\
p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}
\end{pmatrix}
=
m_s \int f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})
\begin{pmatrix}
[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]^2 \\
\frac{1}{2}\left|(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})-[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]\mathbf{b}\right|^2
\end{pmatrix}
\, d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ and
$p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ are the pressure components for species $s$
in ionization state $q$, $m_s$ is the ion mass for species $s$,
$f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal part of the distribution
function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the mean flow velocity of the same
population, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field,
and the integral is over velocity space.

The scope is gyrotropic pressure: the two transverse directions
perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$ are averaged, so the perpendicular component
is one half of the transverse fluctuation moment. A fully non-gyrotropic
pressure tensor with unequal transverse components or off-diagonal terms is
outside this standard name. Because pressure is an extensive per-volume
velocity moment, aggregate [parallel fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure) are obtained by summing the
corresponding components over all fast-ion species and ionization states.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Angular velocity vector of a specified ion charge state, characterizing its
bulk rotational motion; each resolved component is determined from the
corresponding bulk-flow component and its geometric rotation lever arm.
NAMES.long:
Angular velocity vector of a specified ion charge state is the vector of
angular rates associated with the bulk flow of that charge-state population.
It is charge-state-resolved and excludes density-weighted averaging over
other charge states.

For any resolved angular coordinate $q$, the component is the corresponding
bulk-flow velocity component divided by the geometric rotation lever arm for
that coordinate:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{A}} \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}, \qquad \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta} = \frac{\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}}{h_q}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta}$ is the ion-charge-state
rotation-frequency vector, $i$ labels the ion species, $\zeta$ labels the
charge state, $\mathcal{A}$ is the set of resolved angular coordinate
directions, $\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}$ is the bulk velocity vector of the same
charge-state population, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}$ is the positive tangent
direction of angular coordinate $q$, and $h_q=|\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial
q|$ is its geometric rotation lever arm. For the toroidal component in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, $q=\phi$ and
$h_\phi=R$, so the component is the [toroidal ion-charge-state rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency).

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved counterpart of [ion rotation
frequency](name:ion_rotation_frequency). The charge-state-aggregated ion
quantity is the density-weighted mean over charge states, not a sum, because
rotation frequency is an intensive bulk-flow quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component corresponds to motion in
the positive tangent direction of its associated angular coordinate; in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the toroidal component is
positive for motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Temperature of ions in a specified charge state measures their random
translational kinetic energy after bulk flow is removed, rather than their
ionization or excitation energy.
NAMES.long:
Temperature of ions in a specified charge state is an energy-equivalent
measure of their random translational motion relative to that population's
bulk flow. It characterizes the selected ion population, not its internal
electronic energy.

For an individual charge state, the defining kinetic relation is

$$
T_s = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle E_{\mathrm{rand}}\right\rangle_s
$$

where $T_s$ is the energy-equivalent temperature, $s$ identifies the ion
species and charge state, $E_{\mathrm{rand}}$ is a particle's translational
kinetic energy relative to that population's bulk flow, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_s$ denotes a number-weighted average over particles in
that state.

The quantity is charge-state-resolved, rather than averaged over all charge
states or ion species. When the selected population is a defined
charge-state bundle, its temperature is the density-weighted mean over the
included charge states, not their sum. The species-level temperature is
instead the density-weighted mean over all its charge states. Bulk-flow
kinetic energy, ionization energy, and excitation energy are excluded.

For a thermal population, this temperature supplies the random kinetic
energy per particle entering the [thermal ion charge-state
pressure](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure). Unlike [plasma
temperature](name:plasma_temperature), it does not combine the electron and
ion populations into a single effective thermal state.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Mean bulk-flow velocity vector of ions belonging to one specified ionization
charge state, obtained from the first velocity moment of that charge-state
population.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state velocity is the mean translational velocity of ions in
a specified ionization charge state. It describes the charge-state-resolved
bulk flow and is distinct from the charge-state-averaged [ion
velocity](name:ion_velocity).

Let $f_Z(\mathbf{v})$ be the velocity distribution function for ions in
charge state $Z$, and let $n_Z$ be their number density. The velocity is
defined by

$$
\mathbf{u}_Z = \frac{1}{n_Z}\int \mathbf{v}\,f_Z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}, \qquad n_Z = \int f_Z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_Z$ is the charge-state bulk velocity and $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity. The vector may be resolved into directional projections,
including the [radial ion charge-state
velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity), without summing or
averaging over other ionization states.
NAMES.sign:
Positive components point along the corresponding positive
directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number
density of a specified ion species, charge state, or population; a
species-level quantity without an explicit charge state is summed over all
charge states. It is not electric charge density or mass density.
NAMES.long:
Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number
density of the specified ion species, charge state, or population. It counts
ions as particles and is distinct from electric charge density and mass
density. For a species-level quantity without an explicit charge state, the
density is summed over all charge states of that species represented in the
same population scope.

The local differential definition is:

$$
n_i = \frac{dN_i}{dV}
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $N_i$ is the number of ions in the
specified population, and $V$ is physical volume.

For species $s$, the charge-state-summed convention is $n_{i,s} = \sum_Z
n_{i,s,Z}$, where $n_{i,s,Z}$ is the ion number density of charge state $Z$
within the same species and population scope. A charge-state-resolved
counterpart fixes $Z$ instead of applying this sum; [ion charge-state
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) denotes such a quantity at its own
stated population scope. Population-qualified forms restrict the same
density concept, such as [thermal ion density](name:thermal_ion_density) for
thermal ions and [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density) for suprathermal
ions, while [total ion density](name:total_ion_number_density) aggregates
over ion species and [volume-averaged ion
density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) is a spatial average of the local
density.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Number density of fast, nonthermal ions of a specified species, summed over
all positive charge states and excluding thermal ions and neutral particles.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ion

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{fast}} = \sum_{q>0} n_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $i$ labels the selected ion species, $n_{i,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its
fast-ion number density, $q$ is the positive ionic charge number, and
$n_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [fast-ion charge-state
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density) for that species and charge
state.

The sum includes all positive charge states of the selected species, not
different ion species. Both trapped and passing fast ions are included.
Thermal ions and neutral particles are excluded, and the quantity is
distinct from electric charge density and mass density.

This is the fast-population contribution to [ion density](name:ion_density).
Adding the [thermal-ion density](name:thermal_ion_density) of the same
species gives its full ion number density when the thermal and fast
populations form a complete, nonoverlapping partition.

NAMES.name: ion_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity coefficient for diamagnetic, advective, non-diffusive
transport of aggregate ion momentum, distinct from the ions’ actual bulk
flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the diamagnetic
contribution to advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum for the ion
population, selected momentum component, and transport direction. It is a
transport-closure quantity rather than the actual bulk flow velocity of the
ions.

For the selected momentum component and transport direction, the diamagnetic
convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}} = V_{\mathrm{ion,dia}} P_{\mathrm{ion}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to
convective ion-momentum flux, $V_{\mathrm{ion,dia}}$ is this effective
convection velocity, $P_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the corresponding ion momentum
density, and the subscript $\mathrm{dia}$ identifies the diamagnetic
contribution.

The quantity applies to the aggregate ion population and uses the
density-weighted mean over all ion charge states, rather than resolving one
particular charge state. It represents only the diamagnetic advective
contribution; neutral-particle transport, diffusive momentum transport, and
the ions’ actual bulk flow velocity are excluded.

This is the ion-population specialization of the [diamagnetic momentum
convection velocity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity). The
[ion charge-state diamagnetic momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity)
resolves the corresponding effective coefficient for one ion charge state
instead of the charge-state-aggregated ion population.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the associated diamagnetic momentum flux is
outward, toward the last closed flux surface, for positive transported ion
momentum density.

NAMES.name: ion_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Particle diffusivity for an ion species, relating its charge-state-summed
diffusive flux to the opposing number-density gradient without selecting a
spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
The ion diffusion coefficient characterizes ion particle diffusion through a
local Fickian relation between diffusive particle flux and the
number-density gradient of a specified ion species. It does not select a
spatial direction or a particular transport mechanism.

For a scalar Fickian closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_i\nabla n_i
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion particle
flux density, $D_i$ is the ion diffusion coefficient, $n_i$ is the ion
number density, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. Both flux and
number density are summed over all ionic charge states of the specified
species, excluding neutral particles. The minus sign expresses down-gradient
transport for positive diffusivity.

This is an ion-specific [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity),
not an ion energy or momentum transport coefficient. It excludes convective
contributions to the ion particle flux. The population is aggregated over
ionic charge states, not over all ion species; the effective coefficient is
not a sum of charge-state diffusion coefficients. In contrast, the [ion
charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) relates the flux
of one specified charge state to that state's number-density gradient.

The [radial ion diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient) and [poloidal ion
diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient) are
directional diagonal specializations within an anisotropic
particle-diffusion tensor. The scalar closure above applies when a single
coefficient represents the flux-gradient response; the general quantity does
not require equal diffusion in all directions, represent a sum of
directional coefficients, or encode off-diagonal tensor couplings.

NAMES.name: ion_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion energy is the aggregate energy attributed to an ion population in a
specified plasma region. As a parent quantity, it does not by itself specify
thermal, fast-ion, suprathermal, bulk-flow, or internal-energy content;
those distinctions are supplied by child names.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy is the aggregate energy attributed to an ion population in a
specified plasma region. It is the parent concept for extensive ion-energy
quantities whose child names specify the included ion population and the
energy component being counted.

The scope is the ion contribution to plasma energy: electron and
neutral-particle energies are outside this quantity. Because this is an
extensive quantity, contributions from the included ion species and charge
states are summed over the populations included by the specific ion-energy
definition.

This parent quantity must not be read as specifically thermal, random
translational, fast-ion, suprathermal, internal, or directed bulk-flow
energy. Those component distinctions belong to more specific names; for
example, [thermal ion energy](name:thermal_ion_energy) is the specialization
for the volume-integrated internal energy of the thermal-ion ensemble and
carries its own exclusions of electron, fast-ion, and suprathermal
contributions.

NAMES.name: ion_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient linking an ion population's density-normalized
diffusive heat flux to its temperature gradient, without prescribing a
transport direction.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy diffusivity characterizes gradient-driven transport of thermal
energy carried by an ion population. It specifies the effective
proportionality between density-normalized diffusive heat flux and the
corresponding temperature gradient, without selecting a transport direction
or implying isotropic transport.

For a chosen physical transport direction, the defining Fickian closure is:

$$
\frac{Q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_i} = -k_{\mathrm{B}}D_{i,W}\frac{\partial T_i}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $Q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux component
along that direction, $n_i$ is the ion population's number density,
$D_{i,W}$ is its effective energy diffusivity, $T_i$ is its thermodynamic
temperature, $\ell$ is physical distance along the selected direction, and
$k_{\mathrm{B}}$ is Boltzmann's constant. The subscript $i$ denotes the ion
population, and $W$ labels the energy channel. The minus sign makes positive
diffusivity correspond to down-gradient transport.

The population may comprise one ion species or collectively all ion species.
Number density and diffusive heat flux are summed over all included ionic
charge states and species, while temperature is their density-weighted mean.
When the constituents share a common temperature, the effective diffusivity
is their density-weighted mean diffusivity; otherwise it is defined by the
combined flux–gradient closure rather than an unqualified average of
constituent coefficients.

This coefficient excludes convective and advective energy transport and is
distinct from particle diffusivity. Electron and neutral heat transport are
outside its scope. The [ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead
describes transport associated with one specified ionic charge state.

The [parallel ion energy diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusivity)
specializes this definition to field-aligned transport for the collective
ion population, whereas the [poloidal ion energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity) specializes it to
poloidal transport for a specified ion species.

NAMES.name: ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion energy flux is the net energy carried by ions across an oriented surface
per unit area and time, including conductive and convective transport.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy flux is the signed rate of energy transport carried by an ion
population across an oriented surface per unit area. It is the transport
flux entering the ion energy balance, rather than a volume energy source or
a surface-integrated power.

The local surface flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{W,i} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n} = \lim_{\Delta A,\Delta t\to 0}\frac{\Delta W_i}{\Delta A\,\Delta t}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,i}$ is the signed ion energy flux through the surface,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}$ is the underlying ion energy-flux vector, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface unit normal. The subscript $i$
identifies the ion population, $\Delta W_i$ is the net ion energy crossing a
surface patch during the time interval $\Delta t$, and $\Delta A$ is the
patch's actual area, not its projected area.

The population may be one ion species or an aggregate of ion species. For
one species, the flux is summed over all its ionic charge states; the [ion
charge-state energy flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) resolves
individual charge-state contributions. The [total ion energy
flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux) sums over all ion species and charge
states. Energy carried by electrons or neutrals is excluded.

The flux includes conductive thermal-energy transport and convective
enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport according to the ion energy balance
represented; it is not restricted to gradient-driven diffusion. The [energy
convection velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity) multiplies the
transported energy density to give the convective contribution, not the full
flux when conduction is also present.

The [radial](name:radial_ion_energy_flux),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_ion_energy_flux), and
[parallel](name:parallel_ion_energy_flux) ion energy fluxes select
directional projections of the same underlying energy-flux vector. The
general surface-flux definition does not select any one of these directions.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net ion energy crosses the surface in the
direction of its chosen unit normal.

NAMES.name: ion_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Multiplicative factor setting the maximum permitted ion energy flux relative
to a collisionless free-streaming reference while preserving the direction
assigned by the transport closure.
NAMES.long:
The ion energy flux limiter coefficient scales the collisionless
free-streaming upper bound on energy flux density carried by a specified ion
population. It limits the permitted flux magnitude without choosing or
reversing its direction.

The limiting relation is:

$$
\left|\mathbf{Q}_i\right| \leq f_i Q_{i,\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_i$ is the limited ion energy flux density, $f_i$ is the
ion energy flux limiter coefficient, and $Q_{i,\mathrm{fs}}$ is the
nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude for the same
ion population. The subscript $i$ identifies that population. The
coefficient is nonnegative; the free-streaming reference and the transition
between unlimited and limited flux are specified by the transport closure.

This is the ion-population specialization of the [energy flux limiter
coefficient](name:energy_flux_limiter_coefficient), with no particular
spatial direction or plasma region prescribed. It applies to
species-resolved or aggregated ion energy closures, rather than necessarily
denoting a total over all ions. The [total ion energy flux limiter
coefficient](name:total_ion_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient) specializes
this definition to energy summed over all ion species; the limiter
coefficient itself is not a sum of species coefficients. The [ion-state
energy flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_state_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient) restricts the
closure to a specified ion charge state.

This coefficient limits energy transport, not particle or momentum
transport. It is neither an energy diffusion coefficient nor the fraction of
the free-streaming reference actually carried by the flux.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective vector velocity at which aggregate ion momentum is advectively
transported in plasma fluid models, serving as a closure coefficient
distinct from the actual bulk ion flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient in
the non-diffusive, advective transport of aggregate ion momentum. It is a
transport-closure quantity and is distinct from the material bulk ion
velocity, as distinguished from the broader momentum convection velocity
framework.

A transport-closure decomposition of ion momentum flux is written as

$$
\mathbf{F}_{p,i} = -D_{p,i}\nabla\mathbf{p}_i + \mathbf{V}_{c,i} \otimes \mathbf{p}_i
$$

where $\mathbf{F}_{p,i}$ is the ion momentum-flux tensor, $D_{p,i}$ is the
ion momentum diffusivity, $\mathbf{p}_i$ is ion momentum density, and
$\mathbf{V}_{c,i}$ is this convection velocity. The dyadic term represents
non-diffusive momentum transport.

The unqualified ion quantity aggregates the ion momentum contribution over
all charge states. A species- or charge-state-resolved form, such as [ion
charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), supplies the
corresponding resolved convention; unlike [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), this coefficient is not the
material flow velocity.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_diffusivity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Fickian coefficient for flux-surface-normal redistribution of total ion
momentum caused specifically by diamagnetic drift, excluding other transport
mechanisms.
NAMES.long:
This diffusivity quantifies the diamagnetic-drift contribution to
cross-field redistribution of ion momentum, with the ion quantity aggregated
over all ionic charge states. It is distinct from the charge-state-resolved
coefficient and from the mechanism-unspecified [ion diamagnetic momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity).

The Fickian constitutive relation is

$$
\Pi_{i,\mathrm{dia}} = -\rho_i D_{i,\mathrm{mom}}^{\mathrm{dia}} \, \nabla_\perp V_i
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic-drift contribution to ion
momentum flux, $\rho_i$ is total ion mass density,
$D_{i,\mathrm{mom}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this diffusivity, $\nabla_\perp$ is
the gradient normal to magnetic flux surfaces, and $V_i$ is the
corresponding ion flow-velocity component. The coefficient describes only
the diffusive momentum-transport contribution due to diamagnetic drift;
convective and other mechanism-resolved contributions are excluded. Its
constitutive sign follows the negative-gradient relation, so outward flux
results from an outward-decreasing flow component.

NAMES.name: ion_particle_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective advective ion transport velocity whose product with ion number
density gives the convective particle flux, excluding
density-gradient-driven diffusion.
NAMES.long:
Ion particle convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient of the
density-proportional advective ion particle flux. It represents directed
particle transport after density-gradient-driven diffusion has been
separated.

The convective ion particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_i\mathbf{v}_i
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective ion particle
flux, $n_i$ is the number density of the specified ion population, and
$\mathbf{v}_i$ is its particle convection velocity; the subscript $i$
denotes ions.

For a specified ion species, the density is summed over all ionic charge
states, excluding neutral particles, and the velocity is the
density-weighted mean over all charge states rather than a sum of
velocities. The [ion charge-state particle convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity) instead
applies to a specified charge state. This quantity describes particle
transport, not heat or momentum transport, and need not equal the ion fluid
velocity. It is not restricted to the edge plasma or to a particular
transport direction.

The [parallel ion particle convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_particle_convection_velocity) is its
magnetic-field-aligned projection. The [radial ion particle convection
velocity](name:radial_ion_particle_convection_velocity) is its major-radius
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
[effective ion particle convection
velocity](name:effective_ion_particle_convection_velocity) specializes to
transport across magnetic flux surfaces; that direction need not coincide
with the cylindrical radial direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a projected convection velocity points along
its defining positive direction: toward increasing $R$ for the cylindrical
radial component, or along the magnetic field for the parallel component.

NAMES.name: ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion particle flux is the signed net number of ions of one species crossing
an oriented surface per unit area and time, summed over all ionic charge
states.
NAMES.long:
Ion particle flux is the signed net number flow of ions of one specified
species through an oriented surface per unit area and time. It is the
surface-normal projection of ion number transport, without selecting a fixed
geometric or magnetic-field direction.

The local flux is defined by the normal velocity moment summed over ionic
charge states:

$$
\Gamma_i = \sum_q \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}) f_{i,q}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_i$ is the ion particle flux, $i$ labels the specified ion
species, $q$ labels its ionic charge states, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen surface unit normal, $f_{i,q}$ is
the local velocity distribution of that species in charge state $q$, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The velocity integral of each
distribution is the corresponding charge-state number density.

The quantity includes thermal and nonthermal ions and is summed over all
ionic charge states of the specified species; neutral particles and other
ion species are excluded. It is a local net flux, not a one-way incident
flux or a surface-integrated particle rate. Particles are counted without
charge weighting, so this is not electric current density.

Each charge-state contribution is an [ion charge-state particle
flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux); their sum gives this
species-level quantity. Unlike [ion energy flux](name:ion_energy_flux), it
counts transported particles rather than the energy they carry.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net ion number flow crosses the surface
in the direction of the chosen unit normal.

NAMES.name: ion_particle_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion particle source rate is the net contribution of ion production and
removal to the particle-number balance of a specified ion population.
NAMES.long:
Ion particle source rate is the signed contribution of ion production and
removal to an ion population's particle-number balance. This shared concept
encompasses local source terms, their explicit and density-proportional
contributions, and volume-integrated rates.

The volume-integrated form is defined by

$$
S_i(V)=\int_V s_i\,dV'
$$

where $S_i(V)$ is the net ion particle source rate integrated over the
plasma region $V$, $s_i$ is the local net volumetric [ion source
rate](name:ion_source_rate), and $dV'$ is a physical volume element. The
subscript $i$ identifies the ion population. In the cumulative form, $V$ is
the entire volume enclosed by the specified magnetic flux surface. This
integral is neither a flux-surface average nor the particle flux through
that surface.

For a specified ion species, the source is summed over all ionic charge
states without charge weighting. The [charge-state-resolved cumulative
source
rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_ion_charge_state_source_rate)
restricts the enclosed-volume integral to one charge state. The [total ion
particle source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate) additionally sums
over all ion species. All contributing production and removal processes
enter the net source; positive values indicate net addition and negative
values indicate net removal. Transport across the region's boundary is a
separate particle-balance contribution.

For the local decomposition, $s_i=s_i^{\mathrm{exp}}+\alpha_i n_i$, where
$s_i^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is the additive explicit source contribution
independent of ion number density, $n_i$ is the number density of the
considered ion population, and $\alpha_i$ is the [implicit ion particle
source rate](name:implicit_ion_particle_source_rate). The implicit
coefficient must be multiplied by density to give its local
particle-production contribution; neither that coefficient nor the additive
volumetric term alone is the volume-integrated rate.

NAMES.name: ion_rotation_frequency
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Angular-velocity vector of an ion species’ bulk rotational motion,
density-weighted over all ionic charge states and distinct from gyrocenter
orbit motion.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the bulk rotational angular-velocity vector of an ion
species, aggregated over its ionic charge states. It describes collective
ion motion rather than the orbital angular velocity of individual
gyrocenters.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_i = \frac{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,Z}}{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_i$ is the species bulk rotation-frequency vector,
$n_{i,Z}$ is the number density of species $i$ in charge state $Z$, and
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,Z}$ is the rotation-frequency vector of that charge
state, represented by [ion charge state rotation
frequency](name:ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency). The toroidal
projection is represented by [toroidal ion rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency).

The quantity includes only bulk rotational motion and is not a gyrocenter
orbit-frequency diagnostic or a charge-state-resolved value.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_i$ points
along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

NAMES.name: ion_state_mean_ionisation_potential
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short:
Concentration-weighted mean cumulative energy required to reach the charge
states in an ion-state bundle by successive ionization from the neutral
ground state.
NAMES.long:
Ion-state mean ionization potential is the concentration-weighted mean of
the cumulative successive ionization energies required to reach, from the
neutral ground state, the charge states represented in an ion-state bundle.
It expresses the mean ionization energy per particle associated with the
bundle's charge-state composition.

For a populated bundle, the mean is defined by:

$$
\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s} = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}_s} n_q \displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{q} I_k}{\displaystyle\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}_s} n_q}
$$

where $\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}$ is the mean cumulative ionization potential
of bundle $s$, $\mathcal{B}_s$ is its set of represented charge states, $q$
is the ionic charge number, $n_q$ is the number density of that charge
state, $k$ indexes successive ionization steps, and $I_k$ is the
ground-state ionization energy for the transition from charge number $k-1$
to $k$. The cumulative energy of the neutral ground state is zero.

The averaging includes only the charge states represented in the specified
bundle of one ion species and requires a nonzero total bundle number
density. For a bundle containing a single charge state, the mean reduces to
that state's cumulative ionization energy, not the threshold energy for
removing its next electron.

This quantity excludes thermal internal energy, excitation energy, radiation
losses, and kinetic energy exchanged during ionization or recombination. The
[change in ion-state mean ionization potential] is the value after a
specified state change minus the value before it for the same bundle.

NAMES.name: change_in_ion_state_mean_ionisation_potential
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short:
Change in ion-state mean ionization potential is the signed difference
between the concentration-weighted mean cumulative ionization potential of
an ion charge-state bundle after and before a specified state change.
NAMES.long:
Change in ion-state mean ionization potential is the signed difference in
the ion-state mean ionization potential of an ion charge-state bundle across
a specified state change. The base quantity is the concentration-weighted
mean of the cumulative successive ionization energies required to reach,
from the neutral ground state, the charge states represented in the bundle.

The change is defined as the value after the change minus the value before
the change:

$$
\Delta \bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s} = \bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{after}} - \bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{before}}
$$

where $\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{after}}$ and
$\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{before}}$ are the ion-state mean
ionization potentials of the same ion-state bundle after and before the
change.

This quantity accounts only for the change in the mean cumulative ionization
energy associated with the represented charge-state composition. It excludes
thermal internal energy, excitation energy, radiation losses, and kinetic
energy exchanged during ionization or recombination.

NAMES.name: ion_state_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short:
Ion charge-state source rate is the net volumetric rate of particle addition
or removal for one specified charge state of an ion species.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state source rate is the net volumetric rate at which particles
enter or leave a specified charge state of an ion species. It supplies the
particle-number source term in that charge state's density transport
equation.

The source enters the particle continuity equation as

$$
\frac{\partial n_q}{\partial t}+\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_q=S_q
$$

where $q$ is the specified ion charge number, $n_q$ is the number density of
that charge state, $t$ is time, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_q$ is its
particle-number flux density, $S_q$ is its net volumetric particle source
rate, and $\nabla\cdot$ denotes spatial divergence.

This quantity is resolved by ion species and charge state, not summed over
charge states. Positive values indicate net particle gain and negative
values indicate net particle loss for the specified state. Transfers between
charge states contribute even when they leave the species' total particle
number unchanged. The quantity counts particles rather than electric charge;
spatial transport is represented separately by the flux-divergence term.

Integrating this volumetric source over the volume enclosed by a magnetic
flux surface gives the [cumulative ion charge-state source rate inside that
surface](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_ion_charge_state_source_rate),
rather than another volumetric source rate.

sources.leaf_definition: Source term for the charge state density transport equation
