NAMES.name: ion_torque
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated torque vector acting on the ion population, representing
the net source or sink of ion angular momentum while retaining its
direction.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the net torque vector exerted on the ion population and
integrated over the relevant plasma volume. It represents the global source
or sink of ion angular momentum, with ionic charge states aggregated rather
than represented separately.

$$
\boldsymbol{T}_i = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}_i(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{T}_i$ is the integrated ion torque vector,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_i$ is the local [ion torque
density](name:ion_torque_density), $V$ is the integration volume, and
$\mathbf{x}$ is position. The quantity includes the contributing ion species
and charge states; the [toroidal ion
torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque) is its toroidal component about
the toroidal symmetry axis.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a vector component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: explicit_ion_torque
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated explicit torque vector acting on the combined ion
population, summed over ion species and charge states and independent of the
primary transported momentum variable.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the global explicit source or sink of angular momentum for
the combined ion population, represented as a torque vector integrated over
the relevant plasma volume. It retains the full directional torque rather
than selecting a single cylindrical component.

The volume-integrated torque is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{T}_{i,\mathrm{exp}} = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\boldsymbol{T}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}$ is the explicit ion torque vector,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}$ is the corresponding local
torque-density vector, $V$ is the relevant plasma volume, and $\mathrm{d}V$
is its volume element. The subscript $i$ denotes the combined ion
population, and $\mathrm{exp}$ denotes the explicit source contribution.

The quantity applies globally to all included ion species and ionic charge
states, which are summed rather than represented separately. It is
independent of the primary transported momentum variable and excludes any
torque contribution defined solely through that variable; it is also
distinct from a local torque density and from a single-direction projection.

The broader [ion torque](name:ion_torque) is the net volume-integrated
torque on the ion population, while [toroidal explicit ion
torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque) is the toroidal projection of
this explicit vector contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each vector component points in its
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is increasing toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to a thermal plasma
population when fast or nonthermal particles undergo thermalization.
NAMES.long:
Torque density due to thermalization is the signed rate at which angular
momentum is transferred per unit volume from a fast or otherwise nonthermal
population to the thermal plasma population as particles become assimilated
into the thermal background. It represents a momentum source for the thermal
population, rather than an energy-transfer rate.

For a resolved angular-momentum component $a$, the defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)} = \left.\frac{\partial \ell_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{thermalization}}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)}$ is the thermalization-attributed torque
density and $\ell_{\mathrm{th}}^{(a)}$ is the angular-momentum density of
the thermal population in component $a$.

The quantity includes only momentum transfer attributed to thermalization
and is not the total torque from all momentum-transfer mechanisms. The
[thermal-ion torque density due to
thermalization](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization) is a
species-resolved instance of this general quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when thermalization increases the angular-momentum
density of the thermal population in the resolved component.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of iron ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier, summed over all iron ion charge states and
excluding neutral iron.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of iron ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the iron-ion
population at that flux-surface location. It is the iron-specific member of
the [density at the internal transport
barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) family. Iron has atomic
number $Z=26$.

The number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is
the number of counted iron ions, and $V$ is volume. The count is summed over
all iron ionic charge states and excludes neutral iron. The internal
transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced
cross-field turbulent transport can sustain steep impurity-density
gradients, as for [carbon density at the internal transport
barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the iron ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local iron-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all iron ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the iron ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local iron-ion count per physical volume at that location. It
represents iron ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral iron, or
another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe,axis}}$ is the iron-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of iron ions summed over all iron
ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete ionic iron population at that location,
with all iron charge states aggregated, and is neither a flux-surface or
volume integral nor a neutral-iron density.

This is the iron-specific realization of the population-independent [density
at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It is distinguished
from [hydrogen density at the magnetic
axis](name:hydrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts hydrogen ions,
and from [iron density at the internal transport
barrier](name:iron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), which is
evaluated on the flux surface assigned to that barrier rather than at the
magnetic axis.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: kinetic_energy_density
NAMES.short:
Kinetic energy carried by a specified particle population per unit volume,
combining random thermal motion with directed or nonthermal translational
motion.
NAMES.long:
Kinetic energy density is the translational kinetic energy carried by a
defined particle population per unit volume. It includes random thermal
motion and directed or nonthermal motion represented within that population.

The local kinetic energy density is defined from the particle velocity
distribution by

$$
K_{\mathrm{kin}}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \int \varepsilon_{\mathrm{kin},s}(\mathbf{v})\, f_s(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $K_{\mathrm{kin}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the kinetic energy density at
position $\mathbf{r}$, $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of included particle species
or states, $s$ identifies one member of that set,
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{kin},s}(\mathbf{v})$ is the translational kinetic
energy of a particle with velocity $\mathbf{v}$, and
$f_s(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity-distribution density.

The population and aggregation are defined by the specific application:
species and charge states may be summed, while a designated population such
as runaway electrons may be represented by its population mean. The quantity
may be evaluated locally or resolved by magnetic flux surface; neither
spatial representation changes its kinetic-energy definition. The [ion
kinetic energy density](name:ion_kinetic_energy_density) is the
ion-population instance, while the [runaway electron kinetic energy
density](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density) is the
runaway-electron instance.

This component of [energy density](name:energy_density) includes
translational particle motion only. It excludes magnetic, electric,
potential, and non-translational internal-state energy, while random thermal
motion remains included when it belongs to the specified particle
population.

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of krypton ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over krypton charge states
and excluding neutral krypton.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of krypton ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the
krypton-ion population at that flux-surface location. The [density at the
internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) is
the parent quantity for this krypton-specific population.

The number density is defined by

$$
n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n$ is number density, $N$ is the number of particles, and $V$ is
volume. The quantity sums all ionized krypton charge states and excludes
neutral krypton atoms. It is therefore an elemental ion density, analogous
to the ion density at the internal transport barrier, rather than a density
for one specified charge state. The internal transport barrier is the
designated flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent
transport permits steep impurity-density gradients.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the krypton ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local krypton-ion count per physical volume at that
location.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the krypton ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local krypton-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents krypton ions specifically, summed over all ionic
charge states and excluding neutral krypton.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr,axis}}$ is the krypton-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the number of krypton ions summed over
ionic charge states, $V$ is physical volume, and the subscript axis denotes
evaluation at the magnetic axis.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete krypton-ion population at that
location, with number density summed over all krypton ionic charge states;
it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of neutral
krypton, electrons, or other ion species.

This is the krypton-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). The [neon
density at the magnetic axis](name:neon_density_at_magnetic_axis) has the
same local locus and charge-state-summed convention but counts neon ions
rather than krypton ions.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Linear neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vector-valued
signed transport rate of linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one
specified internal state across an oriented surface.
NAMES.long:
The linear neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vector-valued
transport of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one
specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It describes
momentum transport rather than particle-number transport or a local momentum
source.

For an oriented surface, the momentum-flux vector is defined by

$$
\mathbf{F}_{\Pi}^{(s)}(\hat{n}) = \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{n} = \int m_s\mathbf{v}\, (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\hat{n}$ is the oriented surface
normal, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$
is the state-resolved velocity distribution, and $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is
the corresponding momentum-flux tensor.

This is the linear-momentum form of the parent neutral internal-state
momentum flux. Projection onto a specified direction produces components
such as [poloidal linear neutral internal-state momentum
flux](name:poloidal_linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux); no
particular radial, poloidal, toroidal, vertical, or magnetic-field-parallel
direction is implied here.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when particles cross the oriented surface in its
positive normal direction while carrying linear momentum in the selected
positive direction.

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Local number density of lithium ions at the internal transport barrier
reference radius, where reduced cross-field transport can produce steep
impurity density gradients.
NAMES.long:
Lithium density at an internal transport barrier is the local number density
of lithium ions on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference
location. Unless a charge state is specified separately, it represents the
elemental lithium ion concentration summed over all ionization states,
consistent with the broader
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
family.

The quantity is the sum of charge-state-resolved contributions evaluated at
the ITB reference coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$:

$$
n_\mathrm{Li}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_{k=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{k+}}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB})
$$

where $k$ indexes the lithium ionization states (Li$^{1+}$, Li$^{2+}$,
Li$^{3+}$) and $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the normalized radial coordinate of
the barrier.

Lithium (atomic number $Z = 3$) enters fusion plasmas through pellet
injection, evaporation from lithium-coated plasma-facing components, or
deliberate wall conditioning. As a low-Z impurity it contributes less
radiative cooling than high-Z species, but significant concentrations at the
ITB can dilute the fuel ion population. The local value at the barrier is
inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or from inversion
of line-integrated visible or soft-X-ray emission measurements.

The corresponding toroidal flow of lithium ions at the same barrier location
is given by
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
and the lithium density adjacent to plasma-facing components is separately
described by [lithium_density_at_limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the lithium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local lithium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all lithium ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the lithium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local lithium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all lithium ionic charge states. It represents ionized
lithium specifically, rather than electrons, neutral lithium, or another
plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\sum_{q\ge 1} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li,axis}}$ is the total lithium-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of lithium ions, $V$ is
physical volume, $q$ is the positive integer labeling a lithium ionic charge
state, and $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the number density of lithium ions in
charge state $q$.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete ionized lithium population at that
location and uses a sum over all lithium ionic charge states, not a density
for one selected charge state or a sum over different chemical elements. It
is neither a flux-surface nor volume integral and excludes neutral lithium.

This is the lithium-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the
same local-density and magnetic-axis scope as [deuterium density at the
magnetic axis](name:deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis), but counts lithium
ions rather than deuterium ions; unlike [electron density at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_density_at_magnetic_axis), it does not count electrons.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: magnetic_shear_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short:
Magnetic shear at an internal transport barrier is the normalized
logarithmic derivative of the safety factor with respect to the outward
normalized toroidal-flux radial coordinate at the internal-transport-barrier
flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Magnetic shear at an internal transport barrier is the local magnetic shear
evaluated on the flux surface identified as the internal-transport-barrier
location. It characterizes the radial variation of field-line pitch through
the safety factor at that locus.

The defining relation is

$$
s_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \left.\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}{q}\frac{d q}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}\right|_{\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}=\rho_{\mathrm{tor,ITB}}}
$$

where $s_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the magnetic shear at the internal transport
barrier, $q$ is the [safety factor](name:safety_factor),
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux radius used as an
outward flux-surface radial coordinate, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,ITB}}$ is the
value of that coordinate at the internal-transport-barrier location.

The scope is the local value at the internal-transport-barrier flux surface
in a magnetically confined plasma. It is not an average over the barrier
width, not the position or width of the barrier, and not the magnetic shear
at the pedestal top or another named flux-surface locus. Its aggregation
convention is a single flux-surface evaluation with no averaging over
neighboring flux surfaces.

This quantity is a locus-specific specialization of [magnetic shear at a
flux surface](name:magnetic_shear_at_flux_surface): it uses the same
normalized logarithmic safety-factor derivative, with the flux-surface label
fixed to the internal-transport-barrier location. The derivative is local in
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, so the quantity represents the local radial slope of
$q$ rather than an integral measure across the barrier.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the safety-factor gradient with respect to
increasing outward $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ has the same sign as the safety
factor at the internal transport barrier.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

NAMES.name: magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Vector field whose curl gives the magnetic induction, gage-dependent but
physically central to canonical momentum, gyrokinetic, and
magnetohydrodynamic formulations of magnetized plasmas.
NAMES.long:
The magnetic vector potential $\mathbf{A}$ is a gage-dependent vector field
characterizing the electromagnetic state of a plasma. It enters fundamental
physics through the canonical particle momentum $\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v} +
q\mathbf{A}$, where $m$ is particle mass and $q$ is particle charge, and it
governs inductive electromagnetic effects in both equilibrium and perturbed
plasma states.

The defining relation connecting $\mathbf{A}$ to the magnetic induction
$\mathbf{B}$ is:

$$
\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic induction. Only the curl of $\mathbf{A}$
is directly physical; the vector potential itself is gage dependent. Its
time derivative contributes to the inductive electric field via
$\mathbf{E}_\mathrm{ind} = -\partial\mathbf{A}/\partial t$, which is central
to Faraday's law in electromagnetic plasma models.

Specific projections serve distinct physical roles. The field-aligned
component $A_\parallel = \mathbf{A} \cdot \hat{b}$, where $\hat{b}$ is the
equilibrium field unit vector, governs Alfvénic dynamics and is the
component retained in gyrokinetic and reduced-MHD formulations; its
normalized perturbed amplitude is used in eigenmode studies. Cylindrical
components in the right-handed $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame — radial, toroidal, and
vertical — are natural for equilibrium and MHD calculations, while the
poloidal projection in flux coordinates $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$ arises in
neoclassical transport analyzes. In vacuum regions, $\mathbf{A}$ is
generated solely by external coil currents, with no plasma-current
contribution.

NAMES.name: mhd_mode_number
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless mode-number vector labeling the radial branch and poloidal and
toroidal periodicities of a linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the collection of discrete mode labels that identifies a
linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation across its radial, poloidal, and
toroidal structure. It is a mode-index vector, not a spatial wavevector or a
physical displacement vector.

$$
\mathbf{N} = (n_r, m, n_\phi)
$$

where $n_r$ is the non-negative radial branch index, $m$ is the integer
poloidal Fourier harmonic, and $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier
harmonic. The components correspond to the [radial mode
number](name:radial_mode_number), [poloidal mode
number](name:poloidal_mode_number), and [toroidal MHD mode
number](name:toroidal_mhd_mode_number).

The radial index labels branch structure by radial nodes, while the angular
indices label periodicity around the poloidal and toroidal coordinates.
Coupled poloidal harmonics may belong to one eigenmode, so this quantity
identifies the mode labels without requiring a single separable spatial
harmonic.

NAMES.name: momentum
NAMES.short:
Linear momentum associated with plasma motion, covering concrete quantities
that either represent momentum content in a plasma volume or momentum
transported through an oriented surface. The specific child name defines
whether the quantity is an extensive momentum or a momentum-flux component.
NAMES.long:
Momentum is the mass-weighted linear-velocity content associated with plasma
matter, together with the corresponding transport of that content when the
quantity is defined across an oriented surface. As a parent quantity, it
denotes the common linear-momentum concept shared by concrete
momentum-content and momentum-transport quantities, not a single fully
specified observable.

This parent must not be interpreted as imposing one governing equation on
all children: [plasma momentum](name:plasma_momentum) is an integrated
momentum content, whereas [radial momentum](name:radial_momentum) is a
component of momentum transport in the $\hat{R}$ direction of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. A concrete child supplies the
necessary scope, such as included species, volume integration, component
direction, and oriented-surface convention.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a specified component is directed along the
positive basis vector or oriented-surface direction named by the concrete
child quantity.

NAMES.name: momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.short:
Effective inverse relaxation time for loss of ordered fluid momentum through
collisional friction and neoclassical viscosity; the general structural
parent for species-, charge-state-, and projection-resolved momentum damping
rates.
NAMES.long:
The momentum damping rate $\nu_D$ is the reciprocal relaxation time that
quantifies how rapidly ordered fluid momentum is dissipated within a plasma
population through inter-species collisional friction and neoclassical
viscous stresses. It enters the fluid momentum balance as a linear loss
coefficient applied to the local momentum density, capturing the collective
effect of Coulomb collisions and drift-driven viscosity acting on any
directed flow component.

The defining relation for a fluid momentum component $p$ subject to damping
is:

$$
\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\nu_D \, p
$$

where $\nu_D$ is the damping rate and $p$ is the local fluid momentum
density. The magnitude of $\nu_D$ depends on plasma collisionality, species
masses and charges, and the local magnetic geometry.

This name is the structural parent for species- and projection-resolved
variants. In transport models, $\nu_D$ is derived analytically from
neoclassical friction-force coefficients or from velocity-space integrals of
the collision operator evaluated at the local plasma parameters.
Ion-population values are provided by
[ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate);
charge-state-resolved counterparts are given by
[ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).
Directional projections include poloidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate,
toroidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate,
parallel_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate, and
[radial_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical
dissipation of fluid momentum for a specified ion charge state, expressed as
a vector whose components quantify the damping rate along distinct geometric
projections.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge state momentum damping rate is the effective inverse
relaxation timescale at which ordered fluid momentum of a specified ion
charge state is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical
viscous stresses. As a vector, it encodes the direction-dependent damping
coefficient along the radial, poloidal, toroidal, and field-parallel
geometric projections.

The defining relation for a fluid momentum density component $p_s$ of ion
charge state $s$ subject to dissipation is:

$$
\frac{\partial p_s}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\nu_{D,s} \, p_s
$$

where $\nu_{D,s}$ is the charge-state damping rate and $p_s$ is the directed
fluid momentum density of the specified charge state. The magnitude of
$\nu_{D,s}$ is set by Coulomb collisionality, the charge-state mass and
effective charge number, and the local magnetic geometry through
neoclassical friction-force coefficients.

This quantity resolves the general
[momentum_damping_rate](name:momentum_damping_rate) at the level of an
individual ion charge state, in contrast to
[ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate), which
represents the charge-state-aggregated ion population. Scalar projections
along each geometric direction include
[parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate)
for the field-aligned component.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical
dissipation of bulk ion fluid momentum, expressed as a vector whose
components each quantify the damping rate along a distinct geometric
projection of the ion velocity.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale
at which ordered bulk ion fluid momentum is dissipated through Coulomb
collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. As a vector, it encodes the
geometric anisotropy of momentum loss in a magnetized plasma, where the
field-aligned and toroidal projections relax through distinct mechanisms
compared with the poloidal or radial projections.

In the ion fluid momentum balance the damping contribution enters as:

$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{p}_i}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\boldsymbol{\nu}_D^{\,i} \cdot \mathbf{p}_i$$

where $\mathbf{p}_i = m_i n_i \mathbf{v}_i$ is the ion momentum density,
with $m_i$ the ion mass, $n_i$ the number density, and $\mathbf{v}_i$ the
bulk ion fluid velocity. The rate $\boldsymbol{\nu}_D^{\,i}$ is applied
component-wise and aggregates contributions from all ion charge states.

Component-resolved scalar rates are
[radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate),
[toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate),
[poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate),
and
[parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate).
These are computed from neoclassical transport theory or
turbulent-momentum-transport models. This quantity serves as the
ion-species-level structural parent described by
[momentum_damping_rate](name:momentum_damping_rate), which covers the
general multi-species case.

NAMES.name: momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of bulk-flow momentum.
This generic parent does not specify the transported plasma or neutral
population.
NAMES.long:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of bulk-flow momentum.
This generic parent does not specify the transported plasma or neutral
population; population-qualified standard names identify that population.
Each component is a kinematic diagonal coefficient for one named transport
direction, not a full viscosity tensor.

For component $\chi_{m,i}$ associated with coordinate $x_i$ along direction
$\hat{e}_i$, the diagonal diffusive closure for momentum-density component
$M_j$ is

$$
\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{m,i}\,\frac{\partial M_j}{\partial x_i}\qquad\text{(no summation over }i\text{)}
$$

where $\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux in direction
$\hat{e}_i$ of momentum component $j$, $\chi_{m,i}$ is the directional
momentum diffusion coefficient, $M_j$ is the bulk-flow momentum density
component of the same transported population, and $x_i$ is distance along
$\hat{e}_i$.

The component basis must be explicit. A radial component is the $\hat{R}$
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from
the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed
from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is
the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel,
perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are
separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward
increasing flux label.

Population-qualified specializations include plasma momentum diffusion
coefficient, [ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and [neutral momentum
diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). Scalar
specializations include radial momentum diffusivity and ion momentum
diffusivity. This name is the momentum-channel specialization of diffusion
coefficient, and excludes convective momentum transport, external momentum
sources, off-diagonal couplings between flux and gradient directions, and
the dynamic viscosity-like coefficient obtained by multiplying by mass
density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diffusive momentum flux is directed
opposite to the corresponding gradient of bulk-flow momentum density.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients governing diffusive transport
of bulk-ion momentum in a magnetized plasma, with distinct radial, poloidal,
and toroidal components forming the diagonal of the ion momentum diffusivity
tensor.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum diffusion coefficient vector collects the anisotropic
diagonal components of the bulk-ion momentum diffusivity tensor, each
relating the diffusive flux of bulk-ion momentum along a given geometric
direction to the local gradient of ion momentum density in that direction.
In a gradient-diffusion closure, each directional component $\chi_{\rm mom}$
satisfies the constitutive relation:

$$
\Gamma_{\rm mom} = -\chi_{\rm mom}\,\nabla(m_i n_i v_i)
$$

where $\Gamma_{\rm mom}$ is the diffusive ion momentum flux density, $m_i$
is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, and $v_i$ is the bulk ion
flow velocity component in the corresponding direction. The three
projections are radial_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing
cross-flux-surface momentum mixing;
poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing transport along the
poloidal direction tangent to flux surfaces; and
toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing diffusion of toroidal
angular momentum. The radial component is the confinement-relevant quantity
and is inferred from toroidal momentum balance analyzes or gyrokinetic and
fluid turbulence simulations. The scalar analog ion_momentum_diffusivity
represents the same physical concept without directional decomposition,
while plasma_momentum_diffusivity extends the concept to the full plasma
mixture.

NAMES.name: momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Vector Fick's-law transport coefficient relating the diffusive momentum flux
to the local momentum-density gradient, abstracting over plasma species,
neutral populations, charge states, and directional projections in a
magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the
diffusive momentum flux and the negative local gradient of momentum density,
following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum balance. Physically,
it encapsulates contributions from collisional viscosity, turbulent mixing,
charge-exchange friction, and diamagnetic drifts. As a vector quantity, its
radial, poloidal, toroidal, parallel, and vertical components capture the
strongly anisotropic transport characteristic of magnetized plasma, where
diffusivity along magnetic field lines greatly exceeds cross-field values.

The diffusive momentum flux density component along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is

$$
\Gamma_{m,i} = -D_{m,i} \frac{\partial (m n v_i)}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $D_{m,i}$ is the momentum diffusivity component, $m$ is particle mass,
$n$ is number density, and $v_i$ is the fluid velocity component along
$\hat{e}_i$, making $m n v_i$ the local momentum density.

This parent name abstracts over species-resolved and process-attributed
children including plasma_momentum_diffusivity for the total plasma and
analogous neutral-population variants; the
[radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:flux_surface_normal_plasma_momentum_diffusivity)
is the cross-field specialization and
[parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity)
is the field-aligned form. Values are inferred from fluid transport
simulations by computing the diffusive momentum flux relative to the local
momentum-density gradient, or estimated analytically from neoclassical and
turbulence theory.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the Fick's-law coefficient relating
diffusive momentum flux to the negative gradient of momentum density for a
specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient
between the diffusive momentum flux of a specified ion charge state and the
negative local gradient of its momentum density, following a Fick's-law
closure for the fluid momentum balance. It describes directional
redistribution of momentum for that charge state.

For transport direction $i$, the diffusive momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)} = -D_{m,i}^{(q)} \frac{\partial\left(\rho_q u_i^{(q)}\right)}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)}$ is the diffusive momentum flux, $D_{m,i}^{(q)}$
is the corresponding momentum diffusivity, $\rho_q$ is the mass density of
the specified ion charge state, $u_i^{(q)}$ is its flow-velocity component,
and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the transport direction.

The quantity is general over directional projections, including the
cross-flux-surface form represented by [radial ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) and the
field-aligned form represented by [parallel ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). It is
resolved for one ion charge state rather than summed over charge states as
in ion momentum diffusivity, and is a charge-state-specific instance of
[momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic pressure, and viscous
stress contributions from any species or population.
NAMES.long:
The momentum flux describes the rate at which linear momentum crosses a unit
area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It encompasses the convective
ram-pressure term, the isotropic thermal pressure, and viscous or turbulent
stress contributions, and appears as the divergence term in the plasma fluid
momentum-balance equation.

The momentum-flux tensor for a single plasma fluid is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi} = \rho \mathbf{v}\mathbf{v} + p\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}
$$

where $\rho$ is the mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ the bulk flow velocity, $p$
the scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ the identity tensor, and
$\boldsymbol{\pi}$ the viscous stress tensor. The momentum current through a
surface with outward unit normal $\hat{n}$ is
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}$.

This name is the structural parent for species- and direction-resolved
forms. Species-specific instances include [ion momentum
flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux), and [plasma momentum
flux](name:plasma_momentum_flux), each summed over the relevant population.
Directional projections such as parallel momentum flux isolate field-aligned
transport, while [poloidal momentum flux](name:poloidal_momentum_flux)
captures cross-field transport through toroidally symmetric surfaces. The
complementary volume source density entering the momentum balance is given
by volumetric plasma momentum source.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Vector of linear-momentum transport rate per unit area for ions in a
specific charge state, with directional projections characterizing
charge-state-resolved momentum transport across magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state momentum flux is the vector flux density of linear
momentum carried by ions in a single ionization state $z$, combining
convective transport from bulk flow and non-convective contributions from
pressure and viscous stress. It appears in the charge-state-resolved
momentum-balance equation as the flux term whose divergence governs local
momentum redistribution across flux surfaces and couples to electromagnetic
forces, inter-species friction, and anomalous transport terms.

The component form of the momentum-flux tensor for charge state $z$ is:

$$
\Pi_{z,ij} = m_i n_z v_{z,i} v_{z,j} + p_z \delta_{ij} + \pi_{z,ij}
$$

where $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state
$z$, $v_{z,i}$ and $v_{z,j}$ are fluid velocity components, $p_z$ is the
scalar pressure, $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta, and $\pi_{z,ij}$ is
the viscous stress tensor for that charge state.

Scalar projections onto coordinate axes are resolved in the component names:
[radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux)
for outward transport across flux surfaces,
toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux and
[poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux)
for the respective in-surface momentum components, and
[parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux)
for field-aligned transport. Summing over all ionization stages recovers the
total ion [momentum_flux](name:momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when momentum is transported in the direction of
increasing $R$ for the radial component, in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ for the toroidal component, and along the local
magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$ for the parallel component.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Vector rate of linear momentum transport per unit area for the total ion
population, summed over all ion species and charge states, encompassing
convective, pressure, and viscous stress contributions.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum flux represents the rate at which the total ion population
transports linear momentum through a unit area, summed over all ion species
and charge states. It combines convective bulk-flow momentum, scalar
pressure (isotropic kinetic stress), and viscous or turbulent off-diagonal
stress contributions. Its divergence appears in the ion momentum balance
equation, governing the forces that drive and redistribute plasma rotation
and bulk flows; this quantity is the ion-specific instance of the general
[momentum_flux](name:momentum_flux).

The total ion momentum flux density is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion} = \sum_s \left( m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s \mathbf{v}_s + p_s \mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_s \right)
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion species mass, $n_s$ is the number density,
$\mathbf{v}_s$ is the mean fluid velocity, $p_s$ is the scalar pressure,
$\mathbf{I}$ is the unit tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ is the viscous
stress tensor for species $s$, with the sum running over all ion species.

Specific resolved components isolate distinct transport channels:
[toroidal_ion_momentum_flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux) quantifies the
radial flux of toroidal momentum relevant to rotation drive,
[parallel_ion_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux) captures
transport along the magnetic field, and
[poloidal_ion_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux) resolves the
poloidal channel. The convective contribution can be parameterized through
the radial_ion_momentum_effective_convection_velocity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when ion momentum is transported in the positive
direction of the resolved projection axis in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with outward (increasing $R$) as positive for radial
projections.

NAMES.name: momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short:
Momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed transfer rate of a
selected linear-momentum component per surface area, attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport.
NAMES.long:
Momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of a
selected component of linear [momentum](name:momentum) attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport. The direction of the
transported momentum is distinct from the normal direction of the surface
across which it is transferred.

The contribution through an oriented surface is defined by

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_p \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the momentum-flux tensor contribution
attributed to diamagnetic drift, $\hat{\mathbf e}_p$ is the unit vector
selecting the transported momentum component, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the
chosen positive unit normal to the transfer surface. The tensor's first
index denotes the transported momentum direction and its second index
denotes the transport direction.

For the total momentum balance, the contributing population and charge-state
fluxes are summed. No particular species, charge state, momentum axis,
surface orientation, or plasma region is selected by this general quantity.
It is normalized to the actual surface area, not integrated over that area,
and excludes contributions from non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms.

The [ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [neutral
momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:neutral_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) specialize the
participating population. Neutral specializations denote momentum transport
attributed to this mechanism, not a direct magnetic drift of uncharged
particles.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive momentum along $\hat{\mathbf e}_p$
is transported through the surface in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf n}$.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Ion charge-state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed
transfer of a selected linear-momentum component per surface area for one
ion charge state, attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic
transport.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux
density of a selected component of linear [momentum](name:momentum) for one
specified charge state of an ion species, attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport. The transported momentum
component and the surface-crossing direction are distinct specifications;
neither a toroidal momentum projection nor a flux-surface-normal crossing
direction is imposed.

For the selected momentum component and oriented surface, the flux is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{a,s}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_a \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{a,s}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux, $s$ labels the
specified ion species and charge state, $a$ labels the selected momentum
component, $\hat{\mathbf e}_a$ is its direction unit vector, $\hat{\mathbf
n}$ is the oriented surface-normal unit vector, and
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to that
state's momentum-flux tensor, with its first index denoting transported
momentum and its second index denoting crossing direction.

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved specialization of [momentum flux
due to diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It
contains no sum over ion species or charge states, unlike the
charge-state-aggregated [ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It excludes
contributions from non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms and is not the total
momentum flux.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive momentum in the selected component
is transported along the oriented surface normal.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-R flux
density of toroidal linear momentum for the ion population, attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
NAMES.long:
Ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-$R$
flux density of toroidal linear momentum carried by the ion population and
associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The
transported momentum is the $\hat{\phi}$ component and the flux direction is
$\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The diamagnetic contribution is defined by summing the charge-state
contributions to the toroidal momentum flux:

$$
\Pi_{R\phi,i}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \sum_{\alpha} m_i n_{i,\alpha} u_{\phi,i,\alpha} v_{R,i,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $\Pi_{R\phi,i}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux, $\alpha$ labels
the included charge states, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_{i,\alpha}$ is the
charge-state number density, $u_{\phi,i,\alpha}$ is its toroidal flow
velocity, and $v_{R,i,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is its cylindrical-$R$
diamagnetic-drift velocity.

This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [momentum flux due to
diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and is
charge-state aggregated, whereas [ion charge state momentum flux due to
diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) retains
one charge state. It excludes momentum-flux contributions from
non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive toroidal linear momentum is
transported toward increasing $R$.

NAMES.name: momentum_source
NAMES.short:
Directed rate of momentum transfer to or from a plasma population,
represented as a source density resolved by species, internal state, or
spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
A momentum source density represents the directed transfer of momentum
caused by physical processes acting on a plasma population or one of its
resolved states. It may retain vector direction or represent a selected
component of the momentum-transfer rate.

The area-normalized source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{p} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}$ is the momentum transferred by the source
processes, $A$ is the surface over which the source is normalized, and $t$
is time. Concrete variants may resolve a radial component, an internal
state, or an ion charge state, as in [radial momentum
source](name:radial_momentum_source) and [ion charge-state momentum
source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). Population-level quantities
may sum the corresponding state-resolved contributions, as for [ion momentum
source](name:ion_momentum_source).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Momentum source density for a specified ion charge state gives the net
directed momentum transfer into that state, retaining the full vector before
directional projection.
NAMES.long:
The momentum source density for a specified ion charge state is the net
directed rate of momentum transfer into that state, represented by a
physical vector before projection onto a coordinate or magnetic-field
direction. It is the charge-state-resolved member of the [momentum source
density](name:momentum_source), whereas
[ion_momentum_source](name:ion_momentum_source) aggregates the corresponding
ion contributions over charge states.

$$
\mathbf{S}_{m,s} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_s}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_s$ is the net momentum transferred to ion charge state
$s$, $A$ is the reference area, and $t$ is time.

The state index $s$ identifies one resolved ion charge state; contributions
are not summed over charge states. Positive and negative terms represent net
momentum addition and removal. Directional forms, such as the [toroidal ion
charge-state momentum
source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), are projections of
this vector. It differs from
[ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), which
describes momentum transported across a surface rather than locally
transferred into the state.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a vector component points along its stated
positive direction: increasing $R$, $\phi$, or $Z$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, or along the defined positive local
magnetic-field direction for a parallel component.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge
states.
NAMES.long:
Ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge
states. It retains the direction of the net transfer rather than reducing it
to a magnitude.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
\mathbf{S}_{i} = \sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{i}} \mathbf{S}_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i}$ is the total-ion momentum source vector, $z$ indexes
the ion charge states in the set $\mathcal{Z}_{i}$, and $\mathbf{S}_{i,z}$
is the corresponding source for one charge state. The [momentum
source](name:momentum_source) defines this same directional
momentum-transfer concept at the general species and projection level.

This quantity includes all ion charge states and excludes neutral species.
It is distinct from the [ion charge-state momentum
source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which resolves one state;
its axis and field-aligned projections are components of the same total-ion
vector, including the [parallel net ion momentum
source](name:parallel_net_ion_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a projected component points along its
defined positive direction—$+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; flux-coordinate
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ and field-parallel projections use their stated
positive directions.

NAMES.name: momentum_source_rate
NAMES.short:
Rate characterizing the addition, removal, or transfer of momentum to a
plasma population, expressed relative to its associated momentum content.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is a scalar rate for momentum supplied to, removed from, or
transferred within a plasma population. It describes the temporal strength
of a momentum source without selecting a particular particle species,
direction, mechanism, or spatial region.

When the source is expressed relative to the associated momentum density,
its defining relation is

$$
\nu_{p,\mathrm{src}} = \frac{S_p}{P}
$$

where $\nu_{p,\mathrm{src}}$ is the momentum source rate, $S_p$ is the
momentum source density, and $P$ is the corresponding momentum density. The
parent covers concrete specializations such as the [ion momentum source
rate](name:ion_momentum_source_rate), while excluding the momentum density
itself and any directional component not specified by the specialization.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion momentum source rate is a scalar rate coefficient for proportional
source, sink, or transfer terms in an ion momentum balance. Its population
scope is ions, while child names may add qualifiers such as an implicit
treatment; the parent does not choose a component, projection, isotope, or
charge state.
NAMES.long:
Ion momentum source rate is a scalar coefficient that parameterizes a
source, sink, or transfer term proportional to an ion momentum quantity in
an ion momentum-balance equation. Its population scope is ions, not
electrons, neutrals, or a species-free momentum balance.

For a proportional contribution to an ion momentum source term, the defining
relation is

$$
S_{M_i}^{(\gamma)} = \gamma_i M_i
$$

where $\gamma_i$ is the ion momentum source rate, $M_i$ is the associated
ion momentum quantity for the ion population under consideration, and
$S_{M_i}^{(\gamma)}$ is the corresponding proportional contribution to the
ion momentum source term.

This quantity is the rate coefficient itself, not the ion momentum, the full
source term, a force density, or a torque. The parent name does not select a
spatial component, coordinate direction, flux-surface projection, explicit
or implicit numerical treatment, isotope, or charge state; those
distinctions require more specific names.

The [implicit ion momentum source
rate](name:implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate) is an implicit-treatment
specialization of this ion parent, used when the proportional source or sink
contribution is represented implicitly. Source contributions that are not
proportional to the associated ion momentum quantity are outside this
rate-coefficient definition.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the proportional source term has the same
sign as, or acts in the same direction as, the associated ion momentum
quantity.

NAMES.name: implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Rate coefficient multiplying the primary ion momentum quantity to represent
its implicit source or sink contribution in transport equations.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the coefficient for the implicit contribution to an ion
momentum source term. It represents proportional momentum addition or
removal associated with the primary ion momentum quantity, without selecting
a particular directional component.

The implicit source contribution is defined by

$$
S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} = C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} M_i
$$

where $S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit ion momentum source
contribution, $C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is this rate coefficient, and $M_i$
is the primary ion momentum quantity to which the coefficient is applied.

The quantity applies to ion momentum and is independent of the component or
direction selected by a specialization. It describes the coefficient itself,
not the resulting momentum source and not the primary momentum quantity. A
positive coefficient represents proportional momentum sourcing, whereas a
negative coefficient represents proportional momentum removal.

It is the implicit, proportional component of the broader [ion momentum
source rate](name:ion_momentum_source_rate). The [toroidal implicit ion
momentum source rate](name:toroidal_implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate) is a
directional specialization in which the same coefficient concept is applied
to the toroidal ion momentum quantity.

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of neon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier, summed over ionization states and
excluding neutral neon.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of neon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the neon-ion
population at that flux-surface location. Neon has atomic number $Z=10$;
unless a charge state is specified separately, all neon ionization states
are included and neutral neon is excluded.

The number density is defined by

$$
n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n$ is number density, $N$ is the number of counted neon ions, and $V$
is volume. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface
location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density
gradients. This quantity is the neon-specific member of [density at the
internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier),
analogous to [carbon density at the internal transport
barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the neon ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local neon-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the neon ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local neon-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all neon ionic charge states. It represents neon ions
specifically, rather than neutral neon, electrons, or another plasma
population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne,axis}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne,axis}}$ is the total neon-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the number density of
neon ions with charge state $q$ at that location, $q$ is the positive ionic
charge-state index, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the atomic number of neon.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the neon-ion population at that location and is
summed over ionic charge states; neutral neon is excluded, and the quantity
is neither a flux-surface nor a volume integral.

This is the neon-specific realization of the population-independent [density
at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the same locus
and charge-state aggregation convention as [oxygen density at the magnetic
axis](name:oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis), but counts neon ions rather
than oxygen ions.

NAMES.name: net_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Net ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to all ion charge states, including all contributing
physical processes.
NAMES.long:
Net ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge
states. It retains the direction of the net transfer rather than reducing it
to a magnitude.

The charge-state and process aggregation is

$$
\mathbf{S}_{i} = \sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{i}}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \mathbf{S}_{i,z,p}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i}$ is the total-ion momentum source vector, $z$ indexes
ion charge states in $\mathcal{Z}_{i}$, $p$ indexes contributing physical
processes in $\mathcal{P}$, and $\mathbf{S}_{i,z,p}$ is the corresponding
source for one charge state and process. The [ion momentum
source](name:ion_momentum_source) defines the same directional
momentum-transfer concept at the general species and projection level.

This quantity includes all ion charge states and excludes neutral species.
Its directional projections are components of the same vector, including the
[parallel net ion momentum source](name:parallel_net_ion_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a projected component points along its
defined positive direction—$+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, or along the defined positive
field-parallel direction.

NAMES.name: neutral_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms
and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. Unless a resolved
variant is specified, it aggregates over neutral species, thermal and
suprathermal populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated
neutral states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms
and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. It is a pointwise
volumetric particle density, not a flux-surface-averaged or volume-averaged
quantity unless an averaging operation is part of the named quantity.

The local aggregate neutral density is defined by the neutral particle count
per volume element:

$$
n_0 = \frac{dN_0}{dV} = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathcal{P}_0} n_\alpha
$$

where $N_0$ is the number of neutral particles in the infinitesimal volume
element $dV$, $\mathcal{P}_0$ is the set of neutral population classes
included by the unresolved quantity, and $n_\alpha$ is the local density of
population class $\alpha$.

For the unresolved name, $\mathcal{P}_0$ includes neutral species, thermal
and suprathermal kinetic populations, internal quantum states, and
parent-ion-associated neutral states that are not otherwise resolved by the
standard name. When only thermal and fast kinetic classes are distinguished,
the aggregate satisfies $n_0 = n_{0,\mathrm{thermal}} +
n_{0,\mathrm{fast}}$, corresponding to
[thermal_neutral_density](name:thermal_neutral_density) and
[fast_neutral_density](name:fast_neutral_density). It excludes ions,
electrons, and any averaging represented by
[volume_averaged_density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density).

NAMES.name: neutral_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective particle diffusivity relating an internal-state-summed neutral
population's diffusive flux to its opposing number-density gradient, without
selecting a spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
The neutral diffusion coefficient characterizes particle transport driven by
the local number-density gradient of an aggregate neutral population. It
does not select a spatial direction, a particular neutral species, or a
spatial region.

For a Fickian closure along a chosen physical direction:

$$
\Gamma^{0,\mathrm{diff}}_{s} = -D_0\,\hat{\mathbf{s}}\cdot\nabla n_0
$$

where $\Gamma^{0,\mathrm{diff}}_{s}$ is the diffusive neutral particle flux
density along the unit direction vector $\hat{\mathbf{s}}$, $D_0$ is the
neutral diffusion coefficient for that closure, and $n_0$ is the neutral
number density. The operator $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient, and the
superscript or subscript $0$ identifies neutrals. The minus sign expresses
down-gradient transport for nonnegative diffusivity; choosing a direction
for this relation does not impose isotropy.

The number density and particle flux are summed over the internal states
belonging to the specified neutral population, excluding charged particles.
The effective coefficient is defined by the aggregate flux-gradient
relation, not by summing internal-state coefficients. In contrast, the
[neutral-state diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_state_diffusion_coefficient) applies to one
specified internal state. This quantity excludes convective particle flux
and is distinct from neutral energy or momentum diffusivity.

Directional specializations, such as the [radial neutral diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient), apply the same
particle flux-gradient relation to a specified direction.

NAMES.name: neutral_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral energy flux is the signed thermal energy transported across an
oriented surface per unit area and time by neutral atoms and molecules,
summed over species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral energy flux is the net thermal-energy transport carried by neutral
atoms and molecules across an oriented surface per unit area and time. It
represents a surface-normal projection of the full neutral energy-flux
vector, without selecting a particular geometrical or magnetic-field
direction.

Its defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{W,0} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,0}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n} = \frac{d\dot W_{0,\mathrm{net}}}{dA}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,0}$ is the signed neutral thermal-energy flux through the
surface, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,0}$ is the corresponding energy-flux
vector, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface unit normal, $\dot
W_{0,\mathrm{net}}$ is the net neutral thermal-energy transfer rate across
that surface, and $dA$ is an infinitesimal surface area.

Contributions are summed over the included neutral species and their
internal states; [neutral-species energy
flux](name:neutral_species_energy_flux) resolves the species contributions.
The total includes neutral thermal-energy transport without restriction to
diffusion and excludes energy carried by charged particles or radiation. It
is neither an area-integrated power nor the magnitude or sum of geometrical
vector components. Unlike [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux), it expresses energy transport rather than
particle-number transport.

The [radial neutral energy flux](name:radial_neutral_energy_flux) is the
projection along increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical
height. The [parallel neutral energy
flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux) is the projection along the local
magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral thermal energy crosses the oriented
surface in the direction of its chosen unit normal.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Number density of neutral particles of a specified species in one internal
quantum state, including both thermal and nonthermal velocity populations.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neutral

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the neutral-state
distribution:

$$
n_{s,a}^{0} = \int f_{s,a}^{0}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v = n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{th}} + n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{nt}}
$$

where $n_{s,a}^{0}$ is the total neutral-state number density, $s$ labels
the neutral species, $a$ labels its selected internal quantum state, and the
superscript $0$ denotes electrical neutrality. The function $f_{s,a}^{0}$ is
the velocity-space number distribution for that species and state, and
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity. The contributions
$n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{th}}$ and $n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{nt}}$ are the [thermal
neutral internal-state density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density)
and the [fast neutral internal-state number
density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density), respectively,
evaluated at the same location and time.

The quantity is summed over velocity populations, not over species or
internal states. Charged particles and neutral particles in other internal
states are excluded. The definition applies locally or to a flux-surface
average in the closed-field-line region; an evaluation at the outboard
equatorial midplane in the scrape-off layer is local rather than
flux-surface averaged.

Summing this state-resolved density over all internal states of the same
neutral species gives the [neutral-species
density](name:neutral_species_density). The thermal contribution alone
excludes the nonthermal particles included here.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective transport velocity multiplying the thermal energy-density factor
to give the convective energy flux of one neutral species in a specified
internal state.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal-state energy convection velocity is the effective
vector coefficient describing convective thermal-energy transport by one
neutral species in a specified internal state. It is the population-resolved
specialization of [energy convection
velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity), without restriction to a
particular direction.

The convective contribution is defined by:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{0,a,\mathrm{conv}} = W_{0,a}\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W} = n_{0,a}T_{0,a}\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{0,a,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective thermal-energy
flux, $\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}$ is this energy convection velocity, and
$W_{0,a}=n_{0,a}T_{0,a}$ is the thermal energy-density factor used in the
transport closure. Here $n_{0,a}$ is the population number density and
$T_{0,a}$ is its temperature expressed as an energy; the subscript $0$
identifies neutrals and $a$ identifies the specified internal state of the
selected species.

This quantity is resolved by neutral species and internal state, with no sum
or average over either. Its flux contribution excludes gradient-driven
diffusion and any separately specified energy transport proportional to the
particle flux; it therefore does not represent the total energy flux. As an
effective energy-channel coefficient, it need not equal the [bulk neutral
internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity).

The [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity)
and [poloidal
component](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity)
are directional projections of this vector for the same population. The
poloidal direction is defined in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$,
where $\rho$ labels magnetic flux surfaces, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle,
and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the parallel component transports thermal
energy along the local magnetic field, or the poloidal component transports
thermal energy toward increasing $\theta$.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying
the temperature gradient of neutral particles in one internal state in
diffusive thermal-energy transport, serving as the direction-agnostic parent
over its radial and poloidal component forms.
NAMES.long:
Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar
diffusivity that relates Fickian diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by
neutral particles in a specified internal state to the temperature gradient
of those same particles. It is resolved for one internal state, not summed
or averaged over internal states, and is independent of any chosen spatial
projection.

The isotropic Fickian contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s} = - n_{n,s} D_{E,n,s} \nabla T_{n,s}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy
flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, $n_{n,s}$ is their
number density, $D_{E,n,s}$ is this coefficient, and $T_{n,s}$ is their
temperature.

The coefficient includes only the Fickian term driven by $\nabla T_{n,s}$
and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, and effective
coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. It specializes the
internal-state energy diffusion coefficient to neutral particles and is the
internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

As the direction-agnostic parent, it is distinct from the [radial neutral
internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral internal-state energy flux is the net thermal energy transported per
unit area and time across an oriented surface by one neutral species in one
specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state energy flux describes thermal-energy transport across
an oriented surface by neutral particles of one species in one specified
internal state. It is direction-agnostic: the surface orientation determines
which projection of the transport is represented.

The local flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{0,s,W} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{0,s}^{\mathrm{net}}}{\partial A\,\partial t} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,s,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,s,W}$ is the signed surface-normal thermal-energy flux,
$W_{0,s}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net thermal energy transferred through the
surface, $A$ is surface area, $t$ is time, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,s,W}$ is
the corresponding thermal-energy transport vector, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is
the chosen surface unit normal. The subscripts $0$, $s$, and $W$ identify
the neutral population, specified internal state, and energy channel,
respectively.

The quantity is not summed over internal states or neutral species and is
not restricted to a single transport mechanism. It is a flux density, not a
surface-integrated power or particle-number flux; the internal-state label
selects the carrier population rather than identifying an excitation-energy
flux.

Summing the underlying transport vectors over all internal states of the
same species gives the [neutral-species energy
flux](name:neutral_species_energy_flux). The [poloidal
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) and [field-parallel
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) are projections of
the same state-resolved transport vector onto the local poloidal direction
and local magnetic-field direction, respectively.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net thermal energy carried by the selected
neutral population crosses the surface in the direction of the chosen unit
normal.
