NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless closure parameter that limits the admissible energy-flux
density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient specifies the strength of the limiter applied to energy
transport by neutral particles occupying one selected internal state. It is
a closure parameter rather than an energy flux or an energy density.

The limiter imposes the bound

$$
\lvert \mathbf{q}_E \rvert \leq \alpha_E q_{E,\max}
$$

where $\alpha_E$ is this flux-limiter coefficient, $\mathbf{q}_E$ is the
energy-flux-density vector carried by the selected neutral internal state,
and $q_{E,\max}$ is the prescribed maximum admissible magnitude for that
energy flux.

The coefficient applies to the energy channel of neutral transport for the
specified internal state. It does not sum over neutral internal states or
neutral species, does not represent the energy flux itself, and has no
edge-region restriction in its definition. It is distinct from the
corresponding momentum limiter, such as the [neutral internal-state momentum
flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region),
which constrains momentum rather than energy transport.

The coefficient scales the admissible energy-flux bound in the closure:
increasing $\alpha_E$ permits a larger maximum energy flux relative to
$q_{E,\max}$, while the coefficient itself remains a dimensionless scalar.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy flux limiter coefficient, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient is the vector
kinematic transport coefficient in Fick's-law down-gradient transport of
momentum density carried by neutrals in a specified electronic, vibrational,
or rotational state. Its directional children specify the flux and gradient
direction, not the transported momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient is the vector
kinematic transport coefficient in Fick's-law down-gradient transport of
momentum density carried by neutrals occupying a specified electronic,
vibrational, or rotational internal state. It is the direction-agnostic
parent whose directional members identify the direction of flux and
gradient, while the transported quantity remains the full momentum vector of
that state-resolved neutral population.

For a diagonal directional member in transport direction $j$, the defining
Fick law is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j} = -D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}\,\frac{\partial \mathbf{M}_{\alpha}}{\partial x_j}
$$

where $\alpha$ denotes the specified neutral internal state,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j}$ is the vector diffusive flux
of momentum through surfaces normal to direction $j$,
$D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}$ is the corresponding diagonal momentum
diffusion coefficient, $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$ is the momentum density carried
by neutrals in state $\alpha$, and $x_j$ is a coordinate increasing along
the flux and gradient direction. The superscript $\mathrm{mom}$ labels
momentum transport, not a transported momentum component; the minus sign
gives down-gradient transport of each component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$.

This parent covers diagonal directional coefficients only: a directional
qualifier selects $j$, the flux and gradient direction, and not a component
of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$; off-diagonal tensor transport, where a gradient
along one direction contributes to flux through another, is outside this
standard name. The radial and toroidal directional children use $\hat{R}$
and $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height;
the poloidal directional child uses the direction tangent to the poloidal
circuit in a meridional plane spanned by $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$.

The defining gradient is the gradient of internal-state momentum density; a
form proportional only to a neutral velocity gradient represents the same
coefficient only when the state-resolved mass density is uniform or treated
outside the gradient. This quantity belongs to the [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) family, has the same internal-state
resolution as internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient, differs from
[neutral momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) by resolving the
neutral population by internal state, and differs from [neutral
internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) by
transporting momentum rather than energy.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Vector flux-limiter coefficient that sets an edge-region, nonnegative
componentwise cap on neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a specified
internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming bound,
without reversing any flux component.
NAMES.long:
Vector flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles occupying
a specified internal state over the edge region is the set of directional
coefficients used to bound components of the corresponding neutral
internal-state momentum-flux density. The internal state may be an
electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation state, and
the coefficient applies separately to each physical direction used to
decompose the momentum-flux vector.

For directional component $k$, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},k}| \le \lambda_k\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},k}|,\qquad 0 \le \lambda_k \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},k}$ is the limited directional component of the
neutral internal-state momentum flux over the edge region,
$\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},k}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
component whose magnitude defines the bound, $\lambda_k$ is this coefficient
component, and $k$ indexes a physical direction rather than the internal
state. If a component is specified in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, then $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when
viewed from $+\hat{Z}$, $Z$ is vertical height, and $k$ may identify an
$\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ projection; field-aligned components
use their explicitly named local directions, such as parallel to the
magnetic field.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the
realized momentum flux. Because $\lambda_k$ is nonnegative, applying the
limiter may reduce or bound a signed momentum-flux component but does not
reverse its direction; a nonzero limited component retains the sign of the
underlying component to which the cap is applied. This coefficient is not
the momentum-flux vector itself and is distinct from limiters for particle
flux or energy flux.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single
resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral
population. It includes charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and
elastic collisions.
NAMES.long:
Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single
resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral
population after normalization by the transport area. It represents the
vector rate at which charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic
collisions add momentum to, or remove momentum from, that resolved neutral
state.

The defining process decomposition is:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)} = \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cx}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{ion}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{rec}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{el}}
$$

where \(\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)}\) is this momentum source for neutral
species \(n\) in internal state \(\alpha\), and the terms on the right are
the contributions from charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and
elastic collisions, respectively.

The quantity is resolved for one neutral species and one internal state; it
is not the state-summed [neutral momentum
source](name:neutral_momentum_source), which is obtained by summing this
vector over all resolved internal states of that neutral species. It is the
neutral-state analog of the [ion charge-state momentum
source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), with resolution by internal
state rather than ion charge state. A directional component such as the
[radial neutral-internal-state momentum
source](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) is the
projection of this vector onto the corresponding direction; `radial` denotes
the \(\hat{R}\) component in the right-handed cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\)
frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})\).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a vector component represents momentum
transferred to the neutral species in the resolved internal state along the
positive basis direction used for that component; in the right-handed
cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\) frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi},
\hat{Z})\), the radial, toroidal, and vertical components are positive along
\(+\hat{R}\), increasing toroidal angle \(\phi\), and \(+\hat{Z}\),
respectively.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Velocity characterizing convective momentum transport by neutral particles
in a resolved internal quantum state, forming the bulk-flow coefficient in
the neutral internal-state momentum flux equation.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity is the fluid
velocity at which momentum is transported by bulk convective flow in a
neutral particle population that is resolved by internal quantum state (such
as a vibrational, rotational, or electronic level). It enters the neutral
momentum transport equation as the convective coefficient of the
state-resolved momentum flux:

$$
\Pi_{\rm conv,s} = m_n n_s v_{\rm conv,s}
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_s$ is the number density of
internal state $s$, and $v_{\rm conv,s}$ is this convection velocity for
state $s$.

This is the neutral-species-specific form of the internal-state momentum
convection velocity, enabling state-resolved neutral momentum transport to
be tracked separately from ionic or electron channels. Its effective
counterpart,
[effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection),
incorporates transport contributions beyond simple bulk advection that enter
the convective momentum channel. For comparison,
neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection describes the
corresponding convective velocity for particle (number) transport rather
than momentum transport.

NAMES.name: effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective advective drift velocity of neutral particles in a specified
internal state for convective momentum transport; it multiplies the
population's momentum density to form the convective momentum flux.
NAMES.long:
Effective advective drift velocity of neutral particles in a specified
internal state for convective momentum transport is the vector transport
coefficient that multiplies the population's momentum-density vector to give
the convective momentum-flux tensor. It represents the advective velocity
appearing in a momentum-transport closure for that resolved neutral
internal-state population.

The convective momentum flux is defined by the outer-product relation

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\alpha} = \boldsymbol{g}_{\alpha} \otimes \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\alpha}$ is the convective
momentum-flux tensor of neutral particles in internal state $\alpha$,
$\boldsymbol{g}_{\alpha}$ is their momentum-density vector, and
$\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}$ is this effective convective
momentum velocity.

The effective qualifier means the coefficient is defined by this
momentum-flux closure and need not equal the neutral population's
microscopic mean particle velocity. It is the momentum-transport analog of
[effective neutral internal-state velocity due to
convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection),
which enters the convective particle-flux relation, and is distinguished
from the non-effective counterpart [neutral internal-state momentum velocity
due to
convection](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection).
This name denotes the full vector; [radial effective neutral internal-state
momentum velocity due to
convection](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
denotes its cylindrical $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a vector component of
$\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}$ is aligned with the positive
direction of the corresponding explicitly chosen basis vector.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Signed surface-normal particle flux density of neutral atoms or molecules in
a specified internal quantum state, giving the net number crossing unit area
per unit time.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal-state particle flux is the surface-normal component of
the particle flux vector for neutral atoms or molecules occupying a
specified internal quantum state (such as a vibrational, rotational, or
electronic level). It quantifies the net number of neutral particles in that
state crossing an oriented surface element per unit area per unit time, and
specializes internal_state_particle_flux to the neutral-particle
subpopulation.

The defining relation for neutral species $\alpha$ in internal state $s$ is:

$$
\Gamma_{\alpha,s} = \int f_{\alpha,s}(\mathbf{v})\, \mathbf{v} \cdot \hat{n} \, d^3v
$$

where $f_{\alpha,s}$ is the velocity distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is
the particle velocity, and $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal to the reference
surface. Summing $\Gamma_{\alpha,s}$ over all internal states $s$ recovers
the total neutral particle flux for species $\alpha$.

Projected onto specific coordinate directions, this quantity yields
[radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux)
and the equivalently defined poloidal and magnetic-field-parallel
components. The energy transported by the same state-resolved neutral
population is captured by
[neutral_internal_state_energy_flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net neutral particle flow is in the
direction of $\hat{n}$.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle flux in the direction perpendicular to the edges or faces of the grid (flow crossing that surface divided by its actual area), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper
bound on particle flux for a neutral species in a specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient limits particle transport for one neutral species in one
specified internal state by setting the permitted fraction of its
collisionless free-streaming particle flux bound.

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}} \le f_{\mathrm{p}}\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limiting particle-flux magnitude,
$f_{\mathrm{p}}$ is this particle flux-limiter coefficient, and
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming particle-flux
bound.

The coefficient applies to the particle channel only and to the specified
neutral internal state. No summation over neutral species or internal states
is implied, and the coefficient does not limit energy or momentum transport.
A physical limiter is nonnegative and, when used as a fraction of the
free-streaming bound, satisfies $0 \le f_{\mathrm{p}} \le 1$.

The quantity is distinct from the [neutral momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which limits
momentum transport rather than particle transport. It also differs from the
[neutral internal-state source
rate](name:neutral_internal_state_source_rate), which represents particle
creation or destruction rather than a bound on transported particle flux.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle flux limiter coefficient, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Pressure of a neutral species in one internal quantum or excitation state,
equal to the isotropic part of the selected population's translational
kinetic stress.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or
excitation state is one-third of the trace of their translational pressure
tensor. It describes the isotropic part of that tensor without requiring an
isotropic velocity distribution.

For a selected neutral population, the defining kinetic moment is:

$$
p_{0,s,a}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{3}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{0,s,a}(\mathbf{x})|^2 f_{0,s,a}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{0,s,a}$ is the state-resolved neutral pressure, $0$ denotes
electrical neutrality, $s$ labels the neutral species, $a$ labels its
internal state, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_s$ is the particle mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{0,s,a}$ is the velocity distribution
of the selected population, $\mathbf{u}_{0,s,a}$ is its mean translational
velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The selected population may be thermal, suprathermal, or their combination.
The quantity retains one species and one internal state: it is neither
summed over species or internal states nor averaged over those states.
Internal excitation energy is not included in this translational moment, and
bulk-flow momentum flux is excluded by subtracting the mean velocity.

The [thermal neutral internal-state
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) restricts this
definition to thermal particles. The [total neutral internal-state
pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) includes both thermal
and nonthermal particles within the same specified state; it does not denote
a sum over internal states. Contributions from a population decomposition
are additive when evaluated relative to the same mean-flow velocity.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_source_rate
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which particles enter or leave one specified internal state of a
neutral species.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which particles enter or leave one specified internal state of a
neutral species. It supplies the source term in that state's particle-number
density transport equation, separately from spatial transport by particle
flux.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_{0,a}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}-S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{0,a}$ is the neutral internal-state source rate,
$S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}$ and $S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}$ are the local
volumetric rates of particle addition and removal, respectively, $0$ denotes
electrically neutral particles, $a$ identifies the specified internal state,
$\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$
denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity applies to one neutral species and one internal energy or
excitation state, not to a nonzero ionic charge state. It is averaged over
each magnetic flux surface but is not summed over internal states or neutral
species. Positive values indicate net particle gain in the selected state;
negative values indicate net loss. It describes particle number, not
internal-energy transfer or particle flow through a surface.

Summing over all internal states of the same neutral species gives the
aggregate [neutral source rate](name:neutral_source_rate): $S_0=\sum_a
S_{0,a}$, where $S_0$ is that species' aggregate source rate. Transfers
between internal states contribute oppositely to the participating state
source rates and cancel in this sum.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_temperature
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Temperature of neutral particles in one specified internal state sets the
energy scale of their random translational motion after subtracting that
population's mean flow.
NAMES.long:
Temperature of neutral particles in a specified internal state characterizes
their random translational kinetic energy relative to the bulk motion of
that state-resolved population. The internal-state label selects a quantum
or excitation state; it does not make this an internal-excitation
temperature.

A cold or hot neutral temperature is that of the named component alone;
without the component it covers the whole neutral population of the selected
species.

Using temperature in its energy-equivalent form, the defining second-moment
relation is

$$
T_{0,a} = \frac{m_0}{3n_{0,a}}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{0,a}|^2 f_{0,a}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved neutral temperature, $m_0$ is the
neutral-particle mass, $n_{0,a}$ is the number density of that population,
$f_{0,a}$ is its velocity distribution normalized to that number density,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\mathbf{u}_{0,a}$ is its [bulk
translational velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). The
subscript $0$ identifies neutral particles, $a$ labels the specified
internal state, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies locally to one neutral species in one internal state,
without summing or averaging over internal states, species, or spatial
regions. It excludes directed bulk kinetic energy and the energy stored in
internal excitation. It is the state-resolved counterpart of [neutral
temperature](name:neutral_temperature), retaining an internal-state
restriction that the species-level quantity does not.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles in one specified
internal quantum or energy state, given by the first moment of their
velocity distribution.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles
occupying one specified internal state, such as a quantum or energy state.
It retains resolution of that state rather than combining distinct neutral
internal states.

The state-resolved bulk velocity is the first velocity moment of the
corresponding distribution:

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\alpha} = \frac{\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}{\int f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}$ is the bulk velocity, $\alpha$ identifies the
internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{\alpha}$ is the
velocity distribution for that state.

This is the neutral specialization of internal_state_velocity. Unlike
[neutral_velocity](name:neutral_velocity), which may combine or resolve
internal states, this quantity is defined for one specified state. The full
vector is the parent quantity for projections such as
[radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity)
and
[poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component points along its corresponding
positive unit vector $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles in one specified
internal quantum or energy state, given by the first moment of their
velocity distribution.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles
occupying one specified internal state, such as a quantum or energy state.
It retains resolution of that state rather than combining distinct neutral
internal states.

The state-resolved bulk velocity is the first velocity moment of the
corresponding distribution:

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}} = \frac{\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}{\int f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$ is the state-resolved bulk
neutral velocity, $\alpha$ identifies the internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $f_{\alpha}$ is the neutral-particle velocity
distribution for that state.

This is the direction-agnostic vector parent for component projections of
the same bulk neutral population in the same resolved internal state; it is
not itself a radial, toroidal, poloidal, or vertical component. Component
quantities such as [vertical bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity) are
projections of this vector, with the vertical component defined along
$\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes
thermal speed and velocity spread, which are moments about the bulk velocity
rather than this first velocity moment.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved cylindrical component is directed
along the corresponding positive unit vector $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or
$+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral internal-state velocity due to convection is a scalar
advective-velocity quantity characterizing convective transport of neutral
particles in a specified internal quantum state. It does not by itself
choose a spatial projection or effective-vector convention; concrete
specializations provide that extra semantics.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state velocity due to convection is a scalar
advective-velocity quantity characterizing convective transport of neutral
particles in a specified internal quantum state. It denotes the velocity
factor for the convective part of state-resolved neutral-particle transport,
abstracted over the particular scalar component, projection, magnitude, or
effective reduction chosen by a concrete specialization.

For any scalar realization $q$ of the convective neutral flux for internal
state $a$, the defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)} = n_a v_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)}$ is the scalar convective
particle-flux realization for neutrals in internal state $a$, $n_a$ is the
neutral-particle number density in that internal state, and
$v_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)}$ is the corresponding neutral internal-state
velocity due to convection.

This parent name is not the unprojected vector itself and does not define a
unique positive direction. A child such as [effective neutral internal-state
velocity due to
convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection)
specializes the parent by adding the effective, unprojected-vector
interpretation; other children may specialize it by component, projection,
or magnitude semantics.

NAMES.name: effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective vector velocity for convective transport of neutral particles in a
specified internal quantum state, without selecting a particular spatial
component.
NAMES.long:
The effective neutral internal-state convection velocity is the vector that
represents particle transport caused by convection for one specified
internal quantum state. It is an advective transport velocity, distinct from
the bulk translational velocity of that state,
[neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity).

The effective velocity is defined from the convective particle flux:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{conv}} = n\,\boldsymbol{v}_{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective particle-flux
vector, $n$ is the number density of neutral particles in the specified
state, and $\boldsymbol{v}_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective velocity.

The vector includes all spatial components. Its radial component is
represented by
[radial_effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection](name:radial_effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection);
this quantity concerns particle convection rather than velocity associated
specifically with convective momentum transport, represented by
[neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection).
Components are interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each component points along its positive
direction: $+\hat{R}$, toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, or
$+\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective vector velocity at which neutral particle momentum is advectively
transported in edge-plasma fluid models, aggregated over all neutral species
and excited states as a transport closure coefficient distinct from the
actual neutral particle flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum convection velocity is the effective bulk vector
velocity appearing in the non-diffusive, advective contribution to neutral
momentum transport in edge-plasma and scrape-off-layer fluid models. It
encapsulates the net effect of charge-exchange, ionization, and
recombination reactions on the aggregate neutral momentum balance across all
neutral species and excited states, serving as a transport closure
coefficient rather than the physical flow speed of any individual neutral
population.

In multi-fluid edge-plasma transport frameworks, the total neutral momentum
flux is decomposed into a diffusive part proportional to the local
momentum-density gradient and a convective (pinch-like) part proportional to
the momentum density:

$$
\mathbf{F}_p = -D_p \nabla p_n + \mathbf{V}_c \, p_n
$$

where $D_p$ is the neutral momentum diffusivity and $p_n$ is the neutral
momentum density. The convection velocity $\mathbf{V}_c$ (this quantity)
drives advective momentum transport independently of the local gradient,
functioning as a neutral momentum pinch.

The quantity is computed in fluid neutral transport solvers as a closure
derived from atomic physics rate coefficients and the local plasma state.
Its directional projections include the
radial_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($R$ component) and the
vertical_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($Z$ component) in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The analogous
charge-state-resolved quantity is
[radial_neutral_state_effective_momentum_convection_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity).
The parent momentum_convection_velocity establishes the general
momentum-flux decomposition framework from which this neutral-species
specialization is derived.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Vector diffusion coefficient governing diffusive transport of momentum in
the neutral particle population, with directional components representing
anisotropic momentum diffusivities along the radial, poloidal, and toroidal
directions.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum diffusion coefficient quantifies the effective
diffusivity that drives collisional and turbulent spreading of
neutral-particle momentum down local velocity gradients. As a vector
quantity, its components represent the diagonal entries of the momentum
diffusion tensor for neutrals in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, capturing anisotropy across the radial, poloidal, and toroidal
directions independently.

The diffusive neutral momentum flux density along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is
governed by:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{diff},i} = -\rho_n \, D_{\mathrm{mom},i} \, \frac{\partial u_{n,i}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\rho_n$ is the neutral mass density, $u_{n,i}$ is the neutral flow
velocity component along $\hat{e}_i$, and $D_{\mathrm{mom},i}$ is the
corresponding directional component of this coefficient.

In edge plasma modeling, the dominant physical mechanisms determining this
diffusivity are charge-exchange with background ions, neutral-neutral
collisions, and elastic scattering; the resulting coefficient is strongly
anisotropic in realistic magnetic geometries. The
radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient gives the cross-field
component driving transport across magnetic flux surfaces. For comparison,
the analogous momentum diffusivity for the bulk plasma is captured by
plasma_momentum_diffusivity, and the toroidal ion channel counterpart is
described by toroidal_momentum_diffusivity.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Vector diffusion coefficient for bulk neutral-particle momentum, governing
anisotropic diffusive redistribution driven by neutral-neutral viscosity and
charge-exchange collisions in edge and divertor plasma.
NAMES.long:
Neutral momentum diffusivity is the direction-dependent transport
coefficient that relates the diffusive neutral-fluid momentum flux in each
spatial direction to the local gradient of neutral momentum density, forming
the neutral-particle analog of plasma_momentum_diffusivity. As a vector
quantity it encompasses distinct directional components — including
parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity,
poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity,
[toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity),
and
[vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity)
— reflecting the anisotropy imposed by the magnetic geometry and the varying
collisional regimes of edge and divertor regions.

The component $\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom}}$ along a direction $\hat{e}$ enters the
neutral fluid momentum balance through the diffusive flux:

$$
\Gamma_{n,\mathrm{mom}} = -\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom}} \, \nabla_{\hat{e}}(m_n n_n u_n)
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number
density, and $u_n$ is the neutral fluid velocity component along $\hat{e}$.

The dominant physical mechanisms contributing to neutral momentum
diffusivity are neutral-neutral viscous collisions and charge-exchange
interactions with background ions; the latter can transfer substantial
momentum between the neutral and ion populations and are especially
significant in dense regions where charge-exchange mean-free paths are
short. This coefficient is computed within fluid-neutral transport models
that solve the neutral momentum equation self-consistently alongside the
plasma fluid equations.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Rate per unit area at which neutral atoms and molecules transport linear
momentum across an oriented surface in the edge plasma, combining convective
and isotropic-pressure contributions summed over all neutral species and
internal states.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum flux describes the rate at which the collective neutral
population transports linear momentum across a unit area of an oriented
surface in the edge plasma. It captures both the directed convective flow of
neutral particles and the isotropic thermal pressure of the neutral gas,
aggregated over all neutral species and their internal quantum states.

The neutral momentum-flux tensor $\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n$ is:

$$
\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n = m_n n_n \mathbf{v}_n \mathbf{v}_n + p_n \mathbf{I}
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number
density, $\mathbf{v}_n$ is the bulk neutral velocity, $p_n = n_n k_B T_n$ is
the neutral thermal pressure with $T_n$ the neutral temperature, and
$\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor. The divergence of this tensor drives
the neutral momentum balance equation and couples neutral dynamics to the
ion fluid through charge-exchange and elastic collisions.

This quantity is evaluated within edge fluid or kinetic neutral transport
models rather than measured directly. Directional projections include
toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux,
[poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux),
[vertical_neutral_momentum_flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux), and
[parallel_neutral_momentum_flux](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux) along
the local magnetic-field direction. The analogous ion-fluid momentum
transport rate is
[radial_edge_ion_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_momentum_flux_over_edge_region),
while the effective convective transport coefficient for neutral momentum is
radial_neutral_effective_momentum_convection_velocity.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of
linear momentum carried by neutral particles and attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
NAMES.long:
Neutral momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of
linear momentum carried by neutral particles and attributed to the
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic contribution. It is the neutral-species
specialization of [momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

With $i$ denoting the transported momentum component and $j$ denoting the
flux direction, the underlying diamagnetic contribution is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,ij} = \rho_n u_{n,i} v^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,j}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,ij}$ is the neutral momentum-flux contribution,
$\rho_n$ is neutral mass density, $u_{n,i}$ is the neutral velocity
component carrying momentum, and $v^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,j}$ is the velocity
contribution associated with diamagnetic drift.

This quantity includes only the diamagnetic contribution and excludes
neutral momentum flux attributed to other transport mechanisms. It is not
resolved by internal neutral state, unlike [neutral state momentum flux due
to diamagnetic
drift](name:neutral_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and the
name imposes no particular momentum component or flux direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral momentum is transported in the
positive direction of the oriented flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Diamagnetic component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Momentum flux, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population,
summed over all neutral internal states, giving the net directed rate of
momentum transfer.
NAMES.long:
Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population is
the net directed rate of momentum transfer to all neutral internal states.

The aggregate source is the sum of the contributions from each resolved
neutral internal state:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{N}}\mathbf{S}_{n,a}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{n}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum source density,
$\mathcal{N}$ is the set of neutral internal states, and $\mathbf{S}_{n,a}$
is the [neutral internal-state momentum
source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) for state $a$. It is
the neutral specialization of the general [momentum
source](name:momentum_source), and its projections include the [poloidal
neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source) and toroidal
counterpart.

The quantity is summed over neutral internal states and is not a
single-state source. Its vector direction is retained rather than reduced to
a magnitude.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each resolved component points along its
designated positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, or along the local magnetic-field direction for a parallel
projection.

NAMES.name: neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral particle flux is the signed net number of particles of one neutral
atomic or molecular species crossing an oriented surface per unit area and
time, summed over internal states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral particle flux is the local net number flow of particles of one
neutral atomic or molecular species through an oriented surface, divided by
its actual area. It counts crossings in opposite directions with opposite
signs, without selecting a fixed geometric or magnetic-field direction.

The flux is the surface-normal velocity moment of the neutral distribution:

$$
\Gamma_0 = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})\,f_0(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_0$ is the neutral particle flux, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit normal to the surface, $f_0$
is the velocity distribution of the specified neutral species summed over
its internal states, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
integral covers all particle velocities.

The quantity includes all internal states of the specified species and
excludes ions and other neutral species. It equals the sum of the
corresponding [neutral internal-state particle
fluxes](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) through the same oriented
surface. It is not a one-way incident flux, a surface-integrated particle
rate, or the energy-weighted transport represented by [neutral energy
flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).

The [radial](name:radial_neutral_particle_flux),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), and [parallel neutral
particle fluxes](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux) are projections of the
same neutral particle-number transport onto their respective specified
directions. The general quantity instead uses the normal of the surface
under consideration and is not the magnitude of the particle-flux vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net neutral particle flow crosses the
surface in the direction of its chosen unit normal.

NAMES.name: neutral_source_rate
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Neutral source rate is the flux-surface-averaged net gain or loss of
particles of a specified neutral species per physical volume and time.
NAMES.long:
Neutral source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which
particles enter or leave a specified neutral species. It supplies the
particle-number source term in that species' density continuity equation.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_0(\psi)=\left\langle S_{0,\mathrm{gain}}-S_{0,\mathrm{loss}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_0$ is the neutral source rate, $S_{0,\mathrm{gain}}$ and
$S_{0,\mathrm{loss}}$ are the nonnegative local rates of neutral particle
production and removal, $\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity is summed over all internal states of the specified neutral
atomic or molecular species, not over different species. It combines
contributing source and sink processes, including ionization losses and
recombination gains. Charge exchange contributes through its net effect on
the specified species; transitions solely between its neutral internal
states cancel in the state sum. Charged particles are excluded, and the rate
is not integrated over the enclosed plasma volume.

The divergence of the [neutral particle flux](name:neutral_particle_flux)
supplies the spatial-transport term in the same continuity equation, whereas
this source describes particle production or removal. Unlike the [thermal
particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), this quantity
selects its population by charge neutrality rather than membership in a
thermal population.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when contributing processes produce a net gain of
particles of the specified neutral species; negative values indicate net
removal.

NAMES.name: neutral_species_atomic_mass
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Neutral-species atomic mass is the neutral-atom reference mass per atom of a
selected elemental or isotopic constituent, including its bound electrons.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-species atomic mass is the reference mass assigned to one atom of a
selected elemental or isotopic constituent of a neutral species. It
specifies atomic composition using the neutral reference atom, including its
bound electrons.

The atomic mass is related to the corresponding relative atomic mass by

$$
m = A_{\mathrm r}\,m_{\mathrm u}
$$

where $m$ is the constituent's reference atomic mass, $A_{\mathrm r}$ is its
relative atomic mass, and $m_{\mathrm u}$ is the atomic mass constant,
defined as one twelfth of the rest mass of a free neutral carbon-12 atom in
its ground state.

The value applies per constituent atom, whether the neutral species is
atomic or molecular; it is not the total molecular mass or the mass of the
neutral population. It is a physical mass, not the integer nucleon count
called the mass number, a mass density, or a mass flow rate. The number of
constituent atoms per particle is specified separately by [atomic
count](name:atomic_count).

This quantity specializes [atomic mass](name:atomic_mass) to constituents of
neutral species. Unlike [neutral-beam atomic
mass](name:neutral_beam_atomic_mass), its scope is not restricted to atoms
in an injected beam.

NAMES.name: neutral_species_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Neutral species energy flux is the signed neutral-species
energy-flux-density vector; its projection normal to an oriented surface
gives the crossing power per unit area for one specified neutral species,
summed over all internal states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral species energy flux is the signed energy-flux-density vector carried
by one specified neutral atom or molecule species. Its projection onto an
oriented surface normal gives the rate at which energy carried by that
neutral species crosses the surface per unit area, summed over all internal
states of the species and including convective and conductive contributions
when those channels are in scope.

For an oriented surface with unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, the signed
surface-normal flux associated with the neutral-species energy flux
$\mathbf{q}_{E,N_s}$ is defined by

$$
F_{E,N_s}^{(\hat{\mathbf{n}})} = \mathbf{q}_{E,N_s} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $N_s$ labels the selected neutral species, the subscript $E$ denotes
energy transport, $\mathbf{q}_{E,N_s}$ is the neutral-species
energy-flux-density vector, $F_{E,N_s}^{(\hat{\mathbf{n}})}$ is its signed
surface-normal projection, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive
crossing direction.

This quantity applies to one selected neutral species in the neutral
population and is aggregated by summing contributions from all internal
states of that species. It is species-resolved: it is not the all-neutral
[neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux), not total plasma energy
flux, not an electromagnetic Poynting flux, and not [electron energy
flux](name:electron_energy_flux) or [ion energy flux](name:ion_energy_flux).

The vector may be projected onto specified directions to form directional
components. [Poloidal neutral species energy
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_species_energy_flux) is the poloidal directional
component of this neutral-species vector, whereas this parent quantity does
not itself select a poloidal, parallel, or surface-normal projection. When
the same energy channels and internal-state aggregation are used, summing
this species-resolved vector over neutral species gives the all-neutral
[neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neutral-species energy-flux-density
vector has a component in the chosen positive projection direction or chosen
unit normal to an oriented surface.

NAMES.name: neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Vector velocity attributed to a specified species or internal state for
motion associated with crossed local electric and magnetic fields.
NAMES.long:
The E×B-drift velocity is the vector velocity attributed to a particle
population or specified internal state for motion associated with crossed
local electric and magnetic fields.

For a nonzero magnetic field, the ideal drift contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}=\frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
local magnetic-field vector, and $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}$ is the attributed
drift velocity. The quantity represents only the E×B-drift contribution and
excludes other drift mechanisms. For neutral internal states, it is an
assigned kinematic velocity associated with the local fields rather than
direct acceleration by the Lorentz force; its vertical component is
represented by [vertical neutral species internal-state E×B-drift
velocity](name:vertical_neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component points along increasing $R$,
$\phi$, or $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Momentum convection velocity is an effective velocity coefficient for
advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum carried by one neutral
species, aggregated over its neutral states.
NAMES.long:
Momentum convection velocity is an effective velocity coefficient for
advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum carried by a specified
neutral species. Its neutral-species form aggregates momentum over all
resolved neutral internal states and is distinct from the material bulk
velocity.

For a resolved transport direction $i$ and transported momentum component
$j$, the advective contribution to the momentum-flux tensor is defined by:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{adv}}_{ij}=V_iP_j
$$

where $P_j$ is the selected momentum-density component,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{adv}}_{ij}$ is its advective flux, and $V_i$ is the
corresponding effective transport velocity. For a vector quantity, the
resolved $V_i$ values form the effective transport-velocity vector.

The coefficient applies only to the selected neutral species, momentum
component, and transport direction; it excludes diffusive transport,
external source terms, and the material bulk velocity. It is the
neutral-species realization of momentum convection velocity. The [toroidal
neutral-species
form](name:toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity) and
[vertical neutral-species
form](name:vertical_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity) show that
the component label identifies the transported momentum in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, not necessarily the direction of the
effective velocity.

NAMES.name: neutral_state_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity multiplying the number density of neutral particles in a
specified internal state to give their convective particle flux.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-state convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient of the
density-proportional advective particle flux for one resolved internal state
of a neutral species. It describes directed particle transport after
density-gradient-driven diffusion has been separated.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_s\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the specified internal state of the neutral species,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its convective particle flux,
$n_s$ is its particle number density, and $\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$
is this effective convection velocity.

The coefficient applies to the particle-number balance of that species and
state, including both thermal and nonthermal particles. It is not summed or
averaged over internal states or neutral species. The vector definition has
no prescribed directional projection; for transport across magnetic flux
surfaces, its outward-normal projection distinguishes outward convection
from inward pinch.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and does
not represent a heat- or momentum-transport coefficient. It need not equal
the [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), which is the first
velocity moment of the state's particle distribution.

When internal states of the same species are combined, their convective
particle fluxes add. Consequently, the corresponding [effective
neutral-particle convection
velocity](name:effective_neutral_particle_convection_velocity) is the
number-density-weighted mean of the state-resolved coefficients, not their
sum.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the flux-surface-normal convective transport
is outward toward the last closed flux surface; negative when it is inward
toward the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: neutral_state_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient that limits the energy flux density of neutrals in
a specified internal state relative to its collisionless free-streaming
bound.
NAMES.long:
The energy-flux limiter coefficient for a specified neutral internal state
is a dimensionless factor that sets the maximum allowed energy flux density
carried by that state relative to its collisionless free-streaming bound.

The limiting relation is

$$
|q_E| \leq \alpha_E q_{E,\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $q_E$ is the energy flux density carried by neutrals in the specified
internal state, $\alpha_E$ is this energy-flux limiter coefficient, and
$q_{E,\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
energy-flux bound.

The coefficient applies only to energy transport by the specified neutral
internal state; it is not summed over other neutral internal states and does
not limit ion, electron, momentum, or particle flux. It is the neutral-state
specialization of the broader [energy flux-limiter
coefficient](name:energy_flux_limiter_coefficient). The related [neutral
momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) has the same
neutral-particle scope but limits momentum-flux density rather than
energy-flux density.

sources.parent_definition: Energy flux limiter coefficient, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: neutral_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Net energy gain or loss per unit physical volume for neutral particles of a
specified species and internal state, entering that population's energy
transport equation.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-state power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred
to or from neutral particles of a specified species and internal state per
unit physical volume. It is the source or sink term in that population's
energy transport equation.

Its role in the state energy balance is

$$
\frac{\partial u_{s,a}}{\partial t} + \nabla\cdot\mathbf{F}_{s,a} = p_{s,a}
$$

where $s$ identifies the neutral species, $a$ identifies its internal state,
$u_{s,a}$ is that population's energy density, $t$ is time,
$\mathbf{F}_{s,a}$ is its spatial energy flux density, and $p_{s,a}$ is its
net volumetric energy source. The operator $\nabla\cdot$ denotes spatial
divergence.

The quantity combines the included energy-source and energy-sink
contributions, including applicable ionization, charge-exchange, and heating
processes. It applies to the specified internal state only, without summing
over other states or species. It is not stored energy density or a particle
production rate.

Summing over all internal states of the same neutral species gives the
[neutral power density](name:neutral_power_density), $p_s = \sum_a p_{s,a}$,
where $p_s$ is the state-summed volumetric energy source. The [ion
charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density) is the
corresponding energy-source quantity for a specified ionic charge state or
charge-state bundle rather than a neutral internal state.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net energy is transferred to the specified
neutral-state population.

NAMES.name: neutral_temperature
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Temperature of a neutral species measures random translational kinetic
energy per particle relative to the population's mean flow.
NAMES.long:
Temperature of a neutral species characterizes the energy of random
translational motion relative to that population's mean flow. It applies to
neutral atoms or molecules and excludes directed-flow energy and internal
excitation energy.

A cold or hot neutral temperature is that of the named component alone;
without the component it covers the whole neutral population of the selected
species.

The underlying kinetic definition is

$$
\frac{3}{2}T_0 = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}m_0\left|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_0\right|^2\right\rangle
$$

where $T_0$ is the neutral translational temperature expressed as an energy,
$m_0$ is the particle mass of the specified neutral species, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $\mathbf{u}_0$ is the [mean neutral
velocity](name:neutral_velocity). The angle brackets denote a
particle-number-weighted average over the selected neutral population. This
second-moment definition remains applicable to a non-Maxwellian
distribution.

The species-level aggregation convention is the density-weighted mean over
all charge states, not a sum of state temperatures. Since the particles here
are neutral, only the zero-charge state contributes; ion temperatures are
excluded. No particular plasma region, cold or hot population, or internal
state is selected by the unqualified quantity.

The [cold-neutral temperature](name:cold_neutral_temperature) and
[hot-neutral temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature_at_plasma_boundary)
restrict this definition to their respective populations. The [neutral
internal-state temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature) applies
the same translational definition to particles in one specified internal
state; it is not an internal excitation temperature. The [volume-averaged
neutral temperature](name:volume_averaged_neutral_temperature) is a spatial
average of this quantity rather than its value at an individual location.

NAMES.name: neutral_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Mean translational velocity of a neutral-particle population, resolved or
averaged over internal states and energy ranges, with component projections
representing the same bulk flow.
NAMES.long:
The neutral velocity is the mean translational flow of a selected
neutral-particle population, whether resolved by internal state or energy
range or aggregated over several such populations.

At position $\mathbf r$, it is defined by the first velocity moment:

$$
\mathbf{u}_n(\mathbf r)=\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int \mathbf v\,f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $\mathbf r$ is position in m, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity in m
s$^{-1}$, $f_{n,a}$ is phase-space density in m$^{-6}$ s$^3$, $a$ labels
included internal-state or energy subpopulations, and $\mathcal A$ is the
included set. A resolved form is represented by [neutral internal-state
velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity), while aggregation over
included states gives a bulk form such as [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). Vertical, poloidal,
parallel, cold, and hot variants select projections or population subsets of
this same mean flow.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of nitrogen ions evaluated at the radial position of the
internal transport barrier, where locally reduced cross-field turbulent
transport sustains steep impurity density gradients within the confined
plasma.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen (atomic number $Z = 7$) is a medium-Z impurity that is seeded into
fusion plasmas for radiative power exhaust control and divertor heat-load
mitigation. This quantity gives the local number of nitrogen particles per
unit volume at the radial reference position of an internal transport
barrier (ITB) — a narrow region within the confined plasma where cross-field
turbulent transport is locally suppressed, enabling steep radial gradients
to develop and persist. Unless a charge-state-resolved quantity is specified
separately, it represents the nitrogen ion density summed over all
ionization states, consistent with the parent
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

In hot plasma core conditions above approximately 1 keV, nitrogen is found
predominantly in high ionization states ($N^{5+}$–$N^{7+}$). Within an ITB,
neoclassical impurity transport — including temperature-screening and
centrifugal effects on the impurity density profile — can drive strong
inward or outward peaking of $n_\mathrm{N}$ at the barrier radius, with
direct consequences for the local $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ and radiated power
balance.

Nitrogen density in the plasma core is measured by charge-exchange
recombination spectroscopy, which resolves individual charge states whose
sum yields the total impurity density; transport analysis then extracts the
value at the ITB reference location from the fitted profile. Compare with
[neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
for a noble-gas impurity of similar use, and with
[nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary)
for the corresponding boundary value of the same species.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states and excluding neutral
nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states. It represents
nitrogen ions specifically, rather than neutral nitrogen, electrons, or
other ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{N,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{N,ion}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{N,axis}}$ is the nitrogen-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{N,ion}}$ is the total number of nitrogen ions
summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete nitrogen-ion population at that
location, uses a sum over nitrogen ionic charge states, and excludes neutral
nitrogen; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of
another species.

This is the nitrogen-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It follows
the same charge-state-summed convention as [helium-4 density at the magnetic
axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis), while differing in the ion
species counted.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of oxygen ions at the internal transport barrier,
the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent
transport permits steep radial impurity density gradients to form; summed
over all oxygen ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of oxygen ions at the internal transport barrier is
the local oxygen-ion particle density on the flux surface selected as the
barrier reference location. The internal transport barrier (ITB) is a
confined-plasma region where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport
can sustain steep gradients in density, temperature, and pressure. Oxygen
(atomic number $Z = 8$) is a low-$Z$ impurity; this species-level quantity
is summed over all oxygen ion charge states and excludes neutral oxygen
atoms.

The local oxygen-ion number density $n_\mathrm{O}$ at the ITB reference flux
label is the zeroth velocity moment of the aggregate oxygen-ion distribution
function $f_\mathrm{O}$:

$$
n_\mathrm{O}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \int f_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{v},\, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the
normalized minor-radius flux label identifying the ITB flux surface, and
$f_\mathrm{O}$ represents the combined ion population over oxygen charge
states.

At the elemental-species level, the aggregation convention is unweighted by
charge state: equivalently, $n_\mathrm{O} = \sum_{q=1}^{8}
n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$, covering $\mathrm{O}^{1+}$ through fully stripped
$\mathrm{O}^{8+}$. This quantity is the oxygen-specific child of
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and a specialization of ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier;
charge-state-resolved oxygen densities are distinct quantities.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states. It represents oxygen
ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral oxygen, or another plasma
population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{O,axis}} = \left.\sum_q \frac{dN_{\mathrm{O},q}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O,axis}}$ is the oxygen-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $q$ is an oxygen ionic charge state, $N_{\mathrm{O},q}$ is the number
of oxygen ions in charge state $q$, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the oxygen ion population and is summed over all
oxygen ionic charge states; neutral oxygen is excluded. It is a local
density, not a flux-surface or volume integral.

This is the oxygen-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [neon density at the magnetic
axis](name:neon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local,
charge-state-summed convention to neon ions.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: parallel_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.short:
Signed plasma flow along the local magnetic field, equal to the
mass-density-weighted mean of the field-parallel velocities of all
constituent species.
NAMES.long:
The parallel center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the
local magnetic field. It retains the mass-density weighting of the full
barycentric velocity.

The defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},\parallel} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},\parallel}$ is the parallel center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the full center-of-mass velocity vector, $s$
indexes constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density,
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit
vector directed along the local magnetic field.

The sum includes all species in the plasma mixture, not only ions. This is a
local mass-density-weighted mean, not a particle-number-weighted mean or an
unweighted sum of species velocities. The definition requires nonzero total
mass density and a nonzero magnetic field.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its perpendicular
components and is distinct from its speed.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points
along the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_conductivity
NAMES.short:
Local electrical response coefficient relating the electric field along the
magnetic field to the conductive current density it drives in plasma.
NAMES.long:
Parallel conductivity is the local parallel-parallel component of the plasma
electrical-conductivity response, with both projections taken along the
local magnetic-field direction. It relates the electric-field component
along that direction to the conductive current-density component along the
same direction.

The tensor projection and same-direction conductive response are defined by

$$
\sigma_\parallel = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b},\qquad j_\parallel^{\mathrm{cond}} = \sigma_\parallel E_\parallel
$$

where $\sigma_\parallel$ is parallel conductivity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the
unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the
local [plasma electrical conductivity](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity)
tensor for the response being described. $E_\parallel$ is the [parallel
electric field](name:parallel_electric_field), and
$j_\parallel^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive current-density component
due to the same-direction parallel response; for the total response, it is
the [parallel ohmic current density].

This is a local coefficient for plasma at the location where the response is
defined, not a spatial average or integral. For the total plasma response,
it represents the combined electrical response of the charged constituents
rather than a species-resolved coefficient. When attributed to a particular
source, it denotes that source's conductivity contribution and corresponding
driven parallel conductive-current response, not the total conductivity.

Only the parallel-parallel coefficient is included. Off-diagonal tensor
terms, which can also contribute to parallel current when the electric field
has transverse components, are distinct from this coefficient; separately
driven currents such as bootstrap current are also excluded. Unlike
[poloidal conductivity](name:poloidal_conductivity), which selects the
poloidal tangent to a magnetic flux surface, or [toroidal
conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity), which selects the cylindrical
$\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
this projection follows the local magnetic-field direction.

Parallel conductivity is a directional component of [plasma electrical
conductivity](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity). Its value is governed
primarily by electron temperature and Coulomb collisions; for the total
bulk-plasma response, it equals Spitzer conductivity in the classical
collisional limit.

sources.leaf_definition: Parallel conductivity
sources.parent_definition: Transport coefficient profiles for various time slices. The transport of particles, energy and momentum is described by diffusion coefficients, D, and convection velocities, v. In 1D (radial) equations, these are defined by the total fluxes of particles, energy and momentum, across a flux surface given by : V' [-D Y' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v Y <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>], where Y represents the particles, energy and momentum density, respectively, while V is the volume inside a flux surface, the primes denote derivatives with respect to rho_tor_norm and < X > is the flux surface average of a quantity X. This formulation remains valid when changing simultaneously rho_tor_norm into rho_tor in the gradient terms and in the derivatives denoted by the prime. The average flux stored in the IDS as sibling of D and v is the total flux described above divided by the flux surface area V' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>. Note that the energy flux includes the energy transported by the particle flux, in this form: Q =  V' [- n D (T)' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v (nT) <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>] + flux_multiplier * T * particle_flux. Fluxes and convection are positive (resp. negative) when outwards i.e. towards the LCFS (resp. inwards i.e.  towards the magnetic axes).

NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
NAMES.short:
Parallel current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
conventional-charge flux along the local magnetic field attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.
NAMES.long:
Parallel current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
field-aligned projection of the conventional electric-current contribution
attributed to turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

The defining projection is

$$
j_\parallel = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is the parallel anomalous current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the [anomalous-transport current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The
projection requires a nonzero local magnetic field.

This quantity is a local component of the net anomalous current
contribution, with no individual species selected and no spatial averaging
implied. It excludes current contributions attributed to other mechanisms
and is not the total parallel plasma current density.

Unlike the [toroidal anomalous current
density](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), which
projects onto the geometric toroidal direction, this component follows the
local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the anomalous contribution to conventional
electric current flows along the local magnetic-field vector.

NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short:
Parallel current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed projection
of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic-drift current-density
contribution onto the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed
field-aligned scalar projection of the pressure-gradient-driven current
described by [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It represents the
component along the local magnetic-field line, including field-aligned
return-current contributions associated with maintaining current continuity.

The field-aligned projection is defined by

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [diamagnetic-drift current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic field.

This quantity is the generic parallel component of the diamagnetic-drift
current-density contribution. The [Pfirsch-Schlüter diamagnetic-drift
current
density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is
a specific field-aligned return-current contribution, and [parallel
Pfirsch-Schlüter diamagnetic-drift current
density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
denotes that contribution when represented explicitly as a parallel
projection. It is distinct from [toroidal current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which is
projected onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic-drift current-density
contribution has a component in the direction of the local magnetic-field
unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia
NAMES.short:
Parallel current density due to ion inertia is the signed projection of the
electric current produced by ion-fluid inertial acceleration along the local
magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel current density due to ion inertia resolves the electric-current
contribution from ion-fluid inertial acceleration along the local magnetic
field. It represents a finite-ion-mass contribution rather than the total
current along the field.

The component is defined by directional projection:

$$
j_{\parallel} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inertia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_{\parallel}$ is the parallel ion-inertia current-density component,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inertia}}$ is the [current density due to ion
inertia](name:current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} =
\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.
Here, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its
magnitude, which must be nonzero for this projection to be defined.

This quantity is a local, mechanism-specific projection of [current
density](name:current_density), not the complete ion-inertia current vector,
its magnitude, or a spatially averaged current. It is distinct from the
total [parallel ion current density](name:parallel_ion_current_density),
which includes ion charge transport without restriction to the inertial
contribution. Unlike the [diamagnetic component due to ion
inertia](name:diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), it resolves
current along the magnetic field rather than along a perpendicular
direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion-inertia current flows along the local
magnetic-field direction.
