NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Parallel current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed
magnetic-field-aligned projection of the electric current contribution
associated with parallel viscous stress.
NAMES.long:
Parallel current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
projection of the current contribution associated with the divergence of
parallel viscous stress onto the magnetic-field direction. The two uses of
parallel distinguish the current projection from the viscous-stress
mechanism.

For a nonzero magnetic field, the defining projection is:

$$
j_\parallel^{(\mathrm{pv})} = \mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $j_\parallel^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the parallel current-density
contribution, $\mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the full [current-density
vector due to parallel
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The
superscript $\mathrm{pv}$ identifies the parallel-viscosity contribution.

In the magnetized edge plasma, this is a local, mechanism-resolved
contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the total
parallel current density or a flux-surface average. It excludes the
perpendicular-viscosity contribution, whose field-aligned projection is
[parallel current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).

Parallel viscosity does not require its full current-density contribution to
be field aligned. The [radial current density due to parallel
viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) is a
different projection of the same parent vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the parallel-viscosity current-density
contribution has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Parallel current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the signed
field-aligned projection of electric current generated by the divergence of
perpendicular viscous stress.
NAMES.long:
Parallel current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the local
field-aligned projection of the electric-current contribution generated by
the divergence of perpendicular viscous stress in a magnetized plasma.

The signed component is defined by:

$$
j_\parallel = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is this parallel component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}}$
is the vector [current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This is a local, mechanism-resolved contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), not the total parallel current density or a
flux-surface average. “Perpendicular” identifies the viscous-stress
mechanism; it does not restrict the resulting current to directions
perpendicular to the magnetic field. The [parallel current density due to
parallel viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity)
uses the same projection but attributes the current to a different
viscous-stress contribution.

The [toroidal current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) is
another directional projection of the same parent vector, rather than its
field-aligned component.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the perpendicular-viscosity current
contribution has a projection in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Parallel effective neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to
convection is the signed, field-aligned component of the effective
convection velocity representing transport of momentum carried by neutrals
in a resolved internal state. The parallel direction is along the local
magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel effective neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to
convection is the scalar component, along the local magnetic-field
direction, of an effective convection velocity for transport of momentum
carried by a neutral population in one resolved internal state. It is a
transport velocity for momentum, not the neutral bulk-flow velocity itself.

The scalar projection is defined by

$$
v_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{eff}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}$ is this parallel effective neutral
internal-state momentum velocity due to convection,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the corresponding
[neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection),
and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/\lvert\mathbf{B}\rvert$ is the unit
vector in the direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

The scope is a single resolved neutral internal state, so no summation or
averaging over internal states is implied. This quantity is the
field-aligned component only; it excludes perpendicular components,
particle-density convection velocities, energy convection velocities,
diffusivities, and source terms. In a convective momentum-transport closure,
it is the effective velocity factor associated with the transported neutral
internal-state momentum.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the projection of the effective convection
velocity is in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient relating diffusive electron particle flux along the
magnetic field to the electron number-density gradient in that direction.
NAMES.long:
Effective parallel electron diffusivity is the directional transport
coefficient describing electron-particle spreading driven by an electron
number-density gradient along the magnetic field. It is the field-parallel
specialization of [electron particle
diffusivity](name:electron_particle_diffusivity) and enters the diffusive
term of the electron density transport equation.

For the field-parallel direction, the diffusive electron particle flux is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial s_{\parallel}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel
diffusive electron particle flux, $D_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}$ is the parallel
electron diffusivity, $n_{\mathrm{e}}$ is electron number density, and
$s_{\parallel}$ is physical arclength increasing along the magnetic-field
direction. For a positive diffusivity, the minus sign specifies transport
down the electron number-density gradient.

This quantity describes density-gradient-driven electron particle transport,
excluding convective particle flux. It is distinct from [parallel electron
energy diffusivity](name:parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity), which
describes diffusive electron thermal-energy transport. Its directional
counterpart, [poloidal electron
diffusivity](name:poloidal_electron_diffusivity), resolves particle
transport in the poloidal direction rather than along the magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed field-aligned transport velocity that multiplies electron
thermal-energy density to give the convective electron energy flux along the
local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electron energy convection velocity parameterizes the nondiffusive
transport of electron thermal energy along the local magnetic field. It is
the field-aligned component of the [electron energy convection
velocity](name:electron_energy_convection_velocity), rather than the full
transport-velocity vector.

The defining relation is:

$$
Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_e v_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_e\,\mathbf{v}_{e,W}^{\mathrm{conv}}\cdot\mathbf{b}
$$

where $Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the parallel convective
electron thermal-energy flux, $\mathcal{W}_e$ is the local electron
thermal-energy density, $v_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this signed
convection velocity, and $\mathbf{v}_{e,W}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its vector
parent. The unit vector $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ points along
the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This local coefficient applies to the electron thermal-energy channel and
excludes gradient-driven energy diffusion. It multiplies energy density
rather than particle number density and need not equal the [parallel
electron bulk-flow velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity). Its
associated flux is only the convective contribution to the [parallel
electron energy flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux), not the total
flux.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective electron energy convection
velocity points along the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Fickian coefficient relating diffusive electron thermal-energy flux along
magnetic-field lines to the electron thermal-energy-density gradient in that
direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electron energy diffusivity quantifies gradient-driven transport of
electron thermal energy along the local magnetic field. It is the
field-aligned specialization of [electron energy
diffusivity](name:electron_energy_diffusivity).

The defining energy-density-gradient closure is:

$$
Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,W,\parallel}\,\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\nabla\mathcal{W}_e
$$

where $Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive electron
thermal-energy flux projected along the magnetic field, $D_{e,W,\parallel}$
is this diffusivity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector co-directed with
the local magnetic field, $\mathcal{W}_e$ is the local electron
thermal-energy density, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The minus
sign expresses transport down the field-parallel energy-density gradient.

This local coefficient applies to the electron thermal-energy population,
not to the combined electron and ion energy content. It describes only the
diffusive contribution, excluding convective, advective, and perpendicular
transport. For the down-gradient closure, the coefficient is nonnegative.

The [electron energy diffusion
coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead multiplies
a temperature gradient in a density-normalized heat-flux closure. The two
coefficients are not interchangeable without specifying electron density,
heat capacity, and the treatment of density gradients.

Unlike [poloidal electron energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity), this coefficient
follows the magnetic-field direction, which generally includes both poloidal
and toroidal directions.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Parallel electron particle flux is the net electron crossing rate per unit
area perpendicular to the local magnetic field, signed along that field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electron particle flux is the signed net number flow of electrons
along the local magnetic field per unit area perpendicular to that field.
Electron motions in opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

The defining velocity moment is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\parallel} = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}) f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v = n_e u_{e,\parallel}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\parallel}$ is the parallel electron particle flux,
$\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector
along the local magnetic field, $f_e$ is the electron velocity distribution
normalized to the electron number density $n_e$, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The integral covers all electron velocities,
and $u_{e,\parallel}$ is the density-weighted bulk [parallel electron
velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity).

This quantity is local, not an area-integrated particle rate or a one-way
incident flux. Its reference area is perpendicular to the magnetic field,
rather than the actual area of an inclined material surface. No thermal or
nonthermal population restriction is implied.

It specializes [electron particle flux](name:electron_particle_flux) by
choosing the local magnetic-field direction as the surface normal. Unlike
[parallel electron energy flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux), it
counts transported electrons without weighting them by their energy or
electric charge.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net electron number flow is along the
local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed projection of the electron-fluid bulk flow along the local magnetic
field, distinct from the random velocity spread associated with thermal
motion.
NAMES.long:
The parallel electron velocity is the component of the local electron-fluid
bulk velocity along the magnetic-field direction. It describes directed
electron motion, including in the edge plasma, rather than random thermal
motion.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{e\parallel}=\mathbf v_e\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $v_{e\parallel}$ is the parallel electron velocity, $\mathbf v_e$ is
the [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is
the unit vector along the local magnetic field. The projection is defined
where the magnetic field is nonzero.

The electron-fluid velocity is the number-weighted mean over the local
electron velocity distribution; no spatial or flux-surface averaging is
implied. Its parallel component is not the total flow speed, a perpendicular
velocity component, a particle flux, or a thermal velocity spread.

Unlike [parallel plasma velocity](name:parallel_plasma_velocity), which
projects the mass-weighted bulk flow of all contributing plasma species,
this quantity projects only the electron-fluid flow.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electron-fluid bulk motion has a
component along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Pressure of fast electrons parallel to the local magnetic field is the
normal stress from random field-aligned motion of the suprathermal electron
population.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of fast electrons parallel to the local magnetic field is the
field-aligned normal component of the nonthermal electron pressure tensor.
It describes random momentum transport along the field without requiring an
isotropic or Maxwellian distribution.

In the nonrelativistic kinetic description, this component is defined by

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}=\hat{b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{e,\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{b}=m_e\int \bigl[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{e,\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\hat{b}\bigr]^2 f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}$ is the parallel fast-electron
pressure, $\mathbf{P}_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [fast-electron pressure
tensor](name:fast_electron_pressure), $m_e$ is the electron mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
local mean velocity of the fast-electron population, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$
is its velocity distribution function normalized to its number density, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The unit vector
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ points along the local magnetic field
$\mathbf{B}$; all quantities are evaluated at the same position and time.

The velocity-space integral includes the entire specified fast-electron
population, not thermal electrons or ions. Subtracting the population's mean
velocity excludes directed bulk-flow momentum flux. This quantity selects
the field-aligned stress rather than the full pressure tensor or its
isotropic trace.

For a gyrotropic distribution, this component and the [perpendicular
fast-electron pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure) are the
two independent normal stresses. They need not be equal; the perpendicular
component is the mean of the two transverse normal stresses, whereas the
parallel component contains only the field-aligned contribution.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Pressure of suprathermal ions of one species and charge state arising from
velocity fluctuations along the local magnetic field, with the population's
mean flow removed.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of suprathermal ions of one specified species and charge state is
the field-aligned normal stress from velocity fluctuations about that
population's mean flow. It is one of the two independent components of the
gyrotropic fast-ion pressure tensor, the other being perpendicular to the
local magnetic field.

The parallel pressure is defined by the field-aligned central second moment
of the fast-ion distribution:

$$
p_{s,c,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = m_s \int \left((\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right)^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{s,c,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-ion pressure
for species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position,
$m_s$ is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$
is the mean velocity of that fast-ion population, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$
is its velocity distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
volume element. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$
follows the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity includes only the specified suprathermal ion species and
charge state, with no sum over species or charge states. It excludes
thermal-ion and electron pressures, the perpendicular pressure component,
and stress from the population's mean directed motion. It is not the
isotropic trace pressure and does not require an isotropic distribution.

It is the parallel component of [fast-ion charge-state
pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure). Adding the contributions
from all charge states of a fixed ion species gives its [parallel fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure); this aggregation is an additive
sum, not a density-weighted mean.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species in a specified internal
quantum or excitation state is their kinetic normal stress along the local
magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species in a specified internal
quantum or excitation state is the field-parallel component of their kinetic
pressure tensor. It describes directional translational stress without
requiring an isotropic velocity distribution.

The parallel component is defined by projection onto the local
magnetic-field direction:

$$
p_{0,s,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf P_{0,s,a}^{\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $p_{0,s,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the state-resolved parallel
fast-neutral pressure, $\mathbf P_{0,s,a}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
corresponding kinetic pressure-tensor contribution, $0$ denotes electrical
neutrality, $s$ labels the neutral species, and $a$ labels its internal
quantum or excitation state. The superscript $\mathrm{fast}$ selects the
suprathermal population. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf
B|$ follows the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, which must be nonzero to
define this projection.

This quantity includes only the selected species, internal state, and
suprathermal population. It excludes thermal-neutral pressure,
charged-particle pressure, and transverse pressure components.
Internal-state resolution distinguishes neutral excitation states, not ionic
charge states; internal excitation energy is not itself translational
pressure.

Summing the state-resolved pressure contributions over all internal states
gives the [parallel fast-neutral
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure) of that species. This
aggregation is an additive sum, not a density-weighted mean. The quantity
retains the species and state selection of [suprathermal neutral
internal-state pressure](name:suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure)
while explicitly selecting its field-parallel component.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species is the
magnetic-field-parallel normal component of their kinetic pressure tensor.
It is summed over internal quantum and excitation states and, where multiple
charge-state contributions are represented, over charge states.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species is the field-aligned normal
component of their kinetic pressure tensor. The local magnetic-field
direction defines the projection axis; this is a directional component, not
an isotropic scalar pressure.

The parallel component is the projection of the kinetic pressure tensor onto
that direction:

$$
p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf b} \cdot \mathbf P_{0,\mathrm{fast}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}$ is this parallel fast-neutral
pressure, $\mathbf P_{0,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the kinetic pressure tensor of
the suprathermal neutral population, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit
vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$.

The quantity applies to suprathermal neutrals of one species. Contributions
are summed over all internal quantum and excitation states and, when
multiple charge-state contributions are represented, over all charge states;
this is an additive sum, not an average. It excludes thermal-neutral
pressure and pressure from other species. Unlike the [parallel fast-neutral
internal-state
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure), it is not
resolved by a single internal state.

This is a directional component, distinct from the isotropic trace quantity
[fast-neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure). Together with
[perpendicular fast-neutral
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure), it specifies the
gyrotropic pressure decomposition; the parallel and perpendicular components
need not be equal.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the field-aligned Fickian
diffusivity for thermal-energy transport of a specified ion charge state,
defined so the parallel diffusive energy flux is proportional to and
opposite the field-aligned gradient of that state's thermal-energy density.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the effective transport
coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of the thermal-energy density of
one specified ionization stage along the magnetic-field direction. It
represents the field-aligned Fickian part of that stage's thermal-energy
transport, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources,
and is the parallel component of ion charge-state energy diffusivity.

The defining field-aligned closure is

$$
q_{E,z,\parallel} = -\chi_{E,z,\parallel}\nabla_\parallel w_z
$$

where $q_{E,z,\parallel}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the parallel
component of the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ionization stage
$z$, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field,
$\chi_{E,z,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity,
$w_z$ is the thermal-energy density of that ionization stage, and
$\nabla_\parallel w_z=\mathbf{b}\cdot\nabla w_z$ is the field-aligned
spatial gradient of that density. The minus sign specifies down-gradient
transport along the magnetic field.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed
over ion species or charge states, unlike [ion energy
diffusivity](name:ion_energy_diffusivity). It is a coefficient multiplying
the thermal-energy-density gradient, not a temperature-gradient
heat-transport coefficient unless the relevant density and heat-capacity
factors are explicitly included in the coefficient.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Parallel ion charge-state energy flux is the signed conductive and
convective energy transported along the local magnetic field per unit
perpendicular area and time for one ion species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state energy flux is the net conductive and convective
energy transport along the local magnetic field, measured per unit area
perpendicular to that field and per unit time.

The field-aligned projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel}$ is the signed parallel energy flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W}$ is the [ion charge-state energy-flux
vector](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) for the selected species and
charge state, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and $|\mathbf{B}|$
is its magnitude. The subscript $W$ identifies the energy transport channel.

This local quantity applies to one ion species in one specified charge
state, without summing over species or charge states. Its edge-plasma scope
includes the scrape-off layer and divertor. It excludes perpendicular energy
transport and is not restricted to the conductive contribution alone.

It is the parallel component of the parent energy flux, not its magnitude or
a surface-integrated power. Unlike the [parallel ion charge-state particle
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), it represents
transported energy rather than transported particle number.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net energy transport by the specified ion
charge state is in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective convection coefficient relating the nondiffusive flux of
magnetic-field-parallel momentum to the parallel momentum density of a
specified ion species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient governing advective, nondiffusive
transport of magnetic-field-parallel [momentum](name:momentum) carried by
ions of one specified species and charge state. It is a transport-closure
coefficient, not the charge state's bulk parallel flow velocity.

The convective contribution to the parallel-momentum flux is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} g_{s,\parallel}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its convective flux of parallel
momentum in the specified transport direction,
$V_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection coefficient,
and $g_{s,\parallel}$ is its parallel momentum density. The momentum density
is $g_{s,\parallel}=m_s n_s u_{s,\parallel}$, where $m_s$ is the ion mass,
$n_s$ is the number density of that charge state, and $u_{s,\parallel}$ is
its mean flow velocity projected along the local magnetic field.

The parallel label identifies the transported momentum component; it does
not require the transport direction itself to follow the magnetic field. The
coefficient is charge-state resolved, with no sum or average over charge
states implied. It excludes the diffusive and residual-stress contributions
to momentum flux and is distinct from a particle convection coefficient.

This is the parallel-momentum specialization of [ion charge-state momentum
convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity).
Unlike [diamagnetic momentum convection
velocity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity), it does not
specifically isolate a diamagnetic contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the convective parallel-momentum flux in the
specified positive transport direction has the same sign as the parallel
momentum density; the parallel momentum component is positive along the
local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical damping of
magnetic-field-aligned ordered momentum carried by ions of one specified
species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and
neoclassical damping of ordered [momentum](name:momentum) parallel to the
local magnetic field. It governs relaxation of the selected ion charge
state's parallel flow in core-plasma momentum balance.

The local linear damping contribution is defined by:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial g_{s,\parallel}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{s,\parallel}g_{s,\parallel}
$$

where $g_{s,\parallel}$ is the ordered field-parallel momentum density of
ions of the specified species and charge state, $s$ identifies that
population, $t$ is time, and $\nu_{s,\parallel}$ is this damping rate. The
subscript $\parallel$ denotes the field-aligned component, and the
restriction labeled $\mathrm{damp}$ isolates the damping contribution to the
momentum balance. For a constant rate, this contribution produces
exponential relaxation with a relaxation time equal to the rate's
reciprocal.

The coefficient is charge-state resolved, not summed or averaged over
species or charge states. It describes local relaxation rather than
diffusive or convective momentum transport or an externally applied momentum
source. Collisional relaxation can transfer momentum to other populations
without implying loss of total plasma momentum.

This is the parallel-component specialization of [ion charge-state momentum
damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate). It differs from
[parallel ion momentum damping
rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate), which describes aggregate
bulk-ion flow rather than the flow of one specified ion charge state.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Kinematic coefficient for down-gradient diffusion along the magnetic field
of field-parallel flow momentum carried by ions of one species and charge
state.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity governs diffusive
redistribution along the magnetic field of field-parallel flow
[momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion species and charge
state. It is the field-parallel directional component of [ion charge-state
momentum diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity).

In a local Fick-law closure, the diffusive momentum flux is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{s,\parallel}\,\mathbf{b}\cdot\nabla g_{s,\parallel}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the flux of field-parallel momentum
along the magnetic field, $\chi_{s,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, and
$g_{s,\parallel}$ is the selected state's field-parallel momentum density.
The unit vector $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ follows the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The
momentum density is $g_{s,\parallel}=m_s n_s v_{s,\parallel}$, where $m_s$
is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the charge-state number density, and
$v_{s,\parallel}$ is the mean field-parallel flow velocity.

The coefficient is resolved for one charge state, not summed or averaged
over charge states. It describes only the diffusive contribution, excluding
convective momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum
sources. Unlike [poloidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity], which
describes transport along a poloidal arc on a flux surface, this coefficient
follows the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Parallel momentum flux for one ion charge state is the net transfer rate per
unit area of field-aligned momentum across a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum flux across a magnetic flux surface is
the signed transport rate per unit area of magnetic-field-aligned [linear
momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one species in one specified
charge state.

It is the field-aligned projection of the [ion charge-state momentum
flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) across the same oriented surface:

$$
\Gamma_{s,\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathsf{T}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel}$ is this parallel momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is the vector of momentum transported across the
surface per unit area and time, $\mathsf{T}_s$ is the material momentum-flux
tensor of that ion charge state, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along
the magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the surface-normal unit vector
toward increasing flux-surface label.

The quantity is resolved for one charge state, not summed over charge states
or species. It includes convective and non-convective momentum transport,
rather than only the diffusive contribution or a transport coefficient.
Isotropic pressure contributes no parallel momentum flux across a magnetic
flux surface because the magnetic field is tangent to that surface.

Unlike [poloidal ion charge-state momentum
flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), it selects the
magnetic-field-aligned component of the transported momentum. The transport
is across the flux surface, not along the magnetic field; it is therefore
distinct from [parallel ion charge-state particle
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which describes
along-field number transport.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net transfer carries momentum along the
magnetic field toward increasing flux-surface label, or oppositely directed
momentum toward decreasing label.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Mean directed flow along the local magnetic field for ions of a specified
species and ionization charge state, distinct from their random thermal
motion.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion charge-state velocity is the field-aligned projection of
the bulk flow of ions belonging to one specified species and ionization
charge state. It describes mean directed motion at the position under
consideration.

The component is defined by the projected first velocity moment:

$$
u_{\parallel,Z}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf b}(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf u_Z(\mathbf r)=\frac{\int [\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}(\mathbf r)]f_Z(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_Z(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{\parallel,Z}$ is the parallel velocity component, $\mathbf r$ is
position, $Z$ is the selected ionic charge number, $\mathbf u_Z$ is the [ion
charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), $\mathbf v$ is
particle velocity, and $f_Z$ is the velocity distribution of the selected
species and charge state. The integration element $d^3v$ spans velocity
space. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the
local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, whose magnitude is $|\mathbf B|$.

The particle-velocity average is restricted to the selected charge-state
population; no averaging over other charge states is implied. This is a
signed projection of the parent velocity vector, not its magnitude, a
particle flux, or a random thermal velocity spread. Its definition requires
a nonzero magnetic field and nonzero density of the selected population.

The corresponding [parallel ion velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity) is the
density-weighted mean of these components over all ionic charge states of
the same species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected charge-state bulk flow has a
component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Field-aligned projection of the pressure-gradient diamagnetic fluid velocity
of one ion charge state in the edge plasma, identically zero because this
drift is perpendicular to the magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the local
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma onto the magnetic-field direction. It represents a
fluid-moment contribution rather than the guiding-center motion of
individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state with scalar partial pressure, the defining
projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\parallel} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}} = 0
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the specified ion charge state,
$v_{\ast\alpha,\parallel}$ is its field-parallel diamagnetic-drift velocity
component, $p_\alpha$ is its partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its
pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector,
$B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge,
$n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow. Its vanishing value follows from the perpendicularity of the
pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift, not from the absence of total parallel
ion flow.

The [perpendicular ion charge-state velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
instead resolves the same drift along a specified local direction
perpendicular to the magnetic field and need not vanish. The species-level
[ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted
mean over all ionic charge states of that species, not their sum; its
parallel projection therefore also vanishes for this pressure-gradient
drift.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Parallel ion energy flux is the signed component of ion energy-flux density
along the local magnetic-field direction for a specified,
charge-state-summed ion population, including convective and conductive
transport when those channels are in scope.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion energy flux is the signed component of ion energy-flux density
along the local magnetic-field direction. It gives the rate at which energy
carried by a specified ion population crosses a surface whose chosen unit
normal is the local magnetic-field direction, including convective,
conductive, or other channels only when they belong to the stated ion-energy
reservoir.

For local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the scalar parallel
ion energy flux $F_{E,i,\parallel}$ is the projection of the ion
energy-flux-density vector $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ onto $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$:

$$
F_{E,i,\parallel} = \mathbf{q}_{E,i} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ is the vector density of energy transport for the
selected ion population and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of the local [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field) $\mathbf{B}$.

Parallel ion energy flux applies where the local magnetic-field direction is
defined and the selected ion-energy reservoir is specified. For an ion
species identified without a charge state, it is summed over all charge
states of that species; the charge-state-resolved counterpart is [parallel
ion charge-state energy flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux).
[Total ion energy flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux) aggregates all ion
species and charge states.

Parallel ion energy flux is a field-aligned specialization of [ion energy
flux](name:ion_energy_flux) and a species-scoped specialization of energy
flux. It is distinct from ion energy density, a volumetric energy source or
sink, ion velocity, and perpendicular, radial, or poloidal projections;
related [parallel heat flux](name:parallel_heat_flux) denotes heat transport
along the magnetic field rather than the full ion-energy reservoir unless
that reservoir is explicitly limited to heat.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ has a component in the

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Field-parallel projection of the effective velocity coefficient for
advective ion momentum transport, distinct from the bulk ion flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum convection velocity is the signed field-aligned
component of the effective coefficient governing advective, non-diffusive
transport of ion [momentum](name:momentum). It is a transport-closure
coefficient, not the material bulk ion flow velocity.

It is the projection of the parent vector onto the local magnetic-field
direction:

$$
V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathbf{V}_i^{\mathrm{conv}} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this parallel coefficient,
$\mathbf{V}_i^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the [ion momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The subscript
$i$ identifies the specified ion species; the projection requires a nonzero
magnetic field.

The species-level intensive coefficient is the density-weighted mean over
all ionic charge states, not a sum of velocities. In contrast, the [parallel
ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
applies to one specified charge state. This species-level quantity does not
aggregate electron or neutral momentum transport.

Within the advective closure, this coefficient relates the convective
momentum flux along the magnetic field to the transported ion momentum
density. It is distinct from the [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity), which describes gradient-driven
diffusive transport, and is not itself a momentum flux or momentum source.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective ion momentum convection
velocity has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional or neoclassical decay of
magnetic-field-aligned bulk-flow momentum in an ion species, including all
its ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation
time for collisional or neoclassical relaxation of an ion species' ordered
flow along the local magnetic field. It describes damping of the
field-aligned momentum component, not the direction of momentum transport.

In a local linear damping closure, the damping contribution to the momentum
balance is:

$$
\left(\frac{\partial g_{i,\parallel}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{i,\parallel}g_{i,\parallel}
$$

where $g_{i,\parallel}$ is the ion species' parallel momentum density,
$\nu_{i,\parallel}$ is this damping rate, and $t$ is time. The index $i$
identifies the ion species, $\parallel$ denotes the field-aligned
projection, and the subscript $\mathrm{damp}$ selects only the damping
contribution. For a constant positive rate with no other terms acting, its
reciprocal is the exponential relaxation time.

The species momentum density is summed over all ionic charge states, and the
corresponding bulk-flow velocity is the density-weighted mean over all ionic
charge states. This effective species-level coefficient is not a sum of
charge-state damping rates; the [parallel ion charge-state momentum damping
rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) instead
describes one specified charge state. Diffusive and convective momentum
fluxes and externally applied momentum sources are excluded from this
damping term.

This quantity is the field-aligned entry of the [ion momentum damping
rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate), whose directional entries describe
anisotropic relaxation of ordered ion [momentum](name:momentum). The damping
coefficient is nonnegative for dissipative relaxation and does not inherit
the sign of the parallel flow.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Parallel directional diffusion coefficient governing down-gradient transport
of bulk-ion momentum along the local magnetic-field direction in a
magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum diffusion coefficient is the parallel directional
component of the [ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) vector. It
parameterizes down-gradient diffusion of bulk-ion momentum along the local
magnetic-field direction, distinct from radial and poloidal transport
components.

In a gradient-diffusion closure, its constitutive relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}=-\chi_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}\nabla_{\parallel}(m_i n_i v_{i,\parallel})
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}$ is the diffusive parallel flux
density of ion momentum, $\chi_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}$ is this
coefficient, $\nabla_{\parallel}$ is the derivative along the local magnetic
field, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, and
$v_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel bulk-ion flow velocity. The coefficient
describes parallel momentum diffusion only; it is not the momentum flux
itself and does not represent cross-field transport. The species-agnostic
[parallel momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and the
directionally distinct toroidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient define
related but broader or differently projected quantities.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective kinematic coefficient for field-aligned diffusion of an ion
species’ momentum, driven by gradients of its charge-state-averaged parallel
flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion momentum diffusivity is the effective kinematic coefficient
governing field-aligned diffusive transport of the parallel component of
[momentum](name:momentum) for a specified ion species. It is the
field-aligned ion specialization of [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).

In a local kinematic diffusion closure, the field-aligned diffusive flux of
parallel ion momentum is:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_i n_i D_{i,\parallel}\frac{\partial v_{i,\parallel}}{\partial \ell_\parallel}
$$

where $i$ labels the ion species, $\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
flux of parallel momentum along the magnetic field, $m_i$ is the ion mass,
$n_i$ is the species number density summed over all ionic charge states,
$D_{i,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the
density-weighted mean parallel flow velocity over all ionic charge states,
and $\ell_\parallel$ is arc length increasing along the local magnetic-field
direction. For nonnegative diffusivity, the flux opposes the parallel
velocity gradient.

The coefficient applies to the collective momentum of one ion species,
excluding neutral particles and other ion species. It belongs to the
collective-flow closure and is not a sum of charge-state diffusivities; the
[charge-state-resolved parallel momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
instead applies to one specified charge state.

This closure acts on the parallel flow-velocity gradient rather than
directly on the momentum-density gradient. It excludes convective momentum
transport, residual stress, and external momentum sources. Unlike the
[parallel ion momentum damping
rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate), it describes spatial
diffusive redistribution rather than local momentum relaxation.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Parallel ion momentum flux is the rate per unit area at which the
magnetic-field-aligned momentum of an ion species crosses an oriented
surface.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the
magnetic-field-aligned component of ion [momentum](name:momentum) across an
oriented surface. The parallel label selects the transported momentum
component, while the surface normal specifies the direction across which
transport is evaluated.

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\parallel}$ is this parallel momentum flux, $i$ identifies
the ion species, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is its momentum-flux vector through
the oriented surface, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_i$ is its momentum-flux tensor, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface-normal unit vector. The
magnetic-field unit vector is $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$, where
$\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic field.

For the specified ion species, the flux is summed over all ionic charge
states, combining the corresponding [parallel ion charge-state momentum
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) contributions. It
includes convective transport, pressure, and viscous or turbulent stresses,
rather than only diffusive transport; electron and neutral contributions are
excluded. The surface need not be a magnetic flux surface, and its normal
need not be parallel to the magnetic field.

Summing the species contributions gives the parallel component of the total
[ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), which aggregates over all ion
species and ionic charge states.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net momentum transported through the
surface in its chosen normal direction has a component co-directed with the
local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Parallel ion particle flux is the signed net number flow of one ion species
along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time, summed
over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion particle flux is the local net transport of particles of one
ion species along the magnetic field, expressed per unit area perpendicular
to that field.

The parallel particle flux $\Gamma_{i,\parallel}$ of ion species $i$ is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \sum_{q\geq 1} \Gamma_{iq,\parallel}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the species' total particle-flux vector,
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $q$ is
the positive ionic charge number, and $\Gamma_{iq,\parallel}$ is the
[parallel ion charge-state particle
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for species $i$ in
charge state $q$.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of the selected species,
excluding its neutral form and other ion species. It counts net particle
transport rather than incoming particles alone and is neither a
surface-integrated particle rate nor the charge-weighted [parallel ion
current density](name:parallel_ion_current_density).

It specializes [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux) by choosing the
oriented surface normal along the local magnetic field. Its reference area
is therefore perpendicular to the field, not the area of an arbitrarily
inclined material surface.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net ion number flow is co-directed with
the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of
total momentum in the field-parallel direction, distinct from the total
momentum bulk flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective,
non-diffusive transport of total momentum in the field-parallel direction.
It is a transport closure quantity, not the actual bulk flow velocity
associated with total momentum.

For the parallel momentum component, the convective momentum flux is defined
by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv},\parallel} P_\parallel
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of
parallel momentum, $V_{\mathrm{conv},\parallel}$ is the parallel component
of momentum convection velocity, and $P_\parallel$ is the parallel momentum
density.

The parallel component is directed along the local magnetic-field direction.
The quantity applies to the total momentum equation without restricting the
momentum to ions, neutrals, a species, or a charge state; it therefore
differs in population scope from [parallel neutral particle convection
velocity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity) and in
direction from [vertical momentum convection
velocity](name:vertical_momentum_convection_velocity).

NAMES.name: parallel_net_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Area-normalized net rate of ion momentum transfer along the local magnetic
field, summed algebraically over ionic charge states and contributing source
and sink processes.
NAMES.long:
The parallel net ion momentum source is the signed, area-normalized rate of
[momentum](name:momentum) transfer to the ion population along the local
magnetic field. It is the field-aligned projection of the vector [net ion
momentum source](name:net_ion_momentum_source), not its magnitude.

The projection and aggregation are defined by

$$
S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_i^{\mathrm{net}} = \sum_q\sum_a \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_{iq}^{(a)}
$$

where $S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is this parallel source, $\mathbf
S_i^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net ion momentum-source vector, and $\mathbf
S_{iq}^{(a)}$ is the area-normalized momentum-source contribution from
process $a$ to ionic charge state $q$ of ion population $i$. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ points along the nonzero local
magnetic field $\mathbf B$.

All ionic charge states and contributing source and sink processes are
summed algebraically, allowing opposing contributions to cancel. The
quantity is charge-state summed rather than charge-state resolved;
momentum-source terms assigned to electrons or neutrals are excluded. Its
area normalization does not make it a [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux):
it describes momentum supplied to or removed from ions, rather than momentum
transported across a surface.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net transfer of ion momentum is in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Parallel neutral energy flux is the net thermal energy transported per unit
area and time along the local magnetic field, summed over neutral species
and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral energy flux is the signed thermal-energy transport carried
by neutral atoms and molecules along the local magnetic-field direction. The
reference area is perpendicular to that direction.

The field-parallel projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{0,W,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,W}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,W,\parallel}$ is the signed parallel neutral thermal-energy
flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,W}$ is the full neutral thermal-energy flux
vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$
is its magnitude. The projection requires a nonzero local magnetic field.

The quantity is summed over all neutral species and internal states. The
[parallel neutral internal-state energy
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) supplies a
state-resolved contribution to this aggregate. Energy transport carried by
ions and electrons is excluded.

This quantity specializes [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux) by
choosing the oriented surface normal along the local magnetic field. The
field specifies the projection direction; it does not require neutral
trajectories to follow magnetic field lines.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral thermal energy is transported in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Signed effective velocity along the local magnetic field relating the
thermal energy-density factor to the convective energy flux of one neutral
species in a specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral internal-state energy convection velocity is the
field-aligned component of the effective velocity coefficient governing
convective thermal-energy transport. It specializes [energy convection
velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity) to one neutral species in one
specified internal state.

Its defining energy-flux relation is:

$$
Q_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_{0,a}\,v_{0,a,W,\parallel}
$$

where $Q_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the parallel convective
thermal-energy flux, $\mathcal{W}_{0,a}$ is the transported thermal
energy-density factor, and $v_{0,a,W,\parallel}$ is the effective parallel
energy-convection velocity. The subscript $0$ identifies the neutral
population, $a$ identifies its specified internal state, $W$ denotes the
energy transport channel, and $\parallel$ denotes projection along the local
magnetic field.

This coefficient applies separately to the specified species and internal
state; it is neither summed nor averaged over species or internal states. It
describes the convective contribution, not gradient-driven energy diffusion,
and need not equal the [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity).

It is the projection of the [neutral internal-state energy convection
velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity):
$v_{0,a,W,\parallel}=\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}$, where
$\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}$ is that parent vector coefficient and $\hat{\mathbf b}$
is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. This projection requires
a nonzero local magnetic field and does not imply that neutral particles are
magnetically confined.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective energy-convection velocity
points along the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Fickian coefficient relating density-normalized diffusive thermal-energy
flux of neutrals in one species and internal state to their temperature
gradient along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral internal-state energy diffusivity quantifies
gradient-driven transport of thermal energy carried by a specified neutral
species in one internal state, along the local magnetic-field direction. The
magnetic field defines the projection direction; it does not imply that
neutral particles are magnetically confined.

The density-normalized diffusive thermal-energy flux satisfies:

$$
\frac{Q_{0,a,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{0,a}} = -D_{0,a,W,\parallel}\,\mathbf{b}\cdot\nabla(k_B T_{0,a})
$$

where $D_{0,a,W,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity,
$Q_{0,a,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the field-parallel projection of the
diffusive thermal-energy flux, $n_{0,a}$ is the population's number density,
and $T_{0,a}$ is its thermodynamic temperature. The symbol $k_B$ is
Boltzmann's constant, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. The
subscripts $0$, $a$, and $W$ identify neutral particles, the specified
internal state, and the energy transport channel, respectively. The minus
sign denotes transport down the temperature gradient for a nonnegative
diffusivity.

This coefficient applies to one neutral species and internal state; it is
neither summed nor averaged over species or internal states. It describes
only the field-aligned diffusive contribution, excluding convective and
advective energy transport and transport perpendicular to the magnetic
field.

The [poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity)
describes the corresponding state-resolved transport coefficient in the
poloidal direction, which is distinct from the local magnetic-field
direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Field-parallel neutral energy flux is the signed thermal-energy transport
per unit area and time along the local magnetic field by one neutral species
in one specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
Field-parallel neutral internal-state energy flux describes thermal-energy
transport across a surface perpendicular to the local magnetic field by one
neutral species in one specified internal state. It is the field-aligned
component of the [neutral internal-state energy
flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{0,a,W,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,a,W,\parallel}$ is the signed field-parallel thermal-energy
flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a,W}$ is the thermal-energy flux vector of the
selected neutral species in internal state $a$, and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf
B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf
B$, whose magnitude is $|\mathbf B|$. The subscripts $0$, $W$, and
$\parallel$ identify the neutral population, energy channel, and
field-parallel projection, respectively.

This contribution applies to one internal state, not a sum over states or
species. Summing over all internal states of the same neutral species gives
the [parallel neutral energy flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux). The
magnetic field defines the projection direction; it does not imply that
neutral particles are constrained to follow magnetic field lines. The
projection requires a nonzero local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when thermal energy carried by the selected
neutral population flows in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Kinematic coefficient for field-aligned diffusion of a neutral species'
momentum in one internal state, relating momentum flux to the opposing
flow-velocity gradient.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the kinematic transport coefficient governing diffusive
transport of a neutral species' linear [momentum](name:momentum) along the
local magnetic-field direction, resolved for one specified internal state.
It specializes [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) by
selecting the neutral population, internal state, and transport direction.

In a local flow-gradient closure, the field-aligned diffusive momentum flux
satisfies:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_0 n_{0,a} D_{0,a,\parallel}\left(\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\nabla\right)\mathbf u_{0,a}
$$

where the subscript $0$ denotes the neutral species, $a$ identifies its
internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
vector of momentum components transported diffusively along the magnetic
field, $m_0$ is the neutral-particle mass, $n_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved
number density, $D_{0,a,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, and $\mathbf
u_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved mean flow velocity. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the local magnetic field
$\mathbf B$, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

The parallel qualifier selects the transport and velocity-gradient
direction; it does not require that the transported momentum itself be
field-parallel. The coefficient applies to one neutral species and internal
state, without averaging over internal states. Internal-state resolution is
distinct from ion charge-state resolution. Only gradient-driven diffusive
transport is included; convective momentum transport, residual stress, and
momentum sources are separate contributions. A down-gradient closure uses a
nonnegative coefficient.

This is the field-aligned directional member of the [neutral internal-state
momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient),
rather than its complete set of directional coefficients.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Parallel neutral momentum flux is the signed rate per area at which
magnetic-field-parallel momentum carried by neutral atoms and molecules
crosses an oriented surface, summed over species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral momentum flux is the rate per unit area at which the
magnetic-field-parallel component of neutral [linear
momentum](name:momentum) crosses an oriented surface in the edge plasma. The
parallel qualifier identifies the transported momentum component, not the
direction normal to the transport surface.

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\parallel}(\hat{n}) = \hat{b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0(\hat{n})
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral momentum flux,
$\hat{n}$ is the chosen unit normal to the oriented surface, $\hat{b}$ is
the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0(\hat{n})$ is the vector [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) across that surface. The subscript $0$
denotes the neutral population.

This quantity includes convective momentum transport and neutral
thermal-pressure contributions, summed over all neutral atomic and molecular
species and their internal states. It excludes charged-particle momentum and
is not restricted to transport along the magnetic field. The [parallel
neutral internal-state momentum
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) resolves an
individual internal-state contribution; summing those contributions over
states and species gives this aggregate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net momentum transferred across the
surface in its chosen normal direction has a component along the local
magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Signed rate of momentum transfer per transport area along the local magnetic
field to an edge-plasma neutral population, summed over all neutral internal
states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral momentum source is the signed, area-normalized rate at
which [momentum](name:momentum) is added to or removed from the represented
neutral population along the local magnetic field in the edge plasma. It is
the field-parallel projection of the state-summed vector source.

The projection and internal-state aggregation are defined by:

$$
S_{0,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_0=\sum_{a\in\mathcal N_0}\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_{0,a}
$$

where $S_{0,\parallel}$ is this parallel source, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the
unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf S_0$ is the [neutral
momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), $\mathcal N_0$ is the set of
all internal states of the represented neutral species, $a$ labels one such
state, and $\mathbf S_{0,a}$ is its area-normalized vector momentum source.

The aggregation is a sum over neutral internal states, not a
density-weighted mean or a single-state contribution. Charged-particle
source terms are excluded. This quantity describes momentum input to the
neutral population, not momentum transported across a surface, and its area
normalization distinguishes it from a volumetric force density.

Unlike the [poloidal neutral momentum
source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), which uses the geometric
poloidal direction, this component uses the local magnetic-field direction.
That direction defines the projection even though the particles are
electrically neutral.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net momentum transfer to the neutral
population points along the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Parallel neutral particle flux is the signed net number flow of one neutral
species along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time,
summed over internal states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral particle flux is the local signed net number flow of one
neutral atomic or molecular species along the magnetic-field direction, per
area perpendicular to that direction. Particle crossings in opposite
directions contribute with opposite signs.

The parallel projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is the particle number-flux vector of the selected
neutral species, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and
$|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The subscript $0$ identifies neutral
particles. This projection requires a nonzero magnetic field.

The quantity is summed over all internal states of the selected species, not
over different neutral species. The [parallel neutral internal-state
particle flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) resolves
the individual state contributions whose sum gives this quantity.

This is the specialization of [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) for a crossing surface whose normal
follows the local magnetic-field direction. It is not a flux per actual
material-surface area at an arbitrary field-incidence angle, a
surface-integrated arrival rate, or a one-way incident flux. The magnetic
field defines the projection direction without implying that neutral
trajectories follow magnetic field lines.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net neutral particle transport points
along the local magnetic-field vector.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Field-aligned velocity attributed to an effective diamagnetic
pressure-gradient contribution for one internal state of a neutral species
in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of an effective pressure-gradient transport velocity onto the
local magnetic-field direction. For an uncharged neutral state, it
represents an assigned fluid-transport contribution, not a direct magnetic
guiding-center drift.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},a,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}_{\mathrm{dia},a} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{dia},a,\parallel}$ is the parallel velocity contribution
for the neutral species and internal state labeled $a$,
$\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}_{\mathrm{dia},a}$ is its effective diamagnetic
velocity vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local magnetic-field unit
vector. The direction is defined by
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its nonzero magnitude.

This quantity applies locally in the edge plasma to one specified neutral
species and internal quantum state, without summing or averaging over other
states or species. It fixes the field-aligned projection direction left
unspecified by [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

It excludes independent contributions to the total neutral flow and cannot
be obtained by substituting zero charge into the charged-particle
diamagnetic-drift formula. If the assigned effective velocity is strictly
perpendicular to the magnetic field, its parallel projection vanishes; a
transverse projection is instead represented by [perpendicular neutral-state
velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:perpendicular_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective diamagnetic velocity
contribution has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Signed component of a neutral species' mean translational flow along the
local magnetic field, density-weighted over contributing internal states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral velocity is the projection of a selected neutral species'
bulk flow onto the local magnetic-field direction. It describes directed
motion averaged over particle velocities and over the contributing neutral
internal states.

The component is defined by:

$$
u_{0,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf u_0=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_{0,a}\mathbf u_{0,a}}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_{0,a}}
$$

where $u_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral velocity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$
is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\mathbf u_0$ is the
[neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) vector. The set $\mathcal A$
contains the included internal states, $a$ labels one such state, $n_{0,a}$
is its neutral number density, and $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is its [bulk neutral
internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), defined
as the mean particle velocity within that state.

Internal-state contributions form a number-density-weighted mean, not a sum
of state velocities. The aggregation applies only to the selected neutral
species and excludes charged particles. This component is distinct from the
flow-speed magnitude, particle flux, and random thermal velocity spread; it
is defined wherever the local magnetic-field direction and neutral mean flow
are defined.

The [poloidal neutral velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_velocity) projects the
same mean neutral flow onto the poloidal direction rather than onto the
magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neutral mean flow has a component in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_current_density
NAMES.short:
Parallel total current density is the flux-surface average of the total
current–magnetic-field dot product divided by the reference vacuum toroidal
field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel total current density represents the net field-aligned conventional
charge flow using a magnetic-field-weighted flux-surface average and a
reference vacuum toroidal field. It is the parallel-basis member of [total
current density](name:total_current_density), rather than the full
current-density vector.

The defining relation is:

$$
j_\parallel = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle}{B_0}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is the parallel total current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the net plasma [current-density
vector](name:current_density), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field
vector, angle brackets denote a normalized flux-surface average, and $B_0$
is the signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field at the specified
reference major radius. The reference field must be nonzero.

The total is the algebraic sum over all included charged species and charge
states. It includes ohmic current and non-inductive current, with bootstrap
and externally driven currents included within the non-inductive
contribution. Every contribution uses the same averaging and reference-field
convention. This quantity is neither a current magnitude nor, in general,
the local field-aligned projection or its unweighted flux-surface average.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [vertical total
current density](name:vertical_total_current_density), which resolves charge
flow along the vertical direction, this quantity resolves the
magnetic-field-aligned contribution; it is also distinct from the toroidal
projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the flux-surface-averaged total
current–magnetic-field dot product and $B_0$ have the same sign; $B_0$ is
positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$.

NAMES.name: particle_density
NAMES.short:
Particle number density is the concentration of a selected species,
including thermal and nonthermal particles and all orbit classes unless a
narrower population is specified.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density is the local concentration of particles belonging to
a selected species or population. For the full species distribution, it
includes both thermal and nonthermal particles and all orbit classes.

The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the distribution
function:

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ labels the selected species, $n_s$ is its local particle number
density, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_s$ is its particle-number distribution in position and velocity
space, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity refers to one selected species, not a sum over different
species. For a species specified without charge-state resolution, its number
density is summed over all charge states; a charge-state-resolved population
retains only the selected state's contribution. The local value does not
imply flux-surface averaging; a flux-surface-averaged form averages this
same local moment over a magnetic flux surface.

The [fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density) is the same moment
restricted to suprathermal particles and excludes the thermal population. It
contributes to, but is distinct from, the full species density. Distinct
nonthermal populations of the same species contribute additively to that
full density.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_density
NAMES.short:
Local or flux-surface-averaged concentration of suprathermal particles of a
selected species, including trapped and passing orbits and excluding thermal
particles.
NAMES.long:
Fast-particle number density is the concentration of the suprathermal,
nonthermal population of a selected species. It includes all orbit classes
and may denote either a local density or its magnetic-flux-surface average.

The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the fast-particle
distribution:

$$
n_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\int f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle number density, $s$ labels
the selected species, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its fast-particle velocity
distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $t$ is time, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The flux-surface-averaged form is the differential-volume-weighted average
of this local moment over a magnetic flux surface. Superposed fast
populations of the same species contribute additively; different species are
not implicitly combined. For an ion species specified without charge-state
resolution, the fast-particle density is summed over all charge states.

This quantity is the fast-population contribution to [particle
density](name:particle_density), which also includes thermal particles. The
thermal population is excluded here; the name does not prescribe a universal
energy threshold separating the populations.

Orbit restrictions define [co-passing fast-particle
density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density), [counter-passing
fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density), and
[trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density). For a
complete, nonoverlapping orbit partition, these contributions sum to the
fast-particle density when evaluated with the same species selection and
averaging convention. Volume integration, followed by summation over the
included species, gives the [total fast-particle
count](name:total_fast_particle_count).
