NAMES.name: particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Particle flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales a
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on particle flux density while
preserving its direction or sign.
NAMES.long:
Particle flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales a
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on particle flux density in a
particle-transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while
preserving the direction or sign assigned by the underlying closure.

For a resolved particle-flux component, the limited flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{p,i}=\operatorname{sgn}\!\left(\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|,L_{p,i}\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{p,i}$ is the limited particle flux density, $p$ identifies
the transported particle population, $i$ identifies the resolved flux
component, $\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure flux
density, $\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless
free-streaming bound, and $L_{p,i}$ is the particle flux limiter
coefficient. The functions $\operatorname{sgn}$ and $|\cdot|$ denote the
sign and magnitude of the unconstrained closure flux, respectively.

The coefficient applies to particle transport rather than energy or momentum
transport. Its population scope may be electrons, aggregate ions, aggregate
neutrals, one specified ionization charge state, or one specified neutral
state; an aggregate form and a state-resolved form retain their respective
population definitions and are not summed across unlike populations. The
[electron particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:electron_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [ion
charge-state particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) are
specific instances of this common quantity.

As a particle-specific specialization of the [flux limiter
coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient), this quantity supplies the
multiplier for a particle flux-density bound; the parent also covers limiter
coefficients for other transported quantities, such as momentum flux.

NAMES.name: electron_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless multiplier that limits electron particle-flux density relative
to its collisionless free-streaming bound without reversing the transport
direction.
NAMES.long:
The electron particle flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor
that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on electron
particle-flux density in a particle-transport closure. It limits the
permitted magnitude while preserving the direction or sign assigned by the
underlying closure.

The admissible electron particle-flux magnitude satisfies:

$$
\left\lVert\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e\right\rVert \leq \Gamma_{e,\max} = L_e\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the electron particle-flux density, the
norm denotes its magnitude, $\Gamma_{e,\max}$ is its maximum permitted
magnitude, $L_e$ is the electron particle flux limiter coefficient, and
$\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming
bound. The subscript $e$ denotes electrons. The coefficient is nonnegative;
values below unity impose a stricter cap than the free-streaming bound. This
bound does not prescribe a particular interpolation between unconstrained
and limited transport.

This coefficient applies to the electron density equation, not to electron
energy or momentum transport. It is the electron-specific specialization of
the [particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), within the broader
[flux limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient) family. It is
distinct from the [ion particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), which limits ion
particle transport.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless multiplier that limits particle flux transport for one
specified ionization charge state relative to its free-streaming bound.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state particle flux limiter coefficient sets the maximum
permitted particle-flux density for one specified ionization charge state
relative to its free-streaming bound.

$$
\left\lVert \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s} \right\rVert \leq f_s \left\lVert \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{fs},s} \right\rVert
$$

where $f_s$ is the flux limiter coefficient, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s}$ is
the particle flux density of the specified ion charge state,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{fs},s}$ is its free-streaming particle-flux
bound, and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes vector magnitude.

The coefficient applies to particle transport for the selected ion charge
state, including thermal and nonthermal contributions when represented. It
is not summed over ion charge states and does not limit energy or momentum
transport. The corresponding [ion charge-state particle
flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) is the bounded vector quantity;
this coefficient is not itself a flux. The particle-channel limitation is
distinct from the [ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which applies to
momentum transport.

NAMES.name: ion_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for ions in a specified
charge state that scales the admissible particle flux relative to its
collisionless free-streaming bound.
NAMES.long:
The dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for an ion in a
specified charge state controls the admissible particle flux in the density
equation by scaling its collisionless free-streaming bound. It applies to
the thermal and nonthermal particle populations represented by that ion
state.

The limiting relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}} = \alpha_{p}\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited particle flux for the selected
ion state, $\alpha_{p}$ is this particle flux-limiter coefficient, and
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
particle-flux bound.

The coefficient is resolved for one specified ion charge state and is not
summed over ion charge states. It applies to particle transport only,
excluding the distinct energy- and momentum-flux limiter coefficients; it is
also distinct from the [neutral-state particle flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), which
applies to a neutral internal state. The undirected coefficient is not a
poloidal, parallel, or vertical projection.

This quantity is the ion-state specialization of the broader [particle
flux-limiter coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient): the
parent supplies the same particle-transport limiting concept without this
ion-state restriction.

NAMES.name: neutral_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient that limits the particle flux carried by a
specified neutral state by scaling its collisionless free-streaming bound.
NAMES.long:
The dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for a specified neutral
state controls the admissible particle flux in the density equation by
scaling its collisionless free-streaming bound. It applies to thermal and
nonthermal particles belonging to that neutral state.

The limiting relation is

$$
|\Gamma_s| \leq \alpha_s\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs},s}
$$

where $\Gamma_s$ is the particle flux of the specified neutral state,
$\alpha_s$ is this flux-limiter coefficient, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs},s}$ is
the collisionless free-streaming bound for the same state.

The coefficient is specific to the named neutral state and applies to the
total particle-flux contribution from its thermal and nonthermal
populations; it is not summed over different neutral states. It limits
particle transport only and does not represent the separate momentum-flux
limitation described by [neutral momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

This quantity is the neutral-state specialization of the broader [particle
flux limiter coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient). The
corresponding [ion-state particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) applies the
same limiting relationship to a specified ion state rather than to a neutral
state.

NAMES.name: particle_source_rate_due_to_distribution_function_driven
NAMES.short:
Distribution-function-driven particle source rate is the net particle gain
or loss per physical volume and time from a kinetic source acting on a
specified population.
NAMES.long:
Distribution-function-driven particle source rate is the net volumetric
particle production or removal contributed by a source acting on a specified
population's kinetic distribution. It is the contribution of that source to
the particle continuity equation.

The rate is the zeroth velocity moment of the kinetic source term:

$$
S(\mathbf{x},t) = \int Q(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $S$ is the volumetric particle source rate, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial
position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $Q$ is the kinetic
particle source density per velocity-space volume, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the full velocity space
of the specified population.

The quantity includes particle gains and losses from the specified source,
not a total over unrelated source mechanisms. It does not impose a
particular species, charge state, or thermal-population restriction. It is
distinct from the velocity-space-resolved source density and from density
changes caused by transport-flux divergence.

No spatial averaging or volume integration is implied. Integrating this
quantity over a specified physical volume gives the corresponding
[volume-integrated particle source
rate](name:volume_integrated_particle_source_rate).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the specified source adds particles to the
population; negative when it removes them.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Pressure of fast electrons perpendicular to the local magnetic field is the
mean of the two transverse normal stresses carried by their random motion.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of fast electrons perpendicular to the local magnetic field is the
transverse normal stress contributed by the suprathermal electron
population. In a gyrotropic description, it is the common normal stress in
either of the two field-perpendicular directions.

The perpendicular pressure is the transverse projection of the fast-electron
pressure tensor:

$$
p_{e,f,\perp}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{e,f}-\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{e,f}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right)
$$

where $p_{e,f,\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-electron pressure,
$\mathbf{P}_{e,f}$ is the [fast-electron pressure
tensor](name:fast_electron_pressure) describing momentum transport from
random motion, $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the tensor trace, and
$\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the nonzero
local magnetic field $\mathbf B$.

This quantity includes only suprathermal electrons and excludes
thermal-electron pressure, ion pressure, and stress from directed bulk
motion. The factor of one-half averages the two transverse normal stresses
rather than summing them; it does not imply isotropy between perpendicular
and parallel stresses.

The complementary [parallel fast-electron
pressure](name:parallel_fast_electron_pressure) is the field-aligned
projection, $p_{e,f,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf
b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{e,f}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}$, where $p_{e,f,\parallel}$
denotes that parallel pressure. Together, the parallel and perpendicular
pressures specify the gyrotropic fast-electron pressure tensor, but they
need not be equal.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Pressure of fast ions of one species and charge state arising from random
motion perpendicular to the local magnetic field, averaged over the two
transverse directions.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of fast ions of one specified species and charge state is the
field-perpendicular principal component of their gyrotropic kinetic pressure
tensor. It describes stress from velocity fluctuations about that
population's mean flow, averaged over the two transverse directions.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse second central
moment of the fast-ion distribution:

$$
p_{\perp,s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{2}\int w_\perp^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\perp,s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular fast-ion pressure
for species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_s$ is the
ion mass, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is that population's velocity
distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The quantity $w_\perp$ is the magnitude of
the component of $\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ perpendicular to the local
magnetic field, where $\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ is the mean velocity of the
specified fast-ion population.

This quantity includes only the suprathermal ions of the specified species
and charge state, without summation over species or charge states. It
excludes thermal-ion pressure, electron pressure, and mean-flow momentum
flux. It is one transverse principal pressure, not the sum of the two
transverse stresses or the isotropic trace pressure.

Together with the field-parallel component, it specifies the gyrotropic
[fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure).
Summing over all charge states of the same ion species gives the
[perpendicular fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure);
summing additionally over all fast-ion species gives the [perpendicular
total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure).

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Pressure of a suprathermal neutral species is the mean normal kinetic stress
perpendicular to the local magnetic field, averaged over internal states.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of a suprathermal neutral species perpendicular to the local
magnetic field is the mean of its two transverse normal kinetic stresses. It
is the field-perpendicular component in a gyrotropic description of neutral
kinetic stress; the magnetic field supplies the reference direction, not a
magnetic confinement force on the neutrals.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse projection of the
kinetic pressure tensor:

$$
p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\perp} = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}\left(\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a} - \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right)\right\rangle_a
$$

where $p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-neutral
pressure, $0$ denotes the neutral population, $a$ labels an internal state,
$\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a}$ is the kinetic pressure tensor of the
suprathermal neutral species in that state, $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the
tensor trace, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_a$ denotes averaging over internal
states. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the
local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, which must be nonzero to define this
projection.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and excludes thermal neutrals,
ionized particles, and contributions from other species. When multiple
internal states are present, their perpendicular pressures are averaged
rather than summed; the averaging weights are unspecified. The
[state-resolved perpendicular suprathermal neutral
pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure)
instead applies to one specified internal state.

The transverse projection corresponds to the perpendicular component of
[fast neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure), but the internal-state
average defined here differs from that parent's internal-state-summed
aggregation. Its directional counterpart is the [parallel fast neutral
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure), which resolves stress along
the local magnetic field rather than across it.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift of one ion
charge state onto a specified direction perpendicular to the magnetic field
in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma onto a specified direction perpendicular to the
magnetic field. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the
guiding-center motion of individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\perp} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,\perp}$ is the signed perpendicular diamagnetic-drift
velocity component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure,
$\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the
signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp$ is the specified positive unit vector perpendicular
to the local magnetic field. Directions may be expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical frame $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry
axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow.

Perpendicularity alone does not select a unique direction within the plane
normal to the magnetic field; the orientation of $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp$
must therefore be specified. This quantity is a signed component, not the
drift-speed magnitude, and its direction is not necessarily cylindrical
radial or flux-surface-normal. Because the diamagnetic drift vector is
perpendicular to the magnetic field, the corresponding [parallel ion
charge-state velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
vanishes.

The species-level [perpendicular ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:perpendicular_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of that species, using
the same perpendicular projection direction. It is not the sum of their
velocity components.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified
ion charge state has a component along the specified positive perpendicular
unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp$, expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density produced by diamagnetic drift in a
magnetized plasma, representing the signed field-aligned return current that
cancels the divergence of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current.
NAMES.long:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed
field-aligned scalar return current associated with the
pressure-gradient-driven current described by
[current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
It enforces charge-current continuity by canceling the divergence of the
perpendicular diamagnetic current on a magnetic flux surface in toroidal
geometry.

The scalar amplitude $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is defined by the
current-continuity condition

$$
\nabla \cdot \left(j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}\mathbf{b}\right) = -\nabla \cdot \left(\frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p}{B^2}\right)
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is the signed scalar Pfirsch-Schlueter current
density due to diamagnetic drift, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit
vector along the magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field,
$B^2=\mathbf{B}\cdot\mathbf{B}$, and $p$ is the isotropic scalar plasma
pressure.

This scalar denotes the amplitude multiplying the magnetic-field unit
vector, not an independent vector current and not a cylindrical component. A
flux-surface-constant parallel current component not required by the
diamagnetic-current divergence is excluded; the component-oriented
[parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
denotes the parallel projection of the same field-aligned contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional positive charge flows along the
local magnetic field direction $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short:
Parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the
signed field-aligned return current balancing the divergence of
pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular current in magnetized edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the
signed field-aligned return-current contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density) in magnetized edge plasma. It maintains
current continuity by balancing the divergence of the
pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular diamagnetic current.

The field-aligned projection is defined by

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS,dia}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is the parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter
diamagnetic-return-current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is its
field-aligned current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along that field.

In the quasineutral current-continuity balance, this contribution satisfies
$\nabla\cdot(j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS,dia}}\hat{\mathbf{b}})=-\nabla\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\perp,\mathrm{dia}}$,
where $\mathbf{j}_{\perp,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the perpendicular
diamagnetic-current-density vector and $\nabla\cdot$ denotes spatial
divergence. The quantity is local, without flux-surface averaging, and
excludes the perpendicular diamagnetic current itself and unrelated
parallel-current contributions.

The parent [Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is
intrinsically field-aligned, so the explicit parallel projection preserves
its signed amplitude rather than introducing a distinct mechanism. This is
the Pfirsch–Schlüter return-current contribution within [parallel current
density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), not the
total parallel plasma current.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the Pfirsch–Schlüter diamagnetic return
current flows in the direction of the local magnetic-field unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

NAMES.name: plasma_electrical_conductivity
NAMES.short:
Local plasma electrical-conductivity tensor mapping the electric-field
vector to the conductive current-density vector, including anisotropic
diagonal and off-diagonal coupling.
NAMES.long:
Plasma electrical conductivity is the local rank-two material response that
relates the plasma electric field to the conductive electric-current
density. It represents the collective plasma response without selecting a
particular species, orbit class, direction, or transport mechanism.

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}} = \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\mathrm{plasma}} \cdot \mathbf{E}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive
electric-current-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is
the plasma electrical-conductivity tensor, and $\mathbf{E}$ is the
electric-field vector. In components, $J_i = \sigma_{ij}E_j$, where $i$
identifies the current-density direction and $j$ identifies the
electric-field direction. The tensor may be represented in the right-handed
cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, or in the
magnetic-field-aligned basis $(\hat{b},\hat{e}_{\perp 1},\hat{e}_{\perp
2})$, where $\hat{b}$ is the local magnetic-field direction.

The full tensor retains all diagonal and off-diagonal couplings and is
therefore broader than any single component coefficient. It excludes
displacement current and contributions that are not the local conductive
response of the plasma. The [radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity),
[toroidal conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity), and [vertical
conductivity](name:vertical_conductivity) are diagonal component instances
in the cylindrical frame; [poloidal
conductivity](name:poloidal_conductivity) and [parallel
conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity) are corresponding projections in
flux-surface-tangent and magnetic-field-aligned directions, respectively.

NAMES.name: plasma_momentum
NAMES.short:
Plasma momentum is the volume-integrated linear momentum carried by the
included plasma species, for the component, projection, or aggregate
specified by a qualified child name. It is an extensive momentum integral,
not kinetic energy, angular momentum, or momentum flux.
NAMES.long:
Plasma momentum is the linear momentum carried by plasma matter after
integration over the stated plasma volume. For a scalar standard name it
denotes the specified component or projection of that integrated momentum; a
qualified aggregate such as [total plasma
momentum](name:total_plasma_momentum) denotes the corresponding net plasma
momentum rather than an axis-specific value.

For component or projection label $\alpha$, the plasma momentum is defined
by the volume integral of species momentum density:

$$
P_\alpha = \int_V \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x}) v_{s,\alpha}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_\alpha$ is the plasma momentum component or projection labeled by
$\alpha$, $V$ is the plasma volume, $s$ indexes the included plasma species,
$m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $n_s$ is the number density of
species $s$, $v_{s,\alpha}$ is the corresponding component or projection of
the species flow velocity, and $dV$ is a volume element.

This quantity is extensive over the included plasma volume and additive over
the included species. It excludes angular momentum, momentum flux or stress,
kinetic energy, and electromagnetic field momentum unless a more specific
qualified name explicitly changes that scope.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the scalar component or projection of the
volume-integrated species momentum points in the positive direction named by
the qualified standard name.

NAMES.name: plasma_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Vector Fick's-law transport coefficient relating the diffusive plasma
momentum flux to the local plasma momentum-density gradient, abstracting
over charged plasma constituents, ion charge states, and directional
projections in a magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Plasma momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the
diffusive plasma momentum flux and the negative local gradient of plasma
momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum
balance. It describes effective redistribution of aggregate charged-particle
momentum by collisional, neoclassical, turbulent, and drift-related
transport processes. As a direction-dependent vector coefficient, its
components represent anisotropic momentum transport along selected
directions or projections in a magnetized plasma.

The diffusive plasma momentum flux component along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is

$$
\Gamma_{g,i}^{p} = -D_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{p}\frac{\partial g_i^{p}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $D_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{p}$ is the plasma momentum diffusivity component
along $\hat{e}_i$, $\Gamma_{g,i}^{p}$ is the diffusive flux of the plasma
momentum-density component in that direction, $g_i^{p}$ is the aggregate
plasma momentum-density component, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along
$\hat{e}_i$. The negative sign encodes down-gradient diffusion: when
$D_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{p}$ is positive, the diffusive flux opposes the local
momentum-density gradient in that direction.

The aggregate plasma momentum density is formed from charged plasma
constituents, including electrons and ions; ion contributions are summed
over all charge states before the closure is applied, so this quantity is
distinct from an [ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). This parent name
abstracts over plasma-scoped specializations such as [edge plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity) and directional
components such as [vertical plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:vertical_plasma_momentum_diffusivity), where vertical
denotes the $\hat{Z}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame. It excludes neutral-fluid momentum diffusivity.

NAMES.name: edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Effective kinematic coefficient governing down-gradient transport of a
selected component or projection of aggregate edge-plasma momentum.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective kinematic momentum diffusivity associated
with a selected component or projection of edge-plasma momentum. Edge-plasma
momentum is the aggregate plasma momentum carried in the edge region; the
field-aligned specialization is [parallel edge-plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity).

For a scalar down-gradient closure for selected qualifier $a$, the diffusive
flux of edge-plasma momentum is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{a} = -\rho D_{a} \nabla u_{a}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{a}$ is the diffusive flux vector of
edge-plasma momentum associated with qualifier $a$, $\rho$ is the mass
density of the transported aggregate, $D_{a}$ is this diffusivity, $u_{a}$
is the corresponding edge-plasma velocity component or projection, and
$\nabla$ is the spatial gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient
transport.

The qualifier $a$ identifies the resolved momentum component, projection, or
transport direction; it is not necessarily the direction in which the flux
crosses a surface. The transported aggregate is ion-fluid momentum density
summed over ion species and charge states, excluding electron inertial
momentum, so this quantity is distinct from species-resolved momentum
diffusivities and from non-edge plasma momentum diffusivity.

NAMES.name: parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Kinematic coefficient relating the diffusive flux of field-parallel
edge-plasma bulk momentum to the opposing velocity gradient along the
magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel edge-plasma momentum diffusivity is the kinematic transport
coefficient governing field-aligned diffusion of the parallel component of
aggregate plasma bulk-flow [momentum](name:momentum). It applies to the
plasma population in the edge region, rather than to an individual ion
species or charge state.

In a local velocity-gradient closure, the field-parallel diffusive momentum
flux is:

$$
\Pi_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\rho_m\chi_{\parallel}\frac{\partial v_{\parallel}}{\partial \ell_{\parallel}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the flux of parallel bulk-flow
momentum along the magnetic field, $\rho_m$ is the aggregate plasma mass
density, $\chi_{\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, $v_{\parallel}$ is the
projection of the plasma [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the local magnetic field, and
$\ell_{\parallel}$ is arc length increasing along that field.

The aggregate momentum and mass density include the charged constituent
species and their charge states; the bulk velocity is their
mass-density-weighted mean. Neutral momentum is excluded. This coefficient
describes diffusive transport, not advective momentum transport, residual
stress, or external momentum sources. The parallel direction follows the
magnetic field and is not a synonym for the toroidal direction or the
flux-surface-normal direction.

This quantity is the field-aligned specialization of [edge-plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity). It has the kinematic
transport role described by [parallel momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), with the
additional restriction to aggregate edge-plasma momentum.

NAMES.name: poloidal_conductivity
NAMES.short:
Local electrical response coefficient relating a poloidal electric field to
conductive current density along the flux-surface tangent in a
constant-toroidal-angle plane.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal conductivity is the poloidal-poloidal projection of the local
electrical-conductivity tensor. The poloidal direction is tangent to a
magnetic flux surface within a plane of constant toroidal angle, rather than
normal to the surface.

The defining projection is:

$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{pp}} = \hat{e}_{\mathrm{p}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \hat{e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\sigma_{\mathrm{pp}}$ is poloidal conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$
is the electrical-conductivity tensor, and $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the
geometric poloidal unit tangent. The geometry is specified in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For an electric field directed entirely along the poloidal tangent, the
conductive response satisfies
$j_{\mathrm{c,p}}=\sigma_{\mathrm{pp}}E_{\mathrm{p}}$, where
$j_{\mathrm{c,p}}$ is the induced poloidal conductive current density and
$E_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal electric-field component. This is a local
plasma response coefficient, not a flux-surface average or an integrated
conductance. It does not include off-diagonal coupling from electric-field
components in other directions. Reversing the poloidal unit tangent leaves
the coefficient unchanged.

Unlike [parallel conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity), this coefficient
projects onto a geometric poloidal tangent rather than the magnetic-field
direction. [Toroidal conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity) is the
corresponding toroidal-toroidal projection of the same
electrical-conductivity tensor.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
poloidal projection of the electric current contribution associated with
magnetic-field-aligned viscous stress.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
projection of the current contribution associated with the divergence of
parallel viscous stress onto the poloidal direction. Parallel identifies the
viscous-stress mechanism, not the direction of this current component.

The defining projection is:

$$
j_{\mathrm p}^{(\mathrm{pv})} = \mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm p}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the poloidal current-density
contribution, $\mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the full [current-density
vector due to parallel
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), and
$\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the oriented local poloidal unit tangent.
The superscript $\mathrm{pv}$ identifies the parallel-viscosity
contribution. The tangent follows a magnetic-flux contour in the
major-radius–vertical plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. Its orientation toward increasing poloidal angle must be
specified by the poloidal-angle convention.

In the magnetized edge plasma, this is a local, mechanism-resolved
contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the total
poloidal current density or a flux-surface average. It excludes the
perpendicular-viscosity contribution, whose poloidal projection is [poloidal
current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).

Poloidal and magnetic-field-aligned directions are distinct: [parallel
current density due to parallel
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) projects
the same parent vector onto the local magnetic-field direction instead.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the parallel-viscosity current-density
contribution has a component along the poloidal tangent toward increasing
poloidal angle.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Poloidal component of the electron particle diffusion coefficient. It is the
poloidal-poloidal diagonal tensor component in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ),
where ρ labels magnetic flux surfaces, θ is poloidal angle, and φ is
toroidal angle, relating diffusive electron particle flux to the electron
density gradient along θ.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal electron diffusion coefficient is the electron particle
diffusivity acting along the poloidal direction tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ on a magnetic flux surface in flux coordinates
$(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ labels magnetic flux surfaces, $\theta$
is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. It is the poloidal-poloidal
diagonal component of an anisotropic particle-transport tensor, relating
diffusive electron particle flux to the electron density gradient along that
poloidal tangent.

For a Fickian closure of the diffusive part of the [poloidal electron
particle flux](name:poloidal_electron_particle_flux), the component along
the poloidal tangent satisfies:

$$
\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_{\theta} = -D^{e}_{\theta\theta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla n_e
$$

where $\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_{\theta}$ is the diffusive poloidal
component of the electron particle flux density, $D^{e}_{\theta\theta}$ is
the poloidal electron diffusion coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is
the unit tangent in the direction of increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and
$\phi$, and $n_e$ is the electron number density. The minus sign expresses
the down-gradient convention for positive diffusivity.

This is a particle transport quantity, distinct from electron energy
transport such as poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient. It
excludes convective contributions to the electron particle flux and
off-diagonal tensor couplings; radial transport across flux surfaces is
represented by radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient, and a
non-direction-specific electron particle diffusivity is represented by
[electron_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Poloidal electron energy flux is the signed electron kinetic-energy flow per
unit area normal to the local poloidal direction around the magnetic axis.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron energy flux represents local electron kinetic-energy
transport around the magnetic axis through a surface normal to the poloidal
direction. It includes conductive and particle-carried contributions to the
electron energy balance.

The component is defined by projection:

$$
\Gamma_{e,W,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,W,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal electron energy flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}$ is the full [electron energy
flux](name:electron_energy_flux) vector, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$
is the local poloidal unit vector. The poloidal direction lies in a plane of
constant toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is upward vertical position.

This is a local directional component, not a poloidal integral, flux-surface
average, or integrated power. It excludes ion-carried energy, whose
corresponding component is [poloidal ion energy
flux](name:poloidal_ion_energy_flux). Unlike [poloidal electron particle
flux](name:poloidal_electron_particle_flux), it describes transported energy
rather than transported electron number.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when electron energy flows clockwise around the
magnetic axis in a poloidal cross-section viewed with the toroidal symmetry
axis on the left and increasing $Z$ upward.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Poloidal electron particle flux is the signed net electron crossing rate per
unit area perpendicular to the local poloidal direction around a plasma
cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron particle flux is the signed net electron number flow per
unit area normal to the local poloidal direction. It describes particle
transport around a plasma cross-section, rather than transport along the
toroidal direction or necessarily along the magnetic field.

The defining velocity moment is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}} = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}) f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal electron particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the electron number-flux vector,
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the positive local poloidal unit tangent,
$\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $f_e$ is the local electron velocity
distribution normalized to electron number density, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The poloidal tangent lies in a
constant-toroidal-angle cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height. Its positive orientation must be specified by the
poloidal-direction convention.

The integral includes the full electron velocity distribution, with opposite
crossings contributing opposite signs. In the plasma edge, this remains a
local flux density: neither surface integration nor flux-surface averaging
is implied.

This component specializes [electron particle
flux](name:electron_particle_flux) to an oriented surface whose normal is
the poloidal unit tangent. It is a number flux, not an electric-charge flux;
unlike [poloidal electron energy flux](name:poloidal_electron_energy_flux),
it has no energy weighting.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net electron number flow follows the
specified positive local poloidal tangent, independently of the negative
electron charge.

NAMES.name: poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Poloidal flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on poloidal momentum-flux density
while preserving the direction or sign assigned to that component by the
transport closure.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on poloidal momentum-flux density
in a transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving
the sign assigned to the poloidal momentum-flux component by the
unconstrained closure.

For an unconstrained poloidal momentum-flux density
$\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}$, a direction-preserving limited flux can
be expressed as:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}} = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_{\mathrm{pol}} \Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited poloidal
momentum-flux density, $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the
unconstrained closure value, $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the
non-negative collisionless free-streaming bound for the same poloidal
component, and $L_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal flux limiter coefficient.

This quantity is the poloidal component of the [momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and a
component-specific child of the [flux limiter
coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient). It is distinct from the [radial
flux limiter coefficient](name:radial_flux_limiter_coefficient) and
[toroidal flux limiter coefficient](name:toroidal_flux_limiter_coefficient),
and it does not by itself specify a particle species, charge state, neutral
internal state, or spatial region. Because $L_{\mathrm{pol}}$ multiplies the
non-negative bound $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$, it is a non-negative
magnitude-scaling coefficient; the signed direction of the limited flux is
carried by $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and
$\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$, not by the coefficient.

NAMES.name: poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short:
Poloidal component of gyrocenter orbit angular frequency, equal to the
signed rate of gyrocenter advance in poloidal angle θ within flux
coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal gyrocenter frequency is the poloidal component of gyrocenter
orbit angular frequency in the flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$,
where $\rho$ is a radial flux-surface label, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and
$\phi$ is toroidal angle. It describes gyrocenter advance after averaging
over the fast cyclotron gyration, retaining the slower drift and bounce or
transit motion.

It is defined by

$$
\omega_{\theta,gc} = \frac{d\theta_{gc}}{dt}
$$

where $\omega_{\theta,gc}$ is the poloidal gyrocenter angular frequency,
$\theta_{gc}$ is the gyrocenter poloidal angle measured in radians, and $t$
is time measured in seconds.

This component is distinct from the [toroidal gyrocenter
frequency](name:toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency), which measures advance in
$\phi$; together they form the [gyrocenter
frequency](name:gyrocenter_frequency). Passing particles can circulate
continuously in poloidal angle, whereas trapped particles reverse their
poloidal motion during bounce excursions. The fast cyclotron angular
frequency is excluded.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma. It is the
poloidal component of the vector defined by [ion charge state convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), rather than an energy-
or momentum-transport velocity.

The associated advective particle flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}} = n_z v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}}$ is the poloidal advective
particle flux density, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, and
$v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is this velocity component. The
component is expressed in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The charge state is resolved rather than summed over ionization states.
Unqualified convection velocity denotes particle transport; [poloidal ion
charge state energy convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity)
represents the distinct energy-transport channel.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the component points toward increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective convection (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Poloidal component of the effective velocity convecting energy for one ion
charge state along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective poloidal convection velocity for the energy
carried by one specified ion charge state. It is the poloidal component of
the ion charge-state energy convection velocity, representing advective
rather than diffusive energy transport.

The poloidal convective energy flux is defined by

$$
\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}} = v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}\,\mathcal{E}_{i,q}
$$

where $\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the poloidal
convective energy flux, $v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}$ is this effective velocity,
$\mathcal{E}_{i,q}$ is the energy density of ion charge state $q$, and $i$
identifies the ion species. The component is expressed in flux coordinates
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\theta$ the poloidal coordinate.

This quantity is distinct from the particle-transport velocity [poloidal ion
charge-state convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and from the
energy diffusivity [poloidal ion charge-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the associated convective energy flux is
directed toward increasing poloidal coordinate $\theta$.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective convection (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity coefficient relating the non-diffusive convective flux of
poloidal momentum to the poloidal momentum density of ions of one species in
a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient governs advective, non-diffusive transport of poloidal
[momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one specified species and
charge state. It specializes the [ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) to the
poloidal-momentum channel and is not the ion charge state's bulk poloidal
flow velocity.

The convective contribution to the momentum-flux closure is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,\mathrm p}\,g_{s,\mathrm p}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\mathrm p$ denotes
the poloidal momentum component, $\Pi_{s,\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its
convective flux through an oriented surface, $g_{s,\mathrm p}$ is its local
momentum density, and $V_{s,\mathrm p}$ is this effective convection
coefficient.

The poloidal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface within a plane
containing the toroidal symmetry axis. The poloidal label identifies the
transported momentum component; it does not independently specify the
direction through which that momentum is transported. The positive flux
direction must therefore be specified by the oriented transport surface.

This coefficient applies to one charge state, without summation or averaging
over charge states. It excludes the gradient-driven diffusive contribution
described by [poloidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity], as well as
separately represented residual stress and external momentum sources.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive poloidal momentum is convected along
the positive normal of the oriented transport surface.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical damping of ordered
poloidal flow momentum carried by ions of one specified species and charge
state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate quantifies how rapidly
collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses relax the ordered poloidal
[momentum](name:momentum) of a specified ion species and charge state. The
poloidal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface within a plane
containing the toroidal symmetry axis.

In a linear relaxation closure, its contribution to the poloidal
momentum-density balance is:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial \delta g_{s,\mathrm{p}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{s,\mathrm{p}}\,\delta g_{s,\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\delta g_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is the departure of the poloidal flow
momentum density from its relaxed value, $s$ identifies the ion species and
charge state, $\nu_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is this damping rate, $t$ is time, and
the subscript $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal direction. The restriction
labeled $\mathrm{damp}$ includes only the relaxation contribution. For a
fixed positive rate, this contribution produces exponential decay of the
departure from the relaxed value.

This is the poloidal directional coefficient of [ion charge-state momentum
damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate). It applies to
one specified charge state, without summation or averaging over charge
states; [poloidal ion momentum damping
rate](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate) instead describes the
species-level bulk-flow relaxation.

The rate describes local momentum relaxation, not transport driven by a
spatial gradient. It is therefore distinct from [poloidal ion charge-state
momentum diffusivity], which governs diffusive momentum transport. It does
not include convective transport or externally applied momentum sources.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective kinematic coefficient relating diffusive transport of poloidal
flow momentum to flow shear for ions of one species in a specified charge
state.
NAMES.long:
This effective kinematic coefficient governs diffusive redistribution of the
poloidal component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one
species in a specified ionization state. It enters that charge state's
poloidal momentum balance; the poloidal label identifies the transported
momentum component rather than prescribing transport along a poloidal arc.

In a local velocity-shear closure, the associated diffusive momentum flux
is:

$$
\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_s n_s D_{s,\mathrm{p}}\frac{\partial v_{s,\mathrm{p}}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\mathrm{p}$ denotes
the poloidal component, $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
diffusive flux of that component along the transport direction, $m_s$ is the
ion mass, $n_s$ is the charge-state number density, $D_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is
this diffusion coefficient, $v_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is the charge-state mean
poloidal velocity, and $\ell$ is physical distance along the transport
direction specified by the closure.

The poloidal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface at fixed
toroidal angle in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels
flux surfaces, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal
angle. The coefficient is charge-state resolved, not summed or averaged over
charge states, and is not restricted to an edge region.

It specializes the [momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) to poloidal flow momentum
and a specified ion charge state. The velocity-shear closure acts on the
charge-state poloidal velocity gradient, not the gradient of total plasma
momentum density. It excludes advective transport, represented separately by
the [ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), as well as
residual stress and external momentum sources.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Poloidal momentum flux for one ion charge state is the net transfer rate of
that state's poloidal linear momentum across a magnetic flux surface,
divided by the surface area.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal momentum flux for an ion charge state is the
surface-area-normalized rate at which that state's poloidal linear
[momentum](name:momentum) crosses a magnetic flux surface. The poloidal
label selects the transported momentum component; transport is across the
surface, not along a poloidal arc.

The defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{p}} = \frac{\dot{P}_{z,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{out}}}{A}
$$

where $\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{p}}$ is this momentum flux,
$\dot{P}_{z,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the signed net outward transfer
rate of poloidal linear momentum across the entire flux surface, $A$ is that
surface's area, and $z$ identifies the specified ionic charge state. The
subscript $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal component. The positive poloidal
direction is tangent to the surface toward increasing poloidal angle
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels flux
surfaces and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

This quantity includes convective and nonconvective momentum transport,
rather than only its diffusive contribution. It is a flux density, not the
surface-integrated transfer rate or a local momentum source. It applies to
one ionic charge state and is not summed over charge states.

It is the poloidal transported-momentum component of [ion charge-state
momentum flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). Summing it over all
ionic charge states of the same species gives the [poloidal ion momentum
flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net transport of positive poloidal
momentum is outward toward the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Poloidal ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net ion crossing rate
per unit area normal to the local poloidal direction for one species and
ionization state, including thermal and nonthermal ions.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net number flow of
ions of one specified species and ionization charge state per unit area
perpendicular to the local poloidal direction. It describes local poloidal
particle transport in the edge plasma, including thermal and nonthermal
ions.

The flux is the poloidal projection of the state's particle-flux vector:

$$
\Gamma_{s,q,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,q}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{s,q,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,q}$ is the net particle-flux vector including
thermal and nonthermal contributions, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$
identifies its ionization charge number, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$
is the local poloidal unit vector. In the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height. The poloidal unit vector lies in a plane of constant
$\phi$ and follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$; the geometric
orientation of that angle must be specified.

This is the [ion charge-state particle
flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) evaluated through an oriented
surface whose normal is the poloidal unit vector. It is local, not
surface-integrated or flux-surface-averaged, and it is not summed over
charge states. Summing the charge-state contributions for the same species
gives the [poloidal ion particle flux](name:poloidal_ion_particle_flux).
Unlike [parallel ion charge-state particle
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), this projection selects
a geometric poloidal direction rather than the magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net ion number flow follows increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed mean ion flow along the poloidal tangent for one specified species
and ionization charge state, distinct from thermal motion and
charge-state-averaged flow.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state velocity is the local poloidal projection of
the bulk-flow velocity of ions belonging to one specified species and
ionization charge state. It describes directed motion after averaging over
particle velocities, rather than the random thermal velocity spread.

For a nonzero charge-state population, the component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{p},q}=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\mathbf u_q=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\frac{\int\mathbf v f_q(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_q(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{\mathrm{p},q}$ is the poloidal velocity component, $q$ identifies
the ionic charge number, $\mathbf u_q$ is the [ion charge-state
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity,
and $f_q$ is the local velocity distribution of the selected species and
charge state. The vector $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the unit poloidal
tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the specified
flux-coordinate frame $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels magnetic
surfaces and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The orientation of $\theta$ must
be specified with that frame.

This quantity retains charge-state resolution and implies neither
charge-state averaging nor flux-surface averaging. No particular spatial
locus is imposed. The [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity), by contrast, is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of the selected species.

Unlike the [parallel ion charge-state
velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity), which projects along the
local magnetic field, this component projects along the poloidal tangent. It
is also distinct from the effective [poloidal ion-state momentum convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_state_momentum_convection_velocity), which
parameterizes momentum transport rather than defining the population's first
velocity moment.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the bulk flow of the selected ion charge
state projects toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed poloidal projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid
velocity for one ion charge state, distinct from individual guiding-center
motion and total poloidal flow.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the
guiding-center motion of individual ions and is not restricted to the plasma
edge.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\mathrm{p}} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal diamagnetic-drift velocity
component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla
p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field
vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle
charge, and $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is tangent to the local poloidal contour
toward increasing specified poloidal angle $\theta$. It lies in a
constant-toroidal-angle plane of the right-handed cylindrical frame
$(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The orientation of $\theta$ must
be specified independently of the magnetic-field direction.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow. It is the diamagnetic contribution to the [poloidal ion
charge-state velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity), not the
total poloidal flow. Although the diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular
to the magnetic field, its geometric poloidal component need not vanish.

For a species-level velocity, the diamagnetic contribution is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, not their sum.
Projecting that mean onto the local binormal direction gives the sibling
[binormal ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which differs
from this quantity in both projection and charge-state aggregation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified
ion charge state has a component toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$
in a constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective particle transport coefficient relating an ion species’ poloidal
diffusive flux to the opposing poloidal gradient of its number density
summed over ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion diffusion coefficient characterizes local Fickian particle
diffusion of a specified ion species along the poloidal tangent. It
describes the poloidal-poloidal diagonal response rather than a
direction-independent diffusivity or a particular microscopic transport
mechanism.

In flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, $\rho$ labels magnetic flux
surfaces, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.
Retaining only the poloidal density-gradient contribution, the defining
relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,\mathrm{p}}\,\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}\cdot\nabla n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive ion
particle flux density contributed by that gradient, $D_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is
the poloidal ion diffusion coefficient, $n_i$ is the ion species’ number
density, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit tangent toward
increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$, and $\nabla$ denotes the
spatial gradient. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for
positive diffusivity.

The density and particle flux are summed over all ionic charge states of the
specified species, excluding neutrals and other ion species. The coefficient
describes the effective flux-gradient response of this aggregate; it is not
a sum of charge-state diffusion coefficients. In contrast, the [poloidal ion
charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) applies
to one specified ionic charge state.

This is the poloidal-poloidal diagonal specialization of the
particle-diffusion response associated with the direction-unspecified [ion
diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient). It excludes
convective particle flux and ion energy or momentum diffusion, is not a sum
of directional coefficients, and does not encode off-diagonal tensor
couplings. Consequently, the displayed relation represents the complete
poloidal diffusive flux only when contributions from other gradient
directions vanish or are neglected.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Poloidal ion particle flux is the signed net ion crossing rate per area
normal to the local poloidal direction for one species, summed over all
ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion particle flux is the local net number flow of one specified ion
species through a surface perpendicular to the local poloidal direction,
divided by that surface's area. It includes thermal and nonthermal ions and
counts oppositely directed crossings with opposite signs.

The poloidal projection and charge-state aggregation are defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm p} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p} = \sum_{z>0}\Gamma_{i,z,\mathrm p}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm p}$ is the species-level poloidal ion particle
flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the ion number-flux vector for species $i$,
$\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the local positive poloidal unit vector,
$z$ is the ionic charge number, and $\Gamma_{i,z,\mathrm p}$ is the
[poloidal ion charge-state particle
flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for that species and
charge state.

The sum includes all ionic charge states of the selected species, excludes
neutral particles, and does not aggregate different species. This quantity
is [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux) evaluated with the surface
normal aligned with the local poloidal direction; it is not an
electric-charge flux, a surface-integrated particle rate, or a flux-surface
average.

The poloidal direction lies in a plane of constant toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position. Its positive
orientation follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$; the orientation
chosen for $\theta$ must be specified. A poloidal projection is not, in
general, a magnetic-field-parallel or flux-surface-normal projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net ion number flow is directed along
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming upper bound on the flux
of poloidal momentum carried by a specified ion state in edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient sets the free-streaming bound used to limit the flux of
poloidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one specified ion state in
edge plasma. It is the state-resolved poloidal member of the [momentum flux
limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) family.

The limited momentum flux satisfies:

$$
\left|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}\right| \leq \alpha_{s,\mathrm{p}}\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion state, $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal
momentum component, $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is its limited flux
across an oriented surface, $\alpha_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is this nonnegative
limiter coefficient, and $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the
nonnegative free-streaming reference flux magnitude. Limiting reduces the
flux magnitude without reversing its direction; the coefficient does not
specify a unique interpolation between unrestricted and limited fluxes.

Poloidal identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction in
which momentum crosses the oriented surface. The coefficient is neither the
momentum flux itself nor a momentum diffusivity.

The selected ion state may distinguish ionization or other internal states.
This coefficient applies to that state alone, without aggregation over
states, unlike the species-level [poloidal ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). When the
state is specifically a charge state, the corresponding specialization is
the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the internal transport barrier is the ψ value on
the nested magnetic flux surface that marks the barrier location between the
magnetic axis and plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the internal transport barrier is the
poloidal-flux-function value $\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ on the nested magnetic
flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier. An internal
transport barrier is a core or mid-radius region of reduced turbulent
transport; this quantity gives the barrier location as a poloidal-flux
label, not the magnitude of the transport reduction.

The surface-value definition is

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \psi(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ITB}})
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the magnetic flux surface identified
with the internal transport barrier and $\psi(\mathcal{S})$ is the [poloidal
magnetic flux at a flux
surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface) for surface
$\mathcal{S}$.

Relative to the axis and boundary references, the normalized poloidal-flux
label is $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ITB}} = (\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}} -
\psi_{\mathrm{axis}})/(\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})$,
where $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic
axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) and
$\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary). Absolute $\psi$
values include an additive reference; direct comparison of
$\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ values requires the same additive reference and sign
convention, whereas flux differences and normalized labels are unchanged by
a common additive offset. This poloidal-flux location is distinct from the
[toroidal flux radius at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
from edge pedestal loci such as the [poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal
top](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a flux surface outward from the magnetic axis
toward the plasma boundary has $\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}} > 0$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Poloidal projection of the gage-dependent magnetic vector potential along
the unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates (psi,
θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component $A_\theta$ is the projection of the [magnetic vector
potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) $\mathbf{A}$ onto the unit
tangent in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux
coordinates $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$. It is a signed, gage-dependent component
of the electromagnetic potential.

The defining projection is:

$$
A_\theta(\psi,\theta,\phi)=\mathbf{A}(\psi,\theta,\phi)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta
$$

where $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic vector potential,
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the unit tangent toward increasing $\theta$,
$\psi$ is the flux label, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The full
potential satisfies $\mathbf{B}=\nabla\times\mathbf{A}$, where $\mathbf{B}$
is the magnetic induction.

Only the curl of $\mathbf{A}$ is gage invariant, so this component depends
on the chosen gage. Unlike the [parallel magnetic vector
potential](name:parallel_magnetic_vector_potential), it projects onto the
flux-coordinate poloidal tangent rather than the magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\mathbf{A}$ points along
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$, toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Magnetic vector potential, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Poloidal momentum flux is the signed rate per unit area at which the
poloidal component of linear momentum crosses an oriented surface.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal momentum flux is the poloidal component of the linear-momentum
transfer across an oriented surface per unit area and time. The poloidal
qualifier identifies the transported momentum component, while the surface
normal identifies the transport direction.

The component is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm p} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\mathsf{T}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm p}$ is the poloidal momentum flux, $\hat{\mathbf
e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the positive poloidal unit vector, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}$
is the [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) across the oriented surface,
$\mathsf{T}$ is the linear-momentum-flux tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is
the chosen surface-normal unit vector. The poloidal direction lies in a
constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

This quantity applies to a selected ion or neutral population, or to a
combined population whose constituent momentum fluxes are summed. Unlike
[poloidal ion momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux), it does not
specify an ion carrier. It includes convective transport, pressure, and
viscous or turbulent stress contributions rather than only diffusive
transport. It is a transport rate of [momentum](name:momentum), not momentum
itself, and implies neither transport along the poloidal tangent nor
flux-surface averaging.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net transfer across the chosen surface
normal carries clockwise poloidal momentum, viewed around the magnetic axis
in the poloidal plane with the machine symmetry axis to the left and
increasing $Z$ upward.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective poloidal advection velocity for particle transport of a specified
neutral internal state, defined by the coefficient multiplying its number
density in the poloidal particle flux.
NAMES.long:
The effective poloidal convection velocity is the coefficient describing
non-diffusive advection of particles in a specified neutral internal state.
It is the poloidal component of the [neutral internal-state convection
velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity), rather than a
scalar speed.

For the corresponding particle flux, the defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol}} = n_{\mathrm{n,s}} v_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal particle-flux component,
$n_{\mathrm{n,s}}$ is the number density of the specified neutral internal
state, and $v_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is this effective convection velocity.

This quantity applies to particle-density transport and excludes
coefficients for energy or momentum transport, such as the [poloidal
neutral-state energy convection
velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_energy_convection_velocity). The
poloidal direction is defined by increasing $\theta$ in the flux coordinates
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective particle convection is directed
toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.
