NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective poloidal particle diffusivity for neutral atoms or molecules in a
specified internal state, relating poloidal diffusive flux to that state's
physical number-density gradient along the poloidal direction in flux
coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the neutral internal-state diffusion coefficient
governs Fickian particle transport of neutral atoms or molecules in a
specified internal state along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates
$(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is the proportionality coefficient between the
signed poloidal diffusive particle flux and the physical poloidal gradient
of that state's number density.

For a neutral internal state $s$, the poloidal Fickian relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\theta,s}\,\frac{1}{h_\theta}\frac{\partial n_s}{\partial \theta}
$$

where $D_{\theta,s}$ is the poloidal neutral internal-state diffusion
coefficient, $\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
particle-flux component, $n_s$ is the number density of neutral atoms or
molecules in internal state $s$, and $h_\theta =
|\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial\theta|_{\rho,\phi}$ is the poloidal metric
scale factor for flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The factor
$h_\theta^{-1}\partial/\partial\theta$ is the derivative along physical
poloidal arc length, not a bare angular derivative.

This coefficient applies only to particle-number diffusion of the specified
neutral internal state. It excludes momentum diffusion, energy diffusion,
radial diffusion, and off-diagonal transport couplings unless such effects
are explicitly represented as part of the effective scalar coefficient.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the poloidal diffusive particle flux is
opposite to the physical poloidal gradient of the state number density, with
a positive flux component pointing toward increasing poloidal coordinate
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Particle effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Poloidal effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density
of a specified neutral internal state, directed along increasing poloidal
angle θ in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density
of a specified neutral internal state is the component of the effective
convection velocity along the tangent direction of increasing poloidal angle
$\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is the
poloidal directional realization of the [neutral internal-state energy
convection
velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity).

For the poloidal transport direction, the convective energy-flux component
is defined by

$$
q_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}} = u_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}} w_{E,\nu}
$$

where $q_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the poloidal convective
energy-flux component, $u_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this poloidal
effective convection velocity, $w_{E,\nu}$ is the energy density of the
neutral internal state, and $\nu$ identifies that state.

The quantity applies to the specified state and does not sum over all
neutral internal states. It is the poloidal member of the directional set
that also includes the radial neutral internal-state energy convection
velocity and the [field-aligned neutral internal-state energy convection
velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity);
by contrast, neutral species energy convection velocity represents the
corresponding energy transport aggregated over a neutral species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective velocity points in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate
system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, making the convective energy flux positive in
that direction.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective convection (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient
multiplying the poloidal temperature gradient of neutral particles in a
specified internal state in diffusive thermal-energy transport. It is
internal-state-resolved and represents only the Fickian poloidal
contribution.
NAMES.long:
Fick's-law poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is
the scalar poloidal diffusivity for energy transport by neutral particles in
a specified internal state, and is the poloidal component form of the
[neutral internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It
is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal
states, and relates only the poloidal projection of the diffusive
thermal-energy flux to the poloidal temperature gradient of those same
particles.

The poloidal projection is taken along the tangent obtained by increasing
the poloidal angle $\theta$ at constant flux coordinate $\rho$ and toroidal
angle $\phi$ in a chosen flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The
Fickian poloidal contribution is defined by

$$
q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,\theta} = - n_{n,s} D^{\theta}_{E,n,s} \, \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla T_{n,s}
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,\theta}$ is the poloidal component of the
diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state
$s$, positive in the direction of increasing $\theta$;
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the corresponding unit poloidal tangent;
$n_{n,s}$ is the number density of those particles; $D^{\theta}_{E,n,s}$ is
this coefficient; and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature.

The coefficient includes only the diagonal Fickian term driven by
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla T_{n,s}$ and excludes convective
energy transport, sources, sinks, cross-gradient tensor terms, and effective
coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. The factor
$n_{n,s}\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla T_{n,s}$ is the
temperature-gradient contribution to the poloidal gradient of internal
thermal-energy density; an energy-density-gradient form using
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla(n_{n,s}T_{n,s})$ is equivalent only
when the density-gradient contribution along the poloidal tangent is absent.

It specializes the internal-state energy diffusion coefficient to neutral
particles and the poloidal projection. It is distinct from the [radial
neutral internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the
[poloidal neutral energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity).

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Poloidal component of the effective advective velocity transporting momentum
for a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma transport,
distinct from bulk particle flow; it lies in the poloidal direction of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the [neutral internal-state momentum convection
velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection)
is the effective advective velocity for poloidal momentum transport of a
single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport,
distinct from bulk particle flow. The poloidal direction lies in the $R$-$Z$
plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The component is defined by projecting the effective momentum-convection
velocity onto the local poloidal unit vector:

$$
V_{\mathrm{mom},\mathrm{pol}}^{(n,\alpha)} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is the effective
momentum-convection velocity for neutral species $n$ in internal state
$\alpha$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local poloidal unit
vector, and $V_{\mathrm{mom},\mathrm{pol}}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is the resulting
component.

This quantity represents momentum-transport advection rather than neutral
center-of-mass or particle-flow velocity. The [vertical neutral
internal-state momentum convection
velocity](name:vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
provides the complementary cylindrical projection, while the [poloidal
neutral state momentum convection
velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity) does not
express the explicit internal-state resolution retained here.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the projected velocity points in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\theta$ the poloidal angle of the
adopted flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

sources.leaf_definition: Momentum effective convection (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets
sources.parent_definition: Transport coefficients related to the momentum equations of the state considered. The various components two levels below this node refer to the momentum vector components, while their flux is given in the direction perpendicular to the edges or faces of the grid.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux is the signed net number flow
of one neutral species in a specified internal quantum state per area
perpendicular to the local poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux is the local net number
transport of one neutral atomic or molecular species in a specified internal
quantum state along the poloidal direction. It counts oppositely directed
crossings with opposite signs, using area perpendicular to that direction.

The component is the poloidal projection of the state-resolved particle-flux
vector:

$$
\Gamma^{0}_{a,\mathrm p} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p} = \int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}) f^{0}_{a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma^{0}_{a,\mathrm p}$ is this poloidal component,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{a}$ is the neutral particle-flux vector for the
selected species and state, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the local
poloidal unit vector, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, $f^{0}_{a}$ is the
velocity distribution normalized to the state's number density, and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space volume element. The superscript $0$ identifies
neutrals, $a$ labels the internal state, and $\mathrm p$ identifies the
poloidal projection.

The poloidal direction lies in a plane of constant toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position. Its
orientation follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ around the magnetic
axis; the orientation of $\theta$ must be specified independently of the
magnetic-field direction.

This specializes [neutral internal-state particle
flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) to a surface normal aligned
with the poloidal direction. It includes thermal and nonthermal neutrals in
the selected state and is neither a sum over internal states nor a
surface-integrated arrival rate. Summing over all internal states of the
same species gives the [poloidal neutral particle
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux). The [parallel neutral
internal-state particle
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) instead projects
transport along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net neutral particle transport is toward
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Signed projection onto an oriented local poloidal direction of an effective
E×B fluid drift assigned to one neutral species in a specified internal
state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state E×B drift
velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
is its signed projection along a specified local poloidal direction. This
direction lies in a constant-toroidal-angle plane of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
positive local poloidal orientation must be specified explicitly.

For the assigned ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v^0_{E,\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{v}^0_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v^0_{E,\mathrm{p}}$ is the effective poloidal drift component for the
specified neutral internal state, $\mathbf{v}^0_E$ is its assigned ideal E×B
drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit
vector along the specified positive local poloidal direction. The
superscript $0$ labels the neutral population, and the subscript
$\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal projection. The definition requires a
nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified internal state of one neutral
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over internal
states or species. It denotes an effective fluid-velocity contribution, not
a direct charged-particle guiding-center drift of electrically neutral
particles. Other contributions to neutral motion are excluded. It is a
linear velocity component, not a poloidal angle or angular velocity.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the assigned ideal E×B drift, the poloidal
projection need not vanish: the local poloidal direction is not generally
aligned with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the assigned E×B velocity has a component
along the specified positive local poloidal direction
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Poloidal neutral momentum flux is linear momentum transported per unit area
and time in the local poloidal direction by the represented neutral
population.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral momentum flux is the local rate per unit area at which a
represented neutral population transports linear [momentum](name:momentum)
in the poloidal direction. The poloidal qualifier specifies the transport
direction, not an additional choice of transported momentum component.

As a directional component of [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux), it satisfies:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is this poloidal flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$
is the neutral flux vector for the transported momentum component under
consideration, and $\hat{\boldsymbol e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local poloidal
unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$. The subscripts $0$
and $\mathrm{p}$ identify the neutral population and poloidal direction,
respectively. The tangent lies along a magnetic-flux-surface contour in a
constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

For a represented neutral species, contributions from its internal states
are summed; the [poloidal neutral-state momentum
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux) instead retains resolution
of a specified neutral state. Charged-particle contributions are excluded.
The flux includes convective and thermal-pressure contributions and is not
restricted to diffusive transport.

Unlike the [poloidal neutral particle
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), which counts transported
particles, this quantity accounts for transported momentum. It is a local
directional projection, not a surface-integrated transport rate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the momentum-flux vector has a component
toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Poloidal neutral particle flux is the net particle crossing rate per unit
area normal to the poloidal direction for one neutral species, summed over
internal states.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral particle flux is the local signed number flow of one
neutral atomic or molecular species around the magnetic axis, divided by the
actual area perpendicular to the local poloidal direction. Crossings in
opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

The poloidal projection is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal neutral particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is the neutral particle number-flux vector summed
over internal states, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local unit
vector in the positive poloidal direction. This direction lies in a
constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and sums over all its internal
states, rather than selecting the state represented by [poloidal neutral
internal-state particle
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux). The
state-resolved contributions sum to this quantity. It is a local net flux
per unit area, not an area-integrated arrival rate or an incident-only flux.

This quantity specializes [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) to an oriented surface whose normal is the
local poloidal direction. The poloidal direction is geometric and must not
be identified with the magnetic-field direction used for [parallel neutral
particle flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral particles travel clockwise around the
magnetic axis in a poloidal plane viewed with the toroidal symmetry axis to
the left and increasing $Z$ upward.

NAMES.name: power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short:
Signed local rate of collisional energy exchange per unit volume for a
specified plasma population, species, charge state, or internal state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb
collisions for a designated target population. It is positive for energy
deposited in the target and negative for energy transferred from it.

$$
P_a^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_a^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the target power density in W m$^{-3}$,
$Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate
per unit volume from partner population $b$ to target $a$, and the sum
includes the collision partners and subpopulations specified by the
quantity's aggregation scope.

The target may be a broad population, as in particle collisional power
density, or a species, ion charge state, internal state, or electron
population. Aggregated electron and ion quantities include the designated
contributing species and states, whereas resolved quantities retain only
their specified target, as in [ion charge-state collisional power
density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and
internal-state collisional power density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the designated target population gains energy
from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for a
designated electron population, positive for net energy gain.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb
collisions for a designated electron target population. It represents energy
deposited in or removed from that target, excluding noncollisional
energy-transfer mechanisms.

The collisional power density is defined by

$$
P_a^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_a^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the net collisional power density for
electron target population $a$, $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate from partner population $b$ to
target $a$, and the superscript $\mathrm{coll}$ denotes the
Coulomb-collisional contribution.

The target $a$ is an electron population, and the sum over $b$ includes the
collision partners and subpopulations established by the quantity's
aggregation scope. This is an electron-target contribution rather than an
unrestricted sum of collisional energy exchange for all plasma populations;
noncollisional transfer mechanisms are excluded.

It is the electron-target specialization of [power density due to
collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions). The accepted [thermal
electron collisional power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) is a more
specific instance with the bulk thermal electron population as target and
fast particle populations as partners, whereas [thermal ion collisional
power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) has
an ion target and is not included in this electron quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the designated electron target population
gains energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for ions
in a specified charge state, positive for net energy gain and negative for
net energy loss.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state collisional power density is the net local volumetric
energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for ions in a specified charge
state. It includes the contributing thermal and fast ion populations
represented by that charge state.

$$
P_{i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{i,z\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional power density for ion
population $i$ in charge state $z$, and $Q_{i,z\leftarrow
b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the rate of collisional energy transfer from partner
population $b$ to that target. The sum covers the collision partners
included by the aggregation scope. This is the charge-state-resolved
specialization of [power density due to
collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions); unlike [fast-ion
charge-state collisional power
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), it is
not restricted to fast ions.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the specified ion charge state gains energy
from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for the
aggregate ion population, including thermal and fast ions.
NAMES.long:
Ion collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange
caused by Coulomb collisions for the aggregate ion population. It combines
energy exchange for the included thermal and fast ion subpopulations.

$$
P_{\mathrm{ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the aggregate ion power density,
$\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included ion target populations, and
$Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate
to target population $a$ from partner population $b$. The aggregation
includes the contributing ion species, charge states, and orbit classes.
This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [power density due to
collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions); its thermal and fast
components are represented by [thermal ion power density due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [fast ion
power density due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the aggregate ion population gains energy
from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume to
a specified fast-ion species, summed over all ionic charge states without an
orbit-class restriction.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion collisional power density is the signed local rate at which Coulomb
collisions transfer kinetic energy to the nonthermal population of a
specified ion species. It is an energy source or sink for the receiving fast
ions, not their stored kinetic-energy density or the collisional heating
delivered to bulk thermal ions.

The defining kinetic-energy moment is

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_q \sum_b \int \frac{1}{2}m_i |\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{iq,b}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{fast}},f_b](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-ion collisional
power density, $i$ identifies the receiving ion species, $q$ labels its
ionic charge states, $b$ labels the designated collision partners,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $m_i$ is
the receiving ion mass. The function $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
fast-ion velocity distribution for charge state $q$, $f_b$ is the
collision-partner distribution, and $C_{iq,b}$ is the Coulomb collision
operator giving the collisional time derivative of the receiving
distribution due to that partner.

The receiving population is summed over all ionic charge states and includes
all guiding-center orbit classes. Contributions from multiple distributions
representing the fast-ion population are additive. The partner sum includes
only the designated exchanges and reduces to one contribution when a single
distribution species supplies the collision partner. This quantity is
spatially local; neither a magnetic-flux-surface average nor a volume
integral is implied.

The [co-passing](name:co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and
[counter-passing](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions)
variants restrict the contributing particle distribution, whereas the
[trapped fast-ion
variant](name:trapped_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) restricts
the receiving population to trapped fast ions. The related [fast-ion
charge-state collisional power
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
resolves an ion collision-partner charge state; that partner resolution is
distinct from summing the receiving species over charge states here.

This quantity supplies a fast-population contribution to [ion collisional
power density](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). Summing the
fast-ion contributions over the included ion species and adding the
corresponding thermal-ion contributions gives the aggregate ion collisional
power density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the
kinetic-energy density of the receiving fast-ion population.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Local Coulomb-collisional power transferred from co-passing fast particles
to fast ions of a specified species per unit volume, summed over all ionic
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing fast-ion collisional power density is the local rate at which
Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from co-passing fast particles to
the fast-ion population of a specified ion species. The co-passing
designation identifies the donor particles' passing orbit class; it does not
restrict the receiving ions to that orbit class.

The power density is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision
operator acting on the receiving fast ions:

$$
P_{i\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{q\in Q_i} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{1}{2}m_{iq}v^2 C_{iq\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}[f_{iq},f_{f,\mathrm{co}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this power density;
$i$ identifies the receiving fast-ion species; $Q_i$ is the set of its ionic
charge states; $q$ identifies a charge state; $m_{iq}$ is the mass of ions
in that state; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is receiving-ion
velocity and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed; $f_{iq}$ is the distribution of
receiving fast ions in charge state $q$; $f_{f,\mathrm{co}}$ is the
distribution of co-passing donor fast particles; $C_{iq\leftarrow
f,\mathrm{co}}$ is the Coulomb collision operator giving the collisional
rate of change of the receiving distribution due to those donors; and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the receiving
ions' full velocity space.

The quantity is local and is summed over all charge states of the specified
receiving ion species, not averaged over charge states or summed over
different ion species. The co-passing restriction applies to the donor fast
particles; counter-passing and trapped donors are excluded. This is an
energy-transfer rate, not stored kinetic-energy density, and it excludes
energy deposited in thermal ions. The [co-passing fast-ion charge-state
collisional power
density](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
resolves a single receiving ionic charge state rather than summing over
charge states.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic
energy of the receiving fast-ion population.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated net power transferred to a plasma particle population
through Coulomb collisions, abstracting over all source and receiving
population combinations without prescribing which species serve as donor or
receiver.
NAMES.long:
Coulomb collisions mediate energy exchange between plasma populations —
electrons, thermal ions, fast particles, impurity ions, and neutrals —
converting differential kinetic energy into thermal energy of the receiving
species. This abstract parent captures the general concept of
volume-integrated collisional power transfer without specifying which
populations participate; every concrete child quantity carries explicit
population labels to identify the donor and receiver.

The volume-integrated collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm coll}$ is the local collisional power exchange density and the
integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

Concrete population-resolved instances of this quantity include
[ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which
covers the total ion population summed over all species and charge states,
and ion_state_power_due_to_collisions, which resolves this to a specified
ionization state. Source-resolved variants such as
[fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions),
[thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions),
and
[thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions)
additionally identify the donating population.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net energy is deposited into the specified
receiving population (net collisional heating); negative when the receiving
population loses energy to others (net collisional cooling).

NAMES.name: ion_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total ion
population, aggregating both thermal and fast ion sub-populations across all
ion species and charge states without prescribing the thermal or fast
character of the receiving ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the
complete ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with all
colliding plasma constituents. As a structural abstraction within the
collisional-power family, it aggregates thermal and fast ion receiving
populations across all ion species and charge states without resolving which
ion sub-population receives the energy.

The volume-integrated ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm ion,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm ion,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm ion,coll}$ is the local [ion power density due to
collisions](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) into the aggregate ion
receiving population and the integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

The receiving population is charge-state-summed for each ion species and
species-summed over the ion population. Collisional exchanges among ion
sub-populations contained in this aggregate cancel in the all-ion sum; the
retained value is the net transfer between the aggregate ion population and
populations outside that aggregate, including the complementary electron
power due to collisions. Population-resolved components include [fast ion
power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions), [thermal
ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions), and
the charge-state-resolved [ion-state power due to
collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions); [power due
to collisions](name:power_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding
population-abstract parent.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net
energy into the complete ion population.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total
fast-ion population by background ions, summed over all fast-ion species and
charge states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the
complete fast-ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with
background ions. It aggregates all fast-ion species and charge states
without resolving the receiving fast-ion subpopulation.

The volume-integrated fast-ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}} = \int_V Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}$ is the local collisional
power-exchange density into the aggregate fast-ion population, $\mathbf{r}$
is position, $dV$ is the differential volume element, and $V$ is the plasma
volume.

This quantity is the fast-ion component of [ion power due to
collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions). Its charge-state-resolved
counterpart is [fast ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), while
[thermal ion power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) describes transfer
into thermal ions. Internal exchanges among fast-ion species cancel in the
summed net value.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net
energy into the complete fast-ion population.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
NAMES.short:
Power carried by neutral-beam particles that traverse the plasma without
ionization or stopping and exit through the far plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
The neutral-beam shine-through power is the energy carried per unit time by
injected neutral particles that cross the plasma without ionization or
another stopping interaction and leave through the far plasma boundary. It
includes only the outgoing neutral energy that is not deposited in the
plasma.

The defining outward energy-flux integral is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{st}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{far}}} \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{E,n} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the shine-through power,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{E,n}$ is the energy-flux vector carried by the exiting
neutral particles, $A_{\mathrm{far}}$ is the far plasma-boundary surface,
and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is its outward unit normal. It is excluded from the
power absorbed by the plasma from a neutral beam injector.

NAMES.name: radial_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.short:
Signed major-radius component of plasma flow, equal to the
mass-density-weighted mean of that component over all constituent species.
NAMES.long:
The radial center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the
major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
It retains the mass-density weighting of the full barycentric velocity.

The defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},R} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},R}$ is the radial center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the full center-of-mass velocity vector, $s$
indexes constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density, and
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$
points toward increasing major radius $R$, measured from the toroidal
symmetry axis; $\phi$ is the toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The sum includes all species in the plasma mixture, not only ions. This is a
local mass-density-weighted mean, not a particle-number-weighted mean or an
unweighted sum of species velocities. The definition requires nonzero total
mass density.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its toroidal and
vertical components and is distinct from its speed. The major-radius
direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface or
perpendicular to the magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points away
from the toroidal symmetry axis, toward increasing $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_conductivity
NAMES.short:
Local electrical response coefficient relating a major-radius electric field
to the conductive current density it drives along the cylindrical
major-radius direction.
NAMES.long:
Radial conductivity is the major-radius–major-radius projection of the local
plasma electrical-conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the
radial direction points toward increasing $R$.

The defining tensor projection is

$$
\sigma_{RR} = \hat{R} \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\sigma_{RR}$ is radial conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the
[plasma electrical-conductivity
tensor](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity), and $\hat{R}$ is the unit
vector in the major-radius direction.

For an electric field directed solely along the major-radius direction, the
conductive response satisfies $j_R^{\mathrm{cond}} = \sigma_{RR} E_R$, where
$j_R^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the major-radius component of conductive current
density and $E_R$ is the major-radius electric-field component. For a
general electric field, off-diagonal tensor components can also contribute
to the major-radius current density.

This is a local plasma transport coefficient, not a spatial average or
integrated conductance. Its projection direction is geometric: it is not
defined by a minor-radius flux label, a flux-surface normal, or the
magnetic-field direction. In contrast, [parallel
conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity) projects the same electrical
response along the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
NAMES.short:
Radial current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
conventional-charge flux along the major-radius direction attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.
NAMES.long:
Radial current density due to anomalous transport is the signed major-radius
projection of the conventional electric-current contribution attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

The defining projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height, is

$$
j_R = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $j_R$ is the radial current density due to anomalous transport,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the [current-density vector due to anomalous
transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), and $\hat{R}$
is the unit vector toward increasing major radius.

This local plasma quantity represents the net conventional-charge flux
attributed to anomalous transport, not the [current
density](name:current_density) summed over all mechanisms. No spatial
averaging or integration is implied. The major-radius direction is not
generally normal to a magnetic flux surface or perpendicular to the magnetic
field.

Together with the
[toroidal](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) and
[vertical](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) current
densities due to anomalous transport, it specifies the cylindrical
components of the same anomalous-current vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional electric current attributed to

NAMES.name: radial_diamagnetic_current_density
NAMES.short:
Radial diamagnetic current density is the signed major-radius projection of
pressure-gradient-driven electric current in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Radial diamagnetic current density is the local major-radius projection of
the pressure-gradient-driven contribution to [current
density](name:current_density) in the edge plasma. It is a signed component
of the vector [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},R} = \hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},R}$ is the radial diamagnetic current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic current-density vector, and
$\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius measured
from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

This quantity includes the algebraic sum of diamagnetic contributions from
all included charge carriers, without species or charge-state resolution. It
excludes current contributions attributed to other mechanisms. The radial
direction is the cylindrical major-radius direction, not a
flux-surface-normal direction or the magnetic-field-perpendicular
projection.

The [diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) is the
magnitude of the same vector, whereas this component retains its directional
sign. The [parallel diamagnetic current
density](name:parallel_diamagnetic_current_density) instead projects that
vector onto the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic conventional current flows
toward increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_effective_electron_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient relating the radial diffusive flux of electron
particles to the radial gradient of electron number density in edge-plasma
transport.
NAMES.long:
Effective coefficient relating the radial diffusive flux of electron
particles to the radial gradient of electron number density is the scalar
Fickian closure coefficient for radial electron particle diffusion in the
edge plasma. It describes the diffusive, cross-field radial part of electron
particle transport.

The radial diffusive electron particle flux is related to the radial density
gradient by

$$
\Gamma_{e,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,r}^{\mathrm{eff}}\,\frac{\partial n_e}{\partial r}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive electron
particle flux, $D_{e,r}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is this effective radial electron
diffusivity, $n_e$ is the [electron number
density](name:electron_number_density), and $r$ is the radial transport
coordinate.

The scope is electron particles in the edge plasma and the radial component
of the diffusive particle-flux closure. It excludes the convective or
advective part of electron particle flux, particle sources and sinks,
parallel transport along the magnetic field, and the total electron particle
flux.

It is the radial member of the direction-dependent [effective electron
diffusivity](name:effective_electron_diffusivity). The broader [electron
diffusion coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient) denotes electron
particle diffusion without the radial effective-component restriction, while
the radial electron diffusion coefficient denotes the corresponding radial
coefficient when the effective-closure distinction is not made. With the
minus sign in the defining relation, a positive $D_{e,r}^{\mathrm{eff}}$
produces diffusive electron particle flux down the gradient of $n_e$; an
effective negative value represents an up-gradient flux contribution in the
same closure.

NAMES.name: radial_effective_ion_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian coefficient relating the radial diffusive flux of the
charge-state-summed ion population to its total particle-density gradient.
NAMES.long:
The radial effective ion diffusivity is the Fickian transport coefficient
for ion particle diffusion in the radial direction. It applies to the ion
population summed over all ionic charge states and is the radial component
of [effective ion diffusivity](name:effective_ion_diffusivity).

The defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,r}^{\mathrm{eff}}\,\frac{\partial n_i}{\partial r}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive ion-particle
flux, $D_{i,r}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is this effective diffusivity, $n_i$ is the
total ion particle number density, and $r$ is the radial coordinate. The
radial flux is positive away from the magnetic axis; consequently, a
positive diffusivity gives flux down the total-ion density gradient. This
quantity excludes convective, conductive, and source terms.

NAMES.name: radial_effective_neutral_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective neutral-particle diffusivity relating diffusive flux to the
neutral number-density gradient along R in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the effective Fickian diffusivity governing neutral-particle
diffusion along the cylindrical radial direction. It is the radial component
of [effective neutral diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_diffusivity),
rather than an aggregate over transport directions.

The radial diffusive flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{n,R}^{\mathrm{eff}}\frac{\partial n_n}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the neutral-particle diffusive flux
in the radial direction, $D_{n,R}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is this effective radial
diffusivity, $n_n$ is neutral-particle number density, and $R$ is major
radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The negative
sign specifies diffusion down the neutral-density gradient. The coefficient
applies to the diffusive contribution of the neutral density transport
equation; advective transport and particle source or sink terms are distinct
contributions.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Radial electron particle flux is the signed net electron-number transport
across magnetic flux surfaces per unit area normal to a surface. It includes
diffusive and convective contributions to electron-density transport.
NAMES.long:
Radial electron particle flux is the signed net transport of electron number
across magnetic flux surfaces, per unit area normal to a surface. It is the
flux-surface-normal component of [electron particle
flux](name:electron_particle_flux); crossings in opposite directions
contribute with opposite signs.

The flux-surface-normal component is defined by projection:

$$
\Gamma_{e,\rho} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_\rho
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\rho}$ is this flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the
electron particle-flux vector, $\hat{\mathbf n}_\rho$ is the unit normal to
a surface of constant $\rho$ oriented toward increasing $\rho$, and the
subscript $e$ identifies electrons. The flux coordinates
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ label magnetic surfaces and specify position on them,
with $\rho$ the radial flux label, $\theta$ the poloidal angle, and $\phi$
the toroidal angle.

The quantity applies to the electron population in plasma and includes both
diffusive and convective contributions. It is a local per-area particle
flux, not a surface-integrated rate, electron energy flux, or
electric-current density.

In the electron-density transport balance, this total flux contributes to
the evolution of [electron density](name:electron_density) through radial
transport; it is not itself a source or sink. Its convective contribution is
the product of electron density and [radial electron convection
velocity](name:radial_electron_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net electron particle flow crosses a
surface of constant $\rho$ toward increasing $\rho$.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed projection of the local electron-fluid bulk flow onto the
major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial electron velocity is the major-radius component of the local
electron-fluid bulk flow in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It describes mean
translational motion of electrons rather than their random thermal motion.

The component is defined by projection:

$$
u_{eR} = \mathbf{u}_e \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $u_{eR}$ is the radial electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the local
[electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{R}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing major radius.

The bulk flow is the mean over the electron velocity distribution at the
same location; it is not a mass-weighted mean over all plasma species. This
quantity is a signed component, not the magnitude of the electron bulk
velocity. The major-radius direction does not generally coincide with the
normal to a magnetic flux surface or with a direction perpendicular to the
magnetic field.

Like [toroidal electron velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity), it is a
directional projection of the same electron-fluid velocity vector, rather
than a separate flow contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electron bulk flow has a component toward
increasing major radius, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Radial flux limiter coefficient is a dimensionless factor that caps radial
momentum-flux density at its collisionless free-streaming bound without
reversing the flux direction.
NAMES.long:
Radial flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on radial momentum-flux density in
a transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving the
sign assigned to the radial flux component.

For the radial component, the direction-preserving limited flux is defined
by:

$$
F_R = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_R F_R^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_R$ is the limited radial momentum-flux density, $F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}$
is its unconstrained closure value, $F_R^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the collisionless
free-streaming bound, and $L_R$ is the radial component of the
[flux_limiter_coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient). Nonnegative $L_R$
values below unity impose a stricter cap relative to the free-streaming
bound.

This quantity is distinct from the
[poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which limits the poloidal component, while
[momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
denotes the component-independent momentum-flux limiter.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian coefficient relating major-radius-directed diffusive
particle flux to the opposing number-density gradient for ions of one
species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient characterizes particle
diffusion of one specified ion species and charge state along the
major-radius direction. It selects the radial-radial diagonal response in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the diffusive flux contribution driven by the major-radius density
gradient, the defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{s,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff},RR} = -D_{s,q,RR}\frac{\partial n_{s,q}}{\partial R}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is its ionic charge number,
$\Gamma_{s,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff},RR}$ is the radial diffusive particle flux
density contributed by this diagonal response, $D_{s,q,RR}$ is the radial
ion charge-state diffusion coefficient, and $n_{s,q}$ is that species'
number density in the specified charge state. The derivative is taken at
fixed toroidal angle and vertical height. The minus sign expresses
down-gradient transport for positive diffusivity.

The population includes thermal and nonthermal ions of the specified species
and charge state, without summing over charge states. This is a particle
transport coefficient, not an energy or momentum transport coefficient, and
it excludes convective contributions. The major-radius direction is not
generally normal to magnetic flux surfaces or perpendicular to the magnetic
field.

This is the radial-radial diagonal specialization of the [ion charge-state
diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient), not a
sum of directional coefficients. Off-diagonal diffusion-tensor couplings,
when present, provide additional radial flux contributions outside the
defining relation above. In contrast, the [ion diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient) applies to a
charge-state-summed ion population; its effective value is not obtained by
simply summing charge-state diffusion coefficients.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Major-radius component of the effective velocity coefficient relating
advective, non-diffusive momentum flux to the momentum density of ions in
one specified species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the major-radius component of the effective coefficient
describing advective, non-diffusive transport of [momentum](name:momentum)
carried by a specified ion species and charge state. It is a
transport-closure coefficient, not the bulk flow velocity of those ions.

For a selected momentum component, the convective closure is:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,R}^{\mathrm{mom}} g_s
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of the selected momentum
component along increasing major radius, $g_s$ is the corresponding local
momentum density, and $V_{s,R}^{\mathrm{mom}}$ is this effective convection
coefficient.

The coefficient applies to one specified ion species and charge state; it is
neither summed nor averaged over charge states. The closure term excludes
gradient-driven diffusive momentum flux, residual stress independent of
momentum density, and local momentum sources.

This quantity is the major-radius projection of the [ion charge-state
momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The major-radius
direction is not generally normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The [poloidal
ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
resolves a different directional component of the same transport
coefficient.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective convection is directed toward
increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective kinematic diffusion coefficient for redistribution of the
major-radius component of momentum carried by ions of one specified species
and charge state.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient governs diffusive redistribution of the major-radius
component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one specified
species and charge state. The major-radius direction is the direction of
increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local flow-gradient closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_s n_s D_{s,R}\,\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\nabla v_{s,R}
$$

where $s$ identifies the selected ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of its major-radius
momentum through an oriented surface, $m_s$ is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the
charge-state number density, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusion coefficient,
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the surface's unit normal, $\nabla$ is the
spatial-gradient operator, and $v_{s,R}$ is the major-radius component of
the charge-state mean flow velocity.

The radial qualifier selects the transported momentum component, not the
direction of the flux or velocity gradient. It therefore does not prescribe
flux-surface-normal or magnetic-field-perpendicular transport. The
coefficient is charge-state resolved, neither summed nor averaged over
charge states, and excludes convective momentum transport, residual stress,
and external momentum sources.

It is a component-resolved specialization of [effective ion-state momentum
diffusivity](name:effective_ion_state_momentum_diffusivity). The
corresponding [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
applies to the field-parallel momentum component instead.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Major-radius projection of the mean flow of ions of one specified species
and ionization charge state, directed toward or away from the toroidal
symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion charge-state velocity is the projection of the bulk [ion
charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity) onto the direction of
increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. It describes mean translational motion within one specified ion
species and ionization charge state.

The component is defined by the projected first velocity moment:

$$
u_{R,q}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf R}\cdot\mathbf u_q(\mathbf r)=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf R})f_q(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_q(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{R,q}$ is the radial bulk velocity, $\mathbf u_q$ is the
charge-state bulk velocity vector, $q$ is the ionic charge number, $\mathbf
r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_q$ is the velocity
distribution of the selected species and charge state. The integration
covers particle velocity space. Here $R$ is distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical position, and
$\hat{\mathbf R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing $R$.

The component is evaluated at the position of maximum major radius on each
magnetic flux surface; it is not a flux-surface average. It retains
charge-state resolution rather than combining charge states. The
corresponding [radial ion velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity) is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of the species, not their
sum.

This signed component is distinct from flow speed, random thermal motion,
and particle flux. The major-radius direction is not generally normal to a
magnetic flux surface, so this quantity is not a flux-surface-normal
velocity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the charge-state bulk flow projects toward
increasing major radius, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed major-radius projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic
fluid velocity for one ion charge state, distinct from individual
guiding-center motion and total radial flow.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
major-radius projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one
ion charge state. It represents a local fluid-moment contribution rather
than the guiding-center motion of individual ions and is not restricted to
the plasma edge.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,R} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,R}$ is the radial diamagnetic-drift velocity component,
$p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its
pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector,
$B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge,
and $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ points toward increasing major radius in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow; it is not the total radial velocity. Cylindrical radial
projection is distinct from flux-surface-normal projection and does not by
itself represent transport across magnetic flux surfaces. Although the
diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular to the magnetic field, its
cylindrical radial component need not vanish.

For a species-level velocity, the diamagnetic contribution is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, not their sum. The
[binormal ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the binormal
projection of that species-level mean, rather than the charge-state-resolved
cylindrical radial projection defined here.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic fluid velocity has a
component toward increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal
symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian diffusivity for total-ion particle transport, relating the
radial diffusive flux across magnetic surfaces to the opposing radial
gradient of charge-state-summed ion density.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion diffusion coefficient is the effective particle diffusivity for
total ions moving radially across nested magnetic flux surfaces. It
parameterizes Fickian radial mixing of charge-state-summed ion density.

For radial transport, the defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(r)} = -D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(r)}\nabla_r n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(r)}$ is the radial diffusive particle-flux
component, $D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(r)}$ is the radial effective diffusivity,
$\nabla_r n_i$ is the radial gradient of total ion number density, and $n_i$
is the ion density summed over all ionic charge states. The minus sign
specifies transport down the density gradient.

This is the radial member of the general [ion diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient) family. Neutral particles and
charge-state-resolved coefficients, such as the [radial ion charge-state
diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient),
are excluded.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical decay of
a specified ion species' ordered momentum along increasing distance from the
toroidal symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion momentum damping rate quantifies relaxation of the ordered radial
component of ion [momentum](name:momentum) through collisional friction and
neoclassical viscous stresses. It is a species-level bulk-flow damping
coefficient rather than a momentum-transport flux.

The radial direction is the direction of increasing major radius in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from
the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. In a local linear damping closure, its contribution to the radial
momentum balance is defined by:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{iR}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damping}} = -\nu_{iR} p_{iR}
$$

where $t$ is time, $p_{iR}$ is the radial bulk-flow momentum density of the
specified ion species, and $\nu_{iR}$ is this damping rate. The momentum
density is $p_{iR}=\rho_i v_{iR}$, where $\rho_i$ is the species mass
density and $v_{iR}$ is its bulk radial velocity.

The bulk velocity is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states
of the specified species, excluding neutral particles. The damping rate is
an effective coefficient for that aggregate flow, not a sum of charge-state
rates or rates for different ion species. It excludes diffusive and
convective momentum transport and does not identify the radial direction
with the magnetic-flux-surface normal. A nonnegative rate describes damping;
zero denotes no damping from this term.

This is the radial member of the directional coefficients represented by
[ion momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate). It differs from
[toroidal ion momentum damping
rate](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate) by acting on major-radius
flow rather than toroidal flow.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Diffusion coefficient relating the diffusive radial ion momentum flux to the
local radial ion momentum gradient, expressing down-gradient redistribution
within the total ion population summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion momentum diffusivity $D_{[3m\mathrm{rad}}^i$ is the effective
diffusion coefficient characterizing down-gradient redistribution of the
radial component of momentum across magnetic flux surfaces within the total
ion population summed over all charge states. It is the radial component of
the broader ion momentum diffusivity.

The flux-surface-integrated diffusive radial ion momentum flux is
represented by

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{mom},i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -V'\mathcal{M}_iD_{\mathrm{rad}}^i\left\langle \left|\nabla\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\right|^2 \right\rangle \frac{d v_{r,i}}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}}
$$

where $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{mom},i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux
of radial ion momentum through a flux surface, $V'$ is the derivative of
enclosed volume with respect to the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, $\mathcal{M}_i$ is the total ion mass density,
$v_{r,i}$ is the radial component of the mean ion fluid velocity, $\nabla$
is the spatial gradient, and angle brackets denote a flux-surface average.

The coefficient applies to the total ion population, with contributions
summed over ion species and all charge states. Here radial denotes the
flux-surface transport direction associated with increasing
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, not a cylindrical-$R$ projection; parallel and
poloidal momentum channels are distinct quantities. Unlike [ion-state
momentum diffusivity](name:ion_state_momentum_diffusivity), this quantity is
not resolved by charge state.

Replacing the radial momentum component with the poloidal component gives
the corresponding [poloidal ion momentum
diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity); both are directional
components of ion momentum diffusivity, while the minus sign expresses
down-gradient diffusive transport.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_flux_over_edge_region
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Radial ion momentum flux in the edge region is the signed transfer of a
specified ion species' major-radius-directed momentum per unit area and time
across a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion momentum flux in the edge region describes transport of the
major-radius component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified
ion species across a magnetic flux surface. It includes the total momentum
transport, rather than an isolated diffusive or convective contribution.

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,R} = \hat{R} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_i \cdot \hat{n}_{\mathrm{out}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,R}$ is this momentum flux, $i$ identifies the ion species,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_i$ is its total linear-momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{R}$ is
the unit vector toward increasing major radius, and $\hat{n}_{\mathrm{out}}$
is the outward unit normal to the magnetic flux surface. The major-radius
direction belongs to the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. The transported momentum projection and the surface-normal transport
direction are distinct; the surface normal need not coincide with $\hat{R}$.

The flux is summed over all ionic charge states of the specified species,
excluding neutral atoms, electrons, and other ion species. Its individual
charge-state contributions are [radial ion charge-state momentum
fluxes](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). The total tensor
includes convective momentum transport, pressure, and viscous or turbulent
stresses. This quantity is a flux per unit surface area, not momentum
density, a local momentum source, or an area-integrated momentum transfer
rate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net transport carries momentum directed
toward increasing major radius outward across the magnetic flux surface, or
equivalently carries momentum directed toward decreasing major radius
inward.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed local rate of ion linear-momentum transfer per unit volume in the
major-radius direction, summed over all ionic charge states of a specified
species.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion momentum source is the local rate of transfer of linear
[momentum](name:momentum) to a specified ion species per unit volume,
projected along the major-radius direction. It includes contributions summed
over all ionic charge states of that species.

The projection and charge-state aggregation are defined by:

$$
S_{i,R} = \mathbf{S}_i \cdot \hat{R} = \sum_q \mathbf{S}_{i,q} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $S_{i,R}$ is the radial source component, $\mathbf{S}_i$ is the [ion
momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source) vector for species $i$,
$\mathbf{S}_{i,q}$ is its contribution from ionic charge state $q$, and $q$
denotes the ionic charge number. The sum covers all ionic charge states of
species $i$. The unit vector $\hat{R}$ points toward increasing major radius
$R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is
the toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is species-specific rather than summed over different ion
species; it excludes electron and neutral-particle contributions. The
major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface.
This is a local source density, not momentum density or a [momentum
flux](name:momentum_flux) through a surface. The declared unit is
inconsistent with this volumetric momentum-transfer-rate definition.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the momentum transferred to the ion species
has a component toward increasing $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Radial ion particle flux is the net ion crossing rate per area normal to
increasing major radius for one specified species, summed over all ionic
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion particle flux is the signed net ion crossing rate per area
perpendicular to the major-radius direction for one specified species.
Crossings in opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the defining projection
is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,R} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,R}$ is the radial ion particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the ion number-flux vector, $i$ identifies the
selected ion species, and $\hat{R}$ points toward increasing major radius
$R$. The coordinate $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The flux includes thermal and nonthermal ions and is summed over all ionic
charge states of the selected species without charge weighting. It excludes
neutral particles and is not summed over ion species. It is a local
particle-number flux, not an electric-current flux or a surface-integrated
particle rate.

This quantity specializes [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux) by
fixing the oriented surface normal to $\hat{R}$. The [ion charge-state
particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) instead retains a
specified charge state. The major-radius direction generally differs from
the outward normal to a magnetic flux surface, so these two projections are
not interchangeable.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net ion flow is toward increasing major
radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Rate of transport of radial linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous
or turbulent-stress contributions, with radial defined along increasing
major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial momentum flux is the radial component of the linear-momentum flux
crossing an oriented surface in the plasma. It includes convective transport
together with isotropic pressure and viscous or turbulent stress
contributions projected onto the $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from
the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The radial projection of the momentum current through an oriented surface
is:

$$
\Gamma_{\Pi,R} = \hat{R}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\Pi,R}$ is this radial momentum flux, $\hat{R}$ is the radial
basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ is the tensor associated with [momentum
flux](name:momentum_flux), and $\hat{n}$ is the chosen unit normal of the
oriented surface. For a single plasma fluid, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ contains the
convective term $\rho\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}$, scalar-pressure term
$p\mathbf{I}$, and viscous or turbulent stress term $\boldsymbol{\pi}$,
where $\rho$ is mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ is bulk flow velocity, $p$ is
scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}$
is the viscous or turbulent stress tensor.

This name denotes the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ radial
projection of the momentum current, not a flux-surface-normal projection and
not a derivative with respect to a radial flux label. It is the radial
direction-resolved form of [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux), distinct
from other direction-resolved or population-resolved momentum-flux
quantities.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the momentum current through the oriented
surface has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
