NAMES.name: thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred from fast
non-Maxwellian particles to bulk thermal electrons across trapped and
passing orbit classes, with positive values indicating electron heating.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate into the
bulk thermal-electron population from fast non-Maxwellian particles. It is
the thermal-electron component of electron power due to collisions,
including the represented trapped and passing orbit classes.

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V p_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the volume-integrated power,
$p_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local
[thermal-electron collisional power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), $V$ is the
integration volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is position. The quantity includes
energy received by thermal electrons and excludes the corresponding
donor-side energy change represented by [fast-particle collisional
power](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions). Positive values denote
net heating of the bulk thermal-electron population.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_pressure_at_post_sawtooth_crash
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Pressure of thermal electrons at the post-sawtooth-crash locus is the
isotropic stress from random electron motion in the plasma edge and
scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of electron at post sawtooth crash

The pressure is defined by the isotropic second central velocity moment:

$$
p_e = \frac{m_e}{3}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_e|^2 f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_e$ is the thermal electron pressure, $m_e$ is the electron mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the mean velocity of
the thermal electron population, $f_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is its velocity
distribution whose integral equals the thermal-electron number density, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral extends over
velocity space for the thermal population only.

This quantity includes only thermal electrons, not a sum over plasma
species. It excludes fast and other nonthermal electron contributions, ion
pressure, and stress from directed bulk motion. It is an isotropic pressure
rather than a field-parallel or field-perpendicular tensor component.

It supplies the electron contribution to [thermal plasma
pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure), which also includes thermal-ion
contributions. At the same evaluation locus, [total electron
pressure](name:total_electron_pressure) is the additive combination of this
thermal contribution and any nonthermal electron pressure.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity for convective transport of thermal energy carried by a
specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective velocity associated with convective transport
of thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state. It characterizes
energy transport rather than the transport of particles alone.

$$
v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)} = \frac{q_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}}{w_{\mathrm{th}}^{(s)}}
$$

where $v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}$ is the effective energy-convection
velocity, $q_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}$ is the convective thermal-energy flux
associated with charge state $s$, and $w_{\mathrm{th}}^{(s)}$ is the
corresponding thermal-energy density. The ratio is an energy-transport
weighting and need not equal the [ion charge-state particle convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity). It is the
thermal effective specialization of [ion charge-state energy velocity due to
convection](name:ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection),
including the more specific [effective thermal ion charge-state energy
velocity due to
convection](name:effective_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection).

NAMES.name: effective_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective vector velocity for convective transport of thermal energy by ions
in one specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
The thermal ion charge-state energy convection velocity is the effective
vector advection velocity assigned to convective transport of thermal energy
by ions in one specified charge state. It represents the convective channel
rather than the full particle velocity or diffusive energy transport.

For the selected charge state, it is defined through the convective
thermal-energy flux:

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{th}}\,\mathbf{v}_{E,\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective thermal-energy flux,
$\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-energy transport density used in
the flux decomposition, and $\mathbf{v}_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the effective
convection velocity. No summation over ion charge states is implied. The
quantity excludes diffusive and conductive energy transport and need not
equal the mass-weighted [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity); its radial instance is represented
by the [radial effective thermal ion charge-state energy convection
velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each vector component points along its
positive basis direction—increasing $R$, increasing $\phi$, or increasing
$Z$—in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Thermal ion charge-state number density is the local abundance per physical
volume of one ion species in one charge state, excluding fast and
suprathermal ions.
NAMES.long:
Thermal ion charge-state number density is the local abundance per physical
volume of thermalized bulk ions of one selected species in one specified
positive charge state. It counts particles rather than weighting them by
charge, mass, or energy.

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the thermal population:

$$
n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal ion number density, $s$ labels
the ion species, $q$ is its positive ionic charge number, and the
superscript $\mathrm{th}$ identifies the thermal population. The function
$f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local thermal-ion velocity distribution,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element; the integral covers all velocity space.

No summation over species or charge states is implied. Neutral particles,
ions in other charge states, and fast or suprathermal ions are excluded. The
quantity is local, including spatial variation within a poloidal
cross-section, rather than a flux-surface or volume average.

For the same species and charge state, [ion charge-state
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) is the sum of this thermal
contribution and [fast ion charge-state
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density). Summing this thermal
contribution over all ion species and positive charge states gives the
[total thermal ion density](name:total_thermal_ion_density).

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the thermal
(Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the thermal
(Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state,
obtained by integrating the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange rate
density over the plasma volume.

It is defined as the volume integral of the local collisional
energy-exchange rate density for that thermal charge-state population:

$$
P_{\rm th}^{s,z} = \int_{V_{\rm p}} q_{\rm th,coll}^{s,z}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$ is the thermal ion charge-state collisional power,
$q_{\rm th,coll}^{s,z}$ is the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange
rate density for thermal ions of species $s$ and charge state $z$, $V_{\rm
p}$ is the plasma volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position.

Together with the [fast ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), it forms
the [total ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions) for the
same species and charge state through $P_{\rm coll}^{s,z}=P_{\rm
th}^{s,z}+P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}$. The aggregate [thermal ion power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) is recovered only
after summing over all thermal ion species and charge states, $P_{\rm
th}=\sum_s\sum_z P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$; summing only over charge states of one
species gives a species-resolved contribution rather than the all-species
thermal aggregate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the specified thermal ion charge state is a
net recipient of energy from Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per
plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state through
Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source associated
with Coulomb momentum transfer to a specified thermal ion charge state.
Orbit classes and directional components select particular contributions
without changing this common physical meaning.

For a selected angular-momentum direction, the torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a} = (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}$ is the torque density about direction $a$,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the rotation axis,
$\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to
the specified charge state, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the corresponding
unit vector. For toroidal angular momentum in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this relation reduces to $R f_\phi$.

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved realization of ion charge-state
torque density due to collisions; [co-passing thermal ion charge-state
torque density due to
collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is one orbit-resolved instance.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected angular-momentum transfer is in
the positive orientation of its stated axis; for toroidal angular momentum,
positive is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Co-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per plasma volume to a specified thermal ion charge state from
Coulomb collisions with co-passing particles.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state
from Coulomb collisions with the co-passing population.

With $\mathrm{co}$ denoting this collision channel, the local torque density
is defined by the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{co}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the
local plasma volume, and $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the collisional force
density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state by co-passing
particles. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over
ionization states. This is the co-passing contribution to [thermal ion
charge-state collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and differs from the corresponding [counter-passing
quantity](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by the collision-partner orbit class.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ points along the corresponding positive
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Counter-passing collisional torque density is the vector angular-momentum
transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge
state from Coulomb collisions with counter-passing particles.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a
specified charge state from Coulomb collisions with the counter-passing
population.

With $\mathrm{cp}$ denoting this collision channel, the local torque density
is defined by the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{cp}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the
local plasma volume, and $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the collisional force
density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state by counter-passing
particles. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over
ionization states. This is the counter-passing contribution to [thermal ion
charge-state collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and differs from the corresponding [co-passing
quantity](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by the collision-partner orbit class.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ points along the corresponding positive
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque vector transferred to thermal
ions in a selected charge state.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque vector transferred to thermal
ions in a selected charge state is the net vector angular-momentum transfer
received by that thermal-ion population through Coulomb collisions. It
retains all spatial components of the collisional torque rather than only a
single projection.

It is defined as the volume integral of the local Coulomb-collisional torque
density transferred to the selected charge-state population:

$$
\boldsymbol{T}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi} = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi}(\boldsymbol{x})\, dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{T}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi}$ is this torque vector,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi}$ is the local
Coulomb-collisional torque density transferred to thermal ions in charge
state $\chi$ of ion species $i$, $\boldsymbol{x}$ is position, $V$ is the
integrated plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

The scope is one thermal-ion species in one selected charge state within the
integrated plasma volume; as an extensive vector quantity, it is
volume-integrated and not averaged. It is charge-state-resolved, not summed
over charge states, and excludes electrons, neutrals, fast ions, external
momentum input, noncollisional electromagnetic torques, charge-exchange or
other atomic-process torques, transport-flux divergences, and wall or
boundary torques.

When resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height,
[`toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions`](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions)
is the $\phi$ projection of this vector. Only that toroidal projection
enters
[`total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions`](name:total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions);
the radial and vertical components of this vector are not included in that
scalar total. The charge-state-summed vector
[`thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions`](name:thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions)
is obtained by summing this vector over all charge states of the same
thermal-ion species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component resolved in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame points along $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or
$+\hat{Z}$, respectively; the toroidal projection is positive in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Number density of thermal ions in a selected species or species group,
summed over all positive charge states and excluding fast ions and neutral
particles.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ion

For a selected ion species, the charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \sum_{q\geq 1} n_{i,q,\mathrm{th}}
$$

where $i$ labels the selected ion species, $n_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is its
thermal ion number density, $q$ is the positive integer charge-state number,
and $n_{i,q,\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal ion charge-state number
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density) for species $i$ in
charge state $q$.

The sum includes all positive charge states and excludes neutral particles.
Both trapped and passing thermal ions are included, while fast, nonthermal
ions are excluded. No spatial averaging or uniformity on a magnetic flux
surface is implied.

For a specified species group, the individual species densities are added;
[total thermal ion density](name:total_thermal_ion_density) is the special
case summed over all ion species. This quantity is the thermal-population
contribution to [ion density](name:ion_density). The thermal contribution
and [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density) together recover ion density
when these two populations exhaust the selected ion population.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated internal energy of the thermal-ion ensemble over a
specified plasma region, excluding electron, fast-ion, and suprathermal
contributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the internal energy stored by the thermal-ion ensemble
within a specified plasma volume. It aggregates the included thermal-ion
populations and excludes electron energy and nonthermal ion populations,
including fast and suprathermal ions.

For an isotropic thermal-ion pressure, the volume-integrated energy is
defined by

$$
E_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \int_V u_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,dV = \frac{3}{2}\int_V p_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,dV
$$

where $E_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion energy, $V$ is the selected
plasma volume, $u_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion internal-energy
density, $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the total isotropic thermal-ion pressure,
and $dV$ is the physical volume element.

The integration region is part of the concrete specialization: it may be
restricted to the H-mode pedestal, as in [pedestal thermal ion
energy](name:pedestal_thermal_ion_energy), or encompass the complete
thermal-ion ensemble, as in [total thermal ion
energy](name:total_thermal_ion_energy). The quantity is an aggregate over
the included thermal-ion populations rather than a single-ion or
charge-state-resolved energy.

This is the thermal-ion component of [ion energy](name:ion_energy). It
differs from total ion energy by excluding fast and suprathermal ion
contributions, and it differs from electron energy by including only thermal
ions.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from fast or
non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions, summed over all ionic charge
states.
NAMES.long:
Thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed local rate at which
Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from a designated fast or
non-Maxwellian particle population to thermal ions. It is an energy source
or sink for the thermal recipient population, not its stored kinetic-energy
density.

The exchange is defined by the kinetic-energy moment of the recipient
collision operator:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i|\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{iq,d}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_d](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-ion collisional power
density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is recipient velocity,
$\mathcal{I}$ is the included set of thermal-ion species, $i$ labels an ion
species, $q$ is its ionic charge number, and $m_i$ is its particle mass. The
function $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal recipient distribution for
species $i$ and charge state $q$, $f_d$ is the designated donor
distribution, and $d$ labels the donor species. The operator $C_{iq,d}$
gives the collisional rate of change of the recipient distribution caused by
that donor; the integral covers recipient velocity space.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of each included
species, with the species set comprising either one species or several. The
[charge-state-resolved thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
supplies an individual species-and-charge-state contribution. Contributions
from multiple designated donor distributions add. The quantity is locally
defined and is not intrinsically flux-surface averaged; a flux-surface
average represents the corresponding average of this local exchange.

This is the thermal-recipient contribution to [ion collisional power
density](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), excluding energy
deposited into fast-ion or electron recipients. It includes all donor orbit
classes. Orbit-restricted quantities, such as [co-passing thermal-ion
collisional power
density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions),
select the corresponding donor orbits. Summing co-passing, counter-passing,
and trapped contributions for the same recipients recovers the unrestricted
exchange; applying the same flux-surface average preserves this
decomposition.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy
from the designated donor population to the thermal ions.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Local Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from co-passing nonthermal
particles to thermal ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the local signed rate of
kinetic-energy transfer from the co-passing part of a fast or non-Maxwellian
particle distribution to thermal ions of a specified species. The co-passing
restriction selects untrapped donor trajectories, not recipient-ion orbits.

By conservation of energy in pairwise Coulomb collisions, the recipient
power density is the negative of the corresponding donor kinetic-energy
moment:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) = -\sum_a\sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_a|\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{a,iq}\!\left[f_a^{\mathrm{co}},f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}\right](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the thermal-ion power density at
spatial position $\mathbf{x}$, $i$ identifies the recipient ion species, $q$
is its ionic charge number, and $a$ indexes species represented in the
donating distribution. The quantity $m_a$ is the donor particle mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is donor velocity, $f_a^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing donor
distribution, and $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal recipient
distribution for charge state $q$. The Coulomb collision operator $C_{a,iq}$
gives the collisional time derivative of the donor distribution due to that
recipient population; the integral covers all donor velocities.

The recipient contribution is summed over all ionic charge states of the
specified species, not over different recipient species. The thermal
qualifier identifies the recipient population, not the donors; energy
deposited in electrons or fast-ion recipients is excluded. This quantity
retains local spatial variation across a poloidal cross-section and includes
neither flux-surface averaging nor volume integration.

It is the co-passing donor contribution to [thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions); adding the
counter-passing and trapped donor contributions recovers that parent
quantity. Its flux-surface average equals the charge-state sum of the
[flux-surface-averaged co-passing thermal-ion charge-state
contributions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy
from the co-passing donor population to the specified thermal-ion
population.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional power transferred from
counter-passing nonthermal particles to thermal ions of a specified species,
summed over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed
volumetric rate of kinetic-energy transfer from counter-passing nonthermal
particles to thermal ions of a specified species, averaged over a magnetic
flux surface. Counter-passing particles follow passing guiding-center orbits
whose transit is opposite to the reference co-passing direction. This orbit
restriction selects the nonthermal source distribution, not the thermal-ion
recipient orbits.

For nonthermal source species $a$ and recipient ion species $i$, the
contribution is defined by the recipient kinetic-energy moment of the
Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iq,a}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{counter}}] \, d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the counter-passing
thermal-ion collisional power density, $q$ labels the recipient's ionic
charge states, $m_i$ is the recipient-ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is
recipient-ion velocity, and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed. The function
$f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion velocity distribution for charge
state $q$, and $f_a^{\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing portion of
the nonthermal source distribution. The operator $C_{iq,a}$ gives the
collisional time derivative of the recipient distribution due to that
source. The integral covers all recipient-ion velocities, and angle brackets
denote the magnetic-flux-surface average weighted by the volume element
between neighboring flux surfaces.

The charge-state sum includes all ionic charge states of the specified
recipient species, not all ion species. The recipients are thermal ions,
excluding fast-ion recipients; the quantity is their collisional energy
source or sink, not their stored energy. In contrast, [charge-state-resolved
thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
retains one specified ionic charge state.

This quantity is the counter-passing contribution to the flux-surface
average of [thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). Adding the
corresponding [co-passing
contribution](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and trapped contribution, with the same averaging convention, recovers that
orbit-summed average.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic
energy to the thermal-ion recipients from the counter-passing nonthermal
population.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total
thermal-ion population from a fast-particle distribution, summed over all
thermal ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the
complete thermal-ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with a
colliding fast-particle distribution. It aggregates all thermal ion species
and charge states without resolving the receiving ion species or charge
state.

The volume-integrated thermal-ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm th\,ion,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm th\,ion,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm th\,ion,coll}$ is the local collisional power density
transferred into the aggregate thermal-ion population and $V$ is the plasma
volume. The quantity is the thermal-ion counterpart of [fast ion power due
to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions) and is a
population-resolved component of [ion power due to
collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions). Charge-state-resolved
components include [thermal ion charge-state power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net
energy into the complete thermal-ion population.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume deposited in thermal ions
when fast particles undergo thermalization.
NAMES.long:
This torque-density vector is the angular-momentum source deposited in the
thermal-ion population by the thermalization of fast particles. It
represents only the momentum transfer associated with this process, rather
than the total torque acting on the ions.

The torque-density vector is defined from the thermal-ion angular-momentum
density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{th}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{thermalization}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the angular-momentum density of the
thermal-ion population, and $t$ is time.

Only transfer caused by fast-particle thermalization is included;
contributions from other momentum-transfer processes are excluded. The
toroidal projection is represented by the [toroidal thermal-ion torque
density due to
thermalization](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component of the torque points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: thermal_neutral_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Number density of neutral particles in the thermal population of a specified
atomic or molecular species, including all internal states but excluding
ions and nonthermal neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neutral

At a given position and time, the density is defined by

$$
n_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int f_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal neutral number density, $s$
labels the selected species, $0$ denotes zero electric charge, and the
superscript $\mathrm{th}$ identifies the thermal population. The function
$f_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is that population's velocity distribution summed
over internal states, and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity. The integral
covers all velocity space.

The quantity excludes ionized particles and fast or other nonthermal
neutrals. Different neutral species are not summed. The defining density is
local; spatial averaging, when applied, preserves these population
restrictions.

Summing the [thermal neutral internal-state
density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density) over a complete set of
internal states recovers this quantity. It is the thermal contribution to
[neutral species density](name:neutral_species_density) for the same species
and contributes to [neutral density](name:neutral_density) when species and
population contributions are combined.

NAMES.name: thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Pressure of thermal neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or
excitation state, arising from random translational motion rather than bulk
flow or suprathermal particles.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of thermal neutral particles of one species in a specified internal
quantum or excitation state is the isotropic mechanical stress from their
random translational motion. It is the thermal-population component of
[neutral internal-state pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure).

The pressure is defined by the central second velocity moment of the thermal
distribution:

$$
p_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}} = \frac{m_0}{3}\int |\mathbf{c}|^2 f_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{c})\,d^3c
$$

where $p_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the state-resolved thermal neutral
pressure, $m_0$ is the particle mass of the selected neutral species, $a$
labels its internal state, $\mathbf{c}$ is particle velocity relative to the
thermal population's mean flow, $f_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is its
number-density distribution in that relative velocity, and $d^3c$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles,
and the superscript $\mathrm{th}$ denotes the thermal population.

The quantity applies to the Maxwellian thermal population in one internal
state, with no sum over internal states or species. In the edge and
scrape-off-layer setting, it is evaluated locally at the outboard equatorial
midplane rather than averaged over a flux surface. It is the state-resolved
counterpart of [thermal neutral pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure).

Bulk-flow momentum flux and internal excitation energy are excluded: the
internal state selects the particles but does not contribute excitation
energy to their translational pressure. Unlike [total neutral internal-state
pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this quantity
excludes the nonthermal contribution described by [suprathermal neutral
internal-state pressure](name:suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure).

NAMES.name: thermal_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Pressure of a neutral species arising from random thermal motion about its
mean flow, excluding nonthermal particles and directed-flow stress.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of a neutral species is the isotropic part of its thermal kinetic
stress, arising from random translational motion about the mean flow. It is
one-third of the thermal pressure-tensor trace, rather than a selected
field-parallel or field-perpendicular component.

The defining central velocity moment is

$$
p_{0,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{m_0}{3}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_0|^2 f_0^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{0,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal neutral pressure, $m_0$ is the
neutral-particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_0$ is
the mean velocity of the thermal neutral population, $f_0^{\mathrm{th}}$ is
its velocity distribution normalized to its number density, and $d^3v$ is
the velocity-space volume element. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral
species. This trace definition does not require equal directional stresses.

The quantity applies to a specified neutral species, not a sum over
different neutral species. Thermal pressures are summed over all charge
states when multiple charge states are considered, rather than
density-weighted; for an exclusively neutral population, only the
zero-charge state contributes. Unlike [thermal neutral internal-state
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this species-level
quantity is not restricted to one specified internal state.

This is the thermal contribution to [total neutral
pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure). It excludes nonthermal
neutral-particle contributions and the momentum flux associated with mean
directed motion; subtracting the mean velocity in the defining moment
removes that directed-flow contribution.

NAMES.name: thermal_particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.short:
Local volumetric heating rate delivered to thermal particles when fast or
suprathermal particles lose kinetic energy through Coulomb thermalization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the thermal-particle component of particle power density
due to thermalization: the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer
kinetic energy from a fast or suprathermal population to the specified
thermal population.

$$
q_{\mathrm{th}}=\left.\frac{\partial u_{\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{Coulomb\ thermalization}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the transferred power density, in W m$^{-3}$, and
$u_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal population's kinetic-energy density. The
derivative includes only energy exchange attributable to collisional
relaxation toward thermal equilibrium; it excludes direct injection, wave
heating, radiation, and other non-thermalization sources. Positive values
represent net energy gain by the thermal population.

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of energy density within the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

NAMES.name: thermal_particle_power_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated net power transferred to the thermal particle population
as nonthermal particles lose energy and join the thermal background.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net rate of energy transfer to the thermal particle
population from the thermalization of nonthermal particles. It represents
the global contribution of this process to the thermal-particle energy
balance, rather than a local power density or particle source rate.

The volume-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{\rm th,therm} = \int_{\mathcal{V}} p_{\rm th,therm}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\rm th,therm}$ is the integrated power in W, $p_{\rm
th,therm}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local thermalization power density in W
m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume.

Positive values represent net energy gain by the thermal particle
population; negative values represent net transfer of energy from the
thermal population to a nonthermal population. The local counterpart is
[thermal particle power density due to
thermalization](name:thermal_particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization),
while particle-number transfer is represented separately by [total thermal
particle source rate](name:volume_integrated_particle_source_rate).

sources.leaf_definition: Power input to the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Volume integrated source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

NAMES.name: thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short:
Thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged net rate per
volume at which particles enter or leave the thermal population.
NAMES.long:
Thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at
which particles enter or leave the thermal population of a specified
species. It is the source term for thermal particle-number density,
aggregated over orbit classes.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_n^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{th}}-S_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{th}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_n^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal particle source rate,
$S_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local volumetric rate of addition
to the thermal population, $S_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local
volumetric rate of removal from it, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux surface
label, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity combines the included particle source and sink processes for
the specified species; it is neither summed over different species nor
integrated over the enclosed volume. Positive values indicate net addition
and negative values net removal. Thermalization of nonthermal particles can
contribute positively, while acceleration out of the thermal population can
contribute negatively, but the quantity is not restricted to thermalization.
It excludes changes confined to the nonthermal population and is distinct
from the full thermal-density time derivative, which also includes spatial
transport.

Its orbit-resolved decomposition is the sum of the [co-passing thermal
particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate),
[counter-passing thermal particle source
rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), and [trapped
thermal particle source rate](name:trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate).
Transfers between these thermal orbit classes cancel in the aggregate and do
not alone change the total thermal particle number.

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particle density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particle density due to the thermalization of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short:
Co-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the co-passing
orbit class. Positive values indicate net addition; negative values indicate
net removal.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the co-passing
orbit class. Co-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center
toroidal circulation is in the plasma-current direction.

The net source rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}} = \left\langle s_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{co,th}} - s_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{co,th}} \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the co-passing thermal particle
source rate, $s_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{co,th}}$ is the local rate of
thermal-particle addition, $s_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{co,th}}$ is the
local rate of thermal-particle removal, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes
averaging over a magnetic flux surface, and $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux
label of that surface.

The quantity applies only to the thermal population on co-passing, untrapped
passing orbits and is aggregated by flux-surface averaging. Positive values
represent a net source to this orbit class, while negative values represent
a net sink. It excludes trapped and counter-passing orbit populations and
describes particle-number transfer rather than energy or momentum transfer.

This is one orbit-class contribution to the broader [thermal particle source
rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), which aggregates source and sink
contributions over the thermal orbit populations. The [counter-passing
thermal particle source
rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) is the
corresponding orbit-class contribution for particles circulating opposite to
the plasma-current direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particle density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short:
Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the
counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles
whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current
direction.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the
counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles
whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current
direction.

The source contribution to the evolution of the counter-passing thermal
particle number density is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)=\left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{source}}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is this source rate,
$n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged number density
of counter-passing thermal particles, $\psi$ is the magnetic flux-surface
label, $t$ is time, and the source subscript denotes the explicit
particle-source contribution. Positive values represent net particle
addition, while negative values represent net particle removal.

This quantity applies only to the thermal population in the counter-passing
orbit class and is averaged over magnetic flux surfaces. It is not summed
over co-passing or trapped orbit classes and excludes nonthermal particle
populations. The corresponding [co-passing thermal particle source
rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) applies the same source
definition to the co-passing orbit class.

The broader [thermal particle source
rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate) aggregates the orbit-population
contributions, including this counter-passing component; this quantity
therefore represents only the counter-passing contribution rather than the
total thermal source.

NAMES.name: thermal_plasma_energy
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated stored thermal energy of the confined plasma, equal to 3/2
times the volume integral of the total thermal pressure; the thermal
component of total stored plasma energy excluding fast-particle and
electromagnetic-field contributions.
NAMES.long:
Thermal plasma energy $W_{th}$ is the internal kinetic energy of the thermal
electron and ion populations within the confined plasma. It excludes
fast-particle energy and electromagnetic-field energy.

For scalar isotropic thermal pressure, it is defined by

$$
W_{th} = \frac{3}{2} \int_V p_{th}\,dV
$$

where $p_{th}$ is the sum of the thermal electron and ion pressures and $V$
is the confined plasma volume. It is the thermal contribution to [plasma
energy](name:plasma_energy).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Thermal plasma energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the thermal pressure

NAMES.name: time_derivative_of_total_thermal_plasma_internal_energy
NAMES.short:
Temporal rate of change of the plasma’s total thermal internal energy,
representing net thermal power deposited into or removed from the plasma.
NAMES.long:
The time derivative of total thermal plasma internal energy is the net
temporal rate at which the aggregate thermal energy of the plasma changes.
Positive accumulation denotes increasing thermal energy, while negative
accumulation denotes net thermal-energy loss.

$$
P_{\mathrm{net,th}}(t) = \frac{dU_{\mathrm{th,pl}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{net,th}}$ is the total thermal-energy change rate,
$U_{\mathrm{th,pl}}$ is the total thermal internal energy of the plasma, and
$t$ is time.

The underlying energy is integrated over the plasma volume and aggregated
over the included thermal plasma populations. It excludes
nonthermal-particle energy, bulk-flow kinetic energy, and
electromagnetic-field energy; it is not restricted to a single species or
energy-transfer channel.

This quantity is the time derivative of [total thermal plasma internal
energy](name:total_thermal_plasma_internal_energy). It is a global
thermal-energy balance quantity, distinct from [volume-integrated electron
power density](name:volume_integrated_electron_power_density), which is
restricted to the electron population, and from [power at inside flux
surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface), which is associated with a
specified enclosed region.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the total thermal plasma internal energy
increases with time.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Time derivative of the thermal plasma energy content

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions, density-weighted over
charge states and evaluated at the radial location of an internal transport
barrier.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the density-weighted mean bulk-flow velocity of all argon
ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport
barrier. Neutral argon is excluded, and the value is not a volume average
over the barrier or surrounding plasma.

For argon charge states indexed by $q$, the velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$ and
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow component along the toroidal
unit vector. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\phi$ increasing toroidally. The
charge-state aggregation is the same as for
[toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the argon-ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions at the magnetic
axis, combining all ionization states in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic axis is the local bulk-flow
component of argon ions projected onto the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It combines Ar+
through Ar18+ and excludes neutral argon; the magnetic axis is where the
gradient of poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ are toroidal
velocities in m.s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ is the local number density
in m$^{-3}$, and $(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})$ are the
magnetic-axis coordinates in m. The denominator corresponds to the
charge-state-summed [argon density at the magnetic
axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis); the species and locus semantics
parallel [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the charge-state-averaged argon-ion bulk flow
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, along
$+\hat{\phi}$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of beryllium ions at the
internal transport barrier, combining all beryllium ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal beryllium velocity at the internal transport barrier is the
bulk-flow component of the beryllium ion population evaluated at the radial
position of the barrier. It combines all beryllium ionization states and
excludes neutral beryllium.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{\sum_Z n_{\mathrm{Be},Z} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be},Z}}{\sum_Z n_{\mathrm{Be},Z}}
$$

where $Z$ is beryllium charge state, $n_{\mathrm{Be},Z}$ is its ion number
density, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be},Z}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow component.
It is the internal-transport-barrier counterpart of [toroidal beryllium
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal
beryllium velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the beryllium-ion flow is in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Toroidal beryllium-ion bulk velocity at the magnetic axis, density-weighted
over all beryllium ionization states in the right-handed (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal beryllium-ion bulk-flow velocity is the charge-state-aggregated
toroidal component of beryllium ion motion evaluated at the magnetic axis.
Neutral beryllium is excluded.

$$
V_{phi,\mathrm{Be}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}} V_{phi,\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

Here $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the density of beryllium ions
in charge state $z$ at the magnetic axis, and
$V_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is that charge state's toroidal
bulk-flow component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The
denominator is the [beryllium ion density at the magnetic
axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis), and the sum covers all
beryllium ionic charge states.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the beryllium-ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Toroidal carbon velocity at an internal transport barrier is the signed
toroidal component of the carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, evaluated on the barrier flux
surface. At species level it is the density-weighted mean over all carbon
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal carbon velocity at an internal transport barrier is the signed
toroidal component of the carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, evaluated on the flux surface
identified as the internal transport barrier. For the species-level carbon
quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all carbon ion charge states
present at that surface.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{C}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}\,v_{\phi,\mathrm{C}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes carbon ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}$ is the
local number density of carbon ions in charge state $q+$ at the
internal-transport-barrier flux surface, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{C}^{q+}}$ is
the corresponding toroidal fluid-velocity component.

This quantity is a local value on the internal-transport-barrier flux
surface, not a flux-surface average; a flux-surface-averaged quantity must
be named explicitly. It excludes poloidal and cylindrical-radial velocity
components, total speed, and charge-state-resolved carbon velocities. The
denominator of the aggregation is the [carbon density at the internal
transport barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), and
the same carbon toroidal velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis is
[toroidal carbon velocity at magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the carbon ion fluid velocity points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the
magnetic axis, combining all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The carbon impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis is projected
onto the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame. It represents the density-weighted mean flow of the carbon ion
population rather than a simple average of charge-state velocities.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{C},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C},q}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}}$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{C},q}$ are toroidal
velocities in m s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{C},q}$ is the number density in
m$^{-3}$, and $q$ indexes carbon ionization states. The quantity includes
all carbon ion charge states and excludes neutral carbon. Its boundary
counterpart is [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while the
corresponding magnetic-axis quantity for another impurity is [toroidal
nitrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}}$ points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.short:
Signed flow around the symmetry axis, equal to the mass-density-weighted
mean of the toroidal velocities of all constituent plasma species.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) around the
symmetry axis. It retains the mass-density weighting of the full barycentric
velocity.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance
from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height, the defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},\phi} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\phi} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},\phi}$ is the toroidal center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the full center-of-mass velocity vector, $s$
indexes constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density,
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector
directed toward increasing toroidal angle.

The sum includes all species in the plasma mixture, not only ions. This is a
local mass-density-weighted mean, not a particle-number-weighted mean or an
unweighted sum of species velocities. The definition requires nonzero total
mass density and a position away from the symmetry axis, where the toroidal
direction is defined.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its cylindrical radial
and vertical components. It is distinct from the vector's speed and from an
angular rotation rate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from
above the $+Z$ side.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal angular-momentum transfer density delivered to bulk thermal
electrons by collisions with co-passing particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the local collisional
angular-momentum transfer delivered to the bulk thermal electron population
by co-passing particles. It retains only the transfer along the geometric
toroidal direction.

The toroidal projection is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this toroidal torque
density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow
cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the full collisional torque-density vector
transferred to thermal electrons from co-passing particles. The unprojected
quantity is [co-passing thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
Non-toroidal components and transfers involving the counter-passing orbit
class are excluded; the latter are represented by [toroidal counter-passing
thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisional angular-momentum transfer to
thermal electrons points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: toroidal_conductivity
NAMES.short:
Electrical conductivity governing the toroidal conductive current response
to an electric field directed around the plasma symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal conductivity is the toroidal–toroidal projection of the local
electrical-conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the toroidal direction
follows increasing $\phi$.

The directional coefficient is defined by

$$
\sigma_{\phi\phi} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\sigma_{\phi\phi}$ is toroidal conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is
the local electrical-conductivity tensor, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal
unit vector. For an electric field directed entirely toroidally, the
toroidal conductive current density satisfies $j_\phi^{\mathrm{cond}} =
\sigma_{\phi\phi} E_\phi$, where $j_\phi^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the toroidal
current-density contribution driven by that field and $E_\phi$ is the
toroidal electric-field component.

This is a local response coefficient, with no toroidal or flux-surface
averaging implied. It is neither an angular coordinate nor a total
conductance. Cross-directional electrical responses and independently driven
current contributions are not included in this diagonal coefficient.

The [poloidal conductivity](name:poloidal_conductivity) describes the
corresponding response along the poloidal tangent. Unlike [parallel
conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity), which follows the local magnetic
field, toroidal conductivity follows a geometric direction and need not
equal the field-parallel coefficient.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_current_density
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density driven locally by counter-passing particles,
including direct charge transport and the collisional back-current carried
by electrons and thermal ions.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density attributed to counter-passing particles is the
local, signed toroidal projection of the net current driven by that orbit
class. It includes direct particle charge transport and the associated
collisional back-current carried by electrons and thermal ions.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{cp}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{cp}}
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{cp}}$ is the toroidal counter-passing current
density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the [counter-passing current-density
vector](name:counter_passing_current_density), and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$
is the toroidal unit vector. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, $R$ is the distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ points toward
increasing $\phi$.

Counter-passing particles occupy untrapped passing orbits circulating
opposite to the plasma-current direction. This quantity is evaluated locally
at a position in a poloidal cross-section, not averaged over a magnetic flux
surface. Its aggregation includes the direct current and the back-current
attributed to this population, rather than all contributions to plasma
[current density](name:current_density).

Unlike [toroidal counter-passing fast current
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density), which excludes
compensating return currents, this quantity retains the associated electron
and thermal-ion back-current. It is a signed component of the parent vector,
not its magnitude or its magnetic-field-parallel projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net conventional current attributed to
counter-passing particles flows toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per volume
from counter-passing fast particles to thermal ions of one specified charge
state through Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged torque per unit plasma volume
delivered to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state through
Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles. It represents
angular-momentum transfer associated with rotation about the symmetry axis.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{T}_\phi = \left\langle R F_{\phi,\mathrm{cp,coll}} \right\rangle
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_\phi$ is this averaged toroidal torque density, $R$ is
the major radius, and $F_{\phi,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the toroidal
collisional force density acting on the specified thermal ion charge state
through interactions with counter-passing fast particles. The labels
$\mathrm{cp}$ and $\mathrm{coll}$ identify the counter-passing contribution
and Coulomb collisions, respectively. Angle brackets denote flux-surface
averaging with differential-volume weighting. The toroidal direction is
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height.

The counter-passing restriction applies to the contributing fast-particle
distribution, not to the receiving thermal-ion orbits. The receiving
population is restricted to one specified ionic charge state; no sum over
charge states is taken. Unlike [toroidal counter-passing fast-ion
charge-state torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
this quantity describes transfer to thermal rather than fast ions.

It is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal specialization of [counter-passing
thermal ion charge-state torque density due to
collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
within the broader [torque-density](name:torque_density) family of
angular-momentum source densities. The average remains a torque density and
is not a volume-integrated torque.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net collisional transfer increases the
receiving thermal ions' angular momentum for rotation toward increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density due to anomalous transport quantifies the signed
conventional-charge flow around the symmetry axis arising from turbulent,
nonclassical plasma transport.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density due to anomalous transport is the signed toroidal
projection of the conventional electric-current contribution attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

The defining projection is

$$
j_\phi = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_\phi$ is this toroidal current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the [current density due to anomalous
transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The
right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R, \phi, Z)$, where $R$ is the distance
from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

This quantity denotes the local net conventional-charge flux attributed to
anomalous transport, not the total toroidal current density or a
particle-number flux. No spatial or flux-surface averaging is implied.

The [parallel current density due to anomalous
transport](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport)
projects the same vector onto the local magnetic-field direction instead;
the toroidal and parallel components need not coincide.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional electric current flows toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above
along the positive vertical axis.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_fast_ion
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density carried by nonthermal ions is their
flux-surface-averaged toroidal charge flux, excluding electron and
thermal-ion back-currents.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density due to fast ions is the signed electric-current
contribution carried by nonthermal ions in the toroidal direction, averaged
over a magnetic flux surface. The projection uses the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry
axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining charge-weighted velocity moment is:

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}} = \left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right\rangle = \left\langle \sum_a q_a \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\phi})f_a\,d^3v\right\rangle
$$

Here $j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}}$ is this averaged toroidal component,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [fast-ion current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_fast_ion), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The index $a$ labels included
fast-ion populations, $q_a$ is their ionic charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_a$ is their phase-space number-density distribution, and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space volume element. Angle brackets denote a
magnetic-flux-surface average.

All represented fast-ion populations are included, with multiple
distributions for the same species superposed. The aggregate is not
restricted to one orbit class; [toroidal trapped fast current
density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density) is its trapped-orbit
contribution, rather than an equivalent quantity.

Compensating electron and thermal-ion back-currents are excluded.
Consequently, this population-restricted, flux-surface-averaged projection
does not represent the full toroidal component of [current
density](name:current_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the flux-surface-averaged conventional
current carried by fast ions flows toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density due to heat viscosity is the signed charge flux
around the symmetry axis generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a
collisional magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density due to heat viscosity is the geometric-toroidal
component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity
stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame
is

$$
j_\phi = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_\phi$ is the toroidal current density due to heat viscosity,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the
unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$. Here $R$ is the major
radius measured from the symmetry axis, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This is a local, unaveraged contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density), not a surface-integrated current or the
total current density from all mechanisms. Only the heat-viscosity
contribution is included; the definition imposes no restriction to a
particular plasma region.

Unlike [parallel current density due to heat
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), which
projects the same parent vector along the local magnetic field, this
quantity projects onto the geometric toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the heat-viscosity current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the signed
electric-charge flux contribution along the toroidal direction arising from
momentum exchange between ions and neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the toroidal
projection of the [current density due to ion–neutral
friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). It represents
the electric-current contribution attributable to frictional momentum
exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles.

The component is defined by

$$
j_\phi = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_\phi$ is this toroidal current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion–neutral-friction current-density
vector, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector. The direction is
defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
the distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$
is the vertical height.

This is a local contribution in a partially ionized plasma, without spatial
averaging or integration. It excludes contributions assigned to other
mechanisms and does not represent the total plasma [current
density](name:current_density). The [radial current density due to
ion–neutral
friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) is a
different projection of the same mechanism-resolved vector, rather than an
additional mechanism.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion–neutral-friction contribution carries
conventional electric current in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$.
