NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium
fuel species evaluated at the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the bulk velocity assigned to
deuterium–tritium fuel treated as one effective species at the radial
location of the internal transport barrier. It describes collective fuel
motion rather than the velocity of an individual isotope or charge state.

The component is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{DT}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the effective deuterium–tritium bulk
velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [toroidal deuterium velocity at
the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
this quantity represents the effective deuterium–tritium fuel species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $V_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}}$ points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium
fuel species evaluated at the magnetic axis.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of
deuterium–tritium fuel treated as an effective single species at the
magnetic axis, the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux
surfaces. It represents collective fuel motion rather than speed or an
isotope-specific velocity.

The effective velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,DT} = \frac{\rho_D v_{\phi,D} + \rho_T v_{\phi,T}}{\rho_D + \rho_T}
$$

where $\rho_D$ and $\rho_T$ are the deuterium and tritium mass densities,
and $v_{\phi,D}$ and $v_{\phi,T}$ are their toroidal bulk-flow velocities in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The isotope-specific
[toroidal tritium velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) is therefore not
identical to this effective-species value. The quantity excludes poloidal
and radial velocity components and differs from the corresponding fuel
velocity at the [internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the effective deuterium–tritium bulk velocity
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Signed deuterium-ion fluid velocity along the geometric toroidal direction,
evaluated at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The deuterium-ion toroidal velocity is the projection of the deuterium-ion
fluid velocity onto the geometric toroidal direction at the flux-surface
radius assigned to the internal transport barrier. Neutral deuterium is
excluded. It is the deuterium-specific counterpart of the [toroidal hydrogen
velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the defining
projection is

$$
v_{D,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_D \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_D$ is the deuterium-ion fluid velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is
the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and
$v_{D,\phi}$ is evaluated at the internal-transport-barrier location.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the deuterium-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of deuterium ion bulk velocity at the magnetic axis,
density-weighted over all deuterium ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The deuterium ion velocity at the magnetic axis is the density-weighted mean
flow component along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It describes ion motion at the magnetic-axis location
and excludes neutral deuterium.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{D}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})=\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{D},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{D},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{D},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included deuterium ion charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{D},q}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$,
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{D},q}$ is its toroidal velocity component in m s$^{-1}$,
and $(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})$ are the major-radius and
vertical coordinates of the magnetic axis. The charge-state weighting
distinguishes this species quantity from the all-ion [toroidal ion
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), while the magnetic-axis locus
distinguishes it from [toroidal deuterium velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the deuterium ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, namely $+\hat{\phi}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: toroidal_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed component of the local mean electron flow tangent to circles about
the symmetry axis, describing toroidal electron transport in the edge
plasma.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal electron velocity is the signed projection of the local
electron-fluid bulk flow onto the toroidal direction in the edge plasma.
This direction is tangent to circles about the symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{e,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_e \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{e,\phi}$ is the toroidal electron velocity, $\mathbf{v}_e$ is the
local [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the
unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle.

The underlying electron-fluid velocity is the particle-number-weighted first
moment of the local electron velocity distribution, rather than the
center-of-mass velocity of all plasma species. The toroidal component is a
local linear velocity, not an angular velocity, the full flow magnitude, or
a measure of random thermal motion; no spatial averaging is implied.

The [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity) projects the
same electron-fluid velocity along increasing major radius, rather than
around the symmetry axis.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the toroidal electron flow is directed toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque on
fast ions in a selected charge state, equal to the net angular momentum
transfer rate about the machine symmetry axis from background plasma
species.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal scalar component of the volume-integrated torque vector exerted
by Coulomb collisions on fast (suprathermal) ions in a single specified
charge state. It represents the net angular momentum transfer rate about the
machine toroidal symmetry axis from background plasma species to this
charge-state-resolved energetic ion population.

$$
\tau_\phi = \boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll}$ is the charge-state-resolved
fast-ion collisional torque vector
fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity covers only the suprathermal ion population in one charge
state; the thermal-ion charge-state analog is
[thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions),
the total charge-state collisional torque summed over all species is
[total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions),
and the fast-ion toroidal torque summed over all charge states is
[toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the collisional angular momentum transfer is
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the gyrocenter orbit angular frequency, equal to the
signed rate of gyrocenter advance in toroidal angle φ in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal gyrocenter frequency is the toroidal component of gyrocenter
orbit angular frequency in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. It describes the angular advance of a charged-particle
gyrocenter after averaging over its fast cyclotron gyration.

$$
\omega_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}} = \dot{\phi}_{\mathrm{gc}} = \frac{d\phi_{\mathrm{gc}}}{dt}
$$

where $\omega_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}}$ is the toroidal gyrocenter frequency,
$\phi_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is the gyrocenter toroidal angle, and $t$ is time.
Passing orbits contribute toroidal transit motion, whereas trapped orbits
can contribute toroidal precession. This component complements the [poloidal
gyrocenter frequency](name:poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency) and belongs to the
angular-frequency vector [gyrocenter_frequency](name:gyrocenter_frequency);
unlike [toroidal ion rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency), it describes individual
gyrocenter orbit motion rather than bulk species rotation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the radial location identified with the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The helium-3 ion velocity at the internal transport barrier is the
density-weighted mean fluid velocity of the helium-3 ion charge states,
excluding neutral helium-3. It is evaluated at the radial location assigned
to the internal transport barrier and is not a flux-surface average unless
separately specified.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component,
$\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion fluid velocity, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The corresponding species comparison at the same locus
is [toroidal deuterium velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
while evaluation at another characteristic location is given by [toroidal
helium-3 velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the helium-3 ion velocity has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of helium-3 ions evaluated at the
magnetic axis and projected along the direction of increasing toroidal
angle.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local bulk-flow component of the helium-3 ion
population at the magnetic axis, rather than the individual thermal speed or
the full velocity vector.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, its density-weighted
charge-state average is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,3\mathrm{He}}=\left[\frac{\sum_q n_{3\mathrm{He},q}\,\mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{He},q}}{\sum_q n_{3\mathrm{He},q}}\right]_{\mathrm{axis}}\!\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes helium-3 ionic charge states, $n_{3\mathrm{He},q}$ is the
corresponding ion number density, $\mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{He},q}$ is its fluid
velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle. Neutral helium-3 is excluded. The
species-specific quantity complements the all-ion [toroidal ion
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), while [toroidal helium-3 velocity at
pedestal top](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top) uses a
different radial locus.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the helium-3 ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of helium-4 ions, evaluated on the
flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal helium-4 velocity is the density-weighted bulk-flow component
of helium-4 ions, evaluated on the flux surface identified with the internal
transport barrier. It includes helium-4 ions across their ionization charge
states and excludes neutral helium-4.

$$
v_{\phi,4}=\frac{\sum_z n_{4,z}v_{\phi,4,z}}{\sum_z n_{4,z}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,4}$ is the charge-state-averaged helium-4 toroidal velocity,
$n_{4,z}$ is the helium-4 ion number density in charge state $z$, and
$v_{\phi,4,z}$ is that charge state's toroidal velocity in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The toroidal component is projected along
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ and is distinct from the
flux-surface-averaged quantity at the plasma boundary and from the analogous
[toroidal helium-3
velocity](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the helium-4 ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons (4He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions evaluated at the radial
location identified with the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion bulk flow projected onto the toroidal
direction at the radial location of the internal transport barrier. It
describes directed ion motion and excludes neutral-hydrogen motion.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity and
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity is evaluated on the
flux-surface radius assigned to the internal transport barrier and is the
hydrogen counterpart of
[toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the hydrogen-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal component of hydrogen-ion bulk velocity, averaged
over ionization states at the magnetic axis in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity component in the
toroidal direction at the magnetic axis. It includes the hydrogen ion
population across its ionization states and excludes neutral hydrogen.

At the magnetic axis, the charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}} V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes hydrogen ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and
$V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The
magnetic axis is the location where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic
flux vanishes. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The same hydrogen-ion quantity at other loci is given by [toroidal hydrogen
velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal hydrogen
velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
Species-specific counterparts include [toroidal deuterium velocity at the
magnetic axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and
[toroidal helium-3 velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the hydrogen-ion flow points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate is the signed coefficient
multiplying one ion species’ toroidal momentum, with negative values
describing proportional damping.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate is the coefficient of the
proportional source contribution treated implicitly in an ion species’
toroidal momentum equation. It is the toroidal specialization of [implicit
ion momentum source rate](name:implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate), rather
than a dimensional momentum source.

Its defining relation is:

$$
\left(\frac{\partial P_{i,\phi}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{imp}} = S_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{imp}} P_{i,\phi}
$$

where $P_{i,\phi}$ is the primary toroidal [momentum](name:momentum)
quantity for ion species $i$, $t$ is time, $S_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is
this source coefficient, and the label $\mathrm{imp}$ identifies the
implicitly treated source contribution. The toroidal direction is the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The coefficient applies to one specified ion species, with the primary
momentum summed over that species’ ionic charge states. It is neither summed
over all ion species nor explicitly charge-state resolved; the coefficient
itself is not a sum of charge-state coefficients.

Unlike a positive [momentum damping rate](name:momentum_damping_rate), this
signed coefficient can describe either proportional amplification or
damping. It excludes the additive source contribution independent of the
primary momentum and is not a volume-integrated torque such as [toroidal
explicit ion torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the implicit source contribution reinforces
the existing toroidal momentum; negative when it opposes that momentum and
damps its magnitude.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the momentum-convection velocity for ions of one
specified species and charge state, evaluated at the maximum-major-radius
point of each magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the velocity associated with
momentum convection for ions of one selected species and charge state. It is
a velocity component, not an angular rotation frequency.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the component
is the projection

$$
v_{s,q,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_{s,q} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{s,q,\phi}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{v}_{s,q}$ is the
momentum-convection velocity vector for ion species $s$ and charge state
$q$, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies its charge state, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle.

The quantity is resolved for one ion species and one charge state and is
evaluated at the point of maximum major radius on each magnetic flux
surface, not as a surface average. It is not summed over charge states; the
species-level [toroidal ion momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity) is the
density-weighted mean over all charge states. This scalar is the toroidal
component of the [ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) vector and is
distinct from its [radial
component](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), which
is along $\hat{R}$. It is a linear velocity component, distinct from the
[toroidal ion charge-state rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency), an angular
rate.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical decay of
ordered toroidal flow momentum carried by ions of one specified species and
charge state.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate quantifies relaxation of
the toroidal component of ordered [momentum](name:momentum) through
collisional friction and neoclassical viscous stresses. It applies to ions
of one specified species and charge state. The toroidal direction follows
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local linear relaxation closure, the damping contribution to the
momentum balance is:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial \delta g_{s,\phi}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{s,\phi}\,\delta g_{s,\phi}
$$

where $\nu_{s,\phi}$ is this damping rate, $\delta g_{s,\phi}$ is the
departure of the ordered toroidal momentum density from its relaxation
equilibrium, $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, and $t$ is
time. The restriction labeled $\mathrm{damp}$ isolates the damping
contribution rather than the complete momentum balance. For damping, the
coefficient is nonnegative regardless of the direction of the momentum
departure.

This coefficient is charge-state resolved, not summed or averaged over
charge states, and is distinct from the species-level [toroidal ion momentum
damping rate](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate). It excludes momentum
diffusion, convection, and external momentum injection. Momentum transferred
out of this charge state need not represent a loss of total plasma momentum.

It is the toroidal directional entry of the [ion charge-state momentum
damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), whereas the
[poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping
rate](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) governs
relaxation of the poloidal momentum component.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective kinematic coefficient relating diffusive transport of toroidal
momentum in a specified ion species and charge state to its opposing
momentum-density gradient.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective kinematic coefficient governing diffusive
redistribution of toroidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one
specified species and charge state. Toroidal denotes the direction of
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

In a local directional Fick-law closure, the coefficient is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{s,\phi}\frac{\partial g_{s,\phi}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $s$ identifies the specified ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of toroidal momentum
along the selected transport direction, $\chi_{s,\phi}$ is this diffusivity,
$g_{s,\phi}$ is the toroidal momentum density, and $\ell$ is physical
distance increasing along that transport direction. The momentum density is
$g_{s,\phi}=m_s n_s v_{s,\phi}$, where $m_s$ is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the
charge-state number density, and $v_{s,\phi}$ is the charge-state mean
toroidal velocity.

This is the toroidal-momentum component of [ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). The toroidal
qualifier selects the transported momentum component, not the direction of
its flux or gradient; it does not require transport along a toroidal arc.
The coefficient is resolved for one charge state, without summation or
averaging over charge states. It excludes the advective contribution
represented by [toroidal ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity),
residual stress, and external momentum sources.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid
velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, distinct from
individual guiding-center motion.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather
than the guiding-center motion of individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\phi} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,\phi}$ is the toroidal diamagnetic-drift velocity
component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla
p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field
vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle
charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal
angle. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is
distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow. Although the diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular to the
magnetic field, its geometric toroidal component need not vanish.

The species-level [ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted
mean over all ionic charge states of that species. Its toroidal projection
is therefore the density-weighted mean of the corresponding charge-state
toroidal components, not their sum.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified
ion charge state has a component toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective inverse relaxation time for dissipative decay of the toroidal
bulk-flow momentum of a specified ion species, aggregated over its ionic
charge states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion momentum damping rate quantifies dissipative relaxation of
ordered toroidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion
species on magnetic flux surfaces. The toroidal direction follows increasing
toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a linear flow-damping closure, the damping contribution to the momentum
balance is:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{i,\phi}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{i,\phi}p_{i,\phi}
$$

where $\nu_{i,\phi}$ is this damping rate, $p_{i,\phi}$ is the toroidal
bulk-flow momentum density summed over the species' ionic charge states, $t$
is time, and the index $i$ identifies the ion species. The restricted
derivative includes only the damping contribution. A constant positive rate
produces exponential decay under this term alone.

The coefficient applies to one ion species, not to the combined momentum of
all plasma species. Its underlying bulk velocity is the density-weighted
mean over all ionic charge states, excluding neutral particles; the rate is
an effective coefficient for that aggregate flow, not a sum of charge-state
damping rates. The [toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping
rate](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) instead applies
to a specified charge state.

This quantity is the toroidal flow-component coefficient of the [ion
momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate). It describes
relaxation rather than diffusive or convective transport of momentum between
flux surfaces, and it excludes imposed momentum sources. The effective
damping may include collisional, neoclassical, or anomalous contributions;
no single mechanism is prescribed.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Toroidal ion momentum flux is the area-averaged transport of toroidal linear
momentum across a magnetic flux surface for one ion species, summed over
ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal ion momentum flux describes transport of the toroidally directed
component of linear [momentum](name:momentum) across a magnetic flux
surface. Toroidal specifies the transported momentum component, not the
direction in which that momentum crosses the surface.

The surface-area-averaged flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\phi} = \frac{1}{A_\rho}\int_{S_\rho} \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathsf{T}_i\cdot\hat{n}_\rho\,dA
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\phi}$ is this toroidal ion momentum flux, $i$ identifies
the selected ion species, $S_\rho$ is the magnetic flux surface labeled by
the outward-increasing flux label $\rho$, $A_\rho$ is its total area, $dA$
is a surface-area element, and $\hat{n}_\rho$ is its outward unit normal.
The tensor $\mathsf{T}_i$ is the selected species' linear-momentum flux
tensor, summed over ionic charge states, with its first index denoting the
momentum component and its second the transport direction. The unit vector
$\hat{\phi}$ points along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The flux includes convective transport and pressure, viscous, or turbulent
stress contributions; it is not restricted to diffusive transport. It
applies to one ion species and excludes neutrals and other ion species.
Summing the corresponding [charge-state-resolved
fluxes](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) over all ionic charge
states gives this species-level flux. Summing over ion species gives the
toroidal component of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux).

This quantity is a flux per unit surface area, not a surface-integrated
transport rate. It transports linear momentum rather than angular momentum
and is distinct from the local angular-momentum source represented by
[toroidal ion torque density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net transport carries momentum directed
along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ outward, or oppositely directed
momentum inward.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed rate of toroidal linear-momentum transfer to the total ion population
per unit area, summed over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion momentum source is the signed rate of transfer of
toroidally directed linear momentum to the ion population per unit area. It
is the toroidal projection of the [ion momentum
source](name:ion_momentum_source) vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The projection and charge-state aggregation are defined by

$$
S_{i,\phi} = \mathbf{S}_i \cdot \hat{\phi} = \sum_z S_{i,z,\phi}
$$

where $S_{i,\phi}$ is this toroidal source, $\mathbf{S}_i$ is the ion
momentum-source vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing
toroidal angle, and $S_{i,z,\phi}$ is the toroidal source for ionic charge
state $z$. The index $i$ identifies the ion population, and the sum includes
all ionic charge states.

This is a charge-state-summed source, not a source for one selected charge
state; electrons and neutral particles are excluded from the receiving
population. It describes transfer of [linear momentum](name:momentum) to
ions, rather than [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) through a surface. Its
area-normalized linear-momentum transfer is also distinct from [ion torque
density](name:ion_torque_density), which describes angular-momentum transfer
per unit volume.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net linear momentum transferred to ions
points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed angular rate of an ion species’ bulk motion about the symmetry axis,
equal to toroidal flow velocity divided by local major radius and
density-weighted over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion rotation frequency is the signed angular rate of a
specified ion species’ bulk motion about the toroidal symmetry axis. It is
the toroidal rotation-rate component of [ion rotation
frequency](name:ion_rotation_frequency).

The defining relation is

$$
\Omega_{i\phi} = \frac{v_{i\phi}}{R} = \frac{\sum_q n_{iq}\Omega_{iq\phi}}{\sum_q n_{iq}}
$$

where $i$ labels the selected ion species, $q$ labels its ionic charge
states, $\Omega_{i\phi}$ is the species’ toroidal angular rotation rate,
$v_{i\phi}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow velocity, and $R$ is the local major
radius. The quantity $n_{iq}$ is the number density of charge state $q$, and
$\Omega_{iq\phi}$ is its [toroidal ion charge-state rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency). The toroidal
direction is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height.

This is a local quantity in a poloidal cross-section; no flux-surface
averaging or uniform rotation on a flux surface is implied. It is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of one species, not a sum
of their angular rates or an average over different ion species. With only
one populated charge state, it equals that charge state’s toroidal rotation
frequency. It describes collective bulk rotation rather than individual
gyrocenter transit or precession.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion species’ bulk toroidal flow is in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed projection of an ion species' bulk flow along the geometric toroidal
direction, using the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion velocity is the projection of the bulk [ion
velocity](name:ion_velocity) onto the direction of increasing toroidal angle
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It describes mean
directed motion rather than random thermal motion.

The projection, including charge-state averaging, is defined by

$$
v_{i\phi}=\mathbf{v}_i\cdot\hat{\phi}=\frac{\sum_q n_{iq}\,\mathbf{v}_{iq}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{iq}}
$$

where $v_{i\phi}$ is the toroidal ion velocity, $\mathbf{v}_i$ is the
charge-state-averaged ion bulk velocity, $i$ identifies the selected ion
species, $q$ labels its ionic charge states, $n_{iq}$ is the number density
of each charge state, and $\mathbf{v}_{iq}$ is its mean velocity vector. The
unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$; $R$
is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The sums include all ionic charge states of the selected species and exclude
neutrals. The result is a density-weighted mean, not a sum of charge-state
velocities or a combination of distinct ion species. Unlike [plasma
velocity](name:plasma_velocity), it does not represent the mass-weighted
flow of all plasma species. It is a linear velocity component, not a speed
magnitude or an angular rotation rate; no spatial averaging or fixed
evaluation locus is implied.

Dividing this component by the total magnetic-field magnitude gives the
[ratio of toroidal ion velocity to magnetic-field
magnitude](name:ratio_of_toroidal_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion bulk flow projects toward increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_toroidal_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude
NAMES.short:
Ratio of an ion species' local toroidal bulk velocity, density-weighted over
all ionic charge states, to the local total magnetic-field magnitude.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of the local toroidal component of an ion species' bulk velocity to
the magnitude of the local total magnetic field. It expresses signed
toroidal ion motion scaled by the inverse field magnitude.

For ion species $i$, the defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{V}_{i\phi} = \frac{v_{i\phi}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathcal{V}_{i\phi}$ is this ratio, $v_{i\phi}$ is the [toroidal ion
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local total
magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its
[magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude). The index $i$ identifies the ion
species.

For each ion species, $v_{i\phi}$ is the density-weighted mean over all its
ionic charge states, not a sum of charge-state velocities or an average
across species; neutral particles are excluded. The toroidal component is
along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
The numerator and denominator refer to the same local position, with no
spatial aggregation.

The denominator is the magnitude of the total magnetic field, not a signed
toroidal or poloidal component. Multiplying the ratio by this magnitude
recovers the toroidal ion velocity. The [parallel ion velocity
ratio](name:ratio_of_parallel_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude)
instead uses the component along the magnetic-field direction, while the
[radial ion velocity
ratio](name:ratio_of_radial_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude) uses
the major-radius component.

$$a/b$$
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion bulk-velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted iron-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing toroidal
angle, averaged over all ionization charge states at the internal transport
barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the bulk velocity of ionized iron
at the flux-surface locus of the internal transport barrier. It is a
density-weighted mean across iron ionization charge states in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal
angle.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the ionization charge number, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of iron ions in state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is that state's toroidal bulk-flow component in
m.s$^{-1}$. Neutral iron is excluded from the sum.

The internal-transport-barrier value is distinct from the corresponding
values at the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_magnetic_axis)
and [pedestal top](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top), which use
different flux-surface loci.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the iron-ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron at the magnetic
axis, directed along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the charge-state-aggregated toroidal bulk-flow velocity of
ionized iron evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the
number-density-weighted mean of the iron-ion fluid velocities, excluding
neutral iron.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}}(\mathrm{axis}) = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})\,v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})}
$$

Here $q$ indexes the included positive iron-ion charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity component in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; the velocity is in m s$^{-1}$
and the density is in m$^{-3}$. The weighting is over charge states, so this
is an intensive mean rather than a sum of velocities. It is the
magnetic-axis counterpart of [toroidal iron velocity at the internal
transport
barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
follows the same aggregation principle as [toroidal deuterium velocity at
the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the iron bulk flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of krypton ions, averaged over
charge states at the radial location of an internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the krypton-ion bulk flow
evaluated at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier.
It includes ionic krypton charge states and excludes neutral krypton.

$$
v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr}} = \\frac{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr},q}}{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ionization states, $n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}$ is the
number density of ions in state $q$, and $v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr},q}$ is their
toroidal bulk-flow component. The result is the density-weighted mean over
all included krypton ionization states, analogous to the corresponding
[toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal krypton
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

The toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\\phi, Z)$ frame, where $\\phi$ increases in the toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the krypton-ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the
krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis, defined as the
density-weighted mean over all krypton ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of
the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis is the
charge-state-aggregated krypton velocity projected along $\hat{\phi}$. Here
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and
the magnetic axis is the innermost closed-flux-surface locus where the
gradient of [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity at this locus is defined by
projecting the density-weighted krypton velocity onto the toroidal unit
vector:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr},0} =
\left.
\left(
\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}
\right)
\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ionization charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$
is the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$
is its bulk-flow velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle, and the subscript $0$ denotes evaluation at
the magnetic axis.

This is an intensive species velocity: krypton charge-state velocities are
combined as a density-weighted mean over all ionization states, not as a
sum. It is distinct from flux-surface-averaged toroidal krypton velocity at
the plasma boundary and from local toroidal krypton velocities at the
[internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
[pedestal top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the krypton velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Krypton (Kr)

NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal lithium velocity at an internal transport barrier
is the signed toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity,
evaluated at the barrier flux-surface location. It is the density-weighted
mean over Li+ through Li3+ and is positive along increasing toroidal angle φ
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Density-weighted toroidal lithium velocity at an internal transport barrier
is the signed toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity evaluated
at the flux-surface location of that barrier. It is an intensive
species-level velocity, formed as the density-weighted mean over the lithium
ion charge states Li$^{+}$ through Li$^{3+}$.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{ITB}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the density-weighted toroidal
lithium velocity at the internal transport barrier,
$n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the number density of lithium
charge state $q+$ at that location,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the fluid velocity of that
charge state at that location, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Neutral lithium atoms are excluded from the aggregation. The value is not a
flux-surface average unless explicitly identified as such by a separate
quantity, and it is undefined where the summed lithium ion density in the
denominator is zero.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted lithium ion velocity has
a positive projection on $\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal fluid velocity of lithium impurity ions at the
magnetic axis, taken as the density-weighted mean over lithium ion charge
states Li+, Li2+, and Li3+. Neutral lithium is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Density-weighted toroidal fluid velocity of lithium impurity ions at the
magnetic axis is the local toroidal component of the lithium impurity-ion
fluid velocity at the magnetic axis. The magnetic axis is the innermost
flux-surface locus where the poloidal magnetic flux has an extremum. Because
this is an intensive species-level quantity, the charge-state aggregation is
the density-weighted mean over lithium ion charge states $\mathrm{Li}^{+}$,
$\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$, and $\mathrm{Li}^{3+}$; neutral lithium is excluded.

The density-weighted toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the lithium ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is
the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is
its fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height.

This is a local on-axis value, not a flux-surface average or a boundary
value. The analogous local lithium-ion quantities include
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted lithium-ion flow points
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: toroidal_mhd_mode_number
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless integer Fourier index specifying toroidal periodicity of a
magnetohydrodynamic perturbation, including the perturbation harmonic
associated with a particle-orbit integral.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal MHD mode number is a dimensionless integer Fourier index that
specifies periodic structure around the symmetry axis for a
magnetohydrodynamic perturbation. It identifies a toroidal angular harmonic
rather than a radial branch, harmonic amplitude, or spatial wavevector.

The toroidal harmonic dependence is defined by

$$
\delta F(\phi) = \widetilde{F}\exp(i n_\phi\phi)
$$

where $\delta F$ is a complex harmonic of a perturbed physical quantity,
$\widetilde{F}$ is its complex amplitude independent of toroidal angle, $i$
is the imaginary unit, and $n_\phi$ is the toroidal MHD mode number. The
toroidal angle $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from
the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height. Other coordinates and time are
held fixed in this expression.

Each value labels one harmonic, not a sum or average over modes. The
absolute value $|n_\phi|$ counts toroidal phase cycles per complete circuit;
$n_\phi=0$ denotes an axisymmetric perturbation. This definition applies to
linear MHD eigenmodes and tearing-mode perturbations. For an associated
particle [orbit integral](name:orbit_integral), it identifies the
perturbation harmonic considered, not an ordinal position in a list of modes
or the value of the integral.

This index is the toroidal component of the [MHD mode-number
vector](name:mhd_mode_number). Together with the [poloidal mode
number](name:poloidal_mode_number), it specifies the angular harmonic
structure and helicity of the perturbation.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of neon ions, averaged over ionic
charge states and evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport
barrier.
NAMES.long:
The neon-ion toroidal velocity is the density-weighted mean flow of all neon
ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport
barrier; neutral neon is excluded.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included neon ionic charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density, and
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is its flow-velocity component along the
geometric toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity is the toroidal counterpart of the
radial-location-specific
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis)
and uses the same charge-state aggregation convention as the analogous
[toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon ions at the
magnetic axis, averaged over all neon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the neon impurity-ion bulk
velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the density-weighted mean
over all neon ionization states and excludes neutral neon.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined
by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}}=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the charge-state-aggregated neon-ion
bulk velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle. The magnetic axis is the point
inside the confined plasma where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux
$\psi$ vanishes, $\nabla\psi=0$. The analogous quantity at the plasma
boundary is [toroidal neon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neon-ion bulk flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Toroidal flux-limiter coefficient that sets an edge-region, nonnegative cap
on the toroidal component of neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a
specified internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming
bound, without reversing the signed component.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles
occupying a specified internal state over the edge region is the directional
coefficient used to bound the toroidal component of the corresponding
neutral internal-state momentum-flux density. The internal state may be an
electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation state, and
the toroidal component is the projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},
\hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle
increasing counterclockwise when viewed from $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

For the toroidal direction, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\phi}| \le \alpha_{\phi}\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\phi}|,\qquad 0 \le \alpha_{\phi} \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\phi}$ is the limited toroidal component of the
neutral internal-state momentum flux over the edge region,
$\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\phi}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
toroidal component whose magnitude defines the bound, and $\alpha_{\phi}$ is
this toroidal limiter coefficient.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the
realized momentum flux. Because $\alpha_{\phi}$ is nonnegative, applying the
limiter may reduce or bound a signed toroidal momentum-flux component but
does not reverse its direction; a nonzero limited component retains the sign
of the underlying toroidal component. This scalar coefficient is the
toroidal member of the [neutral internal-state momentum-flux limiter
coefficient over the edge
region](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region),
is distinct from the [toroidal neutral internal-state momentum
flux](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and is in the
same directional family as the [parallel neutral internal-state
momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
and the [poloidal momentum neutral internal-state flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_momentum_neutral_internal_state_flux_limiter_coefficient).

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_torque_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the angular-momentum source density transferred to the
plasma by neutral particles in a specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the torque density transferred to
the plasma by neutral particles occupying a specified internal state. It is
the state-resolved toroidal projection of neutral internal-state torque
density, rather than a sum over all neutral internal states.

$$
\tau_{\phi,s}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\left(\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{f}_s\right)
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the
toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the machine symmetry axis,
and $\mathbf{f}_s$ is the force density exerted on the plasma by neutrals in
internal state $s$.

Summing this state-resolved quantity over all neutral internal states gives
[toroidal neutral torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density); it
is distinct from the direction-independent [neutral torque
density](name:neutral_torque_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the torque points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective toroidal fluid velocity of a neutral species occupying a specified
internal quantum state, retaining only the contribution attributed to
diamagnetic drift.
NAMES.long:
The effective neutral internal-state diamagnetic drift velocity is the
fluid-level velocity of a neutral species population occupying a defined
internal quantum state, restricted here to its toroidal component and
diamagnetic contribution. This component is derived from the parent
effective neutral internal-state diamagnetic drift velocity and is distinct
from the corresponding state-aggregated [toroidal neutral-state diamagnetic
drift
velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the effective neutral internal-state
diamagnetic drift velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal
unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Velocity due to the diamagnetic drift, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal projection of an effective E×B fluid drift assigned to one
neutral species in a specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state E×B drift
velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
is its signed projection along the geometric toroidal direction. This
direction follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the assigned ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v^0_{E,\phi} = \mathbf{v}^0_E \cdot \hat{\phi} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v^0_{E,\phi}$ is the effective toroidal drift component for the
specified neutral internal state, $\mathbf{v}^0_E$ is its assigned ideal E×B
drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic field, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward
increasing toroidal angle. The superscript $0$ labels the neutral
population. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified internal state of one neutral
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over internal
states or species. It denotes an effective fluid-velocity contribution, not
a direct charged-particle guiding-center drift of electrically neutral
particles. Other contributions to neutral motion are excluded. It is a
linear velocity component, not a toroidal angle or angular velocity.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the assigned ideal E×B drift, the toroidal
projection need not vanish: the geometric toroidal direction is not
generally aligned with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the assigned E×B velocity has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Toroidal neutral momentum convection velocity is the toroidal projection of
the effective velocity that convects aggregate neutral momentum. The
toroidal label denotes the velocity component along increasing toroidal
angle, not the component of momentum being transported or a particular
neutral particle flow.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral momentum convection velocity is the toroidal component of
the effective velocity vector that advects neutral momentum in a transport
closure for the aggregate neutral population. The toroidal component is the
projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height; toroidal modifies the velocity component, not the momentum
component being transported. It is a convection coefficient and need not
equal the toroidal neutral velocity.

The projection defining this component is

$$
u_{\phi,\mathrm{mom}} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is the [neutral momentum convection
velocity](name:neutral_momentum_convection_velocity), $\hat{\phi}$ is the
unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $u_{\phi,\mathrm{mom}}$
is this quantity.

The unqualified neutral population denotes an aggregate over neutral species
and internal states; resolved counterparts keep those populations separate.
This coefficient belongs to the convective part of the neutral momentum flux
and excludes diffusive, viscous, source, sink, and residual terms; it is not
the [toroidal neutral momentum flux](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux)
itself.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}}$ has a component
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Momentum effective convection, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Kinematic coefficient relating diffusive toroidal transport of a neutral
species' bulk momentum to its opposing toroidal momentum-density gradient.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral momentum diffusivity is the kinematic coefficient governing
diffusive transport of bulk neutral [momentum](name:momentum) along the
toroidal direction. It is the toroidal directional component of [neutral
momentum diffusivity](name:neutral_momentum_diffusivity). This direction
follows increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local, componentwise Fick-law closure:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{0,\phi}\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial \mathbf{g}_0}{\partial \phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of
neutral linear momentum across a surface normal to the toroidal direction,
$D_{0,\phi}$ is this diffusivity, and $\mathbf{g}_0$ is the bulk neutral
momentum density. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population. The
derivative is taken at fixed major radius and vertical height; the factor
$1/R$ converts differentiation with respect to toroidal angle into
differentiation along physical toroidal arc length.

The quantity applies to a specified neutral species with its internal states
combined, rather than to one resolved internal-state channel. Bulk momentum
density is summed over those states, but this effective coefficient is not
the sum of their diffusivities. The [toroidal neutral internal-state
momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
instead applies to a resolved state. Charged-particle contributions are
excluded from the population, and the diffusive closure excludes convective
momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum sources.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of toroidal momentum
carried by one neutral species, aggregated over neutral states. Toroidal
denotes the momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame, not velocity direction.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral species momentum convection velocity is the
flux-surface-normal convection coefficient that multiplies the toroidal
momentum density carried by neutrals of one chemical species. The toroidal
momentum component is defined along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the coefficient itself is not a
velocity directed along $\hat{\phi}$. It is the toroidal component of the
[neutral species momentum convection
velocity](name:neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity).

The defining relation preserves the total convective flux of toroidal
momentum across a magnetic flux surface:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = P_{\phi,a} V_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_{s \in a} P_{\phi,s} V_{\phi,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ denotes one neutral chemical species, $s$ runs over its resolved
neutral states, $P_{\phi,s}$ and $P_{\phi,a}$ are signed toroidal momentum
densities, $V_{\phi,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $V_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ are
state-resolved and species-aggregated convection coefficients, and
$\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum
flux. The state sum excludes other chemical species; this is a local
coefficient, not a flux-surface average. The one-species aggregation
distinguishes it from the broader [toroidal neutral momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and
$P_{\phi,a}$ have the same sign, with positive toroidal momentum directed
toward increasing $\phi$ and positive flux-surface-normal transport directed
toward increasing magnetic flux label.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Momentum effective convection, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Effective velocity coefficient relating convective transport of toroidal
momentum across an oriented surface to the toroidal momentum density of one
resolved neutral internal state.
NAMES.long:
This effective convection velocity multiplies the toroidal
[momentum](name:momentum) density of one neutral internal state to give its
convective flux through an oriented surface. The toroidal label identifies
the transported momentum component, not the direction of transport. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing toroidal angle.

For a surface with chosen unit normal $\hat{\mathbf n}$, the defining
convective closure is:

$$
\Pi_{s,\phi n}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}} M_{s,\phi}
$$

where $s$ identifies one internal state of one neutral species, $\Pi_{s,\phi
n}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its convective toroidal-momentum flux through the
oriented surface, $V_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection
coefficient, and $M_{s,\phi}$ is its toroidal momentum density. The momentum
density is $M_{s,\phi}=m_s n_s u_{s,\phi}$, where $m_s$ is the neutral
particle mass, $n_s$ is the state-resolved number density, and $u_{s,\phi}$
is the projection of the state's mean translational velocity onto
$\hat{\phi}$.

The quantity is resolved by neutral internal state, without summation over
states or species. Its [neutral-species
counterpart](name:toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity)
applies to momentum transport aggregated over internal states; state
momentum fluxes, rather than velocity coefficients, are additive.

This is a transport coefficient, not the toroidal projection of the [bulk
neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity),
and it need not equal that projection. It excludes gradient-driven diffusive
transport, represented by [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity),
and does not represent a momentum source.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when effective convection is directed along the
chosen surface normal, so that convective toroidal-momentum flux and
toroidal momentum density have the same sign; positive toroidal momentum
points toward increasing $\phi$.
