NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Signed nitrogen-ion fluid velocity component along the geometric toroidal
direction, evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport
barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed nitrogen-ion fluid velocity component along the
geometric toroidal direction, evaluated at the radial location of the
internal transport barrier.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the nitrogen-ion fluid velocity and
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the geometric toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity represents directed nitrogen-ion flow at the barrier location,
not the total speed or radial and poloidal velocity components. It follows
the same component definition as [toroidal neon velocity at the internal
transport
barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), with
nitrogen as the species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the nitrogen-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the nitrogen impurity ion bulk-flow velocity at the
magnetic axis, taken along increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical
height. It is the density-weighted mean over all nitrogen ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the nitrogen impurity ion bulk-flow velocity at the
magnetic axis is the projection of the local nitrogen impurity-ion bulk flow
onto the toroidal direction at the innermost confined-plasma locus where the
poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes. For this species-level intensive
quantity, the nitrogen velocity is the density-weighted mean over all
nitrogen ion charge states. The toroidal direction is $\hat{\phi}$, the unit
vector for increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases
counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity is defined by the
density-weighted projection of charge-state-resolved ion flows:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},0}
=
\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}\,\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right)}
{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},0}$ is this on-axis nitrogen toroidal velocity,
$q$ indexes nitrogen ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}$ is the local
density of charge state $q$ at the magnetic axis,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}$ is its bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic
axis, and the subscript $0$ denotes the magnetic-axis value. The denominator
is the charge-state sum that forms [nitrogen density at the magnetic
axis](name:nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis).

This is a local on-axis species-level velocity, not a flux-surface-averaged
quantity and not a charge-state-summed velocity. It is defined only where
the charge-state-summed nitrogen ion density at the magnetic axis is
nonzero. It is the nitrogen counterpart, at the same locus, of [toroidal
deuterium velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), and it is
distinguished from nitrogen toroidal velocity at other radial loci such as
[the pedestal top](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top) or [an
internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted nitrogen impurity-ion
flow at the magnetic axis is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the oxygen ion bulk velocity, evaluated at the radial
location of the internal transport barrier in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame. For species-level oxygen, this is the density-weighted mean
over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the oxygen ion bulk velocity at an internal transport
barrier is the component of the oxygen bulk-flow velocity along the toroidal
basis direction at the radial location of the internal transport barrier.
The toroidal direction is $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

For species-level oxygen, the velocity is the density-weighted mean over all
oxygen charge states:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}}) = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})}
$$

where $r_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the radial location of the internal transport
barrier, $q$ indexes oxygen charge states, $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of oxygen charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is
its bulk velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle.

This quantity is a local toroidal component at the
internal-transport-barrier locus, not a flux-surface average or a boundary
value. Same-locus species counterparts include [toroidal carbon velocity at
internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
[toroidal xenon velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
[toroidal nitrogen velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), and
[toroidal deuterium velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier);
the same-species boundary counterpart is toroidal flux-surface-averaged
oxygen velocity at plasma boundary.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted oxygen ion bulk flow is
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of oxygen ions at the magnetic axis,
averaged over all oxygen ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the oxygen-ion bulk flow
evaluated at the magnetic axis, with contributions from all oxygen
ionization states combined as a density-weighted mean.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O},q} V_{\phi,\mathrm{O},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes oxygen ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{O},q}$ is the number
density of state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{O},q}$ is its
toroidal velocity component in m.s$^{-1}$. The component is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The magnetic axis is the
innermost confined-plasma location where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient
vanishes. Neutral oxygen and other species are excluded. The corresponding
boundary quantity is [toroidal oxygen velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted oxygen-ion bulk flow
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short:
Signed total linear momentum along increasing toroidal angle within a closed
flux surface as it approaches the magnetic axis, in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total toroidal linear momentum carried by electrons and
all ion species within the volume enclosed by a closed magnetic flux surface
as that surface approaches the magnetic axis. It is a linear-momentum
projection, not toroidal angular momentum.

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\psi\to\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}} \int_{V(\psi)} \sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,\phi}\,dV
$$

Here $P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the limiting toroidal momentum, $\psi$ is a
flux-surface label, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its magnetic-axis value,
$V(\psi)$ is the enclosed volume, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $n_s$ is
its number density, $v_{s,\phi}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and
$dV$ is the volume element. The sum includes electrons and ions and excludes
neutral species. Its aggregation and projection match [toroidal total plasma
momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum), while the corresponding
boundary quantity is toroidal total plasma momentum at plasma boundary.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net enclosed momentum points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total plasma toroidal momentum, summed over ion species and electrons

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer to
bulk thermal electrons through Coulomb collisions with other plasma species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque transferred to the
bulk thermal electron population by Coulomb collisions. It is the toroidal
projection of the volume-integrated thermal electron collisional torque,
including contributions from all specified collisional partners and
excluding noncollisional momentum transfer.

The volume-integrated torque is defined from the local [toroidal thermal
electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \tau_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal collisional
torque on thermal electrons, $\tau_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
corresponding local torque density, and $V$ is the integration volume. The
toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisional angular momentum is transferred
to the thermal electrons in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque on
thermal ions of a selected charge state, giving the net rate of toroidal
angular momentum transfer to that ion population by collisions.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal projection of the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque
vector
[thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions),
restricted to thermal ions of a selected ionic charge state $Z$. It is
defined as:

$$
\tau_\phi(Z) = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}(Z)
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}(Z)$ is the volume-integrated
Coulomb-collisional torque vector for ions in charge state $Z$, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector.

This scalar captures the net toroidal angular momentum deposited per unit
time into the specified thermal ion charge state by all Coulomb-collisional
partners, including fast particles, electrons, and background ion species.
It is volume-integrated over the plasma, not a local density; the
density-form analog for fast ions is
[toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
For the analogous thermal electron quantity see
[toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net collisional angular momentum transfer
to the ion charge state is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal component of the local collisional angular-momentum transfer
rate per unit volume deposited in thermal ions by fast-particle
thermalization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the angular-momentum source
deposited in the thermal-ion population through Coulomb collisions with fast
particles undergoing thermalization. It represents only this collisional
exchange, rather than the total torque on the ions or the full
torque-density vector. The corresponding vector quantity is [thermal-ion
torque density due to
thermalization](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization).

The toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{th}} = \left(\frac{\partial \ell_{\phi,\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{th}}$ is the transferred toroidal torque density
and $\ell_{\phi,\mathrm{th}}$ is the toroidal angular-momentum density of
thermal ions. The collision subscript restricts the transfer to Coulomb
collisional exchange with the fast-particle distribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when angular momentum is transferred to the
thermal ions in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various ion species

NAMES.name: toroidal_torque_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short:
Local rate of angular-momentum transfer about the plasma symmetry axis per
unit volume attributable to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic dynamics.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the diamagnetic contribution to the local source of angular
momentum about the plasma symmetry axis. It describes the torque per unit
volume associated with the toroidal momentum source, rather than the
toroidal projection of a torque vector.

Its relation to the toroidal force density is

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}} = R f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic toroidal torque
density and $f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to the
toroidal force density in the momentum balance. In the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The quantity includes only the contribution attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic dynamics, not the full torque density
from all mechanisms. It applies to the population included in the momentum
balance; no particular species or all-species sum is implied. Population
contributions add when an aggregate torque density is formed.

Unlike [momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which describes
linear-momentum transfer across an oriented surface, this quantity is a
volume source of angular momentum. A nonzero local contribution does not by
itself establish a nonzero net torque integrated over the plasma.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic momentum source acts in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_plasma_momentum
NAMES.short:
Total linear momentum of all plasma species projected onto the toroidal
direction by integrating their momentum density over the confined plasma
volume.
NAMES.long:
The total toroidal plasma momentum is the integrated linear momentum of all
ion species and electrons projected onto the geometric toroidal direction.
It is the toroidal component of the [total plasma
momentum](name:total_plasma_momentum), not an angular momentum or a local
momentum-flux quantity.

$$
P_\phi = \int_{V_p} \left(\sum_s \boldsymbol{\pi}_s\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}\,dV
$$

where $P_\phi$ is the total toroidal momentum, $V_p$ is the confined plasma
volume, $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ is the local linear-momentum density of species
$s$, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $dV$ is the volume
element. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the integrated linear momentum points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered by Coulomb
collisions to trapped fast ions interacting with a specified ion charge
state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum source density
transferred to the trapped fast-ion population through Coulomb collisions
with a specified ion charge state. It is the toroidal component of the
collisional torque contribution identified by the [trapped fast-ion
charge-state collisional torque
density](name:trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The toroidal torque density is related to the toroidal collisional force
density by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal torque density, $R$ is the
major radius measured from the symmetry axis, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$
is the toroidal component of the collisional force density transferred to
trapped fast ions. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Only the trapped fast-ion contribution and the specified ion-charge-state
collision channel are included; passing-orbit contributions such as
[toroidal counter-passing fast ion charge-state collisional torque
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
are excluded. This quantity is a local density, not a volume-integrated
toroidal torque.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the collisional force transferred to the
trapped fast-ion population has a toroidal component in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted mean toroidal fluid-velocity component of all tritium ion
charge states at the internal transport barrier, directed along increasing
toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid-velocity
component for all tritium ions at the internal transport barrier. It
excludes neutral tritium and aggregates the ionic charge states.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{T}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q} v_{\phi,\mathrm{T},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q}}
$$

Here $q$ indexes tritium ionic charge states, $n_{\mathrm{T},q}$ is the
corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{T},q}$ is the
toroidal fluid-velocity component in m s$^{-1}$. The denominator is the
total tritium-ion density, related to [tritium density at the internal
transport barrier](name:tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The
internal transport barrier is the flux-surface location where cross-field
transport is locally reduced and kinetic gradients are steep; this quantity
is distinct from the corresponding value at the [magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted tritium-ion velocity
component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal fluid velocity of the tritium-ion population evaluated at
the magnetic axis and resolved in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle.
NAMES.long:
The tritium-ion toroidal velocity is the density-weighted fluid-velocity
component of tritium ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, where the gradient
of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes. It describes collective ion motion
rather than thermal speed or individual-particle gyro-orbit velocity.

For all tritium ion charge states included in the species definition, the
quantity is

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{T}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the ionic charge state, $n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}$ is its number
density, $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}$ is its fluid velocity, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The corresponding local tritium abundance is given by
[tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the tritium-ion velocity component points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted tungsten impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing
toroidal angle, averaged over all ionization charge states at the internal
transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of the tungsten impurity-ion
bulk-flow velocity at the internal transport barrier, with contributions
from ionic charge states combined by density weighting.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{W}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right)}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the tungsten ionic charge state, $n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its
number density, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow velocity,
and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The sum includes all tungsten
ionization charge states and excludes neutral tungsten. The corresponding
[toroidal tungsten velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) differs only by its
spatial locus, while [toroidal iron velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier)
illustrates the analogous charge-state-averaged quantity for another
impurity species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the tungsten-ion flow points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the magnetic axis, the innermost point of the confined plasma where the
poloidal magnetic flux gradient vanishes.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion bulk flow velocity at
the magnetic axis quantifies the net rotation of tungsten ions about the
torus axis at the innermost flux surface, where the gradient of poloidal
magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes ($\nabla\psi = 0$). This on-axis value anchors
the full radial toroidal rotation profile and complements the edge
measurement given by [toroidal tungsten velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

The toroidal fluid velocity is the first velocity moment of the tungsten ion
distribution function $f_W$, summed over all ionization states and projected
onto the toroidal direction $\hat{\phi}$:

$$
v_\phi^W = \frac{\int v_\phi \, f_W(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v}{\int f_W(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the individual particle velocity in the $\hat{\phi}$
direction.

Core tungsten rotation is driven by neutral beam injection torque, intrinsic
rotation, and radial momentum transport; in H-mode plasmas, on-axis values
range roughly $10^4$–$3\times10^5$ m s$^{-1}$, depending on beam torque and
intrinsic rotation contributions. Measurement is performed via
charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy of tungsten line emission. The
analogous quantity for lighter impurity species is [toroidal nitrogen
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), and for the main
ion species [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the tungsten ion flow is directed in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of xenon ions at the radial location
assigned to the internal transport barrier, averaged over all xenon
ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the
toroidal direction at the flux-surface radius assigned to the internal
transport barrier. It is averaged over xenon ionic charge states; neutral
xenon is excluded.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}}=\frac{\sum_q n_q\left(\mathbf{v}_q\cdot\hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_q}
$$

where $q$ indexes xenon ionization states, $n_q$ is the number density of
state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_q$ is its bulk velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle,
and $Z$ the vertical height. The corresponding xenon-ion quantities at the
[magnetic axis](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [pedestal
top](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) use the same aggregation
and projection at different radial locations.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the xenon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of xenon ions at the magnetic axis,
averaged over all xenon ionization states and signed by the toroidal
direction.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity
evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the density-weighted mean over all
xenon ionization states; neutral xenon is excluded. The component is defined
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

At the magnetic axis, the charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included xenon ionization states,
$n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density,
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and
$V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the resulting mean. This quantity differs from
[toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), which is not restricted
to xenon, and from [toroidal xenon velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), which
is evaluated at another locus.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the xenon-ion flow component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: torque_density
NAMES.short:
Local vector rate of net angular-momentum transfer per unit volume to or
from plasma, with population-, orbit-class-, mechanism-, and
component-specific forms.
NAMES.long:
Torque density is the local vector rate at which angular momentum is
transferred to or from a specified plasma content, expressed per unit
volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction unless a
component-specific form is selected.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau} = \left(\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{transfer}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ is the torque-density vector and
$\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is the angular-momentum density of the selected plasma
content. The transfer term is net over the mechanisms and populations
included by the specific quantity. Population- and orbit-class-resolved
instances include [ion torque density](name:ion_torque_density), [neutral
torque density](name:neutral_torque_density), and trapped or passing
contributions; [toroidal torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density) is
the corresponding directional component.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the torque vector points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ basis; the toroidal component is positive when it increases angular
momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: co_passing_torque_density
NAMES.short:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for the co-passing plasma
population, retaining the complete torque-vector direction and all
applicable transfer mechanisms.
NAMES.long:
Torque density for the co-passing plasma population is the net
angular-momentum transfer rate to that population per unit volume. It
retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a
toroidal component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{co}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the angular momentum of the co-passing
population, $\Delta V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.

Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, the quantity is the net sum of all
applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions. The [toroidal co-passing
torque density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density) is its
major-radius-weighted toroidal projection, while [toroidal torque
density](name:toroidal_torque_density) selects the corresponding toroidal
component without restricting the orbit class. The [torque
density](name:torque_density) parent provides the common vector quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_torque_density
NAMES.short:
Torque density for counter-passing particles is the net angular-momentum
transfer rate to that orbit class per unit volume, retaining the complete
torque-vector direction.
NAMES.long:
Torque density for counter-passing particles is the net angular-momentum
transfer rate to the counter-passing population per unit volume. It retains
the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a toroidal
component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{cp}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the angular momentum of the
counter-passing population, $\Delta V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.
The subscript $\mathrm{cp}$ identifies the counter-passing orbit class.

This is the counter-passing specialization of [torque
density](name:torque_density). The [toroidal counter-passing torque
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density) is its
major-radius-weighted toroidal projection, while [co-passing torque
density](name:co_passing_torque_density) applies the same vector definition
to the co-passing orbit class. Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, all
applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions are included.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Local vector rate of net angular-momentum transfer per unit volume for a
specified ion charge state, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
NAMES.long:
Torque density for a specified ion charge state is the local vector rate at
which angular momentum is transferred to or from that ion population per
unit volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than
selecting a toroidal or other component, and is a charge-state-resolved
instance of [torque_density](name:torque_density).

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau} = \left(\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{transfer}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ is the torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}$
is the angular-momentum density of the specified ion charge state, and $t$
is time. The transfer term represents the net angular-momentum exchange
included by this unqualified quantity.

The selected plasma content is one specified ion species in one specified
ionization state. The quantity is local, net over the applicable transfer
mechanisms, and not summed over other ion species or charge states. It
excludes any restriction to a particular orbit class or spatial component.

Unlike [ion_torque_density](name:ion_torque_density), which aggregates over
all ion species and charge states, this quantity resolves the selected ion
charge state. Its toroidal component is represented by
[toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density),
while the present quantity retains the full vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the torque vector points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ basis; its toroidal component is positive when it increases angular
momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: ion_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for all ion species and
charge states, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
NAMES.long:
Torque density for all ion species and charge states is the net
angular-momentum transfer rate to the ion population per unit volume. It
retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a
toroidal component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{i}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i}$ is the ion torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{L}_{i}$ is the total angular momentum of all ion species and
charge states in the volume element $\Delta V$, and $t$ is time.

Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, the quantity is the net sum of all
applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions. The parent [torque
density](name:torque_density) gives the corresponding general torque-density
concept, while [toroidal ion torque
density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density) is its major-radius-weighted
toroidal projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: neutral_torque_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume from neutral particles to
the plasma, summed over all neutral internal states and retaining the
complete torque-vector direction.
NAMES.long:
Torque density for neutral particles is the net angular-momentum transfer
rate to the plasma per unit volume produced by neutral–plasma momentum
exchange, summed over all neutral internal states. It retains the complete
torque-vector direction rather than selecting a toroidal component or a
particular neutral state.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{n\to p} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0} \frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{p\leftarrow n}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{n\to p}$ is the torque-density vector transferred
from neutrals to the plasma, $\boldsymbol{L}_{p\leftarrow n}$ is the
corresponding angular momentum transferred to the plasma, $\Delta V$ is a
volume element, and $t$ is time.

This is the neutral-exchange contribution to the broader [torque
density](name:torque_density); it excludes source terms unrelated to
neutral–plasma momentum exchange. The [toroidal neutral torque
density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density) is its toroidal component.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_torque_density
NAMES.short:
Local toroidal angular-momentum source density contributed by passing
particles whose parallel motion follows the co-current direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of torque density contributed
by the co-passing particle population. It gives the source rate of toroidal
angular momentum per unit volume for that orbit class.

The toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing toroidal torque density,
$R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the toroidal force-density component on
co-passing particles. The parent [co-passing torque
density](name:co_passing_torque_density) includes the corresponding
angular-momentum source without selecting this toroidal component.

This is a local quantity, not a flux-surface average, and is distinct from
the [toroidal counter-passing torque
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density), which resolves the
opposite passing-orbit branch.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the co-passing force increases toroidal
angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of toroidal angular momentum density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular-momentum source rate per unit volume from counter-passing
particles, obtained by applying the major-radius lever arm to their net
toroidal force density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum source rate per unit
volume associated with counter-passing particles. Counter-passing particles
have guiding-center parallel motion opposite to the plasma-current
direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the toroidal torque
density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}(R,\phi,Z)=R\,f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}(R,\phi,Z)
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the counter-passing toroidal torque
density, $R$ is the major-radius lever arm, and $f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is
the net toroidal force density on the counter-passing population. The force
density is summed over the included particle species and momentum-exchange
mechanisms.

This is the toroidal component of counter_passing_torque_density,
distinguished from the co-passing contribution represented by
[toroidal_co_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net toroidal force on the counter-passing
population points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of toroidal angular momentum density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the net angular-momentum source density acting on a
specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque density acting on
a specified ion species in a specified charge state. It represents the local
source or sink of toroidal angular momentum, without attribution to a
particular transport or collisional mechanism.

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is
the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
and $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}$ is the full torque-density vector for ion
species $i$ and charge state $q$. The vector parent is [ion charge state
torque density](name:ion_charge_state_torque_density).

The quantity is a total over all contributing processes for the specified
ion charge state; process-resolved contributions are distinct quantities.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the torque-density vector has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Local toroidal torque density on all ion species and charge states, giving
the external source rate of ion angular momentum about the symmetry axis
with its major-radius moment arm.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion torque density is the local rate at which external
processes change the angular momentum of the combined ion population about
the symmetry axis. It is the toroidal component of the parent [ion torque
density](name:ion_torque_density), summed over ion species and charge
states; internal ion–ion exchanges cancel in this aggregate.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it is defined from the
net external ion force density by

$$
\tau_{\phi,i} = R f_{\phi,i} = R\,\mathbf{f}_i \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,i}$ is the toroidal ion torque density, $R$ is major
radius in m, $\mathbf{f}_i$ is the external force density on the combined
ion population in N m$^{-3}$, $f_{\phi,i}$ is its toroidal component, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle. Unlike the broader [toroidal torque
density](name:toroidal_torque_density), this quantity is restricted to the
ion population.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the external torque increases ion angular
momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations (sum over states when multiple states are considered), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_torque_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the plasma angular-momentum source density produced by
neutral–plasma momentum exchange, summed over all neutral internal states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral torque density is the local source of plasma angular
momentum about the machine symmetry axis produced by momentum exchange with
neutral particles. It is aggregated over all neutral internal states and is
distinct from the state-resolved quantity [toroidal neutral internal-state
torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_torque_density).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,n}(R,\phi,Z) = R\sum_s \mathcal{R}_{\phi,n,s}(R,\phi,Z)
$$

where $R$ is major radius in m, $s$ indexes neutral internal states, and
$\mathcal{R}_{\phi,n,s}$ is the toroidal component of the momentum-exchange
force density from state $s$. The sum gives the neutral contribution to the
parent [neutral torque density](name:neutral_torque_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when neutral momentum exchange increases plasma
angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations (sum over states when multiple states are considered), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short:
Local rate at which collisions transfer angular momentum to or from a plasma
population, expressed as torque per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate
imparted to a specified plasma population by collisional interactions,
divided by volume. It applies to electron, ion, charge-state, and
orbit-class populations, including the specific cases represented by
[electron collisional torque
density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [ion
collisional torque density](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

For a resolved scalar torque component, the defining relation is

$$
\tau_{s,\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \ell_s}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{s,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque density, $\ell_s$
is the corresponding angular-momentum density of population $s$, and the
subscript indicates that only collisional transfer is included.

The quantity excludes torque caused by electromagnetic forces, pressure
forces, or other noncollisional processes. More specific population and
orbit restrictions, such as co-passing fast-ion charge-state collisional
torque density, refine the recipient population without changing the
underlying definition.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisions increase the resolved angular
momentum of the recipient population.

NAMES.name: electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Torque density due to collisional processes is the angular-momentum transfer
rate per unit volume imparted to the electron population, encompassing fast
and thermal electrons.
NAMES.long:
Torque density due to collisional processes is the local rate of
angular-momentum transfer to the electron population per unit volume. It is
the common parent of the fast- and thermal-electron specializations, which
distinguish the electron populations receiving the collisional transfer.

Using $\dot{L}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ for the collisional angular-momentum
transfer rate to electrons and $V$ for volume, the torque density is defined
by

$$
\tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{\partial \dot{L}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}}{\partial V}
$$

The quantity refines
[torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:torque_density_due_to_collisions),
while
[fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
and
[thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
provide its population-specific forms. The corresponding ion-family quantity
is
[ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions);
this name does not imply a volume-integrated torque.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisions transfer angular momentum to
electrons in the positive direction defined for the torque component.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Fast-electron collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum
transfer rate per unit volume delivered to fast electrons through Coulomb
collisions.
NAMES.long:
Fast-electron collisional torque density is the vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer to the fast-electron population through Coulomb
momentum exchange with other plasma species. It is the fast-population
specialization of [electron collisional torque
density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

For position vector $\mathbf{r}$ relative to the chosen torque origin and
collisional force density $\mathbf{F}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ acting on fast
electrons, the torque density is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-electron
collisional torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector, and
$\mathbf{F}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density.

The quantity may be resolved by orbit class or directional component,
including co-passing fast-electron collisional torque density and [toroidal
fast-electron collisional torque
density](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons).
It excludes torque from noncollisional forces and is distinct from
[thermal-electron collisional torque
density](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each torque-density component points along
the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volumetric counter-passing torque density deposited in the fast-electron
population through Coulomb collisions, the local vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
The counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque density is the net rate
at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum per unit volume to
the counter-passing suprathermal electron population. It is the orbit-class
specialization of [fast-electron torque density due to
collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The vector torque density is defined from the corresponding collisional
force density by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}=\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{f}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density
vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin,
and $\mathbf{f}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density
transferred to counter-passing fast electrons. Its toroidal projection is
[toroidal counter-passing fast-electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
The quantity excludes thermal-electron and other orbit-class contributions.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Collisional torque density is the signed rate of angular-momentum transfer
per unit volume to a specified plasma population.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density is the signed angular-momentum transfer rate per
unit volume delivered to a recipient plasma population by collisions. The
quantity applies across species-resolved forms, including [fast-ion
collisional torque density](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
and [thermal-ion collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), within the
shared context of [collisional torque
density](name:torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque density and $\ell$ is
the corresponding angular-momentum density of the recipient population. The
definition excludes torque from noncollisional forces and does not prescribe
a species, orbit class, or directional projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisions transfer angular momentum into the
recipient population.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Fast-ion collisional torque density is the local vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer to fast ions per unit plasma volume caused by
Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion collisional torque density is the local vector source of angular
momentum delivered to the fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It is
the fast-ion component of the broader [ion torque density due to
collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [thermal-ion
torque density due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) describes the
corresponding thermal-ion contribution.

The local defining relation is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_f}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-ion collisional
torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_f$ is fast-ion angular-momentum
density, and $t$ is time; the subscript $\mathrm{coll}$ selects the
Coulomb-collisional contribution. Orbit-resolved and component-resolved
forms are specific instances of this vector quantity, and it is distinct
from collisional energy-transfer density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved vector component points along its
positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Collisional co-passing torque density for fast ions is the local vector rate
of angular-momentum transfer to or from the co-passing fast-ion population
caused by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
NAMES.long:
Collisional co-passing torque density for fast ions is the local source
density of angular momentum transferred to or from the co-passing fast-ion
population by Coulomb collisions. It retains the full torque-density vector
for fast ions on the co-passing orbit branch rather than selecting a
particular component.

The local defining relation is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{co},\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{f,\mathrm{co}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{co},\mathrm{coll}}$ is the co-passing
fast-ion collisional torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{\ell}_{f,\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing fast-ion
angular-momentum density, and $t$ is time; the subscript $\mathrm{coll}$
selects the Coulomb-collisional contribution.

This quantity is restricted to the co-passing fast-ion population; it is not
the all-orbit [fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and is not an
aggregate over counter-passing or trapped fast ions. The [toroidal
co-passing fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is the toroidal component-resolved instance of this vector quantity, and
this quantity is distinct from collisional energy-transfer density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved vector component points along its
positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Collisional counter-passing torque density for fast ions is the local vector
rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume caused by Coulomb
collisions.
NAMES.long:
Collisional counter-passing torque density for fast ions is the local source
density of angular momentum transferred to or from the counter-passing
fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It retains the full
torque-density vector rather than resolving it along one direction.

The vector quantity is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the
collisional torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is
the local angular-momentum density of counter-passing fast ions, and $t$ is
time. This quantity provides the vector parent for the [toroidal
counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
and complements the toroidal sibling [toroidal fast-ion torque density due
to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It
is a local source density, not a volume-integrated torque, and belongs to
the broader [fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the radial, toroidal, or vertical component
points in the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local
angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to thermal electrons by
Coulomb collisions with fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local
angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to the thermal electron
population by Coulomb collisions with fast particles.

Its vector form is related to the collisional momentum-transfer density by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from the torque origin, and
$\mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional momentum-transfer density
acting on thermal electrons.

The quantity is independent of orbit-class and component selection;
co-passing, counter-passing, trapped, and directional forms are specialized
instances. It is distinct from the broader [electron torque density due to
collisions](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and includes the
[toroidal thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
as a component-resolved form. Torque transferred to fast particles is
excluded.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ points toward increasing $R$,
increasing $\phi$, or increasing $Z$, respectively, in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the
local angular-momentum transfer rate to bulk thermal electrons from Coulomb
collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the
local rate per unit volume at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular
momentum to the bulk, near-Maxwellian thermal electron population,
restricted to collisions with counter-passing fast particles.

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,cp}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{e,\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll,cp}}
$$

Here $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,cp}}$ is the
collisional torque-density vector deposited in thermal electrons, and
$\boldsymbol{\ell}_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is their angular-momentum density. The
subscript $\mathrm{cp}$ restricts the transfer to counter-passing fast
particles. This quantity is an orbit-resolved contribution to the [thermal
electron torque density due to
collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions); its
[toroidal counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is the toroidal projection, while the [toroidal thermal electron torque
density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
resolves the corresponding axis component without this orbit restriction.
Contributions deposited in fast electrons and torque from non-Coulomb
processes are excluded.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame: increasing $R$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, or increasing
$Z$.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population
per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, without restricting orbit
class or spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
Thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local vector source of
angular momentum transferred to the bulk thermal-ion population by Coulomb
collisions with other charged populations. It is the thermal-ion member of
the broader [ion torque density due to
collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) family.

For the selected thermal-ion population, the collisional torque-density
vector is defined from its distribution function by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the
ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the thermal-ion
distribution function, and $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its Coulomb-collision
operator.

At parent level, the quantity includes the allowed orbit and
spatial-direction contributions; [co-passing thermal-ion torque density due
to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
and [toroidal thermal-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) are
corresponding restrictions. It excludes torque deposited in fast-ion
populations.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population
per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, restricted to co-passing
orbit-class contributions and without restricting spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque
per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal ion population by Coulomb
collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is restricted
to the co-passing orbit-class contribution of those collisions and is
represented by the full torque-density vector, not by a single spatial
component.

For the selected thermal-ion population, the co-passing collisional
torque-density vector is defined from the co-passing contribution to its
collision operator by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the
thermal-ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the
thermal-ion distribution function, and $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}}$
is the Coulomb-collision operator term giving momentum transfer to thermal
ions from the co-passing orbit-class contribution.

Co-passing denotes passing-orbit contributions whose toroidal motion in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is in the same sense as the
plasma current, distinct from counter-passing and trapped orbit-class
contributions. At parent level, the quantity retains the full vector
direction for that orbit class; [toroidal co-passing thermal-ion torque
density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is the corresponding $\hat{\phi}$-component restriction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes torque deposited in fast-ion
populations.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Counter-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local
angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal
ions by Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local
torque per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal ion population by
Coulomb collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is
restricted to the counter-passing particle component while retaining the
full torque-vector quantity rather than a single axis component.

The collisional torque density is related to the collisional force density
by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque density transferred
to thermal ions, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the axis about
which torque is resolved, and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the force
density transferred to thermal ions by collisions.

This quantity is the counter-passing contribution to
[thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions);
collision partners and channels are included in the collisional transfer,
while other orbit classes are excluded. Its toroidal component is
represented by
[toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
while
[toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
provides the corresponding toroidal component aggregated over contributing
orbit classes.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved torque component points along its
corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal collisional torque per unit volume delivered to a specified
bulk thermal-ion species by co-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal co-passing thermal-ion collisional torque density is the local
toroidal component of the angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume
delivered to a specified bulk thermal-ion species through Coulomb collisions
with co-passing fast particles.

Its relation to the vector parent is

$$
\tau_{i\phi,\mathrm{co,coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{co,coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\tau_{i\phi,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the signed toroidal torque-density
component, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the [co-passing
thermal-ion torque-density vector due to
collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The
right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from
the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
subscripts $i$, $\mathrm{co}$, and $\mathrm{coll}$ identify the receiving
ion species, co-passing contribution, and collisional mechanism,
respectively.

The co-passing restriction applies to the colliding fast-particle
distribution, not to the orbit class of the receiving thermal ions.
Counter-passing and trapped contributions are excluded. The quantity is
local, without spatial averaging or volume integration. Ionic charge-state
contributions are summed within the selected species, while different
receiving ion species remain distinct; [co-passing thermal-ion charge-state
torque density due to
collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
retains charge-state resolution in the corresponding vector quantity.

This is a population- and component-resolved contribution to [torque
density](name:torque_density). The adjacent [toroidal co-passing
thermal-electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
describes transfer to thermal electrons instead and is not included here.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the torque-density component delivered to
thermal ions points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit
volume to fast electrons through Coulomb collisions involving the
counter-passing particle distribution.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque density is the
flux-surface-averaged angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to
fast electrons through Coulomb collisions involving the counter-passing
particle distribution. It is a component-resolved specialization of [torque
density](name:torque_density).

Its relation to the local collisional torque-density vector is

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{cp,coll}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp,coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi} \right\rangle
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ denotes this averaged toroidal
component, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the [counter-passing
fast-electron collisional torque-density
vector](name:counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The
direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. Angle brackets denote the volume-weighted average over an
infinitesimally thin shell between neighboring magnetic flux surfaces.

The counter-passing restriction applies to the contributing particle
distribution; the receiving population is the fast electrons. Co-passing and
trapped contributions are excluded. Torque delivered to bulk thermal
electrons is a distinct quantity, represented by [toroidal counter-passing
thermal-electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
Flux-surface averaging retains torque per volume rather than producing a
volume-integrated torque.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the flux-surface-averaged collisional torque
received by the fast electrons has a component toward increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per plasma
volume to counter-passing fast ions through Coulomb collisions with a
specified ion species.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal counter-passing fast-ion collisional torque density is the
flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma
volume delivered to counter-passing fast ions through Coulomb collisions
with a specified ion species.

It is related to the full [counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by

$$
\tau_{\phi i,\mathrm{cp,coll}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}\cdot\hat{\phi} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the averaged toroidal torque
density, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the local collisional
torque-density vector acting on counter-passing fast ions, and the angle
brackets denote the differential-volume-weighted average over a magnetic
flux surface. The subscripts $i$, $\mathrm{cp}$, and $\mathrm{coll}$
identify ions, the counter-passing restriction, and collisions,
respectively. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is distance from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

The orbit restriction applies to the fast-ion distribution, not to the
collision partners. Co-passing and trapped fast-ion contributions are
excluded; co-passing contributions belong instead to [co-passing fast-ion
torque density due to
collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
Charge-state contributions are summed at the species level, rather than
resolved for one ionic charge state, while different collision-partner
species remain separate.

This is a toroidal component of [torque density](name:torque_density), not
the full vector or a volume-integrated torque. The local toroidal projection
is taken before flux-surface averaging.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the collisional torque acting on the fast
ions points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Toroidal torque density transferred to bulk thermal ions through Coulomb
collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the local angular-momentum
transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal ions by Coulomb
collisions with counter-passing fast particles. It isolates the toroidal
component of the underlying [counter-passing thermal ion torque density due
to
collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
\tau_\phi^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}
$$

Here $\tau_\phi^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}$ is the toroidal torque density,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}$ is the corresponding
torque-density vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in
the toroidal direction. The projection is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only transfer to bulk thermal ions from the counter-passing fast-particle
population is included; electron transfer and co-passing contributions are
distinct quantities.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit volume to bulk
thermal electrons through Coulomb collisions with particles of a specified
distribution.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal thermal-electron collisional torque density is the signed
angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal
electrons through Coulomb collisions with particles of a specified
distribution. It selects one directional component of the collisional
transfer, rather than the full torque-density vector.

Its defining projection is

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal torque density,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [thermal electron
torque-density vector due to
collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The
right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R, \phi, Z)$, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The thermal electrons are the receiving population; this is not the
reciprocal torque acting on the particles of the specified distribution. No
additional orbit-class restriction is imposed, and contributions from
distinct distributions representing the same species are superposed. The
[toroidal co-passing thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
restricts the contributing fast-particle distribution to co-passing orbits.
As a component of [torque density](name:torque_density), this quantity is
not a volume-integrated torque and excludes noncollisional contributions.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the torque-density component delivered to
thermal electrons points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
