NAMES.name: torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.short:
Torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local
toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per volume to a specified plasma
population caused by Coulomb collisional momentum exchange with electrons.
NAMES.long:
Torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local
toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per volume to a specified plasma
population caused by Coulomb collisional momentum exchange with electrons.
It is the torque density about the vertical symmetry axis associated only
with electron collision partners.

The scalar torque density is the moment arm times the toroidal component of
the Coulomb-collisional force density from electrons in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
\tau_e^{\mathrm{C}} = R f_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $R$ is major radius and $f_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{C}}$ is the toroidal
component, along $\hat{\phi}$, of the force density on the receiving
population due to Coulomb collisions with electrons.

This parent quantity does not specify the receiving population;
species-specific children such as electron torque density due to Coulomb
collisions with electrons identify that population. It excludes torque
density from collisions with ions or neutrals, from external fields or
waves, and from any non-Coulomb momentum-transfer mechanism.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the Coulomb-collisional force density from
electrons on the receiving population points in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.short:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume delivered to
a specified particle population by Coulomb collisions with electrons.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local vector torque density delivered to a specified
recipient particle population by Coulomb collisions with electrons. It
represents angular-momentum transfer to that population and excludes the
equal-and-opposite reaction torque assigned to the electrons.

For a local collisional force density, the torque density is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
torque-density vector transferred to recipient population $a$, $\mathbf{r}$
is the displacement from the torque origin to the local volume element, and
$\mathbf{f}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the Coulomb-collisional
force density transferred from electrons $e$ to population $a$.

The quantity is local, resolved for the receiving particle population, and
restricted to Coulomb collisions with electrons; it is not volume-integrated
and is not summed over other receiving populations or collision partners.
Non-Coulomb forces, energy-transfer rates, and the opposite reaction torque
on electrons are excluded. The [fast-particle torque-density
instance](name:fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons)
applies this shared definition to fast particles.

This is the population-resolved vector specialization of [torque density due
to Coulomb collisions with
electrons](name:torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons).
Its vector components retain the directional information of the collisional
angular-momentum transfer, while any component or aggregate defined
elsewhere is a derived restriction of this vector quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a reported torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.short:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume delivered to
fast particles by Coulomb collisions with background electrons, excluding
the reaction torque on electrons.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local torque-density vector transferred to the
fast-particle population through Coulomb collisions with background
electrons. It represents angular-momentum exchange received by fast
particles, rather than the equal-and-opposite reaction torque assigned to
electrons.

The local collisional angular-momentum balance is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{fp}\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{C}}
=
\left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{fp}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{C},e}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{fp}\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{C}}$ is the
torque-density vector received by fast particles from electrons,
$\boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{fp}}$ is the angular-momentum density of the
fast-particle population, $t$ is time, and the subscripts and superscript
identify Coulomb-collisional exchange from background electrons.

This quantity is local and retains the complete torque vector rather than
selecting a toroidal, poloidal, or radial component. Its recipient
population is the fast-particle population, its collision partner is the
background electron population, and its aggregation is over the
fast-particle population represented locally; it is not volume-integrated
and excludes the opposite reaction torque on electrons.

It is the fast-particle specialization of the broader [particle torque
density due to Coulomb collisions with
electrons](name:particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons),
while [toroidal fast-particle torque density due to Coulomb collisions with
electrons](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons)
is the toroidal component-resolved instance of this vector quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the relevant vector component points in the
corresponding increasing-coordinate direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Torque density due to j cross b force is the vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force acting on a
specified plasma population. It is the parent concept for
orbit-class-restricted and directionally projected forms.
NAMES.long:
Torque density due to $j \times B$ force is the local vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force density acting on a
specified plasma population. It represents the electromagnetic torque
density before any optional orbit-class selection, flux-surface averaging,
or directional projection is applied.

The local torque density is defined as the moment of the Lorentz force
density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{r}(\mathbf{x}) \times \left[\mathbf{j}(\mathbf{x}) \times \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from the chosen torque reference
point to position $\mathbf{x}$, $\mathbf{j}$ is the electric current density
associated with the force acting on the population, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic field.

This parent quantity denotes the shared torque-density concept. Specialized
names may restrict the orbit class, such as
[co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force)
or
[trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force](name:trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force),
or may take a directional projection such as
[toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).
A toroidal projection is onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical
height.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}$ points in the positive direction of its
stated basis vector; for a toroidal projection this is $+\hat{\phi}$, the
direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Co-passing torque density due to j cross b force is the vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force acting on the
co-passing plasma population. It is the parent concept for co-passing
directionally projected forms.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing torque density due to $j \times B$ force is the vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force density acting on
the co-passing plasma population. Co-passing particles are passing-orbit
particles whose guiding-center motion belongs to the branch circulating
around the torus in the same sense as the plasma current. It represents the
co-passing electromagnetic torque density before any directional projection
is applied.

The vector torque density for the co-passing population is defined as the
moment of its $j \times B$ force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{r}(\mathbf{x}) \times \left[\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) \times \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}$ is the co-passing torque
density due to the $j \times B$ force, $\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from
the chosen torque reference point to position $\mathbf{x}$,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the electric current density associated with
co-passing particles, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field.

This parent quantity is already restricted to the co-passing orbit class; it
is distinct from the orbit-unrestricted [torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force). A specialized co-passing
name may add a component and flux-surface averaging, such as [toroidal
co-passing torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force),
whose toroidal projection is onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$
increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is
vertical height. [Counter-passing torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and
[trapped torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) refer to
different orbit-class populations, not components of this co-passing
quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}$ points in the positive
direction of its stated basis vector; for a toroidal projection this is
$+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated by the Lorentz force,
averaged over a magnetic flux surface for counter-passing particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged torque density transferred to
counter-passing particles by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with
their current contribution. Counter-passing particles are the orbit
population whose parallel motion is opposite the plasma-current direction.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{cp}}(\psi)=\left\langle\mathbf{r}\times\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp}}\times\mathbf{B}\right)\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density
vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin,
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the current-density contribution associated
with counter-passing particles, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and
$\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface. The angle brackets denote a
flux-surface average.

This orbit-resolved vector is a member of the [torque density due to J×B
force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) family. Its toroidal
projection is represented by [toroidal counter-passing torque density due to
J×B
force](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force),
while [co-passing torque density due to J×B
force](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) describes the
corresponding population with parallel motion along the plasma-current
direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved torque component points in the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source per unit volume from
the magnetic force on counter-passing particles' current across magnetic
flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source
density delivered to counter-passing particles by the magnetic Lorentz force
associated with their current across magnetic flux surfaces. Toroidal
angular momentum is angular momentum about the symmetry axis; its source is
a [torque density](name:torque_density), not a toroidal force density.

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ctr}} = \left\langle R\,\left(j_{n,\mathrm{ctr}}\hat{\mathbf n}\times\mathbf B\right)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol\phi}\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ctr}}$ is this torque density,
$j_{n,\mathrm{ctr}}$ is the signed conventional current density carried
across magnetic flux surfaces by counter-passing particles, $\hat{\mathbf
n}$ is the unit normal toward increasing flux-surface label $\psi$, and
$\mathbf B$ is the magnetic field. The brackets denote a normalized average
over the surface labeled by $\psi$. In the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is the distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
the toroidal angle, $Z$ is the vertical coordinate, and
$\hat{\boldsymbol\phi}$ points toward increasing $\phi$. The moment arm $R$
remains inside the average.

Counter-passing particles occupy nontrapped passing orbits whose circulation
along the magnetic field opposes the plasma-current direction. Only the
counter-passing part of the specified particle species' distribution
contributes; co-passing and trapped particles and other torque mechanisms
are excluded. This is a flux-surface average, not an unaveraged local source
or a volume-integrated torque.

This quantity is the toroidal angular-momentum source component of the
[counter-passing Lorentz-force torque
density](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force). The
[co-passing
counterpart](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force)
applies the same mechanism to co-passing particles. It is distinct from the
[thermal-plasma return-current
torque](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force), which acts on
thermal plasma through compensating currents.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the magnetic force supplies toroidal angular
momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short:
Net torque transferred to a plasma particle population through collisional
interactions with other particles, expressed as the corresponding rate of
angular-momentum change.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net angular-momentum transfer to a specified plasma
particle population caused by collisions with other particles. It applies to
electron, fast-particle, and ion populations, including the concrete [ion
collisional torque](name:ion_torque_due_to_collisions) and [fast collisional
torque](name:fast_torque_due_to_collisions) forms.

The scalar torque is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{dL_{\mathrm{pop}}}{dt}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque, $L_{\mathrm{pop}}$
is the relevant angular-momentum component of the population, and $t$ is
time.

The quantity represents the net exchange integrated over the plasma volume
and over the collisional partners included in the population definition. It
is distinct from the local [electron collisional torque
density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), which gives torque
per unit volume.

NAMES.name: electron_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Collisionally transferred net torque on the electron population,
representing angular-momentum exchange with other plasma populations for
both fast and thermal electrons.
NAMES.long:
Collisionally transferred net torque on the electron population is the
volume-integrated rate of angular-momentum transfer caused by Coulomb
collisions with other plasma populations. It is the electron-specific member
of the broader [torque due to collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions)
family and parallels [fast torque due to
collisions](name:fast_torque_due_to_collisions).

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{dL_{e,\mathrm{coll}}}{dt}
$$

where $\tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the net collisional torque on the electron
population, $L_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its volume-integrated angular momentum
transferred by collisions, and $t$ is time.

This parent covers both fast and thermal electron cases, represented by
fast-electron torque due to collisions and [thermal-electron torque due to
collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions). It excludes
torque on ions, which belongs to [ion torque due to
collisions](name:ion_torque_due_to_collisions), and excludes non-collisional
torque mechanisms.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisions increase the electron population's
angular momentum in the positive rotational sense about the torque axis.

NAMES.name: fast_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short:
Collisional torque on the fast-particle population is the volume-integrated
angular-momentum transfer caused by Coulomb momentum exchange with the
thermal background plasma.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque on the fast-particle population is the angular-momentum
transfer caused by Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma,
integrated over the plasma volume. It is the fast-population specialization
of [torque_due_to_collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions), with
axis-resolved forms such as
[toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions);
the corresponding electron-population quantity is
[electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:electron_torque_due_to_collisions).

The torque about a chosen origin is defined from the collisional force
density by:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the chosen origin,
$\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force
density acting on the fast-particle population, and $V$ is the plasma
volume. The aggregate includes collisional contributions from thermal
electrons and thermal ion species and charge states; electromagnetic forces,
external sources, and noncollisional mechanisms are excluded.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a torque component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

NAMES.name: ion_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Collisional torque on the ion population is the net angular-momentum
transfer produced by interactions with other particle populations.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque on the ion population is the net angular-momentum
transfer produced by collisional forces acting on ions.

For a volume-integrated torque component about a selected axis, the defining
relation is

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}^{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_V \left(\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ion}}\right)_a\,dV
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}^{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the torque transferred to
ions, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the selected rotation
axis, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the collisional force
density acting on ions, $V$ is the plasma volume, and $a$ identifies the
reported torque direction.

This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [torque due to
collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions); [thermal ion torque due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions) is a more specific
instance restricted to thermal ions. It represents momentum exchange with
collision partners and excludes noncollisional torque sources.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisional momentum exchange transfers
angular momentum to the ion population in the positive sense of the selected
axis; for the toroidal direction, positive means increasing $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Net torque vector transferred to the thermal ion population through
Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange, representing volume-integrated
angular-momentum transfer.
NAMES.long:
The collisional thermal-ion torque is the net angular-momentum transfer to
the thermal ion population from Coulomb collisions, integrated over the
plasma volume. Its vector form retains the direction of the transferred
torque; the toroidal component is represented by [toroidal thermal-ion
torque due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions).

The defining volume integral is:

$$
\mathbf{T}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the torque origin,
$\mathbf{R}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force
density transferred to thermal ions, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity is the thermal-ion specialization of [ion torque due to
collisions](name:ion_torque_due_to_collisions). It describes momentum
exchange, not the collisional energy transfer represented by power.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved torque component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is increasing toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short:
Toroidal fast-particle torque due to collisions is the volume-integrated
toroidal torque exerted on the fast, non-thermal particle population by
Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma. The aggregate
includes thermal electrons and all thermal ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal fast-particle torque due to collisions is the volume-integrated
toroidal torque exerted on the fast, non-thermal particle population by
Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma. It is the component
of collisional angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis associated
with increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The aggregate torque is defined as the plasma-volume integral of the
toroidal collisional force density weighted by the major radius:

$$
T_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V R \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}} f_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}\leftarrow j}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $T_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal fast-particle
torque due to collisions, $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a differential
volume element, $\mathcal{B}$ is the set of thermal-background collision
partners, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}\leftarrow j}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
toroidal component of the collisional force density exerted on fast,
non-thermal particles by partner $j$.

The set $\mathcal{B}$ contains thermal electrons and every thermal ion
species and every charge state of each thermal ion species; the ion part is
charge-state-summed. This quantity is the aggregate over those collision
partners, not an electron-only or charge-state-resolved contribution; the
thermal-electron collision contribution and the [thermal-ion charge-state
collision
contribution](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions)
sum to it when defined over the same volume and fast-particle population.
The equal-and-opposite collisional angular-momentum transfer to the thermal
background is represented by the
[thermal-electron](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions)
and [thermal-ion](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions)
reaction channels.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb collisions exert a net toroidal force
on fast, non-thermal particles in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Net torque about the toroidal symmetry axis transferred to thermal ions by
collisional momentum exchange.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net toroidal angular-momentum transfer to the
thermal-ion population from colliding particle populations, integrated over
the plasma volume. It represents torque about the toroidal symmetry axis
rather than a local torque density.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi,i}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V R\,\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},i}\cdot\hat{\phi}\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi,i}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the integrated collisional
torque, $V$ is the plasma volume, $R$ is major radius in m,
$\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},i}$ is the collisional force density on thermal
ions in N m$^{-3}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$. The thermal-ion contribution is summed
over all represented thermal-ion charge states; its local
charge-state-resolved counterpart is [toroidal thermal-ion charge-state
torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the collisional force on thermal ions has a
component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, producing
positive angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis.

sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various ion species

NAMES.name: torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Net mechanical torque transferred to plasma particles by the Lorentz force
density, obtained by integrating the moment of j cross B over the plasma
volume.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net mechanical torque transferred to charged plasma
particles by the electromagnetic Lorentz force. It is a scalar component of
the volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer associated with the current
density and magnetic field.

For a torque component about a specified axis, the defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\hat{a}} = \int_V \left[\mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j} \times \mathbf{B}\right)\right] \cdot \hat{\mathbf{a}}\,dV
$$

where $\tau_{\hat{a}}$ is the torque component, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position
relative to the torque origin, $\mathbf{j}$ is the electric-current-density
vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$ is the
unit vector along the selected torque axis, and $V$ is the plasma volume.
The [particle torque due to j cross B
force](name:particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force) is a specific instance
of this quantity. Unlike [toroidal torque density due to j cross B
force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force), this parent
denotes a volume-integrated torque rather than a local torque density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the Lorentz-force moment points along the
positive direction of the torque axis; for a toroidal component, this is the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Particle torque due to j cross B force is the volume-integrated
Lorentz-force torque exerted on a represented particle distribution by its
electric current density interacting with the magnetic field. It is the
particle-distribution-resolved parent quantity; species- or
population-specific names refine it without implying a toroidal-only
projection.
NAMES.long:
Particle torque due to j-cross-B force is the volume-integrated torque
exerted on a represented particle distribution by the Lorentz force density
generated from that distribution's electric current density and the magnetic
field. The physical torque is an axial-vector quantity before any species,
population, or coordinate-component qualifier is applied.

The defining volume integral is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_p = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j}_p \times \mathbf{B}\right)\, dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ is the particle-distribution-resolved torque,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the torque origin to the volume
element, $\mathbf{j}_p$ is the electric current density carried by the
represented particle distribution, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and
$V$ is the integration volume.

This parent does not specify fast, thermal, impurity, neutral, or other
particle populations and does not by itself select any coordinate-component
projection. Population-specific instances, such as [fast-particle torque due
to j-cross-B force](name:fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force),
inherit this definition; component-specific quantities are projections of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ rather than redefinitions of the torque source. It
excludes torque contributions not arising from the Lorentz force density
$\mathbf{j}_p \times \mathbf{B}$ and excludes sums over unrelated plasma
sources unless the represented particle distribution is explicitly the
aggregation being described.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a scalar component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$
is aligned with the positive direction of the explicitly named projection
axis; for a toroidal projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, this is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Fast-particle torque due to the j×B force is the volume-integrated torque
vector acting on the fast-particle population through the magnetic Lorentz
force density generated by its current density and the magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$ force is the volume-integrated
torque vector acting on the fast-particle population through the magnetic
part of the Lorentz force density associated with the fast-particle current
density and the magnetic field. It represents angular-momentum transfer to
that fast-particle population, not to thermal particles or material
structures.

The torque vector over a volume $V$ is defined by the moment of the $j
\times B$ force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j}_f \times \mathbf{B}\right)\, dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B}$ is the fast-particle torque due to
the $j \times B$ force, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the chosen
torque origin to the volume element, $\mathbf{j}_f$ is the fast-particle
current density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $dV$ is the volume
element.

This vector parent is distinguished from component-specific projections;
[toroidal fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$
force](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force) is the
toroidal component of the same fast-particle torque. It excludes torque
channels not represented by the fast-particle current-cross-magnetic-field
force density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a reported component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B}$ is aligned with the positive direction of
its stated projection axis, with vector cross products evaluated by the
right-hand rule; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the
toroidal component is positive along $+\hat{\phi}$ toward increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$
side.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated toroidal angular-momentum transfer to fast particles from
the Lorentz force associated with their radial current.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total toroidal torque transferred to the fast-particle
population by the electromagnetic force associated with its radial current,
integrated over the plasma volume.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, the radial-current contribution is
defined by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi}=\int_V -R\,j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}} B_Z\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi}$ is the toroidal torque, $R$ is major radius,
$j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the radial current density carried by fast
particles, $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, and $V$ is the
plasma volume. Equivalently, the integrand is
$R(\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{fast}}\times\mathbf{B})_\phi$ when restricted to the
radial-current contribution.

This is a volume-integrated quantity and is distinct from the local
[toroidal torque density due to the j-cross-B
force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and from
collisional torque transfer to fast particles [toroidal fast torque due to
collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the resulting torque points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
NAMES.short:
Vector torque associated with angular momentum carried away by neutral beam
particles that traverse the plasma without ionization. It represents the
shinethrough contribution to the neutral-beam momentum balance, with
components giving the direction and sense of the loss.
NAMES.long:
Torque due to neutral beam shinethrough is the vector rate at which angular
momentum is carried out of the plasma by injected neutral particles that
traverse the plasma without ionization or absorption. It is a loss term for
plasma angular momentum because the angular momentum of those unabsorbed
particles is not deposited in the plasma.

The shinethrough torque is defined as the time rate of angular momentum
carried by the shinethrough neutral-particle population:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}} = \frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{st}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the torque due to neutral beam
shinethrough and $\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the angular momentum
carried by neutral beam particles after they pass through the plasma without
ionization.

This vector quantity is the parent of component quantities such as the
[toroidal torque due to neutral beam
shinethrough](name:toroidal_torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough), which
is its toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. It excludes angular momentum deposited by absorbed neutral beam
particles and torques due to other momentum-transfer mechanisms.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is directed along the positive basis
direction of that component; the toroidal component is positive in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of torque carried away by neutral beam particles that
traverse the plasma without ionization, representing angular momentum not
transferred to the plasma.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal shinethrough torque is the component of angular-momentum loss
carried away by neutral beam particles that remain neutral while traversing
the plasma and exit without transferring their momentum to the plasma. It is
the toroidal component of the parent [torque due to neutral beam
shinethrough](name:torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough).

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{sh}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{sh}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the total shinethrough torque
vector and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity includes only
angular momentum carried away by non-ionized beam neutrals; it excludes
momentum deposited by neutrals that ionize and is distinct from local
[toroidal torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density) and [toroidal
neutral torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: total_co_passing_particle_density
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of a selected species on untrapped
orbits circulating with the plasma current, including thermal and nonthermal
particles; the corresponding local density is defined at each point before
averaging over its magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Total co-passing particle density is the number density contributed by
particles of a selected species whose untrapped guiding-center orbits
circulate in the direction of the plasma current. It includes thermal and
nonthermal particles and may be specified locally or as a flux-surface
average.

The local density is the velocity-space integral over this orbit class, and
its flux-surface average is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
n_{s,\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) &= \int_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \\
\bar n_{s,\mathrm{co}} &= \left\langle n_{s,\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $n_{s,\mathrm{co}}$ is the local co-passing number density, $\bar
n_{s,\mathrm{co}}$ is its flux-surface average, and $s$ labels the selected
species. The distribution function of species $s$ is $f_s$; $\mathbf{x}$ is
position; $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity; $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
volume element; and $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the
velocity-space region associated with untrapped orbits circulating with the
plasma current. The brackets denote a normalized average over the magnetic
flux surface through $\mathbf{x}$, and $\mathrm{FS}$ denotes that surface.

The local form applies at a spatial point, while the averaged form applies
over the magnetic flux surface through that point; the averaged form is not
a local point value. Thermal and nonthermal particles of the selected
species contribute additively, and the quantity is not summed over different
species. It excludes the [total counter-passing particle
density](name:total_counter_passing_particle_density) and [total trapped
particle density](name:total_trapped_particle_density), which describe
distinct orbit classes.

At matching local or flux-surface-averaged scope, [co-passing fast-particle
density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density) is the suprathermal
contribution included here. This co-passing orbit-class contribution is part
of [particle density](name:particle_density), which also includes other
particle populations.

NAMES.name: total_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Total pressure of electrons is the isotropic kinetic stress from their
combined bulk thermal and nonthermal populations.
NAMES.long:
Total pressure of electrons is the isotropic part of the kinetic pressure
tensor of the combined thermal and nonthermal electron populations. It
represents stress from random electron motion rather than bulk-flow momentum
flux and does not require an isotropic velocity distribution.

The total is defined by the additive population decomposition:

$$
p_e = p_{e,\mathrm{thermal}} + p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $p_e$ is the total electron pressure, $p_{e,\mathrm{thermal}}$ is the
bulk thermal-electron pressure, and $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
[fast-electron pressure](name:fast_electron_pressure), encompassing the
nonthermal contribution.

Both contributions must refer to the same plasma region and averaging
convention. For flux-surface-averaged core-plasma values, both are averaged
over the same magnetic flux surface. The aggregation is a direct sum, not a
density-weighted mean or a volume integral. It excludes ion pressure and
magnetic pressure and does not select a field-parallel or
field-perpendicular stress component.

This is the combined-population specialization of [electron
pressure](name:electron_pressure), whose broader definition also permits
thermal-only or suprathermal-only populations. It differs from either
population-specific pressure by explicitly including both contributions.

NAMES.name: total_electron_source_rate
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Total electron source rate is the net production or removal rate of free
electrons, summed over all contributing processes and integrated over the
entire plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Total electron source rate is the net rate at which free electrons are
produced or removed throughout the plasma volume. It is the global
particle-source contribution to electron-number balance.

The total rate is defined by

$$
S_e^{\mathrm{tot}} = \int_{\mathcal V_p} S_e^{\mathrm{vol}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $S_e^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total electron source rate, $\mathcal V_p$
is the entire plasma volume, $S_e^{\mathrm{vol}}$ is the [electron
volumetric source rate](name:electron_volumetric_source_rate) summed over
all contributing production and removal processes, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes
spatial position, and $dV$ is a physical volume element.

This quantity counts free electrons rather than electrons bound in atoms or
molecules. Positive values indicate net production and negative values
indicate net removal. It is a volume-integrated source, not a local
volumetric rate, a flux-surface average, or a particle transport flux
through the plasma boundary.

The [electron particle source rate inside a magnetic flux
surface](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_electron_particle_source_rate)
uses the same integral restricted to the enclosed volume; it equals this
total when that volume contains the entire plasma. Unlike [electron
deposited power](name:electron_deposited_power), this quantity describes
particle production or removal rather than energy transfer.

NAMES.name: total_fast_particle_count
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated number of suprathermal particles, combining all included
fast-particle species and superposed fast-particle distributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total number of nonthermal or suprathermal particles
represented by the included fast-particle distributions over the plasma
volume. It is an extensive particle-count measure, not a local density or a
count of numerical distribution markers.

$$
N_{\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V n_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the total fast-particle count, $V$ is the
plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
[fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density) summed over the included
fast-particle species and superposed distributions. The count excludes
particles belonging only to the thermal population and is related to the
volume-integrated [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy), which
weights the same population by kinetic energy.

NAMES.name: total_implicit_ion_particle_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total implicit ion particle source rate is the coefficient multiplying total
ion number density in the density-proportional contribution to its
particle-number source.
NAMES.long:
Total implicit ion particle source rate is the coefficient of the
density-proportional, implicit contribution to the total-ion particle-number
source. It multiplies total ion number density in the decomposed density
transport equation.

The source decomposition is defined by

$$
S_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = S_{i,\mathrm{exp}}^{\mathrm{tot}} + S_{i,\mathrm{imp}}^{\mathrm{tot}} n_i^{\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the net total-ion particle source per physical
volume, $S_{i,\mathrm{exp}}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its explicit contribution,
$S_{i,\mathrm{imp}}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is this implicit source coefficient, and
$n_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is total ion number density. The explicit contribution
is independent of the density being advanced within this decomposition; the
implicit contribution is the coefficient multiplied by that density.

Total ion number density is summed over all included ion species and ionic
charge states, counting ions without charge weighting and excluding
electrons and neutral particles. The coefficient acts on this aggregate
density; it is not itself the full volumetric source or a volume-integrated
particle production rate.

This quantity is the total-ion specialization of the [implicit ion particle
source rate](name:implicit_ion_particle_source_rate). In contrast, the
[implicit ion-state particle source
rate](name:implicit_ion_state_particle_source_rate) multiplies the density
of a specified ion state rather than the aggregate ion density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-proportional contribution adds
ions to the total ion population; negative values represent removal.

NAMES.name: total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to an ion charge
state by collisions, summing contributions from both thermal and fast ion
sub-populations.
NAMES.long:
Total Coulomb-collisional power transferred to ions of a specified species
and charge state, integrated over the plasma volume, aggregating
contributions from both the thermal and fast (non-Maxwellian)
sub-populations.

The total is the sum of its population-resolved components:

$$
P_{\rm coll}^{s,z} = P_{\rm th}^{s,z} + P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}
$$

where $P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$ is the [thermal ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions) and
$P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}$ is the [fast ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), with $s$
denoting the ion species and $z$ the resolved charge state.

This charge-state-resolved total is distinct from
[ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which
aggregates over all charge states and both sub-populations without
charge-state resolution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the specified ion charge state is a net
recipient of energy from Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state, integrated
over the plasma and including both the toroidal projection of the
thermal-ion contribution and the summed fast-ion contributions from
angular-momentum exchange with co-existing species.
NAMES.long:
Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state is the signed
toroidal collisional angular-momentum source for that charge state,
integrated over the plasma. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$
direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The total torque is the additive thermal-plus-fast scalar contribution:

$$
\tau^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
=
\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
+
\sum_f \tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies the charge state,
$\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is
the [thermal ion charge-state collisional
torque](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions),
$\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its
axial projection associated with toroidal angular momentum, $f$ indexes
fast-ion sub-populations, and
$\tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [toroidal fast ion
charge-state collisional
torque](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions) for
sub-population $f$.

Only torque due to Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange with co-existing
charged plasma species is included. This quantity is charge-state resolved,
not summed over charge states, and is distinct from the corresponding local
total ion charge-state collisional torque density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when collisions transfer toroidal angular momentum
to the specified ion charge state in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Charge-state-summed number density of all ion species at the internal
transport barrier, excluding neutral particles and charge weighting.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total local number density of all included ion
populations evaluated at the flux-surface location assigned to the internal
transport barrier. It is the aggregate specialization of
ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier, rather than the density of a
selected species or charge state.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{total}} = \sum_s \sum_Z n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state
$Z$, and both sums include every ion population in the defined ion
inventory. The summation counts particles without weighting by ionic charge;
neutral particles are excluded. This convention distinguishes the quantity
from charge-weighted descriptors such as
charge_at_internal_transport_barrier.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total ion number density at the magnetic axis, where the poloidal
magnetic-flux gradient vanishes, summed over all ion species and charge
states.
NAMES.long:
The total ion number density at the magnetic axis is the local number
density of all ion species, including every ionic charge state. The magnetic
axis is the innermost point of the nested closed flux surfaces, defined by a
vanishing gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux.

At the magnetic-axis position, the quantity is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) = \sum_s \sum_Z n_{s,Z}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}})
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density,
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position, $s$ indexes ion
species, and $Z$ indexes their ionic charge states.

This is the all-ion aggregate of ion density at magnetic axis; it excludes
electrons and neutral particles.

NAMES.name: total_ion_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective transport velocity relating the combined convective energy flux of
all ion species to their summed local transported energy density.
NAMES.long:
The total-ion energy convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient
multiplying the combined ion energy density to give the combined convective
ion energy flux. It is the all-ion aggregate specialization of [ion energy
convection velocity](name:ion_energy_convection_velocity), with the
transport-coefficient meaning of [energy convection
velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity).

For nonzero total transported ion energy density, its defining relation is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{i,W}=\frac{\sum_s\mathbf{Q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}}{\sum_s\mathcal{W}_s}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{i,W}$ is the total-ion energy convection velocity, $i$
denotes ions, $W$ labels the energy transport channel, $s$ indexes ion
species and their ionic charge states, $\mathbf{Q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is
each population's convective energy flux, and $\mathcal{W}_s$ is its
transported energy density.

Both sums include all ion species and all their ionic charge states.
Electron and neutral energy contributions are excluded, as is the
gradient-driven diffusive contribution to ion energy flux. Where
population-specific convection velocities are defined using their respective
energy densities, this coefficient is their energy-density-weighted mean,
not their arithmetic sum. It need not equal the [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity).

The [parallel total-ion energy convection
velocity](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity) is the
projection of this vector along the local magnetic field; the parent
quantity is not restricted to that direction or to a particular plasma
region.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a projected convective ion-energy flux points
along the positive projection direction: along the local magnetic field for
a parallel projection, and outward toward the last closed flux surface for a
flux-surface-normal projection.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective field-aligned velocity multiplying the energy density summed over
all ion species to give their combined parallel convective energy flux.
NAMES.long:
Field-parallel total-ion energy convection velocity is the effective
transport coefficient relating the combined ion population's parallel
convective energy flux to its transported energy density in the edge plasma.
It is the field-parallel projection of the [total-ion energy convection
velocity](name:total_ion_energy_convection_velocity).

The defining relation is:

$$
Q_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_i\,v_{i,W,\parallel}
$$

where $Q_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the combined ion convective
energy flux density along the local magnetic field, $\mathcal{W}_i$ is the
combined transported ion energy density, and $v_{i,W,\parallel}$ is this
effective convection velocity. The subscript $i$ denotes the combined ion
population, $W$ identifies the energy transport channel, and $\parallel$
denotes projection along the local magnetic field.

The energy density and convective flux are each summed over all ion species
and ionic charge states included in the total-ion energy equation; electron
and neutral contributions are excluded. The effective velocity is not a sum
of constituent velocities and need not equal the bulk ion flow velocity.
Gradient-driven diffusive energy flux is excluded from the defining
convective flux.

Unlike the [parallel ion energy convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_energy_convection_velocity) for an individual
ion population, this coefficient closes the summed ion energy equation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the convective transport is co-directed with
the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: total_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total ion energy flux is the local ion energy-flux-density vector carried by
all ion species and charge states, including conductive thermal-energy
transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport.
NAMES.long:
Total ion energy flux is the local energy-flux-density vector carried by all
ion species and charge states. It represents the rate at which the aggregate
ion energy reservoir crosses unit oriented area after projection onto the
surface normal, including conductive thermal-energy transport and convective
enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport when those contributions are in scope.

For a multi-species plasma, the aggregate vector
$\mathbf{Q}_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is defined as the sum of conductive and
convective species contributions:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{s \in \mathrm{ions}} \left(\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}\right)
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species and charge states,
$\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive heat-flux vector of species
$s$, and $\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy-flux vector
of species $s$. For an ideal monatomic ion fluid, the enthalpy part of
$\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is $(5/2)p_s\mathbf{v}_s$, where $p_s$ is
scalar pressure and $\mathbf{v}_s$ is mean flow velocity; bulk-kinetic
convection is included only when macroscopic flow energy belongs to the
selected ion energy reservoir.

As an extensive flux-density quantity, the aggregate is summed over all ion
species and over all charge states of each species; it is not a
density-weighted mean. It is local, not a flux-surface average or
area-integrated power. Projection onto an oriented surface normal gives a
scalar [ion_energy_flux](name:ion_energy_flux), and named aggregate
projections include
[radial_total_ion_energy_flux](name:radial_total_ion_energy_flux),
poloidal_total_ion_energy_flux, and
[parallel_total_ion_energy_flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux). The
quantity is distinct from
[total_thermal_ion_heat_flux](name:total_thermal_ion_heat_flux), which
restricts the transported reservoir to total ion thermal heat, and is an ion
contribution to [total_energy_flux](name:total_thermal_ion_heat_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a represented component of the vector carries
ion energy in the positive direction of its stated basis vector, projection
direction, or oriented surface normal.

NAMES.name: poloidal_total_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Poloidal total ion energy flux is the signed local energy-transfer rate per
area normal to the poloidal direction, summed over all ion species and ionic
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal total ion energy flux is the signed projection of the aggregate ion
energy-flux vector onto the local poloidal direction. It includes conductive
thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport
carried by ions.

The defining projection and aggregation are:

$$
\Gamma_{W,i,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}} = \sum_a\sum_z \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,a,z}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,i,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal total ion energy flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}$ is the [total ion energy-flux
vector](name:total_ion_energy_flux), and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,a,z}$ is
the energy-flux vector carried by ion species $a$ in ionic charge state $z$.
The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ points toward increasing
local poloidal angle $\theta$ in a constant-toroidal-angle plane. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The geometric sense of
increasing $\theta$ is set by the specified poloidal-angle convention.

The sum includes all ion species and all their ionic charge states, without
density weighting; electron and neutral energy fluxes are excluded. Each
species contribution, summed over its ionic charge states, is a [poloidal
ion energy flux](name:poloidal_ion_energy_flux). This quantity is a local
flux density, not a surface-integrated power or a flux-surface average. Its
geometric poloidal projection is distinct from the magnetic-field projection
defining [parallel total ion energy
flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when net ion energy is transported toward
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: radial_total_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces is the
flux-surface-averaged net energy transport per unit area and time, summed
over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces represents the net
transport of the aggregate ion energy reservoir through those surfaces. It
includes conductive thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or
bulk-kinetic transport.

The defining projection and averaging relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged outward ion
energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the local [total
ion energy-flux vector](name:total_ion_energy_flux), $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is
the outward unit normal to the magnetic flux surface, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a flux-surface average. The
labels $W$, $i$, and $\mathrm{tot}$ identify energy, ions, and the total ion
contribution, respectively.

The aggregation is a sum over all ion species and all ionic charge states,
not a density-weighted mean. Species-resolved [ion energy
flux](name:ion_energy_flux) and [ion charge-state energy
flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) provide contributions to this
total. Electron and neutral energy fluxes are excluded; the quantity is
neither a diffusion-only contribution nor a surface-integrated power.

The transport direction here is the outward magnetic-flux-surface normal,
not the cylindrical major-radius direction. In the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height; the direction of increasing $R$ is not generally normal
to a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when ion energy crosses the magnetic flux surface
outward toward the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: total_ion_particle_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total ion particle source rate is the net ion addition or removal integrated
over a plasma volume, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Total ion particle source rate is the net rate of ion production or loss,
summed over all ion species and ionic charge states and integrated over a
specified plasma volume. Its global value covers the entire plasma volume
and supplies the source contribution to the total-ion particle-number
balance.

The integrated net rate is defined by

$$
S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}(V)=\int_V\sum_a\sum_{q\geq 1}\left(S_{a,q}^{+}-S_{a,q}^{-}\right)\,dV
$$

where $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}(V)$ is the total ion particle source rate in the
integration region $V$, $a$ indexes ion species, $q$ is the positive ionic
charge number, $S_{a,q}^{+}$ and $S_{a,q}^{-}$ are the local volumetric ion
production and removal rates for that species and charge state, and $dV$ is
a physical volume element. The local rates combine all contributing source
and sink processes.

Each ion is counted once, without charge weighting; neutral particles are
excluded from the ion count. Transitions between included ionic charge
states cancel in the total, whereas conversion between neutral and ionized
populations changes the ion count. Positive values indicate net ion addition
and negative values indicate net removal. This is a particle-number source,
not an electric-charge source or the full inventory change, which also
includes transport across the integration boundary.

This quantity is the species-summed, volume-integrated specialization of
[ion particle source rate](name:ion_particle_source_rate). The [cumulative
inside-flux-surface total ion particle source
rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_total_ion_particle_source_rate)
restricts the integration region to the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux
surface; it recovers the global value when that region encompasses the
entire plasma volume.

sources.parent_definition: Total source quantities integrated over the plasma volume or surface

NAMES.name: total_ion_particle_volumetric_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total ion particle volumetric source rate is the net local production or
removal of ions per physical volume, summed over all ion species and ionic
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Total ion particle volumetric source rate is the net local rate at which a
source contribution adds or removes ion particles per physical volume. It
contributes to the source term in the total ion number-density continuity
equation.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_i = \sum_s \sum_q \left(S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{gain}}-S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{loss}}\right)
$$

where $S_i$ is the total ion particle volumetric source rate, $s$ labels ion
species, $q$ labels ionic charge states, and $S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{gain}}$ and
$S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{loss}}$ are the local volumetric rates of particle
addition and removal for that species and charge state. The sums include all
ion species and all their ionic charge states, excluding neutral states.

The rate includes ionization, recombination, and particle exchange processes
represented by the specified source contribution. Positive values indicate
net ion gain; negative values indicate net ion loss. Transitions between
ionic charge states cancel in the total when both states are included,
whereas transitions between neutral and ionic states can change the total
ion count. This is a particle-number source, not a charge-weighted source or
the density change caused by transport-flux divergence; electron and neutral
inventories are excluded.

Its integral over the considered plasma volume gives the [total ion particle
source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate). Thus, “total” here
denotes summation over ion species and ionic charge states, not volume
integration or mandatory aggregation over independent source contributions.

NAMES.name: total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
total-momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of total bulk-flow
momentum. The transported momentum density is the aggregate total, not an
unspecified or single-population momentum channel.
NAMES.long:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
total-momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of total bulk-flow
momentum. This parent fixes the transported channel to total momentum: the
momentum density is the population-summed aggregate of the constituent
bulk-flow momentum densities included in the total-momentum balance, rather
than an unspecified or single-population channel. Each component is a
kinematic diagonal coefficient for one named transport direction, not a full
viscosity tensor.

For component $\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ associated with coordinate $x_i$
along direction $\hat{e}_i$, the diagonal diffusive closure for total
momentum-density component $M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is

$$
\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff,tot}} = -\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\,\frac{\partial M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial x_i}\qquad\text{(no summation over }i\text{)}
$$

where $\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff,tot}}$ is the diffusive flux in direction
$\hat{e}_i$ of the $j$ component of total bulk-flow momentum,
$\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the directional total momentum diffusion
coefficient, $M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the $j$ component of total bulk-flow
momentum density, $x_i$ is distance along $\hat{e}_i$, $i$ indexes the named
transport direction, and $j$ indexes the momentum component. The minus sign
defines the down-gradient diffusive contribution for a positive coefficient.

The component basis must be explicit. A radial component is the $\hat{R}$
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from
the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed
from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is
the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel,
perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are
separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward
increasing flux label.

This name is the total-momentum specialization of the [momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and is the semantic parent
of direction-qualified components such as the [poloidal total momentum
diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).
It is distinct from species- or population-qualified coefficients such as
the [ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and [neutral momentum
diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and it
is not the arithmetic sum of those coefficients; it relates the diffusive
flux of aggregate total momentum to the gradient of aggregate total momentum
density.

NAMES.name: poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient multiplying the poloidal gradient in diffusive
transport of total bulk-flow momentum within the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective diffusivity governing diffusive transport of
the aggregate bulk-flow momentum in the local poloidal direction within the
edge plasma.

Its relation to the directional momentum-diffusivity tensor is

$$
D_{\mathrm{pol}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}} \cdot \mathbf D_{\mathrm{mom}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $D_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal diffusion coefficient,
$\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local unit vector in the poloidal
direction, and $\mathbf D_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is the effective diffusivity
tensor for total bulk-flow momentum; the dot products denote tensor
contraction.

The total designation means that this coefficient applies to the aggregate
momentum balance without selecting an ion species, ion charge state, or
neutral state. It is restricted to the poloidal transport direction and the
edge-plasma region; it does not represent a species-resolved coefficient or
a coefficient for another transport direction.

This quantity is the poloidal component of the directional coefficient
vector represented by [total momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). It is distinct from
[poloidal ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), which
applies only to ion momentum transport, and from [poloidal neutral-state
momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_diffusivity),
which applies only to neutral-state momentum transport.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Momentum effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: total_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian coefficient relating the diffusive flux of total momentum
to its local momentum-density gradient without selecting a directional
component.
NAMES.long:
Total momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the
diffusive flux of aggregated momentum and the negative local gradient of
aggregated momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for momentum
transport.

For each resolved transport direction, the componentwise closure is

$$
\Gamma_{m,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}\left(\sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,i}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of total momentum
component $i$, $D_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the corresponding total momentum
diffusivity component, $x_i$ is the spatial coordinate in direction $i$, $s$
indexes the momentum-carrying populations included in the total, $m_s$ is
the particle mass of population $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, and
$v_{s,i}$ is its velocity component in direction $i$.

The total aggregation sums the momentum contributions of all populations and
charge states included in the physical definition rather than selecting one
species, charge state, or process. The quantity remains direction-general
and vector-valued; no single toroidal, radial, parallel, or other projection
is selected at this level.

This quantity is the total-momentum specialization of [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity), retaining its Fick's-law transport
meaning while fixing the population aggregation. The [toroidal total
momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_total_momentum_diffusivity) is the
directional specialization obtained by selecting the toroidal component of
this vector.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian coefficient relating the diffusive flux of aggregated
toroidal momentum to its local toroidal momentum-density gradient.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the effective Fickian transport coefficient for the
diffusive part of the total toroidal-momentum flux. It applies to the
toroidal momentum component in the total momentum balance, not to a toroidal
transport direction.

For an outward flux-surface-normal coordinate $\ell$, the local diffusive
closure is:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi,\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}\,\frac{\partial M_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\phi,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the outward diffusive flux density of
total toroidal momentum, $D_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}$ is this effective
diffusivity, $M_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the aggregated toroidal momentum
density, and $\ell$ is distance in the outward flux-surface-normal
direction. The minus sign specifies down-gradient diffusive transport.

The aggregation is over the momentum contributions represented in the total
momentum balance. This quantity excludes convective transport and the total
momentum flux itself; it is a coefficient multiplying the gradient of
toroidal momentum rather than a flux or velocity.

It is the toroidal component specialization of [total momentum
diffusivity](name:total_momentum_diffusivity). The corresponding poloidal
specialization, [poloidal total momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), applies
the same Fickian closure to the poloidal momentum component.

NAMES.name: total_momentum_source
NAMES.short:
Directed rate of momentum transfer to or from all included particle
populations, represented as an area-normalized vector source density.
NAMES.long:
A momentum source density represents the directed transfer of momentum
caused by physical processes acting on a plasma population or one of its
resolved states. The total quantity retains the vector direction of the net
momentum-transfer rate while aggregating the included particle populations.

The aggregate source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{p} = \sum_s \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src},s}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{p}$ is the total momentum source density,
$\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src},s}$ is the momentum transferred by source
processes to or from population $s$, and $A$ is the surface over which the
source is normalized. The sum includes only the particle populations
specified by the physical scope of the quantity. Directional projections,
such as [radial total momentum source](name:radial_total_momentum_source),
are components of this vector quantity, while [momentum
source](name:momentum_source) provides the broader family context.

NAMES.name: radial_total_momentum_source
NAMES.short:
Signed rate of momentum input or removal per unit area in the major-radius
direction, summed over all included particle populations.
NAMES.long:
The radial total momentum source is the major-radius component of the net
momentum-transfer rate per unit area supplied to or removed from all
included particle populations. It is a directional projection of the [total
momentum source](name:total_momentum_source), not a coordinate locating the
momentum.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, this
projection is defined by:

$$
S_R = \mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{tot}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $S_R$ is the radial total momentum source, $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{tot}}$
is the total momentum-source vector, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward
increasing distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.

The total is the algebraic sum of contributions from all included particle
populations, not a sum of their magnitudes. The source is area-normalized
rather than a volumetric force density. The major-radius direction is not
generally normal to a magnetic flux surface; the [toroidal momentum
source](name:toroidal_momentum_source) instead resolves momentum transfer
along the toroidal direction.

This quantity describes gain or loss of [momentum](name:momentum) through
source processes. It is distinct from [total momentum
flux](name:total_momentum_flux), which describes momentum transported across
an oriented surface.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net source adds momentum in the direction
of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: total_neutral_internal_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Kinetic pressure of all neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or
excitation state, combining thermal and nonthermal fast-neutral
contributions.
NAMES.long:
The total neutral internal state pressure is the kinetic pressure associated
with all neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or excitation
state, combining thermal and nonthermal fast-neutral contributions. It is
the total-contribution specialization of [neutral internal state
pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure).

For the aggregate velocity distribution in state $s$, the scalar pressure is
one-third of the pressure-tensor trace:

$$
p_s^{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{1}{3}\int m_n \lvert\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_s\rvert^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral-particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$\mathbf{u}_s$ is the aggregate mean velocity, and $f_s$ is the distribution
of all neutral particles in state $s$. Subtracting the mean flow excludes
common bulk-flow dynamic pressure. Unlike [thermal neutral internal state
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this quantity
includes nonthermal fast-neutral contributions and does not require an
isotropic Maxwellian distribution. It remains restricted to the specified
internal state and therefore differs from [total neutral
pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure), which aggregates over internal
states.

NAMES.name: total_neutral_number_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Total neutral number density is the local abundance per physical volume of
one selected neutral species, combining thermal and nonthermal populations
summed over all charge states. It counts particles rather than weighting
them by charge, mass, or energy.
NAMES.long:
Total neutral number density is the local abundance per physical volume of
one selected neutral species, combining its thermal and nonthermal particle
populations. It counts particles rather than weighting them by charge, mass,
or energy.

For species $s$ at position $\mathbf{r}$, the total is:

$$
n_s^0(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_q \left[n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}^0(\mathbf{r}) + n_{s,q,\mathrm{nth}}^0(\mathbf{r})\right]
$$

where $n_s^0$ is the total neutral number density, $s$ labels the selected
neutral species, the superscript $0$ identifies the neutral population,
$\mathbf{r}$ is spatial position, and $q$ labels charge state. The terms
$n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}^0$ and $n_{s,q,\mathrm{nth}}^0$ are the thermal and
nonthermal number-density contributions, respectively, for species $s$ and
charge state $q$.

The quantity is local at a plasma position, including core and edge or
scrape-off-layer regions as applicable; it is not integrated or averaged
over a spatial region. It applies to one selected species: thermal and
nonthermal contributions are summed over all charge states, but distinct
species are not combined. It is not a charge-, mass-, or energy-weighted
density.

The [fast neutral internal-state number
density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density) is narrower,
applying to fast neutral particles in one specified internal state rather
than defining the full thermal-plus-nonthermal, charge-state-summed
quantity. The [total ion number density](name:total_ion_number_density) is
the corresponding total particle number density for an ion species.
