NAMES.name: total_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Total pressure of a neutral species combines its thermal and nonthermal
pressure contributions, summed over charge states when multiple states are
represented. It applies to neutral populations in the core and edge plasma,
including the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Total pressure of a neutral species combines the pressure contributions from
its thermal and nonthermal neutral populations. It denotes their total
pressure rather than either contribution alone.

The total pressure is the additive combination of the thermal and nonthermal
contributions:

$$
p_0 = p_{0,\mathrm{th}} + p_{0,\mathrm{nt}}
$$

where $p_0$ is the total pressure of the neutral species,
$p_{0,\mathrm{th}}$ is its [thermal neutral
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure), and $p_{0,\mathrm{nt}}$ is its
nonthermal pressure contribution, represented by [fast neutral
pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure). The subscript $0$ identifies neutral
particles; $\mathrm{th}$ and $\mathrm{nt}$ identify the thermal and
nonthermal contributions.

This species-level quantity applies to neutral populations in the core and
edge plasma, including the scrape-off layer. When multiple charge states are
represented, their pressure contributions are summed over all represented
charge states, not averaged. It includes both thermal and nonthermal
contributions, unlike the thermal-only pressure, and is not restricted to a
single internal state; the [total neutral internal-state
pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) resolves pressure by
internal state.

NAMES.name: total_particle_count
NAMES.short:
Total number of particles in the kinetic distribution, obtained by
integrating the distribution function over velocity space and the entire
plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The total particle count is the global normalization integral of the
particle distribution function $f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v})$: it quantifies
the total number of particles of the described species present in the plasma
at a given instant, summed over all spatial positions within the plasma
volume and all velocities in phase space. Being a pure count, it is
dimensionless.

The quantity is defined by the phase-space integral

$$
N = \int_V \int f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v \, d^3x
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector, and
$\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity. In marker-based kinetic simulations,
$N$ reduces to the weighted sum over all simulation markers.

Monitoring $N$ over time provides a particle-conservation diagnostic in
kinetic modeling: systematic drift from the initial value indicates
numerical particle sources or losses. This quantity is closely related to
total_count, which carries the same physical meaning with a less
species-explicit name, and contrasts with
[fast_count](name:total_fast_particle_count), which integrates only over the
non-thermal sub-population of the distribution. The local spatial
counterpart is total_particle_density, whose volume integral recovers $N$.

sources.leaf_definition: Number of particles in the distribution, i.e. the volume integral of the density (note: this is the number of real particles and not markers)
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities (integrated over plasma volume for moments of the distribution, collisional exchange and source terms), for various time slices

NAMES.name: total_particle_source_rate_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
NAMES.short:
Global rate of neutral-beam particles that traverse the plasma without
absorption, representing particle loss from the beam injection source.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the global particle loss rate caused by neutral-beam
shinethrough: injected beam neutrals that pass through the plasma without
being absorbed. It is an all-particle aggregate and represents loss from the
injected beam rather than particle creation within the plasma.

The rate is defined by integrating the local shinethrough loss-rate density
over the plasma volume:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{sh}} = \int_V S_{\mathrm{sh}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the total shinethrough particle loss rate,
$S_{\mathrm{sh}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local rate density of beam particles
not absorbed, $V$ is the plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ is position. It is
a loss magnitude, not the net balance of all plasma particle sources and
sinks. The aggregation is analogous to the global quantity [total ion
particle source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate), but the present
rate is attributed specifically to neutral-beam shinethrough.

NAMES.name: total_runaway_electron_current
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short:
Total runaway-electron current is the electric-current vector carried by the
runaway-electron population, defined component by component by integrating
the corresponding runaway-electron current-density component over a poloidal
cross-section. It represents conventional current, not runaway-electron
particle flux.
NAMES.long:
Total runaway-electron current is the electric-current vector carried by the
runaway-electron population, defined component by component by integrating
the corresponding runaway-electron current-density component over a poloidal
cross-section. It is the conventional electric current associated with
runaway electrons, not the runaway-electron particle flux or momentum.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis
associated with coordinates $(R,\phi,Z)$, with $R$ major radius, $\phi$
toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side,
and $Z$ vertical height, the component definition is:

$$
I_{\mathrm{RE},a} = \int_{S_p} j_{\mathrm{RE},a}\, dA,\qquad a\in\{R,\phi,Z\}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RE},a}$ is the component of the total runaway-electron
current, $j_{\mathrm{RE},a}$ is the corresponding component of the
runaway-electron current-density vector, $S_p$ is a poloidal cross-section
at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$, and $dA$ is its area element.

This quantity denotes the component-general vector, not only the toroidal
projection. The [toroidal total runaway-electron
current](name:toroidal_total_runaway_electron_current) is the $\hat{\phi}$
component specialization obtained by the same cross-sectional component
integral in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$
basis.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a component is aligned with the corresponding
positive basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi},
\hat{Z})$ basis; the toroidal component is positive for conventional current
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_runaway_electron_current
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short:
Total toroidal runaway-electron current is the signed charge-flow rate
carried by the entire runaway-electron population through the full poloidal
plasma cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Total toroidal runaway-electron current is the net conventional electric
current carried by runaway electrons through the full poloidal plasma
cross-section. It is the toroidal component of [total runaway-electron
current](name:total_runaway_electron_current).

The current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{RE},\phi} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{pol}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\, dS
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RE},\phi}$ is the total toroidal runaway-electron current,
$S_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the full plasma cross-section at fixed toroidal angle,
$dS$ is its area element, and $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the
[runaway-electron current density](name:runaway_electron_current_density).
The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The integral includes the entire runaway-electron population and retains
cancelation between oppositely directed current contributions.
Thermal-electron and ion currents are excluded. This is conventional charge
current, not an unsigned particle rate; because electrons carry negative
charge, its direction is opposite their net toroidal motion. The geometric
toroidal projection is distinct from the field-aligned projection
represented locally by [parallel runaway-electron current
density](name:parallel_runaway_electron_current_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the runaway-electron conventional current
flows toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed
from above the positive $Z$ axis.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Number density of thermal ions summed over all ion species and positive
charge states, excluding fast ions and neutral particles.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ion

The species-and-charge-state sum is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{th},\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{q\geq 1} n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{th},\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total thermal ion number
density, $i$ identifies the ion population, $s$ labels an ion species, $q$
is its positive integer charge state, and $n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}$ is the
thermal number density of that species in that charge state.

The definition applies in confined plasma and the scrape-off layer. The
total denotes aggregation over species and charge states, not spatial
integration; no spatial averaging is implied. Neutral particles and
nonthermal ions are excluded, including the population described by [fast
ion density](name:fast_ion_density).

This quantity is the sum of the species-specific [thermal ion
densities](name:thermal_ion_density), rather than the density of one
selected species. It differs from [line-averaged total ion
density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density), which averages along a
specified chord and includes both thermal and nonthermal ions.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated internal energy of the complete thermal-ion ensemble,
obtained from its total isotropic pressure and excluding fast or
suprathermal ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the internal energy stored in the random thermal motion of
all confined thermal ions, summed over every ion species and charge state.
It is the complete-population specialization of thermal_ion_energy.

Its defining relation is

$$
U_i = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\rm pl}} p_i(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $U_i$ is the total thermal-ion energy, $p_i(\mathbf{r})$ is the total
isotropic thermal-ion pressure, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $dV$ is the volume
element, and $V_{\rm pl}$ is the confined plasma volume. The pressure is
summed over all thermal ion species and charge states, consistent with
[total_thermal_ion_pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure). Fast,
suprathermal, and other nonthermal ion populations are excluded.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Thermal ion plasma energy content (sum over the ion species) = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the thermal ion pressure

NAMES.name: total_trapped_particle_density
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of a selected species on magnetically
trapped orbits, including both thermal and nonthermal particles.
NAMES.long:
Total trapped-particle density is the flux-surface-averaged concentration of
a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits. These
orbits undergo magnetic mirror reflection, reversing their motion parallel
to the magnetic field rather than circulating as passing orbits.

The flux-surface-averaged density is defined by

$$
\langle n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}\rangle = \left\langle \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $s$ labels the selected species, $n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}$ is its local
trapped-particle number density, and $f_s$ is its full
thermal-plus-nonthermal velocity distribution. The vectors $\mathbf{x}$ and
$\mathbf{v}$ denote position and particle velocity,
$\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain
corresponding to trapped orbits at that position, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. Angle brackets denote the
differential-volume-weighted average over a magnetic flux surface.

The total includes both thermal and nonthermal trapped particles of the
selected species; it does not sum over different species. Passing particles
are excluded. This quantity is a flux-surface average, not a local density
or a volume-integrated particle count.

It equals the sum of the thermal trapped-particle contribution and the
nonthermal contribution represented by [trapped fast-particle
density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density), with both contributions
averaged over the same magnetic flux surface.

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Collisional torque density for trapped fast ions is the local vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions with
background plasma species.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density for trapped fast ions is the local source density
of angular momentum transferred to or from the trapped fast-ion population
by Coulomb collisions. It retains the full torque-density vector rather than
selecting a single directional component.

The torque-density vector is defined from the collisional force density as

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast,trapped}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast,trapped}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the torque reference
origin and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast,trapped}}$ is the
collisional force density transferred to the trapped fast-ion population.
Its components are represented in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The quantity is restricted to trapped fast-ion orbits and excludes torque
from noncollisional mechanisms. The unrestricted [fast-ion torque density
due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) provides
the broader parent quantity, while [toroidal trapped fast-ion torque density
due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is its toroidal component. The related [toroidal fast-ion torque density due
to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
selects the toroidal component without the trapped-orbit restriction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the relevant torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis vector of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque density transferred to
trapped fast ions, measuring angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry
axis.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the angular-momentum transfer
rate per unit plasma volume delivered to trapped fast ions by Coulomb
collisions with background plasma species. It resolves the parent trapped
fast-ion collisional torque density specifically about the toroidal symmetry
axis.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density
vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and
$\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its scalar component. The vectors are
expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$
frame, with $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ and
$\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ represented in N.m$^{-2}$.

Only the trapped fast-ion population and Coulomb-collision contribution are
included; other orbit classes, ion populations, and collision-independent
torque sources are excluded.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the collisional angular-momentum transfer to
trapped fast ions points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$.

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_particle_density
NAMES.short:
Trapped fast-particle density is the number density of nonthermal particles
of a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits, whose
parallel motion reverses at magnetic mirror points. It may be specified
locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-particle density is the number density of nonthermal particles
of a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits. These
orbits reverse their motion parallel to the magnetic field at mirror points.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, the local density is the zeroth velocity-space
moment of the fast-particle distribution restricted to trapped orbits:

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{\mathcal{V}_{s,\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_s$ is the trapped fast-particle density of species $s$, $s$ labels
the selected species, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle velocity distribution
of species $s$, $\mathcal{V}_{s,\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the
velocity-space region for trapped guiding-center orbits at $\mathbf{x}$, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity applies to nonthermal particles of one selected species,
without implicitly combining different species. It may be expressed as a
local density, which can vary over a magnetic flux surface, or as the
average of that local density over the surface.

Thermal particles and fast particles on passing orbits are excluded. In
particular, co-passing and counter-passing fast-particle populations are
distinct from the trapped population.

This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-particle
density](name:fast_particle_density); [co-passing fast-particle
density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density) and [counter-passing
fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density) describe
distinct passing orbit classes. It is the nonthermal component of [total
trapped-particle density](name:total_trapped_particle_density), which also
includes thermal particles.

NAMES.name: trapped_power_density
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for the trapped orbit
population, representing energy transfer to or from magnetically bouncing
particles.
NAMES.long:
Trapped power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which energy is
transferred to or from the trapped orbit population per unit physical
volume. It is the orbit-class specialization of power density for particles
whose parallel motion reverses at magnetic mirror points, so their
guiding-center orbits bounce rather than circulate toroidally.

For a magnetic flux surface, the flux-surface-averaged trapped power density
is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{tr}} = \left\langle \frac{dE_{\mathrm{tr}}}{dt\,dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped power density, $E_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is
the energy transferred to the trapped orbit population, $t$ is time, $V$ is
physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a
flux-surface average over that magnetic flux surface.

The scope is the trapped part of the particle distribution, with
contributions from applicable heating and collisional energy-transfer
processes. The aggregation convention is a net source term over those
processes for the trapped orbit population on the flux surface; it is not a
diagnostic-specific estimate, a point value before flux-surface averaging,
or a total stored energy.

It excludes passing-orbit populations: [co-passing power
density](name:co_passing_power_density) resolves particles circulating in
the co-current direction, and [counter-passing power
density](name:counter_passing_power_density) resolves particles circulating
opposite to that direction. Together, trapped, co-passing, and
counter-passing orbit-class power densities partition the orbit-resolved
contribution to net plasma power density when defined for the same particle
population and energy channels.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when energy is transferred to the trapped orbit
population.

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Trapped thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local
angular-momentum transfer rate to the trapped part of the bulk thermal
electron population from Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local rate
per unit volume at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum to
the bulk, near-Maxwellian thermal electron population, restricted to the
trapped receiving orbit class.

The vector torque density is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,trap}} = \frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,trap}}}{dV\,dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{L}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,trap}}$ is the angular
momentum transferred to trapped thermal electrons by Coulomb collisions, $V$
is physical volume, and $t$ is time.

This quantity is the trapped-orbit contribution to [thermal electron torque
density due to
collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The
trapped qualifier identifies the receiving thermal-electron orbit class and
does not restrict the collision partner. It excludes non-Coulomb mechanisms
and torque deposited in non-thermal or non-electron populations. No single
directional component is selected; its toroidal projection is [toroidal
trapped thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
with components resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume
from trapped nonthermal particles to thermal ions of one specified species
and charge state.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density is the
flux-surface-averaged rate of kinetic-energy transfer from trapped fast or
non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions of one specified species and charge
state. Trapped guiding-center trajectories undergo magnetic-mirror
reflection rather than continuous passing transit. The trapped restriction
applies to the donating distribution, not to the orbits of the receiving
thermal ions.

The contribution is the flux-surface average of the receiving population's
kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{i q,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\rho) = \left\langle \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_{i q}v^2 C_{i q,a}\!\left[f_{i q}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}\right] \, d^3v \right\rangle_\rho
$$

where $P_{i q,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this collisional power
density, $\rho$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $i$ identifies the
receiving ion species, $q$ is its specified ionic charge number, and $m_{i
q}$ is the receiving ion mass. The vector $\mathbf{v}$ is the receiving ion
velocity, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
integration measure. The distribution $f_{i q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes the
receiving thermal ions, while $f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped part of the
nonthermal donor distribution for species $a$. The operator $C_{i q,a}$
gives the collisional time derivative of the receiving distribution due to
that donor species. Brackets denote the normalized flux-surface average,
equivalently the limiting volume average over an infinitesimally thin shell
surrounding the surface.

The donor sum includes the nonthermal species represented in the collisional
exchange; the receiving contribution is restricted to one species and charge
state and is not summed over charge states. This is an energy-exchange
source or sink, not stored kinetic-energy density or energy transfer through
ionization or internal-state transitions.

Adding the
[co-passing](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and
[counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
contributions to this trapped contribution recovers the flux-surface average
of the [thermal-ion charge-state collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions),
which includes all donor orbit classes.

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Trapped collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per plasma volume to a specified thermal ion charge state from
Coulomb collisions with trapped particles.
NAMES.long:
Trapped collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state
from Coulomb collisions with the trapped population.

With $\mathrm{tr}$ denoting the trapped population and $z$ denoting the
selected thermal ion charge state, the torque-density vector is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped
collisional torque-density vector delivered to charge state $z$,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the angular-momentum origin to the
local plasma point, and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},z}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the
collisional force density transferred to that charge state by Coulomb
collisions with trapped particles.

This quantity is charge-state resolved and orbit-class resolved: it applies
to the selected thermal ion charge state and includes only the
trapped-population contribution to the collisional angular-momentum source.
It excludes co-passing- and counter-passing-population contributions, torque
densities summed over charge states, noncollisional momentum sources, and
the collisional force density before multiplication by the lever arm.

The sum of the trapped, [co-passing collisional torque
density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and [counter-passing collisional torque
density](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
contributions gives the corresponding orbit-class-summed [collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) for
the same thermal ion charge state when these populations form the orbit
partition.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of the torque-density
vector is aligned with the positive orientation of the corresponding basis
direction or angular-momentum axis; for toroidal angular momentum in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, positive is in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb
collisions to trapped thermal ions in a specified charge state, projected in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the collisional torque-density
vector delivered to trapped thermal ions in a specified ionic charge state.
It represents angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb
collisions with background charged species.

The toroidal projection is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}}$ is the
trapped thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density, $q$ identifies
the ionic charge state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity retains only the toroidal projection and remains resolved in
ion charge state; it excludes torque transferred to passing or other ion
populations and contributions attributed to noncollisional processes. The
charge-state-aggregated counterpart is [toroidal trapped thermal ion torque
density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from trapped fast
particles to thermal ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed volumetric rate
of kinetic-energy transfer from trapped fast or non-Maxwellian particles to
thermal ions, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. Trapped particles
execute guiding-center bounce orbits rather than complete passing transits.
The trapped-orbit restriction applies to the source distribution, not to the
recipient thermal ions.

For source species $a$ and recipient ion species $i$, the exchange is
defined by the recipient kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision
operator:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iq,a}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}](\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the trapped-source thermal-ion
collisional power density, $q$ labels the recipient ionic charge states,
$m_i$ is the recipient ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is recipient velocity, and $v$
is its magnitude. The distribution $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes thermal
ions of species $i$ in charge state $q$, while $f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the
trapped part of the source-species distribution. The operator $C_{iq,a}$
gives the collisional time derivative of the recipient distribution due to
that trapped source. The integral covers all recipient velocities; angle
brackets denote the volume-weighted average over an infinitesimally thin
shell between neighboring magnetic flux surfaces.

The quantity applies to one specified recipient ion species and is summed
over all its ionic charge states, not over different ion species. Retaining
one charge-state contribution gives the corresponding [trapped thermal-ion
charge-state collisional power
density](name:trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).
It is an energy source or sink for the thermal recipient population, not its
stored kinetic-energy density, the source particles' energy-loss rate, or a
volume-integrated power.

Together with the [co-passing
contribution](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and the corresponding counter-passing contribution, it forms the orbit-class
decomposition of the flux-surface average of [thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), provided the
same source distribution and recipient species are used throughout.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic
energy from the trapped source population to the thermal ions; negative when
the net transfer is reversed.

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population
per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, restricted to trapped-orbit
contributions and without restricting spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per
unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal-ion population by Coulomb
collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is restricted
to the trapped orbit-class contribution and is not restricted to a single
spatial direction.

For the trapped part of the selected thermal-ion population, the collisional
torque-density vector is defined from its distribution function by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{tr,coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{\mathcal{T}} d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the
ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the thermal-ion
distribution function, $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its Coulomb-collision
operator, and $\mathcal{T}$ is the trapped-orbit region of velocity space.

At parent level, the quantity includes the allowed spatial-direction
components within the trapped orbit class; [toroidal trapped thermal-ion
torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is the corresponding component along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes passing-orbit contributions
and torque deposited in fast-ion populations.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short:
Trapped thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the trapped orbit class.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the trapped orbit class.
Trapped particles are those whose parallel velocity reverses along a
magnetic field line and therefore undergo bounce motion between mirror
points.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{n,\mathrm{in,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}-S_{n,\mathrm{out,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the trapped thermal particle
source rate, $S_{n,\mathrm{in,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local rate of
thermal particles entering the trapped orbit class,
$S_{n,\mathrm{out,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local rate leaving it, $\psi$
is the magnetic-flux surface label, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes
a flux-surface average.

This quantity applies only to the thermal population and the trapped orbit
class. It is averaged over each magnetic flux surface and combines all
contributing particle source and sink processes; positive values represent
net entry into the trapped class, while negative values represent net
removal. It excludes co-passing and counter-passing particles.

It is the trapped-orbit contribution to the aggregate [thermal particle
source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), which combines the source
rates of the thermal orbit populations. It is complementary to the
[co-passing thermal particle source
rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) and [counter-passing
thermal particle source
rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), which describe the
two passing orbit classes.

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particle density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: trapped_torque_density
NAMES.short:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for magnetically trapped
particles, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
NAMES.long:
Torque density for magnetically trapped particles is the net
angular-momentum transfer rate to the trapped-particle population per unit
volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than
selecting a toroidal component or combining the trapped contribution with
passing-particle contributions.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{trap}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0} \frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{trap}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the torque-density vector for
magnetically trapped particles, $\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the
angular momentum transferred to the magnetically trapped population, $\Delta
V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.

This is the trapped-particle contribution to the broader [torque
density](name:torque_density); it excludes co-passing, counter-passing, and
population-unresolved torque contributions. The [toroidal trapped torque
density](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density) is its toroidal component.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_torque_density
NAMES.short:
Toroidal trapped torque density is the local rate of change of toroidal
angular momentum per physical volume, about the symmetry axis, due to
magnetically trapped particles. It equals the major-radius lever arm times
their toroidal force density in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal trapped torque density is the local rate of change of toroidal
angular momentum per physical volume, about the symmetry axis, due to
magnetically trapped particles. It is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation to the local toroidal force density of the trapped
population is:

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}} = R f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the toroidal trapped torque density,
$R$ is the major-radius lever arm measured from the symmetry axis, and
$f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the toroidal component of the trapped-particle
force density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The trapped population consists of particles whose pitch and magnetic
mirroring cause bounce motion between turning points rather than a full
poloidal transit. This quantity excludes the passing-particle contributions
represented by
[toroidal_co_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density)
and
[toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density);
when the same distribution is partitioned by orbit class, the trapped,
co-passing, and counter-passing contributions sum to the corresponding
[toroidal_torque_density](name:toroidal_torque_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the trapped-particle toroidal force density
is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of toroidal angular momentum density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short:
Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated by the Lorentz force,
averaged over a magnetic flux surface for trapped particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged torque density transferred to
trapped particles by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with their
current contribution. Trapped particles are the orbit population whose
guiding-center parallel motion is confined between magnetic-mirror bounce
points rather than circulating as a passing orbit.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{tr}}(\psi)=\left\langle\mathbf{r}\times\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}\times\mathbf{B}\right)\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the torque-density
vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin,
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the current-density contribution associated
with trapped particles, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $\psi$
labels the magnetic flux surface. The angle brackets denote a flux-surface
average.

This orbit-resolved vector is a member of the [torque density due to J×B
force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) family. Its toroidal
projection is represented by [toroidal trapped torque density due to J×B
force](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).
Passing-orbit quantities such as [co-passing torque density due to J×B
force](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and
[counter-passing torque density due to J×B
force](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) describe
different orbit populations and are not specializations of this trapped
quantity.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved torque component points in the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of tritium ions at the internal transport barrier,
the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent
transport permits steep radial fuel-ion density gradients to form.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of tritium ions at the internal transport barrier is
the local number density of tritium ions on the flux surface selected as the
barrier reference location. The internal transport barrier is a
confined-plasma region where effective cross-field transport is locally
reduced, allowing steep density gradients to form and persist.

The local tritium-ion density $n_T$ at the ITB reference surface is the
zeroth velocity moment of the charge-state-resolved distribution functions:

$$
n_T(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_Z \int f_{T,Z}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\,d^3v
$$

where $Z$ labels tritium ion charge states, $f_{T,Z}$ is the corresponding
velocity distribution, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and
$\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ identifies the ITB flux surface in coordinates $(\rho,
\theta, \phi)$. This quantity is summed over all tritium ion charge states
and excludes neutral tritium. It is the tritium-specific counterpart of ion
density at the internal transport barrier and contributes to the
species-agnostic [density at the internal transport
barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the tritium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tritium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all tritium ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the tritium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tritium-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents tritium ions specifically, rather than electrons,
other ion species, neutral tritium, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{T,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{T}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{T,axis}}$ is the tritium-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the number of tritium ions, and $V$ is
physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete tritium-ion population at that location
and is summed over all tritium ionic charge states; neutral tritium is
excluded. It is neither a flux-surface nor a volume integral.

This is the tritium-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [tritium density at the plasma
boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which describes the same
charge-state aggregation at the plasma boundary rather than at the magnetic
axis.

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all positive ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all positive ionic charge states. It represents
tungsten ions specifically, rather than electrons, other ion species, or
neutral tungsten.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{W,\mathrm{axis}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} n_{W^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{W,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the tungsten ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $W$ denotes tungsten, $q$ is the positive integer ionic
charge state, $q_{\max}$ is the highest included tungsten charge state, and
$n_{W^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the number density of tungsten ions in charge
state $q$ at the magnetic axis.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete positively charged tungsten-ion
population at that location, summed over charge states; it is neither a
flux-surface or volume integral nor the density of neutral tungsten or one
individual charge state.

This is the tungsten-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [xenon density at the magnetic
axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local,
charge-state-summed convention to xenon ions instead of tungsten ions.

NAMES.name: velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.short:
A vector velocity representing non-diffusive convective transport of plasma
energy, internal state, or momentum.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective vector velocity associated with convective,
or advective, transport of a plasma quantity. It describes the motion of the
transported quantity rather than diffusive spreading or the transported flux
itself.

For a transported density $Q$, the convective flux is defined by

$$
\mathbf{F}^{\mathrm{conv}}_Q = Q\,\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\mathbf{F}^{\mathrm{conv}}_Q$ is the convective flux, $Q$ is the
local density of the transported quantity, and $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{conv}}$
is this velocity. For vector or tensor quantities, the product is
interpreted componentwise or as the corresponding dyadic flux.

The same parent quantity is specialized by the transported channel in
[energy velocity due to convection](name:energy_velocity_due_to_convection),
internal-state velocity due to convection, and momentum velocity due to
convection. It excludes diffusive transport contributions.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a vector component points along the
corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: energy_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.short:
Effective advection velocity characterizing transport of plasma energy by
bulk convection, without restricting the transported energy to a particular
species or ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
Energy convective velocity is the effective advection velocity associated
with non-diffusive transport of plasma energy by bulk convection. It is the
energy-channel instance of [velocity due to
convection](name:velocity_due_to_convection), without resolving a particular
species or ion charge state.

The convective energy-flux density is related to the transported energy
density by

$$
\Gamma_{E,\mathrm{conv}} = w_E v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy-flux density,
$w_E$ is the transported energy density, and $v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the
effective advection velocity in the represented transport direction.

The quantity excludes diffusive, conductive, and source contributions.
Charge-state-resolved energy transport is represented by [ion charge-state
energy velocity due to
convection](name:ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection), while
the electron-specific formulation is [electron energy convection
velocity](name:electron_energy_convection_velocity).

NAMES.name: particle_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.short:
Effective advection velocity characterizing non-diffusive transport in the
plasma particle channel by bulk convection, without selecting a species or
internal state.
NAMES.long:
Particle convective velocity is the effective vector velocity associated
with non-diffusive transport of plasma particles by bulk convection. It
describes motion of the transported particle quantity rather than diffusive
spreading or the particle flux itself.

For the particle transport channel, the convective particle flux is defined
by

$$
\mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p = n_p\,\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p
$$

where $\mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p$ is the convective particle flux,
$n_p$ is the local particle number density, and
$\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p$ is the particle convective velocity. The
subscript $p$ identifies the particle transport channel, and the superscript
$\mathrm{conv}$ identifies its non-diffusive convective contribution.

This is the full vector, channel-level quantity with no selected radial,
poloidal, toroidal, or field-parallel component. It applies generically to
plasma-particle transport without selecting a particular species, charge
state, or internal state; no additional species-level aggregation is implied
by the generic channel name. It excludes diffusive transport and must not be
interpreted as the single-particle kinematic velocity of an individual
particle.

The quantity is the particle-channel specialization of [velocity due to
convection](name:velocity_due_to_convection). The corresponding [energy
velocity due to convection](name:energy_velocity_due_to_convection) uses the
same effective-velocity construction for convective energy transport, while
[neutral state convection velocity](name:neutral_state_convection_velocity)
is a narrower quantity restricted to a specified neutral internal state.

The vector components are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a vector component points along the
corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short:
Velocity due to E cross B drift is the nonnegative magnitude of the drift
velocity produced by crossed local electric and magnetic fields in a
magnetized plasma; it is a speed, not a signed projection along a named
axis. For magnetized charged species this drift is independent of particle
mass and charge sign.
NAMES.long:
Velocity due to E cross B drift is the nonnegative magnitude of the drift
velocity arising from crossed electric and magnetic fields in a magnetized
plasma. Because the underlying drift depends only on the local field ratio,
it is identical for all magnetized charged species regardless of particle
mass or charge sign, and the drift by itself carries no net current.

The defining relation is:

$$
v_{E\times B} = \frac{|\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}|}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector and $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic-field vector. The underlying drift vector
$\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|^2$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$
and has no component along the magnetic-field direction; consequently any
parallel projection of this drift vanishes identically.

This quantity is the speed of the drift and is therefore nonnegative; it
must not be confused with signed axis-resolved projections of the drift
vector, such as the toroidal projection for a specific ion charge state in
[toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
or the parallel projection for a neutral internal state in
[parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
Population-resolved counterparts of the same drift family are provided for
individual ion charge states in
[ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
for internal states in internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift, and
for neutral-species internal states in
neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Velocity due to E cross B drift for a specified ion charge state is the
guiding-center drift vector produced by crossed local electric and magnetic
fields, independent of ion mass and charge.
NAMES.long:
Velocity due to E cross B drift for a specified ion charge state is the
guiding-center drift vector produced by local crossed electric and magnetic
fields in a magnetized plasma. It is common to all magnetized charged
species at the same position, although this name resolves it to one ion
charge state.

The defining relation is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{E\times B} = \frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector and $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic-field vector. The resulting vector is perpendicular to
$\mathbf{B}$, and its magnitude is the parent [velocity due to E cross B
drift](name:velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

This vector quantity must be distinguished from its signed axis projections,
including the [radial ion charge-state velocity due to E cross B
drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) and
[toroidal ion charge-state velocity due to E cross B
drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). The
ion charge-state resolution identifies the represented population but does
not introduce mass- or charge-dependent variation in the drift itself.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Field-aligned projection of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma, identically zero for the ideal drift.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
projection along the local magnetic-field direction. For the ideal E×B
drift, this component vanishes identically.

For the ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2} = 0.
$$

Here $v_{E,\parallel}$ is the parallel drift component for the specified ion
charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its ideal E×B guiding-center drift velocity,
$\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic
field, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector
along the magnetic field. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field
and applies to magnetized ions.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge
states or species. It includes only the E×B drift contribution, not the
total field-aligned ion flow, which may be nonzero. Other contributions to
ion motion are excluded.

The zero parallel projection follows from the perpendicularity of the ideal
E×B drift to the magnetic field. Other projections, such as the [toroidal
component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
need not vanish because their projection directions are not generally
field-aligned.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed poloidal projection of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion
charge state in the edge plasma, along a specified local poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
signed projection along a specified local poloidal direction. This direction
lies in the meridional plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; its positive orientation must be
specified.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal drift component for the specified
ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its ideal E×B drift velocity,
$\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic
field, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit vector along the
specified positive local poloidal direction. The definition requires a
nonzero magnetic field and magnetized ions.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge
states or species. At fixed local fields, the ideal drift is independent of
ion mass and charge. Other contributions to the ion fluid velocity are
excluded. It is a linear velocity component, not a poloidal angle or angular
velocity.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the ideal E×B drift, the poloidal projection
need not vanish: the local poloidal direction is not generally aligned with
the magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the E×B drift has a component along the
specified positive local poloidal unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed major-radius component of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion
charge state in the edge plasma, positive away from the toroidal symmetry
axis.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
signed projection along the major-radius direction. This direction points
away from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,R} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{R} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{R}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,R}$ is the radial drift component for the specified ion charge
state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$
is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and
$\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. The definition
requires a nonzero magnetic field and applies to magnetized ions; at fixed
local fields, the ideal drift is independent of ion mass and charge.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma, including the scrape-off layer; it is neither
summed nor averaged over charge states or species. Other contributions to
ion motion are excluded. It is a signed linear velocity component, not a
speed, a flux-surface-normal projection, or the magnitude of the
field-perpendicular velocity.

Together with the
[toroidal](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
and
[vertical](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
components, it resolves the parent drift vector in the cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. Although the ideal drift is perpendicular to the magnetic
field, its major-radius projection need not vanish because the major-radius
direction is not generally field-aligned.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the E×B drift has a component toward
increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed toroidal projection of the mass- and charge-independent E×B
guiding-center drift of one ion charge state in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
signed projection along the geometric toroidal direction. This direction
follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\phi} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,\phi}$ is the toroidal drift component for the specified ion
charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity,
$\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic
field with magnitude $|\mathbf{B}|$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector
toward increasing toroidal angle. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic
field and the magnetized guiding-center regime. At fixed local fields, the
ideal drift is independent of ion mass and charge.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge
states or species. Other contributions to ion motion are excluded. It is a
linear velocity component, not a toroidal angle, angular velocity, or
drift-speed magnitude.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the ideal E×B drift, the toroidal projection
need not vanish: the geometric toroidal direction is not generally aligned
with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the E×B drift velocity has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Projection along the toroidal symmetry axis of the mean translational
velocity of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy
state.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the vertical component of the bulk translational flow of a
neutral species occupying one specified internal quantum or energy state.
Vertical denotes the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

At a given position, the component is the vertical projection of the first
velocity moment:

$$
u_{0,a,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_{0,a}=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf z})f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{0,a,Z}$ is the vertical bulk velocity, $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is the
[bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), $\hat{\mathbf z}$ is
the unit vector toward increasing vertical position, $\mathbf v$ is particle
velocity, and $f_{0,a}$ is the local velocity distribution of the selected
neutral species in internal state $a$. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral
particles, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The average is taken over particle velocities within the specified species
and internal state; distinct internal states and neutral species are not
combined. Bulk denotes mean translational flow, without imposing a hot- or
cold-population selection. This signed component is not the flow-vector
magnitude, a random thermal spread, or a particle flux; unlike a
mechanism-specific effective transport velocity, it is not restricted to one
transport contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neutral bulk flow points toward
increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_conductivity
NAMES.short:
Local electrical conductivity relating an electric field along the toroidal
symmetry axis to the conductive current density induced in that same
direction.
NAMES.long:
Vertical conductivity is the vertical-vertical projection of the local
electrical-conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The defining tensor projection is:

$$
\sigma_{ZZ} = \hat{\mathbf{z}}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\sigma_{ZZ}$ is the vertical conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is
the [plasma electrical-conductivity
tensor](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity), and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the
unit vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing height. For a purely
vertical electric field, this coefficient gives the induced vertical
conductive current density per applied electric field.

This is a local transport coefficient, not a height coordinate or a
spatially averaged conductivity. Vertical current driven by radial or
toroidal electric fields involves off-diagonal tensor components and is not
included in this coefficient.

[Radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity) is the corresponding
diagonal projection along the major-radius direction. In contrast, [parallel
conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity) projects along the local magnetic
field rather than the geometric vertical direction.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
NAMES.short:
Vertical current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
conventional-charge flux along the toroidal symmetry axis attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.
NAMES.long:
Vertical current density due to anomalous transport is the signed vertical
projection of the conventional electric-current contribution attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height along the toroidal
symmetry axis. The defining projection is

$$
j_Z = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $j_Z$ is the vertical anomalous current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the vector [current density due to anomalous
transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis toward
increasing $Z$.

This quantity is a local component of the anomalous contribution, not the
total vertical current density or a spatially integrated electric current.
Its direction is fixed by the symmetry axis, whereas [parallel current
density due to anomalous
transport](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport)
projects the same anomalous-current vector along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the anomalous conventional current flows
toward increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
NAMES.short:
Vertical current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the signed
symmetry-axis projection of electric current generated by the divergence of
perpendicular viscous stress.
NAMES.long:
Vertical current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the local
symmetry-axis projection of the electric-current contribution generated by
the divergence of perpendicular viscous stress in a magnetized charged
plasma.

The component is defined by

$$
j_Z = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $j_Z$ is the signed vertical component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}}$ is
the [current-density vector due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), and the
subscript $\mathrm{pv}$ labels that mechanism. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ points along increasing vertical height in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This is a local, mechanism-resolved contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), not the total vertical current density or a
spatial average. “Perpendicular” identifies the viscous-stress mechanism,
not a restriction of the resulting current vector to directions
perpendicular to the magnetic field. The [parallel component due to
perpendicular
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity)
projects the same vector along the local magnetic-field direction rather
than the symmetry axis.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the conventional electric-current
contribution due to perpendicular viscosity has a component toward
increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_diamagnetic_current_density
NAMES.short:
Vertical diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of
pressure-gradient-driven electric current per unit area along the toroidal
symmetry axis in edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Vertical diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of the
diamagnetic contribution to [current density](name:current_density) onto the
direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It represents
pressure-gradient-driven charge transport in the edge plasma.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},Z} = \hat{\mathbf{z}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},Z}$ is the vertical diamagnetic current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing vertical height. In
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$
points along increasing $Z$.

This quantity is the local algebraic sum of the vertical diamagnetic-current
contributions from all included charge carriers and charge states; it is not
species- or charge-state-resolved. It includes only the diamagnetic
contribution, not the total vertical plasma current from all mechanisms, and
implies neither spatial averaging nor integration.

The underlying vector has the magnitude given by [diamagnetic current
density](name:diamagnetic_current_density); the vertical projection is
signed and is not that magnitude. It differs from [radial diamagnetic
current density](name:radial_diamagnetic_current_density), which projects
the same vector along increasing major radius, and from [parallel
diamagnetic current density](name:parallel_diamagnetic_current_density),
which projects it along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic current has a component in
the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Signed height-axis component of the local electron-fluid bulk flow in the
edge plasma, parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
The vertical electron velocity is the height-axis projection of the local
bulk electron flow in the edge plasma. It represents directed electron
motion after averaging over particle velocities, rather than random thermal
motion.

The defining projection is

$$
u_{e,Z} = \mathbf{u}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $u_{e,Z}$ is the vertical electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the
local bulk [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis. The
right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The underlying bulk flow is the particle-density-weighted mean electron
velocity at each position; no spatial averaging is implied. This signed
component is distinct from the electron speed, thermal velocity spread, and
particle flux. The vertical direction is geometric and need not coincide
with the local magnetic-field direction.

Together with [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity) and
[toroidal electron velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity), it specifies
the cylindrical components of the electron-flow vector.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electron bulk flow has a component toward
increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient relating the convective flux of vertical momentum to
its density for one ion species and charge state in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient for advective, non-diffusive
transport of vertical [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion
species in one charge state. Vertical is parallel to the toroidal symmetry
axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a transport surface with a chosen positive unit normal $\hat{\mathbf
n}$, the convective flux of vertical momentum is defined by:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z} = V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z}\,g_{s,Z}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z}$ is its convective vertical-momentum flux through
the surface along $\hat{\mathbf n}$, $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z}$ is this
effective convection coefficient, and $g_{s,Z}$ is its vertical momentum
density.

The vertical label selects the transported momentum component; the transport
normal need not be vertical. The coefficient is charge-state resolved,
without summation or averaging over charge states. It is distinct from the
charge state's bulk vertical flow velocity and excludes gradient-driven
diffusive momentum transport.

It resolves the vertical momentum component of [ion charge-state momentum
convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) and
specializes [vertical momentum convection
velocity](name:vertical_momentum_convection_velocity) to the specified ion
species and charge state.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the convective flux along the chosen surface
normal has the same sign as the vertical momentum density, with positive
vertical momentum directed toward increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Mean edge-plasma ion flow along the toroidal symmetry axis, resolved for one
specified species and ionization charge state.
NAMES.long:
The vertical ion charge-state velocity is the projection of the local bulk
flow of a specified ion species and ionization charge state onto the
vertical direction. It describes directed motion in the edge plasma in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

It is the vertical component of the [ion charge-state
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), defined by the first velocity
moment:

$$
u_{s,q,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_{s,q}=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf z})f_{s,q}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{s,q}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{s,q,Z}$ is the vertical bulk-flow component, $\mathbf u_{s,q}$ is
the bulk velocity vector, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is its
ionization charge number, $\mathbf r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle
velocity, and $f_{s,q}$ is the selected population's phase-space number
density. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf z}$ points along the symmetry axis
toward increasing $Z$. Both integrals cover particle velocity space; the
definition requires nonzero population density.

Only the selected ion species and charge-state population contribute;
neutral particles and other species are excluded. If a charge-state bundle
is specified, its distribution combines the member states, giving their
number-density-weighted mean velocity rather than a sum of velocities. This
quantity is a signed flow component, not a speed, thermal velocity spread,
or particle flux; the vertical direction is not generally the poloidal or
magnetic-field-parallel direction.

The [vertical ion velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity) is instead the
density-weighted mean of these components over all ionic charge states of
the species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected ion population's bulk flow has a
component toward increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed vertical projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid
velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, distinct from
individual guiding-center motion.
NAMES.long:
The vertical ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather
than the guiding-center motion of individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,Z} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,Z}$ is the vertical diamagnetic-drift velocity
component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla
p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field
vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle
charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the toroidal symmetry axis
toward increasing vertical height. The right-handed cylindrical frame is
$(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow. Although the diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular to the
magnetic field, its geometric vertical component, like its [toroidal
component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift),
need not vanish.

The species-level [ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted
mean over all ionic charge states of that species. Its vertical projection
is therefore the density-weighted mean of the corresponding charge-state
vertical components, not their sum.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified
ion charge state has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$ in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
