NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis of the mass- and
charge-independent E×B guiding-center drift for one specified ion charge
state in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The vertical component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis. This direction is the
vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,Z} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,Z}$ is the vertical drift component for the specified ion charge
state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$
is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis toward
increasing vertical height. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field
and magnetized ions.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma, including the scrape-off layer; it is neither
summed nor averaged over charge states or species. The ideal drift is
independent of ion mass and charge and is perpendicular to both local
fields. Other contributions to ion motion are excluded. This is a signed
velocity component, not a vertical position or the magnitude of the drift
velocity.

Together with the [radial
component](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) and
[toroidal
component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
it resolves the parent drift vector in the cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
The vertical component need not vanish because the symmetry axis is not
generally aligned with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the E×B guiding-center drift has a component
toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Vertical ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the
vertical component of linear momentum for the total ion population through a
surface whose normal is parallel to the Z direction in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, summed over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Vertical ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the
vertical component of linear momentum for the total ion population through a
surface whose normal is parallel to the $Z$ direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height, summed over
all ion species and charge states. It is the $Z$-momentum, $Z$-normal
projection of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux),
including convective, scalar-pressure, and viscous or turbulent stress
contributions.

The $ZZ$ component of the ion momentum-flux tensor gives this quantity:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{ion},ZZ} = \hat{\mathbf{Z}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}} = \sum_s \left( m_s n_s v_{s,Z}^2 + p_s + \pi_{s,ZZ} \right)
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{ion},ZZ}$ is the vertical ion momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion}$ is the [ion momentum
flux](name:ion_momentum_flux) tensor, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unit vector
in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$, $m_s$ is the ion mass of
population $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, $v_{s,Z}$ is its vertical
mean-fluid velocity component, $p_s$ is its scalar pressure, and
$\pi_{s,ZZ}$ is its viscous or turbulent stress component, with the sum
running over all ion species and charge states.

This quantity is the total-ion, charge-state-summed counterpart of the
charge-state-resolved [vertical ion charge-state momentum
flux](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). It differs from
[toroidal ion momentum flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux), [poloidal ion
momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux), and [parallel ion momentum
flux](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux) by resolving both the transported
momentum component and the surface-normal direction along $Z$ rather than
along toroidal, poloidal, field-aligned, or flux-surface-normal projections.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when ion linear momentum in the
$+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame is transported across a surface whose normal points in the
$+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Directed flow of a specified ion species along the toroidal symmetry axis,
defined as the number-density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
The vertical ion velocity is the local projection of the bulk [ion
velocity](name:ion_velocity) onto the symmetry-axis direction in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The projection and charge-state average are defined by

$$
u_{i,Z}=\mathbf{u}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}=\frac{\sum_q n_{i,q}\,\mathbf{u}_{i,q}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{\sum_q n_{i,q}}
$$

where $u_{i,Z}$ is the vertical ion velocity, $\mathbf{u}_i$ is the
charge-state-averaged ion bulk velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit
vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$. The index $i$
identifies the selected ion species, $q$ indexes its ionic charge states,
$n_{i,q}$ is the number density of each state, and $\mathbf{u}_{i,q}$ is
that state's bulk velocity.

For the edge-plasma ion population, this is a local directed-flow component,
not a spatial average, velocity magnitude, or thermal velocity spread. It
excludes neutral particles and other ion species. The [vertical ion
charge-state velocity](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity) retains
individual charge-state resolution; this quantity combines those components
through a density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, not a sum of
velocities.

Unlike [vertical plasma velocity](name:vertical_plasma_velocity), which
projects the mass-weighted center-of-mass flow of all contributing plasma
species, this component describes only the selected ion species.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ion bulk flow has a component toward
increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective convection coefficient relating convective flux of vertical
momentum to its density for one neutral species in one resolved internal
state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed effective coefficient governing convective
transport of the vertical component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by
one neutral species in one specified internal state in edge plasma. Vertical
is the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The convective closure for the selected vertical momentum component is:

$$
\Pi_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}} g_{0a,Z}
$$

where $\Pi_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of vertical
momentum across a surface along its chosen normal,
$V_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection coefficient, and $g_{0a,Z}$ is
the vertical momentum density. The subscript $0$ denotes the selected
neutral species, and $a$ identifies its resolved internal state.

No sum over neutral species or internal states is implied. The vertical
label identifies the transported momentum component; the surface-normal
transport direction need not be vertical. This effective transport
coefficient is distinct from the [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). Its convective flux
contribution excludes gradient-driven transport represented by [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity), as well as local momentum sources.

The [toroidal neutral-state momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity) is the
corresponding coefficient for transport of toroidal rather than vertical
momentum.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the convective flux of momentum directed
along increasing $Z$ crosses the surface along its chosen normal.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical
transport rate of vertical linear momentum carried by neutral particles in
one specified internal state. It is the vertical-vertical component of the
neutral momentum-flux tensor for that state.
NAMES.long:
The vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical
transport component of linear momentum carried by neutral particles
restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state.
It is the $ZZ$ component of the state-resolved momentum-flux tensor, not a
particle flux or a local momentum source.

For the state-resolved neutral distribution, the vertical component is
defined by

$$
\Pi_{ZZ}^{(s)} = \hat{Z} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{Z} = \int m_s v_Z^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is its
momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis direction of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $m_s$ is the mass of a
neutral particle in state $s$, $v_Z=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{Z}$ is the vertical
velocity component, and $f_s$ is the state-resolved velocity distribution.

The vertical direction is the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height; it is not the radial, toroidal, or
magnetic-field-parallel direction. As a diagonal $ZZ$ tensor component
formed from $v_Z^2$, this quantity is nonnegative for any nonnegative
state-resolved velocity distribution.

This component is the vertical member of the parent neutral internal-state
momentum flux, differs from the
[radial](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux),
[toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux),
[parallel](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and linear
internal-state components, and is the state-resolved counterpart of
[vertical neutral momentum flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux).

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of
an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor, governing
down-gradient redistribution of aggregate neutral momentum density along Z
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The vertical qualifier
identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of
an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor. It parameterizes
down-gradient diffusive transport of aggregate neutral momentum density
along the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. The vertical qualifier identifies the flux and gradient
direction, not the momentum component.

For a diagonal Fick's-law closure, the vertical diffusive flux of a neutral
momentum-density component is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z} = -D^{(n)}_{m,Z}\,\frac{\partial P_{n,\alpha}}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the transported momentum component,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z}$ is the vertical diffusive flux of that
momentum component, $D^{(n)}_{m,Z}$ is the vertical neutral momentum
diffusivity, $P_{n,\alpha}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum density
component, and $Z$ is vertical height. The minus sign denotes down-gradient
diffusion: for positive diffusivity, the diffusive flux is directed from
larger toward smaller aggregate neutral momentum density along $Z$.

This coefficient applies to the aggregate neutral population represented by
the neutral momentum-density field. It does not denote a diffusivity for a
particular transported momentum component, and it is distinct from
off-diagonal tensor components or convective transport of neutral momentum.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Vertical neutral momentum flux is the signed Z component of the aggregate
momentum-flux vector carried by neutral particles in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It aggregates neutral species and internal
states rather than retaining an individual state contribution.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral momentum flux is the signed vertical component of the
momentum-flux vector carried by neutral particles. The vertical direction is
parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

The vertical component is the projection of the aggregate neutral
momentum-flux vector:

$$
\Gamma_{0,Z} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,Z}$ is this vertical component, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is
the aggregate [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) vector,
and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the toroidal symmetry
axis. In the stated frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

At a spatial location, this quantity aggregates contributions from neutral
species and internal states; it does not retain an individual state
contribution, unlike [vertical neutral state momentum
flux](name:vertical_neutral_state_momentum_flux). It describes transported
neutral momentum, not a local momentum source or neutral particle flux.

This is the vertical directional component of [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux). In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, [radial neutral momentum
flux](name:radial_neutral_momentum_flux) and [toroidal neutral momentum
flux](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux) are the corresponding components
along the radial and toroidal directions. [Parallel neutral momentum
flux](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux) is instead a projection along the
local magnetic-field direction, not a cylindrical component.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the aggregate neutral momentum-flux vector
has a component toward increasing $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Signed flow along the toroidal symmetry axis, equal to the
mass-density-weighted mean vertical velocity of all constituent plasma
species.
NAMES.long:
The vertical center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the
toroidal symmetry axis. It retains the mass-density weighting of the full
barycentric velocity.

The defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},Z} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},Z}$ is the vertical center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the [parent velocity
vector](name:neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity), $s$ indexes
constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density, and
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$
points along the symmetry axis toward increasing vertical height in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The sum includes all species in the local plasma mixture, rather than only
ions or only neutral particles. This is a local mass-density-weighted mean,
not a particle-number-weighted mean or an unweighted sum of species
velocities. The definition requires nonzero total mass density.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its radial and toroidal
components and is distinct from its speed. The vertical direction need not
coincide with the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points
toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis of the effective E×B
drift velocity assigned to a neutral species in one internal state.
NAMES.long:
The vertical component of the [neutral-species internal-state E×B drift
velocity](name:neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
is its signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis. This direction
follows increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

For the assigned ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v^0_{E,Z} = \mathbf{v}^0_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v^0_{E,Z}$ is the effective vertical drift component for the specified
neutral internal state, $\mathbf{v}^0_E$ is its assigned ideal E×B drift
velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
local magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the
symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$. The superscript $0$ labels the neutral
population. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified internal state of one neutral
species; it is neither summed nor averaged over internal states or species.
It denotes an effective fluid-velocity contribution, not a direct
electromagnetic guiding-center drift of electrically neutral particles.
Other contributions to neutral motion are excluded, so it is not the total
neutral fluid velocity.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the assigned ideal E×B drift, the vertical
component need not vanish: the symmetry-axis direction is not generally
aligned with the magnetic field.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the assigned E×B drift velocity has a
component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of vertical momentum
carried by one neutral species, aggregated over neutral states. Vertical
denotes the momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame, not velocity direction.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral species momentum convection velocity is the
flux-surface-normal convection coefficient that multiplies the vertical
momentum density carried by neutrals of one chemical species. The vertical
momentum component is defined along $hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height; the coefficient itself is not a velocity
directed along $hat{Z}$. It is the vertical component of the [neutral
species momentum convection
velocity](name:neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity).

The defining relation preserves the total convective flux of vertical
momentum across a magnetic flux surface:

$$
\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = P_{Z,a} V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_{s \in a} P_{Z,s} V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ denotes one neutral chemical species, $s$ runs over its resolved
neutral states, $P_{Z,s}$ and $P_{Z,a}$ are signed vertical momentum
densities, $V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ are
state-resolved and species-aggregated convection coefficients, and
$\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum
flux. The state sum excludes other chemical species and this local
coefficient is not a flux-surface average. Unlike [vertical neutral
velocity](name:vertical_neutral_velocity), it is defined by momentum
transport.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $P_{Z,a}$
have the same sign, with positive vertical momentum directed toward
increasing $Z$ and positive flux-surface-normal transport directed toward
increasing magnetic flux label.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound
on the vertical (Z) momentum-flux-density component in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame for a specified neutral particle state in
edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The vertical neutral-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter factor assigned to a specified neutral particle state in
edge-plasma transport closures. It scales the free-streaming bound on the
magnitude of the vertical component of momentum-flux density, where the
component is projected along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, preventing unphysical supersonic neutral-momentum transport
without changing the direction carried by the modeled flux.

The defining relation for the vertical projection is:

$$
\Pi_Z = c_Z \, \Pi_Z^{\rm FS}
$$

where $\Pi_Z$ is the modeled vertical momentum-flux-density component of the
specified neutral particle state, $\Pi_Z^{\rm FS}$ is the corresponding
free-streaming momentum-flux-density component, and $c_Z$ is the vertical
neutral-state momentum coefficient.

It is the vertical projection component of the vector [neutral-state
momentum
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region).
It is distinct from the [radial neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:radial_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[toroidal neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[poloidal neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
and [parallel neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which apply the same limiter concept to other projection directions.

When flux limiting is active, $c_Z$ is bounded in $[0, 1]$: $c_Z = 1$ leaves
the free-streaming bound unscaled, while smaller values impose a stronger
limiter on the vertical momentum-flux-density magnitude. The coefficient is
non-negative; the sign of the vertical momentum-flux-density component is
carried by $\Pi_Z$ rather than by $c_Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Mean directed motion of a selected neutral species along the vertical
symmetry-axis direction, averaged over contributing internal states with
number-density weighting.
NAMES.long:
The vertical neutral velocity is the projection of the bulk drift of a
selected neutral species onto the direction parallel to the toroidal
symmetry axis. It represents directed motion after averaging over particle
velocities and contributing internal states.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position, its local
definition is:

$$
u_{0,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_0=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\mathbf v\,f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{0,Z}$ is the vertical neutral velocity, $\mathbf u_0$ is the
[neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) vector, $\hat{\mathbf z}$ is the
unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis, $\mathbf v$ is particle
velocity, $f_{0,a}$ is the local velocity distribution of neutral internal
state $a$, and $\mathcal A$ is the set of contributing internal states. The
subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
volume element.

The state distributions combine with number-density weighting for one
selected neutral species, not by summing state velocities or averaging
different species together. This is a local flow component, including for
neutrals in the scrape-off layer and divertor, rather than a spatial
average, flow-speed magnitude, particle flux, or random thermal spread.

Unlike [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), which retains one
specified internal state, this quantity averages over the contributing
internal states before taking the vertical projection.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the neutral bulk flow points toward
increasing vertical position $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short:
Kinematic coefficient relating vertical diffusive transport of plasma ion
momentum to the opposing vertical gradient of ion momentum density.
NAMES.long:
Vertical plasma momentum diffusivity is the kinematic transport coefficient
governing vertical diffusion of [momentum](name:momentum) in the plasma ion
momentum balance. The vertical direction is parallel to the toroidal
symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is distance from that axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical position.

For a momentum component entering the ion balance, the local Fick-law
closure is:

$$
\Pi_{i,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_Z\frac{\partial g_i}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\Pi_{i,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of that momentum
component through a surface normal to increasing $Z$, $g_i$ is its ion
momentum density, $D_Z$ is this vertical directional diffusivity, and the
subscript $i$ denotes the ion population represented in the balance.

The momentum density is aggregated over the ionic constituents and charge
states included in that population; the diffusivity itself is not a sum of
charge-state coefficients. Neutral-particle momentum is excluded. This
coefficient describes the gradient-driven contribution only, excluding
convective momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum
sources. Vertical transport need not be normal to a magnetic flux surface or
parallel to the magnetic field.

Within the ion momentum balance, this coefficient supplies the vertical
directional component of [plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:plasma_momentum_diffusivity). The [vertical ion
charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) instead
resolves the corresponding transport coefficient for a specified ionization
state.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_argon_density
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged number density of argon ions over the confined plasma
volume, summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged argon ion number density is the spatial mean of the
local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) throughout the confined plasma
volume, including contributions from every argon ionization stage. It is
distinct from a local or charge-state-resolved density.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{Ar}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}}\int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is
position, $\mathrm{d}V$ is a volume element, and $n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})$
is the local argon ion density. The local density is charge-state summed,
$n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r})$,
where $q$ is the argon ionization stage. This quantity provides the
argon-density numerator for the impurity concentration ratio [ratio of
volume-averaged argon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Deuterium-tritium density is the volume-averaged ion number density of the
combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species, treating deuterium and
tritium as one effective species.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-tritium density is the volume-averaged ion number density of the
combined deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, treating deuterium and
tritium ions as one effective species. It is obtained from the local
[deuterium-tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density), which is summed
over all ion charge states.

The defining volume average is

$$
\bar n_{DT} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{DT}\,dV
$$

where $\bar n_{DT}$ and $n_{DT}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $V$ is
the specified averaging volume in m$^{3}$, and $dV$ is its volume element.
The local density satisfies $n_{DT}=n_D+n_T$, with $n_D$ and $n_T$ the
corresponding charge-state-summed deuterium and tritium ion densities.

The quantity includes only deuterium and tritium fuel ions represented by
the effective pseudo-species; neutral atoms and molecules, reaction
products, and impurity ions are excluded. Unlike the [line-averaged
deuterium-tritium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), it
uses a volume measure rather than a line-of-sight average, and it supplies
the numerator of the [ratio of volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density to
volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_hydrogen_density
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma,
giving the mean H+ concentration across the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the mean concentration of
ionized protium throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatial
average of the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density), rather than
its value at a particular position.

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_H(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_H$ is the volume-averaged hydrogen density,
$n_H(\mathbf{r})$ is the local ionized-protium density at position
$\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume
element. The average includes ionized protium throughout $V_p$ and excludes
neutral atomic hydrogen and other isotopes. Unlike [line-averaged hydrogen
density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), it averages over the full
plasma volume. Its isotope fraction relative to all hydrogenic fuel is
represented by [the volume-averaged hydrogen-density
fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless hydrogen-isotope fraction equal to the volume-averaged
protium-ion density divided by the volume-averaged density of all hydrogenic
ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the fraction of the hydrogenic ion population attributable
to protium, evaluated from volume-averaged densities over the same plasma
volume. The numerator is the [volume-averaged hydrogen
density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator
includes the corresponding hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion populations.

$$
f_H = \frac{\overline{n}_H}{\overline{n}_H + \overline{n}_D + \overline{n}_T}
$$

Here $f_H$ is the hydrogen-isotope fraction; $\overline{n}_H$,
$\overline{n}_D$, and $\overline{n}_T$ are the volume-averaged densities of
protium, deuterium, and tritium ions, respectively. The quantity is a ratio
of separately volume-averaged densities, not a local isotope fraction or a
fraction restricted to a single charge state.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fraction of hydrogen density among the hydrogenic species (nH/(nH+nD+nT))

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma
volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified
ion species or lumped-ion population.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma
volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified
ion species or lumped-ion population. It is a normalized volume average
representing the global mean ionization level of that selected charge state.

For ion species $i$, the volume-averaged ion charge is defined by

$$
\langle Z_{\mathrm{dom},i} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\Omega}\int_\Omega Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})$ is the [ion charge](name:ion_charge)
number of the dominant ionization state of species $i$ at position
$\mathbf{x}$, $\Omega$ is the confined plasma volume, and $V_\Omega$ is the
volume of $\Omega$.

The population is one specified ion species; if the species represents a
lumped-ion population, the same definition applies to that lumped
population. The charge-state convention is dominant-state selection: the
quantity is not a charge-state sum and is not the density-weighted mean over
all charge states.

This quantity differs from [volume-averaged ion charge-state average charge
number](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number), which
represents the density-weighted mean charge number over all charge states of
the ion species. It also differs from [volume-averaged ion
density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), which is a particle population
density rather than a charge number.

sources.leaf_definition: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed), volume averaged over plasma radius
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species, in the sense of isonuclear or isomolecular sequences

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Mean ionization state of a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species,
weighted locally by charge-state concentration and then averaged over the
plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the plasma-volume average of the local
concentration-weighted mean ionic charge number within a specified
charge-state bundle of one ion species. Charge-state averaging within the
bundle precedes spatial volume averaging.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and
$\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the local [bundle-averaged ionic charge
number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number). Locally,
$\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} q x_q$, where
$\mathcal{B}$ is the specified bundle, $q$ is the ionic charge number, and
$x_q$ is the local number-density fraction of charge state $q$ within that
bundle, with $\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}}x_q = 1$.

Only charge states within the specified bundle contribute; different ion
species are not combined. The spatial average uses volume weighting without
additional ion-density weighting, so it is not generally equal to the ratio
of total ionic charge to total ion number over the plasma. For a bundle
containing one fixed charge state, the result equals that state's charge
number.

This first charge-number moment is distinct from the [bundle mean-square
charge number](name:square_of_ion_charge_state_charge_number), which
averages the squared ionic charge number rather than the charge number.

sources.leaf_definition: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Number density of ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic charge
states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed
flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ion

The volume average of the local [ion density](name:ion_density) is defined
by

$$
\langle n_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_i\,dV
$$

where $i$ labels the specified ion species, $n_i$ is its local ion number
density, $\langle n_i\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$
is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and
$dV$ is a volume element.

The species density is summed over all ionic charge states and includes
thermal and nonthermal ions; neutral particles are excluded. This is a
single-species particle number density, not an all-species total, electric
charge density, or mass density. It is a volume mean rather than a local
value or a chord mean.

Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the total
number of ions of the specified species within that volume. The
[volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) is a
species-specific instance of the same averaging definition.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_lithium_density
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged total number density of lithium ions, summed over all charge
states from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, within the confined plasma
volume.
NAMES.long:
This is the volume average of lithium ion number density, summed over all
ionization stages from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, throughout the
confined plasma. Neutral lithium is excluded. The quantity provides a global
measure of lithium impurity content rather than a local or boundary value.

The volume average is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_{Li} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{Li}\,dV
$$

where $n_{Li}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $V_p$ is the
confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is
the physical volume element. Unlike the boundary value flux-surface-averaged
lithium density at the plasma boundary, this quantity averages over the full
confined volume. Its electron-normalized counterpart is the ratio of
volume-averaged lithium density to volume-averaged electron density.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short:
Mean number density of runaway electrons over the confined plasma volume,
obtained by averaging the local suprathermal population that remains in the
accelerating tail.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged runaway electron density is the spatial mean of the local
runaway-electron population over the confined plasma volume. Runaway
electrons are suprathermal electrons whose momentum makes collisional
slowing-down ineffective compared with continued electromagnetic
acceleration, as described by
[runaway_electron_density](name:runaway_electron_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE}$ is the volume-averaged runaway electron
density, $n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local runaway electron density
at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, and
$\mathrm{d}V$ is the physical volume element.

This quantity averages the local density rather than reporting the total
runaway-electron count; the latter is obtained by multiplying the average by
$V_\mathrm{p}$. It includes the full confined plasma volume and excludes
regions outside that volume.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged total ion number density over the confined plasma volume,
summing all ion species and charge states and including thermal and
non-thermal ion populations.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged total ion density is the aggregate ion number density
averaged over the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface. It includes all ion species, resolved charge states, and thermal
and non-thermal ion populations; it excludes electrons and neutral
particles.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the volume-averaged density,
$n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [total ion
density](name:total_ion_number_density) in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined
plasma volume in m$^3$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume
element. This is a density average, not the total ion inventory. Unlike
[volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), it
aggregates all ion species rather than one selected species.

NAMES.name: volume_integrated_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated particle source rate is the net number of particles added
to a specified distribution per unit time by a source contribution over the
plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated particle source rate is the net particle-number input to a
specified particle distribution from a given source contribution, integrated
over the plasma volume.

The defining volume integral is

$$
S(t) = \int_V s_p(\mathbf{x},t)\,d^3x
$$

where $S$ is the volume-integrated particle source rate, $t$ is time, $V$ is
the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $d^3x$ is the volume
element, and $s_p$ is the local net particle source rate per physical
volume. For a kinetic source term, $s_p$ is its velocity-space integral, the
particle-number moment.

The rate applies to the species and population represented by the specified
distribution. Volume integration does not imply summation over other
distributions, species, or source mechanisms. For a
distribution-function-driven contribution, it is the volume integral of the
[particle source rate due to distribution-function-driven
processes](name:particle_source_rate_due_to_distribution_function_driven),
not its volume average.

No restriction to thermal particles or thermalization is implied. When the
contribution describes thermalization, it counts transfer from fast
particles into the thermal background, rather than particle creation in the
combined populations; reverse transfer constitutes a sink for the thermal
population.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the source contribution adds particles to the
specified distribution; negative when it removes particles.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of xenon ions at the internal transport barrier, the
flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport
permits steep radial impurity-density gradients to form; summed over all
xenon ion charge states and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of xenon ions at the internal transport barrier is
the local xenon-ion particle density, summed over all xenon ion charge
states, on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. The
internal transport barrier is a confined-plasma flux-surface region where
locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep radial
impurity-density gradients to form. Xenon (atomic number $Z = 54$) is a
high-$Z$ noble-gas impurity species.

The charge-state-summed xenon-ion density at the barrier reference surface
is the sum of zeroth velocity moments of the xenon ion distribution
functions:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_{q=1}^{54} \int f_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\, d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the elemental xenon ion number density, $q$ is
the xenon ion charge number, $f_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the distribution
function of xenon ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, and $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the scalar flux-surface label
identifying the internal-transport-barrier reference surface. The range
$q=1,\ldots,54$ spans all positive xenon ion charge states and excludes
neutral xenon atoms.

At the species level this per-volume particle amount is charge-state-summed:
charge-state-resolved xenon ion densities are distinct populations, and
summing them over all positive charge states recovers this elemental
density. It is the xenon-specific instance of
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and the barrier-local counterpart of [xenon_density](name:xenon_density),
distinct from
[electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and from other noble-gas impurity densities at the same locus.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all xenon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents xenon ions specifically, rather than neutral xenon,
electrons, or another ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe,axis}}$ is the xenon-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the number of xenon ions summed over all xenon
ionization states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete xenon-ion population at that location
and is charge-state-summed; it is neither a density of neutral xenon nor an
integral over a flux surface or volume.

This is the xenon-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It is the
on-axis counterpart of [xenon density](name:xenon_density), which applies at
a general plasma location, and it is distinguished from [argon density at
the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts a
different ion species.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Co-passing fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace
carried by suprathermal particles on untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged
toroidal motion is in the same direction as the plasma current. It sums
contributions over fast-particle species and charge states and retains
directed-motion stress.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace
carried by the suprathermal particles on untrapped co-passing orbits. These
orbits have orbit-averaged toroidal motion in the same direction as the
plasma current; the scalar trace includes field-aligned, transverse, and
directed-motion contributions without requiring an isotropic velocity
distribution.

The pressure is defined by the second velocity moment restricted to the
co-passing region:

$$
P_{\mathrm{co,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s\int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{co},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,c,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the co-passing fast-particle pressure,
$\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $c$
labels charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_{s,c,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal distribution
function for species $s$ and charge state $c$,
$\Omega_{\mathrm{co},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space region of
untrapped co-passing particles at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The distribution includes represented
fast-particle populations additively, and the velocity is not centered on
the selected population's mean, so directed-motion stress is retained.

The quantity applies to the suprathermal co-passing population only.
Contributions are summed over all fast-particle species and charge states;
thermal particles and the counter-passing and trapped orbit classes are
excluded. The pressure is defined locally, and its flux-surface-averaged
form averages this same local quantity over a magnetic flux surface without
changing the orbit-class selection.

The trace combines the [parallel co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and the
[perpendicular co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure):
$P_{\mathrm{co,fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{co,fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{co,fast}})/3$,
where $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the field-aligned kinetic stress
and $P_{\perp,\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the mean stress per transverse direction
for the same population. This orbit-selected contribution is part of
[fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure), not the all-orbit
fast-particle pressure itself.

NAMES.name: parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged stress along the magnetic field carried by
suprathermal particles whose untrapped orbits follow the plasma-current
direction, including directed motion.
NAMES.long:
The parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned kinetic
stress of suprathermal particles, averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
Co-passing particles occupy untrapped guiding-center orbits whose
orbit-averaged toroidal motion follows the plasma current.

In the nonrelativistic kinetic description, this component is defined by the
parallel second velocity moment:

$$
p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}(S) = \left\langle m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_S
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged
parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure of species $s$, $S$ is the
magnetic flux surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_S$ denotes its
volume-weighted thin-shell average. Here $m_s$ is the particle mass,
$f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing suprathermal portion
of the species distribution function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$
is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
parallel velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b}$, where
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity applies to the fast population of the represented species, not
a total over all fast-ion species. Multiple fast-particle distribution
contributions for that species add linearly. The velocity moment is not
centered on the population's mean velocity, so directed parallel motion
contributes. Thermal particles, trapped particles, counter-passing
particles, and transverse stress are excluded.

It is the co-passing orbit-class contribution to the [parallel fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure). Its relationship to the
[co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure)
is $\langle
p_s^{\mathrm{co,fast}}\rangle_S=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}})/3$,
where $p_s^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the local kinetic trace pressure and
$p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged transverse
stress per perpendicular degree of freedom for the same species and orbit
class. Thus the parallel component is not the isotropic trace pressure.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged transverse kinetic stress of nonthermal particles on
untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion follows the plasma
current.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure is the
flux-surface-averaged field-perpendicular component of the kinetic stress of
a represented nonthermal particle species. Co-passing particles occupy
untrapped guiding-center orbits with orbit-averaged toroidal motion in the
plasma-current direction.

The component is defined by the transverse second moment of the co-passing
fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\psi)=\left\langle\int_{\mathcal{C}_s(\mathbf{x})}\frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2}\,f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the perpendicular
co-passing fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels the represented species,
$\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is position,
$\mathcal{C}_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset belonging to
co-passing orbits at that position, $m_s$ is the particle mass,
$f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element. The squared transverse speed is
$v_\perp^2=|\mathbf{v}-(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|^2$, where
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The factor of one-half gives the mean stress in
the two field-perpendicular directions.

The brackets denote a normalized magnetic-flux-surface average with weight
proportional to $dS/|\nabla\psi|$, where $dS$ is the surface-area element
and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux label. Thus the
quantity is a surface average, not a local stress at one point.

Only the co-passing nonthermal population contributes; thermal, trapped, and
counter-passing particles are excluded. Multiple fast-particle populations
of the represented species contribute additively, not through a
density-weighted mean; no all-species or all-charge-state total is implied.
Particle velocities are used without subtracting the mean flow, so
perpendicular directed-motion stress is retained.

Together with the [parallel co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure), this component
determines the [co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) through
$p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}=(p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}+2p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}})/3$,
where $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is one-third of the kinetic-stress
trace and $p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the corresponding
field-parallel component, with the same population restriction and
flux-surface averaging.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
One-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by suprathermal particles on
untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma
current, including directed-motion contributions.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress
trace carried by suprathermal particles on counter-passing guiding-center
orbits. These particles are untrapped and have orbit-averaged toroidal
motion opposite to the plasma current.

For a nonrelativistic species, the local pressure is defined by the
restricted second velocity moment:

$$
p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{3}\int_{\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the counter-passing
fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels the specified particle species, $m_s$ is
its particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its suprathermal distribution
function, $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space
region belonging to counter-passing orbits at that position, and $d^3v$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

The velocity moment does not subtract the population mean velocity, so
directed motion contributes alongside random motion. Only the suprathermal
counter-passing population is included; thermal particles, [co-passing fast
particles](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure), and [trapped fast
particles](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure) are excluded. Contributions
from multiple represented fast-particle populations of the specified species
add linearly, rather than forming a density-weighted mean; no sum over
different species is implied.

The definition retains local spatial variation. A flux-surface average
averages this same local moment and is not intrinsic to the quantity's
definition.

This is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to [fast-particle
pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure). Its component relationship is
$p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s}+2p_{\perp,s})/3$, where
$p_{\parallel,s}$ is the [parallel counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and
$p_{\perp,s}$ is the [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure),
averaged over the two transverse directions relative to the local magnetic
field. The trace combines these components without requiring them to be
equal; it is neither a single directional component nor an assumption of an
isotropic distribution.

NAMES.name: parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Parallel pressure is the kinetic-stress component along the magnetic field,
including directed motion, carried by suprathermal particles on untrapped
orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current.
Flux-surface averaging aggregates this same component without changing its
orbit-class or parallel-component scope.
NAMES.long:
Parallel counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the component of kinetic
stress along the local magnetic-field direction, carried by suprathermal
particles on counter-passing orbits. Counter-passing particles are untrapped
and have orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposite to the plasma-current
direction; the uncentered moment includes directed parallel motion.

The local component is the second velocity moment of the counter-passing
suprathermal distribution:

$$
p_{parallel,mathrm{cp,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} v_\parallel^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is this pressure, $s$ labels a
fast-particle species, $c$ labels its charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of
species $s$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{b}$ is the velocity component parallel
to $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic
field, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the phase-space number distribution of
fast particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$,
$\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset at
$\mathbf{x}$ associated with their counter-passing orbits, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The subscripts $\mathrm{cp}$ and
$\mathrm{fast}$ denote counter-passing and suprathermal particles,
respectively.

The quantity applies to the suprathermal population and is summed additively
over fast-particle species and all charge states. It excludes thermal
particles, trapped particles, co-passing particles, and stress perpendicular
to the magnetic field. The local component and its flux-surface average have
the same population and orbit-class scope; the average aggregates the local
component over a magnetic surface.

This is the counter-passing contribution to [parallel fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure), which includes parallel
stress from other fast-particle orbit classes. Together with the
[perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), it
determines the [counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), the one-third trace
of the kinetic stress for the same population:
$p_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}})/3$,
where $p_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the counter-passing fast-particle pressure
and $p_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the perpendicular counter-passing
fast-particle pressure.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Local kinetic stress per degree of freedom perpendicular to the magnetic
field, carried by suprathermal particles on untrapped orbits whose
orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current; its
flux-surface-averaged form is the average of this local quantity over a
magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the mean of the two
kinetic-stress components perpendicular to the local magnetic field, carried
by suprathermal particles on counter-passing orbits. These are untrapped
orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current.

For a species $s$, the local perpendicular pressure is the transverse second
moment of its fast-particle distribution restricted to counter-passing
trajectories:

$$
p_{perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{2}\int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s}(\mathbf{x})} v_\perp^2 f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

Here $p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is the perpendicular counter-passing
fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels a fast-particle species, $m_s$ is its
particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
and $v_\perp$ is the magnitude of its component perpendicular to the local
magnetic field. The function $f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the distribution
function of that species' suprathermal particles, and
$\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset
corresponding to counter-passing trajectories at $\mathbf{x}$. The element
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The factor one-half averages
the stresses in the two perpendicular directions; the moment retains
directed-motion contributions rather than subtracting the population's mean
velocity.

The quantity applies to suprathermal particles in the counter-passing
population and excludes thermal particles, trapped particles, co-passing
particles, and the field-parallel stress. It is defined locally; its
flux-surface-averaged form is the average of the local pressure over a
magnetic flux surface. When a total over fast-particle species is
represented, the species contributions are added directly.

For the same counter-passing population, the [counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), which is one-third
of the kinetic-stress trace, satisfies
$p_s^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}})/3$.
Here $p_s^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is that scalar trace pressure,
$p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is the [parallel counter-passing
fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), and
$p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is this perpendicular component. Thus this
quantity is neither the sum of the two perpendicular stresses nor the full
scalar trace pressure.

NAMES.name: fast_current_density
NAMES.short:
Fast-particle current density is the signed conventional electric-charge
flux per unit area carried by fast particles and resolved by magnetic-orbit
class.
NAMES.long:
Fast-particle current density is the signed conventional charge-flux density
carried by fast particles. It is an orbit-resolved contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), with passing and trapped populations
represented as distinct contributions.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment
restricted to a selected magnetic-orbit class:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{fast},\mathcal{O}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_{s\in\mathrm{fast}}q_s\int_{\mathcal{O}}\mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes included
fast-particle species, $q_s$ is particle charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_s$ is the velocity-space distribution function, and
$\mathcal{O}$ is the selected orbit class.

The orbit class may be co-passing, counter-passing, or trapped, as
represented by [co-passing fast current
density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density), [counter-passing fast
current density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density), and [trapped
fast current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). Compensating
electron and thermal-ion return-current contributions are excluded from the
fast-particle contribution; they belong to other components of the total
current density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected scalar projection of the
fast-particle charge flux is aligned with the positive direction defining
that projection.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_current_density
NAMES.short:
Co-passing fast-particle current density is the signed conventional
electric-charge flux per unit area carried by fast particles on co-passing,
untrapped guiding-center orbits. It is a vector orbit-class contribution and
excludes compensating electron and thermal-ion return currents.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing fast-particle current density is the signed conventional
charge-flux density carried by fast particles on co-passing, untrapped
guiding-center orbits. It is the co-passing orbit-class contribution to
[current density](name:current_density), not the sum over all fast-particle
orbit classes.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment
restricted to the co-passing orbit class:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{fast,co}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_{s\in\mathrm{fast}} q_s \int_{\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{co}}} \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes included
fast-particle species, $q_s$ is the particle charge of species $s$,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the velocity-space distribution
function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the velocity-space subset whose
guiding-center orbit invariants classify the particle as co-passing.

Specific scalar components, such as [toroidal co-passing fast current
density](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density), are projections of
this vector; the vector quantity itself is not limited to the $\hat{\phi}$
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is
distinct from [counter-passing fast current
density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density) and [trapped fast
current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). Compensating electron
and thermal-ion return-current contributions are excluded; they belong to
other components of the total current density.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected scalar projection of the
co-passing fast-particle charge flux is aligned with the positive direction
defining that projection.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_current_density
NAMES.short:
Electric current density contributed by counter-passing fast particles on
guiding-center orbits, excluding thermal and compensating return-current
contributions.
NAMES.long:
Electric current density contributed by fast particles classified as
counter-passing guiding-center orbits, excluding thermal and compensating
return-current contributions. It represents the charged fast-particle
contribution to the local plasma current rather than the total plasma
current.

The current density is the first velocity moment of the selected
fast-particle distributions:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_a q_a \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{cp}}} \mathbf{v}\, f_a(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $a$ identifies an included fast-particle
species or charge state, $q_a$ is its particle charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_a$ is its phase-space distribution, and
$\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ selects the counter-passing fast-particle
population. It is an orbit-resolved member of the broader [fast current
density](name:fast_current_density) family; [co-passing fast current
density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density) represents the corresponding
co-passing class. A toroidal, flux-surface-averaged specialization is
[toroidal counter-passing fast current
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis; the toroidal component is positive toward increasing
$\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density carried by co-passing fast particles, averaged over
a magnetic flux surface and excluding compensating electron and thermal-ion
return currents.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density carried by co-passing fast particles is the
flux-surface-averaged toroidal projection of [co-passing fast-particle
current density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density). The particles are
nonthermal and follow untrapped guiding-center orbits whose toroidal transit
is in the plasma-current direction.

The averaged projection is defined by:

$$
j_\phi = \left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co,fast}}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right\rangle
$$

where $j_\phi$ is this toroidal current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the co-passing fast-particle
current-density vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector
toward increasing toroidal angle. The brackets denote a volume-weighted
average over an infinitesimal shell between neighboring magnetic flux
surfaces. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the co-passing portion of the fast-particle distribution contributes.
Multiple distributions representing the same fast-particle species are
superposed. Compensating electron and thermal-ion drag currents are
excluded, so this quantity is not the net driven current density including
those return currents.

This is one signed component contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), not the magnitude of its vector parent. The
[toroidal counter-passing fast-particle current
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density) and [toroidal
trapped fast-particle current
density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density) describe separate
orbit-class contributions and are not included here. Co-passing
classification is relative to the plasma-current direction and does not
itself imply a positive toroidal component.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the surface-averaged conventional
fast-particle charge flux is directed toward increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_current_density
NAMES.short:
Trapped fast-particle current density is the vector electric current density
carried by fast particles on magnetically trapped orbits, excluding
compensating electron and thermal-ion return currents.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-particle current density is the contribution to electric
current density from fast particles whose guiding-center orbits are
magnetically trapped. It excludes compensating currents carried by electrons
and thermal ions and is not the total plasma current density.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, its kinetic definition is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{trap}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s q_s \int_{\mathrm{trapped, fast}} \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,\mathrm{d}^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
and $f_s$ is its phase-space distribution. The integration is restricted to
the trapped fast-particle population. This quantity is an orbit-selected
contribution to [fast current density](name:fast_current_density); [toroidal
trapped fast current density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density) is
its toroidal component, while [co-passing fast current
density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density) represents a distinct
passing-orbit contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of the conventional
electric current-density vector points along the corresponding positive
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density
NAMES.short:
Toroidal current density is the flux-surface-averaged charge flux carried by
magnetically trapped fast particles in the toroidal direction, excluding
electron and thermal-ion back-currents.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density carried by trapped fast particles is the
magnetic-flux-surface average of the toroidal projection of [trapped
fast-particle current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). It
represents conventional electric-charge transport by nonthermal particles on
magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits.

The averaged projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast,tr}} = \left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right\rangle
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal
trapped-fast-particle current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is
the local trapped-fast-particle current-density vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the
toroidal unit vector, and angle brackets denote the magnetic-flux-surface
average. The direction $\hat{\phi}$ follows increasing toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the trapped portion of the specified species' fast-particle
distribution contributes; multiple included fast populations of that species
are superposed linearly. Passing fast particles and compensating electron
and thermal-ion back-currents are excluded. This is a signed,
surface-averaged component, not a local value, a vector magnitude, or the
total plasma [current density](name:current_density).

Unlike this direct fast-particle contribution, [toroidal trapped current
density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) also includes the
collisional drag back-current attributed to trapped particles.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the flux-surface-averaged conventional charge
transport by trapped fast particles follows increasing $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population at a plasma
location, summed over all ion species and charge states and excluding the
Maxwellian thermal ion contribution.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion pressure is the kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion
population, defined through the second central velocity moment of the
fast-ion distribution function. It is summed over all ion species and all
charge states present in that suprathermal population, so it is the
charge-state-summed aggregate of [fast-ion charge-state
pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure). It excludes the Maxwellian
thermal ion contribution represented by [thermal ion
pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure).

The tensor is defined as the species and charge-state sum of the second
central velocity moment:

$$
\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\alpha,q} m_\alpha \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}) \otimes (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q})\, f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion pressure tensor,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\alpha$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes charge
state, $m_\alpha$ is the ion mass for species $\alpha$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}$ is the mean velocity of the
corresponding fast-ion subpopulation, $f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
suprathermal distribution function whose velocity-space integral gives
number density, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\otimes$
denotes the dyadic product.

The tensor may be anisotropic. The scalar fast-ion contribution entering the
isotropic [ion pressure](name:ion_pressure) is the trace pressure
$p_{\mathrm{fast}}=\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}/3$; for a
gyrotropic distribution in the local right-handed field-aligned basis
$(\hat{e}_1,\hat{e}_2,\hat{b})$, with $\hat{e}_1 \times \hat{e}_2=\hat{b}$
and $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, this is
$p_{\mathrm{fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})/3$.
Here $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ and $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ are the
normal stresses parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic-field
direction; related directional quantities include [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), [perpendicular total
fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure), [parallel
fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure), and [perpendicular
fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure). The scalar
fast-ion contribution combines with the thermal contribution in total ion
pressure when the same population aggregation is used.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Pressure of fast ions of one species is their kinetic stress from random
motion along the magnetic field, summed over all charge states and excluding
thermal-ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of fast ions of a specified species is the field-parallel principal
component of their gyrotropic pressure tensor, summed over all charge
states. Together with the [perpendicular fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure), it characterizes the
species' anisotropic suprathermal stress relative to the local magnetic
field.

The parallel pressure is defined by the charge-state-summed second central
velocity moment:

$$
p_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_c m_i \int \left[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{i,c})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right]^2 f_{i,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-ion pressure of
species $i$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $c$ labels ionic charge states, $m_i$
is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$f_{i,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion number distribution in velocity
space for species $i$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{u}_{i,c}$ is that
distribution's mean velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ follows
the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

Only the suprathermal population of the specified ion species is included.
Contributions from all charge states are added directly, not
density-weighted; each contribution is a [charge-state-resolved parallel
fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_state_pressure). Thermal-ion
pressure, electron pressure, and directed bulk-flow momentum flux are
excluded. This component is neither the perpendicular pressure nor an
isotropic trace average.

Summing this quantity over ion species gives the [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), which is the
field-parallel component of the aggregate [fast-ion pressure
tensor](name:fast_ion_pressure).
