NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Pressure of fast ions of a specified species is the gyrotropic stress
perpendicular to the local magnetic field, summed over all ionic charge
states.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of fast ions of a specified species is the principal
field-perpendicular component of their gyrotropic pressure tensor, summed
over all ionic charge states. Together with the field-parallel component, it
characterizes the anisotropic stress of that suprathermal ion population.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse second central
velocity moment:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{fast},\perp}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_q \int \frac{m_i w_\perp^2}{2}\,f_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{w})\,d^3w
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{fast},\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-ion pressure,
$i$ labels the specified ion species, $q$ labels its ionic charge states,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_i$ is the ion mass, and $f_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}$
is the fast-ion velocity distribution for species $i$ and charge state $q$.
The random velocity $\mathbf{w}$ is measured relative to the mean velocity
of the corresponding fast-ion charge-state population, and $d^3w$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The squared perpendicular random speed is
$w_\perp^2=|\mathbf{w}-(\mathbf{w}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|^2$, where
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The factor one-half averages the two transverse
degrees of freedom.

This quantity includes only nonthermal ions of the specified species. Its
charge-state aggregation is a direct additive sum of the [perpendicular
fast-ion charge-state
pressures](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure), not a
density-weighted mean. It excludes thermal-ion pressure, electron pressure,
and directed bulk-flow stress; it is neither the parallel pressure component
nor the isotropic trace pressure.

This species-resolved component contributes to the [fast-ion pressure
tensor](name:fast_ion_pressure). Summing it over all ion species gives the
[perpendicular total fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure), which is distinct
from the single-species quantity defined here.

NAMES.name: total_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Gyrotropic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population summed over
all charge states, characterized by independent components parallel and
perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The total fast-ion pressure represents the full gyrotropic kinetic stress of
the suprathermal ion population, summed over all charge states, as a
contribution to the plasma pressure balance. Fast ions — including
fusion-born alpha particles, neutral-beam-injected ions, and
radio-frequency-accelerated ions — retain pressure anisotropy with
$P_\parallel \neq P_\perp$ relative to the local magnetic field because
their pitch-angle scattering rate is slow compared with their energy
transfer rate to the bulk plasma. The anisotropic structure is fully
captured by the two independent scalar components [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular total
fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure).

For a gyrotropic fast-ion distribution, the pressure tensor is:

$$
\overleftrightarrow{P}_\text{fast} = P_{\perp}\,\overleftrightarrow{I} + (P_{\parallel} - P_{\perp})\,\hat{b}\hat{b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel}$ and $P_{\perp}$ are the parallel and perpendicular
scalar pressure components, $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit
vector along the local magnetic field, and $\overleftrightarrow{I}$ is the
identity tensor.

Fast-ion pressure profiles are obtained from kinetic particle-following or
Fokker-Planck solvers that evolve the suprathermal distribution function
under collisional slowing-down and pitch-angle scattering. The anisotropic
fast-ion stress enters the MHD force balance and can drive
pressure-anisotropy-driven instabilities when $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$
departs significantly from unity. The parent quantity
[fast_ion_pressure](name:fast_ion_pressure) provides per-charge-state
resolution.

In high-performance discharges with strong neutral beam or ion cyclotron
resonance heating, fast-ion pressure can reach 10–50% of the total plasma
pressure in the core, with anisotropy ratios $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$
ranging from near unity for isotropized distributions to several for
strongly beam-like distributions.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total fast-ion parallel pressure, summed over all fast-ion species and
charge states, is the gyrotropic stress component along the local magnetic
field.
NAMES.long:
The parallel total fast-ion pressure is the principal field-aligned
component of the gyrotropic pressure tensor of suprathermal ions, summed
over all fast-ion species and charge states. It is one of the two
independent components that determine the anisotropic pressure represented
by [total fast-ion pressure](name:total_fast_ion_pressure).

It is defined by the projection

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}} = \hat{\mathbf b} \cdot \overleftrightarrow{\mathbf P}_{\mathrm{fast}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel pressure component,
$\overleftrightarrow{\mathbf P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the total fast-ion
pressure tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf b} = \mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit
vector along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf B$. The complementary
[perpendicular total fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure) describes stress
transverse to the field; equality of the two components corresponds to an
isotropic fast-ion pressure.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total fast-ion perpendicular pressure, summed over all fast-ion species and
charge states, is the gyrotropic stress component perpendicular to the local
magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular total fast-ion pressure is the principal
field-perpendicular component of the gyrotropic pressure tensor of
suprathermal ions, summed over all fast-ion species and charge states. It is
one of the two independent components that characterize anisotropic fast-ion
stress relative to the local magnetic field, the other being the [parallel
total fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure).

The perpendicular component is defined by the transverse second moment of
the fast-ion distribution:

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c \int \frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2}\, f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3 v
$$

where $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular total fast-ion pressure
at position $\mathbf{x}$, $s$ labels fast-ion species, $c$ labels charge
state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $f_{s,c}$ is the fast-ion
distribution function for species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $d^3 v$ is the velocity-space volume element, $v_\perp^2
= |\mathbf{v} - (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|^2$ is the squared velocity
component perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction,
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field.

This quantity applies only to the suprathermal ion population. The
aggregation convention is a direct additive sum over all fast-ion species
and over all charge states; it is not a density-weighted mean. It excludes
thermal-ion pressure, electron pressure, species-specific fast-ion pressure,
charge-state-resolved perpendicular fast-ion pressure, and the field-aligned
fast-ion component.

As a component of the [total fast-ion
pressure](name:total_fast_ion_pressure), $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ enters
the gyrotropic tensor relation
$\overleftrightarrow{P}_\mathrm{fast}=P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}\overleftrightarrow{I}+(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}-P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})\hat{b}\hat{b}$,
where $\overleftrightarrow{P}_\mathrm{fast}$ is the total fast-ion pressure
tensor, $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), and
$\overleftrightarrow{I}$ is the identity tensor. The [perpendicular fast-ion
charge-state pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure) is
a charge-state-resolved contribution; summing the corresponding
perpendicular contributions over the included fast-ion species and charge
states gives this total component.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_energy
NAMES.short:
Fast-particle energy is the total kinetic energy stored in a specified
suprathermal population, integrated over the plasma volume and including
parallel and perpendicular motion.
NAMES.long:
Fast-particle energy is the global kinetic-energy content of a specified
suprathermal particle population. It includes motion both parallel and
perpendicular to the local magnetic field, without restricting the
population to ions or to a particular energization mechanism.

The defining distribution moment is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{fast}}(t)=\sum_s\int_V d^3x\int \varepsilon_s(\mathbf{p})\,f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{p},t)\,d^3p
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle energy, $t$ is time, $s$
indexes the included particle species, $V$ is the plasma volume,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{p}$ is particle momentum, $\varepsilon_s$
is the single-particle kinetic energy excluding rest energy, and
$f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle phase-space number density.

Only the specified fast populations contribute; the background thermal
population is excluded. Contributions from included species are summed, and
multiple fast populations of the same species are superposed without double
counting particles. This is the volume-integrated fast-population
specialization of [particle energy](name:particle_energy), not an individual
particle's energy coordinate.

The [parallel](name:parallel_fast_particle_energy) and
[perpendicular](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy) quantities
partition the kinetic energy according to motion along and across the local
magnetic field. In the nonrelativistic limit, their sum equals the total
fast-particle energy, with the perpendicular contribution including both
perpendicular degrees of freedom. Unlike [diamagnetic
energy](name:diamagnetic_energy), this quantity is a full fast-particle
kinetic-energy moment rather than a perpendicular-pressure-based measure
that also includes thermal populations.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_particle_energy
NAMES.short:
Parallel fast-particle energy is the volume-integrated energy content of the
parallel degree of freedom of a specified suprathermal particle population,
defined as three-halves of its parallel-pressure integral.
NAMES.long:
Parallel fast-particle energy is the energy content associated with the
parallel degree of freedom of a specified suprathermal particle population.
It is integrated over the plasma volume, rather than being a local energy
density.

The defining pressure-integral relation is:

$$
W_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{\mathcal{V}} p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}\,dV
$$

where $W_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-particle energy,
$\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume, $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
parallel pressure of the specified fast-particle population, and $dV$ is a
differential volume element.

The integral covers the plasma volume and the specified fast (suprathermal)
population. It excludes bulk thermal particles and the population's
perpendicular-motion contribution; contributions over the volume are
accumulated, not averaged.

This is the parallel contribution to [fast-particle
energy](name:fast_particle_energy). The [perpendicular fast-particle
energy](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy) is the corresponding
contribution from motion perpendicular to the local magnetic field;
together, these directional contributions distinguish the components of the
same population's kinetic energy.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local
temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its
radial and poloidal component forms.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E}$ quantifies
gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in a
specified charge state $z$, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between
the density-normalized diffusive ion heat flux for that charge state and the
local ion temperature gradient for the same charge state. It is the
charge-state-resolved specialization of the [ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from
convective, advective, or $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat
flux.

The defining relation for the density-normalized diffusive energy flux of
charge state $z$ is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}\,\nabla T_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux
carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their number density, and
$T_{i,z}$ is their [temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature). The
minus sign denotes transport down the local temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not an
aggregation over charge states. The corresponding charge-state-aggregated
[ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is
a density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states. Directional
children include radial_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient, for
the component associated with $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height, and
poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient, for the poloidal
component.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective diffusivity, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
poloidal diffusive thermal-energy flux of one ion charge state to its local
temperature gradient.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient in the poloidal direction
quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by
ions in one specified charge state. It is the poloidal directional
specialization of the [ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and
excludes convective, advective, and other nondiffusive contributions.

The defining relation for the density-normalized poloidal diffusive energy
flux is:

$$
\frac{Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}^{\mathrm{pol}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{pol}}\,\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}} T_{i,z}
$$

where $Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component of
the diffusive thermal-energy flux, $n_{i,z}$ is the number density of ion
charge state $z$, $T_{i,z}$ is its temperature, and
$\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}}T_{i,z}$ is the poloidal component of its local
temperature gradient.

This coefficient applies to one specified charge state and is not aggregated
over charge states. It is distinct from the ion-level [poloidal ion energy
diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and
the broader [poloidal total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Energy effective diffusivity (in the poloidal direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
radial diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its
local temperature gradient.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient in the radial direction
quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by
ions in one specified charge state. It is the radial directional
specialization of the [ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), applying
to the component along increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation for the density-normalized radial diffusive energy
flux of charge state $z$ is:

$$
\frac{Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff},R}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E,R}\,\frac{\partial T_{i,z}}{\partial R}
$$

where $Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff},R}$ is the radial component of the diffusive
thermal energy flux carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their
number density, $T_{i,z}$ is their
[temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature), and $D_{i,z,E,R}$ is this
radial diffusion coefficient. The minus sign denotes radial transport down
the local radial temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not an
aggregation over charge states. It excludes convective, advective, and $E
\times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux; the
charge-state-aggregated [ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is a density-weighted
mean over all ion species and charge states. Other directional
specializations include the [parallel ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
and the [poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the collisionless
free-streaming upper bound on momentum-flux density for a specified ion
charge state, applied component-by-component in multi-fluid edge plasma
transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state momentum coefficient is the charge-state-resolved ion
specialization of
[momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
providing one dimensionless limiter factor per spatial transport direction
for momentum flux attributed to a specific ion charge state in multi-fluid
edge plasma transport closures.

Each vector component $\alpha_s$ bounds the corresponding directional
momentum-flux density through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux
estimate for charge state $s$, and $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s
v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming reference scale with $m_s$ the
ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the
thermal speed. When $|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_s
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm\alpha_s
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

The vector components provide separate limiter factors for each spatial
direction; the
[parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
is the scalar projection onto the magnetic-field direction. The
neutral-particle analog is
[neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
Each component is intrinsically non-negative.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Nonnegative factor scaling the collisionless free-streaming cap on the flux
of magnetic-field-parallel momentum carried by a specified ion charge state
in edge-plasma transport.
NAMES.long:
This coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming bound on transport
of the magnetic-field-parallel component of [momentum](name:momentum)
carried by one specified ion charge state in an edge-plasma fluid closure.
Parallel identifies the transported momentum component, not necessarily the
direction in which that momentum crosses a surface.

The coefficient enters the flux bound as:

$$
\left|\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{lim}}(\hat{n})\right| \leq \alpha_{s,\parallel}\,\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}(\hat{n})
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\parallel$ denotes
the local magnetic-field direction, $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal to the
transport surface, $\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited flux of
parallel momentum through that surface, $\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is
the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude, and
$\alpha_{s,\parallel}$ is this limiter coefficient. The reference magnitude
and the detailed limiting function are closure-dependent.

The coefficient is nonnegative and charge-state resolved; it is neither
summed nor averaged over charge states. It scales the flux-magnitude bound
without reversing the underlying flux direction and is distinct from a
momentum diffusivity or damping rate.

It specializes the [ion charge-state momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) to
magnetic-field-parallel momentum. The [diamagnetic momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) instead
limits transport of the diamagnetic momentum contribution.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient
that scales the free-streaming bound on poloidal momentum transport for a
specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge
state in the poloidal direction. It is the poloidal component of the vector
quantity [ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

The coefficient $lpha_{s,\box{pol}}$ bounds the poloidal momentum-flux
density through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \, \Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive
poloidal momentum-flux estimate for charge state $s$, and
$\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming
reference scale with $m_s$ the ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number
density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the thermal speed. When
$|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}}
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at
$\pm\alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}}\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise the diffusive
value is recovered unchanged.

The poloidal component is distinct from the [parallel ion charge-state
momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which projects onto the magnetic-field direction, and from the [toroidal ion
charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which applies in the geometric toroidal direction. The coefficient is
intrinsically non-negative; the sign of the limited poloidal momentum flux
is inherited from the reference poloidal momentum-flux estimate.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless toroidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient
that scales the free-streaming bound on toroidal momentum transport for a
specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge
state in the geometric toroidal direction. It is the toroidal component of
the vector quantity [ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

If $\Pi_{\phi}$ is the modeled toroidal momentum flux and
$\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{fs}}$ is its collisionless free-streaming reference
bound, the limiter constrains their magnitudes according to

$$
|\Pi_{\phi}| \leq \alpha_{\phi}|\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{fs}}|
$$

where $\alpha_{\phi}$ is this coefficient and the toroidal direction is the
direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame. The coefficient limits the magnitude of the modeled flux; it does not
define the flux direction or its sign. The corresponding axis-specific
quantity for poloidal transport is the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum
flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

sources.parent_definition: Momentum flux limiter coefficient, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective coefficient relating an ion population's density-normalized
diffusive energy flux to its temperature gradient, without selecting a
transport direction.
NAMES.long:
The ion energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven energy
transport for the ion population represented by an energy-transport closure.
It is the ion specialization of the [energy diffusion
coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient), distinct from coefficients
describing particle transport and from separately represented convective or
advective energy fluxes.

The defining scalar Fickian closure is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_i} = -D_{i,W}\,\nabla T_i
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux
carried by the included ions, $n_i$ is their number density, $T_i$ is their
temperature expressed as thermal energy per particle, and $D_{i,W}$ is the
effective diffusion coefficient. The subscripts $i$ and $W$ identify ions
and the energy channel, respectively, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial
gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport for a positive
coefficient.

At species level, the population includes all charge states: number density
is summed, while temperature is the density-weighted mean over all charge
states. The coefficient is an intensive effective closure coefficient, not a
sum of charge-state coefficients. When charge states share the same
temperature gradient, their aggregate coefficient is their density-weighted
mean over all charge states. The [ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead
applies to one specified charge state.

No restriction to a thermal-ion subpopulation or particular transport
direction is imposed. The [thermal-ion
specialization](name:thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) restricts the
population, while the [total-ion
specialization](name:total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) describes the
aggregate ion energy channel. Directional variants such as the [parallel ion
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) select a
transport direction; the direction-unspecified parent does not imply
isotropic transport.

NAMES.name: neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless factor setting the free-streaming upper bound on flux of a
neutral species’ diamagnetic momentum component in edge-fluid transport
closures.
NAMES.long:
The neutral-species diamagnetic momentum flux limiter coefficient scales the
collisionless free-streaming bound on transport of the diamagnetic component
of [momentum](name:momentum) in edge-fluid closures. Flux limiting restricts
the corresponding momentum-flux magnitude without reversing its direction.

The limiting magnitude is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\max} = \alpha_{0,\mathrm{dia}}\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\alpha_{0,\mathrm{dia}}$ is this nonnegative coefficient,
$\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\max}$ is the maximum permitted momentum-flux
magnitude, and $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative
collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude for the same momentum
component. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population. This relation
specifies the cap, not a particular interpolation between diffusive and
free-streaming transport.

The coefficient applies to a specified neutral species without selecting an
individual neutral state; it is not a total-plasma coefficient. The
diamagnetic label identifies the transported momentum component, not the
direction in which its flux crosses an oriented surface, and does not imply
a charge-driven diamagnetic drift of neutral particles.

This is the neutral-species specialization of the [diamagnetic momentum flux
limiter coefficient](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
The [neutral-state diamagnetic momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_state_diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
instead applies to a specified neutral state; the species-level coefficient
is not defined as a sum of state-resolved coefficients.

NAMES.name: neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Fickian transport coefficient relating a neutral population's
density-normalized diffusive thermal-energy flux to its temperature
gradient, without selecting a direction or internal state.
NAMES.long:
The neutral energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven
diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by a specified neutral
population. It is the neutral-population specialization of the [energy
diffusion coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient), without selecting
a transport direction or resolving an internal state.

For a local isotropic diffusive closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{0,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_0} = -D_{0,W}\,\nabla T_0
$$

where $D_{0,W}$ is the neutral energy diffusion coefficient,
$\mathbf{Q}_{0,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the neutral diffusive thermal-energy flux,
$n_0$ is the neutral number density, $T_0$ is the neutral temperature
expressed as thermal energy, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The
subscripts $0$ and $W$ identify the neutral population and energy channel,
respectively. The minus sign gives transport down the temperature gradient
for a positive coefficient.

This is a population-level coefficient, with the included neutral internal
states treated collectively rather than resolved separately. It is not a sum
of internal-state diffusion coefficients. The defining flux excludes
convective and advective contributions to the total neutral thermal-energy
flux, and the coefficient describes energy transport rather than particle
transport.

The [radial](name:radial_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), and
[parallel](name:parallel_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
specializations apply the flux-gradient definition to their corresponding
directional projections. Their coefficients need not be equal; the
direction-agnostic parent does not impose isotropy on these specializations.
The [effective neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:effective_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) retains
the same density-normalized flux-gradient interpretation.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient is the effective down-gradient
flux-gradient coefficient for diffusive transport of neutral-particle
thermal energy in the poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar effective
transport coefficient for diffusive transport of neutral-particle thermal
energy in the poloidal direction. It characterizes only the poloidal
component of the neutral thermal-energy flux associated with gradients of
neutral thermal-energy density.

In a Fickian closure for the poloidal diffusive energy flux, it is the
coefficient $D^{\mathrm{pol}}_{E,n}$ in the flux-gradient relation:

$$
q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,\mathrm{pol}} = -D^{\mathrm{pol}}_{E,n}\,\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}} w_{E,n}
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component of
the diffusive flux of neutral thermal energy, $D^{\mathrm{pol}}_{E,n}$ is
the poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient, $\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}}$
is the directional derivative along the poloidal direction, and $w_{E,n}$ is
the neutral thermal-energy density. The minus sign defines the down-gradient
closure: a positive coefficient gives a diffusive flux toward decreasing
$w_{E,n}$ along the poloidal direction.

The scope is edge-plasma transport of neutral particles represented by one
effective coefficient for the aggregate neutral population. It is not
resolved by neutral internal state, is not an ion charge-state-resolved
quantity, and excludes charged-particle transport. The energy qualifier
denotes thermal energy carried by neutrals; it excludes particle-number
diffusion, momentum diffusion, radiative loss terms, source terms, and
convective energy flux.

This quantity is the poloidal member of [neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is directionally
distinct from [parallel neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It is
closely related to [poloidal neutral energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity), but this name
specifically denotes the coefficient in the neutral thermal-energy-density
flux-gradient law above. The internal-state-resolved counterpart is
[poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
which applies to a specified neutral internal state rather than to the
aggregate neutral population; the analogous internal-state diffusivity is
[poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Parallel fast-particle pressure measures the field-aligned kinetic stress of
a specified suprathermal population, including random and directed particle
motion.
NAMES.long:
The parallel fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned component of the
kinetic stress carried by a specified suprathermal particle distribution.
Together with the perpendicular component, it characterizes pressure
anisotropy relative to the local magnetic field.

For a nonrelativistic species, the defining second velocity moment is:

$$
p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-particle pressure
of species $s$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_s$ is the particle mass,
$f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element. The parallel velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b}$,
where $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

Only the suprathermal population represented by the specified distribution
contributes; thermal-particle pressure is excluded. The quantity is not
restricted to ions and does not imply an all-species or all-charge-state
total. The velocity moment is not centered on the fast-particle mean flow,
so directed parallel motion contributes in addition to random motion.

For the same population and spatial averaging, the [fast-particle
pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) is the trace pressure
$p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}+2p_{\perp,s,\mathrm{fast}})/3$,
where $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ denotes the isotropic trace pressure and
$p_{\perp,s,\mathrm{fast}}$ denotes the [perpendicular fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), the transverse kinetic
stress per perpendicular degree of freedom. Parallel and perpendicular
pressures need not be equal.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Effective Fickian coefficient governing down-gradient ion particle transport
along the local magnetic-field direction in the ion continuity equation.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion particle diffusivity is the effective Fickian coefficient for
particle transport along the local magnetic-field direction. It describes
the diffusive contribution to the particle flux of the ion population
represented by the ion continuity equation.

The diffusive parallel particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,\parallel} = -D_{i,\parallel}\nabla_{\parallel} n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel particle flux density of ion
species $i$, $D_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion particle diffusivity,
$\nabla_{\parallel}$ is the spatial derivative along the local
magnetic-field direction, and $n_i$ is the number density of ion species
$i$.

This quantity applies to ion particle transport only and is resolved for the
ion species represented by the continuity equation. It is not an energy or
momentum diffusivity, and it does not represent the total particle flux,
which may also contain convective or other non-diffusive contributions. The
corresponding radial coefficient [radial ion diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient) describes the analogous
particle transport across the radial direction, while [parallel ion energy
diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusivity) belongs to the distinct
energy-transport channel.

sources.parent_definition: Particle effective diffusivity (in the parallel direction), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Effective parallel particle diffusivity for neutral species, relating
neutral-particle spreading to the local neutral number-density gradient.
NAMES.long:
Effective parallel particle diffusivity for neutral species is the
directional transport coefficient that represents neutral-particle spreading
driven by a neutral number-density gradient. It is the parallel
specialization of [neutral particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_particle_diffusivity), with transport resolved
along the magnetic field.

For the field-parallel direction, the diffusive neutral-particle flux is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\parallel}\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{n}}}{\partial s_{\parallel}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel diffusive
neutral-particle flux, $D_{\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral particle
diffusivity, $n_{\mathrm{n}}$ is neutral-particle number density, and
$s_{\parallel}$ is physical arclength along the magnetic-field direction.
The minus sign specifies transport down the neutral number-density gradient.

This quantity describes particle transport only; it is distinct from the
parallel energy transport coefficient [parallel neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient). Its
directional counterpart is [poloidal neutral particle
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_total_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.short:
Effective field-parallel advection coefficient for transport of aggregate
ion momentum in the edge plasma, distinct from the ion bulk-flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing advective,
non-diffusive transport of aggregate ion [momentum](name:momentum) along the
local magnetic field in the edge plasma. It is a transport-closure
coefficient, not the ion bulk-flow velocity.

For a selected transported momentum component, the convective flux
satisfies:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} g_i
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-parallel convective
flux of that ion momentum component, $V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is
this effective convection coefficient, and $g_i$ is the corresponding
aggregate ion momentum density. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion
population. The parallel direction follows $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf
B/|\mathbf B|$, where $\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic field and
$\hat{\mathbf b}$ is its direction unit vector.

The transported momentum density is summed over the included ion species and
their ionic charge states; electron and neutral momentum are excluded. The
coefficient acts on this aggregate momentum density and is not a sum of
charge-state convection velocities. The parallel qualification specifies the
transport direction, not an additional restriction on the transported
momentum component.

This quantity is the field-parallel projection of [ion momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity). Unlike [total momentum
convection velocity](name:total_momentum_convection_velocity), it applies
specifically to ion momentum rather than total plasma momentum. It is
distinct from [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity): the
convective coefficient multiplies momentum density, whereas the diffusive
coefficient multiplies its negative gradient.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when effective momentum convection is along the
local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_vorticity
NAMES.short:
Projection of the curl of plasma center-of-mass velocity along the local
magnetic field, measuring signed local rotation of the bulk flow about that
direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel vorticity is the component of plasma [vorticity](name:vorticity)
along the local magnetic-field direction. For solid-body rotation, it is
twice the component of a fluid element's angular velocity along that
direction.

The field-aligned projection of the bulk-velocity curl is defined by:

$$
\omega_{\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\boldsymbol{\omega} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}\cdot(\nabla\times\mathbf{v})
$$

where $\omega_{\parallel}$ is parallel vorticity, $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is
the full plasma vorticity vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field,
$|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its direction unit
vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), and $\nabla\times$ is the curl
operator with right-handed orientation.

The scope is the local single-fluid plasma bulk flow wherever the magnetic
field is nonzero. Constituent flows enter through the mass-weighted
center-of-mass velocity; this is not a species- or charge-state-resolved
vorticity. No surface, volume, or time averaging is implied. It is not
vorticity magnitude, flow shear, strain rate, velocity divergence, or
magnetic-field-line twist.

The projection is applied after taking the curl of the full velocity field;
[parallel plasma velocity](name:parallel_plasma_velocity) alone does not
determine it. Unlike [toroidal vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity), which
projects onto the geometric toroidal direction, parallel vorticity follows
the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the bulk-flow curl has a component along the
local magnetic field, corresponding to rotation in the right-handed sense
about that direction.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Flux-surface-averaged kinetic stress of suprathermal particles of one
species per degree of freedom perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular fast-particle pressure is the flux-surface average of the
field-perpendicular component of the gyrotropic kinetic stress carried by
suprathermal particles of a specified species. It represents stress per
transverse degree of freedom, rather than the sum of the two transverse
stresses.

The perpendicular component is defined by the transverse second moment of
the fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{2}\int v_\perp^2 f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular fast-particle
pressure, $s$ labels the specified particle species, $m_s$ is its particle
mass, $f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is its suprathermal distribution function,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v_\perp$ is
the magnitude of the velocity perpendicular to the local magnetic field, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The brackets denote a
normalized flux-surface average with weight proportional to the reciprocal
magnitude of the gradient of a smooth flux-surface label.

This quantity includes only the nonthermal population of the selected
species. Multiple fast-particle populations of that same species are
superposed in the distribution function and therefore contribute additively
to the pressure. It is not a sum over distinct species, is not restricted to
a single orbit class, and excludes the thermal-population pressure. Unlike
the local perpendicular stress, it includes flux-surface averaging.

The corresponding [parallel fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure), denoted by
$p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}$, is the independent field-aligned stress
component. Together they determine the isotropic [fast-particle
pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure), $p_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$, through
$p_s^{\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}})/3$,
with all three quantities referring to the same species, suprathermal
population, and flux-surface average. The parallel and perpendicular
components need not be equal.

NAMES.name: pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density is the vector flux density of conventional
electric charge, equal to electric current per unit area normal to the flow,
for the neoclassical return current that restores current continuity when
the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current is divergent in toroidal magnetic
geometry. It denotes the full vector before scalar projection.
NAMES.long:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the vector
density of conventional electric charge flux associated with the
neoclassical return current in toroidal magnetic confinement geometry. It
restores local current continuity when the pressure-gradient
diamagnetic_current_density has finite divergence caused by magnetic-field
inhomogeneity. It is a contribution to
[current_density](name:current_density) and varies around a magnetic flux
surface while remaining predominantly aligned with the magnetic field.

The defining continuity relation for the pressure-gradient part of the
current is:

$$
\nabla\cdot\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}+\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{B^2}\right)=0
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch-Schlueter current density,
$\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, and $p$ is the total
scalar plasma pressure. The term $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p/B^2$ is the
pressure-gradient diamagnetic current density, so the equation states that
the Pfirsch-Schlueter return current closes its divergence. In the
field-aligned neoclassical representation, the vector is reconstructed from
the parallel amplitude as
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}=j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}\mathbf{b}$ with
$\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$; scalar component names are projections of this
vector.

This quantity excludes bootstrap_current_density, Ohmic current density,
externally driven current density, and the diamagnetic current density
itself, although these may enter the total current balance. The generic name
denotes the unprojected vector; related projections include
[parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density)
along $\mathbf{b}$,
[poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density)
along increasing $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where
$\rho$ labels flux surfaces, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and
[radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density),
[toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density),
and
[vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density)
along $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short:
Poloidal Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the signed poloidal projection
of the neoclassical return current that compensates divergent
pressure-gradient diamagnetic current in toroidal magnetic geometry.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the signed projection of the
[Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density
vector](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) onto the local poloidal
tangent. This return-current contribution restores local current continuity
where the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current is divergent in toroidal
magnetic geometry.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm p}=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\mathbf j_{\mathrm{PS}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm p}$ is the poloidal Pfirsch–Schlüter current density,
$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the parent Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density
vector, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the oriented poloidal unit
tangent. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The poloidal
tangent lies within a plane of constant $\phi$ and is tangent to the
magnetic flux surface. Its orientation follows increasing poloidal angle
$\theta$, whose orientation must be specified by the poloidal-angle
convention.

This quantity is the local net Pfirsch–Schlüter contribution from the
included plasma charge carriers, without species or charge-state resolution.
It is a mechanism-specific component of [current
density](name:current_density), not the total plasma current density, the
parent vector's magnitude, or a flux-surface average; no restriction to the
edge plasma is implied.

The [parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current
density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) projects the same
parent vector onto the magnetic-field direction instead. Its projection
direction is therefore distinct from the geometric poloidal tangent.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional positive charge flows in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short:
Vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the signed height-axis
projection of the neoclassical return current that restores current
continuity in toroidal confinement.
NAMES.long:
Vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the height-axis projection of
the [Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density
vector](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density). This neoclassical return
current restores local current continuity by balancing the divergence of the
pressure-gradient diamagnetic current in toroidal confinement.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{PS},Z} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{PS},Z}$ is the vertical Pfirsch–Schlüter current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector,
and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector parallel to the toroidal
symmetry axis. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is the local edge-plasma contribution to [current
density](name:current_density) associated with the Pfirsch–Schlüter return
current, summed over participating charge carriers rather than resolved by
species or charge state. It is neither the total current density from all
mechanisms nor the magnitude of the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector;
no flux-surface averaging is implied.

Unlike [parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current
density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), which projects
the same vector onto the local magnetic-field direction, this component
projects onto the fixed vertical direction.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density vector
has a component in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming bound on poloidal ion
momentum flux in edge-plasma transport, limiting its magnitude without
reversing its direction.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient sets the collisionless
free-streaming bound on the poloidal component of gradient-driven ion
[momentum](name:momentum) transport in edge-plasma fluid closures. The
poloidal direction follows a magnetic-flux-surface contour in a plane
containing the toroidal symmetry axis, rather than the toroidal or
flux-surface-normal direction.

The coefficient defines the upper bound:

$$
\left|\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}\right| \leq \alpha_{i,\mathrm{p}}\,\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited poloidal ion
momentum flux, $\alpha_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is this nonnegative limiter
coefficient, and $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative
collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude specified by the momentum
closure. The subscripts $i$ and $\mathrm{p}$ identify ions and the poloidal
component. Limiting preserves the direction of the original flux; the bound
does not prescribe a particular interpolation formula.

This coefficient applies at the ion-species level rather than to an
individually resolved charge state. It is a closure parameter, not a sum of
charge-state coefficients, and it excludes electron and neutral momentum
transport. It controls a flux bound rather than the momentum diffusivity
that determines the unrestricted gradient-driven flux.

It is the poloidal member of the component-resolved [ion momentum
flux-limiter coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). The
[poloidal neutral momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) serves
the corresponding limiting role for neutral momentum transport, not for
ions.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming bound on poloidal
neutral momentum flux, limiting its magnitude without reversing its
direction.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient sets the
free-streaming bound on the poloidal component of neutral-particle
[momentum](name:momentum) transport in a fluid closure. It constrains the
modeled flux magnitude rather than specifying a momentum source or a
diffusivity.

The limiting bound is expressed as:

$$
\left|\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}\right| \leq \Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\max} = \alpha_{0,\mathrm{p}}\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited poloidal neutral
momentum-flux component, $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\max}$ is its allowed
magnitude, $\alpha_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is this nonnegative coefficient, and
$\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming
reference magnitude defined by the closure. The subscript $0$ denotes
neutrals and $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal component. Limiting preserves
the direction of the unrestricted flux; this coefficient does not prescribe
a particular interpolation formula.

This is the poloidal directional component of the [neutral momentum
flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
not a magnitude combining all directional components. It applies to the
neutral population represented by the closure, excluding ion momentum
transport. Unlike the [poloidal neutral-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
it is not resolved for an individual neutral internal state; no summation or
averaging rule for state-specific coefficients is implied.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the collisionless free-streaming bound on
ion momentum flux along the major-radius direction, limiting flux magnitude
without reversing its direction.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient scales the collisionless
free-streaming bound on gradient-driven transport of ion
[momentum](name:momentum) along the major-radius direction. It caps the flux
magnitude without reversing its direction. Here radial denotes increasing
major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$\phi$ is toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The limiting flux magnitude is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{i,R}^{\max} = \alpha_{i,R}\,\Pi_{i,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Pi_{i,R}^{\max}$ is the upper bound on the magnitude of the limited
momentum flux, $\alpha_{i,R}$ is this coefficient, and
$\Pi_{i,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming reference
magnitude. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion population, and $R$
identifies the major-radius transport direction. This relation does not
prescribe a particular interpolation between gradient-driven transport and
the limiting bound.

This is the major-radius component of the [ion momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), not a sum over
directional coefficients. It applies to ion momentum transport rather than
neutral momentum transport and is not restricted to one specified ion charge
state. The coefficient is neither a momentum diffusivity nor a spatial
coordinate.

The major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux
surface. The [poloidal ion momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) is a
distinct directional member of the same family.

NAMES.name: radial_total_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.short:
Effective radial velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport
of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma, distinct from the plasma bulk
flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the radial advective,
non-diffusive transport of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma. It is a
transport closure quantity, not an actual plasma bulk flow velocity.

For the selected total-momentum component, the radial convective flux is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}} P_\mathrm{tot}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective
flux of total plasma momentum, $V_{\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}}$ is this
radial total-momentum convection velocity, and $P_\mathrm{tot}$ is the
corresponding total plasma momentum density. The relation applies
componentwise when the transported momentum component is resolved.

The scope is total plasma momentum in the edge plasma, aggregated according
to the total-momentum transport equation and evaluated for radial transport.
It excludes species-resolved, charge-state-resolved, neutral-only, and
separately attributed momentum-convection contributions, and it must not be
interpreted as the plasma bulk flow velocity. As a radial specialization of
the [total momentum convection
velocity](name:total_momentum_convection_velocity), it fixes the transport
direction to the outward radial direction; it differs from the [radial
neutral particle convection
velocity](name:radial_neutral_particle_convection_velocity), which describes
neutral-particle transport rather than total plasma momentum transport.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the associated convective total-momentum flux
is directed toward increasing major-radius coordinate $R$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame for positive transported
total-momentum density.

NAMES.name: radial_total_momentum_flux
NAMES.short:
Radial component of total edge-plasma momentum-flux density, combining
advective, isotropic-pressure, viscous, and turbulent-stress contributions;
radial means the increasing-major-radius R direction in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the radial component of the total edge-plasma momentum-flux
density, representing transport of radial linear momentum rather than stored
momentum or a force source. The radial projection is the component along
$\hat{R}$, the increasing-major-radius direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle and $Z$
is vertical height.

The radial projection of the total momentum-flux tensor through an oriented
surface is:

$$
\Pi_R = \hat{R}\cdot\left(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{n}\right),
\qquad
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \rho_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}} + p_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $\Pi_R$ is the radial total momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total momentum-flux tensor,
$\hat{n}$ is the unit normal defining the orientation of the crossed
surface, $\rho_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the mass density of the aggregated total
plasma population, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its bulk flow velocity,
$p_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity
tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its viscous or turbulent
stress tensor.

The scope is the total edge-plasma population: contributions from all plasma
species and charge states in that population are summed at the level of
momentum flux, including convective, isotropic-pressure, viscous, and
turbulent-stress terms. It excludes single-species or charge-state-resolved
momentum fluxes, scalar pressure alone, stored momentum density, and force
or torque source densities.

This quantity is the radial projection of [total momentum
flux](name:total_momentum_flux). It uses the same radial coordinate
convention as [radial momentum flux](name:radial_momentum_flux): radial
means increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, not distance from the magnetic axis and not a flux-surface-normal
projection; [toroidal total momentum
flux](name:toroidal_total_momentum_flux) is the matched toroidal projection
of the same total momentum-flux tensor.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{n}$
has a component in the $+\hat{R}$ direction, toward increasing major radius
$R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_line_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless line-averaged protium fraction among hydrogenic ions, obtained
by dividing the protium density by the total hydrogenic density along the
same chord.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the fraction of hydrogenic ion content carried by protium
along a specified chord through the plasma. It is a ratio of consistently
line-averaged densities, rather than a local fraction or a volume-averaged
fraction.

$$
f_{\rm H}^{\rm line} = \frac{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}}{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}}
$$

where $f_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium fraction,
$\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium-ion number
density, $\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding deuterium-ion
number density, and $\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding
tritium-ion number density. The symbols H, D, and T denote protium,
deuterium, and tritium, respectively.

The quantity applies to the hydrogenic ion population along one common chord
and aggregates the isotope densities through the total hydrogenic
denominator. Neutral atomic hydrogen and non-hydrogenic species are
excluded. The numerator is the [line-averaged hydrogen
density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator is the
[total hydrogenic density](name:total_hydrogenic_density) under the same
line-averaging convention.

This ratio differs from the [ratio of volume-averaged hydrogen density to
volume-averaged total hydrogenic
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density),
because the latter uses volume-averaged rather than chord-averaged isotope
densities.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_parallel_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude
NAMES.short:
Ratio of the density-weighted mean field-aligned bulk velocity of an ion
species over all ionization charge states to the local total magnetic-field
magnitude.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of the density-weighted mean field-parallel bulk velocity of one ion
species over all its ionization charge states to the local total
magnetic-field magnitude. It expresses signed field-aligned motion scaled by
the inverse total-field strength.

For ion species $i$, the ratio is defined by

$$
K_{i,\parallel} = \frac{v_{i,\parallel}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $K_{i,\parallel}$ is this ratio, $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the [parallel
ion velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity), and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
total magnetic-field vector. The subscript $\parallel$ denotes projection
parallel to $\mathbf{B}$, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the [magnetic-field
magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude). The index $i$ identifies the ion
species.

For each ion species, $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the density-weighted mean over
all ionization charge states, formed from the field-parallel components of
the [charge-state-resolved ion velocities](name:ion_charge_state_velocity).
This is a mean, not a sum or a single-charge-state value; it excludes other
ion species and neutral particles. The numerator and denominator refer to
the same local position, with no spatial aggregation. The ratio is defined
only where the local total magnetic-field magnitude is nonzero.

Multiplying the ratio by the local [magnetic-field
magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude) recovers the [parallel ion
velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity), which is the parallel component of
the [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity). Unlike the [parallel plasma
velocity-to-field
ratio](name:ratio_of_parallel_plasma_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude),
this quantity describes one ion species rather than the aggregate plasma
center-of-mass motion.

$$a/b$$
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the density-weighted mean ion bulk velocity
has a component in the direction of the local total magnetic-field vector.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_total_ion_density_to_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Ratio of total ion number density to free-electron number density, summing
ions over all species and positive charge states and including thermal and
nonthermal populations in both densities.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of total ion number density to free-electron number density at the
same plasma location and time. It expresses the abundance of all ion
particles relative to free electrons, rather than their relative electric
charge or mass.

The local ratio is defined as

$$
R_{i/e} = \frac{n_{i,\mathrm{total}}}{n_e} = \frac{\sum_s\sum_{z\geq 1} n_{s,z}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{i/e}$ denotes this abundance ratio, $n_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the
total ion number density, $n_e$ is the [free-electron number
density](name:electron_density), $s$ indexes ion species, $z$ is the
positive ionic charge number, and $n_{s,z}$ is the [ion charge-state number
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) for species $s$ and charge state
$z$. Each sum includes all populated positive charge states of the
corresponding species.

Both densities include thermal and nonthermal populations. The numerator is
summed over all ion species and charge states without charge weighting;
neutral particles are excluded. The denominator counts free electrons and
excludes bound electrons. This is a local ratio, not a ratio of spatially
averaged densities or a spatial average of local ratios, and it is defined
only when $n_e>0$.

Unlike the [species-specific ion-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density), this quantity
includes every ion species. It is not an effective-charge measure or the
ratio of positive charge density to electron charge-density magnitude.

For a plasma whose charge carriers are positive ions and free electrons,
quasineutrality gives $n_e\simeq\sum_s\sum_{z\geq1}z\,n_{s,z}$.
Consequently, this ratio is approximately the reciprocal of the
ion-number-density-weighted [average charge
number](name:average_charge_number) over the complete ion population.
Multiply charged ions can therefore make it less than unity without implying
a departure from quasineutrality.

NAMES.name: runaway_electron_current_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short:
Runaway-electron current density is the vector density of conventional
electric charge flux carried by suprathermal electrons beyond the
collisional drag limit.
NAMES.long:
Runaway-electron current density $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the vector
density of conventional electric charge flux carried by suprathermal
electrons beyond the collisional drag limit. Because electron charge is
negative, its direction is opposite to the net runaway-electron particle
flux.

It is defined by the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the
runaway-electron distribution:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{x},t)=q_e\int_{\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{RE}}}\mathbf{v}\,f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $q_e$ is electron charge,
$\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-space
distribution, and $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the velocity-space subset
beyond the collisional drag limit.

As a population-restricted form of [current density](name:current_density),
it excludes thermal and nonrunaway electrons, ion contributions, and
displacement-current density. The vector precedes geometric projection and
volume averaging; its field-aligned projection is [parallel runaway-electron
current density](name:parallel_runaway_electron_current_density), while
volume-averaged runaway-electron current density represents its volume
average. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, components are
projections onto the corresponding basis directions.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a stated component or scalar projection of
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ aligns with the positive direction of its
defining basis vector or unit vector.

NAMES.name: parallel_runaway_electron_current_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short:
Parallel runaway-electron current density is the signed field-aligned
component of conventional current density carried by runaway electrons.
NAMES.long:
Parallel runaway-electron current density is the signed field-aligned
contribution to conventional electric-current density carried by runaway
electrons. It is the runaway-electron contribution to [parallel current
density](name:parallel_current_density), not the total plasma current.

For a flux-surface-resolved value, the magnetic-field-weighted definition
is:

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{B_0}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the flux-surface-resolved
parallel runaway-electron current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the
current-density vector carried by runaway electrons, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a
flux-surface average, and $B_0$ is the signed reference vacuum toroidal
magnetic field. The reference field is positive toward increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The contribution includes runaway electrons without restriction to a
particular orbit class; currents carried by other particle populations are
excluded. It is a signed scalar component, not the magnitude of the
runaway-electron current-density vector, a toroidal projection, or total
[current density](name:current_density).

At a point, the field-aligned component is the projection of the
current-density vector onto the local magnetic-field direction,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the local magnetic-field unit
vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude. The flux-surface
value above is not generally the unweighted flux-surface average of this
pointwise component. [Volume-averaged parallel runaway-electron current
density](name:volume_averaged_parallel_runaway_electron_current_density)
instead uses a plasma-volume average.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the flux-surface-averaged contraction
$\langle\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ has
the same sign as $B_0, with $B_0$ positive toward increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of thermal electrons is the local concentration of free
electrons in the bulk thermal population, excluding fast and other
nonthermal electrons. It is a population component of total electron
density, not a fraction.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electron

Total density is the sum of the thermal and fast populations of the species;
thermal excludes the suprathermal particles that fast names.

The local thermal-electron density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of
the thermal-electron distribution:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \int f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-electron number density,
$f_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the distribution of thermal electrons in position and
velocity space, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$
is electron velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
integral covers the thermal component, not the separate fast-electron
population.

This quantity applies to the local bulk thermal-electron population in the
core, edge, and scrape-off layer. Fast, suprathermal, and other nonthermal
electrons are excluded, as are electrons bound in atoms or molecules. The
density is defined locally; any spatial average is an average of this local
quantity rather than part of its population definition.

It is the thermal-population component of [electron
density](name:electron_density), distinct from [fast electron
density](name:fast_electron_density). When thermal and fast electrons form a
complete, nonoverlapping partition, [total electron
density](name:total_electron_density) is the sum of this thermal component
and the fast component.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_energy
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Volume-integrated thermal energy content of the electron population,
excluding fast suprathermal electrons and non-electron plasma populations.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated thermal energy content of the electron population is the
total kinetic energy carried by bulk thermal electrons throughout the
confined plasma. It is an extensive energy content, not a power or
energy-transfer rate, and excludes fast suprathermal electrons and
non-electron populations.

The defining relation is

$$
E_{e,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_\mathrm{plasma}} p_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $E_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the integrated thermal electron energy,
$p_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local thermal electron pressure,
$V_\mathrm{plasma}$ is the confined plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes
position. This quantity is the thermal-electron component of [electron
energy](name:electron_energy); unlike [thermal plasma
energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), it excludes thermal-ion energy.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Thermal electron plasma energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the thermal electron pressure

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress from random motion,
summed over ionic charge states and excluding fast-ion and bulk-flow
contributions.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress arising from random
motion about each thermal population's mean flow. It is the thermal
contribution to [ion pressure](name:ion_pressure), rather than the combined
thermal and nonthermal ion pressure.

The thermal pressure is defined by the central second velocity moment:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{1}{3}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}_i}\sum_c m_s\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c}|^2 f^{\mathrm{th}}_{s,c}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal ion pressure, $\mathcal{S}_i$ is
the selected set of ion species, $s$ labels species, $c$ labels ionic charge
state, $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ is the mean velocity of the corresponding thermal
population, $f^{\mathrm{th}}_{s,c}$ is its local velocity distribution
function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

For a species-resolved quantity, the species set contains only that species.
All ionic charge states are included through a direct additive sum of their
[thermal pressures](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure), not a
density-weighted mean. Fast-ion pressure, electron pressure, and kinetic
stress associated with directed bulk motion are excluded. The quantity is
isotropic pressure, not a separately selected field-parallel or
field-perpendicular stress component.

Summing the species-resolved contributions over every ion species gives
[total thermal ion pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure). That total is
the ion contribution to [thermal plasma
pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure), which additionally includes
thermal-electron pressure.
