NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Total pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress from random
motion, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states, excluding fast
ions and bulk-flow stress.
NAMES.long:
Total pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic part of the kinetic pressure
tensor arising from random motion of all thermal-ion populations. It
combines their thermal stresses rather than selecting one ion species, one
charge state, or one directional pressure component.

The total is defined by summing the centered thermal pressure moments:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{th}} = \sum_s p_s^{\mathrm{th}} = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c}|^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the total thermal-ion pressure,
$s$ labels ion species, $p_s^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal ion
pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure) of species $s$ summed over its ionic
charge states, $c$ labels ionic charge states, $m_s$ is the species mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ is the mean velocity
of the corresponding thermal population, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is its
velocity distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

The aggregation is a direct additive sum over all ion species and ionic
charge states, not a density-weighted mean. It excludes electron pressure,
neutral pressure, fast-ion pressure, and bulk-flow kinetic stress. The word
“total” denotes species aggregation within the thermal-ion population, not
inclusion of nonthermal ions.

Each [thermal ion charge-state
pressure](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure) contributes to its species
pressure and hence to this total. Adding the thermal electron pressure gives
the [thermal plasma pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure).

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short:
Non-negative radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface
coinciding with the internal transport barrier, derived from enclosed
toroidal magnetic flux rather than geometric distance.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier is the
non-negative, radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface on which
the barrier is located. It identifies the barrier by magnetic-surface
position and is not a direct geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux:

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux coordinate,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the
associated magnetic surface, $B_0$ is the positive reference toroidal
magnetic field, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

The locus is the internal transport barrier, represented as a particular
nested magnetic flux surface rather than the entire plasma or a finite
transport-barrier region. This quantity has no species or charge-state
aggregation and is not a spatial average or an integral over a region.

It is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike the [normalized
toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport
barrier](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier),
it retains the radius-like coordinate scale rather than applying boundary
normalization.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal flux coordinate. rho_tor = sqrt(b_flux_tor/(pi*b0)) ~ sqrt(pi*r^2*b0/(pi*b0)) ~ r [m]. The toroidal field used in its definition is indicated under global_quantities/b0
sources.parent_definition: Radial position at which physics quantities are evaluated

NAMES.name: toroidal_vorticity
NAMES.short:
Projection of the curl of plasma center-of-mass velocity along the toroidal
direction, measuring signed local bulk-flow rotation about that direction.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal vorticity is the component of plasma [vorticity](name:vorticity)
along the geometric toroidal direction. For solid-body rotation, it is twice
the toroidal component of a fluid element's angular velocity.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the toroidal
projection is defined by:

$$
\omega_\phi = (\nabla \times \mathbf{v}) \cdot \hat{\phi} = \frac{\partial v_R}{\partial Z} - \frac{\partial v_Z}{\partial R}
$$

where $\omega_\phi$ is toroidal vorticity, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
[center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), $v_R$ and $v_Z$ are
its cylindrical radial and vertical components, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector along increasing toroidal angle, and $\nabla \times$ is the
right-handed curl operator.

The scope is the local single-fluid plasma bulk flow, without restriction to
a particular plasma region or any surface, volume, or time averaging. The
underlying velocity is the mass-weighted mean flow of the constituent plasma
species, not a species- or charge-state-resolved velocity. This quantity is
not vorticity magnitude, flow shear, strain rate, divergence, or
magnetic-field-line twist; it is also distinct from toroidal flow speed and
angular velocity.

Unlike [parallel vorticity](name:parallel_vorticity), which projects the
same curl along the local magnetic field, toroidal vorticity uses the
geometric toroidal direction independently of magnetic-field orientation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the plasma-flow curl has a positive
projection along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when
viewed from above the plasma.

NAMES.name: total_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of electrons in the complete free-electron population,
including both thermal and nonthermal contributions and excluding bound
electrons.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electron

Total density is the sum of the thermal and fast populations of the species;
thermal excludes the suprathermal particles that fast names.

The total density is defined by

$$
n_e = \int f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the total free-electron number density, $f_e$ is the full
electron number distribution in velocity space at the location and time
considered, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

The total refers to a sum over electron populations, not a volume-integrated
particle count or a spatial averaging operation. Electrons bound in atoms,
molecules, or ions are excluded. The definition applies in the core, edge,
and scrape-off layer without imposing a particular evaluation location.

This quantity is [electron density](name:electron_density) with the complete
population sum explicitly specified. For an exhaustive, nonoverlapping
thermal and nonthermal decomposition, $n_e = n_{e,\mathrm{th}} +
n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$, where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal electron
density](name:thermal_electron_density) and $n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
[fast electron density](name:fast_electron_density). Neither component alone
represents the total.

NAMES.name: trapped_current_density
NAMES.short:
Trapped current density is the vector density of conventional electric
charge flux associated with trapped-particle transport, including its
collisional drag back-current.
NAMES.long:
Trapped current density is the vector density of conventional electric
charge flux associated with the trapped-particle contribution. It includes
direct charge transport by trapped particles and the collisional drag
back-current attributed to that contribution.

A kinetic decomposition is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_s q_s\int_{\mathcal{T}_s}\mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v+\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{drag,tr}}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes charged species,
$q_s$ is species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the
velocity-space distribution function, $\mathcal{T}_s$ is the
trapped-particle region of velocity space, and
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{drag,tr}}$ is the associated collisional drag
back-current.

This vector contribution is a specialization of
[current_density](name:current_density), not a scalar electric current or a
particular geometric projection. toroidal_current_density supplies a
geometric projection, while
[toroidal_trapped_current_density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) is
the toroidal, flux-surface-averaged specialization of the trapped
contribution.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when any stated component or scalar projection of
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is aligned with the positive direction of its
defining basis vector or unit vector.

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Scalar trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress
trace carried by the total suprathermal population on magnetically trapped
orbits. It combines field-aligned and transverse stress contributions and
may be evaluated locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace
carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It is the
trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-particle
pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure); taking the scalar trace does not
require the field-aligned and transverse stresses to be equal.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, the local pressure is defined by the
trapped-particle second velocity moment:

$$
p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s \int_{\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}$ is the trapped fast-particle pressure,
$\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $s$ labels a fast-particle species, $c$
labels its charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $|\mathbf{v}|$ is particle speed, $f_{s,c}$ is the
distribution function for suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge
state $c$, $\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain of
those particles on magnetically trapped orbits at $\mathbf{x}$, and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space integration element.

The quantity applies to the total suprathermal population: contributions are
added over fast-particle species and summed over all charge states, not
density-weighted across charge states. It excludes thermal particles and
fast particles on co-passing or counter-passing orbits. The local value
retains spatial variation; flux-surface averaging gives an average over the
surface and is not part of the trapped-orbit selection itself.

The [parallel trapped fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure),
$p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the field-aligned stress component, and
the [perpendicular trapped fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure),
$p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the mean stress per transverse degree of
freedom for the same population. Their relation to the scalar trace is
$p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}})/3$.
For a common population and spatial aggregation, the trapped contribution
together with [co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and [counter-passing
fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) sums to
the [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) when those orbit
classes partition the population.

NAMES.name: parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned kinetic
pressure moment of suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It
is defined locally; its flux-surface-averaged form is the average of that
moment over a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned component of
the kinetic stress carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped
orbits. It is distinct from the scalar trace pressure of the same
population.

The local parallel pressure is the second velocity moment of the trapped
fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast,tr}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the parallel trapped fast-particle
pressure, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $c$
labels charge state where applicable, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the
velocity-space number-density distribution restricted to trapped
suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$. The integral is
over velocity space, with $d^3v$ its volume element. The field-aligned
velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude.

The population comprises trapped nonthermal particles; thermal particles and
co-passing and counter-passing particles are excluded. Contributions are
added over fast-particle species and charge states, rather than
density-weighted. The local moment retains variation within a magnetic flux
surface; its flux-surface average is the average of the local moment over
that surface. The second moment is not centered on the population mean
velocity, so directed field-aligned motion contributes to the stress.

This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [parallel fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure). Together with
[perpendicular trapped fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), it determines
the [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure),
which is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace:
$p_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast,tr}})/3$.
Here $p_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the scalar trace pressure of the same trapped
population, and $p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is its perpendicular stress per
transverse degree of freedom.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short:
Perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-perpendicular
kinetic-pressure component carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically
trapped orbits.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure is the gyrotropic
kinetic-pressure component perpendicular to the local magnetic field,
carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. Trapped
particles reverse their field-parallel motion at magnetic mirror points.
This is the stress per transverse degree of freedom, not the sum of both
transverse stresses or the scalar trace pressure.

The local perpendicular pressure is defined by the trapped-population second
velocity moment:

$$
p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_c \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} \frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2} f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

Here, $p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}}$ is the perpendicular trapped fast-particle
pressure; $s$ labels the particle species, and $c$ labels its charge state;
$m_s$ is the mass of species $s$; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity; $v_\perp$ is the magnitude of the velocity component
perpendicular to the local magnetic field; $f_{s,c}$ is the suprathermal
distribution for species $s$ and charge state $c$;
$\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the trapped region of velocity
space at that position; and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
factor of one half gives the mean over the two perpendicular velocity
directions. Contributions are summed over all charge states of species $s$;
distinct species are not summed in this species-specific quantity.

The local moment may vary over a magnetic flux surface; its flux-surface
average is the average of that same moment over the surface. The population
is restricted to suprathermal trapped particles and excludes thermal,
co-passing, and counter-passing particles. Perpendicular refers to the
magnetic-field direction, not the normal to a flux surface.

This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [perpendicular fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), excluding the
[perpendicular co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and
[perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure). For
the same trapped population, the [trapped fast-particle
pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure) is the scalar pressure
related to the [parallel trapped fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure) by
$p_{s,\mathrm{tr}}=(p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{tr}}+2p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}})/3$,
where $p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{tr}}$ is the parallel component and
$p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}}$ is this perpendicular component.

NAMES.name: vertical_vorticity
NAMES.short:
Projection of the curl of plasma center-of-mass velocity along the toroidal
symmetry axis, measuring signed local rotation of the bulk flow.
NAMES.long:
Vertical vorticity is the component of plasma [vorticity](name:vorticity)
parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. For solid-body rotation, it is twice
the vertical component of a fluid element's angular velocity.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the vertical
projection of the velocity curl is

$$
\omega_Z = (\nabla \times \mathbf{v}) \cdot \hat{Z} = \frac{1}{R}\left(\frac{\partial(Rv_\phi)}{\partial R} - \frac{\partial v_R}{\partial \phi}\right)
$$

where $\omega_Z$ is vertical vorticity, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
[center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), and $\nabla\times$
is the right-handed curl operator. Here $R$ is major radius measured from
the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical
height, and $\hat{Z}$ is the unit vector along increasing height. The
quantities $v_R$ and $v_\phi$ are the cylindrical radial and toroidal
components of $\mathbf{v}$, respectively.

The quantity describes the local mass-weighted plasma bulk flow rather than
a separately selected species or charge state. It carries no surface,
volume, or time averaging and does not assume axisymmetry. It is a signed
component, not vorticity magnitude, vertical velocity, strain rate, or flow
divergence.

Unlike [parallel vorticity](name:parallel_vorticity), which projects the
same curl along the local magnetic field, vertical vorticity uses the fixed
symmetry-axis direction. Dividing this component by the local major radius
gives the distinct [ratio of vertical vorticity to major
radius](name:ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius); that
inverse-radius scaling is not included here.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the local rotational part of the bulk flow
follows the right-hand rule about $+\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_beryllium_density
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged number density of beryllium impurity ions over the confined
plasma volume, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral
beryllium atoms.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged beryllium ion number density quantifies the mean
beryllium impurity content throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the
volume average of the local [beryllium ion number
density](name:beryllium_density), rather than a value at a particular
position or along a diagnostic chord.

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{Be} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Be}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume
element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the local
number density of beryllium ions with charge state $z+$, with $z=1$ through
$4$. Neutral beryllium is excluded. The resulting global quantity is
distinct from the [line-averaged beryllium
density](name:line_averaged_beryllium_density) and provides the numerator
for the [ratio of volume-averaged beryllium density to volume-averaged
electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_beryllium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_boron_density
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged boron density is the elemental boron number density
integrated over the plasma volume and divided by that volume, including
every boron charge state.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged boron density is the elemental boron particle density
averaged over the plasma volume, with neutral boron and every ionic charge
state included.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_B = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_B(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_B$ is the volume-averaged quantity, $V_p$ is the plasma
volume, $n_B(\mathbf{r})$ is the local [boron density](name:boron_density),
and $\mathbf{r}$ specifies position. The local density includes all boron
charge states through $n_B=\sum_{Z=0}^{5}n_{B,Z}$, where $Z$ is the ionic
charge state and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density in that state.

This is a global volume average, distinct from the local boron density and
from the [ratio of volume-averaged boron density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_boron_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which expresses the same boron content relative to the electron population.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_carbon_density
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Plasma-volume mean of the total number density of elemental carbon, summed
over neutral carbon and all ionic charge states through fully stripped C6+.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged carbon density is the plasma-volume mean of the total number
density of elemental carbon, encompassing neutral carbon atoms and all ionic
charge states from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+.

The volume average of the local [carbon density](name:carbon_density) is
defined by

$$
\langle n_C \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_C(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_C(\mathbf{r})$ is the local total carbon number density in
m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the plasma volume in m$^{3}$, $dV$ is the volume element,
and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. The local density includes the sum over
all carbon charge states before the volume average is taken.

This quantity represents a volume average over the specified plasma volume
and is distinct from [line-averaged carbon
density](name:line_averaged_carbon_density), which averages along a plasma
chord.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_deuterium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local
number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local
number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is the
charge-state-summed spatial average of the local [deuterium
density](name:deuterium_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_D = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_D(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_D$ is the volume-averaged deuterium density, $V$ is the
specified plasma-volume domain, and $n_D(\mathbf{r})$ is the local deuterium
density at position $\mathbf{r}$. The local density is summed over positive
ionization states and excludes neutral atoms, molecular deuterium, and
non-deuterium species.

This quantity averages over the specified plasma volume rather than along a
chord; the latter is represented by [line-averaged deuterium
density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density).

sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_effective_charge
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless volume-averaged effective ionic charge of a plasma mixture,
formed by averaging the local second ionic charge moment normalized by
free-electron density over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged effective ionic charge is the effective charge of the
complete ion mixture after spatially averaging the local charge-weighted
ionic charge moment over the confined plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff},V} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},V}$ is the volume-averaged effective charge,
$Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [effective
charge](name:effective_charge), $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume,
$\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average applies to the complete included ion mixture at every position,
with ionic contributions summed over all represented species and charge
states. It covers the confined plasma volume and is not restricted to one
species, one charge state, one region, or one flux surface; it is distinct
from an ordinary ion charge average.

This quantity is the volume-averaged counterpart of [effective
charge](name:effective_charge). It differs from flux-surface-averaged
effective charge at the plasma boundary, which averages the local effective
charge over a boundary surface, and from [volume-averaged ion
charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge), which represents an ordinary ion
charge number rather than the second charge moment normalized by
free-electron density.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of free electrons averaged over the plasma volume inside the
last closed flux surface, including thermal and nonthermal populations.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electron

The volume average of the local [electron density](name:electron_density) is
defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_e\,dV
$$

where $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $\langle
n_e\rangle_V$ is its volume average, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by
the last closed flux surface and specifies the integration region, and $dV$
is a physical volume element. Multiplying the average by that volume gives
the total number of free electrons inside the boundary.

All free-electron populations, including thermal and nonthermal electrons,
are included; electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions are excluded.
Plasma outside the last closed flux surface is excluded from the average.
Unlike [line-averaged electron
density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), this quantity is a
physical-volume mean rather than a chord mean.

The same spatial averaging applies to [volume-averaged ion
density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), but that quantity counts the
specified ion population rather than electrons. This electron mean supplies
the denominator of abundance ratios such as the [ratio of volume-averaged
carbon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_carbon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density);
such a ratio uses separately averaged densities over the same volume, not a
volume average of their local ratio.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last
closed flux surface, formed from the corresponding volume-averaged
densities. The argon population is summed over all argon ion charge states
and excludes neutral argon.
NAMES.long:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last
closed flux surface is the confined-plasma composition fraction obtained by
normalizing the volume-averaged argon density to the volume-averaged
electron density. The argon population is the species-level ion population
summed over all argon ion charge states.

The ratio is defined as the quotient of the corresponding volume-averaged
densities:

$$
C_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is this argon-to-electron abundance ratio, $\langle
n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged argon-ion number
density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged electron number
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and $V$ denotes the
confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface.

The scope is the confined plasma population inside the last closed flux
surface, with the same volume-averaging operation applied to the argon and
electron densities before forming the quotient. It excludes neutral argon,
is not charge-state-resolved, and is a ratio of volume averages rather than
the volume average of a local argon-to-electron density ratio.

This quantity is related to [argon_density](name:argon_density) as its
volume-averaged, electron-normalized elemental abundance;
[argon_density](name:argon_density) denotes the argon density before
normalization to the electron population.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the quotient of
the volume-averaged deuterium ion number density and the volume-averaged
electron number density over the same plasma volume. The deuterium numerator
is charge-state-summed over positive atomic ion charge states and excludes
neutral or molecular deuterium.
NAMES.long:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the
electron-density-normalized abundance of deuterium ions in a specified
plasma volume. It is the quotient of the [volume-averaged deuterium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) and the [volume-averaged
electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) evaluated over that
same volume.

The ratio is defined by the quotient of volume averages:

$$
f_{D,V} = \frac{\langle n_D \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{D,V}$ is this abundance ratio, $n_D$ is the [deuterium
density](name:deuterium_density), $n_e$ is the electron density, $\langle
n_D \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is
the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and the subscript $V$
denotes averaging over the common plasma volume.

The numerator is the volume average of deuterium ion number density summed
over all positive atomic ion charge states. It excludes neutral deuterium
atoms, molecular deuterium, and deuterium bound in non-ion populations. The
aggregation convention is a quotient of two volume-averaged densities, not
the volume average of the pointwise ratio $n_D/n_e$.

For non-negative number densities and positive $\langle n_e \rangle_V$,
$f_{D,V}$ is non-negative. It is not the fraction of deuterium among all
fuel nuclei and does not represent the absolute deuterium particle
inventory. It differs from the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which uses the combined deuterium-tritium numerator, while this quantity
uses deuterium alone.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged
electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species,
treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged
electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species,
treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species, is the
electron-density-normalized abundance of that fuel species. It compares the
fuel-ion population with the electron population after each density is
averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}}
\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), $\langle n_e
\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the
local number density of the combined deuterium-tritium effective species,
$n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$
denotes averaging over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the plasma volume common to numerator and denominator; the
value is a ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of a
pointwise density ratio. The numerator is a species-level extensive density
for the effective deuterium-tritium fuel species and is summed over all
charge states before averaging. It includes only that fuel species and
excludes helium ash, impurity ions, and separate isotope-composition ratios
such as the [tritium-to-deuterium density
ratio](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density).

Equivalently, this quantity is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) normalized by the
[volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density);
it is a normalized ratio, not a derivative of either density. When the
combined deuterium-tritium density is resolved into deuterium and tritium
contributions over the same volume and denominator, it equals the sum of the
[volume-averaged deuterium-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
and the [volume-averaged tritium-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Temperature of bulk electrons from random translational motion,
volume-averaged inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, including
during plasma initiation.
NAMES.long:
Temperature of bulk electrons averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by
the last closed magnetic flux surface is the spatial mean of their local
energy-equivalent kinetic temperature. For nonrelativistic electrons, the
local temperature equals two-thirds of the mean random kinetic energy per
particle, excluding directed mean-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature,
$T_e$ is the local bulk electron temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the
differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies throughout that enclosed volume, including during
plasma initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial
volume average, not a density-weighted particle average or a local value. It
differs from [line-averaged electron
temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature), which averages along
a plasma chord. It is neither total electron thermal energy nor a radiation
brightness temperature.

This quantity is obtained by applying volume averaging to [electron
temperature](name:electron_temperature); [volume-averaged ion
temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature) applies the corresponding
spatial average to a specified ion species. It supplies the denominator of
the [ratio of magnetic-axis to volume-averaged electron
temperature](name:ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature),
which expresses central electron-temperature peaking relative to the
plasma-wide mean.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.short:
Ratio of electron temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average
inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, expressing central
electron-temperature peaking.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of electron temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average
inside the last closed magnetic flux surface. It expresses central
electron-temperature peaking relative to the enclosed plasma's mean thermal
state.

It is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $P_{T_e}$ is the electron-temperature peaking ratio,
$T_{e,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [electron temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis), and $\langle
T_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature). The volume average
is $\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV$, where $T_e$ is the
local electron kinetic temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the
last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is a physical volume element.

The denominator is weighted by physical volume, not by electron density, and
is not a flux-surface average. The numerator is evaluated at the magnetic
axis rather than at an independently located temperature maximum. The ratio
requires a positive denominator and is not an absolute temperature; unity
means that the axis temperature equals the volume average, while values
greater than unity indicate central peaking relative to that average.

The [corresponding ion-temperature
ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature)
applies the same axis-to-volume-average comparison to ion temperature.

$$a/b$$

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_helium_3_density
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the mean charged-ion
population over the confined plasma volume, summed over singly ionized and
fully stripped states and excluding neutral atoms.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the spatial mean of the
charged helium-3 ion population throughout the confined plasma volume. It is
derived from the local [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density), rather
than representing a density at one location.

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and
$n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion density summed
over singly ionized and fully stripped states. Neutral helium-3 atoms are
excluded. The [line-averaged helium-3
density](name:line_averaged_helium_3_density) instead averages the same
local quantity along a specified path.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3
ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron
density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by
the electron average.
NAMES.long:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3
ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron
density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by
the electron average and represents the global helium-3 ion composition
relative to electrons.

The ratio is defined by applying the volume average separately to each
density over the same confined plasma volume before division:

$$
r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e} =
\frac{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e}$ is this composition ratio,
$n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion number density
summed over all charged ionization states, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local
electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, $dV$ is the volume
element, and $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, with the same symbol
denoting its volume measure in the normalization factors.

The scope is a species-level, volume-averaged, confined-plasma composition
ratio. The helium-3 population includes charged helium-3 ions summed over
charge states and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms; the electron population
is the corresponding electron population in the same confined volume. No
particular time within an evolution is part of the quantity definition.

This quantity is not the confined-volume average of the local ratio
$n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}/n_e$; it equals that average only for special spatial
distributions. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged helium-3
density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), and its denominator is the
[volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).
The [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
is the analogous isotope composition ratio for helium-4.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_helium_4_density
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged number density of helium-4 ions over the confined plasma
volume, providing a global measure of fusion-ash concentration in
deuterium-tritium plasmas.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density quantifies the mean
concentration of fusion-ash ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It
is the global counterpart of the local [helium-4 ion
density](name:helium_4_density) and is distinct from the chord mean
[line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local helium-4 ion number
density in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^3$, and
$\mathbf{r}$ denotes position.

The helium-4 ion population is summed over all ionic charge states, while
neutral helium is excluded. Its ratio to the volume-averaged electron
density is defined by [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to
volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons (4He)

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed
flux surface, comparing the charge-state-summed helium-4 ion density with
the electron density after each density is volume averaged.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed
flux surface is the quotient of the volume-averaged helium-4 ion number
density and the volume-averaged electron number density. It is a global
isotope-abundance measure for ionized helium-4 relative to electrons in the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

The ratio is defined from independent volume averages over the same enclosed
plasma volume:

$$
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}, \qquad \langle n_s\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}}\int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_s(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ is this helium-4 abundance ratio, the
superscript $V$ denotes formation from volume averages, $\langle
n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged helium-4
density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is
the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the
local number density of species $s$ at position $\mathbf{x}$,
$V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface, and $dV$ is an element of that volume. For $s={}^4\mathrm{He}$,
$n_s$ is the local helium-4 ion number density summed over all ion charge
states; for $s=e$, $n_s$ is the local electron number density.

The semantic scope is species-level helium-4 ion density inside the last
closed flux surface. The helium-4 numerator is summed over all ion charge
states before averaging, while neutral helium-4 atoms and helium isotopes
other than helium-4 are excluded. Because the numerator and denominator are
averaged separately, this quantity is not the volume average of the local
ratio $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}/n_e$.

For fully stripped helium-4 ions in a quasi-neutral plasma, $2
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ represents the helium-4 ion contribution to the
electron charge balance, apart from contributions of other ions and
departures from full stripping. The isotope analog is [ratio of
volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
and the analogous elemental abundance quantity is [ratio of volume-averaged
neon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
It is related to ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 ion density to electron
density by the shared helium-4 numerator species, while this name explicitly
normalizes by the independently volume-averaged electron density.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Temperature of a specified ion species from random kinetic motion,
arithmetically averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Temperature of a specified ion species averaged over the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface describes its random
translational kinetic energy. It excludes kinetic energy associated with
directed mean ion flow.

The volume average of the local [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature) is
defined by

$$
\langle T_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_i\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_i\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged temperature of the
specified ion species, $T_i$ is its local temperature, $V$ is the plasma
volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the
differential physical-volume element.

For the specified species, the local temperature is the density-weighted
mean over all charge states, rather than a sum of charge-state temperatures;
[ion charge-state temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature) resolves
an individual charge state. The subsequent spatial average weights local
temperature by physical volume, not by particle number. It is neither a
local temperature nor a volume-integrated thermal energy, and it does not
combine different ion species.

Unlike [ion average temperature](name:ion_average_temperature), which
combines ion species and charge states by number-density weighting, this
quantity retains the selected species. Its sibling, [volume-averaged total
ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), instead
volume-averages the effective temperature of the combined thermal-ion
population. This species-specific volume average also supplies the
denominator of the [axis-to-volume-average ion-temperature
ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature),
which expresses central temperature peaking.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_iron_density
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions,
summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+ and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions,
aggregated over all iron charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and
averaged throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatially averaged
form of [iron_density](name:iron_density), not a charge-state-resolved
quantity.

The volume-averaged density is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \left(\sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\right)\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the volume-averaged iron density in
m$^{-3}$, $V_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^{3}$,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local density of iron charge state
$z$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Neutral iron is excluded, and the result does not preserve the distribution
among charge states. It differs from
[volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) through its
fixed iron-species scope and from
[iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis) because
it represents a volume average rather than a local axis value.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_krypton_density
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Number density of krypton, volume-averaged over the plasma, summed over
neutral krypton and all ionized charge states through fully stripped Kr36+.
NAMES.long:
Number density of krypton, volume-averaged over the plasma, summed over
neutral krypton and all ionized charge states through fully stripped
Kr$^{36+}$.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} \left(\sum_{q=0}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}}^{(q)}(\mathbf{r})\right) d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and
$n_{\mathrm{Kr}}^{(q)}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local number density of krypton
in charge state $q$; $q=0$ denotes neutral krypton and $q=36$ denotes fully
stripped krypton.

Unlike the local [krypton density](name:krypton_density), this quantity
includes neutral krypton and applies a plasma-volume average. It is an
absolute elemental density, distinct from the normalized abundance in the
[volume-averaged krypton-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_krypton_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_neon_density
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Volume average of the charge-state-summed neon number density throughout the
plasma, giving the mean elemental neon content independent of local spatial
variation.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged neon density is the mean elemental neon number density
over the plasma volume. It includes neutral neon and all neon ionization
states, extending the local definition of [neon density](name:neon_density)
to a spatial average.

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ne}} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is
position, and $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local neon number density
summed over all ionization states. The volume integral represents the total
neon inventory divided by the plasma volume. This quantity provides the
numerator in the [neon abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which additionally normalizes it to the volume-averaged electron density.

sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_nitrogen_density
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged nitrogen density is the plasma-volume mean of nitrogen
nuclei number density, with neutral and all ionized charge states included.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged nitrogen density is the plasma-volume mean of the local
number density of nitrogen atomic nuclei. It is a species-level density, so
neutral nitrogen and every ionized charge state contribute to the average;
the local quantity is [nitrogen density](name:nitrogen_density).

The volume average and charge-state aggregation are defined by

$$
\overline{n}_N = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_N(\mathbf{r})\,dV, \qquad n_N(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{z=0}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\overline{n}_N$ and $n_{\mathrm{N}^{z+}}$ are number densities in
m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$
is position, and $z$ is the nitrogen charge-state index from neutral
nitrogen ($z=0$) through fully stripped nitrogen ($z=7$).

The average is over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface. Unlike [line-averaged nitrogen
density](name:line_averaged_nitrogen_density), it weights volume elements
rather than points along a specified chord.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_oxygen_density
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged oxygen density is the spatial mean of the local oxygen
number density, summed over all charge states from neutral O0 through fully
stripped O8+, over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux
surface.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged oxygen density is the volume mean of the local oxygen
number density—summed over all charge states from neutral O$^0$ through
fully stripped O$^{8+}$—within the confined plasma volume bounded by the
last closed flux surface. It characterizes the total oxygen impurity
inventory per confined plasma volume, independent of how that oxygen is
distributed inside the boundary.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{O} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} \int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{r})\, dV
$$

where $\langle n_\mathrm{O} \rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged oxygen
density, $V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the
last closed flux surface, $dV$ is a volume element, and
$n_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local [oxygen
density](name:oxygen_density), with $n_\mathrm{O}=\sum_{Z=0}^{8}
n_{\mathrm{O}^{Z+}}$.

This quantity differs from
[line_averaged_oxygen_density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density), which is
a chord mean rather than a confined-volume mean. It is a charge-state-summed
species density and must not be interpreted as an ionic-only density that
excludes neutral oxygen.

sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_time_derivative_of_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Rate of change of the electron number density averaged over the confined
plasma volume, with positive values indicating increasing mean density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the temporal rate of change of the electron number density
after volume averaging over the confined plasma volume. Positive values
indicate increasing mean electron density, while negative values indicate
decreasing mean electron density.

For a fixed averaging volume, the defining relation is

$$
\frac{d\langle n_e\rangle_V}{dt} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \frac{\partial n_e}{\partial t}\,dV
$$

where $n_e$ is the local electron number density, $V$ is the confined plasma
volume, and $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).

The volume-average operation is applied to the electron density before time
differentiation. This distinguishes the quantity from the more general [time
derivative of electron density](name:time_derivative_of_electron_density),
which does not specify volume averaging.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Time derivative of the electron density

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population, with all included species and charge states contributing by
number density and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged total ion temperature is the volume average of the local
density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It
represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\int_V T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV}{\int_V dV}
$$

where $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is its differential volume
element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})$ is
the local quantity defined by
[total_ion_temperature](name:total_ion_temperature). Species and
charge-state density weighting is performed locally before the volume
averaging. Unlike
[line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature),
this quantity averages over volume rather than along a plasma chord.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged number density of tritium ions over the confined plasma
volume, obtained from the local charge-state-summed fuel-ion density.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged tritium ion number density quantifies the mean concentration
of hydrogen-3 fuel ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the
spatial average of the local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density), rather
than a chord average such as
[line_averaged_tritium_density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density).

$$
\overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_T\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_T$ is the volume-averaged tritium ion number density,
$n_T$ is the local tritium ion number density, $V_c$ is the confined plasma
volume bounded by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume
element. The tritium ion density is summed over all ionic charge states and
excludes neutral tritium. This quantity provides the tritium-density basis
for volume-averaged isotopic ratios and is distinct from the local boundary
value
[tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density
is the volume-averaged tritium number density, summed over all charge
states, divided by the volume-averaged electron number density.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density
is the volume-averaged tritium number density divided by the volume-averaged
electron number density. It expresses the tritium contribution to plasma
composition relative to the electron population after both densities have
been averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined as:

$$
f_{T/e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_T \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{T/e}^{V}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_T \rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density),
$\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_T$ is the local [tritium
density](name:tritium_density), $n_e$ is the local [electron
density](name:electron_density), and $\langle q\rangle_V$ denotes
$V^{-1}\int_V q\,dV$ for scalar field $q$ over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the specified plasma volume and the particle populations
contained in that volume. The tritium density is a species-level per-volume
amount and is therefore summed over all tritium charge states before volume
averaging. The definition contains no selection by the time of peak electron
density or by any other operating condition.

This quantity is the ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the
local ratio $n_T/n_e$, and it is not normalized to the total hydrogenic-fuel
density. It is the tritium-only counterpart of the [ratio of volume-averaged
deuterium-tritium density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which uses the combined deuterium-plus-tritium numerator; it also differs
from the local ratio of tritium density to electron density.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_tungsten_density
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged number density of positively charged tungsten ions within
the plasma enclosed by the last closed flux surface, summed over all
ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged tungsten-ion density is the spatial mean of the local
charge-state-summed density tungsten-ion density over the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed flux surface. It includes all positive tungsten
ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local tungsten-ion density,
$V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the enclosed plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ denotes
position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The local density is the sum of
the densities of all tungsten charge states from W$^{1+}$ through W$^{74+}$.

This quantity is distinct from the boundary flux-surface-averaged tungsten
density and from the impurity-abundance [ratio of volume-averaged tungsten
density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which is normalized to electron density.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_xenon_density
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of xenon ions averaged over the full plasma volume, including
all charged xenon ionization states and excluding neutral xenon.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged xenon ion number density is the plasma-wide mean of the
local [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which sums xenon ions from singly
ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral atoms.

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the volume-averaged xenon ion density,
$n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local xenon ion density at position
$\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the full plasma volume, and $dV$ is the physical
volume element. The averaging is over the plasma volume rather than along a
measurement chord or at a single locus. The resulting global
impurity-content measure can be compared with electron content through the
ratio of volume-averaged xenon density to volume-averaged electron density.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_outboard_midplane
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron particle number density at the low-field-side intersection of a
magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane.
NAMES.long:
Electron number density at the outboard midplane is the local density of the
electron population at the low-field-side intersection of a specified
magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane. It is the
electron-specific member of density_at_outboard_midplane.

At that location, the density is defined by the zeroth velocity-space moment

$$
n_e(R,\phi,Z)=\int f_e(R,\phi,Z,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_e$ is electron number density, $f_e$ is the electron
velocity-distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, and
$d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. The position is
described in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This
quantity counts electrons only and is distinct from total particle density
and from electron density evaluated at the magnetic axis.

sources.leaf_definition: Electron density at outboard equatorial midplane of the flux surface (angle_pol = 0)
sources.parent_definition: Physical quantities used for normalization (useful to link to the original simulation/experience)

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_outboard_midplane
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Kinetic temperature of the bulk electron population at the low-field-side
intersection of a chosen magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane.
NAMES.long:
The electron temperature at the outboard midplane is the local
energy-equivalent kinetic temperature of the bulk electron population at the
low-field-side equatorial intersection of a chosen magnetic flux surface. It
is the electron-specific component of temperature at outboard midplane.

For an isotropic electron velocity distribution, the energy-equivalent
temperature is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}} \right\rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature, and $\left\langle
E_{e,\mathrm{rand}} \right\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per
electron, with both expressed on the same energy scale.

This quantity is local to the outboard-midplane intersection and is not a
field-line average, flux-surface average, or value at the plasma boundary.
