NAMES.name: momentum_flux_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short:
Momentum flux due to E cross B drift is the dimensionless scalar transport
of a selected component of linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface
by the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, expressed
relative to a reference momentum-flux scale. It fixes the drift mechanism
and dimensionless status while abstracting over the momentum component,
surface-normal direction, averaging, and choice of normalization reference
supplied by concrete specializations.
NAMES.long:
Momentum flux due to $E\times B$ drift is the scalar transport of a selected
component of linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface carried by
the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, expressed in
dimensionless form relative to a reference momentum-flux scale. It
represents the $E\times B$ advective transport channel of momentum, not an
unspecified or total momentum-transport channel.

The dimensionless scalar component is the surface-normal advective flux of
the selected momentum density divided by a reference momentum-flux scale:

$$
\Pi_{\alpha}^{E\times B} = \frac{\left\langle p_{\alpha}\, \mathbf{v}_{E\times B}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} \right\rangle}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $p_{\alpha}$ is the selected component of linear plasma momentum
density, $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}$ is the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field
drift velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen oriented surface normal,
$\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes the aggregation or averaging convention
specified by the concrete quantity, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the
reference momentum-flux scale relative to which the quantity is expressed.

This quantity fixes two things: the driving mechanism is the $E\times B$
drift, and the quantity is dimensionless, being expressed relative to a
reference scale. It abstracts over the remaining axes: the transported
momentum component $\alpha$, the orientation of the crossing surface, the
population or velocity-space contribution included in $p_{\alpha}$, the
averaging convention, and the specific choice of $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$.
Concrete specializations fix these axes.

This is a flux of momentum, not the momentum density itself, not a force or
torque density, and not the full momentum-flux tensor. It excludes momentum
transport carried by parallel streaming, magnetic drifts, diamagnetic flows,
collisional viscosity, or external forces except where those effects are
part of the selected momentum density or of the fields that determine the
$E\times B$ drift.

The [normalized momentum flux due to $E\times B$
drift](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the
specialization that explicitly designates a reference normalization as part
of its identity; the present quantity is the mechanism-level abstraction
under which any such normalized member sits, without itself selecting which
reference scale, momentum component, surface, or averaging is used.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive selected linear momentum is advected
by the $E\times B$ drift through the oriented surface in the direction of
the chosen positive surface normal, or equivalently when negative selected
linear momentum is advected opposite to that normal.

NAMES.name: momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Momentum flux due to a perturbed parallel vector potential is the
dimensionless signed contribution to plasma momentum transport produced by
turbulent fluctuations of the electromagnetic vector potential component
parallel to the magnetic field. It is expressed relative to a positive
reference momentum-flux scale.
NAMES.long:
Momentum flux due to a perturbed parallel vector potential is the
contribution to plasma momentum transport produced by turbulent fluctuations
of the electromagnetic vector potential component parallel to the magnetic
field. It is a signed scalar contribution expressed relative to a positive
reference momentum-flux scale, so its sign is inherited from the underlying
momentum transport rather than from the scale.

The scaled contribution is defined by

$$
\widehat{\Pi}_{A_\parallel} = \frac{\Pi_{A_\parallel}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\widehat{\Pi}_{A_\parallel}$ denotes this quantity,
$\Pi_{A_\parallel}$ is the physical momentum-flux contribution due to
perturbed parallel-vector-potential fluctuations, $A_\parallel$ is the
component of the electromagnetic vector potential parallel to the magnetic
field, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference momentum-flux
scale.

This parent fixes the fluctuation mechanism to the perturbed $A_\parallel$
contribution. The parent-level scaling requires only a positive reference
momentum-flux scale; it does not select a named normalization convention, a
toroidal or other momentum component, a species population, a flux-surface
or geometric projection, an averaging domain, or a velocity-space channel.
It denotes the mechanism-selected scalar aggregate over distinctions not
explicitly resolved by a specialization, not a channel-resolved or
component-resolved flux.

This quantity is distinct from local momentum density, from the total
momentum flux formed by summing all fluctuation mechanisms, and from
momentum-flux contributions driven by other turbulent fields. A concrete
child such as [normalized momentum flux due to a perturbed parallel vector
potential](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential)
retains the same perturbed-$A_\parallel$ mechanism while fixing a particular
normalized turbulence quantity and additional component or channel scope; it
is not a statement that the parent lacks the $A_\parallel$ mechanism or
receives a second normalization.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when, for the momentum component and
transport-surface orientation in scope, this contribution carries positive
momentum through the surface in the positive-normal direction.

NAMES.name: momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short:
Normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the dimensionless transport of
resolved linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface by the
electric-field drift. Concrete specializations supply the momentum
component, crossing direction, velocity-space contribution, and
normalization reference.
NAMES.long:
Normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the normalized flux of resolved
linear plasma momentum carried across an oriented surface by the E×B
advective drift. It represents the E×B-drift contribution to turbulent
momentum transport, distinct from the sum over all transport mechanisms.

As a normalized flux, it is the corresponding E×B momentum-flux contribution
divided by the reference momentum flux used for the same normalization
convention:

$$
\widehat{\Pi}^{E\times B}_{a,n} = \frac{\Pi^{E\times B}_{a,n}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\widehat{\Pi}^{E\times B}_{a,n}$ is the normalized momentum flux due
to E×B drift, $\Pi^{E\times B}_{a,n}$ is the E×B-drift contribution to the
flux of the resolved linear-momentum component $a$ through the oriented
surface normal $n$, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference momentum flux
for the same normalization convention.

This parent quantity does not choose a particular momentum component,
crossing direction, velocity-space contribution, species, or surface
orientation; those are supplied by concrete specializations. For example,
[perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
resolves the perpendicular velocity-space contribution while retaining this
E×B-driven parent mechanism.

It excludes normalized momentum flux produced by mechanisms other than E×B
drift, including electromagnetic contributions associated with
[momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
It is not the total normalized momentum flux unless the relevant mechanism,
component, and velocity-space contributions have been combined according to
their own definitions.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when positive resolved linear momentum is carried
by the E×B drift in the positive crossing direction specified by the
concrete specialization.

NAMES.name: momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless toroidal plasma-momentum flux contribution driven by the
perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic
turbulence, generalized across parallel and perpendicular velocity-space
channels.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized contribution to toroidal plasma-momentum
transport produced by fluctuations of the perturbed parallel electromagnetic
vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence. It represents transport across
an oriented surface, not local momentum density or the total momentum
contained in a volume.

The normalization is defined by

$$
\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}^{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the normalized quantity,
$\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}$ is the toroidal momentum-flux contribution driven
by the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential, and
$\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference momentum-flux scale. The
subscript $\delta A_\parallel$ identifies the perturbed parallel
electromagnetic vector potential.

Toroidal momentum refers to the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. This parent is agnostic to
velocity-space projection and covers both the parallel and perpendicular
channel contributions without selecting either channel or requiring that the
channels be summed.

The quantity excludes momentum-flux contributions attributed to other
fluctuation mechanisms and is distinct from local momentum density, total
momentum in a volume, and the channel-resolved [parallel momentum-flux
contribution](name:parallel_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential)
or [perpendicular momentum-flux
contribution](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
It is also distinct from the normalized contribution driven by a perturbed
parallel magnetic field.

This quantity is the normalized, driver-specific specialization of [momentum
flux due to the perturbed parallel vector
potential](name:momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
The normalization changes the reference scale while preserving the signed
character of the underlying momentum-flux contribution.

NAMES.name: normalized_collisionality
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio of a specified interspecies collision frequency to the
characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce frequency used for the plasma
population.
NAMES.long:
This collisionality measures the strength of interspecies collisional
relaxation relative to collisionless motion along magnetic-field
trajectories.

$$
\nu_{ab}^{*} = \frac{\nu_{ab}}{\omega_{\mathrm{char}}}
$$

where $\nu_{ab}$ is the collision frequency between species $a$ and $b$, and
$\omega_{\mathrm{char}}$ is the relevant characteristic streaming, transit,
or bounce angular frequency; both quantities have reciprocal-time units.

The denominator must be interpreted according to the selected orbit or
motion class, so this quantity is distinct from the collision frequency
itself. It generalizes the population-specific electron collisionality and
complements collisionality at the pedestal top when the characteristic
frequency is evaluated there.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized collisionality between two species
sources.parent_definition: Collisions related quantities

NAMES.name: normalized_debye_length
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio of the multispecies Debye shielding length to the
positive reference length used by the gyrokinetic formulation.
NAMES.long:
The multispecies Debye shielding length is the electrostatic screening scale
produced by the combined response of all charged species. This quantity
expresses that scale relative to the positive reference length selected for
the gyrokinetic formulation.

$$
\lambda_{D,\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{1}{L_{\mathrm{ref}}}\left(\sum_s \frac{n_s q_s^2}{\epsilon_0 k_B T_s}\right)^{-1/2}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, $q_s$ is its particle
charge, $T_s$ is its thermodynamic temperature, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's
constant, $\epsilon_0$ is the vacuum permittivity, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is
the gyrokinetic reference length. The sum includes the charged species
contributing to quasistatic Debye shielding and excludes neutral
populations. The underlying shielding length also enters the [Coulomb
logarithm](name:coulomb_logarithm); this normalized quantity is not a
species-specific screening length.

sources.leaf_definition: Debye length computed from the reference quantities (see detailed documentation at the root of the IDS)
sources.parent_definition: Physical quantities common to all species

NAMES.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vector of the charge-weighted first velocity moment of a
perturbed gyrocenter distribution, scaled by a positive reference
current-density magnitude.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized perturbed gyrocenter current-density vector:
the charge-weighted first velocity moment of a perturbed gyrocenter
distribution. It represents the vector current response, distinct from
density and pressure moments.

The charge-weighted moment and its normalization are defined by

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gc}}^{\delta}=\sum_s q_s\int \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}}\,\delta f_{\mathrm{gc},s}\,d^3\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}},\qquad \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{gc}}^{\delta}=\frac{\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gc}}^{\delta}}{J_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is
gyrocenter velocity, $\delta f_{\mathrm{gc},s}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter
distribution, and $J_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference
current-density scale. The vector may be resolved into directional
projections; [parallel normalized gyrocenter perturbed current
density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density) is
one such field-aligned component. The [normalized gyrocenter perturbed
density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density) is the corresponding
zeroth moment, while normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is a second
moment.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a projected component of the charge-weighted
perturbed gyrocenter flow points along its assigned positive basis
direction.

NAMES.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short:
Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth
velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a
positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius
gyrocenter-density fluctuation response, distinct from a gyroaveraged
particle-density perturbation.
NAMES.long:
Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth
velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a
positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius gyrocenter
density fluctuation response; the normalization removes the scale of the
reference density while preserving perturbation amplitude and phase.

For magnetic moment $\mu = m_s v_\perp^2/(2B)$, the normalized moment is
defined by:

$$
\widehat{n}_{gc,s} = \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{ref},s}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{0}^{\infty} \delta f_{gc,s}(v_\parallel,\mu)\,\frac{2\pi B}{m_s}\,d\mu\,dv_\parallel
$$

where $\widehat{n}_{gc,s}$ is the normalized gyrocenter perturbed density
for species $s$, $n_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is the positive reference number
density for that species, $\delta f_{gc,s}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter
distribution with respect to ordinary velocity-space volume, $B$ is the
local magnetic-field magnitude, $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is
velocity parallel to the magnetic field, $v_\perp$ is speed perpendicular to
the magnetic field, and $\mu$ is magnetic moment. The factor $2\pi B/m_s$ is
the gyroangle-integrated velocity-space Jacobian for this definition of
$\mu$.

For a species represented by multiple charge states, the perturbed
gyrocenter-density numerator and the reference density are
charge-state-summed before the ratio is formed. This quantity excludes any
Bessel-function or finite-Larmor-radius weighting inside the velocity-space
integral; that weighted moment is the normalized gyrocenter gyroaveraged
density. The dimensional numerator of the ratio is the unnormalized
gyrocenter-density perturbation; the related perturbed gyrocenter density
denotes a dimensionless gyrocenter-density perturbation in the same family.
The normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is the corresponding perturbed
pressure moment. For complex perturbation amplitudes, the integral is taken
over the complex amplitude; the arbitrary overall mode phase is external to
the definition.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when, for a real perturbation amplitude, the
velocity-space integral of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution gives an
excess gyrocenter density relative to the positive reference density.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized density
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of gyrocenters

NAMES.name: normalized_gyrokinetic_time
NAMES.subject: gyrokinetic
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless independent time coordinate that orders nonlinear gyrokinetic
evolution and indexes time-resolved turbulent fields, fluxes, and moments.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the dimensionless independent time coordinate for nonlinear
gyrokinetic evolution. It orders time-resolved turbulent fields, fluxes, and
velocity-space moments rather than representing a physical field or a
spatial coordinate.

The normalized time coordinate is defined by

$$
t_{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{t}{t_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $t$ is the physical simulation time, $t_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the
positive reference time scale specified by the gyrokinetic normalization,
and $t_{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the resulting normalized time coordinate.

Its scope is the nonlinear gyrokinetic simulation timebase as a whole; it is
not assigned to a particle species, spatial region, mode, or diagnostic
channel. It is a coordinate rather than an averaged, integrated, or
charge-state-aggregated quantity, and it is distinct from an interval
between two time instants or from the unnormalized physical time coordinate.

Differences between two values of this coordinate define normalized time
intervals used to parameterize temporal evolution. Unlike [normalized
particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy), which
is a normalized velocity-space moment, this quantity is the independent
temporal coordinate against which such moments and turbulent fluxes are
resolved.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized time of the gyrokinetic simulation
sources.parent_definition: Non-linear simulation

NAMES.name: normalized_ion_species_number_density
NAMES.subject: ion_species
NAMES.short:
Normalized ion-species number density is the particle-density perturbation
of one ion species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, scaled by a positive
reference density.
NAMES.long:
Normalized ion-species number density is the normalized zeroth
velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution for one
selected ion species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its moment weighting
counts particles rather than weighting them by charge, mass, or energy.

The normalized density perturbation is defined by:

$$
\widehat{n}_s = \frac{\widetilde{n}_s}{n_{\mathrm{ref}}} = \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{ref}}}\int \widetilde{f}^{\,p}_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\widehat{n}_s$ is the normalized density perturbation,
$\widetilde{n}_s$ is the particle-number-density perturbation, $s$ labels
the ion species, and $n_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference density.
The function $\widetilde{f}^{\,p}_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution,
with superscript $p$ identifying particle rather than gyrocenter variables;
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element. The integral covers all velocity space.

The species contribution is summed over all ionic charge states, with no
summation over different ion species and no thermal-only restriction. It is
local rather than a flux-surface or volume average. It represents a
perturbation, not the equilibrium species-to-reference density ratio. Any
eigenmode phase is retained: neither a modulus nor a squared fluctuation is
implied. The particular reference density and the eigenmode amplitude
convention are not fixed by this quantity.

Unlike [normalized gyrocenter perturbed
density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density), this moment uses the
particle distribution, including the transformation from gyrocenter to
particle variables. It is therefore distinct from an explicitly
[first-order-Bessel-weighted gyrocenter density
moment](name:normalized_perturbed_gyrocenter_density_bessel_1).

sources.leaf_definition: normalized density
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of particles

sources.leaf_definition: normalized density
sources.parent_definition: Set of species (including electrons) used in the calculation and related quantities

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_charge
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless charge number of a particle species, obtained by dividing its
physical charge by the positive reference charge used for normalization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized form of particle charge for a particle
species. It preserves the sign of the physical charge and expresses its
magnitude relative to a common positive reference charge.

The normalized charge is defined by

$$
q_{\rm n} = \frac{q}{q_{\rm ref}}
$$

where $q$ is the species' physical electric charge and $q_{\rm ref}$ is the
strictly positive reference charge, both expressed in the same charge units.

The result is dimensionless and is used as the charge-coupling coefficient
in normalized electromagnetic and electrostatic equations. Its sign
distinguishes positive and negative charge, while its magnitude gives the
charge relative to the selected reference.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized charge
sources.parent_definition: Set of species (including electrons) used in the calculation and related quantities

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_mass
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio of a species’ particle mass to a positive reference
mass, preserving relative inertial scales in normalized kinetic equations.
NAMES.long:
This quantity expresses the inertial mass of one particle of a specified
species relative to a strictly positive reference mass. It is the normalized
counterpart of particle mass, rather than an independent mass or mass
density.

The normalized particle mass is defined by

$$
\bar{m}_s = \frac{m_s}{m_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$ and $m_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is
the positive reference mass used by the normalization. The result preserves
the relative inertial ordering of species while removing the mass scale from
normalized equations of motion.

The reference mass must be kept fixed when comparing normalized masses;
changing it rescales all such ratios by the same factor. This quantity
excludes mass associated with a population or volume and does not represent
a mass density.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized mass
sources.parent_definition: Set of species (including electrons) used in the calculation and related quantities

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vector representing the charge-weighted first velocity moment
of a perturbed particle distribution in a gyrokinetic eigenmode.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the dimensionless particle-frame current response
associated with a perturbed species distribution in a gyrokinetic eigenmode.
It represents the charge-weighted first velocity moment while preserving its
vector character rather than selecting one directional projection.

For species $s$, the normalized particle-current moment is defined by

$$
\mathbf{j}_{s,\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{q_s \int \mathbf{v}\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{J_{\mathrm{ref},s}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the species charge, $\delta f_s$ is its perturbed particle
distribution, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{x}$ is position,
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $J_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is the
positive reference current-density scale. The normalization makes
$\mathbf{j}_{s,\mathrm{norm}}$ dimensionless.

The vector can be resolved into directional components; [parallel normalized
particle perturbed current
density](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density) is one
field-aligned member. As a particle-frame moment, it includes the
polarization-drift contribution absent from the corresponding [parallel
normalized gyrocenter perturbed current
density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless vector of normalized energy-weighted velocity-space moments of
a species' perturbed particle distribution in a linear gyrokinetic
eigenmode.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized particle energy moment of a species'
perturbed velocity distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its
components use distinct squared velocity-direction weights while sharing an
energy-weighted normalization from the corresponding unperturbed species
distribution.

For species $s$ and selected velocity direction or weighting component $a$,
the normalized moment is defined by

$$
\mathcal{E}_{a,s} = \frac{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v_a^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v^4 f_{0s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v$ is
its magnitude, $v_a$ is the selected velocity component, $\delta f_s$ is the
perturbed particle distribution, $f_{0s}$ is the unperturbed distribution,
and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity is a particle moment, distinct from gyrocenter moments and from
unweighted density or pressure moments. The [perpendicular normalized
particle perturbed
energy](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) is its
perpendicular directional realization.

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short:
Normalized gyrotropic pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle
distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components
parallel and perpendicular to the background magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The normalized particle perturbed pressure is a gyrotropic vector quantity
representing the pressure fluctuation of the physical particle population in
a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and
perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, each expressed
dimensionlessly as a ratio to a reference thermal pressure $p_\mathrm{ref}$.

For species $s$, the parallel and perpendicular components are the second
velocity-space moments of the perturbed particle distribution function
$\delta f_s$:

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\parallel^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v, \qquad \hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2 \, p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities
parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, and $p_\mathrm{ref} =
n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$ is evaluated at the outboard midplane.

Unlike the corresponding gyroaveraged gyrocenter perturbed pressure, this
quantity is built from the full particle distribution function, implicitly
incorporating finite-Larmor-radius corrections through the
particle-to-gyrocenter coordinate transformation. The isotropic scalar
parent particle_perturbed_pressure is recovered as the trace average
$\hat{p}_s = (\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} + 2\hat{p}_{\perp,s})/3$. The
parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure and
[perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure)
components together encode the pressure anisotropy of the eigenmode, with
the ratio $\hat{p}_{\parallel,s}/\hat{p}_{\perp,s}$ quantifying deviation
from local thermodynamic equilibrium relevant to mirror-mode and fire-hose
stability.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_gyrocenter_current_density_bessel_1
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless first-Bessel-weighted parallel current-density moment of a
perturbed gyrocenter distribution, capturing its field-aligned
finite-Larmor-radius response.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the first-order Bessel-weighted, field-parallel
current-density moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution. It represents
the electromagnetic response of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the
gyrocenter description.

The normalized moment is defined by

$$
j_{parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{q}{j_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int v_{\parallel} J_1(k_{\perp}\rho)\,\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $j_{\parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the normalized Bessel-weighted
parallel current-density moment, $q$ is the charge of the represented
particle species, $j_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference
current-density scale, $v_{\parallel}$ is the velocity component along the
local equilibrium magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function
of the first kind, $k_{\perp}$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude,
$\rho$ is the particle gyroradius, $\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})$ is
the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is the
velocity-space coordinate, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity is restricted to the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, the
field-parallel velocity channel, and the first-order Bessel weighting. Its
aggregation convention is the charge-weighted moment shown in the integral;
it is not an unweighted density moment, a perpendicular current channel, an
equilibrium contribution, or a particle-frame moment.

It is the normalized, parallel specialization of the vector [normalized
gyrocenter perturbed current
density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density), with the
additional $J_1$ finite-Larmor-radius weighting. Removing that weighting
gives the corresponding [parallel normalized gyrocenter perturbed current
density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the charge-weighted perturbed current is
directed along the local equilibrium magnetic field, whose orientation is
expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized parallel current density
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of gyrocenters times 1st order Bessel function of the first kind

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
NAMES.short:
Normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the dimensionless total pressure
response of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic
eigenmode, formed from parallel and perpendicular pressure moments weighted
by the first-order Bessel function evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument
and normalized to the equilibrium species pressure.
NAMES.long:
Normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the dimensionless total pressure
response of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic
eigenmode, formed from parallel and perpendicular pressure moments weighted
by the first-order Bessel function evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument
and normalized to the equilibrium species pressure. It is a species-resolved
complex amplitude representing the finite-Larmor-radius part of the
gyrocenter pressure response.

For species $s$, it is defined by the sum of the first-order Bessel-weighted
parallel and perpendicular pressure moments divided by the equilibrium
species pressure:

$$
\widehat{P}^{(J_1)}_s = \frac{P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)} + P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)}}{p_s}, \qquad P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)} = \int d^3v\, m_s v_\parallel^2 J_1(\lambda_s)\widetilde{F}_{g,s}, \qquad P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)} = \int d^3v\, m_s \frac{v_\perp^2}{2} J_1(\lambda_s)\widetilde{F}_{g,s}
$$

where $P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)}$ and $P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)}$ are
pressure-moment amplitudes with pressure units, $p_s=n_sT_s$ is the
equilibrium species pressure when $T_s$ is expressed as energy per particle,
$m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities
parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field, $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element, and $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$ is the perturbation
amplitude of the gyrocenter distribution. The first-order Bessel function
$J_1$ is evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument $\lambda_s=k_\perp
v_\perp/\Omega_s$, with $k_\perp$ the magnitude of the wave vector
perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field and $\Omega_s=|q_s|B/m_s$
the positive cyclotron-frequency magnitude.

The total moment is the sum of
parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1 and
[perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1).
It is a gyrocenter-distribution moment with explicit $J_1(\lambda_s)$
weighting; it is distinct from normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure,
which lacks this Bessel-1 weighting, and from particle-distribution pressure
perturbations such as normalized_perturbed_pressure and
normalized_total_particle_perturbed_pressure_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode.
Because $J_1(0)=0$, this member vanishes at zero gyroaveraging argument.

In a linear eigenmode, $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$ is the complex coefficient
multiplying the chosen harmonic phase factor. This moment inherits the same
arbitrary global amplitude and phase normalization as the eigenmode;
changing the reference phase multiplies all perturbation amplitudes by the
same complex factor, so its sign and phase are defined only relative to that
reference.

sources.leaf_definition: Normalised pressure, defined as the sum of pressure_parallel and pressure_perpendicular
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of gyrocenters times 1st order Bessel function of the first kind

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless field-aligned component of the charge-weighted first velocity
moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution, normalized to a reference
current-density scale.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the parallel component of the normalized gyrocenter
current-density perturbation. It represents the charge-weighted first moment
of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution along the local magnetic-field
direction and is the field-aligned component of [normalized gyrocenter
perturbed current
density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).

$$
J_{parallel,g}^{(s)} = \frac{q_s}{J_{\rm ref}} \int v_\parallel\,\delta g_s\,d^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $v_\parallel$ is its velocity
along the local magnetic field, $\delta g_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter
distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and
$J_{\rm ref}$ is the reference current-density scale. The underlying
unnormalized moment is the corresponding perturbed gyrocenter current
density. For a linear eigenmode, the quantity may be complex, with its phase
defined by the eigenmode convention.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter current density
points along the local magnetic field.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized parallel current density
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of gyrocenters

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.short:
Parallel normalized particle perturbed current density is the normalized
parallel-current-density moment of the perturbed particle distribution for
one kinetic species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, projected along the
equilibrium magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel normalized particle perturbed current density is the normalized
parallel-current-density moment of the perturbed particle distribution for
one kinetic species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. It represents the
species contribution to the perturbed current projected along the
equilibrium magnetic field in the particle frame.

The normalized moment is defined by the particle-frame parallel
current-density moment divided by its reference normalization:

$$
\hat{j}^{\,p}_{\parallel s} = \frac{\int q_s v_\parallel \delta f^{\,p}_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{j_\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\hat{j}^{\,p}_{\parallel s}$ is the parallel normalized particle
perturbed current density for species $s$, $q_s$ is the charge of that
species, $v_\parallel$ is the particle velocity component along the
equilibrium magnetic field, $\delta f^{\,p}_s$ is the perturbed particle
distribution function, $d^3v$ denotes integration over particle velocity
space, and $j_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference current-density scale for the
normalized moment.

The scope is a species-resolved linear perturbation moment at the selected
eigenmode and wavevector; the aggregation convention is per kinetic species,
with no summation over species. The quantity excludes equilibrium current
density and unperturbed distribution-function moments.

It is the particle-frame counterpart of parallel normalized perturbed
current density, which uses the gyrocenter perturbed distribution rather
than the particle distribution. The particle-frame moment can differ through
the gyrocenter-to-particle transformation, including
polarization-drift-related contributions when they are part of that
transformation. The corresponding particle-frame higher parallel-velocity
moment is parallel normalized particle perturbed heat flux.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the particle-frame perturbed current carried
by the species is directed along the equilibrium magnetic field.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized parallel current density
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of particles

NAMES.name: particle_energy
NAMES.short:
Energy-like measure of particle motion in velocity space, combining parallel
and perpendicular kinetic-energy contributions for distribution-based plasma
quantities.
NAMES.long:
Particle energy denotes the kinetic-energy content or energy coordinate
associated with a species' velocity-space distribution. It is based on both
parallel and perpendicular motion and can characterize an ordering
coordinate, a distribution moment, or a response of a perturbed
distribution.

The underlying single-particle kinetic energy is

$$
E = \frac{1}{2}m\left(v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2\right)
$$

where $E$ is particle kinetic energy, $m$ is particle mass, and
$v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are the velocity components parallel and
perpendicular to the local magnetic field. Distribution-based quantities use
this energy or an equivalent velocity-space weighting;
[fast_particle_energy](name:fast_particle_energy) represents a
fast-population moment, while perturbed_particle_energy represents the
corresponding response of a perturbed distribution. An effective coordinate
may additionally be scaled by a positive reference energy, as in
[effective_particle_energy](name:effective_particle_energy). A moment of a
perturbed distribution may be signed even though the underlying
single-particle kinetic energy is nonnegative.

NAMES.name: effective_particle_energy
NAMES.short:
Effective particle energy is a gyrokinetic kinetic-energy-like coordinate
that orders a species in velocity space and may be scaled by a positive
reference energy.
NAMES.long:
Effective particle energy is a gyrokinetic velocity-space energy assigned to
a particle species through a kinetic-energy-like weight. It provides the
energy coordinate used to order that species in velocity space and is the
unnormalized concept underlying [normalized effective particle
energy](name:normalized_effective_particle_energy). It differs from
[particle energy](name:particle_energy), which denotes the energy content of
the full distribution.

The effective energy is defined by the selected velocity-space weight:

$$
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{eff},s}(\boldsymbol{\xi}) = w_s(\boldsymbol{\xi})
$$

where $s$ labels the species, $\boldsymbol{\xi}$ denotes its velocity-space
variables, and $w_s$ is a kinetic-energy-like weight, such as the total
kinetic energy or a directional component. A normalized specialization
divides $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{eff},s}$ by a strictly positive species
reference energy. This quantity is distinct from perturbed particle energy,
which describes a moment of a distribution perturbation rather than the
effective energy coordinate itself.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short:
Perpendicular normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the dimensionless
linear-eigenmode weight for laboratory-frame toroidal angular-momentum
transport in the perpendicular velocity-space channel.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the electrostatic
contribution to toroidal angular-momentum transport across magnetic flux
surfaces for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the laboratory frame. The
perpendicular label identifies the velocity-space channel relative to the
equilibrium magnetic field, not the direction of transport across the flux
surface.

For a specified eigenmode-amplitude convention, the normalized weight is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_\perp = \frac{\Pi_\perp^{\mathrm{es}}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\Gamma_\perp$ is this normalized linear weight,
$\Pi_\perp^{\mathrm{es}}$ is the perpendicular-channel contribution to
laboratory-frame toroidal angular-momentum flux carried by the fluctuating
E×B drift, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference momentum-flux
scale. The superscript $\mathrm{es}$ denotes the electrostatic contribution
driven by the perturbed electrostatic potential. Neither the reference scale
nor the eigenmode-amplitude convention is fixed by the name.

The weight applies to one linear eigenmode at its specified wavevector; it
does not imply a sum over modes or a saturated nonlinear transport level. It
represents laboratory-frame momentum transport, not rotating-frame momentum
transport.

This is the perpendicular-channel specialization of [normalized momentum
flux due to E×B
drift](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). With matching
population, mode, and normalization conventions, adding the
[parallel-channel
contribution](name:parallel_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
gives the full electrostatic toroidal momentum flux. It excludes the
separate perpendicular-channel contributions attributed to [perturbed
parallel vector
potential](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential)
and [perturbed parallel magnetic
field](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field).

NAMES.name: perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Gyro-Bohm-normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to perturbed parallel
magnetic-field fluctuations is the perpendicular velocity-space contribution
to turbulent transport of toroidal angular momentum. Linear forms are
eigenmode weights, while nonlinear forms are turbulent-flux contributions.
NAMES.long:
Gyro-Bohm-normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to the perturbed
parallel magnetic field is the perpendicular velocity-space contribution to
turbulent transport of toroidal angular momentum across magnetic flux
surfaces.

The normalized quantity is defined by

$$
\widehat{\Gamma}_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel} = \frac{\Gamma_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{GB}}}
$$

where the hat denotes gyro-Bohm normalization, $\Gamma_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta
B_\parallel}$ is the toroidal angular-momentum-flux contribution in the
perpendicular velocity-space channel driven by the perturbed parallel
magnetic field, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{GB}}$ is the gyro-Bohm reference
momentum-flux scale. The subscript $\phi$ identifies toroidal angular
momentum, and $\perp$ identifies the velocity-space channel perpendicular to
the equilibrium magnetic-field direction $\hat{b}$. The perturbation $\delta
B_\parallel$ is the magnetic-field fluctuation along $\hat{b}$, the unit
vector in the direction of the equilibrium magnetic field. The reference
scale follows the gyrokinetic normalization based on [electron density at
the outboard midplane](name:electron_density_at_outboard_midplane) and
[electron temperature at the outboard
midplane](name:electron_temperature_at_outboard_midplane).

For a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, this quantity is expressed as an
eigenmode weight; in nonlinear turbulence, it is the corresponding
turbulent-flux contribution. The quantity does not specify a particular
wavevector summation, time average, or flux-surface average. The
perpendicular designation refers to the velocity-space channel relative to
the equilibrium magnetic field, not to the spatial direction of transport;
the flux is across magnetic flux surfaces.

This is the perpendicular component of the aggregate [normalized momentum
flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field], complementary to its
[parallel-channel
contribution](name:parallel_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field).
It isolates the perturbed-parallel-magnetic-field contribution and excludes
electrostatic contributions and the distinct [perpendicular momentum flux
due to the perturbed parallel vector
potential](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the toroidal angular-momentum flux is
directed outward across magnetic flux surfaces, away from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
NAMES.short:
Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the dimensionless
velocity-space moment of a species' perturbed distribution in a linear
gyrokinetic eigenmode, weighted by the perpendicular speed squared times the
total speed squared and normalized to the unperturbed total-speed-squared
energy moment of the same species.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the perpendicular
member of the particle perturbed-energy moment family for a species in a
linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its velocity-space weight is the perpendicular
speed squared multiplied by the total speed squared, and the reference
normalization is the corresponding unperturbed total-speed-squared energy
moment.

The quantity is defined as the ratio of the weighted perturbed moment to the
unperturbed reference moment:

$$
M_{\perp E,s} = \frac{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2\, v^2\, f_{0,s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $v_\perp$ is the particle
speed perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction, $v_\parallel$ is
the particle speed parallel to the local magnetic-field direction, $v^2 =
v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2$ is the total particle speed squared, $\delta f_s$
is the perturbed particle distribution of the eigenmode, $f_{0,s}$ is the
unperturbed (equilibrium) particle distribution, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The denominator is the unperturbed
total-speed-squared energy moment shared by the parent [normalized particle
perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) and its
parallel counterpart, so the parallel and perpendicular members are directly
comparable.

This scalar is the perpendicular entry of the [normalized particle perturbed
energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) decomposition and is
paired with the parallel normalized particle perturbed energy evaluated with
the same perturbed distribution and normalization. It is distinct from the
[perpendicular normalized particle perturbed
pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure), whose
weight is the perpendicular speed squared alone: the energy moment retains
the additional total-speed-squared factor. Because a linear eigenmode
carries an arbitrary complex amplitude, only comparisons made under the same
eigenmode amplitude and phase convention are physically meaningful.

sources.leaf_definition: Normalized moment (integral over 0.5 * m * v_perp^2 * v^2)
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of particles

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short:
Normalized perpendicular pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle
distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, representing its
perpendicular thermal-energy fluctuation relative to a reference pressure.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure is a dimensionless
complex eigenmode moment of the perturbed particle distribution function. It
represents the fluctuation of thermal energy associated with random particle
motion perpendicular to the background magnetic field and is the
perpendicular component of the [normalized particle perturbed
pressure](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure).

For species $s$, it is defined by the perpendicular second velocity-space
moment:

$$
\hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2\,\delta f_s\,d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the speed perpendicular to the
background magnetic field, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle
distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and
$p_\mathrm{ref}$ is a positive reference thermal pressure. The perpendicular
and parallel normalized particle perturbed pressure components together
describe the gyrotropic pressure perturbation.

Unlike the perpendicular normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure, this
moment is formed from the physical particle distribution and includes
finite-Larmor-radius effects associated with the particle-to-gyrocenter
transformation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the perpendicular pressure perturbation
represents a local increase in perpendicular thermal energy relative to the
equilibrium background.

sources.leaf_definition: Normalized perpendicular pressure
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of particles

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
NAMES.short:
Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular
pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear
gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and
weighted by the first-order Bessel function J1.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular
kinetic-pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear
gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and
weighted by the first-order Bessel function. It is the perpendicular
projection of the Bessel-1 normalized perturbed pressure moment, associated
with particle kinetic energy perpendicular to the background magnetic field.

The normalized moment is defined by

$$
\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1} = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2}\, J_1\!\left(k_\perp \rho(v_\perp)\right)\, \delta f_\mathrm{gc}(\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1}$ is the normalized perpendicular Bessel-1
pressure perturbation, $p_\mathrm{ref}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the
reference thermal pressure, $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference density,
$T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference temperature expressed as particle energy,
$m$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to
the background magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function,
$k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude, $\rho(v_\perp)$ is the
velocity-dependent gyroradius, $\delta f_\mathrm{gc}$ is the perturbed
gyrocenter distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is the perpendicular pressure-tensor projection of
[normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1);
the complementary field-aligned projection is
parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1. It differs from
perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure by the first-order Bessel
weighting and from perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure by
representing the Bessel-1 finite-Larmor-radius contribution rather than the
unweighted gyrocenter moment.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when, after the eigenmode phase has been fixed by
the chosen reference perturbation, the real part of the defining
Bessel-weighted perpendicular kinetic-pressure moment represents an excess
over the equilibrium gyrocenter distribution.

sources.leaf_definition: Normalized perpendicular pressure
sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalized) of the perturbed distribution function of gyrocenters times 1st order Bessel function of the first kind

NAMES.name: ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_particle_reference_temperature
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio comparing a particle species’ kinetic temperature with
the positive reference temperature on the same magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The quantity expresses the kinetic temperature of a selected particle
species relative to a single reference thermal scale on the same magnetic
flux surface. It is the normalized counterpart of [particle
temperature](name:particle_temperature), while retaining the species
dependence of the numerator.

It is defined by

$$
T_p^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{T_p}{T_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $T_p$ is the kinetic temperature of the selected particle species and
$T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference temperature for the flux
surface.

The ratio is dimensionless and is not an absolute temperature; its value
depends on the specified reference temperature.

sources.leaf_definition: normalized temperature
sources.parent_definition: Set of species (including electrons) used in the calculation and related quantities

NAMES.name: electrostatic_potential_amplitude
NAMES.short:
Normalized phase-independent magnitude of an electrostatic-potential
fluctuation relative to its reference field. It describes amplitude only,
not the signed potential perturbation or its phase.
NAMES.long:
Electrostatic potential amplitude is the phase-independent magnitude of a
normalized electrostatic-potential fluctuation about a specified reference
field. It represents the size of the fluctuation in the scalar electrostatic
potential while discarding its sign or complex phase.

The amplitude is defined from the normalized fluctuation as:

$$
A_\Phi = \left|\frac{\Phi_\mathrm{fluc}}{\Phi_\mathrm{norm}}\right|
$$

where $A_\Phi$ is the electrostatic-potential amplitude,
$\Phi_\mathrm{fluc}$ is the electrostatic-potential fluctuation relative to
the chosen reference field, and $\Phi_\mathrm{norm}$ is the potential
normalizing quantity specified for that fluctuation. The vertical bars
denote the modulus; for a real representation they denote absolute value.

This quantity excludes the signed fluctuation, the reference potential
itself, and the complex phase of a fluctuation representation.
Electric-field perturbations require the signed or complex potential
fluctuation; amplitude alone is insufficient to recover sign, phase, or
gradient direction. The [perturbed electrostatic-potential
amplitude](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude) is the
perturbation-specific specialization of this amplitude concept.

NAMES.name: perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude
NAMES.short:
Perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the phase-independent
magnitude of a fluctuating electrostatic-potential perturbation represented
as a complex quantity. It is the modulus of the perturbation and excludes
the arbitrary complex phase.
NAMES.long:
Perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the phase-independent
magnitude associated with an electrostatic-potential fluctuation. It
represents the strength of the scalar perturbation after removal of the
arbitrary complex phase of a complex perturbation representation.

The amplitude is defined by the complex modulus of the perturbation:

$$
A_{\tilde{\Phi}} = \left|\tilde{\Phi}\right|
$$

where $A_{\tilde{\Phi}}$ is the perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude,
$\tilde{\Phi}$ is the complex electrostatic-potential perturbation, and
$|\cdot|$ denotes the complex modulus.

This quantity applies to electrostatic-potential fluctuations in turbulence
for the perturbation variable being represented. No aggregation over
species, modes, times, or spatial regions is implied by the name.

It is distinct from the complex perturbation itself, from the complex phase
of that perturbation, and from amplitudes of other fluctuating fields. It
does not denote a vector component, vector magnitude, or vector projection;
electrostatic potential is a scalar field.

The [normalized perturbed electrostatic potential
amplitude](name:normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude) is a
reference-scaled instance of this parent quantity: the same modulus
operation is applied to a normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude
NAMES.short:
Normalized perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the modulus of the
complex normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation eigenfunction for a
gyrokinetic mode. It retains the phase-independent amplitude while
discarding the arbitrary complex phase.
NAMES.long:
Normalized perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the modulus of the
complex normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation eigenfunction for a
gyrokinetic mode. It represents the phase-independent strength of the
electrostatic potential component of the mode and excludes the arbitrary
complex phase of the eigenfunction.

For a complex normalized perturbed electrostatic potential eigenfunction
$\delta\hat{\phi}$, the amplitude $A_{\phi_N}$ is defined by its complex
modulus:

$$
A_{\phi_N} = |\delta\hat{\phi}| = \sqrt{\left(\operatorname{Re}\delta\hat{\phi}\right)^2 + \left(\operatorname{Im}\delta\hat{\phi}\right)^2}
$$

where $\operatorname{Re}\delta\hat{\phi}$ and
$\operatorname{Im}\delta\hat{\phi}$ are the real and imaginary parts of the
same normalized eigenfunction, and $A_{\phi_N}$ is the corresponding
dimensionless amplitude.

This quantity is not the complex eigenfunction itself and contains no phase
information. Its value is non-negative and depends on the normalization
chosen for $\delta\hat{\phi}$, so it denotes relative mode structure within
that normalization rather than an independently fixed absolute scale.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the perturbed electrostatic potential normalized to the sum of amplitudes of all perturbed fields
sources.parent_definition: Electrostatic potential, magnetic field and magnetic vector potential

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of a flux surface, defined as the midpoint between
its minimum and maximum major-radius values in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Major-radius coordinate of flux surface

In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis, with
coordinate values $(R,\phi,Z)$, the surface coordinate is defined as the
midpoint of those extrema:

$$
R_{\mathrm{fs}} = \frac{R_{\min} + R_{\max}}{2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the representative major-radius coordinate
assigned to the flux surface, $R_{\min}$ and $R_{\max}$ are the minimum and
maximum values, respectively, of $R$ over that complete surface, $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The extrema are taken over the complete flux surface, and their midpoint is
the aggregation convention; this quantity is not an area-, volume-, or
flux-weighted average. It is a single surface-level value, not a pointwise
coordinate or the sequence of coordinates along the [radial outline of a
flux surface](name:radial_outline_of_flux_surface).

This quantity specializes the [major-radius
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) to a flux surface by representing the
surface’s full range with one extrema midpoint. It differs from the
[normalized minor radius of a flux
surface](name:normalized_minor_radius_of_flux_surface), which expresses
radial position as a normalized quantity.

A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a
nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$,
$\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius of the flux surface of interest, defined as (min(R)+max(R))/2
sources.parent_definition: Physical quantities used for normalization (useful to link to the original simulation/experience)

NAMES.name: reference_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Reference magnetic-field vector of the equilibrium magnetic induction
evaluated at the reference point, retaining field strength and direction
before selecting a component such as the toroidal reference magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The reference magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}$ is the equilibrium
[magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) evaluated at the reference point
used to define a local field reference. It represents the vector field at
that locus, retaining both field strength and direction rather than
selecting a cylindrical component or scalar magnitude.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the reference field may
be resolved as

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}=B_{R,{\rm ref}}\hat{R}+B_{\phi,{\rm ref}}\hat{\phi}+B_{Z,{\rm ref}}\hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}$ is the reference magnetic field, $B_{R,{\rm
ref}}$ is its signed radial component, $B_{\phi,{\rm ref}}$ is the [toroidal
reference magnetic field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field),
$B_{Z,{\rm ref}}$ is its signed vertical component, and $\hat{R}$,
$\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ are the basis vectors for increasing major
radius, toroidal angle, and vertical height.

This quantity is defined at the reference point for the equilibrium field;
it is not the spatially unrestricted local [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field). It has no species population, and its
aggregation convention is a point value at the reference locus, not a
spatial average or finite-volume reduction.

The parent quantity is distinct from component-resolved reference fields:
the [toroidal reference magnetic
field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field) is its projection along
$\hat{\phi}$ at the reference point, not a separate vector field. It is also
distinct from the unrestricted [toroidal magnetic
field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), which does not by name impose the
reference locus.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{B}_{\rm
ref}$ points along the corresponding positive basis vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where the positive directions
are increasing major radius $R$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and
increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_reference_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the
equilibrium magnetic field at the reference point whose major radius is the
reference major radius, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the
equilibrium magnetic field at a specified reference point in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The reference point
has major radius equal to the [reference major
radius](name:reference_major_radius).

The defining projection is:

$$
B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \cdot \hat{\phi}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}})
$$

where $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$ is the toroidal reference magnetic field,
$\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field,
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}=(R_{\mathrm{ref}},\phi_{\mathrm{ref}},Z_{\mathrm{ref}})$
is the full reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference major radius, and $\hat{\phi}$ is
the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$. For an axisymmetric
equilibrium, the value is independent of $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$.

This quantity is the reference-location specialization of [toroidal magnetic
field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field). It is distinct from [toroidal magnetic
field at magnetic axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis), from
the magnetic-field magnitude, and from [toroidal vacuum magnetic
field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal magnetic field at major radius r
sources.parent_definition: Physical quantities used for normalization (useful to link to the original simulation/experience)

NAMES.name: total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.short:
Cumulative power transferred from electromagnetic waves to electrons, ions,
and fast populations within a selected magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Cumulative absorbed electromagnetic-wave power deposited in the plasma
volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface. It includes absorption
by electron, ion, and fast populations and represents an enclosed quantity
rather than a local power density.

The defining relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{abs}}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power, $\psi$
is the label of the selected magnetic flux surface, $V(\psi)$ is the volume
enclosed by that surface, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{x})$ is
the total absorbed wave power density at spatial position $\mathbf{x}$
summed over electrons, ions, and fast populations, and $dV$ is the
differential volume element.

This quantity is cumulative over the enclosed volume and is not a local
deposition density or a population-resolved contribution.
Population-specific quantities such as [thermal electron power at an inside
flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and
[thermal ion power at an inside flux
surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) resolve components
of this aggregate. When the selected surface encloses the full absorbing
plasma volume, it equals [total absorbed wave
power](name:total_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.leaf_definition: Total absorbed wave power (electrons + ion + fast populations) inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Source radial profiles (flux surface averaged quantities) for various time slices

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short:
Vertical Z coordinate of a beam-tracing beam position along its propagation
path, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the vertical coordinate of a ray or beam position evaluated
along the propagation path of a beam-tracing beam. It identifies the
position's height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with
basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is the projection of the beam position onto the vertical
direction:

$$
z = \mathbf{r} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $z$ is the vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of
the beam point, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector of the
right-handed cylindrical frame.

This quantity applies to each beam position along the propagation path and
is not aggregated over path positions or over multiple rays or beams. It
describes geometric location only; it is not a wave amplitude, magnetic or
electric field component, or propagation-direction quantity.

It is distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the launching
position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position), which identifies
the beam's physical launch point rather than a general position along the
path. At the launch point, the two coordinates may have the same value.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Position of the ray/beam along its path

NAMES.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field
NAMES.short:
Complex phasor of the E-plus left-hand circular polarization component of an
electromagnetic-wave electric field in a magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
The left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field is the E-plus complex
phasor obtained by projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor
onto the circular polarization basis transverse to the local equilibrium
magnetic field. It retains both polarization amplitude and phase and is a
component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field).

Using the negative-time-harmonic convention, the component is defined by

$$
E_{+}=\mathbf{E}_{w}\cdot\mathbf{e}_{+}^{*},\qquad \mathbf{e}_{+}=\frac{\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}+i\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}}{\sqrt{2}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}=\hat{\mathbf{b}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}_{0}}{|\mathbf{B}_{0}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}_{w}$ is the complex wave-electric-field phasor,
$\mathbf{B}_{0}$ is the local background magnetic field, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$
is its unit direction, the transverse unit vectors $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}$
and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}$ form a right-handed basis, and the asterisk
denotes complex conjugation. The associated physical field uses
$\exp(-i\omega t)$, so this component carries phase information rather than
representing a field magnitude. Its real-part sibling [left-hand circularly
polarized wave electric field real
part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part)
provides one quadrature, while the [right-hand circularly polarized wave
electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field)
represents the opposite circular polarization.

sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Left hand circularly polarized component of the perpendicular (to the static magnetic field) electric field, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude
NAMES.short:
Amplitude representation of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus
component of a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor,
retaining its polarization direction while removing its complex phase.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the amplitude-form representation of the right-hand
circularly polarized E-minus contribution to a coherent electromagnetic-wave
electric field. It retains the polarization basis direction and field
strength while excluding the phasor phase.

$$
\mathbf{E}_{-,\mathrm{amp}} = |\tilde{E}_{-}|\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{-}
$$

Here, $\mathbf{E}_{-,\mathrm{amp}}$ is the amplitude representation of the
polarized field component, $\tilde{E}_{-}$ is the complex E-minus
coefficient of the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric
field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{-}$ is the right-hand circular polarization unit vector
transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field.

The quantity applies specifically to the right-hand E-minus polarization and
excludes the left-hand E-plus component, represented by the [left-hand
circularly polarized wave electric
field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field). It is an
amplitude rather than the full complex phasor and therefore does not retain
phase information; it is also distinct from the separate real and imaginary
quadratures.

The parent quantity imposes no toroidal-mode resolution, flux-surface
aggregation, or power-deposition weighting. The [per-toroidal-mode
right-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field
amplitude](name:per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude)
is a specialization that applies those operations to this common amplitude
quantity.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude
NAMES.short:
Power-deposition-weighted flux-surface amplitude of the right-hand
circularly polarized E-minus wave-electric-field phasor for each toroidal
mode number.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the nonnegative amplitude of the right-hand circularly
polarized (E-minus, or R-wave) component of a coherent wave electric-field
phasor. It represents the mode-resolved field strength after
power-deposition-weighted averaging over a magnetic flux surface.

For toroidal mode number $n$, the amplitude is defined by

$$
\mathcal{E}_{-,n}^{\mathrm{amp}} = \left|\frac{\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\,\widetilde{E}_{-,n}\rangle_{\psi}}{\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle_{\psi}}\right|
$$

where $\mathcal{E}_{-,n}^{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the amplitude of the E-minus
wave-electric-field component, $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number,
$\widetilde{E}_{-,n}$ is its complex phasor, $p_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the
power-deposition density, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a
flux-surface average, and $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface. The
definition applies where the power-deposition-weighted denominator is
nonzero.

The quantity is restricted to the right-hand circular polarization and to
one toroidal mode at a time. It excludes the left-hand circularly polarized
component, the total electric-field amplitude obtained by combining
polarizations, and an unweighted average or an average of pointwise
amplitudes; the modulus is taken after the weighted complex averaging.

It is the toroidal-mode-resolved amplitude specialization of the [right-hand
circularly polarized wave electric-field
amplitude](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude).
The corresponding complex E-minus phasor is described by the [right-hand
circularly polarized wave electric
field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), while this
quantity retains only its amplitude.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude
sources.parent_definition: Right hand polarized electric field component for every flux surface

NAMES.name: total_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.short:
Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to all plasma
particle populations and integrated over all spatial locations.
NAMES.long:
Total absorbed wave power is the total rate at which coherent
electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to all plasma particle
populations, with contributions integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the
combined energy of all included plasma particle populations, $t$ is time,
and the subscript “waves” restricts the derivative to direct energy transfer
from the coherent electromagnetic-wave field.

This quantity is globally aggregated: it is summed over all species, charge
states, populations, and spatial locations. It includes direct
wave-to-particle transfer and excludes electromagnetic power that remains in
the wave field and energy subsequently redistributed between particle
populations by collisions.

It is the species-summed specialization of [absorbed wave
power](name:absorbed_wave_power), unlike [electron absorbed wave
power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), which is restricted to electron
populations. It is also the global counterpart of [total absorbed wave power
at the inside flux
surface](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface), which
retains only the power enclosed within a selected flux surface;
Fourier-resolved contributions are represented by [per-toroidal-mode total
absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.leaf_definition: Total absorbed wave power
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities for various time slices
